## x87 regions: the stack cache by use, truncation in vector registers (2026-10-21)

Measured on this shared server under a load average of 20-60 (other projects): Node only (the one rendered browser run
attempted for bfme1-108 ran its menu at ~5 fps and was useless); medians, concurrent pairs, alternated in-process A/B.

- **The 24-bit precision "gap" was mostly V8's tiers.** x87loop-bench waited 100 ms after its warm-up for TurboFan; the
  24-bit regions (larger: every result tested) were often still partly in Liftoff, so xform measured 24.8 ns at 0x7f
  against 10.7 at 0x27f (the "2.4x" of the 2026-10-21 audit). TurboFan only (`--no-liftoff`, now the tool's default;
  `--liftoff` for the tiers as they come): xform 14.2 vs 10.6 ns, 13.8 vs 12.8 with full 24-bit significands
  (`--full`); sums of squares 17.4 vs 15-19. What remains at round-to-nearest is the exponent test of every f32 result
  (off the dependency chain) and, for values carried across a block boundary, the promotion of the f32 shadow at the
  block's end (dropped at block entry) — a latency-bound recurrence 3.6 vs 2.0 ns. Not changed: keeping f32 shadows
  across blocks needs a dataflow over the region's entries (any block can be entered from the dispatcher with an
  f64 from the state block), for at most a few % of the menu's guest time. The truncating mode (0xc7f), BFME1's map
  load, was the real gap: xform 27.0 vs 12.8 ns at 53-bit.
- **Truncation cut in the XMM register** (`x87VecMask`, default on; translate-x87.js pushCut24): roundTowardZero24
  cleared the 29 low significand bits on the integer pattern — `vmovq` to a general register, `and`, `vmovq` back:
  two domain crossings (~3 cycles each) on the dependency chain of every arithmetic instruction. Now `f64x2.splat ;
  v128.and ; extract_lane 0` (vmovddup + vpand), the bit tests that choose the path still on the integer copy, off the
  chain. The mask is a v128 local set by the prologue (`L_CUT24`, regions translated for mode 0xc00 only): built
  inline at each use, its three-instruction constant ate the gain in the game (one pair: map load +3.7 %).
  x87loop-bench 0xc7f `--full`, mask on vs off in the same tree (11 runs): sums of squares 39.7 -> 30.0 ns, xform 28.2
  -> 23.9, arith across blocks 13.3 -> 12.2, recurrence 4.4 -> 3.5.
- **The stack cache by use** (`x87Live`, default on; Emitter.x87LiveSites): an x87 region loaded all eight stack
  registers at its entry (and after fallbacks) and wrote all eight back at its exits. Code.track records the body's
  gets / sets of the eight locals; once the body is emitted, the loads and stores of the locals it never touches are
  overwritten with `nop`s of the same length (no offset recorded in the body moves: branch hints, the alt slot, visit
  flags). Exact because local L_ST0+k always holds physical register (L_TOP + k) & 7: the locals only move between
  each other in x87Rotate, whose gets and sets mark all eight, and L_TOP otherwise changes only around a write-back
  and reload (fallbacks, FLDENV / FRSTOR, TOP resets). chain-bench x87 call/return 39.3-46.4 -> 29.6-29.9 ns (3
  alternated runs; integer regions 23-26 ns); tools/x87-size.mjs, 27 regions x 3 control words: TurboFan machine code
  124 480 -> 98 020 bytes (-21 %), WASM +0.4 % (the prologue's mask). tests/jit-x87-live.test.js (masks; random
  programs over few registers with every register valued, fallbacks, FNSAVE / FRSTOR, FNSTENV / FLDENV, FDECSTP /
  FINCSTP, slices; it fails when a used register's load is dropped).
- Kernels, this branch against main (x87loop-bench `--full --ab`, 9 alternated runs, medians): 0xc7f xform 27.0 ->
  21.5 ns, sums of squares 36.0 -> 30.4, fild + fmul + fstp 5.4 -> 4.3, recurrence 3.9 -> 3.4, e^x 28.2 -> 25.6, arith
  across blocks 12.2 -> 10.8; 0x7f and 0x27f within the noise (-15 to +15 % on single cases, both directions).
- **BFME1 (bfme-vanilla 2.22, the same lotrbfme.exe as 1.08), Node, concurrent pairs** (startbench, copies of the same
  warm profile, menu 135 s then the map load; guest ns per instruction, map load seconds): both options on vs off —
  loadscreen 1.037 / 1.055 (43.7 / 44.3 s), 1.063 / 1.077 (43.7 / 45.3 s), 1.213 / 1.234 (51.3 / 53.8 s, load 60);
  3D menu 1.340 / 1.346, 1.359 / 1.392, 1.452 / 1.505. Vector mask alone (local mask) on / off: loadscreen 1.009 /
  1.048 (43.2 / 44.7 s), menu 1.303 / 1.296. So -1.5 to -3.7 % on the map load, -0.5 to -3.5 % on the menu: at the
  edge of the noise (single pairs on a machine at load 20-60), every pair in the same direction on the map load.
- The map load's hot loop (region e66cde / e66ecb, mode 0xc00: a sums-of-products fitting loop, 84 guest instructions
  per iteration, 168 M iterations per load: 14 G of the ~40 G instructions) is flat in `perf annotate`: no
  instruction above 1.6 % of the region. Its x87 arithmetic is ~12-14 host instructions an operation (sub / mul,
  bit tests, the cut), its FSTP m32 an exact-demote test and the SMC check. No single pattern left to fuse.
- Not changed: an on-grid but inexact product under truncation (a double operand like 0.9 whose f64 product rounds onto
  the 24-bit grid: x87loop-bench `fmul m64 0.9` at 0xc7f, 21 % of its iterations) leaves the region for the
  interpreter (~57 ns an iteration); the BFME1 map load spent 0.01 s in the interpreter, so it does not happen there.
  A Dekker product's error sign would settle it inline.

## Where BFME1's 3D menu spends its translated code, and eight shorter shapes (2026-10-22)

Measured on this shared server (load average 15-70); Node, `startbench --virtual` on the bfme-vanilla 3D menu (a phase of
6 213 M guest instructions, the same work in every run: `+20:waitframe:300,100000;40:mark:menu;70:mark:end`), real-clock
runs of `bfme-phases.txt` for the map load and play, microbenchmarks. Base: main a36cd74.

- **Profile** (`perf record -F 3999 -k 1` on `node --perf-prof`, `perf inject -j`, samples of the emulator thread in the
  menu phase's window — `--time` from the phase's start / end and the realtime-monotonic offset): translated regions 88 %
  of the thread, flat (the hottest 2.6 %; 2 281 region functions). Over the 200 hottest (69 % of the region samples),
  by instruction: ALU 28 %, guest memory accesses 16 %, stack slots (spills, reloads, stack parameters) 12.3 %, branches
  9.3 %, vector / float 9.3 %, register-to-register moves 8.8 %, the chained-exit tail (exit-kind test to the tail call)
  8.7 %, the f32 exponent tests of 24-bit x87 arithmetic 3.8 %, prologues (to the dispatch loop's stack check) 3.4 %,
  SMC map loads 0.4 %. Menu mix (block counters for that phase only): MOV 21.7 %, JCC 10.5 %, ADD 9.0 %, FLD 7.2 %,
  CMP 6.6 %, FMUL 5.9 %, FSTP 3.9 %, IMUL 2.4 %; 8.2 % of the instructions are checked stores (2.2 per group of the same
  address registers); 10.7 chained transitions per 1 000 instructions, 56 % of them leaving x87 regions. The hottest
  region (10 % of the instructions) is a sound mixer loop (`imul; sar; imul m; add [edi], eax; add [edi+4], ebx`).
- **f32 exponent test** (translate-x87.js arithF32): the result's exponent field in [1, 254] tested as `(bits << 1) -
  2^24 <u 0xfe000000` — `vmovd; lea; cmp; jae` instead of `vmovd; shr; movzx; sub; cmp; jae` on every 24-bit
  round-to-nearest arithmetic instruction with float operands. The double-operand range test (pushFloatRangeTest) and
  the truncating mode's exponent tests (roundTowardZero24's pushOutOfRange, the directed path's) on the pattern shifted
  right by 31 (the significand's top bits under the exponent field move no bound): one mask less each.
  x87loop-bench 0x7f `--pos`, 9 alternated runs at a quiet moment: xform 13.87 → 10.35 ns, sums of squares 17.22 →
  12.33, arith across blocks 8.26 → 8.04; at 0xc7f `--full` (process host instructions, perf stat, the shifted tests
  alone): sums of squares 8.32 → 8.17 G, xform 7.56 → 7.49 G.
- **Chained exits** (emitChain): address 0 and every target from the thunks up (thunks, the private area, past 2 GiB)
  in one unsigned compare (`tv - 1 >= THUNK_BASE - 1`; profiling translations keep the two tests to count them apart);
  JIT_HASH_BASE in the probes' load offsets, no mask on the home slot. chain-bench (5 alternated runs, medians): int
  call/return 24.9 → 24.0 ns, x87 34.6 → 32.6 ns. tests/jit-chain-targets.test.js.
- **x87 tag word** (loadX87Tags / flushX87Tags): the rotation by TOP as one variable shift of the doubled byte (`(tw |
  tw << 8) >> TOP`) instead of two (x64 takes the count in CL) at every x87 region entry and exit. With the previous item:
  chain-bench 1e7 host instructions 27.55 → 25.91 G.
- **Write-back of read-only x87 registers** (`x87LiveStores`): Code tracks sets apart from gets; the exit and fallback
  stores of the stack registers the body reads but never sets become nops like those of untouched ones (such a local
  holds what the cache loaded, the state block is the same). x87-size, 27 regions × 3 control words, with the items
  above: machine code 126 692 → 124 644 B. tests/jit-x87-live.test.js (programs reading the caller's registers; a
  mutation dropping a written register's store fails it).
- **IMUL with dead flags** (`imulDead`): `imul r32, r/m32 (, imm)` whose next instruction in the block writes every
  arithmetic flag (CMP, TEST, ADD, a shift by a constant, another IMUL...) — no exit can lie between them — is a 32-bit
  multiply (no sign extensions and 64-bit product for CF / OF). The mixer loop runs four per iteration.
  tests/jit-imul-dead.test.js.
- **MOVSX m8 / m16** with `i32.load8_s` / `load16_s` (it was a zero-extending load and a `movsx` of the register).
- **Lazy states without a first operand** (`lzaFree`, LZA_FREE in translate.js): ADD, INC, DEC, NEG and a SUB writing
  its destination (a new lazy kind, SUBR; CMP keeps SUB, its first operand being the register the next Jcc reads) leave
  0 in L_LZA; the inline conditions and both flags helpers derive what they need from the result and the second
  operand (ADD: a = res - b, CF = res <u b; SUBR: a = res + b; NEG: a = -res; INC / DEC never read it). The
  destination's old value — `add esi, 4`, `sub ecx, 1`, the word an `add [edi], eax` loaded — no longer lives up to the
  next flag write or to every exit in between (TurboFan kept it in a register or a spill slot for the SMC checks' cold
  paths). The readers ignore the operand for those kinds whatever the option, so regions translated either way exchange
  lazy states. memop-bench `8x add [edi+8], eax` (3 alternated runs): 5.83 / 6.84 / 7.16 → 5.45 / 6.09 / 5.64 ns per
  iteration. tests/jit-lza-free.test.js (randomized programs of every size and destination against the interpreter,
  sliced; the helpers with garbage first operands; mutations of one inline reader and of the JS helper fail it).
  SUBR alone can be turned off (`lzaSub: false`: a SUB keeps the SUB kind and its operand).
- **BFME1 3D menu**, concurrent `--virtual` pairs, guest ns per instruction (load average 15-70 during these):
  - every item but lzaFree, main / branch (4 pairs): 0.940 / 0.923, 1.110 / 1.091, 1.008 / 0.985, 1.080 / 1.066
    (−1.3 to −2.3 %; emulator thread CPU −0.7 to −2.4 %);
  - lzaFree off / on in the same tree (4 sequential pairs, launch order alternated): 1.026 / 0.981, 1.125 / 0.965,
    1.025 / 1.041, 1.077 / 0.997 (−4.4, −14, +1.6, −7.4 %);
  - everything, main / branch (4 more pairs, load 30-70): 1.182 / 1.210, 1.241 / 1.201, 1.110 / 1.038, 1.135 / 1.185
    (+2.4, −3.2, −6.5, +4.4 %) — within this machine's spread.
- **Host instructions of the emulator thread in the menu window** (`perf record -e instructions:u -c 100000`, samples
  counted between the phase's marks; `node --no-liftoff` so that no tier-up timing decides how long code runs in
  Liftoff): main 15.54 G; branch 14.11, 15.50, 15.93 G (three runs of the same build); lzaFree off 14.61, 15.98,
  15.20 G; lzaSub off 16.03 G — the same build's runs differ by up to 12 %: even this count follows the machine's load
  (with Liftoff on it doubled under load: 13.4-14.5 G at load ~15, 23-27 G at load ~60), so it does not resolve a few %
  either. The frames (121) and API calls (295 600-296 400) of the phase are the same in every run. Kept on the
  microbenchmarks, the map-load and play pairs below and the time pairs above; not validated beyond that.
- **BFME1 map load and play** (real clock, `bfme-phases.txt`, concurrent main / branch pairs, the same warm profile
  copied for each, launch order alternated; the same guest work in each phase within 2 %):

  | pair | loadscreen (s) | loadscreen ns / insn | play ns / insn | play thread CPU (s) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1, main launched first | 47.8 / 45.2 (−5.4 %) | 1.109 / 1.072 | 2.786 / 2.704 (−2.9 %) | 79.3 / 78.6 |
  | 2, branch launched first | 40.2 / 39.7 (−1.2 %) | 0.987 / 0.970 | 2.872 / 2.728 (−5.0 %) | 80.5 / 78.3 |

  The menu phase of these real-clock runs (its first 135 s, frame-paced) did not move (1.334 / 1.329, 1.667 / 1.674 ns).

## Registers, region exits and loops in BFME1's 3D menu (2026-10-22): five variants, none kept

Base: main ddfd8e8. Scenario: bfme-vanilla, a warm profile (the canonical seed's Options.ini), `startbench --virtual`,
`+20:waitframe:300,100000; 40:mark:menu; 70:mark:end` — a menu phase of 6 228 M guest instructions, 121 frames, the same
in every run; the whole run 43.9 G guest instructions. Measured with `ab-virtual --perf` style counts (above) and
concurrent timed pairs.

- **Where the guest registers live.** Already in WASM locals for a whole region: the 8 registers, EFLAGS, the four lazy
  flag values and the budget are the region function's parameters (block and state block address first), passed from
  region to region by the chained tail call; the state block sees them only at a non-chained exit (to the dispatcher:
  API thunks, the stop address, an exhausted budget, a miss), around an interpreter fallback (written before, reloaded
  after) and at the dispatcher's entry. The x87 stack (by use, x87Live) and the XMM registers the region names are
  loaded at its entry and written back at its exits. Writing back "only the dirty registers" cannot apply to the general
  registers: a region entered by a chain has a state block older than its parameters, so it does not know which values
  the state block lacks. Those exits are rare anyway: over the whole run 397.7 M chained transitions against 13.1 M
  exits to API thunks and 0.1 M budget exits; in the menu no fallback step. Moving values out of the parameters into
  the state block was measured before (below: +17 % per chained call/return), as were the parameters' order and
  packing.
- **Profile** (`perf record -e cycles:u` of the whole run with `--perf-prof`, the emulator thread in the last 40 % of
  the run, samples in region code by host instruction, branch hints on): memory operands 29.0 %, ALU 27.6 %, stack
  slots 14.2 % (most of them 64-bit spill stores), branches 12.2 %, register moves 10.5 %, vector 6.4 %; Liftoff code 8 %
  of the region samples. The two first instructions of the region functions (`push rbp; mov rbp, rsp`) hold 3.3 % of
  the samples: instruction fetch at the entry of a region entered cold. In the hottest region (an msvcr71 helper, 1.3 %
  of the thread) 19 % of the samples are its x87 / XMM prologue and ~27 % its exit (the merge's moves into the shared
  tail, the x87 and XMM write-back, the hash probe's load, the table's bounds and signature checks waiting on it).
- **Dispatches through a region's br_table** (`--jit-profile`, menu phase): 23.5 M against 60.7 M chained transitions —
  backward transfers outside a structured loop 16.1 M, returns to a call site placed earlier 4.5 M, forward into a
  loop elsewhere than at its header 1.7 M, back into a loop 1.3 M. The hottest sites (a counter per site, whole run):
  an msvcr71 function's RET returning to the call in the region's first block, 41 M — its callee is called from two
  places, and the depth-first layout put it after the second call, in the first call's return path; overlapping
  loops whose headers are one block apart (8.8 M, 8.6 M).
  - RET → local return site counted as a back edge by planUnits (`retLoops`): returns through the top 4.49 → 3.32 M,
    but forward entries into loops 1.66 → 3.86 M and all dispatches 23.5 → 24.7 M; JIT instructions +0.7 % (318.8 vs
    316.6 G).
  - Loops nested (`nestLoops`, re-measured): dispatches 23.5 → 15.6 M (back to the top 16.1 → 4.4 M); JIT instructions
    317.99 / 318.34 vs 316.87 / 316.66 G (+0.4 %), JIT cycles 147.10 / 146.80 vs 147.28 / 146.24 G (0.0 %), process
    instructions +1.3 % (compilation). A dispatch costs about what the structured loop's header costs.
- **XMM write-back of read-only registers** (`xmmLiveStores`, as x87LiveStores: Code tracking the XMM locals' sets, the
  stores of the unset ones made `nop`s): JIT instructions 317.02 / 316.58 vs 316.57 / 316.61 G — this menu's x87 code
  hardly uses XMM registers, and 32-bit code rarely reads one it does not write.
- **Hints in the chained exit** (`chainHint`: the first probe's hit likely, the later probes and the miss out of line,
  the target range test unlikely), with the previous item: JIT instructions 316.67 / 316.09 vs 316.43 / 316.29 G, JIT
  cycles 140.25 / 139.23 vs 139.16 / 139.31 G.
- **Regions of 144 blocks / 1 200 instructions**: JIT instructions +1.0 % in two batches, JIT cycles −3.6 % in one
  (149.55 / 148.08 vs 154.30 / 154.66 G) and +1.2 % in the other (127.20 vs 125.73 G), V8's compilation +18 % of the
  process's instructions; not changed.
- Timed pairs (the same tree, the three first variants off / on, 4 concurrent pairs, launch order alternated): menu
  guest ns per instruction 1.161 / 1.111, 1.158 / 1.168, 1.014 / 0.991, 1.042 / 1.071 — within the spread.

## Measured, not kept

- Region parameters reordered so that the budget rides in a register and the state block's address (the same for
  every region of a thread) on the stack (2026-10-22: block, budget, the 8 registers, state, EFLAGS, the lazy values):
  chain-bench host instructions 25.56 G vs 25.57 G, times equal — the budget's stack store saved, the state block's
  address reloaded where the exits use it (the stop-address test of every chained exit).

- Branch-free x87 condition codes (2026-10-21: compareCC / compareEflags as `(a<b) << 8 | (a==b) << 14 | unordered *
  0x4500` instead of nested ifs): x87loop-bench compares with random signs, one run under load 23-36: fcomp + test ah
  +8.9 %, fcomp + sahf +32 %, fucompp -21.6 %, fcom + fchs + fstp +3.5 % — the nested compares predict as well as the
  guest's own Jcc; not kept.

- Raising ZE / OE for an infinite result of x87 arithmetic at 53 / 64-bit precision in translated code (X87.arith
  does): the test on the arithmetic hot path cost +15 % on the 53-bit sums-of-squares kernel; left unraised by the JIT
  (documented in translate-x87.js).
- Directed rounding up / down on the vector mask as toward zero used to: the sign-dependent step is cheaper as an
  integer add on the bits (kept that way).
- x87 arithmetic cold path (2026-10-06, tools/x87-size.mjs and host instructions per iteration of x87loop-bench's
  `xform` under `perf record`, branch hints on): the inline zero test of a float result on its bit pattern (`x << 1 ==
  0`) instead of float compares — the result's bits, shared with the hot path's exponent test, then stay live past it:
  221 host instructions per iteration against 207; no inline zero test at all (exact zeros through the kernel too):
  203, but every product by zero would be a call. Kept: float compares (207; the earlier code 215).
- Chained exits each with its own chain code (`siteChain`: the hash probe and tail call at every exit site, the probe
  addresses constants for static targets) instead of one shared exit: RotWK +15 %, BFME2 +52 % (Node in-session) —
  every tail-call site pins all sixteen values to the call's argument places, and the code grows.
- Region parameters packed so that none goes through the stack (5 i32 + 6 f64 holding two i32 each, V8's x64 argument
  registers): +4 % in RotWK play, and slower in a calling-convention microbenchmark (the packing costs more than the
  stack arguments it saves).
- 11 i32 region parameters (block, state, 8 registers, budget), EFLAGS and the 4 lazy-flag values in the state block
  (loaded by every region's prologue, stored before every chained tail call) — 2026-10-06, stopped at the gate:
  `tools/chain-bench.mjs` (Node 24 / V8 13.6, alternated with main) int 22.7 → 26.6 ns, x87 36.2 → 43.0 ns per
  call/return pair. The parameter count itself is worth ~0.3 ns per pair (the same 11-parameter code without the five
  loads and stores — exact for that bench only — 22.2 ns); the prologue loads cost ~3.5 ns per pair and the stores
  ~2.2 ns, so skipping the loads for blocks whose flags are dead cannot pay either. The exactness suite passed on the
  prototype (only the listing / code-shape tests needed their local numbering updated).
- Regions that end where another region already translates the block (`dedup`: an exit chaining into it, no copy): the
  translated code shrinks (process CPU −15 %, less compilation) but the extra transitions cost more: guest time per
  instruction RotWK +6.8 %, BFME2 +10 %.
- Region entry at its first block by a compare instead of the br_table (`entryFast`) and the chained exit's probes
  after the first and its non-chained path hinted out of line (`coldChain`): RotWK −1 %, BFME2 +2.8 %, within the
  noise.

- Heat by time windows (visit flags re-armed every 10 s; a successor cold when it ran in fewer than a quarter of the
  windows its branch ran in): worse than "never ran" (RotWK Node in-session: +4 % vs −7 %, and translation storms).
- Weak topological block order (`layout: 'wto'`, Bourdoncle): Node in-session, RotWK +6 % with heat, +15 % without;
  BFME2 −3 % with heat, +2.5 % without.
- 96-block regions with heat: −3 % in one RotWK run, within the spread, more translation work.

- Dead bytes at a region's start (`tierPad`): small regions tier up to TurboFan ~4x sooner in tierup-bench, nothing in
  play (Liftoff is <1 % of the region samples in Node play).
- Lazy flags rebuilt at exits from the registers the flag instruction read (so that the lazy values die at their
  branch instead of living to every exit): exact (randomized test against the interpreter), +1 to +2 % in play.
- Region size 24 blocks (+6 to +11 % in the browser), 96 blocks (before 2026-10-05: −2.5 % in Node play alone, neutral
  with the layout, slower first launch; see "Region size"), nested loops on top of the layout (neutral), `L_BLK` set before back edges (+3 %).
- Dropping the lazy flags at exits entirely (an inexact experiment to bound the previous one): the games misbehave
  within seconds — exits do resume where flags are read.

```

`docs/media-playback.md`:

```md
# Movie and sound file playback: DirectShow (quartz.dll)

Windows games of the DirectX 7-9 era play their movies — and often their music — with DirectShow. Vice City, for
instance (traced with `--log comx,video`), creates the filter graph manager and plays `movies\Logo.mpg` then
`movies\GTAtitles.mpg`:

```
CoCreateInstance(CLSID_FilterGraph e436ebb3-…, IID_IGraphBuilder 56a868a9-…)
IGraphBuilder::RenderFile(L"movies\\Logo.mpg")           (QueryInterface: IMediaControl, IMediaEventEx, IVideoWindow, IMediaSeeking)
IVideoWindow::put_Owner(game window), put_WindowStyle(WS_CHILD | WS_CLIPSIBLINGS | WS_CLIPCHILDREN)
IMediaEventEx::SetNotifyWindow(game window, message 0x40d, 0)
IVideoWindow::SetWindowPosition(0, 0, 640, 480), put_MessageDrain(game window)
IMediaControl::Run()
  … the game's loop polls its input (a key or a click: IMediaControl::Stop, Release) and its messages:
  the notification message → IMediaEventEx::GetEvent → EC_COMPLETE → FreeEventParams → Stop, Release
```

Without DirectShow (before: `REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG`) the game waited for a key on a black screen.

The formats are told apart by their content, as DirectShow's source filters do (an AVI named `.mpg` plays).

## What is implemented (src/win32/quartz.js)

The filter graph manager as an application sees it (`CLSID_FilterGraph`, `CLSID_FilterGraphNoThread`), one COM object
per interface sharing the graph (QueryInterface answers any of them):

- **IGraphBuilder / IFilterGraph(2)**: `RenderFile` (the path relative to the current directory, through the virtual
  file system); building graphs by hand (`AddFilter`, `Connect`, pins) is not available (`E_NOTIMPL`).
- **IMediaControl**: `Run`, `Pause` (the current picture shown), `Stop` (the position kept, as DirectShow does),
  `GetState`, `RenderFile`.
- **IMediaEvent / IMediaEventEx**: an event queue (`EC_COMPLETE` once every stream has ended, `EC_ERRORABORT` on a read
  failure), a manual-reset event handle signaled while events are queued (`GetEventHandle`), `GetEvent` with a timeout,
  `WaitForCompletion`, the notification message posted to the `SetNotifyWindow` window per event.
- **IMediaSeeking / IMediaPosition**: duration, current / stop positions, absolute and relative seeking (backward:
  decoders restarted from the beginning), rate 1 only.
- **IVideoWindow / IBasicVideo(2)**: the video window's owner, style, position, visibility (`AutoShow`: shown on
  Run / Pause), full-screen mode, source and destination rectangles, video size. Without a video stream these methods
  answer `E_NOINTERFACE`, as the filter graph manager does without a video renderer.
- **IBasicAudio**: volume and balance (1/100 dB), applied to the sound stream.

Files that cannot be played get the results of a Windows lacking the codec, so that games skip the movie as before:
`HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND)`, `VFW_E_UNKNOWN_FILE_TYPE` (not a recognized format),
`VFW_E_UNSUPPORTED_STREAM` (MPEG audio layer III with no decoder), `VFW_S_AUDIO_NOT_RENDERED` (video with a sound stream
that cannot be decoded: the video plays silent). A graph run without anything rendered (a game ignoring RenderFile's
failure) completes at once (`EC_COMPLETE`): a movie of no length.

## MCI (src/win32/mci.js)

The other way Windows programs play a movie or a sound file: the Media Control Interface's digital video and wave
audio devices (`MPEGVideo`, `AVIVideo`, `digitalvideo`, `waveaudio`; a file's type from its extension as Windows'
[MCI Extensions] say, or `type` / `device!file`), through `mciSendString(A/W)` and `mciSendCommand(A/W)`:

- `open` (alias, `parent` / `style child`, the device ID returned), `close` (`all`), `play` (`from` / `to`, `notify`,
  `wait`, `fullscreen`, `repeat`; a file name played without `open`: opened on the fly), `stop`, `pause`, `resume`,
  `seek` (`to start` / `end` / a position), `status` (mode, length, position, ready, time format, window handle...),
  `set time format` (milliseconds, frames — `AVIVideo`'s default), `set audio`, `setaudio volume`, `window` (`handle`,
  `state`), `put` / `where` (window, destination, source), `info`, `capability`; `mciGetErrorString`,
  `mciGetDeviceID`; the command messages `MCI_OPEN`, `MCI_PLAY`, `MCI_STOP`, `MCI_PAUSE`, `MCI_RESUME`, `MCI_SEEK`,
  `MCI_STATUS`, `MCI_SET`, `MCI_WINDOW`, `MCI_PUT`, `MCI_WHERE`, `MCI_CLOSE`.
- The pictures: in the window given by `window handle` (its client area, at the video's size unless a destination is
  put), as a child of `parent`, or the device's own window (centered, the video's size); full screen with `fullscreen`.
- `notify`: `MM_MCINOTIFY` posted to the callback window (`MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL` at the end, `SUPERSEDED` / `ABORTED`
  when another play, a stop or a close comes first). `wait`: the calling thread waits for the end (the others run).
- Other device types (`cdaudio`, `sequencer`...) answer `MCIERR_INVALID_DEVICE_ID` as before: programs go on without.

Both APIs drive the same playback engine, `MoviePlayer` (src/win32/movie-player.js).

## Formats (src/media)

What Windows plays with its own splitters and codecs (no codec pack installed). Chrome decodes none of the video and
few of the audio formats, so most are decoded here, written from the standards; the rest goes to the browser:

| file | streams | decoded by |
|---|---|---|
| MPEG-1 system stream (`.mpg`; MPEG-2 program stream pack headers accepted) | MPEG-1 video, MPEG audio | `mpeg-ps.js` + below |
| MPEG-1 video elementary stream (`.m1v`) | I / P / B / D pictures | `mpeg1-video.js` |
| MPEG audio (`.mp2`, `.mp3`, `.mpa`; also inside a WAVE file, format 0x50 / 0x55) | layers I, II | `mpeg-audio.js` |
| | layer III (MP3) | the browser: WebCodecs `AudioDecoder` (asynchronous: `AsyncAudio`) |
| RIFF WAVE (`.wav`) | PCM 8-32 bit, float, extensible, IMA ADPCM, Microsoft ADPCM | `wav-source.js` |
| AVI (`.avi`) | video: uncompressed DIB (1-32 bit), Microsoft RLE (RLE8 / RLE4), Microsoft Video 1 (16-bit), Cinepak | `avi-source.js`, `vfw-codecs.js` |
| | sound: as in WAVE files, MPEG audio | `wav-source.js`, `mpeg-audio.js` / the browser |

- `mpeg-ps.js`: demultiplexer (packs, PES packets with MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 headers, time stamps), incremental.
- `mpeg1-video.js`: half-pel motion compensation with edge extension, quantizer matrices, the inverse DCT in double
  precision (even / odd butterflies; equal to the definition up to the rounding of exact halves).
- `mpeg-audio.js`: layers I and II (all bit allocation tables, MPEG-2 low sampling frequencies, intensity stereo),
  polyphase synthesis. The synthesis window (`mpeg-audio-window.js`, a constant of the standard, table B.3) was
  recovered by `tools/mpa-window-fit.mjs`: the decoder's output is linear in the 512 window values, so a least-squares
  fit against a reference decoding gives them; every value lands within 0.07 units of a multiple of 2^-16 (the table's
  unit) and the halves mirror each other as the standard says.
- `mpeg-source.js`: a file being played: read ahead in 256 KiB chunks (asynchronously when the range is still on the
  network: `file.prepare`), pictures and sound decoded on demand for a stream time; a caller late by more than one
  picture has the B pictures in between dropped undecoded. Layer III frames go to the browser's decoder 1 s ahead of
  the time asked. The duration: from the time stamps of the first and last packs, the VBR header (Xing / Info, VBRI) of
  an MP3, or the bit rate.
- `wav-source.js`: WAVE chunks, PCM and ADPCM blocks. IMA ADPCM follows the reference algorithm's step arithmetic.
- `yuv.js`: BT.601 studio-range Y'CbCr 4:2:0 → RGBA (when the host cannot take the planes itself).
- `avi-source.js`: the header list (first video and audio streams; a stream without a decoder is left out:
  `VFW_S_VIDEO_NOT_RENDERED` / `VFW_S_AUDIO_NOT_RENDERED`, as the filter graph manager answers when some streams
  cannot be rendered), the `movi` chunks parsed as they are read (`rec ` lists, palette changes), every frame decoded in
  order (the codecs' frames depend on the previous picture).
- `vfw-codecs.js`: the Video for Windows decoders Windows ships with, drawing into a persistent RGBA frame: DIBs with
  palettes, RLE8 / RLE4 (deltas, absolute runs), Microsoft Video 1 (skip / 1 / 2 / 8-color 4x4 blocks), Cinepak (strips,
  V1 / V4 codebooks with partial updates and inheritance, intra / inter / V1-only vectors, gray codebooks). Indeo,
  MPEG-4 or WMV video are not decoded (a codec Windows XP may have, through other components).

Accuracy (tests/media-mpeg.test.js, media-audio-files.test.js, media-avi.test.js against ffmpeg's decoders): AVI video
exact (RLE, DIB, gray Cinepak) or within 1 per component (the 5-bit expansion of 5-5-5 colors, Cinepak's color
conversion rounding); MPEG-1 video 45-66 dB PSNR per
picture (only the inverse DCT's rounding differs from ffmpeg's integer transform), layer I / II > 100 dB SNR, PCM and
Microsoft ADPCM exact, IMA ADPCM ~44 dB (ffmpeg computes the step product otherwise); MP3 through WebCodecs in Chromium
118 dB against ffmpeg (tools/media-browser-check.mjs; the browser's decoder, like Windows', plays the encoder delay and
the LAME header frame that ffmpeg drops).

## Output

- **Pictures**: the host display's video layer (`#vid` on the page, a display-sized transparent layer above the GDI
  and Direct3D layers), the picture stretched to the video window's rectangle — the owner's client area plus the
  window's position for a child window, the destination rectangle inside it — as the video renderer's window covers
  the game's. In the browser the decoded planes become a WebCodecs `VideoFrame` drawn on the layer
  (`BrowserDisplay.presentVideoYuv`: the color conversion and scaling are the canvas's); without VideoFrame (or with
  `?dbg=ORTHROS_VIDEO_RGBA=1`) `yuv.js` converts them and `presentVideo` draws the RGBA picture. The layer is hidden
  when the window is hidden or the graph released. Input goes to the game's window (the video window is not a real
  window: the message drain games set is where it would go anyway).
- **Sound**: a stream voice of the DirectSound mixer (`dsound.js createAudioStream`): a looping 16-bit ring in guest
  memory mixed by the AudioWorklet like any DirectSound buffer; the graph writes the decoded samples 250 ms ahead of the
  play cursor, both following the VM clock, so pictures and sound stay together.
- **Clock**: the VM clock. `vm.media` (MediaClock) is advanced by the scheduler at its wake-up passes
  (`Sched.wakeBlocked`) and asks it to wake up for the next picture or sound refill (`Sched.nextWake`): playback goes on
  while the game's threads wait (`WaitForCompletion`, a message wait, `Sleep`).

Logs: `--log video` (RenderFile, Run, completion and release with statistics: pictures shown, decoded then overtaken,
B pictures skipped, decoding and showing time per picture on the game's worker, lateness).

## Measured (Vice City, headless Chromium with SwiftShader on the shared server)

`movies\Logo.mpg`: 640x480, 25 fps, 48 kHz stereo layer II, 39.5 s. Every run: 987 pictures, all shown (none dropped
or skipped), lateness at most 10-16 ms, 39.48 s of sound mixed (no underrun). On the game's worker, per picture:

| presentation (2 runs each, alternated) | decoding | showing |
|---|---|---|
| RGBA conversion here (`?dbg=ORTHROS_VIDEO_RGBA=1`) | 2.9, 2.7 ms | 2.4, 2.3 ms |
| WebCodecs VideoFrame (default) | 2.5, 3.2 ms | 0.3, 0.6 ms |

The movies can be skipped (a key or a click: the game stops and releases the
graph, the layer disappears) and the game goes on to its main menu.

```

`docs/mmo.md`:

```md
# Vice City — Orthros Edition: the shared world ("MMO")

Status: built 2026-10-20/21 (DECISIONS.md D102). The owner's decisions are binding (section 1). This is the contract
between the server (`src/host/mmo.js`, `mmo-proto.js`), the page (`src/host/web/mmo-link.js`, `src/ports/re3/play.js`)
and the engine (fork Lomchat/reVC, branch `orthros`, `src/extras/mmo/`, built with `-DREVC_ORTHROS_EXTRAS=ON`: the
Orthros Edition's release; the plain reVC build has none of it). Engine-defined record bodies (PLAYER_STATE, the
ENTITY_STATE kinds, EVENT / TARGETED subs, the character state blob, debug keys, test commands) are documented at the
top of each engine module (`mmo_players.cpp`, `mmo_entities.cpp`, `mmo_combat.cpp`, `mmo_session.cpp`,
`mmo_world.cpp`, `mmo_social.cpp`, `mmo_lobby.cpp`, `mmo_wire.cpp`).

## 1. The owner's decisions

1. Death works like the game: weapons lost, $100 hospital fee, respawn at the nearest hospital, remaining money kept.
2. A new character starts with $5000 and a pistol, at the Ocean View hotel.
3. Several characters per account (max from the manifest, default 8), each with its pseudo, skin and own state (money,
   weapons, position, health, armour); chosen when entering the multiplayer; the skin can be changed from the
   character menu. All characters of an admin account may use cheats.
4. World cheats (weather, time, traffic, pedestrians' behaviour) apply to everyone. Slow / fast motion is disabled for
   everyone (cheats, adrenaline, scripted time scale). Personal cheats (weapons, vehicles, health, armour, wanted level,
   skin) are visible to everyone through the normal replication.
5. Police and wanted levels are kept: cops spawn around the wanted player and the others see them. Over remote players:
   the pseudo AND the wanted stars, MMO style.
6. Missions and activities are disabled in the multiplayer.
7. Garages are not personal: whatever is in any garage persists on the server; everyone can use every garage. Street
   cars despawn as in the game.
8. "teleport" typed (like HELP) opens a list of all the game's save points; choosing one teleports there. For everyone,
   even with a wanted level.
9. Text chat on T, and names over heads.
10. A server admin list containing lomchat; only admins may use cheats in the multiplayer, the others are refused.
Also: combat everywhere (PvP), money / weapons / position kept except on death, a few players (not thousands),
traffic and pedestrians synchronised ("the same world"), no game saves in the multiplayer (all state on the server,
garage cars included), world persistence: nobody connected → the world is saved and frozen (its clock too); the first
arrival loads it; it stays live until the last one leaves.

The multiplayer is an entry of the game's own main menu ("Multiplayer" / "Multijoueur"), like the free mode: inherent to
the game, not a choice before launching it. It exists only in the Orthros Edition (`vice-city-orthros`), whose
manifest version has an `mmo` object.

## 2. Architecture

```
 engine (C++/wasm, one per browser tab)          page (JS)                     server (Node, one process)
 src/extras/mmo/*.cpp  --EM_JS-->  Module.orthrosNet = mmo-link  --WebSocket-->  src/host/mmo.js
   owns every game rule                generic: framing, queue,          generic hub: accounts, characters,
   (what a record means)               reconnect, heartbeat, away        slots, relay, ownership of ids,
                                                                          records + locks, world clock + vars,
                                                                          admins, persistence
```

* The server knows nothing about Vice City (CLAUDE.md: no game-specific code). It stores opaque blobs (character
  state, records), opaque world variables (id → int32), a clock (game minutes advancing at a rate), and arbitrates
  ownership of 32-bit network ids. Admin rights are checked on the server for world changes; personal cheats are a
  client rule (the engine refuses cheats when the server said "not admin").
* The page is a generic relay (`src/host/web/mmo-link.js`, Standardization rule: one shared module, usable by any
  runtime): the engine builds and parses every record; the page only adds its own PING / AWAY records.
* The engine is authoritative for its own player and for the ambient entities it owns (section 7). Hits are decided
  by the shooter's client and applied by the victim's owner.

## 3. Manifest

Version level (any runtime may use it; validated by the server's `mmoProblem(version)`), e.g. in
`data/games/vice-city-orthros/manifest.json` → `versions[0].mmo`:

```json
"mmo": { "maxCharacters": 8, "maxPlayers": 16 }
```

`maxCharacters` 1–16 (default 8), `maxPlayers` 2–32 (default 16). A version without `mmo` has no shared world: the
WebSocket refuses with reason 2 and the page does not create `Module.orthrosNet`. `docs/game-manifest.schema.json`
documents it. `/api/manifests` exposes `mmo: true` for such versions (the home card may show "Multijoueur").

## 4. Server (`src/host/mmo.js`)

`mmoApi({ getManifest, identify, dir, log, now }) → { handle(req, res, url) → bool, upgrade(req, socket, url) → bool,
flush() → void, close() → void }`, all state in its closure; wired in `server.js` (import; create after the account
API; `handle` in the handler chain; `upgrade` in the `upgrades` array; `server.mmo`; flush on 'close'; SIGTERM/SIGINT
flush in the CLI part). `dir` = `--mmo <dir>`, default `<accountsDir>/mmo`; without accounts the MMO is disabled.

* `GET /api/mmo/<versionId>` → `{ enabled, signedIn, admin, players }` (JSON, no-store).
* WebSocket `GET /api/mmo/<versionId>/ws` (`acceptWebSocket` from lan.js). Same-origin check (Origin's host ==
  Host header, as goldsrc.js udpRelay) before accepting, else raw 403. Not signed in (`identify(req)` null) → accept,
  send REFUSED(1) and close (so the page can tell). Unknown/disabled version → REFUSED(2). Session re-checked every
  60 s (logout → REFUSED(1), close).
* Files under `<dir>`: `admins.json` = `["lomchat"]` (lowercase usernames; re-read when its mtime changes; missing →
  no admin); `<versionId>/characters.json` = `{ nextId, characters: [{ id, user (account id), name, skin, money,
  state (base64), createdAt, updatedAt }] }`; `<versionId>/world.json` = `{ minutes, msPerMinute, vars: {id: value},
  records: {key: base64} }`. Atomic writes (`<f>.<pid>.tmp`, fsync, rename). Debounced 5 s while live; flushed when the
  last player leaves, on `flush()`, on `close()`.
* World lifecycle: a world is loaded at its first JOIN and unloaded (after flushing) when its last player leaves. Its
  clock only advances while it is loaded: `minutes(now) = baseMinutes + (now - baseMs) / msPerMinute`; on unload
  `minutes` is stored. Default `msPerMinute` 1000 (the game's own rate: one game minute per real second); new world
  starts at 12:00 of day 0 (minutes = 720).
* Slots: 0..maxPlayers-1, given at JOIN, freed at LEAVE/close. Rank: a world-wide counter increasing at each JOIN (the
  lowest present rank is the most senior player). Tag: a 12-bit value 1..0xFFE per in-world session, never one in use
  (by a live session, or by an id in the ownership table).
* Network ids (u32): players `0xFFF00000 | slot`; entities `(tag << 20) | counter` (counter 1..0xFFFFF, chosen by the
  engine). Owner of an entity id: the ownership table's entry, else the session whose tag it carries, else none.
* Ownership table: changed by OWN records and by departures. On LEAVE / close / AWAY(away=1) of a slot, every entity
  it owns whose position is known (from its ENTITY_STATE records in the last 15 s) is given to the nearest present,
  not-away player within 300 m (by their last PLAYER_STATE position); otherwise it is orphaned (owner 255: clients
  delete their copies). Each change is broadcast as OWNER. An entry naming another present player lasts until
  ENTITY_GONE, that player's departure or another OWN (forgetting it would hand the entity back to its creator): the
  engine sends ENTITY_GONE for every owned entity it deletes. Only orphan entries untouched for 60 s are forgotten.
  WELCOME's player list includes the joining player itself (its rank); LEAVE is answered LEFT then LOBBY.
* Records + locks (garages, generic): `key` u16 → bytes (≤ 4096) + holder slot. LOCK: if free or held by the asker →
  holder = asker, reply RECORD (holder = asker) to the asker and RECORD (holder) to the others; if held by another →
  reply RECORD (holder = other) to the asker. STORE: only from the holder: store data, holder = none, broadcast
  RECORD. UNLOCK: holder = none, broadcast. A holder leaving / going away releases its locks (data unchanged).
* Characters: name `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 _.-]{1,15}$` (2–16 characters, ASCII), unique case-insensitively per
  version; skin `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,20}$`; state ≤ 4096 bytes, opaque (empty = new character: the engine applies its
  defaults). At most `maxCharacters` per account. JOIN of a character already in the world from another socket:
  that older socket gets REFUSED(5) and is closed; the new one joins.
* Chat: text 1–120 bytes, printable ASCII or Latin-1 0xA0–0xFF only (else DENIED(3)); at most 1 per second (burst 5).
  The server keeps the last 20 lines per world and sends them after WELCOME.
* Admin-only requests (WORLD_SET, WORLD_EVENT) from non-admins → DENIED(type, 1).
* Limits per socket: frames ≤ 64 KB (bigger → close), ≤ 800 records/s and ≤ 256 KB/s inbound on average (token
  buckets; excess dropped, with one DENIED(type, 2) per second at most); lobby requests ≤ 5/s. Output: records to a
  socket are coalesced per event-loop turn into one frame; if `socket.writableLength` > 1 MB, realtime records
  (0x20–0x24) to it are dropped until it drains (control records still go).
* A peer silent for 45 s is closed (the page pings every 15 s).

## 5. Wire protocol

All little-endian. `str8` = u8 length + bytes. One WebSocket binary message = one or more records.
Client → server record: `u16 len | u8 type | body` (len counts type + body, ≤ 65535).
Server → client record: `u16 len | u8 type | u8 from | body` (len counts type + from + body; from = sender slot, 255 =
the server). Unknown types are ignored by both sides (forward compatibility).

### Client → server

| type | name | body |
|---|---|---|
| 0x01 | HELLO | u16 protocol (=1), u8 lang (0 en, 1 fr) — first record after the socket opens; reply LOBBY |
| 0x02 | CHAR_CREATE | str8 name, str8 skin → CHAR_RESULT then LOBBY |
| 0x03 | CHAR_SKIN | u32 charId, str8 skin → CHAR_RESULT then LOBBY |
| 0x04 | CHAR_DELETE | u32 charId → CHAR_RESULT then LOBBY |
| 0x05 | JOIN | u32 charId → WELCOME (+ RECORDs, CHAT history, PLAYER_JOIN to the others) or CHAR_RESULT(op 5, error) |
| 0x06 | LEAVE | — → LEFT; others get PLAYER_LEAVE (+ OWNER changes) |
| 0x07 | PING | f64 clientMs → PONG |
| 0x08 | AWAY | u8 source (0 engine: pause menu; 1 page: tab hidden), u8 away (0/1). A player is away if any source says so |
| 0x09 | CHAR_SAVE | i32 money, u16 n, n bytes state (in world only; stored for the joined character) |
| 0x0A | CHAT | str8 text → CHAT to everyone in the world (sender included) |
| 0x0B | WORLD_SET | admin: u8 op; op 1: u8 varId, i32 value; op 2: u16 minuteOfDay (0–1439, same day); op 3: f32 msPerMinute (30–60000) → WORLD to everyone |
| 0x0C | WORLD_EVENT | admin: u8 id, i32 arg → WORLD_EVENT to everyone (sender included) |
| 0x0D | LOCK | u16 key |
| 0x0E | STORE | u16 key, u16 n, n bytes (≤ 4096) |
| 0x0F | UNLOCK | u16 key |
| 0x10 | OWN | u32 netid, u8 op (1 claim: owner = me; 2 give: owner = `to`), u8 to. Claim refused (OWNER unchanged, to the asker only) when the entity's last state had flag bit 0 (driven by its owner's player) and its owner is present and not away. Give accepted only from the current owner |
| 0x11 | PLAYER_INFO | str8 skin → PLAYER_INFO to the others |
| 0x20 | PLAYER_STATE | f32 x, y, z, then engine bytes (≤ 240) — relayed to the others |
| 0x21 | ENTITY_STATE | u32 netid, u8 kind, u8 flags, f32 x, y, z, then engine bytes (≤ 400) — dropped unless sender owns netid; relayed |
| 0x22 | ENTITY_GONE | u32 netid, u8 reason — owner only; forgets the entry; relayed |
| 0x23 | EVENT | u8 sub, engine bytes (≤ 1000) — relayed to the others |
| 0x24 | TARGETED | u32 target netid, u8 sub, engine bytes (≤ 1000) — sent to the owner of target (player id → that slot) only |

### Server → client

| type | name | body |
|---|---|---|
| 0x80 | REFUSED | u8 reason (1 sign-in needed, 2 no shared world for this version, 3 world full, 4 protocol, 5 joined elsewhere, 6 server error), str8 detail; the socket closes after it |
| 0x81 | LOBBY | u8 admin, u8 maxCharacters, str8 username, u8 n, n × { u32 id, str8 name, str8 skin, i32 money, u8 online } |
| 0x82 | CHAR_RESULT | u8 op (2 create, 3 skin, 4 delete, 5 join), u8 status (0 ok, 1 invalid name, 2 name taken, 3 too many, 4 not found, 5 world full, 6 error, 7 invalid skin), u32 charId |
| 0x85 | WELCOME | u8 slot, u16 tag, f64 serverMs, u8 admin, u32 charId, str8 name, str8 skin, u16 n, n bytes state, WORLD body, u8 nPlayers, nPlayers × PLAYERINFO |
| 0x86 | LEFT | — |
| 0x87 | PONG | f64 clientMs, f64 serverMs |
| 0x8A | CHAT | u8 kind (0 player, 1 server notice), str8 name, str8 text (from = slot) |
| 0x8B | WORLD | f64 baseServerMs, f64 baseMinutes, f32 msPerMinute, u8 n, n × { u8 id, i32 value } |
| 0x8C | DENIED | u8 type (the request's), u8 reason (1 not admin, 2 rate limit, 3 invalid) |
| 0x8D | WORLD_EVENT | u8 id, i32 arg (from = the admin's slot) |
| 0x8E | RECORD | u16 key, u8 holder (255 none), u16 n, n bytes |
| 0x90 | OWNER | u32 netid, u8 owner (255: orphaned, delete it), u8 previous |
| 0x91 | PLAYER_JOIN | PLAYERINFO |
| 0x92 | PLAYER_AWAY | u8 slot, u8 away |
| 0x93 | PLAYER_LEAVE | u8 slot |
| 0x94 | PLAYER_INFO | u8 slot, str8 skin |
| 0x20–0x24 | relayed | as sent, with `from` = sender slot |

PLAYERINFO = u8 slot, u32 rank, u8 admin, u8 away, str8 name, str8 skin. After WELCOME the server sends every RECORD
of the world, then the chat history (CHAT records), then the current OWNER entries (if any). Game minutes are a
double: `minutes(serverNow) = baseMinutes + (serverNow - baseServerMs) / msPerMinute`; day = floor(minutes / 1440).

Page-made records (the shared link, section 6): PING every 15 s, AWAY(source 1) on visibility changes; and one
pseudo-record into the engine queue after a reconnection: `u16 len=2 | u8 0xFE | u8 255` (LINK_RESET).

### Engine-owned ranges (the server never reads them)

* ENTITY kinds (0x21): 1 ped, 2 automobile (cars, flyable helis, Dodo), 3 bike, 4 boat, 5 police heli (CHeli),
  6 plane, 7 object. Flags: bit 0 driven by its owner's player (locks it), bit 1 law entity (wanted player's police),
  bit 2 parked (from a car generator), bit 3 mission/script, bit 4 dead/wrecked.
* EVENT subs (0x23) and TARGETED subs (0x24), by module: 0x01–0x1F players, 0x20–0x3F combat, 0x40–0x5F entities,
  0x60–0x7F world, 0x80–0x9F social, 0xA0–0xBF session.
* World variables (WORLD n × {id, value}): 1 forced weather (-1 none), 2 world cheat bits (bit list in the world
  module), 3–15 reserved for the world module. Records: keys 0x0100 + hideout index (garages, 160 bytes).
* WORLD_EVENT ids: 1 BIGBANG (blow up cars: each client its own), others by the world module.

## 6. Page (`src/host/web/mmo-link.js` + `src/ports/re3/play.js`)

`createMmoLink({ url, log, onState }) → link` (generic, no game knowledge; node-testable):
* `link.open()` connect (idempotent); automatic reconnection with backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 15 s…) after an unexpected
  close, then the LINK_RESET pseudo-record is queued for the engine. A REFUSED record stops reconnection
  (`state 3`, `refusal` = reason) until `open()` again.
* `link.state()` 0 closed, 1 connecting, 2 open, 3 refused, 4 waiting to reconnect; `link.refusal()`.
* `link.send(bytes /*Uint8Array, one or more client records*/, unreliable)` → bool; unreliable data is dropped when
  `bufferedAmount` > 256 KB; reliable data is sent (or queued while connecting, ≤ 1 MB).
* `link.drain(heapU8, ptr, cap)` → bytes written: queued server messages, each as `u32 length | message bytes`
  (whole messages only; a message bigger than cap is dropped); 0 when empty; -1 once after an overflow (queue > 8 MB
  was emptied: the engine resynchronises).
* `link.away(bool)` (page source); `link.close()`; heartbeat PING every 15 s while open.
* play.js: when the version has `mmo`, `engine.orthrosNet = { ...link, user: () => username or '', signIn: () =>
  shell.showLoaderSignIn-like sign-in prompt, testing: URL has `mmotest`, testCommands: [], debug(json) }`, the url
  `/api/mmo/<versionId>/ws` (ws/wss from location). Visibility → `link.away(document.hidden)`; pagehide → close.
  `window.orthrosMmo` = { link, state: last engine debug object, command(str) } for the test harness.

EM_JS functions (engine, `src/extras/mmo/mmo_wire.cpp`), all non-blocking:
`OrthrosNetAvailable()` (Module.orthrosNet exists), `OrthrosNetOpen()`, `OrthrosNetClose()`, `OrthrosNetState()`,
`OrthrosNetRefusal()`, `OrthrosNetSend(ptr, len, unreliable)`, `OrthrosNetDrain(ptr, cap)`, `OrthrosNetUser(ptr, cap)`,
`OrthrosNetSignIn()`, `OrthrosNetTesting()`, `OrthrosNetTestCommand(ptr, cap)` (next command string or 0),
`OrthrosNetDebug(jsonPtr)`. Pointers are converted with `>>> 0`; bodies keep explicit semicolons (EM_JS is
stringified on one line); `EM_JS_DEPS(orthros_mmo, "$UTF8ToString,$stringToUTF8")`.

## 7. Engine (`src/extras/mmo/`, compiled only with ORTHROS_EXTRAS)

Files and owners (one agent each during the build-up; headers `mmo.h` = hooks called by the game's code,
`mmo_internal.h` = between modules; `mmo_weak.cpp` = weak defaults of every function so each module builds alone):

| file | module | content |
|---|---|---|

### Frame order (one main-loop iteration)

1. `OrthrosFrameYield` (sdl2.cpp) — page events, WebSocket messages queue up.
2. `OrthrosMmo::Pump()` — drain the page queue, dispatch every record (handlers may create/delete puppets: this is
   outside CWorld::Process; when the world is not ready they only store), send nothing yet.
3. `inputEventHandler` — keys (`KeyDown`, `TextInput`) and mouse.
4. In game: `CGame::Process`: `BeginProcess()` after `CPad::UpdatePads` (chat key, lists); `CClock::Update` →
   `ClockUpdate()`; …; `PreWorld()` before `CWorld::Process` (puppet creation from pending models, conversions);
   `CWorld::Process` (puppets' ProcessControl = interpolation); `PostWorld()` after it (capture local player + owned
   entities); …; `EndProcess()` at the end (flush the frame's records in one `OrthrosNetSend`).
   In the frontend: `FrontendFrame()` after `FrontEndMenuManager.Process`, then flush.
5. Rendering: `Render2d()` (name tags, before the HUD), `RenderOverlay()` (chat, lists, notices over everything).

Timing rule: interpolation and send rates use wall-clock `emscripten_get_now()` (never CTimer, which pauses, clamps
and scales). Puppet transforms are applied every frame from the buffered states.

### Ownership and population (entities)

* Every non-player ped and every vehicle in the pools is either *owned* (simulated here, has a netid with our tag) or
  a *puppet* (a copy of another client's entity: kinematic, no AI, no physics integration, `CanBeDeleted()` false,
  `bIsLocked`/UNK_CHAR so the game's removers leave it alone).
* Generation (`MayGenerateAt(pos, kind)`, called by every ambient spawner: peds, traffic, boats, parked cars, car
  parks, emergency vehicles): allowed iff no present, not-away remote player in the same area within 300 m of `pos`
  is strictly closer to `pos` than the local player (ties: the more senior rank wins). Law spawns for the local
  wanted player always pass (they belong to the wanted player).
* Migration instead of removal: where the game would delete an owned ambient entity for distance, if a remote player
  is within that entity's removal radius (peds 51 m, vehicles 120 m ×1.5) → OWN give to the nearest such player; the
  local copy becomes a puppet (deleted later when out of our view). Never for law entities or mission entities.
* Puppets beyond 300 m (or in another area) are deleted locally; they come back with the next state.
* OWNER received: owner = us → convert the puppet to a real entity (peds wander, cars `JoinCarWithRoadSystem` +
  cruise); owner = other → our real copy becomes a puppet; 255 → delete.
* Entering a remote-owned empty car (or one with an ambient driver): claim it (and its occupants) optimistically
  before the enter animation; a car driven by a remote player cannot be entered (later: jack request).
* Vehicles driven by the local player are owned by us with flag bit 0.
* Puppets count in the game's ped/car counters (density stays the game's where players overlap).

### Combat authority

* A hit on a puppet (bullet, shotgun pellet, melee, sniper bullet, car impact by our own driven car) is detected by
  the shooter's client, which sends TARGETED damage to the victim's owner with the raw damage, method, piece, direction
  and the attacker netid; nothing is applied to the puppet locally except effects (blood, sparks). The owner calls the
  game's own `InflictDamage` with the attacker's puppet as culprit (armour, the player's ×0.33, death, credit).
* Explosions, projectiles, flames and fires are EVENTs replayed on every client; each client damages only what it
  owns (and its own player); puppets are skipped. A remote shot only draws (trace, muzzle flash, sound).
* The local player's death: EVENT with killer netid (from the last network damage) and weapon; every client prints
  the kill line; the puppet plays its death and is revived at the respawn state.

### Session flow

Main menu → Multiplayer → (page: not signed in → message + "Sign in" opens the page's sign-in) → lobby (LOBBY) →
choose / create a character → JOIN → WELCOME → the base world (`orthros\freemode.b`, as the free mode's new game, but
without the free mode's save rules) loads → `GameLoaded` → world preparation, character, world state, records →
`IsActive()` true → playing. Pause menu: no Save; "Leave multiplayer" → CHAR_SAVE, LEAVE → back to the main menu.
Tab closed: the last CHAR_SAVE (every 10 s and at every money/weapon change) is the character's state.

### Test hooks

With `?mmotest` on the page URL (`OrthrosNetTesting()`), the engine reads one command per frame from
`orthrosNet.testCommands` and publishes a debug JSON every 500 ms (`window.orthrosMmo.state`): `{ mode, link, slot,
admin, inWorld, pos, area, health, maxHealth, infiniteSprint, stamina, money, wanted, weapon, vehicle, players: [{slot, name, pos, dist, area, away,
visible, stars}], owned: {peds, vehicles}, puppets: {peds, vehicles}, lobby: {characters}, chat: [last lines],
fps }`. Commands: `join <name> [skin]` (create if missing, then join; from the main menu), `leave`,
`tp <x> <y> <z>`, `weapon <id> <ammo>`, `fire` (one shot), `aim <slot>` (turn to a remote player), `car <model>`,
`say <text>`, `cheat <code>`, `teleport <index>`, `die`, `money <n>`, `key <rsKey>`, `menu` (open the pause menu).

`docs/null-page.md`:

```md
# The null page: guest accesses near address 0 fault as on Windows

`src/cpu/nullpage.js` (the rule), `src/cpu/interp.js` (`checkNull`, `strAddr`), `src/cpu/jit/translate.js`
(`planNullChecks`, `Emitter.nullCheck`, `NC_STORE_SMC` / `NC_RMW_SMC`), `src/cpu/jit/jit.js` (`run`: the null store exit).

## Semantics

Windows never maps the first 64 KiB of a process (nor the last 64 KiB below 2 GiB, nor the kernel's half above): a read
or a write there raises `EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION` at the instruction, nothing of it done, with
`ExceptionInformation = [0 read / 1 write, address]`, which the program's SEH may handle (crash handlers, `__try`
probes). Orthros' guest memory is one flat WebAssembly memory where those bytes exist: before this change a field of a
null pointer read zeros and a store through one was accepted — a corrupted structure then failed much later, far from
its cause (BFME1's allocator, docs/thread-scheduling.md).

Both executors apply the same rule (`nullChecks`), before the instruction:

- every explicit memory operand that is accessed (LEA, the hint NOPs, PREFETCH: none; INS/OUTS fault with #GP first),
  sources before the destination (MOVS reads first: a null source is reported as a read);
- not the operands addressed by ESP alone (the stack: PUSH/POP/CALL/RET are implicit anyway) nor FS/GS-relative ones
  (the TEB);
- a string instruction with a REP prefix and a zero count accesses nothing; the interpreter checks every element (a
  REP STOS walking down into the null page faults at that element, ECX / EDI as they are then);
- the bit-string forms of BTS/BTR/BTC (memory, register offset) and XLAT compute their own address: their handlers check
  it;
- the faulting range is `[0, 0x10000)` and `[0x7fff0000, 4 GiB)` (`unmapped`): `[ecx-4]` with ECX null faults at
  0xfffffffc instead of trapping in WebAssembly.

The exception record is exact (code, address, read/write, EIP at the instruction). Two documented inexactnesses, both
in the JIT and only for the CONTEXT: the arithmetic flags of a read-modify-write caught after its store (below) are the
instruction's own, and dead flags (never read before being written again) may be an older instruction's — as for every
fault in translated code.

## What faults: writes by default, reads on request

`nullPageMode()`: `'writes'` (the default), `true` (reads too, `?dbg=ORTHROS_NULL_READS=1`, the Vm option `nullPage`),
`false` (the old behaviour, `?dbg=ORTHROS_NULL_PAGE_OPEN=1`). With `'writes'`, a read of the null page still returns
zeros (the pages stay zero: nothing can store there) and a read past 2 GiB still traps.

Why: writes are what corrupt; they are checked at no cost on the JIT's hot path (below). Checking every read costs a
compare and a branch per load that is not proven safe. Measured in Node (`tools/startbench.mjs` with the menu-to-skirmish
scenarios, from the warm profiles, `perf stat -e instructions:u` of the whole process — the compilers' threads included
—, the variants run side by side in pairs):

| variant (RotWK, first 45 G guest instructions) | host instructions | perf record |
|---|---|---|
| no checks | 802 / 820 / 834 / 821 G | JIT code 54.1 %, compiler threads 26.5 % |
| reads and writes, a check per access group | 904 / 948 / 946 G (+13 %) | JIT code +7.6 %, compilation +28 % |

| variant (final code) | RotWK, 60 G instructions | BFME1, 50 G instructions | |
|---|---|---|---|
| no checks | 1008 / 1030 G | 717.0 / 715.7 G | |
| writes only (the default) | 1019 / 1053 G (+1.1 / +2.3 %) | 727.1 / 726.9 G (+1.4 / +1.6 %) | translation time +5 % |

Split by `perf record -e instructions:u` (RotWK, 60 G, one pair): the translated code itself +0.6 % (322.8 K against
320.8 K samples of 2 M instructions), the compiler threads +3.1 %, the JavaScript thread +2.9 %, the whole +1.3 %.
Guest time per instruction in RotWK's play (the frame accounting's `guest` per instruction, 30 s phases) is the same
within the spread: 3.57 / 3.66 / 3.51 ns with the checks, 3.57 / 3.66 / 3.74 without; in-session A/B (`dbg:ORTHROS_JIT_AB=
{"nullPage":false}`, tools/scenarios/*-nullpage-ab.txt, three alternations, both orders) gave +1 to +6 % per session
for the checks, but variants with half of the added code removed gave the same +2 % and −3 to −4 % — the phases of one
session differ by ±5 %, more than what is measured. BFME1 in Node (`tools/scenarios/bfme-phases.txt` to a skirmish, four runs side by side, `ORTHROS_NULL_PAGE_OPEN=1` for
the open page; 2026-10-04 evening, main merged): play (160 s, 6 140 frames) 3.153 / 3.163 ns per guest instruction with
the checks, 3.131 / 3.174 without; the loading screen (40 G instructions) 1.529 / 1.447 against 1.437 / 1.445. What is left of the cost in 'writes' mode is
compilation (the explicit checks of string stores, two stores in the SMC cold path of every plain store); the
translated code runs as fast. The cost of reads is mostly the code they add, not the compare: every check is a cold exit
(the region's state written back), and TurboFan compiles the larger functions more slowly.

## How the JIT checks

- **Plain stores** (`NC_STORE_SMC`: MOV, SETcc, the SSE/MMX moves, the x87 stores, STMXCSR, FNSTCW, FNSTSW) and, in
  `'writes'` mode, **read-modify-writes** (`NC_RMW_SMC`: ALU, shifts, BTS/BTR/BTC) need no check before them: their
  self-modifying-code check after the store already reads the page's byte in the SMC map, where the unmapped pages
  carry `SMC_NULL`. A store there takes the existing SMC exit, with the instruction's start in `ST.EXIT_PC`; `Jit.run`
  clears the bytes written (and undoes the pop of FSTP / FISTP / FISTTP: the register is still in its slot) and lets the
  interpreter execute the instruction again, which raises the fault. Zero instructions on the hot path, two stores in
  an existing cold path.
- **Other writes** (POP to memory, string stores, XCHG/XADD/CMPXCHG, FXSAVE, FNSAVE...) are checked before the
  instruction: one range test
  (`(addr - 0x10000) >=u 0x7ffe0000 - span`), shared by every access through the same base and index registers
  (unchanged) within 64 KiB of each other in a block (`planNullChecks`); when it fails the region is left before the
  instruction (`stepExit`) and the interpreter executes it, faulting or not.
- With reads checked, an if-converted arm's load in the null page sets `L_SPECF` (the load itself reads address 0); after
  the arms the region restores the state before them and leaves before the JCC, whose arm then runs as a block of its
  own; a float compare is not fused with a following SETcc/CMOVcc that may leave before itself.

Not exact, as before these checks: a plain store or read-modify-write to an address past 2 GiB (`[null - 4]`, a register
holding garbage) traps in WebAssembly before its check (an imprecise fault: the process ends); a plain store straddling
0x10000 from below keeps its bytes from 0x10000 on.

## Tests

`tests/null-page.test.js`: 45 instruction forms in both modes, each against the interpreter (EIP, address, read/write,
registers, memory, the null page left zero), sliced and not, with if-conversion everywhere; 300 random programs per mode
(null, small and valid pointers through loads, stores, read-modify-writes, string instructions, null tests and their
mirrors in if-converted arms, loops) in time slices of 1 to 10^6 instructions; mutations of the JIT (no check, no arm
flag) make them fail. `tools/pe/seh.c`: the SEH record of null-page reads and writes, a call through a null vtable, REP
MOVSD from null, `[null - 4]`, 300 times (the JIT's translations included), in both executors.
