```js
/** The adaptive waits are on (ORTHROS_ADAPTIVE_SLEEP not 0). */
export function adaptiveOn() { const v = globalThis.ORTHROS_ADAPTIVE_SLEEP; return v === undefined || v === '' || Number(v) !== 0; }
/**
 * How long a host wait asked for `ms` at `t0` lasts with the injected quantum `q` (ms; `ms` itself without one): whole
 * milliseconds (Chrome rounds a wait's timeout up), then the first multiple of `q` at or after that end.
 */
export function quantised(t0, ms, q = injectedQuantum()) {
  if (!(q > 0) || !(ms > 0)) return ms;
  const end = Math.ceil((t0 + Math.ceil(ms - 1e-9)) / q - 1e-9) * q;
  return Math.max(ms, end - t0);
}

/** A moving estimate of a wake-up source's overshoot: the second largest of the last RING samples. */
export class OvershootEstimate {
  constructor() { this.ring = new Float64Array(RING); this.n = 0; this.value = 0; }
  /** a measured overshoot (ms) */
  add(over) {
    this.ring[this.n++ % RING] = Math.max(0, over);
    let a = 0, b = 0; const k = Math.min(this.n, RING);
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) { const v = this.ring[i]; if (v > a) { b = a; a = v; } else if (v > b) b = v; }
    this.value = k >= 2 ? b : a;
  }
}

/** Per-source wait statistics (telemetry: the bench phases, the summaries). */
function newStats() { return { waits: 0, overMs: 0, overMax: 0, hist: new Array(OVER_BOUNDS.length + 1).fill(0), spins: 0, spinMs: 0, early: 0, plain: 0, lateMs: 0, q: 0, modes: 0 }; }

export class HostWaiter {
  /**
   * @param {() => number} [now] the host clock (ms)
   * @param {(arr: Int32Array, idx: number, value: number, ms: number) => string} [rawWait] the host wait (Atomics.wait)
   */
  constructor(now = () => performance.now(), rawWait = (arr, idx, value, ms) => Atomics.wait(arr, idx, value, ms)) {
    this.now = now; this.rawWait = rawWait;
    this.est = new OvershootEstimate(); // (Atomics.wait)
    this.timerEst = new OvershootEstimate(); // (the worker's setTimeout, measured at the pump)
    this.stats = newStats(); this.timer = newStats();
    this.tot = { waits: 0, overMs: 0, lateMs: 0, spins: 0, spinMs: 0, timers: 0, timerOverMs: 0 }; // (cumulative: the stats messages, summaries take differences)
    this.paceEnd = 0; // (host time: the predicted end of the guest's current pacing loop, 0 none — kernel32 sets it)
    this.lastLate = 0; // (the last wait's lateness that can lengthen a frame, ms: the frame accounting's `late`)
    this.ownSab = null;
  }
  /** One host wait of `ms` (the injected quantum applied): Atomics.wait's result. */
  hostWait(arr, idx, value, ms) {
    if (!(ms > 0)) return 'timed-out';
    return this.rawWait(arr, idx, value, quantised(this.now(), ms));
  }
  /** The guest's pacing loop is predicted to end at host time `t` (0: no prediction). */
  pace(t) { this.paceEnd = t > 0 ? t : 0; }
  /** A wait ending at `deadline` is one of a pacing loop's last ones (its overshoot would lengthen the frame). */
  lastPacingWait(deadline) { const e = this.paceEnd; return e > 0 && deadline > e - this.est.value - 0.5 && deadline <= e + PACE_SLACK_MS; }
  /**
   * A wait ending at `deadline` is one of a pacing loop's earlier waits: waking late only shortens the polling, the
   * frame is not longer (its lateness is not `late` for the frame accounting).
   */
  earlyPacingWait(deadline) { const e = this.paceEnd; return e > 0 && deadline <= e - this.est.value - 0.5; }
  /**
   * Block until the host time `deadline` (ms), or until arr[idx] is notified / no longer `value` (Atomics.wait's
   * result: 'ok' or 'not-equal' woken early, 'timed-out'). `precise` false: a wait without a deadline that matters
   * (a plain host wait, not counted as late).
   */
  waitUntil(arr, idx, value, deadline, precise = true) {
    let r = 'timed-out', t = this.now();
    if (deadline <= t) return r;
    const st = this.stats, adaptive = adaptiveOn();
    st.waits++; st.q = injectedQuantum(); st.modes |= adaptive ? 1 : 2; this.lastLate = 0;
    if (!precise || !adaptive) {
      st.plain++;
      r = this.hostWait(arr, idx, value, deadline - t);
      t = this.now();
      if (r === 'timed-out') { this.est.add(t - deadline); if (precise) this.noteEnd(st, t - deadline, deadline); }
      return r;
    }
    for (;;) {
      const left = deadline - t;
      if (left <= 0) break;
      const est = this.est.value;
      if (est > TOLERATE_MS && left > est) { // woken earlier by the estimate, the rest waited again
        st.early++;
        const t0 = t, ask = left - est; r = this.hostWait(arr, idx, value, ask);
        t = this.now();
        if (r !== 'timed-out') break; // (notified — input, a completion — or the word changed: the caller looks again)
        this.est.add(t - (t0 + ask));
        continue;
      }
      if (est > TOLERATE_MS && left <= SPIN_MAX_MS && this.lastPacingWait(deadline)) { // the frame limiter's last wait: spun
        const s0 = t;
        while ((t = this.now()) < deadline) { if (Atomics.load(arr, idx) !== value) { r = 'not-equal'; break; } }
        st.spins++; st.spinMs += t - s0; this.tot.spins++; this.tot.spinMs += t - s0;
        break;
      }
      // a precise host, or a wait whose overshoot does not lengthen a frame: one host wait (its overshoot accepted)
      st.plain++;
      r = this.hostWait(arr, idx, value, left);
      t = this.now(); if (r === 'timed-out') this.est.add(t - deadline);
      break;
    }
    if (r === 'timed-out') this.noteEnd(st, t - deadline, deadline);
    return r;
  }
  /** A wait (or a timer: st === this.timer) ended `over` ms past its deadline (`deadline`: a wait's, for lastLate). */
  noteEnd(st, over, deadline) {
    if (over < 0) over = 0;
    st.overMs += over; if (over > st.overMax) st.overMax = over;
    let b = 0; while (b < OVER_BOUNDS.length && over > OVER_BOUNDS[b]) b++;
    st.hist[b]++;
    if (st === this.timer) { this.tot.timers++; this.tot.timerOverMs += over; return; }
    this.tot.waits++; this.tot.overMs += over;
    this.lastLate = deadline !== undefined && this.earlyPacingWait(deadline) ? 0 : over;
    st.lateMs += this.lastLate; this.tot.lateMs += this.lastLate;
  }
  /** The cumulative counters (the worker's stats messages: perf-summary.js takes their differences), rounded. */
  totals() { const t = this.tot, r = (x) => Math.round(x * 100) / 100; return { waits: t.waits, overMs: r(t.overMs), lateMs: r(t.lateMs), spins: t.spins, spinMs: r(t.spinMs), timers: t.timers, timerOverMs: r(t.timerOverMs), est: r(this.est.value), timerEst: r(this.timerEst.value) }; }
  /** Sleep `ms` on a private word (tests, tools). */
  sleep(ms) {
    if (!(ms > 0)) return;
    const arr = this.ownSab ??= new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4));
    this.waitUntil(arr, 0, 0, this.now() + ms);
  }

  /**
   * The timer to arm for a wake-up `ms` from now (the worker's schedulePump): `ask` the time it is armed for — earlier by
   * the timers' measured overshoot when that would make it late (the rest is waited by the pump: Vm.runFor waits up to
   * 2 ms in waitUntil) — and `delay` the setTimeout delay (the injected quantum applied).
   */
  timerArm(ms, now = this.now()) {
    if (!(ms > 0)) return { ask: 0, delay: 0 };
    let ask = ms;
    const est = this.timerEst.value;
    if (adaptiveOn() && est > TOLERATE_MS && ms > est) { ask = ms - est; this.timer.early++; }
    return { ask, delay: quantised(now, ask) };
  }
  /** A timer fired: `over` ms past the time it was armed for, `late` ms past the wake-up wanted. */
  noteTimer(over, late) { this.timerEst.add(over); this.timer.waits++; this.noteEnd(this.timer, late); }

  /** The statistics since the last call (then reset), compact: per source waits, mean / max overshoot, histogram, spins. */
  take() {
    const f = (s) => (s.waits ? { waits: s.waits, overMean: Math.round(s.overMs / s.waits * 1000) / 1000, overMax: Math.round(s.overMax * 100) / 100, lateMs: Math.round(s.lateMs * 10) / 10, hist: s.hist.slice(), spins: s.spins, spinMs: Math.round(s.spinMs * 10) / 10, early: s.early, plain: s.plain } : null);
    // (the switches as the window's waits saw them: `adaptive` 'mixed' when they changed within it)
    const m = this.stats.modes, r = { wait: f(this.stats), timer: f(this.timer), est: Math.round(this.est.value * 1000) / 1000, timerEst: Math.round(this.timerEst.value * 1000) / 1000, q: this.stats.waits ? this.stats.q : injectedQuantum(), adaptive: m === 2 ? false : m === 3 ? 'mixed' : m === 1 ? true : adaptiveOn() };
    this.stats = newStats(); this.timer = newStats();
    return r;
  }
}

/**
 * A pacing loop of a guest thread ended at guest time `t` (kernel32: the polling streak broken by other work). `st`:
 * the thread's sleep statistics (machine state: plain numbers in thread.sleepStats).
 */
export function paceEnded(st, t) {
  const e = st.paceEnds ??= [];
  if (e.length && t - e[e.length - 1] > 1000) e.length = 0; // (a pause: the period starts again)
  e.push(t); if (e.length > PACE_RING) e.shift();
}
/**
 * The predicted end (guest time) of the thread's current pacing loop, or -1: the last end plus the loops' period (the
 * second shortest of the last intervals — at least 3 of them). -1 as well once `now` is PACE_SLACK_MS past it.
 */
export function pacePredict(st, now) {
  const e = st.paceEnds;
  if (!e || e.length < 4) return -1;
  let a = Infinity, b = Infinity;
  for (let i = 1; i < e.length; i++) { const d = e[i] - e[i - 1]; if (d < a) { b = a; a = d; } else if (d < b) b = d; }
  const end = e[e.length - 1] + b;
  return now > end + PACE_SLACK_MS ? -1 : end;
}

// snapshot: host-side (the browser's timer behaviour, measured: not machine state)
export const hostWaiter = new HostWaiter();

```

`src/core/procs.js`:

```js
// Child processes (docs/processes.md): a program started with CreateProcess runs in a Vm of its own — its own guest
// memory (a WebAssembly.Memory), JIT, scheduler and DLL state — on the same worker as its parent, interleaved with it
// by the root Vm's runFor. What Windows shares between processes is shared here: the kernel-object namespace (named
// mutexes, events, semaphores, file mappings), the objects inherited or opened by name, process and thread ids, the
// registry, the files, the clock and the host (display, input, audio), which belongs to one process at a time (the
// foreground one: the last to create a Direct3D device). A machine that never starts a child has no group: its path is
// unchanged.
import { TS } from '../win32/process.js';
import { HANDLE_BLOCK } from '../win32/handles.js';
import { acquireMapping, dropViews } from '../win32/mappings.js';

/** time a member's runFor gets per turn when several are busy (ms) */
const TURN_MS = 4;
/** fields the host sets on the root Vm after its construction that a child gets too */
const CHILD_INHERITS = ['registry', 'asyncReads', 'onStdout', 'readSliceMs', 'waitLogMin', 'deadline'];

/**
 * processes running at once at most (a launcher restarting its game, a game relaunching itself: each a machine with a
 * guest memory of its own — 2 GB of address space reserved; an exited one is released, see reap)
 */
export const MAX_LIVE_PROCESSES = 8;

const RUNNING = Object.freeze({ state: 'running' }), IDLE = Object.freeze({ state: 'idle' });

export class ProcessGroup {
  /** @param {import('./vm.js').Vm} root the machine the host created (its first process) */
  constructor(root) {
    this.root = root;
    /**
     * @type {import('./vm.js').Vm[]} every process's machine, the root first. An exited one leaves at the next turn
     * (reap): its memory, JIT and window state released; the handles other processes hold on it name a record of its end.
     */
    this.vms = [root];
    /** the machine the host's display, input and audio belong to */
    this.foreground = root;
    /** named kernel objects, every process's (kernel32.js createNamed): the root's map, shared */
    this.named = root.kernelNamed ?? new Map();
    /** file mappings with views in more than one process (kernel32-file.js): their bytes kept alike at each switch */
    this.mappings = new Set();
    /** the machine running now (between switches: the last one) */
    this.current = root;
    this.idleSince = -1;
    this.spawned = 0;
    /** called when the foreground process changes (the worker re-points its per-process hooks): (vm) => void */
    this.onForeground = null;
    /** exited members not reaped yet (reap: at the group's next turn, when none of them is inside its own run) */
    this.ended = [];
    /** bytes compared or copied to keep the shared mappings alike (diagnostics) */
    this.syncBytes = 0;
    // handle values: every process allocates from blocks of its own (HandleTable.alloc) — the root keeps the block it is
    // in, the others are taken above it
    this.handleTop = 0;
    if (root.proc) this.ownHandles(root.proc.handles, true);
  }

  /** A block of handle values no process of the group has used: its first value. */
  takeHandles() { const b = this.handleTop; this.handleTop += HANDLE_BLOCK; return b; }

  /** `table` allocates from the group's blocks (`keep`: the values it has handed out so far stay its own; else a new block). */
  ownHandles(table, keep = false) {
    table.pool = this;
    if (keep) { table.limit = Math.ceil((table.next + 4) / HANDLE_BLOCK) * HANDLE_BLOCK; this.handleTop = Math.max(this.handleTop, table.limit); return; }
    table.next = this.takeHandles(); table.limit = table.next + HANDLE_BLOCK;
  }

  /** the members still running */
  live() { return this.vms.filter((v) => !v.proc?.exited); }

  /**
   * A new machine for a child process of `parent` (its process not created yet): built like the root — same files,
   * clock, host, options — sharing the group's namespace, with process and thread ids, handle values and window handles
   * of its own range.
   */
  spawn(parent) {
    if (this.live().length >= MAX_LIVE_PROCESSES) throw Object.assign(new Error(`${MAX_LIVE_PROCESSES} processes running already`), { processLimit: true });
    const VmClass = /** @type {any} */ (this.root.constructor);
    const n = ++this.spawned;
    const child = new VmClass({ ...this.root.ctorOpts, group: this });
    for (const k of CHILD_INHERITS) if (parent[k] !== undefined) child[k] = parent[k];
    if (parent.mainWaits) child.mainWaits = new Map();
    child.nextPid = this.root.nextPid + 0x100 * n; // (pids and tids: unique across the processes)
    child.tidBase = 0x800 + 0x10000 * n;
    child.parentVm = parent;
    this.vms.push(child);
    return child;
  }

  /** Wake the waiters of every process whose object a thread of `from` released or signaled (Scheduler.signal). */
  signal() { for (const v of this.vms) if (v.proc && !v.proc.exited) v.sched.signal(); }

  /** The thread of id `tid` in any process. */
  thread(tid) { for (const v of this.vms) { const t = v.proc?.thread(tid); if (t) return t; } return null; }

  /** The machine whose process has id `pid`. */
  byPid(pid) { return this.vms.find((v) => v.proc?.pid === pid) ?? null; }

  /** `vm` takes the display, the input and the audio (it created a Direct3D device, or showed the first window). */
  setForeground(vm) {
    if (this.foreground === vm || vm.proc?.exited) return;
    const prev = this.foreground;
    this.foreground = vm;
    this.root.log('loader', `process ${vm.proc?.pid} (${vm.proc?.exe?.name ?? '?'}) takes the display and the input from process ${prev?.proc?.pid}`);
    // (the page shows its windows, display mode, title and cursor from now on)
    if (vm.wm && vm.wm.proc === vm.proc) { vm.wm.resumeHost(); vm.wm.present(true); }
    this.onForeground?.(vm, prev);
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- shared mappings
  /**
   * `vm` is about to run guest code: the shared mappings' bytes another process wrote brought into its views
   * (win32/mappings.js — only what changed, nothing for a mapping it holds already). A process that only waits is never
   * brought up to date: it does not run guest code (Vm.runOwn calls this before a slice).
   */
  enter(vm) {
    this.current = vm;
    for (const m of this.mappings) this.syncBytes += acquireMapping(vm, m);
  }
  /** a mapping's views changed: shared (synced at switches) while they are in more than one process */
  noteViews(m) {
    const vms = new Set(m.views.map((v) => v.vm));
    if (vms.size > 1) { this.mappings.add(m); return; }
    // (views left in one process only: brought up to date now — no switch keeps them so from here)
    if (this.mappings.delete(m) && vms.size === 1) this.syncBytes += acquireMapping([...vms][0], m);
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- running
  /**
   * The root Vm's runFor when the machine has several processes: every live member runs in turns of TURN_MS (or until
   * `untilMs`), its shared mappings synced around its turn; the members' own idle waits are handed back here (none
   * sleeps while another has work), and the group sleeps, or hands the wait to a cooperative host, when all wait.
   */
  runFor(untilMs) {
    const root = this.root;
    for (;;) {
      let running = false, wake = Infinity, wakeAt = Infinity, ran = 0;
      for (const v of this.vms) {
        if (!v.proc || v.proc.exited) continue;
        const now = performance.now();
        const r = this.turn(v, untilMs === Infinity ? now + TURN_MS : Math.min(untilMs, now + TURN_MS));
        ran++;
        if (r.state === 'exited') { this.exited(v, r.code); continue; }
        if (r.state === 'running') running = true;
        else if (r.state === 'sleep') { wake = Math.min(wake, r.until); wakeAt = Math.min(wakeAt, r.at ?? Infinity); }
      }
      if (this.ended.length) this.reap();
      if (!ran || this.vms.every((v) => !v.proc || v.proc.exited)) return { state: 'exited', code: this.finish() };
      const now = performance.now();
      if (running) { this.idleSince = -1; if (untilMs !== Infinity && now >= untilMs) return RUNNING; continue; }
      // every process waits
      if (untilMs !== Infinity && root.host?.cooperative) return wake === Infinity ? IDLE : { state: 'sleep', until: wake };
      if (untilMs !== Infinity && now >= untilMs) return RUNNING;
      // (slept on the guest's clock — a virtual one advances by it — at most 50 ms at a time)
      const clock = root.clock, ms = Math.min(50, wakeAt === Infinity ? 50 : Math.max(0.5, wakeAt - clock.now())); // (never 0: a wait due now is checked again after a moment)
      if (wake === Infinity) {
        if (this.idleSince < 0) this.idleSince = root.clock.now();
        else if (root.clock.now() - this.idleSince > root.sched.deadlockLimit) {
          const v = this.live()[0], t = v.proc.threads.find((x) => x.state === TS.BLOCKED) ?? v.proc.threads[0];
          v.deadlock(t, `every process waits (${t?.blockReason ?? 'idle'})`);
        }
      } else this.idleSince = -1;
      if (root.host?.waitEvent) root.host.waitEvent(ms); else clock.sleep(ms);
    }
  }

  /** One member's turn: its slices (its shared mappings brought up to date before it runs guest code: enter). */
  turn(v, until) {
    this.current = v;
    return v.runOwn(until, true);
  }

  /**
   * Run the other processes for a moment from a wait of `vm` nested in a JavaScript frame (sched.js nestedWait: a
   * window procedure, a DllMain waits for another process): true when one of them ran.
   */
  runOthers(vm, ms = TURN_MS) {
    let any = false;
    const until = performance.now() + ms;
    for (const v of this.vms) {
      if (v === vm || !v.proc || v.proc.exited || v.depth > 0) continue; // (a machine already inside its own run: not re-entered)
      const r = this.turn(v, until);
      if (r.state === 'exited') this.exited(v, r.code);
      else if (r.state === 'running') any = true;
    }
    this.enter(vm); // (it goes on with its guest code: what the others wrote meanwhile)
    return any;
  }

  /** `v`'s process ended: its waiters woken, its handles closed, the display back to another process. */
  exited(v, code) {
    const proc = v.proc;
    if (v.groupExited) return; // (told twice: terminated by another process, then its own run ended)
    v.groupExited = true;
    proc.exited = true; proc.exitCode = code >>> 0;
    for (const t of proc.threads) if (t.state !== TS.DONE) t.state = TS.DONE;
    // (its objects: the named ones it holds released — a mutex it owned abandoned — the others with their last handle)
    for (const [h, o] of [...proc.handles.map]) {
      if (o?.type === 'mutex' && proc.threads.some((t) => t.id === o.owner)) { o.owner = 0; o.count = 0; o.abandoned = true; }
      if (o && o.type !== 'thread' && o.type !== 'process' && o.type !== 'heap') proc.handles.close(h);
    }
    // (its views of the paging file's mappings: their bytes kept in the mappings, as an unmap does)
    for (const m of new Set(v.mapViews?.values() ?? [])) { dropViews(v, m); this.noteViews(m); proc.handles.forgetName(m); }
    v.mapViews?.clear();
    this.root.log('loader', `process ${proc.pid} (${proc.exe?.name ?? '?'}) exited with code ${code >>> 0}`);
    if (this.foreground === v) { const next = (v.parentVm && !v.parentVm.proc?.exited ? v.parentVm : this.live()[0]); if (next) this.setForeground(next); }
    if (v !== this.root) this.ended.push(v);
    this.signal();
  }

  /**
   * The exited members leave the group, and nothing of the group keeps their machine: the handles other processes hold
   * on their process and threads name a record of its end (what a wait, GetExitCodeProcess/Thread, GetProcessId read),
   * the objects they created no longer point into their memory, their children's parent is theirs, and the host
   * forgets their memory (the render worker's copy of it, its devices). The machine — guest memory, JIT, windows,
   * Direct3D and sound state — is then garbage.
   */
  reap() {
    const gone = this.ended.splice(0);
    const recs = new Map();
    for (const v of gone) {
      const i = this.vms.indexOf(v); if (i > 0) this.vms.splice(i, 1);
      const p = v.proc, rec = new ExitedProcess(p);
      recs.set(p, rec);
      for (const t of p.threads) recs.set(t, new ExitedThread(t, rec));
    }
    const ownedBy = (o) => gone.find((v) => o?.states?.mem === v.mem);
    const fix = (o) => { if (o?.type === 'mutex' && ownedBy(o)) { o.close(); o.states = null; } }; // (its state out of the dead memory: Mutex.close)
    for (const v of this.vms) {
      const map = v.proc?.handles.map; if (!map) continue;
      for (const [h, o] of map) { const r = recs.get(o); if (r) map.set(h, r); else fix(o); }
      if (gone.includes(v.parentVm)) { let p = v.parentVm; while (p && gone.includes(p)) p = p.parentVm; v.parentVm = p ?? this.root; }
    }
    for (const o of this.named.values()) fix(o);
    if (gone.includes(this.current)) this.current = this.root;
    for (const v of gone) { this.root.host?.forgetProcess?.(v); v.parentVm = null; }
  }

  /** every process ended: the host told once, with the root's exit code */
  finish() {
    const code = this.root.proc.exitCode >>> 0;
    if (!this.finished) { this.finished = true; this.root.host?.onExit?.(code); }
    return code;
  }
}

/** What another process's handle on an exited process names once its machine is released (ProcessGroup.reap). */
export class ExitedProcess {
  constructor(p) {
    this.type = 'process'; this.pid = p.pid; this.exited = true; this.exitCode = p.exitCode; this.handle = p.handle;
    this.exe = p.exe ? { name: p.exe.name } : null; this.priorityClass = p.priorityClass;
  }
}

/** What a handle on a thread of an exited process names once its machine is released. */
export class ExitedThread {
  constructor(t, proc) {
    this.type = 'thread'; this.id = t.id; this.state = TS.DONE; this.exitCode = t.exitCode; this.handle = t.handle;
    this.proc = proc; this.priority = t.priority ?? 0; this.suspendCount = 0;
  }
  isRunnable() { return false; }
}

```

`src/core/sched.js`:

```js
// Green-thread scheduler (DECISIONS.md D003/D021). All guest threads run on this JS thread in
// time slices from the top-level run loop. A thread that blocks in an API handler at top level
// *unwinds*: the handler throws WaitUnwind, the API call is rolled back (EIP/ESP at the thunk),
// the thread is parked with its wake condition, and the run loop moves on. When the condition
// holds (or the timeout passes) the thread re-executes the call, whose `block()` then returns
// the recorded result. Blocking inside a nested callback (window procedure, DllMain...) cannot
// unwind through the host's JS frames: it runs other threads nested until the condition holds.
import { TS } from '../win32/process.js';

export const INFINITE = 0xffffffff;
/** how long a ready thread may wait while higher-priority threads run before it runs anyway (pickRunnable): guest
 *  instructions executed (STARVE_INSNS), or scheduling decisions (threads yielding with Sleep(0) execute few) */
export const STARVE_PICKS = 1000;
/**
 * Starvation and the quantum are counted in guest instructions executed (Vm.guestInsns), not in time: a quantum is
 * processor time used, and the host's own load (the emulator descheduled for milliseconds in the middle of a few guest
 * instructions) must not decide where a thread is interrupted. 6 M instructions: ~20 ms at this emulator's speed
 * (~300 M guest instructions per second).
 */
export const STARVE_INSNS = 6_000_000;
/**
 * The quantum (guest instructions, see STARVE_INSNS): how long a thread whose time slice ended keeps the processor while no thread of
 * higher priority is ready — Windows rotates threads of equal priority at the end of a quantum (two clock ticks, ~31 ms
 * on a client system), not at every slice of this scheduler (a few hundred microseconds), and a thread preempted by a
 * higher priority resumes before its equals (see pickRunnable). The starvation delay, which ends it for a thread kept
 * waiting by an equal as well. Off by default (rotation at every slice): on a multi-core Windows machine threads of
 * equal priority run side by side, which every-slice rotation approximates better, and the quantum showed no gain
 * (BFME1 failure rate 4/40 both ways) while delaying hand-offs between polling threads by up to a quantum;
 * ?dbg=ORTHROS_QUANTUM_INSNS=<n> turns it on (QUANTUM_INSNS: the Windows-like value).
 */
export const QUANTUM_INSNS = STARVE_INSNS; // (an equal ready that long is starved anyway: see pickRunnable)
export const WAIT_OBJECT_0 = 0, WAIT_ABANDONED = 0x80, WAIT_TIMEOUT = 0x102, WAIT_FAILED = 0xffffffff;

/**
 * Thrown by a blocking API handler at top level to park its thread (see block()). Not an Error
 * subclass on purpose: an Error captures a stack trace at construction, which costs more than the
 * whole park/resume path (1.5 % of the worker in a scene with thousands of waits per second).
 */
export class WaitUnwind {
  constructor(wait) { this.wait = wait; }
}
/**
 * Returned (not thrown) by a handler whose wait parks its thread (Scheduler.park): the dispatcher rolls the call back
 * as for WaitUnwind, the wait being in thread.parkWait. The hot waits (Sleep, WaitForSingleObject) return it: a
 * thrown WaitUnwind costs far more than a return, at thousands of parks per second.
 */
export const PARK = Object.freeze({ park: true });

export class Scheduler {
  /** @param {import('./vm.js').Vm} vm */
  constructor(vm) {
    this.vm = vm;
    this.rr = 0;
    this.deadlockLimit = 60000; // ms of virtual/real time with nothing runnable and no timers
    this.idleSince = -1;
    /** nested waits in progress (block() on top of a JavaScript frame): the event loop cannot run until they end */
    this.nestedWaits = 0;
    /** clock time of the last wakeBlocked() pass (see nextWake) */
    this.checkedAt = -Infinity;
    /** (measurement, ?dbg=ORTHROS_SCHED_ROUND_ROBIN=1: priorities ignored, every runnable thread in turn) */
    this.roundRobin = !!globalThis.ORTHROS_SCHED_ROUND_ROBIN;
    /** scheduling decisions so far (pickRunnable): starvation */
    this.picks = 0;
    /** (measurement, ?dbg=ORTHROS_STARVE_INSNS=<n>,ORTHROS_STARVE_PICKS=<n>: the starvation thresholds of pickRunnable) */
    this.starveInsns = Number(globalThis.ORTHROS_STARVE_INSNS) || STARVE_INSNS; this.starvePicks = Number(globalThis.ORTHROS_STARVE_PICKS) || STARVE_PICKS;
    /** the quantum (QUANTUM_INSNS; ?dbg=ORTHROS_QUANTUM_INSNS=<n>, 0 none), the thread holding it and where it ends (Vm.guestInsns) */
    this.quantumInsns = globalThis.ORTHROS_QUANTUM_INSNS !== undefined ? Number(globalThis.ORTHROS_QUANTUM_INSNS) : 0;
    this.quantumThread = null; this.quantumEnd = 0;
    /** a thread whose slice ended on its budget (Vm.sliceEnd), candidate to go on with its quantum (pickRunnable) */
    this.sliceExpired = null;
    /** { t, left }: a thread preempted by a higher priority with `left` ms of quantum: first among its equals afterwards */
    this.preempted = null;
    /** the thread whose yield (Sleep(0), SwitchToThread) ended its slice, for the next top-level pick; `yieldAny`: SwitchToThread */
    this.yielder = null; this.yieldAny = false;
  }

  /** `t` ready to run (again): the time and decision count it starts waiting from (starvation, see pickRunnable) */
  markReady(t) { t.state = TS.READY; t.readyTime = this.vm.guestInsns ?? 0; t.readyPick = this.picks; }

  get threads() { return this.vm.proc.threads; }

  /**
   * Next runnable thread other than `except`: the highest priority first (SetThreadPriority), round robin among equals —
   * as Windows schedules. A thread raised above the others (an audio mixer at THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL) that its
   * time slice interrupted resumes before them: it is not left paused in the middle of its work while normal threads run
   * for whole slices (a window of thousands of their instructions where Windows has the high-priority work done at once).
   * A thread ready for STARVE_INSNS (or STARVE_PICKS scheduling decisions) runs whatever its priority (Windows boosts
   * starved threads likewise).
   * The top-level pick after a yield (`yielder`, set by yieldFrom) gives the processor to another ready thread: of a
   * priority at least the yielder's for Sleep(0) (a lower one waits, as on Windows), of any priority for SwitchToThread
   * (`yieldAny`); the yielder goes on only when there is none.
   */
  /** A ready thread's priority for a pick: its own, 16 when starved (see STARVE_INSNS), 0 in round-robin mode. */
  effPrio(t, now = this.vm.guestInsns ?? 0, picks = this.picks) {
    return this.roundRobin ? 0 : now - t.readyTime > this.starveInsns || picks - t.readyPick > this.starvePicks ? 16 : (t.priority ?? 0);
  }

  pickRunnable(except, top = false) {
    const ts = this.threads;
    const n = ts.length, now = this.vm.guestInsns ?? 0, picks = ++this.picks; // (instructions executed: see STARVE_INSNS)
    const y = top ? this.yielder : null;
    if (top) this.yielder = null;
    let best = null, bestK = 0, bestPrio = -Infinity, yK = -1, yPrio = -Infinity;
    for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
      const t = ts[(this.rr + k) % n];
      if (t === except || !t.isRunnable()) continue;
      const prio = this.effPrio(t, now, picks);
      if (t === y) { yK = k; yPrio = prio; continue; } // (the yielder: only if no other thread may run, below)
      if (prio > bestPrio) { best = t; bestPrio = prio; bestK = k; }
    }
    if (yK >= 0 && (best === null || (!this.yieldAny && bestPrio < yPrio))) { best = y; bestPrio = yPrio; bestK = yK; }
    // (the top-level pick: the thread whose slice ended — or the one a higher priority preempted — goes on with its
    // quantum unless a thread of higher priority is ready; a starved thread counts as higher)
    if (top && this.quantumInsns > 0 && !this.roundRobin) {
      const cont = this.sliceExpired;
      this.sliceExpired = null;
      let held = null;
      if (cont && cont === this.quantumThread && cont.isRunnable() && now < this.quantumEnd) held = { t: cont, left: this.quantumEnd - now };
      else if (this.preempted && this.preempted.t.isRunnable()) held = this.preempted;
      this.preempted = null;
      if (held) {
        if (bestPrio <= (held.t.priority ?? 0)) { this.quantumThread = held.t; this.quantumEnd = now + held.left; return held.t; }
        this.preempted = held; // (a higher priority first: the quantum left waits for it)
      }
      if (best) { this.quantumThread = best; this.quantumEnd = now + this.quantumInsns; }
    }
    if (best) this.rr = (this.rr + bestK + 1) % n;
    return best;
  }

  /**
   * Earliest wake-up time among sleeping/blocked threads and process timers. A timer already due at the last
   * wakeBlocked() pass does not count: every wait it could end was checked then and none did (a window timer whose
   * thread is busy or waits for something else stays due until that thread retrieves its WM_TIMER) — counted, it
   * made the idle loop spin without ever sleeping (nor returning to the event loop) until another thread woke.
   */
  nextWake() {
    let w = Infinity;
    for (const t of this.threads) if (t.state === TS.BLOCKED && t.wakeAt < w) w = t.wakeAt;
    const timers = this.vm.proc.timers, checked = this.checkedAt;
    for (const tm of timers) if (tm.due < w && tm.due > checked) w = tm.due;
    const host = this.vm.host?.nextWake?.();
    if (host !== undefined && host < w) w = host;
    const media = this.vm.media?.nextWake(); // (a movie playing: its next picture or sound refill, movie-player.js)
    if (media !== undefined && media < w) w = media;
    return w;
  }

  /** Wake parked threads whose condition holds or whose timeout passed. Returns true if any woke. */
  /** @param {number} [now] the clock's time when the caller has just read it */
  wakeBlocked(now = this.vm.clock.now()) {
    this.checkedAt = now;
    if (this.vm.media && now >= this.vm.media.due) this.vm.media.tick(now); // (movies advanced first: their events may wake waiters)
    let any = false;
    for (const t of this.threads) {
      if (t.state !== TS.BLOCKED || !t.wait) continue;
      if (t.pendingExit) { this.wake(t, false); any = true; continue; }
      let ok;
      try { ok = t.wait.cond(); } catch (e) { this.vm.warn(`wait condition threw: ${e.message} (t${t.id} ${typeof t.blockReason === 'function' ? t.blockReason() : t.blockReason}; ${String(e.stack ?? '').split('\n').slice(1, 4).map((l) => l.trim().replace(/^at /, '').replace(/\(?\S*\/src\//, '(')).join(' < ')})`); ok = true; }
      if (ok) { if (t.wait.claim) { t.wakeValue = t.wait.claim(true); this.vm.proc.syncTrace?.(`wake t${t.id} [${typeof t.blockReason === 'function' ? t.blockReason() : t.blockReason}] -> ${t.wakeValue}`); } this.wake(t, true); any = true; }
      else if (now >= t.wait.deadline) { this.wake(t, false); any = true; }
    }
    return any;
  }

  /**
   * A synchronization object was released or signaled: hand it to a parked waiter right away, before the
   * signaling thread can take it back (Windows satisfies waits at signal time; a releaser that immediately
   * re-acquires never starves a waiter). Only claim-carrying waits (mutex/event/semaphore/critical section)
   * are considered; plain sleeps and message waits wake at the next scheduling point as before.
   */
  signal() {
    for (const t of this.threads) {
      if (t.state !== TS.BLOCKED || !t.wait?.claim || t.pendingExit) continue;
      let ok;
      try { ok = t.wait.cond(); } catch (e) { ok = false; }
      if (ok) { t.wakeValue = t.wait.claim(true); this.vm.proc.syncTrace?.(`signal t${t.id} [${typeof t.blockReason === 'function' ? t.blockReason() : t.blockReason}] -> ${t.wakeValue}`); this.wake(t, true); }
    }
  }

  wake(t, ok) {
    if (t.blockedAt !== undefined) { // (diagnostics, vm.waitLogMin: the main thread's long waits)
      const d = this.vm.clock.now() - t.blockedAt;
      if (t === this.threads[0] && this.vm.mainWaits) { const k = `${t.blockedApi}@${this.vm.proc.symbolize(t.blockedFrom)}`; this.vm.mainWaits.set(k, (this.vm.mainWaits.get(k) ?? 0) + d); }
      if (d >= this.vm.waitLogMin && t === this.threads[0]) this.vm.logFn('hang', `main thread waited ${d.toFixed(0)} ms in ${t.blockedApi} [${typeof t.blockReason === 'function' ? t.blockReason() : t.blockReason}] from ${this.vm.proc.symbolize(t.blockedFrom)} (${ok ? 'satisfied' : 'timed out'})`);
      t.blockedAt = undefined;
    }
    t.wakeResult = ok; t.resuming = true; t.wait = null; t.wakeAt = Infinity; t.blockReason = null;
    this.markReady(t);
  }

  /**
   * Block `thread` until cond() is true or the timeout elapses.
   * @param {import('../win32/process.js').Thread} thread
   * @param {() => boolean} cond
   * @param {number} timeoutMs (INFINITE for no timeout)
   * @param {string} reason
   * @param {(() => any)=} claim runs as soon as cond holds — at the wake-up, before any other thread runs — to
   *   take the awaited object (mutex ownership, auto-reset event, semaphore count) exactly like the Windows kernel
   *   satisfies a wait at signal time; its value is left in `thread.wakeValue` for the re-executed call.
   * @param {boolean=} tick a guest timeout (Sleep, the Wait functions): it ends at the first clock interrupt at or after
   *   it, as Windows' kernel timers do (Sleep(1) lasts a tick: core/timer-res.js); the emulator's own short waits are exact
   * @returns {boolean} true if cond became true, false on timeout
   */
  block(thread, cond, timeoutMs, reason, claim, tick) { return this.wait(thread, cond, timeoutMs, reason, claim, false, tick); }
  /**
   * block() for a handler that returns PARK to the dispatcher instead of throwing WaitUnwind: the result is PARK when
   * the thread parks (the handler must return it at once), else block()'s result.
   */
  park(thread, cond, timeoutMs, reason, claim, tick) { return this.wait(thread, cond, timeoutMs, reason, claim, true, tick); }
  wait(thread, cond, timeoutMs, reason, claim, park, tick) {
    if (thread.wakeResult !== undefined) { // re-executed call after an unwound wait: the recorded outcome
      const r = thread.wakeResult;
      thread.wakeResult = undefined; thread.resuming = false;
      thread.state = TS.RUNNING;
      return r;
    }
    const clock = this.vm.clock;
    if (cond()) { thread.wakeValue = claim ? claim(false) : undefined; return true; }
    const now = clock.now();
    const deadline = timeoutMs === INFINITE ? Infinity : tick && timeoutMs > 0 && this.vm.timerRes ? this.vm.timerRes.tickAt(now + timeoutMs) : now + timeoutMs;
    if (now >= deadline) return false;
    if (this.vm.canUnwind(thread)) {
      const w = { cond, deadline, reason, claim };
      if (park) { thread.parkWait = w; return PARK; }
      throw new WaitUnwind(w);
    }
    // Nested context: run the others on top of this JS frame until the condition holds.
    this.nestedWaits++;
    try { return this.nestedWait(thread, cond, deadline, reason, claim); } finally { this.nestedWaits--; }
  }

  nestedWait(thread, cond, deadline, reason, claim) {
    const clock = this.vm.clock;
    let idleSince = -1;
    // (for the host's frame accounting: a wait for a file read — this thread's, or one another thread's read holds up,
    // or while the thread presenting frames waits for one — is not the game's pacing)
    const ioReason = reason === 'file read' || reason === 'file busy' || (this.vm.readsInFlight > 0 && reason !== 'sleep' && reason !== 'mmtimer' && reason !== 'peek'); // (peek: PeekMessage polling waits, user32.js peekIdle — pacing)
    const io = () => ioReason || !!this.vm.frameThreadWaitsForRead?.();
    const note = (ms) => { const k = `t${thread.id} ${reason}${io() ? ' (io)' : ''}`, m = (this.vm.nestedWaitLog ??= new Map()); if (m.size < 64 || m.has(k)) m.set(k, (m.get(k) ?? 0) + ms); }; // (diagnostics: who waits nested, for what)
    for (;;) {
      if (cond()) { thread.state = TS.RUNNING; thread.wakeAt = Infinity; thread.wakeValue = claim ? claim(false) : undefined; return true; }
      if (clock.now() >= deadline) { thread.state = TS.RUNNING; thread.wakeAt = Infinity; return false; }
      if (thread.pendingExit) { thread.state = TS.RUNNING; return false; }
      thread.state = TS.BLOCKED;
      thread.blockReason = reason;
      thread.wakeAt = deadline;
      this.wakeBlocked();
      const other = this.pickRunnable(thread);
      if (other) {
        idleSince = -1;
        this.vm.runThread(other, { slice: true });
        continue;
      }
      if (this.vm.host?.pump) this.vm.host.pump();
      if (cond()) continue;
      // (several processes, core/procs.js: the others run meanwhile — what this one waits for may be theirs)
      if (this.vm.group && this.vm.group.runOthers(this.vm)) continue;
      const wake = Math.min(this.nextWake(), deadline, this.vm.group ? clock.now() + 5 : Infinity);
      if (wake === Infinity) {
        if (idleSince < 0) idleSince = clock.now();
        if (this.vm.host?.waitEvent) { const w0 = clock.now(); this.vm.host.waitEvent(this.deadlockLimit, io()); note(clock.now() - w0); }
        else clock.sleep(1);
        if (clock.now() - idleSince > this.deadlockLimit) this.vm.deadlock(thread, reason);
        continue;
      }
      idleSince = -1;
      const now = clock.now();
      if (wake > now) {
        if (this.vm.host?.waitEvent) { this.vm.host.waitEvent(wake - now, io()); note(clock.now() - now); }
        else clock.sleepUntil(wake);
      }
    }
  }

  /** Is a thread other than `except` ready to run? (no scheduling decision: nothing changes) */
  hasRunnable(except) {
    for (const t of this.threads) if (t !== except && t.isRunnable()) return true;
    return false;
  }

  /**
   * Would a yield of `thread` hand the processor to another thread? A ready thread of a priority at least its own (a
   * starved one counts as higher: effPrio) for Sleep(0), any ready thread with `any` (SwitchToThread) — what the
   * top-level pick after the yield does (pickRunnable's `yielder`). No scheduling decision: nothing changes.
   * (A ready thread of lower priority does not count: the pick takes the yielder again, so a Sleep(0) spin with only
   * such a thread ready used to look like yields to the throttle — RotWK 2.02's frame limiter, ~2 700 Sleep(0) per
   * frame in the menu beside a ready THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL thread, never throttled; docs/api-layer.md.)
   */
  hasYieldTarget(thread, any = false) {
    if (any || this.roundRobin) return this.hasRunnable(thread);
    const p = thread.priority ?? 0, now = this.vm.guestInsns ?? 0, picks = this.picks;
    for (const t of this.threads) if (t !== thread && t.isRunnable() && this.effPrio(t, now, picks) >= p) return true;
    return false;
  }

  /**
   * Give other runnable threads a turn. At top level this ends the current slice, and the next pick prefers another
   * ready thread (pickRunnable's `yielder`): of a priority at least this thread's for Sleep(0), of any priority with
   * `any` (SwitchToThread). True when another thread is ready.
   * (Until 2026-10-22 the check for another ready thread was itself a pick, which moved the round robin past the thread
   * it found; the top-level pick then started after it and took the yielder again: a thread woken from its Sleep(1)
   * waited up to STARVE_PICKS of the spinning thread's Sleep(0) calls — BFME 1.08's main thread, ~250 of them in a row,
   * 256 a frame in play.)
   */
  yieldFrom(thread, any = false) {
    // (a yield with no other thread runnable still ends the slice: returning at once — as Windows does — was measured to
    // make a frame limiter polling Sleep(0) poll more often, not to make anything cheaper: see docs/api-layer.md)
    if (this.vm.canUnwind(thread)) {
      thread.yieldRequested = true;
      if (!(globalThis.ORTHROS_YIELD_PICK_OLD || globalThis.ORTHROS_SLEEP0_ANY_READY ? this.hasRunnable(thread) : this.hasYieldTarget(thread, any))) return false;
      if (globalThis.ORTHROS_YIELD_PICK_OLD) { this.pickRunnable(thread); return true; } // (measurement: the behaviour before 2026-10-22)
      this.yielder = thread; this.yieldAny = any;
      return true;
    }
    const other = this.pickRunnable(thread);
    if (!other) return false;
    // (Sleep(0) as at top level: a thread of lower priority waits — SwitchToThread, `any`, runs it)
    if (!any && !globalThis.ORTHROS_YIELD_PICK_OLD && this.effPrio(other) < (thread.priority ?? 0)) return false;
    this.vm.runThread(other, { slice: true });
    return true;
  }

  /** Top-level step when nothing is runnable: pump the host, wake threads, or sleep until the earliest wake-up. */
  idle() {
    const clock = this.vm.clock;
    if (this.vm.host?.pump) this.vm.host.pump();
    if (this.wakeBlocked()) { this.idleSince = -1; return; }
    const wake = this.nextWake();
    if (wake === Infinity) {
      if (this.idleSince < 0) this.idleSince = clock.now();
      if (this.vm.host?.waitEvent) this.vm.host.waitEvent(this.deadlockLimit, !!this.vm.frameThreadWaitsForRead?.());
      else clock.sleep(1);
      if (this.wakeBlocked()) { this.idleSince = -1; return; }
      if (clock.now() - this.idleSince > this.deadlockLimit) {
        const t = this.threads.find((x) => x.state === TS.BLOCKED) ?? this.threads[0];
        this.vm.deadlock(t, t?.blockReason ?? 'idle');
      }
      return;
    }
    this.idleSince = -1;
    const now = clock.now();
    if (wake > now) {
      // (frame accounting: while the thread presenting frames waits for a file read, the short waits between the other
      // threads' timers are the read's delay, not pacing)
      if (this.vm.host?.waitEvent) this.vm.host.waitEvent(wake - now, !!this.vm.frameThreadWaitsForRead?.());
      else clock.sleepUntil(wake);
    }
    this.wakeBlocked();
  }
}

```

`src/core/snapshot.js`:

```js
// Snapshot of the emulated machine (docs/snapshot.md, DECISIONS.md D071): the guest memory and the emulator's
// JavaScript state at a quiet point, restored in a fresh Vm built for the same game — the game goes on from there
// instead of running its start-up again.
//
// The JavaScript state is everything reachable from the Vm, walked field by field. A field is in the snapshot unless
// its class declares it transient (a cache, a link to the host: rebuilt at restore). The walk refuses what it cannot
// rebuild — a function, an object of a class nobody registered, an accessor, a view on a buffer it does not know — and
// names the path where it found it: state a later change adds cannot be left out silently, the snapshot is refused
// instead (the game then starts the usual way). Objects every Vm builds alike — the host's, and the whole graph its
// modules leave on the Vm once constructed (knowGraph) — are known: a snapshot refers to them by name and restores their
// contents into the restored Vm's own ones, so the closures holding them stay valid; a function there is code, the
// restored Vm's own, checked to be there. State kept in a closure and not handed over is invisible to the walk:
// tests/snapshot-lint.test.js looks for it in the sources.
import { GUEST_SPACE, PAGE_SIZE, JIT_HASH_BASE, THUNK_BASE, JIT_ALT_BASE, SMC_MAP_BASE, BLOCK_COUNTS_BASE, BLOCK_COUNTS_SLOTS } from '../cpu/memory.js';
import { ModuleBuilder, Code, T } from '../cpu/jit/wasm.js';

export const SNAPSHOT_FORMAT = 1;

/** Guest memory the JIT owns (its tables): left out of a snapshot, rebuilt by the restored Vm's JIT. */
export const JIT_RANGES = [[JIT_HASH_BASE, THUNK_BASE], [JIT_ALT_BASE, SMC_MAP_BASE], [SMC_MAP_BASE, BLOCK_COUNTS_BASE + BLOCK_COUNTS_SLOTS * 4]];

/** A snapshot cannot be taken or restored: `path` says where (e.g. "vm.proc.threads[2].wait.cond"). */
export class SnapshotError extends Error {
  constructor(message, path = '') { super(path ? `${message} at ${path}` : message); this.path = path; }
}
/** A snapshot that does not apply to this machine's start (another profile, registry, format): refused before any change. */
export class SnapshotStale extends SnapshotError {}

const TYPED = { Int8Array, Uint8Array, Uint8ClampedArray, Int16Array, Uint16Array, Int32Array, Uint32Array, Float32Array, Float64Array, BigInt64Array, BigUint64Array };

/**
 * What a snapshot may hold beyond plain data, for one Vm: registered classes (by name and prototype), known objects
 * (by name and identity: built by the host or by the modules of every Vm, restored in place) and constants (shared
 * frozen objects and functions: kept by identity).
 */
export class SnapRegistry {
  constructor() {
    /** @type {Map<string, ClassEntry>} */ this.byName = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<object, ClassEntry>} */ this.byProto = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<string, any>} */ this.knownByName = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<any, string>} */ this.knownName = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<string, {state: boolean, save?: Function, load?: Function}>} */ this.knownOpts = new Map();
    for (const e of GLOBAL_CLASSES.values()) this.addClass(e);
    for (const [name, obj] of GLOBAL_CONSTS) { this.knownByName.set(name, obj); this.knownName.set(obj, name); this.knownOpts.set(name, { state: false }); }
  }

  addClass(e) {
    const old = this.byName.get(e.name);
    if (old && old.proto !== e.proto) throw new SnapshotError(`two snapshot classes named ${e.name}`);
    this.byName.set(e.name, e); this.byProto.set(e.proto, e);
  }

  /** A class of this Vm only (defined in a module's closure): see snapshotClass. */
  cls(cls, opts = {}) { this.addClass(classEntry(cls, opts)); return cls; }

  /**
   * An object every Vm builds the same way (its host links, the containers a module keeps in its closure), known by
   * `name`: a snapshot refers to it by name, and restores its contents into the restored Vm's own one (`state`,
   * default true: a Map's entries, a Set's members, an object's fields; `save(obj) → data` and `load(obj, data)` for
   * others). `state: false`: identity only (the host's objects, constants).
   */
  known(name, obj, opts = {}) {
    if (this.knownByName.has(name) && this.knownByName.get(name) !== obj) throw new SnapshotError(`two known objects named ${name}`);
    this.knownByName.set(name, obj); this.knownName.set(obj, name);
    this.knownOpts.set(name, { state: opts.state ?? true, save: opts.save, load: opts.load, skip: new Set(opts.skip ?? []) });
    return obj;
  }

  /**
   * Every object reachable from `root` (known already) becomes known, named by its path: the graph a Vm's construction
   * leaves (its modules' tables, registries, initial state) is built alike by every Vm. `skip(obj, key)`: fields not
   * followed (the root's transient ones). Functions are not objects of the graph: values.
   */
  knowGraph(root, skip = () => false) {
    const queue = [[root, this.knownName.get(root)]];
    const visit = (v, path) => {
      if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object' || this.knownName.has(v)) return;
      this.known(path, v); queue.push([v, path]);
    };
    while (queue.length) {
      const [o, path] = queue.shift();
      const opts = this.knownOpts.get(path);
      if (opts && (!opts.state || opts.save)) continue; // (opaque, or saved by hooks: not followed)
      if (ArrayBuffer.isView(o) || o instanceof ArrayBuffer) continue;
      if (Array.isArray(o)) { o.forEach((v, i) => visit(v, `${path}[${i}]`)); continue; }
      if (o instanceof Map) { let i = 0; for (const [k, v] of o) { visit(k, `${path}<key ${i}>`); visit(v, `${path}.get(${typeof k === 'object' ? `#${i}` : String(k)})`); i++; } continue; }
      if (o instanceof Set) { let i = 0; for (const v of o) visit(v, `${path}<member ${i++}>`); continue; }
      for (const k of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(o)) {
        if (opts?.skip.has(k) || skip(o, k)) continue;
        const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o, k);
        if ('value' in d) visit(d.value, `${path}.${k}`);
      }
    }
  }
}

/**
 * @typedef {object} ClassEntry
 * @property {string} name
 * @property {object} proto
 * @property {Set<string>} skip fields not in a snapshot (transient: caches, host links)
 * @property {(obj: any, vm: any) => void} [init] after a restore, rebuilds the skipped fields of `obj`
 * @property {(obj: any, vm: any) => (void|Promise<void>)} [resume] once the restored machine is whole: hands the new
 *   host what `obj` had shown the captured one (a display mode, a cursor, fonts...); a promise: what the host waits for
 *   before running the machine (vm.restoring)
 * @property {(obj: any) => any} [save] the object as plain data (no object references), instead of its fields
 * @property {(data: any, vm: any) => any} [load] the object from what save() returned
 */
const GLOBAL_CLASSES = new Map(), GLOBAL_CONSTS = new Map();
function classEntry(cls, opts) {
  return { name: opts.name ?? cls.name, proto: cls.prototype, skip: new Set(opts.skip ?? []), init: opts.init, resume: opts.resume, save: opts.save, load: opts.load };
}

/**
 * Declare a class (defined at a module's top level) whose instances a snapshot may hold. `skip`: transient fields
 * (rebuilt by `init(obj, vm)` after a restore); `resume(obj, vm)`: what the host showed, shown again once the machine
 * is restored; `save`/`load`: the object as plain data instead (a view on the guest memory, ...).
 */
export function snapshotClass(cls, opts = {}) {
  const e = classEntry(cls, opts);
  if (GLOBAL_CLASSES.has(e.name) && GLOBAL_CLASSES.get(e.name).proto !== e.proto) throw new SnapshotError(`two snapshot classes named ${e.name}`);
  GLOBAL_CLASSES.set(e.name, e);
  return cls;
}

// snapshot: constant, the keys cacheKey made
const CACHE_KEYS = new Set();
/**
 * A property key for a cache a module keeps on a plain object — code compiled from the object's data, values derived
 * from it: never in a snapshot, rebuilt where it is read (`obj[KEY] ??= build(obj)`). Any other symbol key is refused.
 */
export function cacheKey(name) { const k = Symbol(name); CACHE_KEYS.add(k); return k; }

/** `vm.snap.known(name, obj, opts)` on a Vm that has a snapshot registry (a test's minimal one may not): `obj`. */
export const snapKnown = (vm, name, obj, opts) => (vm.snap ? vm.snap.known(name, obj, opts) : obj);
/** `vm.snap.cls(cls, opts)` on a Vm that has a snapshot registry. */
export const snapClass = (vm, cls, opts) => (vm.snap ? vm.snap.cls(cls, opts) : cls);

/** A shared constant (a frozen object, a function) a snapshot may refer to, by name. */
export function snapshotConstant(name, obj) { GLOBAL_CONSTS.set(name, obj); return obj; }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the JavaScript state

const isPlainProto = (p) => p === Object.prototype || p === null;

/**
 * The state graph reachable from `root` (a known object): `{ root, objects }`, each object one record, references
 * between them by index; typed arrays' bytes in `blobs`. `problems`: an array to collect every refusal in (each
 * value refused left out) instead of throwing at the first — the list of what to declare.
 */
export function encodeGraph(root, reg, problems = null) {
  const ids = new Map(), objects = [], blobs = [], from = [];
  const refuse = (e) => { if (!problems) throw e; problems.push(e.message); return { u: 1 }; };
  const where = (id, key) => { const parts = [key]; for (let i = id; i >= 0; i = from[i][0]) parts.push(from[i][1]); return parts.reverse().join(''); };
  const queue = [];
  const ref = (v, parentId, key) => {
    let id = ids.get(v);
    if (id === undefined) { id = objects.length; ids.set(v, id); objects.push(null); from.push([parentId, key]); queue.push(v); }
    return { r: id };
  };
  const value = (v, parentId, key, code = false) => {
    if (code && typeof v === 'function' && !reg.knownName.has(v)) return { f: 1 }; // (code of a known object: the restored Vm's own)
    switch (typeof v) {
      case 'number': return Number.isFinite(v) && !Object.is(v, -0) ? v : { n: Object.is(v, -0) ? '-0' : String(v) };
      case 'string': case 'boolean': return v;
      case 'undefined': return { u: 1 };
      case 'bigint': return { b: v.toString() };
      case 'symbol': return refuse(new SnapshotError('a symbol', where(parentId, key)));
      case 'function': if (reg.knownName.has(v)) return ref(v, parentId, key); return refuse(new SnapshotError(`a function (${v.name || 'anonymous'})`, where(parentId, key)));
      default: return v === null ? null : ref(v, parentId, key);
    }
  };
  const fields = (o, id, skip, owner, code) => {
    const p = {};
    for (const k of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(o)) {
      if (skip?.has(k)) continue;
      const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o, k);
      if (!('value' in d)) { refuse(new SnapshotError(`an accessor (${owner})`, where(id, '.' + k))); continue; }
      p[k] = value(d.value, id, '.' + k, code);
    }
    if (Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(o).some((s) => !CACHE_KEYS.has(s))) refuse(new SnapshotError(`symbol keys (${owner})`, where(id, '')));
    return p;
  };
  const rootName = reg.knownName.get(root);
  if (rootName === undefined) throw new SnapshotError('the root is not a known object');
  ref(root, -1, rootName);
  // (known objects with state are in wherever they are referenced from, or not: the containers a module keeps in its
  // closure are reachable from nothing else)
  for (const [name, o] of reg.knownByName) if (reg.knownOpts.get(name).state) ref(o, -1, name);
  while (queue.length) {
    const o = queue.shift(), id = ids.get(o);
    const known = reg.knownName.get(o);
    if (known !== undefined) {
      const ko = reg.knownOpts.get(known);
      let s;
      if (ko.state) s = ko.save ? { d: ko.save(o) } : container(o, id, ko.skip, known);
      objects[id] = s === undefined ? { k: known } : { k: known, s };
      continue;
    }
    try { objects[id] = container(o, id, null, null); } catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof SnapshotError) || !problems) throw e; problems.push(e.message); objects[id] = { c: null, p: {} }; }
  }
  return { root: 0, objects, blobs };

  /** an object's contents as a record (known objects: their state, their functions code) */
  function container(o, id, skip, known) {
    const code = known !== null;
    if (Array.isArray(o)) {
      if (Object.getPrototypeOf(o) !== Array.prototype) throw new SnapshotError('an array subclass', where(id, ''));
      const a = new Array(o.length); for (let i = 0; i < o.length; i++) a[i] = value(o[i], id, `[${i}]`, code);
      return { a };
    }
    if (o instanceof Map) { const m = []; let i = 0; for (const [k, v] of o) { m.push([value(k, id, `<key ${i}>`), value(v, id, `.get(${typeof k === 'object' ? i : String(k)})`, code)]); i++; } return { m }; }
    if (o instanceof Set) { const st = []; let i = 0; for (const v of o) st.push(value(v, id, `<member ${i++}>`, code)); return { st }; }
    if (ArrayBuffer.isView(o)) {
      const name = o instanceof DataView ? 'DataView' : o.constructor?.name;
      if (name !== 'DataView' && (!TYPED[name] || Object.getPrototypeOf(o) !== TYPED[name].prototype)) throw new SnapshotError(`a buffer view (${name})`, where(id, ''));
      if (code && name !== 'DataView') { blobs.push(new Uint8Array(o.buffer, o.byteOffset, o.byteLength).slice()); return { t: name, b: blobs.length - 1 }; } // (a known array: its bytes, in place)
      // (a view: on its buffer — shared with other views, or the guest memory's, a known one — at its offset)
      return { t: name, buf: value(o.buffer, id, '.buffer'), off: o.byteOffset, len: name === 'DataView' ? o.byteLength : o.length };
    }
    if (o instanceof ArrayBuffer) { if (o.byteLength > 1 << 28) throw new SnapshotError(`an ArrayBuffer of ${o.byteLength} bytes (the guest memory's? register it)`, where(id, '')); blobs.push(new Uint8Array(o).slice()); return { ab: blobs.length - 1 }; }
    if (typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' && o instanceof SharedArrayBuffer) throw new SnapshotError('a SharedArrayBuffer (register it)', where(id, ''));
    const proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(o);
    if (isPlainProto(proto)) return { c: proto === null ? '' : null, p: fields(o, id, skip, 'object', code) };
    const e = reg.byProto.get(proto);
    if (!e) {
      if (known) return { p: fields(o, id, skip, known, code) }; // (a known object of any class: its fields, in place)
      throw new SnapshotError(`an object of class ${o.constructor?.name ?? '?'} (not registered)`, where(id, ''));
    }
    if (e.save) return { x: e.name, d: e.save(o) };
    return { c: e.name, p: fields(o, id, skip ? new Set([...skip, ...e.skip]) : e.skip, e.name, code) };
  }
}

/**
 * Restore a graph of encodeGraph into the world of `reg` (another Vm's registry): known objects are that Vm's own, their
 * state put in place; the others are created. Returns `{ root, reimpose }`: reimpose() puts the snapshot's contents again
 * into the same objects (undoing what ran since — see vm-snapshot.js, waits rebuilt by re-executing calls).
 */
export function decodeGraph(graph, reg, vm) {
  const { objects, blobs } = graph, out = new Array(objects.length), inits = [];
  // (pass 1: every object, empty; known ones resolved; buffers before the views on them)
  objects.forEach((rec, i) => {
    if (rec.k !== undefined) {
      if (!reg.knownByName.has(rec.k)) throw new SnapshotError(`no known object ${rec.k} in this Vm`);
      out[i] = reg.knownByName.get(rec.k);
    } else if (rec.ab !== undefined) out[i] = blobs[rec.ab].slice().buffer;
  });
  objects.forEach((rec, i) => {
    if (out[i] !== undefined) return;
    if (rec.a) out[i] = new Array(rec.a.length);
    else if (rec.m) out[i] = new Map();
    else if (rec.st) out[i] = new Set();
    else if (rec.t && rec.buf) { const buf = out[rec.buf.r]; out[i] = rec.t === 'DataView' ? new DataView(buf, rec.off, rec.len) : new TYPED[rec.t](buf, rec.off, rec.len); }
    else if (rec.t) out[i] = new TYPED[rec.t](blobs[rec.b].slice().buffer);
    else if (rec.x) { const e = reg.byName.get(rec.x); if (!e?.load) throw new SnapshotError(`no snapshot class ${rec.x} in this Vm`); out[i] = e.load(rec.d, vm); }
    else if (rec.c === null) out[i] = {};
    else if (rec.c === '') out[i] = Object.create(null);
    else { const e = reg.byName.get(rec.c); if (!e) throw new SnapshotError(`no snapshot class ${rec.c} in this Vm`); out[i] = Object.create(e.proto); if (e.init) inits.push([e, out[i]]); }
  });
  const v = (x) => {
    if (x === null || typeof x !== 'object') return x;
    if (x.r !== undefined) return out[x.r];
    if (x.u) return undefined;
    if (x.n !== undefined) return x.n === '-0' ? -0 : Number(x.n);
    if (x.b !== undefined) return BigInt(x.b);
    throw new SnapshotError('a malformed value');
  };
  // (pass 2: contents; a known object's state in place, its code — {f: 1} — the restored Vm's own, checked)
  const code = (fn, where) => { if (typeof fn !== 'function') throw new SnapshotError('the restored Vm has no function', where); return fn; };
  const fill = (again) => objects.forEach((rec, i) => {
    const o = out[i];
    const known = rec.k !== undefined || again, s = rec.k !== undefined ? rec.s : rec;
    if (!s || rec.x) return;
    if (known && s.d !== undefined) { reg.knownOpts.get(rec.k).load(o, s.d, vm); return; }
    const at = (key) => `${rec.k ?? `#${i}`}${key}`;
    if (s.a) { const old = known ? o.slice() : null; if (known) o.length = 0; s.a.forEach((x, j) => { o[j] = x?.f ? code(old?.[j], at(`[${j}]`)) : v(x); }); }
    else if (s.m) { const old = known ? new Map(o) : null; if (known) o.clear(); for (const [k, x] of s.m) { const key = v(k); o.set(key, x?.f ? code(old?.get(key), at(`.get(${String(key)})`)) : v(x)); } }
    else if (s.st) { if (known) o.clear(); for (const x of s.st) o.add(v(x)); }
    else if (s.t && s.b !== undefined && known) { const b = blobs[s.b]; if (b.length !== o.byteLength) throw new SnapshotError(`a ${s.t} of another size`, at('')); new Uint8Array(o.buffer, o.byteOffset, o.byteLength).set(b); }
    else if (s.ab !== undefined && again) new Uint8Array(o).set(blobs[s.ab]);
    else if (s.p) for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(s.p)) { if (x?.f) code(o[k], at(`.${k}`)); else o[k] = v(x); }
  });
  fill(false);
  for (const [e, o] of inits) e.init(o, vm);
  return {
    root: out[graph.root],
    reimpose() { fill(true); for (const [e, o] of inits) e.init(o, vm); },
    /** The resume hooks run; what they return that the host waits for (promises) before the machine goes on. */
    resume() {
      const waits = [];
      for (const o of out) { const e = o !== null && typeof o === 'object' ? reg.byProto.get(Object.getPrototypeOf(o)) : null; const r = e?.resume?.(o, vm); if (r?.then) waits.push(r); }
      return waits;
    },
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the guest memory

const inJit = (a) => JIT_RANGES.some(([s, e]) => a >= s && a < e);

/** The guest memory's pages holding anything (zero pages implied), the JIT's tables left out. */
export function capturePages(mem) {
  const u8 = mem.u8, n = Math.min(u8.byteLength, GUEST_SPACE) / PAGE_SIZE;
  const index = [], data = [];
  const next = pageScanner(mem);
  for (let p = next(0, n); p < n; p = next(p + 1, n)) {
    const a = p * PAGE_SIZE;
    if (inJit(a)) continue;
    index.push(p); data.push(u8.subarray(a, a + PAGE_SIZE));
  }
  const all = new Uint8Array(index.length * PAGE_SIZE);
  data.forEach((d, i) => all.set(d, i * PAGE_SIZE));
  return { pageSize: PAGE_SIZE, index: Uint32Array.from(index), data: all };
}

// snapshot: cache, a scanner per memory
const scanners = new WeakMap();
/**
 * next(p, end): the first page in [p, end) holding a nonzero byte, else end. WebAssembly SIMD on the memory itself (2 GB
 * scanned in a fraction of the 850 ms a JavaScript loop takes: most of it never touched, the same zero page read again);
 * the JavaScript loop where it is not available.
 */
function pageScanner(mem) {
  let next = mem.memory ? scanners.get(mem.memory) : undefined;
  if (next) return next;
  try {
    const shared = typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' && mem.memory.buffer instanceof SharedArrayBuffer;
    const m = new ModuleBuilder(), c = new Code(), P = 0, END = 1, A = 2, E = 3, ACC = 4;
    m.importMemory('env', 'memory', 1, shared ? 65536 : undefined, shared);
    const found = c.block(), pages = c.loop();
    c.get(P).get(END).ge_u().br_if(found);
    c.get(P).i32(12).shl().tee(A).i32(PAGE_SIZE).add().set(E);
    c.v128const(new Uint8Array(16)).set(ACC);
    const words = c.loop(); // (64 bytes a turn)
    c.get(ACC).get(A).v128load(0).v128or().get(A).v128load(16).v128or().get(A).v128load(32).v128or().get(A).v128load(48).v128or().set(ACC);
    c.get(A).i32(64).add().tee(A).get(E).lt_u().br_if(words);
    c.end();
    c.get(ACC).v128anytrue().br_if(found);
    c.get(P).i32(1).add().set(P).br(pages);
    c.end(); c.end(); void found;
    c.get(P);
    m.exportFunc('next', m.func([T.i32, T.i32], [T.i32], [T.i32, T.i32, T.v128], c, 'next'));
    next = new WebAssembly.Instance(new WebAssembly.Module(m.build()), { env: { memory: mem.memory } }).exports.next;
  } catch {
    const w = new Int32Array(mem.u8.buffer, 0, Math.min(mem.u8.byteLength, GUEST_SPACE) >>> 2), per = PAGE_SIZE >>> 2;
    next = (p, end) => {
      for (; p < end; p++) { let i = p * per; const e = i + per; while (i < e && (w[i] | w[i + 1] | w[i + 2] | w[i + 3]) === 0) i += 4; if (i < e) return p; }
      return end;
    };
  }
  if (mem.memory) scanners.set(mem.memory, next);
  return next;
}

/** Write `pages` into `mem` (whose other pages, the JIT's tables aside, must be zero: a fresh Vm's). */
export function restorePages(mem, pages) {
  const u8 = mem.u8;
  pages.index.forEach((p, i) => { u8.set(pages.data.subarray(i * pages.pageSize, (i + 1) * pages.pageSize), p * pages.pageSize); });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a snapshot as bytes

/** The snapshot as one buffer (persisted, compared): a header, the graph as JSON, then the binary parts. */
export function encodeSnapshot(snap) {
  const enc = new TextEncoder();
  const bins = [snap.pages.index, snap.pages.data, ...snap.graph.blobs].map((b) => new Uint8Array(b.buffer, b.byteOffset, b.byteLength));
  const json = enc.encode(JSON.stringify({ format: snap.format, meta: snap.meta, pageSize: snap.pages.pageSize, root: snap.graph.root, objects: snap.graph.objects, bins: bins.map((b) => b.length) }));
  const out = new Uint8Array(8 + json.length + bins.reduce((s, b) => s + b.length, 0));
  const dv = new DataView(out.buffer);
  dv.setUint32(0, 0x4f534e50); dv.setUint32(4, json.length); // 'OSNP'
  out.set(json, 8);
  let at = 8 + json.length; for (const b of bins) { out.set(b, at); at += b.length; }
  return out;
}

export function decodeSnapshot(bytes) {
  const dv = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
  if (dv.getUint32(0) !== 0x4f534e50) throw new SnapshotError('not a snapshot');
  const len = dv.getUint32(4), head = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes.subarray(8, 8 + len)));
  if (head.format !== SNAPSHOT_FORMAT) throw new SnapshotError(`snapshot format ${head.format}, expected ${SNAPSHOT_FORMAT}`);
  let at = 8 + len; const bins = head.bins.map((n) => { const b = bytes.slice(at, at + n); at += n; return b; });
  return { format: head.format, meta: head.meta, pages: { pageSize: head.pageSize, index: new Uint32Array(bins[0].buffer), data: bins[1] }, graph: { root: head.root, objects: head.objects, blobs: bins.slice(2) } };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- comparing snapshots

/**
 * Where two snapshots differ (empty: they are the same machine): guest memory bytes, then objects, named by the path
 * the walk first reached them by. `ignore`: patterns of field paths not compared (fields read against the host's clock).
 * The oracle of tests/snapshot.test.js and tools/snapshot-check.mjs: a machine restored from a snapshot and the one it
 * was taken from, run alike, must stay the same.
 */
export function snapshotsDiffer(a, b, { ignore = [], max = 20 } = {}) {
  const out = [];
  const pa = new Map(), pb = new Map();
  a.pages.index.forEach((p, i) => pa.set(p, i)); b.pages.index.forEach((p, i) => pb.set(p, i));
  const page = (s, i) => (i === undefined ? null : s.pages.data.subarray(i * s.pages.pageSize, (i + 1) * s.pages.pageSize));
  for (const p of new Set([...pa.keys(), ...pb.keys()])) {
    if (out.length >= max) return out;
    const x = page(a, pa.get(p)), y = page(b, pb.get(p));
    for (let j = 0, n = a.pages.pageSize; j < n; j++) if ((x?.[j] ?? 0) !== (y?.[j] ?? 0)) { out.push(`memory at ${(p * n + j).toString(16)}: ${x?.[j] ?? 0} vs ${y?.[j] ?? 0}`); break; }
  }
  const names = (g) => {
    const n = new Array(g.objects.length);
    const queue = [g.root]; n[g.root] = g.objects[g.root].k ?? 'root';
    while (queue.length) {
      const i = queue.shift(), r = g.objects[i], s = r.k !== undefined ? r.s : r;
      if (r.k !== undefined) n[i] = r.k;
      const visit = (x, key) => { if (x && typeof x === 'object' && x.r !== undefined && n[x.r] === undefined) { n[x.r] = n[i] + key; queue.push(x.r); } };
      if (s?.p) for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(s.p)) visit(x, '.' + k);
      s?.a?.forEach((x, j) => visit(x, `[${j}]`));
      s?.m?.forEach(([k, x], j) => { visit(k, `<key ${j}>`); visit(x, `.get(${typeof k === 'object' ? j : k})`); });
      s?.st?.forEach((x, j) => visit(x, `<member ${j}>`));
    }
    return n;
  };
  const na = names(a.graph), nb = names(b.graph);
  const blob = (s, x) => s.graph.blobs[x];
  const same = (x, y, ga, gb) => JSON.stringify(x) === JSON.stringify(y);
  if (a.graph.objects.length !== b.graph.objects.length) out.push(`${a.graph.objects.length} vs ${b.graph.objects.length} objects`);
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(a.graph.objects.length, b.graph.objects.length) && out.length < max; i++) {
    const x = a.graph.objects[i], y = b.graph.objects[i], path = na[i] ?? `#${i}`;
    if (path !== (nb[i] ?? `#${i}`)) { out.push(`object ${i}: ${path} vs ${nb[i]}`); continue; }
    const sx = x.k !== undefined ? x.s : x, sy = y.k !== undefined ? y.s : y;
    if (sx?.p && sy?.p) {
      for (const k of new Set([...Object.keys(sx.p), ...Object.keys(sy.p)])) {
        const fp = `${path}.${k}`;
        if (ignore.some((re) => re.test(fp))) continue;
        if (!same(sx.p[k], sy.p[k])) out.push(`${fp}: ${JSON.stringify(sx.p[k])?.slice(0, 80)} vs ${JSON.stringify(sy.p[k])?.slice(0, 80)}`);
      }
      continue;
    }
    const bx = sx?.b !== undefined ? blob(a, sx.b) : sx?.ab !== undefined ? blob(a, sx.ab) : null, by = sy?.b !== undefined ? blob(b, sy.b) : sy?.ab !== undefined ? blob(b, sy.ab) : null;
    if (bx || by) { if (!bx || !by || bx.length !== by.length || bx.some((v, j) => v !== by[j])) out.push(`${path}: bytes differ`); continue; }
    if (!same(sx, sy)) out.push(`${path}: ${JSON.stringify(sx)?.slice(0, 100)} vs ${JSON.stringify(sy)?.slice(0, 100)}`);
  }
  return out.slice(0, max);
}
```

`src/core/timer-res.js`:

```js
// The system timer resolution (Windows' clock interrupt), as the guest sees it.
//
// Windows does not wake a sleeping or timed-out thread at an arbitrary instant: timer expirations are checked at the
// clock interrupt, which fires every 15.625 ms by default (64 Hz) and every `p` ms while some program holds
// timeBeginPeriod(p) (winmm; the smallest request wins, down to 1 ms). So:
//   - Sleep(n) / a wait timing out after n ms ends at the first interrupt at or after now + n: Sleep(1) lasts ~15.6 ms
//     at the default resolution, 1-2 ms under timeBeginPeriod(1);
//   - GetTickCount advances only at the clock tick, in steps of 15.625 ms (15 or 16) whatever the resolution;
//   - timeGetTime advances at the interrupt: in 1 ms steps under timeBeginPeriod(1), coarser otherwise.
// Before this model Orthros woke threads at the exact millisecond and both tick counters ran in 1 ms steps: a thread
// looping on Sleep(1) without timeBeginPeriod ran ~15 times more often than on Windows, and a program comparing tick
// counts saw them change between calls where Windows shows the same value.
//
// `?dbg=ORTHROS_TIMER_RES=<ms>` sets the default resolution (15.625; 0: the exact behaviour before, no rounding at all).

/** Windows' default clock interrupt period (ms) and GetTickCount's step */
export const DEFAULT_TIMER_RES = 15.625;

export class TimerResolution {
  /** @param {number} [defaultMs] the resolution with no timeBeginPeriod request (0: no rounding anywhere) */
  constructor(defaultMs = DEFAULT_TIMER_RES) {
    this.defaultMs = defaultMs;
    /** @type {Map<number, number>} active timeBeginPeriod requests: period -> count */
    this.requests = new Map();
    this.ms = defaultMs;
    /** timeGetTime's last value: it never goes back when the resolution gets coarser (timeEndPeriod) */
    this.lastMm = 0;
  }

  /** timeBeginPeriod(p): false (TIMERR_NOCANDO) for a period outside 1..1000000 */
  begin(p) {
    if (!(p >= 1 && p <= 1000000)) return false;
    this.requests.set(p, (this.requests.get(p) ?? 0) + 1);
    this.update();
    return true;
  }

  /** timeEndPeriod(p): false (TIMERR_NOCANDO) without a matching begin */
  end(p) {
    const n = this.requests.get(p);
    if (!n) return false;
    if (n === 1) this.requests.delete(p); else this.requests.set(p, n - 1);
    this.update();
    return true;
  }

  update() {
    let r = this.defaultMs;
    if (r > 0) for (const p of this.requests.keys()) if (p < r) r = p;
    this.ms = r;
  }

  /** the first clock interrupt at or after `t` (ms of the VM clock): when a timeout due at `t` is noticed */
  tickAt(t) {
    const r = this.ms;
    if (!(r > 0) || !Number.isFinite(t)) return t;
    const k = Math.ceil(t / r - 1e-9);
    return k * r;
  }

  /** GetTickCount's milliseconds at clock time `now`: the last 15.625 ms tick (integer ms) */
  tickCount(now) {
    if (!(this.defaultMs > 0)) return Math.floor(now);
    return Math.floor(Math.floor(now / DEFAULT_TIMER_RES) * DEFAULT_TIMER_RES);
  }

  /** timeGetTime's milliseconds at clock time `now`: the last interrupt (integer ms). Monotonic: after a switch to a
   * coarser period (timeEndPeriod(1) at 1010.3 ms: the 15.625 ms grid's last interrupt is 1000) the value holds until the
   * next interrupt of the new period instead of going back, as Windows' interrupt time never does */
  mmTime(now) {
    const r = this.ms;
    const v = !(r > 0) ? Math.floor(now) : Math.floor(Math.floor(now / r) * r);
    return v >= this.lastMm ? (this.lastMm = v) : this.lastMm;
  }
}

/** the resolution from the debug switch (see above) */
export function timerResFromDebug() {
  const v = globalThis.ORTHROS_TIMER_RES;
  return new TimerResolution(v === undefined || v === '' ? DEFAULT_TIMER_RES : Number(v));
}
```

`src/core/vm-snapshot.js`:

```js
// Snapshots of a whole Vm (docs/snapshot.md, DECISIONS.md D071): what a snapshot of the machine holds — the classes it
// may contain and their transient fields, the objects every Vm builds alike (known, restored in place) — and the capture
// and restore at a quiet point. One file lists them, to be read when a snapshot is refused: a field added to one of
// these classes is in snapshots unless declared transient here.
import { THUNK_BASE, THUNK_END, THUNK_SIZE } from '../cpu/memory.js';
import { DEFER_QUEUE } from '../cpu/jit/runtime.js';
import { SnapRegistry, SnapshotError, SnapshotStale, snapshotClass, snapshotConstant, encodeGraph, decodeGraph, capturePages, restorePages, SNAPSHOT_FORMAT } from './snapshot.js';
import { VirtualClock } from './clock.js';
import { MemBackend, seenFingerprint, hashBytes } from '../vfs/vfs.js';

import { Process, Thread, TS } from '../win32/process.js';

import { Com } from '../win32/com.js';
import { Seh } from '../win32/seh.js';

import { WindowManager } from '../win32/user32.js';
import { GdiState } from '../win32/gdi32.js';

import { FileHandle } from '../win32/kernel32-file.js';
import { Surface } from '../gfx/gdi/surface.js';
import { TextEngine } from '../gfx/gdi/text.js';

/** The Vm's fields that are not machine state: the executors, the host's links, diagnostics, the registry itself. */
const VM_TRANSIENT = ['vfs', 'clock', 'host', 'mem', 'api', 'interp', 'jit', 'exec', 'ctx', 'snap', 'logFn', 'logKinds', 'traceApi', 'traceApiBg',
  'traceApiRet', 'traceApiSite', 'traceApiSiteMax', 'apiTrace', 'apiTracePos', 'apiTraceNames', 'apiTraceRets', 'apiTraceTids', 'apiHistCounts',
  'profile', 'progressAt', 'progressEvery', 'onProgress', 'heapProv', 'heapProvMap', 'stdout', 'onStdout', 'deadline', 'sliceInsns',
  'runOptsByDepth', 'restoring', 'traceCom', 'traceComQuiet', 'GuestCrash', 'returnThunk', 'callbackReturnThunk', 'exitThreadThunk', 'exitProcessThunk',

  'ctorOpts', 'group', 'parentVm', 'kernelNamed']; // (group...: child processes, core/procs.js — a machine with several is not snapshotted)

snapshotClass(CpuState, { save: (c) => ({ base: c.base }), load: (d, vm) => new CpuState(vm.mem, d.base) });
// (a parked wait is closures: rebuilt at the restore by re-executing the blocking call — see restoreVm)
// (runMs: host time spent, diagnostics)
snapshotClass(Thread, { skip: ['wait', 'parkWait', 'blockReason', 'runMs'], init: (t) => { t.wait = null; t.parkWait = null; t.blockReason = null; t.runMs = 0; } });

/**
 * Fields read against the host's clock (performance.now()), meaningless in another page: reset at a restore, and
 * not compared by snapshotsDiffer. Each: [path pattern, what restoreVm puts there].
 */
export const HOST_TIME_FIELDS = [];
snapshotClass(Process);
snapshotClass(HandleTable);
snapshotClass(VMem);
snapshotClass(Heap, { skip: ['watchLog'] }); // (debugging hook)
// (the file's bytes are only read while the image is mapped: not kept)
snapshotClass(PeImage, { skip: ['bytes', 'dv'], init: (img) => { img.bytes = null; img.dv = null; } });
snapshotClass(Com, { skip: ['vm', 'failedSeen'], init: (c, vm) => { c.vm = vm; c.failedSeen = new Map(); } });
snapshotClass(Seh, { skip: ['vm'], init: (s, vm) => { s.vm = vm; } });
snapshotClass(Mutex);
snapshotClass(Registry);
```
