`src/host/pcm-units.js`:

```js
// Which bytes of a game file are PCM sound, for the PCM transport units (src/vfs/pcm-codec.js, made by
// src/host/br-cache-worker.js beside the brotli ones; docs/slow-network.md "Audio units"). By format only, every game
// the same, no file name looked at:
// - RIFF WAVE sounds anywhere in a file — a .wav, or one stored as it is inside an archive (EA's .big, a .pak, …) —:
//   the data chunk of each whose format chunk says integer PCM (tag 1, or WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE with the PCM
//   subtype), 8 or 16 bits, mono or stereo (`scanWaves`, once per file version: the generator keeps the answer beside
//   the file's units);
// - a range of a file with no such sound (a raw sample bank without headers): tried as 16-bit mono, 16-bit stereo and
//   8-bit mono (`trialLayouts`) — a coding that is lossless whatever the bytes are, kept only when it beats the range's
//   brotli unit (the proof that the bytes are sampled sound is the coding's size).
import fs from 'node:fs';

const SCAN_CHUNK = 4 << 20;
/** the share of a unit that must be sound for its audio form to be tried (less cannot save the 5 % asked of it) */
export const PCM_SHARE_MIN = 0.15;
const PCM_GUID_TAIL = Buffer.from([0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0xaa, 0x00, 0x38, 0x9b, 0x71]);

/**
 * The PCM sample regions of the RIFF WAVE sound whose header starts at `h` (its first bytes, at file offset `at`), in a
 * file of `size` bytes: { start, end, bits, ch, next } (next: where the sound ends), or null (not one, or not PCM).
 */
export function parseWave(h, at, size) {
  if (h.length < 12 || h.toString('latin1', 0, 4) !== 'RIFF' || h.toString('latin1', 8, 12) !== 'WAVE') return null;
  const riffEnd = Math.min(size, at + 8 + h.readUInt32LE(4));
  let o = 12, fmt = null;
  while (o + 8 <= h.length && at + o + 8 <= riffEnd) {
    const id = h.toString('latin1', o, o + 4), n = h.readUInt32LE(o + 4);
    if (id === 'fmt ' && o + 8 + 16 <= h.length) {
      let tag = h.readUInt16LE(o + 8);
      const ch = h.readUInt16LE(o + 10), align = h.readUInt16LE(o + 20), bits = h.readUInt16LE(o + 22);
      if (tag === 0xfffe && n >= 40 && o + 8 + 40 <= h.length && h.subarray(o + 8 + 26, o + 8 + 40).equals(PCM_GUID_TAIL)) tag = h.readUInt16LE(o + 8 + 24);
      fmt = tag === 1 && (bits === 8 || bits === 16) && (ch === 1 || ch === 2) && align === (bits >> 3) * ch ? { bits, ch } : false;
    } else if (id === 'data') {
      if (!fmt) return null;
      const start = at + o + 8, frame = (fmt.bits >> 3) * fmt.ch;
      const end = start + Math.floor((Math.min(riffEnd, start + n) - start) / frame) * frame;
      return end > start ? { start, end, bits: fmt.bits, ch: fmt.ch, next: Math.max(end, riffEnd) } : null;
    }
    o += 8 + n + (n & 1);
  }
  return null;
}

/** Every PCM region of the RIFF WAVE sounds in file `file` ([{ start, end, bits, ch }], in file order): reads it whole. */
export function scanWaves(file) {
  const fd = fs.openSync(file, 'r');
  try {
    const size = fs.fstatSync(fd).size, buf = Buffer.alloc(SCAN_CHUNK + 3), head = Buffer.alloc(4096), out = [];
    let at = 0, keep = 0; // (keep: the last 3 bytes of the previous chunk, a 'RIFF' across the boundary)
    while (at < size) {
      const n = fs.readSync(fd, buf, keep, Math.min(SCAN_CHUNK, size - at), at);
      if (n <= 0) break;
      const base = at - keep, len = keep + n;
      const view = buf.subarray(0, len);
      let i = 0, skipTo = -1;
      for (;;) {
        i = view.indexOf('RIFF', i, 'latin1');
        if (i < 0) break;
        const off = base + i;
        if (off >= skipTo) {
          const hn = fs.readSync(fd, head, 0, 4096, off), w = parseWave(head.subarray(0, hn), off, size);
          if (w) { out.push({ start: w.start, end: w.end, bits: w.bits, ch: w.ch }); skipTo = w.next; }
        }
        i++;
      }
      at += n;
      if (skipTo > at) { // (inside a sound: on after it)
        at = skipTo; keep = 0; continue;
      }
      keep = Math.min(3, len); buf.copy(buf, 0, len - keep, len);
    }
    return out;
  } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); }
}

/** the regions of `waves` inside [start, end), relative to start, each starting on a sample frame: [{ at, len, bits, ch }] */
export function regionsIn(waves, start, end) {
  const out = [];
  for (const w of waves) {
    if (w.end <= start || w.start >= end) continue;
    const frame = (w.bits >> 3) * w.ch;
    let a = Math.max(w.start, start); a += (frame - ((a - w.start) % frame)) % frame;
    const b = Math.min(w.end, end);
    if (b - a >= frame) out.push({ at: a - start, len: Math.floor((b - a) / frame) * frame, bits: w.bits, ch: w.ch });
  }
  return out;
}

/** the layouts a range without sound headers is tried as (see the header) */
export const trialLayouts = (len) => [{ bits: 16, ch: 1 }, { bits: 16, ch: 2 }, { bits: 8, ch: 1 }].map((l) => ({ at: 0, len, ...l }));

/**
 * A quick estimate of the coded bytes of b as `layout` (order-2 prediction, Rice cost from each 1024 samples' mean),
 * to try only the layouts that may pay: bytes.
 */
export function estimateCoded(b, layout) {
  const { bits, ch } = layout, bps = bits >> 3, frame = bps * ch, frames = Math.floor(b.length / frame);
  let total = 0;
  for (let c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
    let x1 = 0, x2 = 0, sum = 0, cnt = 0;
    for (let f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
      const p = f * frame + c * bps, x = bits === 8 ? b[p] - 128 : ((b[p] | (b[p + 1] << 8)) << 16) >> 16;
      if (f >= 2) { const r = x - 2 * x1 + x2; sum += r < 0 ? -2 * r - 1 : 2 * r; cnt++; }
      x2 = x1; x1 = x;
      if (cnt === 1024 || f === frames - 1) { if (cnt) { const m = sum / cnt; total += cnt * ((m > 1 ? Math.log2(m) : 0) + 1.6); } sum = 0; cnt = 0; }
    }
  }
  return Math.ceil(total / 8);
}

/**
 * The layout a range without sound headers is coded as (bytes `b`; `wire`: its brotli unit's wire bytes), or null:
 * the most promising of trialLayouts by estimateCoded, when it may beat brotli — the estimate runs 5-18 % above the
 * coding's size on sampled sound (Vice City's sfx.RAW blocks), so it is asked to be under wire / 0.85.
 */
export function trialRegion(b, wire) {
  const best = trialLayouts(b.length).map((l) => [l, estimateCoded(b, l)]).sort((x, y) => x[1] - y[1])[0];
  return best[1] * TRIAL_ESTIMATE_SLACK < wire ? best[0] : null;
}
const TRIAL_ESTIMATE_SLACK = 0.85;

```

`src/host/perf-record.js`:

```js
// Passive session performance records (docs/real-machine-bench.md "Passive session records"): every runtime's page —
// the Windows games' (src/host/web/main.js), the browser ports' (GoldSrc, re3, OpenMW) — measures its normal play
// sessions the same way and sends the same compact record (`event: "perf"`): per minute of play (a phase change starts
// a new entry) the frame rate, the frame-time percentiles, the frames over 40 / 100 ms, the work vs the wait per frame,
// the GPU time, the game data's waits; the session's totals — with what its data waits were for (the files, the
// engine's own stops, the announced reads, the background's producers: compactDataSum); the machine; the host timing
// probe once. Hidden time is
// counted apart, its frames left out. This module is the recording and the record's validation (the server's), with
// no DOM: the page's side is src/host/web/perf-page.js.
import { HIST_N, histAddSparse, histBucket, histQuantile, histSparse } from '../core/frame-acct.js';

export const PERF_VERSION = 1;
/** a record every RECORD_MS of the session (and one at its end), one entry per MINUTE_MS */
export const RECORD_MS = 120000, MINUTE_MS = 60000;
/** at most this many records a session (5 hours of play at one per 2 min), entries a record */
export const MAX_RECORDS = 150, MAX_ENTRIES = 12;
/** a phase change closes the current entry once it holds this much time (shorter: it takes the new phase) */
export const MIN_SPLIT_MS = 5000;
/** a record's size limit (the server refuses larger ones; the page trims before) */
export const PERF_MAX_BYTES = 24 * 1024;
/** frames longer than these are counted (ms) */
export const SLOW_A = 40, SLOW_B = 100;
export const RUNTIMES = ['win32', 'goldsrc', 'openmw', 're3'];

const r1 = (v) => Math.round(v * 10) / 10;
const r2 = (v) => Math.round(v * 100) / 100;
/** a quantile of a histogram, rounded to 0.1 ms (the open bucket's: its lower bound, 5000) */
const hq = (h, q, max) => { const v = histQuantile(h, q, max); return v === null ? null : v === Infinity ? 5000 : r1(v); };
const addTo = (into, o, k = 1) => { for (const [n, v] of Object.entries(o ?? {})) if (Number.isFinite(v)) into[n] = (into[n] ?? 0) + v * k; };
/** the largest `top` entries of `o` (scaled, rounded to 0.01, those under `min` dropped) */
const topOf = (o, top, scale = 1, min = 0.05) => {
  const e = Object.entries(o).map(([k, v]) => [k, r2(v * scale)]).filter(([, v]) => v >= min).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, top);
  return e.length ? Object.fromEntries(e) : null;
};
/** a summary's file paths: at most this many characters (their ends kept), this many files */
export const PATH_MAX = 160, TOP_FILES = 3, TOP_BG = 12;
const pathOf = (p) => (p.length > PATH_MAX ? p.slice(-PATH_MAX) : p);
const grow = (a, b) => (b === undefined || b === null ? 0 : a === undefined || a === null || b < a ? b : b - a);

/**
 * A session's data attribution (the page's `data().sum`, perf-page.js portDataSummary), compact for the record's totals:
 * `files` the TOP_FILES files waited for most, [path, ms, waits] (the shared game data's fileWaits, { path: [waits, ms] });
 * `blocked` the engine's own count of its stops for its files when it keeps one ({ count, ms, max, files: ms by path }:
 * { n, ms, max, top: [path, ms] x TOP_FILES }); `want` its waits for its announced reads (wantWaits, wantWaitMs,
 * wantTimeouts: { n, ms, to }); `bg` the background's bytes by producer (NetLink bgBy: { reason: [requests, wire KiB,
 * KiB begun during a load] }, the TOP_BG largest). Parts without anything are left out; null when none is left.
 */
export function compactDataSum(sum) {
  if (!sum || typeof sum !== 'object') return null;
  const out = {}, ms = (v) => Math.round(Number(v) || 0), top = (o, f) => Object.entries(o ?? {}).map(f).filter((e) => e[1] > 0).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, TOP_FILES);
  const files = top(sum.files, ([k, v]) => [pathOf(k), ms(v?.[1]), Math.round(Number(v?.[0]) || 0)]);
  if (files.length) out.files = files;
  const b = sum.blocked;
  if (b && b.count > 0) out.blocked = { n: Math.round(b.count), ms: ms(b.ms), max: ms(b.max), top: top(b.files, ([k, v]) => [pathOf(k), ms(v)]) };
  if (sum.wantWaits > 0) out.want = { n: Math.round(sum.wantWaits), ms: ms(sum.wantWaitMs), to: Math.round(sum.wantTimeouts ?? 0) };
  const bg = Object.entries(sum.bgBy ?? {}).filter(([k, v]) => KEY.test(k) && v && v.wire > 0).sort((x, y) => y[1].wire - x[1].wire).slice(0, TOP_BG)
    .map(([k, v]) => [k, [Math.round(v.requests ?? 0), Math.round(v.wire / 1024), Math.round((v.inLoad ?? 0) / 1024)]]);
  if (bg.length) out.bg = Object.fromEntries(bg);
  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : null;
}

/** Frames and time of one stretch (an entry, or the session's totals). */
class Acc {
  constructor(t0 = 0, ph = null) {
    this.t0 = t0; this.ph = ph; this.vis = 0; this.hid = 0; this.n = 0; this.h = new Array(HIST_N).fill(0); this.max = 0; this.fa = 0; this.fb = 0;
    this.dtSum = 0; this.workSum = 0; this.workN = 0; this.workDt = 0; this.cats = {}; this.catN = 0; this.slow = {};
    this.gpu = null; this.data = null; // (the cumulative counters at the start: differences at the end)
  }
  frame(dt, work) {
    this.n++; this.h[histBucket(dt)]++; this.dtSum += dt; if (dt > this.max) this.max = dt;
    if (dt > SLOW_A) this.fa++; if (dt > SLOW_B) this.fb++;
    if (work !== null && work !== undefined && work >= 0) { this.workSum += Math.min(work, dt); this.workN++; this.workDt += dt; }
  }
  interval(a, dtMs) {
    const n = a.frames ?? 0; if (!n) return;
    this.n += n; this.dtSum += dtMs;
    if (a.h) histAddSparse(this.h, a.h); else this.h[histBucket(dtMs / n)] += n;
    if ((a.max ?? 0) > this.max) this.max = a.max;
    this.fa += a.s40 ?? 0; this.fb += a.s100 ?? 0;
    if (Number.isFinite(a.w)) { this.workSum += a.w * n; this.workN += n; this.workDt += dtMs; }
    if (a.c) { addTo(this.cats, a.c, n); this.catN += n; }
    addTo(this.slow, a.sc);
  }
}

/**
 * The recording of one session. The page calls `clock(now, visible, phase)` about every second (time, visibility,
 * phase), and either `frame(dtMs, workMs, dataMs)` for each frame shown (the ports: their frame meters) or
 * `interval(acct, dtMs)` for each stats interval (Win32: frame-acct.js FrameStats.takeInterval, ~0.5 s), and
 * `counters({ gpu, data })` with the cumulative GPU timer (gpu-probe.js stats.gpu) and game data waits ({ waits, ms },
 * and `sum` the session's attribution so far: compactDataSum, in the totals).
 * `take(now, final)` gives the record when one is due (or at the end).
 */
export class PerfRecorder {
  /** @param {{ header?: object, recordMs?: number, minuteMs?: number }} [o] */
  constructor(o = {}) {
    this.header = o.header ?? {}; this.recordMs = o.recordMs ?? RECORD_MS; this.minuteMs = o.minuteMs ?? MINUTE_MS;
    this.t0 = null; this.last = null; this.visible = true; this.phase = null;
    this.cur = null; this.done = []; this.dropped = 0; this.tot = new Acc(0); this.seq = 0; this.lastRecord = null; this.ended = false;
    this.gpuNow = null; this.dataNow = null; this.dataSum = null; this.dataSumSrc = null; this.probe = null; this.probeSent = false;
    this.slowFrames = {}; // (the ports' slow frames by cause, summed ms: added to the entry's `slow`)
  }
  /** The time since the last clock goes to the visible or the hidden time; entries close at minutes and phase changes. */
  clock(now, visible = true, phase = this.phase) {
    if (this.t0 === null) { this.t0 = now; this.last = now; this.lastRecord = now; }
    const el = Math.max(0, now - this.last); this.last = now;
    this.cur ??= this.open(now);
    if (this.visible) { this.cur.vis += el; this.tot.vis += el; } else { this.cur.hid += el; this.tot.hid += el; }
    this.visible = visible;
    if (phase !== this.phase) {
      this.phase = phase;
      if (this.cur.vis + this.cur.hid >= MIN_SPLIT_MS) this.close(now); else this.cur.ph = phase;
    }
    if (this.cur && now - (this.t0 + this.cur.t0) >= this.minuteMs) this.close(now);
  }
  open(now) { const a = new Acc(now - this.t0, this.phase); a.gpu = this.gpuNow; a.data = this.dataNow; return a; }
  close(now) {
    const c = this.cur; this.cur = this.open(now);
    if (!c || (!c.n && c.vis < 1000)) return; // (hidden, or nothing shown: no entry — the totals keep its time)
    this.done.push(this.entry(c));
    if (this.done.length > MAX_ENTRIES) { this.done.shift(); this.dropped++; }
  }
  /** One shown frame (dt: since the previous one; work: the engine's part, null unknown; data: its waits for the game data). */
  frame(dtMs, workMs = null, dataMs = 0) {
    if (!this.visible || !(dtMs > 0) || this.t0 === null) return;
    this.cur ??= this.open(this.last);
    this.cur.frame(dtMs, workMs); this.tot.frame(dtMs, workMs);
    if (dtMs > SLOW_A) {
      // (a slow frame's time by cause: the game data waited for, the engine's other work, the rest — the browser,
      // the GPU, the compositor)
      const data = Math.min(dtMs, Math.max(0, dataMs || 0)), work = workMs === null || workMs === undefined ? null : Math.max(0, Math.min(dtMs, workMs) - data);
      const s = { data, ...(work === null ? { unknown: dtMs - data } : { work, other: Math.max(0, dtMs - data - work) }) };
      addTo(this.cur.slow, s); addTo(this.tot.slow, s);
    }
  }
  /** One stats interval of the frame accounting (frames, h, s40, s100, max, w, c, sc). */
  interval(a, dtMs) {
    if (!this.visible || !a || this.t0 === null) return;
    this.cur ??= this.open(this.last);
    this.cur.interval(a, dtMs); this.tot.interval(a, dtMs);
  }
  /** The cumulative counters now (GPU timer, game data waits). */
  counters({ gpu, data } = {}) {
    if (gpu !== undefined) this.gpuNow = gpu ? { state: gpu.state ?? null, frames: gpu.frames ?? 0, ms: gpu.ms ?? 0, lost: gpu.lost ?? 0, hist: gpu.hist ? Array.from(gpu.hist) : null } : null;
    if (data !== undefined) this.dataNow = data ? { waits: data.waits ?? 0, ms: data.ms ?? 0 } : null;
    // (what the waits were for: the source kept, compacted only when a record takes it — take() follows counters() in the
    // same task, so the same values; compacting every clock tick sorted every file waited for once a second)
    if (data && 'sum' in data) this.dataSumSrc = data;
    else if (data !== undefined) this.takeDataSum(); // (the source gone: what it said last kept, as when compacted at each tick)
    if (this.tot.gpu === null && this.gpuNow) this.tot.gpu = { state: this.gpuNow.state, frames: 0, ms: 0, hist: this.gpuNow.hist ? new Array(this.gpuNow.hist.length).fill(0) : null };
    if (this.tot.data === null && this.dataNow) this.tot.data = { waits: 0, ms: 0 };
  }
  /** The host timing probe's results (timing-probe.js runTimingProbe), sent once. */
  setProbe(p) { this.probe = compactProbe(p); }
  /** A stretch as a record's entry (or the totals: `total`). */
  entry(c, total = false) {
    const n = c.n, out = { t: Math.round(c.t0 / 1000), ph: c.ph ?? null, s: r1(c.vis / 1000), hid: r1(c.hid / 1000), n,
      fps: c.vis > 0 ? r1(n / (c.vis / 1000)) : 0 };
    if (n) {
      Object.assign(out, { p50: hq(c.h, 0.5, c.max), p90: hq(c.h, 0.9, c.max), p99: hq(c.h, 0.99, c.max), max: Math.round(c.max), f40: c.fa, f100: c.fb });
      if (c.workN) { out.work = r2(c.workSum / c.workN); out.wait = r2(Math.max(0, (c.workDt - c.workSum) / c.workN)); }
      if (c.catN) out.cats = topOf(c.cats, 8, 1 / c.catN);
      const slow = topOf(c.slow, 6, 1, 1); if (slow) out.slow = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(slow).map(([k, v]) => [k, Math.round(v)]));
    }
    // GPU time per frame over the stretch (the timer's sampled windows)
    const g0 = c.gpu, g1 = this.gpuNow;
    if (g1 && g1.state === 'on') {
      const f = total ? c.gpu?.frames ?? 0 : grow(g0?.frames, g1.frames), ms = total ? c.gpu?.ms ?? 0 : grow(g0?.ms, g1.ms);
      const h = total ? c.gpu?.hist : g1.hist ? g1.hist.map((v, i) => grow(g0?.hist?.[i], v)) : null;
      out.gpu = f > 0 ? { n: f, mean: r2(ms / f), p50: h ? hq(h, 0.5, Infinity) : null, p90: h ? hq(h, 0.9, Infinity) : null, p99: h ? hq(h, 0.99, Infinity) : null } : { n: 0 };
      if (!total) { const lost = grow(g0?.lost, g1.lost); if (lost) out.gpu.lost = lost; } // (queries whose result never came)
    } else if (g1) out.gpu = { state: g1.state ?? 'none' };
    // the game data's waits (reads the engine waited for)
    const d0 = c.data, d1 = this.dataNow;
    if (d1) out.data = total ? { n: c.data?.waits ?? 0, ms: Math.round(c.data?.ms ?? 0) } : { n: grow(d0?.waits, d1.waits), ms: Math.round(grow(d0?.ms, d1.ms)) };
    if (total && this.dataSum) out.data = { ...(out.data ?? { n: 0, ms: 0 }), ...this.dataSum }; // (what the session's waits were for)
    if (total) out.h = histSparse(c.h);
    return out;
  }
  /** The totals' GPU and data parts follow the counters (added at each record). */
  syncTotals() {
    const t = this.tot, g = this.gpuNow, d = this.dataNow;
    if (g && t.gpu) { t.gpu.frames += grow(t.gpuBase?.frames, g.frames); t.gpu.ms += grow(t.gpuBase?.ms, g.ms); if (g.hist && t.gpu.hist) g.hist.forEach((v, i) => { t.gpu.hist[i] += grow(t.gpuBase?.hist?.[i], v); }); t.gpu.state = g.state; }
    if (d && t.data) { t.data.waits += grow(t.dataBase?.waits, d.waits); t.data.ms += grow(t.dataBase?.ms, d.ms); }
    t.gpuBase = g; t.dataBase = d;
  }
  /** The kept source's attribution compacted into `dataSum` (the last one known kept: the session's so far). */
  takeDataSum() {
    if (!this.dataSumSrc) return;
    const sum = this.dataSumSrc.sum; this.dataSumSrc = null;
    if (sum !== undefined) this.dataSum = compactDataSum(sum);
  }
  /** A record is due (RECORD_MS since the last one). */
  due(now) { return !this.ended && this.t0 !== null && this.seq < MAX_RECORDS && now - this.lastRecord >= this.recordMs; }
  /**
   * The record of the entries since the last one, with the session's totals so far; null when none is due (`final`:
   * the session's end — the current entry closed, then no more).
   */
  take(now, final = false) {
    if (this.ended || this.t0 === null) return null;
    if (!final && !this.due(now)) return null;
    if (final) { this.clock(now, this.visible, this.phase); this.close(now); this.ended = true; }
    if (final && !this.seq && !this.tot.n && !this.done.length) return null; // (a page that never showed a frame: nothing to send)
    else if (!this.done.length) { this.lastRecord = now; return null; } // (nothing new to say: a hidden tab sends nothing)
    this.lastRecord = now; this.syncTotals();
    this.takeDataSum();
    const rec = { event: 'perf', v: PERF_VERSION, ...this.header, seq: this.seq++, final: !!final,
      len: Math.round((now - this.t0) / 1000), vis: r1(this.tot.vis / 1000), hid: r1(this.tot.hid / 1000),
      mins: this.done.splice(0), tot: this.entry(this.tot, true) };
    if (this.dropped) { rec.dropped = this.dropped; this.dropped = 0; }
    if (this.probe && (!this.probeSent || final)) { rec.probe = this.probe; this.probeSent = true; }
    return fitRecord(rec);
  }
}

/** A record within PERF_MAX_BYTES: the totals' histogram dropped first, then the oldest entries. */
export function fitRecord(rec, max = PERF_MAX_BYTES - 2048) { // (room for the machine, added after)
  const size = () => JSON.stringify(rec).length;
  if (size() <= max) return rec;
  if (rec.tot) delete rec.tot.h;
  while (rec.mins.length && size() > max) { rec.mins.shift(); rec.dropped = (rec.dropped ?? 0) + 1; }
  return rec;
}

const PROBE_KINDS = ['atomicsWait1', 'atomicsWait1Timer', 'setTimeout0', 'setTimeout1', 'messageHop'];
/** The timing probe's results, compact: { kind: [p50, p90, max] }, the battery. */
export function compactProbe(p) {
  if (!p) return null;
  const out = {};
  for (const k of PROBE_KINDS) if (p[k]) out[k] = [p[k].p50, p[k].p90, p[k].max];
  if (p.battery) out.battery = { charging: !!p.battery.charging, level: p.battery.level };
  if (p.injected) out.injected = p.injected;
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the server's validation
const num = (v, max = 1e9) => (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0 && v <= max ? v : undefined);
const int = (v, max = 1e9) => (Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0 && v <= max ? v : undefined);
const str = (v, max = 120) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v.slice(0, max) : undefined);
const KEY = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,23}$/;
/** an object of numbers (categories): at most 24 keys */
const numMap = (o) => {
  if (!o || typeof o !== 'object' || Array.isArray(o)) return undefined;
  const e = Object.entries(o).filter(([k, v]) => KEY.test(k) && num(v) !== undefined).slice(0, 24);
  return e.length ? Object.fromEntries(e) : undefined;
};
const pick = (o, spec) => {
  const out = {};
  for (const [k, f] of Object.entries(spec)) { const v = f(o?.[k]); if (v !== undefined) out[k] = v; }
  return out;
};
const nullable = (f) => (v) => (v === null ? null : f(v));
const gpuPart = (g) => {
  if (!g || typeof g !== 'object') return undefined;
  if (typeof g.state === 'string') return { state: g.state.slice(0, 16) };
  return pick(g, { n: (v) => int(v), lost: (v) => int(v), mean: (v) => num(v, 1e5), p50: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e5)), p90: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e5)), p99: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e5)) });
};
const hist = (h) => (Array.isArray(h) && h.length <= 2 * HIST_N && h.every((x) => Number.isInteger(x) && x >= 0 && x < 1e9) ? h : undefined);
const ENTRY = {
  t: (v) => int(v, 1e7), ph: nullable((v) => str(v, 24)), s: (v) => num(v, 1e7), hid: (v) => num(v, 1e7), n: (v) => int(v), fps: (v) => num(v, 1e4),
  p50: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e6)), p90: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e6)), p99: nullable((v) => num(v, 1e6)), max: (v) => num(v, 1e7), f40: (v) => int(v), f100: (v) => int(v),
  work: (v) => num(v, 1e6), wait: (v) => num(v, 1e6), cats: numMap, slow: numMap, gpu: gpuPart,
  data: (d) => (d && typeof d === 'object' ? pick(d, { n: (v) => int(v), ms: (v) => num(v) }) : undefined),
};
const path = (v) => (typeof v === 'string' && v ? pathOf(v) : undefined);
/** [path, ms] or [path, ms, waits] lists, TOP_FILES at most */
const fileList = (n) => (v) => {
  if (!Array.isArray(v)) return undefined;
  const e = v.slice(0, TOP_FILES).filter((x) => Array.isArray(x) && x.length === n && path(x[0]) && x.slice(1).every((y) => int(y) !== undefined)).map((x) => [path(x[0]), ...x.slice(1)]);
  return e.length ? e : undefined;
};
/** the totals' data: an entry's, with the session's attribution (compactDataSum) */
const TOT_DATA = { n: (v) => int(v), ms: (v) => num(v), files: fileList(3),
  blocked: (b) => (b && typeof b === 'object' ? pick(b, { n: (v) => int(v), ms: (v) => int(v), max: (v) => int(v), top: fileList(2) }) : undefined),
  want: (w) => (w && typeof w === 'object' ? pick(w, { n: (v) => int(v), ms: (v) => int(v), to: (v) => int(v) }) : undefined),
  bg: (o) => {
    if (!o || typeof o !== 'object' || Array.isArray(o)) return undefined;
    const e = Object.entries(o).filter(([k, v]) => KEY.test(k) && Array.isArray(v) && v.length === 3 && v.every((y) => int(y) !== undefined)).slice(0, TOP_BG);
    return e.length ? Object.fromEntries(e) : undefined;
  } };
const TIMES = (v) => (Array.isArray(v) && v.length === 3 && v.every((x) => num(x, 1e6) !== undefined) ? v : undefined);
const PROBE = Object.fromEntries([...PROBE_KINDS.map((k) => [k, TIMES]), ['battery', (b) => (b && typeof b === 'object' ? { charging: !!b.charging, level: num(b.level, 1) ?? null } : undefined)], ['injected', (v) => num(v, 1000)]]);
const bool = (v) => (typeof v === 'boolean' ? v : undefined);
/** the browser's storage (src/host/web/storage-persist.js: persisted, its usage and quota in MiB, persist() asked) */
const STORAGE = { persisted: nullable(bool), usageMB: nullable((v) => int(v, 1 << 30)), quotaMB: nullable((v) => int(v, 1 << 30)), asked: bool };
const ENV = { gpu: (v) => str(v, 200), gpuVendor: (v) => str(v, 120), gpuClass: (v) => str(v, 16), cores: (v) => int(v, 4096), memGB: (v) => num(v, 4096), ua: (v) => str(v, 400), screen: (v) => str(v, 40),
  storage: (v) => (v && typeof v === 'object' ? pick(v, STORAGE) : undefined) };

/**
 * A perf record as received (the page's JSON), checked and rebuilt from its known fields only (unknown ones dropped,
 * strings cut, numbers bounded): { ok: true, rec } or { ok: false, error }.
 */
export function sanitizePerfRecord(r) {
  if (!r || typeof r !== 'object' || r.event !== 'perf') return { ok: false, error: 'not a perf record' };
  if (r.v !== PERF_VERSION) return { ok: false, error: 'unknown version' };
  if (typeof r.session !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,40}$/.test(r.session)) return { ok: false, error: 'bad session' };
  if (!RUNTIMES.includes(r.runtime)) return { ok: false, error: 'bad runtime' };
  const seq = int(r.seq, MAX_RECORDS); if (seq === undefined) return { ok: false, error: 'bad seq' };
  if (!Array.isArray(r.mins) || r.mins.length > MAX_ENTRIES) return { ok: false, error: 'bad entries' };
  if (!r.tot || typeof r.tot !== 'object') return { ok: false, error: 'no totals' };
  const rec = {
    event: 'perf', v: PERF_VERSION, session: r.session, game: typeof r.game === 'string' ? r.game.slice(0, 120) : null, runtime: r.runtime,
    ...pick(r, { version: nullable((v) => str(v, 80)), build: nullable((v) => str(v, 80)), tier: nullable((v) => str(v, 16)), bench: nullable((v) => str(v, 60)) }),
    seq, final: r.final === true, ...pick(r, { len: (v) => num(v, 1e7), vis: (v) => num(v, 1e7), hid: (v) => num(v, 1e7), dropped: (v) => int(v) }),
    mins: r.mins.map((e) => pick(e, ENTRY)),
    tot: { ...pick(r.tot, ENTRY), ...(r.tot.data && typeof r.tot.data === 'object' ? { data: pick(r.tot.data, TOT_DATA) } : {}), ...(hist(r.tot.h) ? { h: r.tot.h } : {}) },
  };
  if (r.env && typeof r.env === 'object') rec.env = pick(r.env, ENV);
  if (r.probe && typeof r.probe === 'object') rec.probe = pick(r.probe, PROBE);
  return { ok: true, rec };
}

```

`src/host/perf-summary.js`:

```js
// Frame summaries over a window of the worker's stats messages (~0.5 s each): the periodic `summary` telemetry records
// and the per-phase measurements of the bench mode (docs/real-machine-bench.md). Built from what the stats already
// carry — the frame accounting of each interval (frame-acct.js FrameStats.takeInterval: slow-frame counts, frame-time
// histogram, mean time by category) and cumulative counters (draws, GPU time, GL calls, render worker waits) — so the
// page does no work per frame. No dependency on the DOM (unit tests).
import { HIST_N, histAddSparse, histQuantile, histSparse, histBucket } from '../core/frame-acct.js';

/** a counter's growth, a counter that restarted (a new device) counting from zero */
const grow = (a, b) => (b === undefined || b === null ? 0 : a === undefined || a === null || b < a ? b : b - a);
const r1 = (v) => Math.round(v * 10) / 10;
const r2 = (v) => Math.round(v * 100) / 100;
/** a quantile of a histogram, rounded to 0.1 ms (the upper bound of a bucket, or the window's maximum) */
const hq = (h, q, max) => { const v = histQuantile(h, q, max); return v === null ? null : r1(v); };

/** The cumulative counters of a stats message the window takes differences of. */
function counters(m) {
  const d = m?.d3d, g = m?.gl, gpu = d?.gpu, gc = d?.glCalls;
  return {
    d3dFrames: d?.frames, draws: d?.draws,
    gpuState: gpu?.state ?? null, gpuFrames: gpu?.frames, gpuMs: gpu?.ms, gpuOver33: gpu?.over33, gpuDisjoint: gpu?.disjoint, gpuLost: gpu?.lost, gpuHist: gpu?.hist ? Array.from(gpu.hist) : null, gpuMax: gpu?.max,
    glState: gc?.state ?? null, glFrames: gc?.frames, glCalls: gc?.calls, glDraws: gc?.draws,
    rwWaitMs: g?.gpuWaitMs, rwFenceMs: g?.fenceMs, rwFrameMs: g?.frameMs, rwReplayMs: g?.replayMs, rwReadbackMs: g?.readbackMs,
    hw: m?.hostWait ?? null, // (core/host-wait.js totals: the worker's host waits, how late they ended, the spins)
  };
}

export class PerfWindow {
  constructor() { this.base = null; this.last = null; this.reset(); }
  reset() {
    this.seconds = 0; this.frames = 0; this.s33 = 0; this.s40 = 0; this.s50 = 0; this.s100 = 0; this.max = 0;
    this.hist = new Array(HIST_N).fill(0); this.work = 0; this.cats = {}; this.slowCats = {}; this.worst = null;
    this.busy = 0; this.mips = 0; this.visible = 0; this.fullscreen = 0; this.samples = 0; this.status = null; this.t0 = null; this.t1 = null;
    this.base = this.last;
  }
  /**
   * One stats message. `extra`: what the page knows of that moment ({ t: Date.now(), visible, fullscreen, status }).
   * @param {any} m
   */
  add(m, extra = {}) {
    const dt = m.dt ?? 0.5, a = m.acct;
    this.samples++; this.seconds += dt; this.t0 ??= extra.t ?? null; this.t1 = extra.t ?? null;
    if (extra.visible !== false) this.visible += dt; if (extra.fullscreen) this.fullscreen += dt; this.status = extra.status ?? this.status;
    if (m.render) this.renderMode = m.render; // (the rendering actually used: 'worker', 'thread', 'inline', ..., 'none')
    this.busy += (m.busy ?? 0) * dt; this.mips += (m.mips ?? 0) * dt;
    if (a) {
      const n = a.frames ?? 0;
      this.frames += n; this.s33 += a.s33 ?? 0; this.s40 += a.s40 ?? 0; this.s50 += a.s50 ?? 0; this.s100 += a.s100 ?? 0;
      if ((a.max ?? 0) > this.max) this.max = a.max;
      histAddSparse(this.hist, a.h);
      // (an interval without a histogram — an older worker — counts its frames at the interval's mean duration)
      if (!a.h && n) this.hist[histBucket(dt * 1000 / n)] += n;
      this.work += (a.w ?? 0) * n;
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(a.c ?? {})) this.cats[k] = (this.cats[k] ?? 0) + v * n;
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(a.sc ?? {})) this.slowCats[k] = (this.slowCats[k] ?? 0) + v;
      if (a.wf && (!this.worst || a.wf[0] > this.worst[0])) this.worst = a.wf;
    }
    const c = counters(m);
    this.base ??= c; this.last = c;
  }
  /**
   * The window as a compact record, then a new window begins (its counters from this one's end). null when the
   * window holds no sample.
   */
  take() {
    if (!this.samples) return null;
    const b = this.base ?? {}, l = this.last ?? {}, n = this.frames, sec = this.seconds, min = sec / 60;
    const per = (x) => (min > 0 ? Math.round(x / min * 10) / 10 : 0);
    const out = {
      seconds: r1(sec), frames: n, fps: sec > 0 ? r1(n / sec) : 0,
      s33: this.s33, s40: this.s40, s50: this.s50, s100: this.s100, per33: per(this.s33), per50: per(this.s50), per100: per(this.s100),
      dt: n ? { p50: hq(this.hist, 0.5, this.max), p90: hq(this.hist, 0.9, this.max), p99: hq(this.hist, 0.99, this.max), max: Math.round(this.max) } : null,
      work: n ? r1(this.work / n) : null,
      cats: n ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(this.cats).map(([k, v]) => [k, r2(v / n)]).filter(([, v]) => v >= 0.05).sort((x, y) => y[1] - x[1])) : null,
      slowCats: Object.keys(this.slowCats).length ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(this.slowCats).map(([k, v]) => [k, Math.round(v)]).sort((x, y) => y[1] - x[1])) : null,
      worst: this.worst, h: histSparse(this.hist),
      busy: sec > 0 ? Math.round(this.busy / sec) : null, mips: sec > 0 ? Math.round(this.mips / sec) : null,
      visible: sec > 0 ? r2(this.visible / sec) : null, fullscreen: sec > 0 ? r2(this.fullscreen / sec) : null, status: this.status, renderMode: this.renderMode ?? null,
    };
    // Direct3D draw calls per presented Direct3D frame
    const d3dFrames = grow(b.d3dFrames, l.d3dFrames), draws = grow(b.draws, l.draws);
    out.d3dFrames = d3dFrames; out.drawsPerFrame = d3dFrames > 0 ? r1(draws / d3dFrames) : null;
    // GPU time per frame (EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 windows: gpu-probe.js), or why there is none
    if (l.gpuState === 'on') {
      const f = grow(b.gpuFrames, l.gpuFrames), ms = grow(b.gpuMs, l.gpuMs);
      const h = l.gpuHist ? l.gpuHist.map((v, i) => grow(b.gpuHist?.[i], v)) : null;
      const max = (l.gpuMax ?? 0) > (b.gpuMax ?? 0) ? l.gpuMax : null; // (the cumulative maximum grew in this window: it is this window's)
      out.gpu = f > 0 ? { state: 'on', frames: f, mean: r2(ms / f), p50: h ? hq(h, 0.5, max ?? Infinity) : null, p90: h ? hq(h, 0.9, max ?? Infinity) : null, p99: h ? hq(h, 0.99, max ?? Infinity) : null, max: max !== null ? r1(max) : null, over33: grow(b.gpuOver33, l.gpuOver33), disjoint: grow(b.gpuDisjoint, l.gpuDisjoint), lost: grow(b.gpuLost, l.gpuLost), h: h ? histSparse(h) : null }
        : { state: 'on', frames: 0, disjoint: grow(b.gpuDisjoint, l.gpuDisjoint), lost: grow(b.gpuLost, l.gpuLost) };
    } else out.gpu = { state: l.gpuState ?? 'none' }; // ('unavailable': no timer query extension; 'none': no Direct3D device)
    // WebGL calls per frame (sampled windows)
    if (l.glState === 'on') { const f = grow(b.glFrames, l.glFrames); out.glCalls = f > 0 ? { frames: f, perFrame: r1(grow(b.glCalls, l.glCalls) / f), drawsPerFrame: r1(grow(b.glDraws, l.glDraws) / f) } : { frames: 0 }; }
    else out.glCalls = { state: l.glState ?? 'none' };
    // render worker: the emulator's waits for it and its replay time, ms per frame
    if (l.rwWaitMs !== undefined && n > 0) out.render = { waitMs: r2(grow(b.rwWaitMs, l.rwWaitMs) / n), fenceMs: r2(grow(b.rwFenceMs, l.rwFenceMs) / n), frameMs: r2(grow(b.rwFrameMs, l.rwFrameMs) / n), replayMs: r2(grow(b.rwReplayMs, l.rwReplayMs) / n), readbackMs: r2(grow(b.rwReadbackMs, l.rwReadbackMs) / n) };
    // the emulator's host waits (core/host-wait.js): how late they woke (ms per wait), spin time per frame, the estimate
    if (l.hw && n > 0) { const w = grow(b.hw?.waits, l.hw.waits), sp = grow(b.hw?.spinMs, l.hw.spinMs); out.hostWait = { waits: w, overMean: w > 0 ? r2(grow(b.hw?.overMs, l.hw.overMs) / w) : 0, lateMsPerFrame: r2(grow(b.hw?.lateMs, l.hw.lateMs) / n), spinMsPerFrame: r2(sp / n), est: l.hw.est, timerEst: l.hw.timerEst }; }
    this.reset();
    return out;
  }
}

/**
 * Periodic summaries for telemetry: one record every `everyMs` of samples (~20 s), at most `cap` per session.
 * `add` returns the record when one is due.
 */
export class SummaryClock {
  constructor(everyMs = 20000, cap = 720) { this.everyMs = everyMs; this.cap = cap; this.sent = 0; this.window = new PerfWindow(); this.acc = 0; }
  add(m, extra = {}) {
    this.window.add(m, extra);
    this.acc += (m.dt ?? 0.5) * 1000;
    if (this.acc < this.everyMs) return null;
    this.acc = 0;
    const s = this.window.take();
    if (!s || this.sent >= this.cap) return null;
    this.sent++;
    return s;
  }
}

/** The compact form of a worker phase report (frame-acct.js FrameStats.phase) kept in bench records. */
export function compactPhase(ph) {
  if (!ph) return null;
  return {
    label: ph.label, frames: ph.frames ?? 0, seconds: ph.seconds ?? 0, fps: ph.fps ?? 0,
    slow33: ph.slow33 ?? 0, slow40: ph.slow40 ?? 0, slow50: ph.slow50 ?? 0, slow100: ph.slow100 ?? 0, per33: ph.per33 ?? 0, per40: ph.per40 ?? 0, per50: ph.per50 ?? 0, per100: ph.per100 ?? 0,
    slowPaced: ph.slowPaced ?? null,
    dt: ph.dt ?? null, work: ph.work ?? null, mean: ph.mean ?? null, slowMean: ph.slowMean ?? null, excessShares: ph.excessShares ?? null, hitches: ph.hitches ?? null,
    worst: (ph.worst ?? []).slice(0, 3),
    hostWait: compactHostWait(ph.hostWait, ph.frames ?? 0),
  };
}

/** A phase's host waits (core/host-wait.js HostWaiter.take), compact: late per wait, spin per frame, the estimates. */
export function compactHostWait(hw, frames) {
  if (!hw) return null;
  const w = hw.wait;
  return { waits: w?.waits ?? 0, overMean: w?.overMean ?? 0, overMax: w?.overMax ?? 0, lateMsPerFrame: w && frames ? r2(w.lateMs / frames) : 0, hist: w?.hist ?? null, spins: w?.spins ?? 0, spinMsPerFrame: w && frames ? r2(w.spinMs / frames) : 0, est: hw.est, timerEst: hw.timerEst, timerOverMean: hw.timer?.overMean ?? null, injected: hw.q || 0, adaptive: hw.adaptive ?? true };
}
```

`src/host/profile-seed.js`:

```js
// Shared first-launch profile ("profile seed"): some games spend a long time on their very first launch (no settings
// file yet: they measure the machine, build caches...) and skip that work once their settings exist. A session that
// starts with an empty emulated user profile (C:\Users\Player) records the small files the game wrote there by the
// time the player first acts on a screen of the game (a click, or typing), and reports them once the session has
// gone on playing; the server offers the set of files that enough distinct sessions reported identical to the next
// player whose profile is empty. Nothing typed by a player is in such a set (the snapshot comes before any typing),
// identical content across sessions means default settings rather than personal data, and the size limits keep out
// saves, previews and caches. Used by the page's worker (snapshot, seeding) and by the server (validation, storage).

/** Limits of a seed: per file, per set, file count, path length. */
export const SEED_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ fileMax: 64 * 1024, setMax: 128 * 1024, files: 32, pathMax: 240 });

/**
 * A profile-relative path a seed may hold: '/'-separated, plain components (no '.', '..', ':' or '\'), not under the
 * profile's Temp directory (the emulated %TEMP%: scratch files).
 */
export function seedPathOk(p, limits = SEED_LIMITS) {
  if (typeof p !== 'string' || !p || p.length > limits.pathMax) return false;
  const parts = p.split('/');
  if (parts.some((c) => !c || c === '.' || c === '..' || /[\\:*?"<>|\x00-\x1f]/.test(c) || c.trim() !== c)) return false;
  return parts.length > 1 ? parts[0].toLowerCase() !== 'temp' : true;
}

/**
 * The files of a seed among a profile's files ({path, data: Uint8Array}): eligible paths and sizes, sorted by path
 * (case-insensitively unique), within the set's size and count limits (smallest first when over). Empty: nothing to share.
 */
export function seedSelect(files, limits = SEED_LIMITS) {
  const seen = new Set(), ok = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    if (!f || !seedPathOk(f.path, limits) || !(f.data instanceof Uint8Array) || f.data.length > limits.fileMax) continue;
    const k = f.path.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(k)) continue;
    seen.add(k); ok.push(f);
  }
  ok.sort((a, b) => a.data.length - b.data.length || (a.path < b.path ? -1 : a.path > b.path ? 1 : 0));
  const out = []; let total = 0;
  for (const f of ok) { if (out.length >= limits.files || total + f.data.length > limits.setMax) break; out.push(f); total += f.data.length; }
  return out.sort((a, b) => (a.path.toLowerCase() < b.path.toLowerCase() ? -1 : 1));
}

/** Identity of a set of files (paths and bytes): two 32-bit FNV-1a lanes over each path, its length and its bytes. */
export function seedKey(files) {
  let h1 = 0x811c9dc5, h2 = 0x01000193 ^ 0x5bd1e995;
  const byte = (b) => { h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ b, 0x01000193); h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ b, 0x5bd1e995) ^ (h2 >>> 15); };
  const enc = new TextEncoder();
  for (const f of files) {
    for (const b of enc.encode(f.path.toLowerCase())) byte(b);
    byte(0); for (let s = 0; s < 32; s += 8) byte((f.data.length >>> s) & 0xff); byte(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < f.data.length; i++) byte(f.data[i]);
  }
  return (h1 >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0') + (h2 >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0') + files.length.toString(16);
}

/**
 * Canonical sets (made by an operator, tools/profile-seed-make.mjs): per manifest, at most one set per game language
 * that the server offers before any learned one — whatever the sessions report. File name in the learn directory.
 */
export const seedCanonFile = (manifest) => `seedcanon-${String(manifest).replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, '_')}.json`;

/**
 * The valid sets of a canonical file's JSON ({ v: 1, sets: [{ lang, files: [[path, base64]], at?, note? }] }): each
 * within the limits (as a reported set: seedSelect keeps every file), one per language (the first; lowercased). Each comes back as
 * { lang, key, files: [[path, base64]], at, note }.
 */
export function canonSets(json, limits = SEED_LIMITS) {
  const out = [], langs = new Set();
  for (const s of Array.isArray(json?.sets) ? json.sets : []) {
    // (the language lowercased, as the server looks it up — server.js seedLang: a manifest may declare 'pt-BR')
    const lang = typeof s?.lang === 'string' && /^[A-Za-z-]{0,16}$/.test(s.lang) ? s.lang.toLowerCase() : null;
    if (lang === null || langs.has(lang) || !Array.isArray(s.files)) continue;
    const files = [];
    for (const f of s.files) { const data = Array.isArray(f) ? fromBase64(f[1]) : null; if (data && seedPathOk(f[0], limits)) files.push({ path: f[0], data }); else { files.length = 0; break; } }
    const sel = seedSelect(files, limits);
    if (!sel.length || sel.length !== s.files.length) continue;
    langs.add(lang);
    out.push({ lang, key: seedKey(sel), files: sel.map((f) => [f.path, toBase64(f.data)]), at: Number(s.at) || 0, note: typeof s.note === 'string' ? s.note.slice(0, 200) : '' });
  }
  return out;
}

/** bytes -> base64 (browsers and Node: btoa) */
export function toBase64(d) {
  let bin = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 0x8000) bin += String.fromCharCode.apply(null, d.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));
  return btoa(bin);
}
/** base64 -> bytes, or null when malformed */
export function fromBase64(s) {
  if (typeof s !== 'string') return null;
  try { return Uint8Array.from(atob(s), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0)); } catch { return null; }
}

/**
 * The worker's side: watches a session that started with an empty profile and decides when to snapshot and report.
 * `files()` lists the profile's files ({path, data}). `input` is called with each click and each printable character
 * as the page delivers them, before the game sees them. The snapshot is the profile at the first click that finds
 * files there (the game reached a screen the player acts on, its first-launch work written), or at the first character
 * typed (whatever is there then: nothing typed is in it). `step` gives the snapshot back once the session has
 * presented `frames` more frames over at least `ms` (it went on running: not the files of a launch that failed).
 */
export class SeedWatch {
  constructor({ files, frames = 600, ms = 60000, limits = SEED_LIMITS }) {
    this.files = files; this.needFrames = frames; this.needMs = ms; this.limits = limits;
    this.snap = null; this.done = false;
  }
  /** A click (`typed` false) or a printable character (`typed` true) at `now` ms, `frames` presented so far. */
  input(now, frames, typed) {
    if (this.done || this.snap) return;
    const sel = seedSelect(this.files(), this.limits).map((f) => ({ path: f.path, data: f.data.slice() }));
    if (sel.length) this.snap = { files: sel, at: now, frames };
    else if (typed) this.done = true; // (typing began with nothing to share: no snapshot may come later)
  }
  /** A periodic check: the snapshot's files to report, once, or null. */
  step(now, frames) {
    if (this.done || !this.snap || frames - this.snap.frames < this.needFrames || now - this.snap.at < this.needMs) return null;
    this.done = true;
    return this.snap.files;
  }
}
```

`src/host/re3.js`:

```js
// re3 browser ports (docs/browser-ports.md, "re3 ports"): a game version whose manifest says "runtime": "re3" does not
// run in the Win32 runtime. Its page (src/ports/re3/) runs a decompiled engine of the re3 family compiled to
// WebAssembly (Emscripten: SDL2 on WebGL 2, OpenAL on WebAudio, JSPI), a pinned release installed outside Git in
// data/engines/<release>/: its ES module and WebAssembly under engine/, and the engine's own extra game files under
// gamefiles/, laid over the version's files (game-files.js releaseGameFiles: the catalog puts that folder in the
// manifest's `overlays`). This module checks such a manifest entry, tells whether its release is installed and which
// module the page imports. Single player only for now: one game, or several ways to play it (`modes`: their own command-line
// arguments, the player's choice on the page). Nothing here names a game: release, arguments, environment, settings
// and modes come from the manifest; the module's name from the release.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { engineFile } from './goldsrc.js';

const ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/;
const ARG = /^[-+]?[A-Za-z0-9_.=]{1,64}$/;
const ENV_NAME = /^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,31}$/;
const MODE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,15}$/;
const PRINTABLE = /^[\x20-\x7e]*$/; // (ASCII: an ini file is edited byte for byte, the environment as C strings)
const isObject = (value) => !!value && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
const safePath = (value) => typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0 && value.length <= 128 && PRINTABLE.test(value) && !path.isAbsolute(value) && !value.includes('\\') && value.split('/').every((part) => part && part !== '.' && part !== '..' && !part.startsWith('.'));
const text = (value, min, max) => typeof value === 'string' && value.length >= min && value.length <= max && PRINTABLE.test(value);
// (an ini file's section and key names: one line each, nothing that would open a section, end a name or start a comment)
const sectionOk = (name) => text(name, 1, 64) && !/[[\]]/.test(name) && name.trim() === name;
const keyOk = (name) => text(name, 1, 64) && !/[=[\]]/.test(name) && !/^[;#]/.test(name) && name.trim() === name;
// (a value as an ini reader reads it: without spaces around, which the line's own spacing would merge with)
const valueOk = (value) => text(value, 0, 128) && value.trim() === value;
const within = (obj, max) => isObject(obj) && Object.keys(obj).length <= max;

/** The settings a language puts in the profile's ini files: { <file>: { <section>: { <key>: <value> } } }. */
function iniOk(ini) {
  return within(ini, 8) && Object.entries(ini).every(([file, sections]) => safePath(file) && within(sections, 16)
    && Object.entries(sections).every(([section, keys]) => sectionOk(section) && within(keys, 32) && Object.keys(keys).length > 0
      && Object.entries(keys).every(([key, value]) => keyOk(key) && valueOk(value))));
}

/** What is wrong with a version's `re3` entry, or null. */
export function re3Problem(r) {
  if (!isObject(r)) return 're3 obligatoire pour le runtime re3';
  if (!ID.test(r.engine ?? '')) return 're3.engine doit nommer une release de data/engines/';
  if (r.module !== undefined && (!safePath(r.module) || !/\.mjs$/.test(r.module))) return 're3.module doit être un module .mjs de la release';
  if (r.args !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(r.args) || r.args.length > 32 || !r.args.every((a) => typeof a === 'string' && ARG.test(a)))) return 're3.args : arguments de ligne de commande ([-+]?[A-Za-z0-9_.=], 64 caractères au plus)';
  // (a game language's own: environment variables and settings of the profile's ini files — the player's choice of the
  // version's `languages`, docs/game-frame.md)
  if (r.languages !== undefined && (!within(r.languages, 16) || !Object.entries(r.languages).every(([code, l]) => /^[a-z]{2}$/.test(code) && isObject(l)
    && (l.env === undefined || (within(l.env, 32) && Object.entries(l.env).every(([name, value]) => ENV_NAME.test(name) && text(value, 0, 64))))
    && (l.ini === undefined || iniOk(l.ini)))))
    return 're3.languages : { <langue>: { env: { <NOM>: <valeur> }, ini: { <fichier>: { <section>: { <clé>: <valeur> } } } } }';
  // (defaults set once in a profile, then the player's choice: their record's key is `<section>.<key>` — a section
  // without '=' and not opening a comment, as a key)
  if (r.defaults !== undefined && (!iniOk(r.defaults) || !Object.values(r.defaults).every((sections) => Object.keys(sections).every((section) => !/=|^[;#]/.test(section)))))
    return 're3.defaults : { <fichier>: { <section>: { <clé>: <valeur> } } } (section sans « = » ni « ; » ou « # » au début)';
  // (ways to play the game, in the page's order: each its command-line arguments after re3.args)
  if (r.modes !== undefined && (!within(r.modes, 4) || Object.keys(r.modes).length < 1 || !Object.entries(r.modes).every(([id, m]) => MODE.test(id) && isObject(m)
    && (m.args === undefined || (Array.isArray(m.args) && m.args.length <= 8 && m.args.every((a) => typeof a === 'string' && ARG.test(a)))))))
    return 're3.modes : { <mode>: { args: [<argument>] } }, 1 à 4 modes ([a-z][a-z0-9-]*, 16 caractères au plus)';
  if (r.solo !== undefined && !isObject(r.solo)) return 're3.solo doit être un objet';
  return null;
}

/** The modes a version offers: its own (re3.modes, in order), else single player. */
export const re3Modes = (r) => (r?.modes ? Object.keys(r.modes) : ['solo']);

/**
 * The engine's ES module, a path of the release (`engine/<name>.mjs`): the manifest's `re3.module`, else the release's
 * only module of engine/ with its WebAssembly beside it (`<name>.wasm`: the Emscripten output; a worker's module has
 * none); null when there is none, or several.
 */
export function re3Module(manifest, enginesDir) {
  const r = manifest.re3;
  if (!ID.test(r?.engine ?? '')) return null;
  if (r.module) return r.module;
  let names; try { names = fs.readdirSync(path.join(enginesDir, r.engine, 'engine')); } catch { return null; }
  const found = names.filter((n) => n.endsWith('.mjs') && names.includes(n.slice(0, -4) + '.wasm'));
  return found.length === 1 ? `engine/${found[0]}` : null;
}

/** The engine release's files an re3 page loads at its start: its module and that module's WebAssembly (installed ones). */
export function re3EngineFiles(manifest, enginesDir) {
  const module = re3Module(manifest, enginesDir);
  return module ? [module, module.slice(0, -4) + '.wasm'].filter((f) => engineFile(enginesDir, manifest.re3.engine, f)) : [];
}

/** The engine release the version names is installed: its release.json, its module and that module's WebAssembly. */
export function re3Installed(manifest, enginesDir) {
  const module = re3Module(manifest, enginesDir);
  return !!module && ['release.json', module, module.slice(0, -4) + '.wasm'].every((f) => engineFile(enginesDir, manifest.re3.engine, f));
}
```

`src/host/request-origin.js`:

```js
// The origin a browser addressed, and the same-origin check every route that changes something or opens a socket makes
// against it. Behind front proxies the Host header names the proxied site, X-Forwarded-Host the name in the address
// bar: Caddy sets it to the requested host, or passes on the one Cloudflare gave — a Worker serving the site under
// another name (orthros.chalco.workers.dev). Not an authority: a client outside a browser sets it as it likes — as it
// sets Origin —; a page cannot, on another site's request, without a CORS preflight this server never grants, nor on a
// WebSocket's handshake at all.

const HOST = /^(\[[0-9a-f:.]+\]|[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9.-]{0,251}[a-z0-9])?)(:\d{1,5})?$/;
const first = (value) => String(value ?? '').split(',')[0].trim().toLowerCase();

/** The host the browser addressed (`name[:port]`, lowercase): the front proxy's X-Forwarded-Host, else Host; '' if neither. */
export function requestHost(req) {
  const forwarded = first(req.headers['x-forwarded-host']);
  if (HOST.test(forwarded)) return forwarded;
  const host = first(req.headers.host);
  return HOST.test(host) ? host : '';
}

/** The origin a front proxy says the browser addressed (`https://name`), or `fallback` without one. */
export function forwardedOrigin(req, fallback) {
  const host = first(req.headers['x-forwarded-host']);
  if (!HOST.test(host)) return fallback;
  return `${first(req.headers['x-forwarded-proto']) === 'http' ? 'http' : 'https'}://${host}`;
}

/** The request comes from a page of the origin it was addressed to (its Origin header's host is the addressed one). */
export function sameOrigin(req) {
  let origin; try { origin = new URL(req.headers.origin); } catch { return false; }
  return (origin.protocol === 'https:' || origin.protocol === 'http:') && origin.host === requestHost(req);
}
```

`src/host/scenario.js`:

```js
// The harness's scenario language (tools/headless.mjs --input, tools/scenarios/*.txt), parsed and played without a
// harness: the page's bench mode (docs/real-machine-bench.md) runs a scenario inside a player's browser. No
// dependency: the page loads this module directly.
//
// A scenario is a list of steps `<time>:<kind>[:<args>]` separated by `;` or new lines (`#` starts a comment line).
// Times are seconds from the launch, `+N` seconds after the first Direct3D frame, and after a wait step (`waitfps`,
// `waitframe`, `waitpixel`) seconds from the moment that wait was satisfied (the anchor). Steps run in order of their
// times; a wait not yet satisfied holds every step after it.
//   move x,y | click x,y | rclick x,y | down x,y / up x,y (left button, drags) | key vk[,scan] | keydown / keyup vk[,scan]
//   text <string> | mark:<label> (phase boundary) | shot (screenshot: the harness only)
//   waitfps F: until the game presents more than F frames/s for 3 s
//   waitframe min,max[,min2,max2...]: until 3 successive checks (1 s apart) see new Direct3D frames whose draws per
//     frame are within one of the ranges
//   waitpixel x,y,r,g,b[,tol]: until a displayed pixel has that colour (the harness only)
//   nudge vk,every: while the next wait holds, the key vk pressed every `every` seconds (an intro or cutscenes skipped
//     until the screen waited for comes, however many there are)
// The browser ports' bench (bench-suite.js, page-meter.js) plays these too, and steps of their own (PORT_KINDS):
//   cmd <command> (the engine's console) | look dx,dy[,n[,ms]] (the mouse moved by dx,dy in n steps over ms: a captured
//   mouse's look) | glide x0,y0,vx,vy,z (the player carried in a straight line from x0,y0 at vx,vy units a second at
//   height z, by the engine's debug teleport, until the next glide; `glide` alone stops)

/** steps whose argument is one string (the rest: comma-separated numbers) */
const STRING_ARGS = new Set(['text', 'find', 'mark', 'jitlist', 'dbg', 'cmd']);
export const WAIT_KINDS = new Set(['waitfps', 'waitframe', 'waitpixel']);
/** the steps the page's player performs; `shot`, `blur` and `focus` are accepted and skipped there */
export const PLAYER_KINDS = new Set(['move', 'click', 'rclick', 'down', 'up', 'key', 'keydown', 'keyup', 'text', 'mark', 'waitfps', 'waitframe', 'nudge', 'shot', 'blur', 'focus']);
/** the steps the browser ports' bench performs besides (their engine's console, a captured mouse, a debug teleport) */
export const PORT_KINDS = new Set([...PLAYER_KINDS, 'cmd', 'look', 'glide']);
const POINTER_KINDS = new Set(['move', 'click', 'rclick', 'down', 'up']);

/**
 * @typedef {{ t: number, rel: boolean, anchored: boolean, kind: string, args: any[], src: string, index: number }} Step
 * @param {string} text
 * @returns {{ steps: Step[], errors: string[] }}
 */
export function parseScenario(text) {
  const steps = [], errors = [];
  let afterWait = false;
  const parts = String(text ?? '').split('\n').filter((l) => !l.trim().startsWith('#')).join(';').split(';').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  for (const src of parts) {
    const [ts, kind = '', ...rest] = src.split(':');
    const a = rest.join(':');
    const t = Number(ts.replace(/^\+/, ''));
    if (!kind || !Number.isFinite(t) || ts.trim() === '') { errors.push(`bad step "${src}"`); continue; }
    const args = STRING_ARGS.has(kind) ? [a] : a === '' ? [] : a.split(',').map(Number);
    if (!STRING_ARGS.has(kind) && args.some((x) => !Number.isFinite(x))) errors.push(`bad arguments in "${src}"`);
    if (POINTER_KINDS.has(kind) && args.length < 2) errors.push(`"${src}": x,y expected`);
    if (kind === 'waitframe' && (args.length < 2 || args.length % 2)) errors.push(`"${src}": min,max pairs expected`);
    if (kind === 'waitfps' && args.length < 1) errors.push(`"${src}": a frame rate expected`);
    if (kind === 'nudge' && (args.length !== 2 || !(args[1] > 0))) errors.push(`"${src}": vk,every expected`);
    if (kind === 'look' && args.length < 2) errors.push(`"${src}": dx,dy expected`);
    if (kind === 'glide' && args.length !== 0 && args.length !== 5) errors.push(`"${src}": x0,y0,vx,vy,z (or nothing: stop) expected`);
    steps.push({ t, rel: ts.trim().startsWith('+'), anchored: afterWait, kind, args, src, index: steps.length });
    if (WAIT_KINDS.has(kind)) afterWait = true;
  }
  return { steps, errors };
}

/** Steps the page's player cannot perform (debugging steps of the harness, pixel waits); `kinds`: PORT_KINDS for a port. */
export function unsupportedSteps(steps, kinds = PLAYER_KINDS) { return steps.filter((s) => !kinds.has(s.kind)); }

/** Is `dpf` (draws per frame) within one of the `[min, max, min2, max2, ...]` ranges? */
export function inRanges(dpf, ranges) { for (let i = 0; i + 1 < ranges.length; i += 2) if (dpf >= ranges[i] && dpf <= ranges[i + 1]) return true; return false; }

/**
 * Plays a parsed scenario against the page's stats. `tick(now, stats)` (now: seconds since the launch; stats: the
 * worker's latest stats message, `stats.seq` changing with each new one) returns the steps due, in order, as actions
 * { kind, args } with pointer coordinates scaled from the scenario's space (`from`: [w, h]) to the game's display
 * (`display()`: [w, h]). Wait conditions follow the harness: waitfps counts 3 s of new samples above the rate;
 * waitframe checks once a second.
 */
export class ScenarioPlayer {
  /**
   * @param {Step[]} steps
   * @param {{ from?: [number, number] | null, display?: () => [number, number] | null }} [opts]
   */
  constructor(steps, opts = {}) {
    this.steps = steps.map((s) => ({ ...s, done: false }));
    this.from = opts.from ?? null; this.display = opts.display ?? (() => null);
    this.anchorAt = null; this.firstFrameAt = null;
    this.lastSeq = undefined; this.fpsStreak = 0; this.marks = [];
    this.nudge = null; // ({ vk, every, next }: a nudge step's key, pressed while the next wait holds)
  }
  get done() { return this.steps.every((s) => s.done); }
  /** steps done / all */
  get progress() { return [this.steps.filter((s) => s.done).length, this.steps.length]; }
  /** the wait holding the scenario, or null */
  get waiting() { const s = this.steps.find((x) => !x.done); return s && WAIT_KINDS.has(s.kind) ? s : null; }
  /** the label of the last mark played */
  get phase() { return this.marks.length ? this.marks[this.marks.length - 1].label : null; }
  /** pointer coordinates from the scenario's space to the display's */
  scale(x, y) {
    const d = this.display(), f = this.from;
    if (!d || !f || (d[0] === f[0] && d[1] === f[1])) return [x, y];
    return [Math.max(0, Math.min(d[0] - 1, Math.round(x * d[0] / f[0]))), Math.max(0, Math.min(d[1] - 1, Math.round(y * d[1] / f[1])))];
  }
  due(s) { return s.anchored ? (this.anchorAt === null ? Infinity : this.anchorAt + s.t) : s.rel ? (this.firstFrameAt === null ? Infinity : this.firstFrameAt + s.t) : s.t; }
  /**
   * @param {number} now seconds since the launch
   * @param {any} stats the latest stats message (fps, dt, d3d: { frames, draws }), with `seq` new for each message
   * @returns {{ kind: string, args: any[], at: number, step: Step }[]}
   */
  tick(now, stats) {
    const out = [];
    const fresh = stats && stats.seq !== this.lastSeq; if (fresh) this.lastSeq = stats.seq;
    if (this.firstFrameAt === null && stats?.d3d?.frames > 0) this.firstFrameAt = now;
    // (a wait that holds this tick: the key of the nudge before it, when due; a wait satisfied ends the nudge)
    const hold = () => { const n = this.nudge; if (n && now >= n.next) { n.next = now + n.every; out.push({ kind: 'key', args: [n.vk], at: now, step: n.step }); } };
    const satisfied = (s, extra = {}) => { s.done = true; this.anchorAt = now; this.nudge = null; out.push({ kind: s.kind, args: s.args, at: now, step: s, ...extra }); };
    for (const s of this.steps) {
      if (s.done) continue;
      const due = this.due(s);
      if (s.kind === 'waitfps') {
        if (now < due) { hold(); break; }
        if (fresh) { this.fpsStreak = (stats.fps ?? 0) > s.args[0] ? this.fpsStreak + (stats.dt ?? 0.5) : 0; }
        if (this.fpsStreak >= 3 - 1e-6) { this.fpsStreak = 0; satisfied(s); continue; } // (the steps due at the anchor run at once)
        hold(); break;
      }
      if (s.kind === 'waitframe') {
        if (now < due) { hold(); break; }
        if (s.checkAt !== undefined && now - s.checkAt < 1) { hold(); break; } // (once a second, as the harness polls)
        s.checkAt = now;
        const d3d = stats?.d3d, prev = s.prev;
        if (!d3d || (prev && d3d.frames === prev.frames)) { hold(); break; } // (no new frame since the last check: a slow loading screen)
        s.prev = { draws: d3d.draws, frames: d3d.frames };
        const dpf = prev ? (d3d.draws - prev.draws) / (d3d.frames - prev.frames) : -1;
        s.streak = prev && inRanges(dpf, s.args) ? (s.streak ?? 0) + 1 : 0;
        if (s.streak >= 3) { satisfied(s, { dpf }); continue; }
        hold(); break;
      }
      if (s.kind === 'waitpixel') break; // (not playable in the page: unsupportedSteps rejects such a scenario first)
      if (now < due) continue;
      s.done = true;
      if (s.kind === 'nudge') { this.nudge = { vk: s.args[0], every: s.args[1], next: now, step: s }; continue; }
      let args = s.args;
      if (POINTER_KINDS.has(s.kind)) args = this.scale(args[0], args[1]);
      if (s.kind === 'mark') this.marks.push({ label: String(args[0]), at: now });
      out.push({ kind: s.kind, args, at: now, step: s });
    }
    return out;
  }
}
```

`src/host/server.js`:

```js
// Development/serving host: static files (the page, the ES modules of the emulator), manifests,
// and the game folder served read-only with HTTP range requests + a JSON directory listing.

import http from 'node:http';

export const listTree = (dir) => listGameTree({ folder: dir });
/** A file version's validator (weak: the same for its encoded answers — a brotli body decodes to the same bytes). */
const etagOf = (st) => `W/"${st.size.toString(36)}-${Math.floor(st.mtimeMs).toString(36)}"`;
/** the page's own text files (src/): sent brotli 11 once made (srcBrotli) */
const SRC_TEXT = /\.(m?js|html|css|json|svg|txt)$/;
/** The size of the file at `rel` ('/'-separated, exact names) in a tree of listGameTree, or null. */
const treeFileSize = (tree, rel) => {
  const parts = rel.split('/'), light = parts[0] === LIGHT_DIR; // (a light copy's: its size the file's `light`)
  if (light) parts.shift();
  let node = tree;
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length - 1; i++) { node = Object.hasOwn(node.dirs, parts[i]) ? node.dirs[parts[i]] : null; if (!node) return null; }
  const f = Object.hasOwn(node.files, parts.at(-1)) ? node.files[parts.at(-1)] : null;
  return !f ? null : light ? f.light ?? null : f.size;
};

export function loadManifests(dir, extra = null) {
  const out = new Map();
  if (fs.existsSync(dir)) {
    for (const f of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
      if (!f.endsWith('.json')) continue;
      const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), 'utf8'));
      m.folder = path.resolve(dir, m.folder ?? '.');
      if (m.baseFolder) m.baseFolder = path.resolve(dir, m.baseFolder);
      out.set(f.slice(0, -5), withDefaults(m));
    }
  }
  for (const [name, m] of extra ?? []) out.set(name, m); // (manifests given by the caller: `orthros run <folder>`)
  return out;
}

/**
 * The build the server serves, for telemetry: the git commit of the tree, '+' when tracked files under src/ differ
 * from it, and the newest modification time of the runtime's files (the page loads src/ directly: an edited tree
 * serves new code without a new commit). Recomputed at most once a minute.
 */
let versionCache = null;
export function buildVersion(root = ROOT) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (versionCache && versionCache.root === root && now - versionCache.at < 60000) return versionCache.value;
  let commit = 'nogit', dirty = false, newest = 0;
  // (--no-optional-locks: the status never writes the index nor takes its lock — the tree may be edited meanwhile)
  const vcs = (...a) => execFileSync('git', ['--no-optional-locks', ...a], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'], timeout: 5000 }).trim();
  try { commit = vcs('rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD') || 'nogit'; dirty = vcs('status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=no', '--', 'src') !== ''; } catch { /* not a checkout */ }
  const walk = (d) => {
    let es; try { es = fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true }); } catch { return; }
    for (const e of es) {
      const f = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) walk(f);
      else if (/\.(m?js|html|css)$/.test(e.name)) { try { const t = fs.statSync(f).mtimeMs; if (t > newest) newest = t; } catch { /* gone */ } }
    }
  };
  walk(path.join(root, 'src'));
  const value = `${commit}${dirty ? '+' : ''}@${newest ? new Date(newest).toISOString().slice(0, 19) + 'Z' : '?'}`;
  versionCache = { root, at: now, value };
  return value;
}

/**
 * A request's path, decoded, when it is safe to route: never a '..' or '.' segment, a backslash or a NUL once decoded
 * (WHATWG URL folds a literal '/../' but leaves '..%2f' and '%5c' encoded, so a decoded path could climb out of the
 * directory a route serves), else null — malformed escapes too.
 */
export function requestPath(pathname) {
  let p; try { p = decodeURIComponent(pathname); } catch { return null; }
  if (p.includes('\\') || p.includes('\0') || p.split('/').some((s) => s === '..' || s === '.')) return null;
  return p;
}

/** `file` is inside the directory `dir` (resolved, a trailing separator: '/srv/orthros2' is not under '/srv/orthros'). */
export const isUnder = (dir, file) => path.resolve(file).startsWith(path.resolve(dir) + path.sep);

export function createServer(opts = {}) {
  const manifestDir = opts.manifests ? path.resolve(opts.manifests) : null;
  const gamesDir = path.resolve(opts.gamesDir ?? DEFAULT_GAMES_DIR);
  const enginesDir = path.resolve(opts.enginesDir ?? DEFAULT_ENGINES_DIR);
  const readCatalog = () => manifestDir ? loadManifests(manifestDir, opts.extra) : loadGameCatalog(gamesDir, opts.extra, { enginesDir });
  let manifests = readCatalog();
  const trees = new Map(), treeObjs = new Map();
  // (the catalog read again — at each /api/manifests: a game added appears —, the trees of the manifests that say the
  // same kept: listing a game's tree is a stat of each of its files, all of them ~0.5 s that held every request)
  const refreshCatalog = () => {
    const before = manifests; manifests = readCatalog();
    // (a tree marks the files of the versions it requires by their owner — listGameTree: one of those changed, it too)
    const same = (id) => manifests.has(id) && JSON.stringify(manifests.get(id)) === JSON.stringify(before.get(id));
    for (const id of [...treeObjs.keys()]) {
      if (same(id) && (manifests.get(id).underlayOwners ?? []).every((o) => same(o.manifest))) continue;
      treeObjs.delete(id); trees.delete(id);
    }
  };
  // (a game's tree, listed once: again when one of the folders it was listed from changed — a file added, removed or
  // renamed there, a version, a map, an re3 engine release installed, removed or rebuilt while the server runs: its
  // gamefiles/, whose files /game/ and /gamez/ resolve at each request —; looked at each time, one stat a folder: all
  // the trees of the library 5.6 ms, against 0.5 s to list them)
  const gameTree = (id, man) => {
    const cached = treeObjs.get(id), contentLight = engineContentLight(man);
    if (cached && dirsStamp(cached.dirs) === cached.stamp && cached.contentLight === contentLight) return cached.tree;
    // (the files of the versions it requires marked with their owner: the browsers store and fetch them under it; its
    // content files' light copies marked when its engine reads them so — engineContentLight)
    const dirs = [], tree = listGameTree(man, dirs, (owner) => manifests.get(owner), { contentLight });
    treeObjs.set(id, { tree, dirs, stamp: dirsStamp(dirs), contentLight }); trees.delete(id);
    return tree;
  };
  /** A tree's bytes (its files', every folder's), summed once per tree object (a tree listed again is a new one). */
  const treeSizes = new WeakMap();
  const treeBytes = (t) => {
    let n = treeSizes.get(t);
    if (n === undefined) { n = 0; for (const f of Object.values(t.files)) n += f.size; for (const d of Object.values(t.dirs)) n += treeBytes(d); treeSizes.set(t, n); }
    return n;
  };
  /** The tree as /api/tree sends it. */
  const gameTreeJson = (id, man) => { const tree = gameTree(id, man); if (!trees.has(id)) trees.set(id, JSON.stringify(tree)); return trees.get(id); };
  /**
   * The tree, brotli or gzip when the browser takes it (a page fetches it at every start and Prepare: 289 KB for
   * Half-Life, 1.3 MB for Morrowind — 2.9 and 13 s at 100 KB/s; brotli 9: 43 KB for Half-Life), made once per tree.
   */
  const treeEncoded = new Map(); // id -> { json, br, gz }
  const sendTree = (req, res, id, man) => {
    const json = gameTreeJson(id, man), accept = String(req.headers['accept-encoding'] ?? '');
    let c = treeEncoded.get(id);
    if (c?.json !== json) treeEncoded.set(id, c = { json, br: null, gz: null });
    const type = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Vary': 'Accept-Encoding' };
    if (/\bbr\b/.test(accept)) {
      c.br ??= zlib.brotliCompressSync(json, { params: { [zlib.constants.BROTLI_PARAM_QUALITY]: 9, [zlib.constants.BROTLI_PARAM_SIZE_HINT]: json.length } });
      return send(res, 200, c.br, { ...type, 'Content-Encoding': 'br', 'Content-Length': c.br.length });
    }
    if (/\bgzip\b/.test(accept)) { c.gz ??= zlib.gzipSync(json); return send(res, 200, c.gz, { ...type, 'Content-Encoding': 'gzip', 'Content-Length': c.gz.length }); }
    return send(res, 200, json, type);
  };
  // (the folders' listings the requests resolve paths with, each checked by a stat of its folder: DirListings)
  const listings = new DirListings(opts.listingNames);
  const getManifest = (id) => { if (!manifests.has(id) && !manifestDir) refreshCatalog(); return manifests.get(id); };
  const coverFile = (man) => man.coverPath ?? (man.cover && resolveGameFile(man, man.cover));
  const runtimeOf = (man) => man.runtime ?? 'win32';
  const headers = (extra = {}) => ({
    'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy': 'same-origin',
    'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy': 'require-corp',
    'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy': 'same-origin',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
    ...extra,
  });
  // testing: a slower network (opts.net = { delayMs, bytesPerSec }): each range answered after a round trip, its bytes
  // crossing one link shared by the answers in flight (see SimLink)
  const link = opts.net ? new SimLink(opts.net) : null;
  const viaLink = (res, bytes, go, onStart = null) => { const cancel = link.send(bytes, go, onStart); res.on('close', cancel); };
  const send = (res, code, body, extra) => { res.writeHead(code, headers({ 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', ...extra })); res.end(body); };
  /**
   * A whole file's answer when the browser has it already (its validators, revalidated: Cache-Control no-cache): 304,
   * no body. The Win32 page's workers each load their module graph (380 fetches of 150 modules, 8.3 MB per visit,
   * measured): every one of them a revalidation once the browser has the module.
   */
  const notModified = (req, st, etag) => {
    if (req.method !== 'GET' && req.method !== 'HEAD') return false;
    const inm = req.headers['if-none-match'];
    if (inm !== undefined) return String(inm).split(',').some((t) => { t = t.trim(); return t === '*' || t.replace(/^W\//, '') === etag.replace(/^W\//, ''); });
    const ims = Date.parse(String(req.headers['if-modified-since'] ?? ''));
    return Number.isFinite(ims) && Math.floor(st.mtimeMs / 1000) * 1000 <= ims;
  };
  const sendNotModified = (res, h) => { const { 'Content-Length': _l, 'Content-Range': _r, ...rest } = h; res.writeHead(304, rest); res.end(); };
  /**
   * A file's bytes piped into a response: a read that fails (a file unreadable for the server's user, one gone between its
   * stat and its open) ends that response, never the process — an unhandled stream error used to bring the whole server
   * down for every game.
   */
  const pipeFile = (res, file, opts) => {
    const s = fs.createReadStream(file, opts);
    s.on('error', (e) => { console.warn(`[serve] ${file}: ${e.code ?? e.message}`); if (!res.headersSent) send(res, 500, 'unreadable'); else res.destroy(); });
    return s.pipe(res);
  };
  const sendFile = (req, res, file, mime, extra = {}) => {
    let st; try { st = fs.statSync(file); } catch { return send(res, 404, 'not found'); }
    if (!st.isFile()) return send(res, 404, 'not found');
    const range = req.headers.range, etag = etagOf(st);
    const h = headers({ 'Content-Type': mime, 'Accept-Ranges': 'bytes', 'Last-Modified': st.mtime.toUTCString(), 'ETag': etag, ...extra });
    if (!range && notModified(req, st, etag)) return sendNotModified(res, h);
    if (range) {
      const m = /^bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$/.exec(range);
      if (!m) return send(res, 416, 'bad range', { 'Content-Range': `bytes */${st.size}` });
      let start = m[1] === '' ? Math.max(0, st.size - Number(m[2])) : Number(m[1]);
      let end = m[1] === '' || m[2] === '' ? st.size - 1 : Math.min(Number(m[2]), st.size - 1);
      if (start > end || start >= st.size) return send(res, 416, 'bad range', { 'Content-Range': `bytes */${st.size}` });
      res.writeHead(206, { ...h, 'Content-Range': `bytes ${start}-${end}/${st.size}`, 'Content-Length': end - start + 1 });
      if (req.method === 'HEAD') return res.end();
      if (link) { viaLink(res, end - start + 1, () => pipeFile(res, file, { start, end })); return; }
      pipeFile(res, file, { start, end });
      return;
    }
    res.writeHead(200, { ...h, 'Content-Length': st.size });
    if (req.method === 'HEAD') return res.end();
    pipeFile(res, file);
  };
  /**
   * A brotli file sent whole as its decoded content (Content-Encoding: br). No Content-Length: a loader counting the
   * decoded bytes against it (Emscripten's package download) falls back to the decoded size it knows. Its sizes said
   * instead, for a client counting the transfer (download-worker.js fetchEngine: the body comes decoded):
   * X-Orthros-Wire-Length (the brotli bytes) and X-Orthros-Decoded-Length (`decoded`, when known).
   */
  const sendBrotli = (req, res, br, mime, extra = {}, decoded = null) => {
    let st; try { st = fs.statSync(br); } catch { return send(res, 404, 'not found'); }
    const etag = etagOf(st), h = headers({ 'Content-Type': mime, 'Content-Encoding': 'br', 'Last-Modified': st.mtime.toUTCString(), 'ETag': etag, ...extra,
      'X-Orthros-Wire-Length': String(st.size), ...(decoded > 0 ? { 'X-Orthros-Decoded-Length': String(decoded) } : {}) });
    if (notModified(req, st, etag)) return sendNotModified(res, h);
    res.writeHead(200, h);
    if (req.method === 'HEAD') return res.end();
    pipeFile(res, br);
  };
  /**
   * An OpenMW lean package (openmw-lean.js: its brotli file `file`, `decoded` bytes), immutable: brotli only — a browser
   * that takes none gets it decoded here. A range asked is not honored (a 200 is a valid answer to one): the brotli
   * body whole when the client takes br — until 2026-10-28 a range went down the decoding way, 204 MB from the origin
   * for a `Range: bytes=0-0` where the br body is 7.9 MB —, else the decoded package whole (a 206 would still decode up
   * to the range's end; nothing in the tree asks one: the loaders and the download worker fetch it whole).
   */
  const sendLean = (req, res, file, decoded) => {
    const cache = 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable';
    if (/\bbr\b/.test(String(req.headers['accept-encoding'] ?? ''))) return sendBrotli(req, res, file, 'application/octet-stream', { 'Cache-Control': cache, 'Vary': 'Accept-Encoding' }, decoded);
    res.writeHead(200, headers({ 'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream', 'Cache-Control': cache, 'Vary': 'Accept-Encoding' }));
    if (req.method === 'HEAD') return res.end();
    return void pipeline(fs.createReadStream(file), zlib.createBrotliDecompress(), res).catch(() => res.destroy());
  };
  /**
   * The page's own files (src/, and the pages: no build step, the browser loads the modules as they are): revalidated
   * at each load (Cache-Control no-cache: a new tree is new code at once), 304 when unchanged (sendFile), and a text
   * file sent brotli 11 once made — 0.90 MB for the Win32 page's 3.26 MB of modules where the reverse proxy's gzip
   * makes 1.03 MB (measured, docs/slow-network.md). Made in the background at its first request (brotli 11: a few
   * hundred ms of a core for the largest modules, on libuv's pool), that one sent as it is; kept in memory by the
   * file's size and mtime (the tree's text is ~4 MB, its brotli ~1 MB), checked again once made.
   */
  const srcBr = new Map(); // file -> { size, mtimeMs, br (Buffer | null: not worth it | undefined: being made) }
  let srcBrBytes = 0;
  const SRC_BR_MAX = 64 << 20;
  // (at most SRC_BR_JOBS made at once: a first load's ~150 modules would otherwise fill libuv's 4-thread pool, the game
  // data's reads — /gamez, /api ranges — waiting behind them)
  const SRC_BR_JOBS = 2, srcBrJobs = [];
  let srcBrRunning = 0, srcBrPeak = 0;
  const srcBrPump = () => {
    while (srcBrRunning < SRC_BR_JOBS && srcBrJobs.length) {
      srcBrRunning++; srcBrPeak = Math.max(srcBrPeak, srcBrRunning);
      let once = false;
      srcBrJobs.shift()(() => { if (once) return; once = true; srcBrRunning--; srcBrPump(); });
    }
  };
  const srcBrotli = (file, st) => {
    const c = srcBr.get(file);
```
