`src/host/web/net-status.js`:

```js
// What the page says about the network while the game waits for its files (docs/slow-network.md): the measured rate,
// what came, and how long the current step should take — instead of a black screen. Pure functions of the worker's
// `net` stats (NetLink.snapshot plus waiting / stepWire, see worker.js netInfo), shared by the loading screen, the
// waiting overlay and the bench banner.

/** "85 KB/s", "1.2 MB/s" (bytes per second) */
export function fmtRate(bps, lang = 'en') {
  if (!(bps > 0)) return '—';
  return frUnits(bps >= 1048576 ? `${(bps / 1048576).toFixed(bps >= 10 * 1048576 ? 0 : 1)} MB/s` : `${Math.max(1, Math.round(bps / 1024))} KB/s`, lang);
}
/** "14 MB", "1.3 GB", "640 KB" (bytes; `lang` 'fr': "14 Mo", "1,3 Go") */
export function fmtBytes(n, lang = 'en') {
  if (!(n > 0)) return frUnits('0 MB', lang);
  return frUnits(n >= 1e9 ? `${(n / 1073741824).toFixed(1)} GB` : n >= 1048576 ? `${Math.round(n / 1048576)} MB` : `${Math.max(1, Math.round(n / 1024))} KB`, lang);
}
/** French units: octets, a decimal comma. */
const frUnits = (t, lang) => (lang === 'fr' ? t.replace(/(\d)\.(\d)/, '$1,$2').replace(/([KMG])B/, '$1o') : t);
/** "about 4 min", "about 40 s", "about 2 h 10 min" (seconds; `lang` 'fr': "environ 4 min"; `short`: "~4 min") */
export function fmtDuration(s, lang = 'en', short = false) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(s) || s < 0) return '';
  const about = short ? '~' : lang === 'fr' ? 'environ ' : 'about ';
  if (s < 90) return `${about}${Math.max(5, Math.round(s / 5) * 5)} s`;
  if (s < 3600) return `${about}${Math.round(s / 60)} min`;
  const h = Math.floor(s / 3600), m = Math.round((s - h * 3600) / 60);
  return `${about}${h} h${m ? ` ${m} min` : ''}`;
}
/** seconds the link needs for `wire` bytes at the measured rate, or null */
export function etaSeconds(wire, net) { return net?.bw > 0 && wire > 0 ? wire / net.bw : null; }

/** bytes received so far over the link (the game's reads and the background downloads) */
export const received = (net) => (net ? (net.demandBytes ?? 0) + (net.bgBytes ?? 0) : 0);

/**
 * The waiting message when the game waits for game data from the network: { title, detail } or null (not waiting).
 * `title` names the rate; `detail` what came and, when the learned order tells how much the current step still needs,
 * about how long it takes at that rate.
 */
export function netWaitText(net, lang = 'en') {
  if (!net || !net.waiting) return null;
  const fr = lang === 'fr';
  const parts = [`${fmtBytes(received(net), lang)} ${fr ? 'reçus' : 'received'}`];
  const eta = etaSeconds(net.stepWire, net);
  if (eta !== null && eta >= 5) parts.push(fr ? `${fmtDuration(eta, lang)} pour cette étape (${fmtBytes(net.stepWire, lang)} à venir)` : `${fmtDuration(eta)} for this step (${fmtBytes(net.stepWire)} to come)`);
  if (net.bw > 0 && net.bw < 512 * 1024) parts.push(fr ? 'connexion lente : l’accueil peut d’abord télécharger tout le jeu' : 'a slow connection: the home screen can download the whole game first');
  const rate = net.bw > 0 ? fmtRate(net.bw, lang) : fr ? 'mesure de la connexion' : 'measuring the connection';
  return { title: fr ? `Téléchargement des données du jeu — ${rate}` : `Downloading game data — ${rate}`, detail: parts.join(' · ') };
}

/** The connection as a bench record carries it (bytes/s, ms, bytes), or null. */
export function benchNetwork(net) {
  if (!net) return null;
  return { bw: net.bw ?? null, measured: !!net.measured, rtt: net.rtt ?? null, demandBytes: net.demandBytes ?? 0, demandRequests: net.demandRequests ?? 0, demandMs: Math.round(net.demandMs ?? 0), bgBytes: net.bgBytes ?? 0, bgRequests: net.bgRequests ?? 0, aborted: net.abortedRequests ?? 0 };
}
```

`src/host/web/page-meter.js`:

```js
// The frames of a page whose engine draws with WebGL on the page's own thread — the browser ports' pages (re3, GoldSrc,
// OpenMW) — measured from outside it, as the Win32 worker measures its own (docs/real-machine-bench.md, "The bench
// suite"): installed by the bench suite (bench-suite.js) into the port's window of its frame, same origin, at any time
// after the page started (the engine's calls look the WebGL methods and requestAnimationFrame up at each call):
// - a frame is a browser frame in which the engine drew (its draw calls counted on the context prototypes), its time,
//   its work and its data waits measured as the passive session records measure them (perf-page.js
//   watchEngineFrames: one measurement of a port's frames), or the port's own count of its engine's work
//   (hooks.workMs);
// - each frame goes to the frame accounting every runtime uses (core/frame-acct.js FrameStats: `guest` its work,
//   `ioWait` the port's reads waited for in it, `wait` the rest), so its phase reports and intervals are the Win32
//   worker's, read by the same summaries (perf-summary.js PerfWindow, compactPhase);
// - GPU time per frame with the Win32 runtime's probe (gfx/gpu-probe.js: EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 windows, WebGL
//   1's extension through perf-page.js timerContext) on the engine's context, and that context's renderer string;
// - every 0.5 s a stats message shaped as the Win32 worker's (fps, dt, acct, d3d: { frames, draws, gpu }) for the
//   scenario player's waits and the bench's windows, with the port's data (hooks.data: its reads waited for).
// The port's page may give hooks (window.orthrosBenchHooks): command(text) (its console), teleport(x, y, z),
// data() → { waits, waitMs, bytes }, workMs() (its engine's work so far, ms); without them, those its portSession
// offers (the re3 and GoldSrc pages': command, files — the game data's reads, src/vfs/data-client.js stats).
// `discard`: the rasterizer discarded (RASTERIZER_DISCARD kept on: every call made, no pixel drawn — this server's
// software GPU measured without its drawing; the harness's --gl-discard).
import { FrameStats, C, N_CATS } from '../../core/frame-acct.js';
import { GpuProbe } from '../../gfx/gpu-probe.js';
import { watchEngineFrames, timerContext } from './perf-page.js';

const DRAWS = ['drawArrays', 'drawElements', 'drawArraysInstanced', 'drawElementsInstanced', 'drawRangeElements'];
const RASTERIZER_DISCARD = 0x8C89;
export const STATS_MS = 500;

export class PageMeter {
  /**
   * @param {Window} win the port's window
   * @param {{ discard?: boolean, now?: () => number, onStats?: (m: any) => void }} [o]
   */
  constructor(win, o = {}) {
    this.win = win; this.discard = !!o.discard; this.now = o.now ?? (() => win.performance.now()); this.onStats = o.onStats ?? null;
    this.draws = 0; this.frames = 0; this.framesDraws = 0;
    this.fs = new FrameStats(); this.gl = null; this.gpu = null; this.renderer = null; this.seq = 0;
    this.lastWorkMs = null; this.statsAt = null; this.statsFrames = 0;
  }
  get hooks() { return benchHooks(this.win); }
  /** The wrappers in the port's window (once a window: a page reloaded in the frame is another window). */
  install() {
    const W = this.win, P = this;
    if (W.__orthrosPageMeter) return W.__orthrosPageMeter === this;
    W.__orthrosPageMeter = this;
    for (const type of [W.WebGL2RenderingContext, W.WebGLRenderingContext]) {
      if (!type) continue;
      const proto = type.prototype;
      for (const k of DRAWS) {
        const f = proto[k]; if (typeof f !== 'function') continue;
        proto[k] = function () { P.draws++; if (P.gl !== this) P.context(this); return f.apply(this, arguments); };
      }
      if (this.discard && type === W.WebGL2RenderingContext) {
        const disable = proto.disable;
        proto.disable = function (cap) { if (cap === RASTERIZER_DISCARD) return undefined; return disable.call(this, cap); };
      }
    }
    // (the frames shown, their work and data waits: the passive records' measurement, perf-page.js)
    watchEngineFrames(W, {
      draws: () => this.draws, now: this.now, stopped: () => this.stopped,
      data: () => { const d = safe(() => this.hooks?.data?.()); return d ? { ms: d.waitMs ?? 0 } : null; },
      onShown: () => { this.frames++; this.framesDraws = this.draws; try { this.gpu?.frame(); } catch { this.gpu = null; } }, // (a lost context: no more timing)
      onFrame: (dt, work, dataMs, t) => this.frame(dt, work, dataMs, t),
    });
    this.statsAt = this.now();
    this.timer = W.setInterval(() => this.emit(), STATS_MS);
    return true;
  }
  stop() { this.stopped = true; try { this.win.clearInterval(this.timer); } catch { /* gone */ } }
  /** The engine's context, seen at its first draw: its renderer, its GPU timer, the rasterizer discarded. */
  context(gl) {
    if (this.gl) { this.otherContexts = (this.otherContexts ?? 0) + 1; if (this.gl.isContextLost?.() === false) return; }
    this.gl = gl;
    try { const info = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info'); this.renderer = String(gl.getParameter(info ? info.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER)); } catch { this.renderer = null; }
    const W2 = this.win.WebGL2RenderingContext;
    // (its timer queries, WebGL 1's extension adapted — perf-page.js timerContext; none: reported unavailable)
    try { this.gpu = new GpuProbe(timerContext(gl), { wrapGl: false, now: this.now }); } catch { this.gpu = null; }
    if (this.discard && W2 && gl instanceof W2) gl.enable(RASTERIZER_DISCARD);
  }
  /**
   * A frame shown (after the first): to the frame accounting — `guest` the engine's work (the port's own count when it
   * has one, hooks.workMs), `ioWait` the data waits within it, `wait` the rest.
   */
  frame(dt, work, dataMs, t) {
    let w = work ?? 0;
    const wm = safe(() => this.hooks?.workMs?.()); if (typeof wm === 'number') { if (this.lastWorkMs !== null) w = wm - this.lastWorkMs; this.lastWorkMs = wm; }
    const cats = new Float64Array(N_CATS), ww = Math.max(0, Math.min(w, dt)), wio = Math.min(dataMs, ww);
    cats[C.guest] = ww - wio; cats[C.ioWait] = wio; cats[C.wait] = Math.max(0, dt - ww);
    this.fs.add(dt, cats, t); // (t: the browser frame that ends it)
  }
  /** The stats message now (the Win32 worker's shape: what the scenario player and PerfWindow read). */
  emit() {
    const now = this.now(), dt = Math.max(1e-3, (now - this.statsAt) / 1000), frames = this.frames - this.statsFrames;
    this.statsAt = now; this.statsFrames = this.frames;
    const g = this.gpu?.stats.gpu, data = safe(() => this.hooks?.data?.()) ?? null;
    const m = {
      seq: ++this.seq, dt, fps: frames / dt, acct: this.fs.takeInterval(),
      d3d: { frames: this.frames, draws: this.framesDraws, gpu: g ? { ...g, hist: Array.from(g.hist) } : { state: this.gl ? 'unavailable' : 'none' } },
      ...(data ? { data } : {}),
    };
    this.last = m;
    this.onStats?.(m);
    return m;
  }
  /** A phase boundary (BenchRun's mark): the phase report since the previous one (frame-acct.js FrameStats.phase). */
  phase(label) { return this.fs.phase(label, this.now()); }
}

function safe(f) { try { return f(); } catch { return undefined; } }

const fromSession = new WeakMap();
/** A port page's bench hooks: its own (window.orthrosBenchHooks), else its portSession's command and data reads. */
export function benchHooks(win) {
  try {
    if (!win) return null;
    if (win.orthrosBenchHooks) return win.orthrosBenchHooks;
    const s = win.portSession; if (!s) return null;
    let h = fromSession.get(s);
    if (!h) {
      h = {
        command: (text) => s.command?.(text),
        data: () => { const st = s.files?.stats; return st ? { waits: st.waits ?? 0, waitMs: st.waitMs ?? 0, bytes: st.fetchedBytes ?? 0 } : null; },
      };
      fromSession.set(s, h);
    }
    return h;
  } catch { return null; }
}
```

`src/host/web/perf-page.js`:

```js
// The page's side of the passive session records (src/host/perf-record.js, docs/real-machine-bench.md "Passive
// session records"), one for every runtime: the Windows games' page feeds it the worker's stats intervals (frame
// accounting), a browser port's page (GoldSrc, re3, the OpenMW engine's page) its frames shown — the engine's work a
// frame measured from the browser's animation frames, its GPU time by the timer query probe (gpu-probe.js, sampled
// windows), its game data waits from the shared game data's counters (data-client.js) and what they were for
// (portDataSummary). It keeps the clock (visible and hidden time, the phase), runs the host timing probe once
// (timing-probe.js), and sends a record every 2 minutes of play and one at the end (sendBeacon, else a keepalive fetch).
import { PerfRecorder, SLOW_A } from '../perf-record.js';
import { GpuProbe } from '../../gfx/gpu-probe.js';
import { runTimingProbe } from './timing-probe.js';
import { gpuClass, gpuInfo } from './gpu-class.js';
import { pageStorage, withStorage } from './storage-persist.js';

export { SLOW_A };
/** the clock's period (ms); the timing probe once after this much visible time */
export const CLOCK_MS = 1000, PROBE_AFTER_MS = 60000;
/** the storage's state (storage-persist.js) read again this often (ms) for the records' env */
export const STORAGE_READ_MS = 30000;

/** Send a telemetry body (an object or its JSON) to the server: sendBeacon, else a keepalive fetch. */
export function beacon(body, url = '/api/telemetry') {
  const text = typeof body === 'string' ? body : JSON.stringify(body);
  try { if (globalThis.navigator?.sendBeacon?.(url, new Blob([text], { type: 'application/json' }))) return true; } catch { /* refused */ }
  try { fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: text, keepalive: true }).catch(() => {}); } catch { /* no fetch */ }
  return false;
}

/**
 * A browser port's session events (/api/telemetry: its start, errors, crash, audio, end — a few a session; the GoldSrc
 * and re3 pages): `port` its runtime, `state()` the page's state, `storage` its pageStorage (the env's storage),
 * `bench` a bench suite's run (bench-suite.js). report(event, data) sends one (20 at most a session); end(data) the
 * session's end, once. `session`: the id the passive record shares (portPerf). `send`: beacon (tests: their own).
 * @param {{ port: string, state: () => string, storage: { state: any }, bench?: string|null, max?: number, send?: (body: object) => void }} o
 */
export function portEvents({ port, state, storage, bench = null, max = 20, send = beacon }) {
  const t = { session: crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '').slice(0, 16), started: performance.now(), sent: 0, ended: false,
    report(event, data = {}) {
      if (t.sent >= max) return; t.sent++;
      send({ session: t.session, game: decodeURIComponent(globalThis.location?.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)[2] ?? ''), port, event, ...(bench ? { bench } : {}),
        seconds: Math.round((performance.now() - t.started) / 1000), state: state(), ...data, env: eventEnv(storage.state) });
    },
    end(data = {}) { if (t.ended) return; t.ended = true; t.report('end', data); } };
  return t;
}

/**
 * A WebGL context's timer queries as GpuProbe expects them (WebGL2's API): the context itself on WebGL2, an adapter
 * of EXT_disjoint_timer_query on WebGL1 (the same enums), a context without the extension otherwise (GpuProbe then
 * reports 'unavailable').
 */
export function timerContext(gl) {
  if (!gl) return gl;
  const has = (n) => { try { return gl.getExtension(n); } catch { return null; } };
  if ((typeof WebGL2RenderingContext !== 'undefined' && gl instanceof WebGL2RenderingContext) || has('EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2')) return gl;
  const ext = has('EXT_disjoint_timer_query');
  if (!ext) return { getExtension: () => null };
  return {
    getExtension: (n) => (n === 'EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2' ? ext : null),
    createQuery: () => ext.createQueryEXT(), deleteQuery: (q) => ext.deleteQueryEXT(q),
    beginQuery: (t, q) => ext.beginQueryEXT(t, q), endQuery: (t) => ext.endQueryEXT(t),
    getQueryParameter: (q, p) => ext.getQueryObjectEXT(q, p), getParameter: (p) => gl.getParameter(p),
    QUERY_RESULT: ext.QUERY_RESULT_EXT, QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE: ext.QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE_EXT,
  };
}

/** The machine as the ports' telemetry already tells it, with the WebGL renderer (of `gl` when given) and its kind. */
export function portEnv(gl = null) {
  const nav = globalThis.navigator ?? {}, { renderer, vendor } = gpuInfo(gl);
  return { gpu: renderer, gpuVendor: vendor, gpuClass: gpuClass(renderer), cores: nav.hardwareConcurrency ?? null, memGB: nav.deviceMemory ?? null, ua: nav.userAgent ?? null,
    screen: globalThis.screen ? `${screen.width}x${screen.height}@${globalThis.devicePixelRatio ?? 1}` : null };
}

/**
 * The env of a browser port's event records (start, error, end — /api/telemetry, the GoldSrc and re3 pages): the
 * browser and machine, and the storage's state (`storage`: the page's pageStorage().state, storage-persist.js).
 */
export function eventEnv(storage = null) {
  const nav = globalThis.navigator ?? {};
  return withStorage({ ua: nav.userAgent ?? null, cores: nav.hardwareConcurrency ?? null, memGB: nav.deviceMemory ?? null, dpr: globalThis.devicePixelRatio ?? 1,
    screen: globalThis.screen ? `${screen.width}x${screen.height}` : null }, storage);
}

export class PerfSession {
  /**
   * @param {{ runtime: string, game: string|null, session: string, version?: string|null, build?: string|null,
   *   tier?: () => string|null, bench?: string|null, env?: () => object, phase?: () => string|null,
   *   data?: () => ({ waits: number, ms: number, sum?: object }|null), gpu?: () => object|null, send?: (rec: object) => void,
   *   win?: any, now?: () => number, probe?: boolean, recordMs?: number, storage?: ReturnType<typeof pageStorage> }} o
   *   storage: the page's (storage-persist.js: its env's `storage`, read again after each record), else one of its own
   */
  constructor(o) {
    this.o = o; this.win = o.win ?? globalThis; this.now = o.now ?? (() => performance.now());
    this.rec = new PerfRecorder({ recordMs: o.recordMs, header: { session: o.session, game: o.game ?? null, runtime: o.runtime, version: o.version ?? null, build: o.build ?? null, tier: null, ...(o.bench ? { bench: o.bench } : {}) } });
    this.sendFn = o.send ?? beacon; this.envCache = null; this.ended = false; this.probeAsked = o.probe === false;
    this.gpuProbe = null; this.dataCum = null; this.gpuStats = null;
    this.storage = o.storage ?? pageStorage(this.win.navigator); // (read by tick: at once, then every STORAGE_READ_MS)
    const doc = this.win.document;
    this.onVis = () => { this.tick(); if (this.meter) { this.meter.prevT = null; this.meter.lastShownT = null; } };
    this.onHide = () => this.end();
    doc?.addEventListener?.('visibilitychange', this.onVis);
    // (capture: before the page's own pagehide listeners — a large telemetry flush there could use up the keepalive quota)
    this.win.addEventListener?.('pagehide', this.onHide, { capture: true });
    this.timer = setInterval(() => this.tick(), CLOCK_MS);
    this.tick();
  }
  visible() { return this.win.document?.visibilityState !== 'hidden'; }
  gpu() { return this.o.gpu ? this.o.gpu() : this.gpuProbe ? this.gpuProbe.stats.gpu : this.gpuStats; }
  data() { return this.o.data ? this.o.data() : this.dataCum; }
  tick() {
    if (this.ended) return;
    const now = this.now(), vis = this.visible();
    this.rec.counters({ gpu: this.gpu() ?? null, data: this.data() ?? null });
    this.rec.clock(now, vis, this.o.phase?.() ?? null);
    if (!this.probeAsked && vis && this.rec.tot.vis >= PROBE_AFTER_MS) {
      this.probeAsked = true;
      runTimingProbe().then((p) => { if (p) this.rec.setProbe(p); }, () => {});
    }
    const r = this.rec.take(now); if (r) this.send(r);
    else if (!(now - (this.storageRead ?? -Infinity) < STORAGE_READ_MS)) { this.storageRead = now; this.storage.read(); } // (the usage grows as the game data comes: the end's record too)
  }
  send(r) {
    if (!this.envCache) { try { this.envCache = this.o.env ? this.o.env() : portEnv(this.meter?.gl ?? null); } catch { this.envCache = null; } if (this.envCache && !this.envCache.gpuClass) this.envCache = { ...this.envCache, gpuClass: gpuClass(this.envCache.gpu) }; }
    r.tier = this.o.tier?.() ?? null;
    if (this.envCache) { const e = this.envCache; r.env = withStorage({ gpu: e.gpu ?? null, gpuVendor: e.gpuVendor ?? null, gpuClass: e.gpuClass ?? null, cores: e.cores ?? null, memGB: e.memGB ?? null, ua: e.ua ?? null, screen: e.screen ?? null }, this.storage.state); }
    try { this.sendFn(r); } catch { /* lost */ }
    this.storage.read(); // (the next record's: the usage grows as the game data comes)
  }
  /** The session's end (the game exited, the page goes): the last record, then nothing more. */
  end() {
    if (this.ended) return;
    const now = this.now();
    this.rec.counters({ gpu: this.gpu() ?? null, data: this.data() ?? null });
    const r = this.rec.take(now, true); this.ended = true;
    clearInterval(this.timer);
    this.win.document?.removeEventListener?.('visibilitychange', this.onVis); this.win.removeEventListener?.('pagehide', this.onHide, { capture: true });
    if (r) this.send(r);
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the Windows games: the worker's stats intervals
  /** One stats message of the emulator's worker (~0.5 s): its frame accounting, GPU timer and file waits. */
  interval(m) {
    if (this.ended || !m) return;
    if (m.d3d?.gpu) this.gpuStats = m.d3d.gpu;
    if (m.netMs !== undefined) { const d = (this.dataCum ??= { waits: 0, ms: 0 }); d.waits += m.netReq ?? 0; d.ms += m.netMs ?? 0; }
    const a = m.acct; if (!a) return;
    // (the frames' own time: the sum of their categories — work and waits —, else the interval's)
    const c = a.c ? Object.values(a.c).reduce((x, y) => x + y, 0) : 0, dtMs = c > 0 ? c * a.frames : (m.dt ?? 0.5) * 1000;
    this.rec.interval(a, dtMs);
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the ports: the frames shown
  /**
   * Measure the frames of an engine that runs in this page: `gl()` its WebGL context once it has one (GPU time, the
   * renderer), `draws()` a counter of its draw calls (a browser frame with draws was shown), else the page calls the
   * returned `shown()` for each frame the engine displayed. The engine's work a frame: from the browser frame's start
   * to the engine's request for the next one made in it (its iteration's end, with an asynchronous main loop as well).
   */
  watchFrames({ gl = null, draws = null } = {}) {
    const w = watchEngineFrames(this.win, {
      draws, gl, data: () => this.data(), active: () => this.visible(), stopped: () => this.ended, now: () => performance.now(),
      onGl: (ctx) => { try { this.gpuProbe = new GpuProbe(timerContext(ctx), { wrapGl: false }); } catch { this.gpuProbe = null; } },
      onShown: () => { try { this.gpuProbe?.frame(); } catch { /* lost context */ } },
      onFrame: (dt, work, dataMs) => this.rec.frame(dt, work, dataMs),
    });
    this.meter = w.meter;
    return { shown: w.shown };
  }
}

/**
 * The frames an engine shows in the page `win` — one measurement for the passive records (PerfSession.watchFrames, in
 * the port's own page) and the bench suite (page-meter.js, from the page around it): a frame shown is a browser frame
 * with draws (`draws()`, a counter of the engine's draw calls) or one the page marks (the returned `shown()`); its time
 * the gap between the animation frames that saw two of them; the engine's work in it from the browser frame's start to
 * the engine's request for the next one made in it (its iteration's end, with an asynchronous main loop as well; null
 * when it made none); the game data's waits in it from `data()` ({ ms } cumulative). `gl()`: the engine's context, asked
 * at shown frames until it has one (onGl). onShown() at each frame shown, onFrame(dtMs, workMs | null, dataMs, t) for
 * each one after the first while `active()`; `stopped()` ends it. `now`: the clock of the page's requests (its
 * performance.now).
 */
export function watchEngineFrames(win, o) {
  const raf0 = win.requestAnimationFrame.bind(win), now = o.now ?? (() => (win.performance ?? performance).now());
  const m = { prevT: null, lastShownT: null, flag: false, drawsSeen: o.draws ? o.draws() : 0, work: 0, known: false, frameT: null, ask: [null, 0], askPrev: [null, 0], dataAt: null, gl: null };
  // (the asks: the last two frames' last requests, by the frame they were made in)
  win.requestAnimationFrame = function (cb) {
    const at = now();
    if (m.ask[0] !== m.frameT) m.askPrev = m.ask;
    m.ask = [m.frameT, at];
    return raf0((t) => { m.frameT = t; cb(t); });
  };
  const tick = (t) => {
    if (o.stopped?.()) return;
    if (m.frameT !== t) m.frameT = t; // (this frame's asks are this frame's)
    if (m.prevT !== null) {
      const a = m.ask[0] === m.prevT ? m.ask : m.askPrev[0] === m.prevT ? m.askPrev : null;
      if (a) { m.work += Math.max(0, a[1] - m.prevT); m.known = true; }
      const d = o.draws ? o.draws() : null, shown = m.flag || (d !== null && d !== m.drawsSeen);
      m.flag = false; if (d !== null) m.drawsSeen = d;
      if (shown) {
        if (!m.gl && o.gl) { const ctx = o.gl(); if (ctx) { m.gl = ctx; o.onGl?.(ctx); } }
        o.onShown?.(m.prevT);
        const dw = o.data?.(), dms = dw ? dw.ms : 0, dd = m.dataAt === null ? 0 : Math.max(0, dms - m.dataAt); m.dataAt = dms;
        if (m.lastShownT !== null && (o.active?.() ?? true)) o.onFrame(m.prevT - m.lastShownT, m.known ? m.work : null, dd, m.prevT);
        m.lastShownT = m.prevT; m.work = 0; m.known = false;
      }
    }
    m.prevT = t; raf0(tick);
  };
  raf0(tick);
  return { meter: m, shown: () => { m.flag = true; } };
}

/**
 * A port's game data for its passive record (PerfSession's `data`, the same for every port): its waits, cumulative
 * ({ waits, ms }: each minute's), and `sum` what they were for so far (the record's totals, perf-record.js
 * compactDataSum) — the files waited for (the shared game data's fileWaits), the engine's own stops for its files when
 * it counts them (`engine.orthrosBlocked`: { count, ms, max, files: ms by path } — reVC; `root` its game folder in the
 * engine's file system, left out of the paths), its announced reads' waits, the background's bytes by producer (the
 * link's bgBy; a getter: the frames' meter reads only `ms`, each frame). gameData: the page's GameData
 * (data-client.js), null before (then null).
 * @param {any} gameData @param {any} [engine] @param {{ root?: string }} [o]
 */
export function portDataSummary(gameData, engine = null, { root = '' } = {}) {
  if (!gameData) return null;
  const s = gameData.stats ?? {}, rel = (p) => (root && p.startsWith(root + '/') ? p.slice(root.length + 1) : p);
  return { waits: s.misses ?? 0, ms: s.stallMs ?? 0,
    get sum() {
      const B = engine?.orthrosBlocked;
      const blocked = B ? { count: B.count ?? 0, ms: B.ms ?? 0, max: B.max ?? 0, files: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(B.files ?? {}).map(([k, v]) => [rel(k), v])) } : null;
      return { files: s.fileWaits ?? null, blocked, wantWaits: s.wantWaits ?? 0, wantWaitMs: s.wantWaitMs ?? 0, wantTimeouts: s.wantTimeouts ?? 0, bgBy: gameData.net?.bgBy ?? null };
    } };
}

/** The WebGL context an engine made on `canvas` (asked once it drew: never creates one), or null. */
export function canvasGl(canvas) {
  try { return canvas?.getContext('webgl2') ?? canvas?.getContext('webgl') ?? null; } catch { return null; }
}

/**
 * A port's session record, started when the server keeps telemetry (/api/config): `o` as PerfSession's, with
 * watchFrames' `gl` and `draws`. Returns at once a handle — `shown()` (a frame the engine displayed, for an engine
 * whose page knows them), `end()` — that forwards to the session once it exists.
 */
export function portPerf(o) {
  const h = { session: null, frames: null, ended: false, shown() { h.frames?.shown(); }, end() { h.ended = true; h.session?.end(); } };
  fetch('/api/config').then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : {})).catch(() => ({})).then((c) => {
    if (!c?.telemetry || h.ended) return;
    h.session = new PerfSession({ ...o, build: c.version ?? null });
    h.frames = h.session.watchFrames({ gl: o.gl, draws: o.draws });
  });
  return h;
}
```

`src/host/web/pointer.js`:

```js
// The page's mouse → the worker's input ring (browser-host.js EV), for every game alike.
//
// Captured (pointer lock): only relative motion exists. Each move goes as EV.MOUSEREL — the device counts
// (movementX/Y, unclamped: DirectInput's relative axes, a mouse-look camera) and the cursor's motion in screen pixels
// (movement / display scale, fractions carried over) — and the worker moves the guest cursor from where *it* is: a
// game re-centering the cursor with SetCursorPos every frame (mouse-look by warping) reads exactly the motion since
// its warp, and the cursor stops at the screen's / ClipCursor's edges (edge scrolling) while the device counts go on.
// The page only draws that cursor (#softcursor): its position is the worker's last report (`cursor-pos`, with the
// sequence number of the last move it had taken) plus the moves sent since.
//
// Free (no capture): the pointer's position over the game, clamped to the game's screen (the page's margins are the
// screen's edges: edge scrolling without capture); the device counts are the position's change only while the pointer
// stays over the game — none when it enters, leaves or moves in the margins (no huge jump after re-entering elsewhere,
// no motion stuck at an edge).
import { EV, BUTTON_AT_CURSOR } from '../host-proto.js';

/**
 * The cursor the page shows over the game: the guest's system cursor and nothing else (a game drawing its own cursor
 * sprite hides the system one — ShowCursor, SetCursor(NULL), an exclusive DirectInput mouse — so the page draws none:
 * never the browser's arrow over the game's sprite). `visible`: the guest's cursor shows (undefined before the worker
 * said: the arrow at start, as Windows). Uncaptured: the guest's shape as the CSS cursor; captured (pointer lock, no
 * CSS cursor exists): the page's soft cursor at the guest cursor's position.
 * @returns {{ css: 'none' | 'guest', soft: boolean }}
 */
export function cursorView(visible, captured) {
  if (visible === false) return { css: 'none', soft: false };
  return captured ? { css: 'none', soft: true } : { css: 'guest', soft: false };
}

const SEQ_MASK = 0xffffff;
const i16 = (v) => Math.max(-32768, Math.min(32767, Math.trunc(v)));
const pack = (x, y) => ((i16(y) & 0xffff) << 16) | (i16(x) & 0xffff);

export class PointerInput {
  /**
   * @param {(type: number, a: number, b: number, c: number) => void} push the input ring's writer
   * @param {() => { width: number, height: number }} mode the game's screen size
   */
  constructor(push, mode) {
    this.push = push; this.mode = mode;
    this.seq = 0; this.pending = []; // (captured moves not yet reported taken by the worker)
    this.fx = 0; this.fy = 0; // (sub-pixel remainders of the captured motion)
    this.vx = 0; this.vy = 0; this.reported = false; // the guest cursor as the page draws it (reported: by the worker once)
    this.lastX = 0; this.lastY = 0; this.inside = false; // (free pointer: the last position, over the game or not)
  }
  clampX(x) { return Math.max(0, Math.min(this.mode().width - 1, x)); }
  clampY(y) { return Math.max(0, Math.min(this.mode().height - 1, y)); }

  /** A captured move: movementX/Y (CSS pixels), the display scale (CSS pixels per screen pixel). */
  lockedMove(mx, my, scale = 1) {
    mx = Math.round(mx) || 0; my = Math.round(my) || 0;
    if (!mx && !my) return;
    const s = scale > 0 ? scale : 1;
    this.fx += mx / s; this.fy += my / s;
    const gdx = Math.trunc(this.fx), gdy = Math.trunc(this.fy);
    this.fx -= gdx; this.fy -= gdy;
    const seq = this.seq = (this.seq + 1) & SEQ_MASK;
    this.push(EV.MOUSEREL | (seq << 8), i16(mx), i16(my), pack(gdx, gdy));
    this.pending.push({ seq, gdx, gdy }); if (this.pending.length > 512) this.pending.shift();
    this.vx = this.clampX(this.vx + gdx); this.vy = this.clampY(this.vy + gdy);
  }
  /** The worker's guest cursor after the captured move `seq` (SetCursorPos warps and clipping included). */
  cursorReport(x, y, seq) {
    // (moves after `seq`: sent, not yet taken — the cursor drawn ahead by them; sequence numbers wrap at 24 bits)
    this.pending = this.pending.filter((p) => ((p.seq - seq) & SEQ_MASK) > 0 && ((p.seq - seq) & SEQ_MASK) < 0x800000);
    let vx = x, vy = y;
    for (const p of this.pending) { vx += p.gdx; vy += p.gdy; }
    this.vx = this.clampX(vx); this.vy = this.clampY(vy); this.reported = true;
  }
  /** Capture starts: the cursor drawn where the guest's is (its last report; else where the free pointer was). */
  locked() { if (!this.reported) { this.vx = this.lastX; this.vy = this.lastY; } this.fx = this.fy = 0; this.inside = false; }
  /** Capture ends: the free pointer's next move carries no motion (it reappears where the capture began). */
  unlocked() { this.inside = false; }

  /**
   * A free move: the pointer at screen pixel (x, y) of the game (unclamped: outside the game in the page's margins).
   * @returns {[number, number]} the clamped position sent
   */
  freeMove(x, y) {
    const inside = x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < this.mode().width && y < this.mode().height;
    const cx = this.clampX(Math.round(x)), cy = this.clampY(Math.round(y));
    const dx = inside && this.inside ? cx - this.lastX : 0, dy = inside && this.inside ? cy - this.lastY : 0;
    this.inside = inside; this.lastX = cx; this.lastY = cy;
    this.push(EV.MOUSEMOVE, cx, cy, pack(dx, dy));
    return [cx, cy];
  }
  /** The free pointer left the page (or the window): its next move over the game carries no motion. */
  left() { this.inside = false; }

  /** A button (Windows numbering: 0 left, 1 right, 2 middle): captured, where the guest cursor is; else at (x, y). */
  button(down, b, locked, x = 0, y = 0) {
    if (locked) this.push(down ? EV.MOUSEDOWN : EV.MOUSEUP, b | BUTTON_AT_CURSOR, this.vx | 0, this.vy | 0);
    else { const cx = this.clampX(Math.round(x)), cy = this.clampY(Math.round(y)); this.push(down ? EV.MOUSEDOWN : EV.MOUSEUP, b, cx, cy); }
  }
}

/** A DOM MouseEvent's button as Windows numbers them (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle). */
export const winButton = (b) => (b === 2 ? 1 : b === 1 ? 2 : b);

```

```html
  <h1>Règles de confidentialité</h1>
  <p class="date">Dernière mise à jour : 27 octobre 2026</p>
  <p class="lead">Orthros (orthros.chalco.website) est un service privé et non commercial qui permet de jouer, dans le navigateur, à des jeux
    dont les fichiers sont sur son serveur. Cette page dit quelles données Orthros garde, pourquoi, combien de temps, et comment les supprimer.</p>

  <h2>Ce qu’Orthros garde</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Ton compte</strong> : ton identifiant, une empreinte de ton mot de passe (scrypt — le mot de passe lui-même n’est jamais
      conservé) et la date de création du compte.</li>
    <li><strong>Si tu te connectes avec Google</strong> : l’identifiant de ton compte Google et ton adresse e-mail. Ton prénom sert seulement
      à t’accueillir et à te proposer un identifiant ; il n’est pas conservé.</li>
    <li><strong>Tes sauvegardes en ligne</strong> : les fichiers de sauvegarde et de profil des jeux auxquels tu joues connecté, jusqu’à
      20 versions par jeu et 512 Mo par compte.</li>
    <li><strong>Ta connexion</strong> : un cookie de session, valable 30 jours ; pendant une connexion avec Google, deux cookies techniques
      de 10 minutes au plus. Aucun cookie publicitaire ni de mesure d’audience.</li>
    <li><strong>Le multijoueur</strong> : ton identifiant est ton nom dans les parties ; les mondes multijoueurs persistants gardent ton
      personnage, lié à ton compte.</li>
    <li><strong>Des mesures techniques</strong> : pendant une partie, la page envoie des mesures de performance (images par seconde, temps de
      calcul), une description technique du navigateur et de la machine (navigateur, carte graphique, écran, place de stockage du navigateur et si elle est persistante) et, en cas de plantage, un
      rapport d’erreur avec la fin du journal technique du jeu. Elles portent un numéro de session tiré au hasard, ne sont pas rattachées
      à ton compte et ne contiennent pas ton adresse IP. Elles servent uniquement à améliorer Orthros.</li>
    <li><strong>Dans ton navigateur</strong> : les fichiers de jeu déjà téléchargés (cache), tes sauvegardes locales et tes réglages restent
      sur ton appareil ; tu peux les voir, les exporter et les effacer dans « Paramètres ».</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Orthros n’enregistre pas ton adresse IP ; le serveur ne la garde en mémoire que quelques minutes, pour limiter les abus (trop de
    tentatives de connexion).</p>

  <h2>Pourquoi</h2>
  <p>Uniquement pour faire fonctionner Orthros : te reconnaître, garder tes sauvegardes et te les rendre sur tous tes appareils, ouvrir le
    multijoueur, et corriger les problèmes de fonctionnement. Pas de publicité, pas de profilage, pas de revente, aucun traceur tiers.</p>

  <h2>Données reçues de Google</h2>
  <p>Avec « Continuer avec Google », Orthros demande seulement les autorisations <em>openid</em>, <em>email</em> et <em>profile</em>. Il en garde
    l’identifiant de ton compte Google et ton adresse e-mail, et ne s’en sert que pour te connecter à ton compte Orthros. Ces données ne
    sont ni partagées, ni vendues, ni utilisées pour de la publicité ou pour entraîner des modèles d’intelligence artificielle.</p>
  <p>L’utilisation et le transfert à toute autre application des informations reçues des API Google respectent les
    <a href="https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy">Règles relatives aux données utilisateur des services d’API Google</a>,
    y compris les exigences d’utilisation limitée (Limited Use).</p>
  <p>Tu peux délier Google à tout moment dans la fenêtre Compte (après avoir défini un mot de passe), et retirer l’accès d’Orthros depuis
    <a href="https://myaccount.google.com/permissions">ton compte Google</a>.</p>

  <h2>Partage</h2>
  <p>Personne d’autre ne reçoit tes données. Le site passe par Cloudflare (réseau et sécurité), qui traite les requêtes comme un hébergeur,
    selon <a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/">ses propres règles</a>. Les autres joueurs voient ton identifiant dans les

  <h2>Combien de temps</h2>
  <p>Ton compte, son lien avec Google et tes sauvegardes en ligne sont gardés jusqu’à ce que tu les supprimes. Une session expire après

<article lang="en">
  <h1>Privacy policy</h1>
  <p class="date">Last updated: October 27, 2026</p>
  <p class="lead">Orthros (orthros.chalco.website) is a private, non-commercial service for playing, in the browser, games whose files are on
    its server. This page says what data Orthros keeps, why, for how long, and how to delete it.</p>

  <h2>What Orthros keeps</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Your account</strong>: your username, a hash of your password (scrypt — the password itself is never stored) and the date the
      account was created.</li>
    <li><strong>If you sign in with Google</strong>: your Google account identifier and your email address. Your first name is only used to
      greet you and to suggest a username; it is not stored.</li>
    <li><strong>Your online saves</strong>: the save and profile files of the games you play while signed in, up to 20 versions per game and
      512 MB per account.</li>
    <li><strong>Your sign-in</strong>: a session cookie, valid for 30 days; during a Google sign-in, two technical cookies of 10 minutes at
      most. No advertising or audience-measurement cookies.</li>
    <li><strong>Multiplayer</strong>: your username is your name in games; persistent multiplayer worlds keep your character, tied to your
      account.</li>
    <li><strong>Technical measurements</strong>: during a game, the page sends performance measurements (frames per second, computing time),
      a technical description of the browser and machine (browser, graphics card, screen, the browser's storage space and whether it is persistent) and, after a crash, an error report with the end
      of the game's technical log. They carry a random session number, are not tied to your account and contain no IP address. They are
      only used to improve Orthros.</li>
    <li><strong>In your browser</strong>: game files already downloaded (cache), your local saves and your settings stay on your device; you
      can see, export and erase them in “Settings”.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Orthros does not record your IP address; the server keeps it in memory for a few minutes only, to limit abuse (too many sign-in
    attempts).</p>

  <h2>Why</h2>
  <p>Only to run Orthros: recognize you, keep your saves and give them back on all your devices, open multiplayer, and fix problems. No
    advertising, no profiling, no selling, no third-party trackers.</p>

  <h2>Data received from Google</h2>
  <p>With “Continue with Google”, Orthros only asks for the <em>openid</em>, <em>email</em> and <em>profile</em> permissions. It keeps your Google
    account identifier and your email address, and only uses them to sign you in to your Orthros account. This data is not shared, sold,
    or used for advertising or to train artificial intelligence models.</p>
  <p>Orthros' use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the
    <a href="https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy">Google API Services User Data Policy</a>, including the Limited
    Use requirements.</p>
  <p>You can unlink Google at any time in the account window (after setting a password), and remove Orthros' access from
    <a href="https://myaccount.google.com/permissions">your Google account</a>.</p>

  <h2>Sharing</h2>
  <p>No one else receives your data. The site goes through Cloudflare (network and security), which processes requests as a host, under
    <a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/">its own policy</a>. Other players see your username in multiplayer games.</p>

  <h2>How long</h2>
  <p>Your account, its Google link and your online saves are kept until you delete them. A session expires after 30 days. Technical
    measurements, not tied to your account, are kept as long as they help diagnose problems.</p>

  <h2>Your rights</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>See and export your online saves: “Settings” → “Online”.</li>
    <li>Delete an online save, or your whole account: the account window → “Delete my account” immediately erases your account, your online
      saves and your Google link.</li>
    <li>For any other request (access, correction, question): <span class="contact">write to Orthros' support address, shown on its Google
      sign-in screen</span>.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>You can also contact the data protection authority of your country.</p>

  <h2>Security</h2>
  <p>Encrypted connections (HTTPS), hashed passwords (scrypt), a session cookie the pages' scripts cannot read, Google sign-in checked by the
    server.</p>

  <h2>Changes</h2>
  <p>This page may change with Orthros; the date at the top gives its latest version.</p>
```

`src/host/web/shell.js`:

```js
// The frame Orthros puts around every game, whatever runs it (the Windows games' page, the browser ports' pages):
//   - the header over the game (hidden in full screen only): Orthros, the game and its version, the runtime's own
//     indicators, whether the mouse is captured by the game, where the progress is saved, the frame rate, the settings,
//     full screen, back to the games;
//   - the loading screen before the game shows: the game's cover blurred behind, who plays (the Orthros account, or a
//     warning that nothing is saved on an account), the runtime's choices when it has some, the steps of the start;
//   - passing messages, the questions asked to the player, the "sound is off" button.
// The page drives it (createShell(...) and the methods it returns); it never names a game. Styles: player.css.
import { pickLang } from './lang.js';
import { h } from './dom.js';
import { gpuInfo, gpuShortName } from './gpu-class.js';
import { accountState, signIn, onAccountChange, googleSignIn, googleText, GOOGLE_G } from './account.js';

const ICON = {
  mouse: '<rect x="6" y="3" width="12" height="18" rx="6"/><path d="M12 7v4"/>',
  lock: '<rect x="5" y="11" width="14" height="10" rx="2"/><path d="M8 11V8a4 4 0 0 1 8 0v3"/>',
  cloud: '<path d="M7 18a4.5 4.5 0 0 1-.6-8.96A6 6 0 0 1 18 9.5 4 4 0 0 1 17.5 18H7z"/>',
  alert: '<path d="M12 4l9 16H3L12 4zM12 10v4M12 17v.5"/>',
  check: '<path d="M5 12l4 4 10-10"/>',
  gear: '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3"/><path d="M12 2v3M12 19v3M4.2 4.2l2.1 2.1M17.7 17.7l2.1 2.1M2 12h3M19 12h3M4.2 19.8l2.1-2.1M17.7 6.3l2.1-2.1"/>',
  sound: '<path d="M11 5 6 9H2v6h4l5 4z"/><path d="m22 9-6 6M16 9l6 6"/>',
  user: '<circle cx="12" cy="8" r="4"/><path d="M4 21c0-4 4-6 8-6s8 2 8 6"/>',
};
/**
 * Full screen: the keyboard locked (Keyboard Lock) — Esc and the keys the browser's shortcuts are made of reach the game
 * (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T, Alt+←, F5…: a game holds Ctrl to fire or crouch while letters move); holding Esc leaves the
 * full screen. Tab, Alt, the system key, F4 and F11 stay the system's (Alt+Tab, Alt+F4).
 */
export async function lockKeys() {
  const codes = ['Escape', 'ArrowLeft', 'ArrowRight', 'PageUp', 'PageDown', 'F1', 'F2', 'F3', 'F5', 'F6', 'F7', 'F8', 'F9', 'F10', 'F12'];
  for (let i = 0; i < 26; i++) codes.push('Key' + String.fromCharCode(65 + i));
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) codes.push('Digit' + i);
  try { await navigator.keyboard?.lock?.(codes); } catch { /* keyboard lock unavailable: Esc leaves the full screen */ }
}
const svg = (name) => { const s = h('span', { class: 'ic', 'aria-hidden': 'true' }); s.innerHTML = `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.9" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">${ICON[name]}</svg>`; return s; };

/**
 * The frame around a game.
 * @param {{ title: string, version?: string, gameLanguage?: string, cover?: string, subtitle?: string, steps: { k: string, label: string }[],
 *   tips?: string[], extras?: HTMLElement[], headless?: boolean,
 *   onQuit?: () => Promise<boolean|void>, onFullscreen?: () => void, onMouse?: () => void, onPerf?: () => void, onSignedIn?: (user) => void,
 *   saves?: () => import('./cloud-sync.js').CloudSave|null }} o
 */
export function createShell(o) {
  const lang = pickLang(), S = STRINGS[lang] ?? STRINGS.en;
  document.documentElement.lang = lang;
  const shell = { lang, S, account: null, accounts: null, running: false };

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the header
  const fpsEl = h('span', { class: 'fps' }, '–'), sub = h('span', { class: 'sub' }), graph = h('canvas', { width: 96, height: 24 });
  // (the GPU the browser draws with, beside the frame rate — on a laptop with two, Windows gives the browser the
  // integrated one unless told otherwise: the player sees which; its full name on hover)
  const gpuFull = o.headless ? null : gpuInfo().renderer, gpuEl = h('span', { class: 'gpu', title: gpuFull ?? '' }, gpuShortName(gpuFull) ?? '');
  const perf = h('div', { class: 'perf', id: 'tbPerf', title: S.perfTitle }, fpsEl, h('span', { class: 'unit' }, 'fps'), graph, sub, gpuEl);
  if (o.onPerf) perf.onclick = o.onPerf; else perf.classList.add('still');
  const mouseText = h('span'), mouse = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'pill mouse', id: 'tbMouse' }, svg('mouse'), mouseText);
  const saveText = h('span'), save = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'pill save', id: 'tbSave' }, svg('cloud'), saveText);
  const settings = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'icon', id: 'tbSettings', title: S.settings, 'aria-label': S.settings, onclick: () => window.orthrosData?.open?.('cloud') }, svg('gear'));
  const full = h('button', { type: 'button', id: 'tbFull', title: S.fullscreenTitle }, S.fullscreen);
  const games = h('button', { type: 'button', id: 'tbGames', class: 'quiet', title: S.gamesTitle }, S.games);
  // (the logo and the name lead home too, as the games button: asked first while a game runs)
  const home = h('a', { href: '/?menu', class: 'home', id: 'tbHome', title: S.gamesTitle }, h('img', { src: LOGO, alt: '' }), h('span', { class: 'name' }, 'Orthros'));
  const gameEl = h('span', { class: 'game', id: 'tbGame' }, o.title), tagEl = h('span', { class: 'tag' });
  const extras = h('div', { class: 'extras' }, ...(o.extras ?? []));
  const bar = h('div', { id: 'topbar' },
    h('div', { class: 'brand' }, home, h('span', { class: 'sep' }), gameEl, tagEl),
    h('div', { class: 'spacer' }), extras, mouse, save, perf, settings, full, games);
  shell.bar = bar; shell.extras = extras;
  shell.setTitle = (title, version = o.version, language = o.gameLanguage) => {
    gameEl.textContent = title; document.title = `${title} · Orthros`;
    tagEl.textContent = [version, language?.toUpperCase()].filter(Boolean).join(' · ');
    tagEl.hidden = !tagEl.textContent;
  };
  shell.setTitle(o.title);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loading screen
  const stepsEl = h('ul', {}, o.steps.map((s) => h('li', { 'data-k': s.k }, h('span', { class: 'ic' }), h('span', {}, s.label), h('span', { class: 'v' }))));
  const fill = h('div', { class: 'fill' }), pctEl = h('span', { class: 'pct' }, '0%'), phaseEl = h('span', { class: 'phase', id: 'status', role: 'status' });
  const tipEl = h('div', { class: 'tip', id: 'tip' }), logEl = h('pre', { id: 'log' }), logBox = h('details', { class: 'log' }, h('summary', {}, S.log), logEl);
  const titleEl = h('div', { class: 'title', id: 'title' }, o.title), subEl = h('div', { class: 'subtitle', id: 'subtitle' }, o.subtitle ?? '');
  const who = h('div', { class: 'who' }), choices = h('div', { class: 'choices' });
  const progress = h('div', { class: 'progress' }, h('div', { class: 'bar' }, fill), h('div', { class: 'row' }, phaseEl, pctEl), stepsEl);
  const loaderBg = h('div', { class: 'bg' });
  const loader = h('div', { id: 'loader' }, loaderBg, h('div', { class: 'box' },
    h('div', { class: 'head' }, h('img', { src: LOGO, alt: '' }), h('div', {}, titleEl, subEl)), who, choices, progress, tipEl, logBox));
  if (o.cover) loaderBg.style.backgroundImage = `url(${o.cover})`;
  shell.loader = loader; shell.choices = choices; shell.logEl = logEl;
  let pct = 0, tipTimer = null;
  const tips = o.tips ?? [];
  if (tips.length) {
    let i = Math.floor(Math.random() * tips.length); tipEl.textContent = tips[i];
    tipTimer = setInterval(() => { i = (i + 1) % tips.length; tipEl.textContent = tips[i]; }, 9000);
  } else tipEl.hidden = true;
  /** One step of the start: '' (to come), 'active', 'done', 'skip'; its figure. */
  shell.step = (k, state, value = '') => { const li = stepsEl.querySelector(`li[data-k="${k}"]`); if (!li) return; li.className = state; li.querySelector('.v').textContent = value; };
  /** The bar (never going back) and the line under it. */
  shell.progress = (value, text) => {
    if (value != null) { pct = Math.max(pct, Math.min(99, Math.floor(value))); fill.style.width = pct + '%'; pctEl.textContent = pct + '%'; }
    if (text != null) phaseEl.textContent = text;
  };
  shell.phase = (text, error = false) => { phaseEl.textContent = text; phaseEl.classList.toggle('error', error); if (loader.classList.contains('hidden') && text) shell.toast(text, error ? 9000 : 5000); };
  /** Progress shown or not (the runtime's choices first, as the browser ports' modes). */
  shell.showProgress = (on) => { progress.hidden = !on; };
  shell.hideLoader = (now = false) => {
    if (loader.classList.contains('hidden')) return;
    clearInterval(tipTimer);
    fill.style.width = '100%'; pctEl.textContent = '100%'; phaseEl.textContent = S.ready;
    if (now) { loader.classList.add('hidden'); return; }
    setTimeout(() => { loader.classList.add('gone'); setTimeout(() => { loader.classList.add('hidden'); o.onLoaderHidden?.(); }, 600); }, 250);
  };
  shell.showLoader = () => { loader.classList.remove('hidden', 'gone'); };
  shell.log = (line) => { logEl.textContent = (logEl.textContent + line + '\n').slice(-20000); };

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- who plays
  function renderWho() {
    who.replaceChildren();
    if (shell.accounts === null) return;
    if (!shell.accounts) { who.className = 'who local'; who.append(svg('cloud'), h('p', {}, S.whoLocal)); return; }
    if (shell.account) { who.className = 'who in'; who.append(svg('user'), h('p', {}, ...S.whoIn(shell.account.username))); return; }
    who.className = 'who off';
    const form = h('form', { class: 'signin', hidden: true });
    const user = h('input', { name: 'username', required: true, minlength: 3, maxlength: 32, autocomplete: 'username', 'aria-label': S.username, placeholder: S.username });
    const pass = h('input', { name: 'password', type: 'password', required: true, maxlength: 128, autocomplete: 'current-password', 'aria-label': S.password, placeholder: S.password });
    const err = h('p', { class: 'err', role: 'alert' }), submit = h('button', { type: 'submit', class: 'primary' }, S.go);
    let mode = 'login';
    form.append(user, pass, submit, h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'ghost', onclick: () => { form.hidden = true; } }, S.cancel), err, h('small', {}, S.rules));
    const open = (m) => { mode = m; form.hidden = false; pass.autocomplete = m === 'register' ? 'new-password' : 'current-password'; pass.minLength = m === 'register' ? 10 : 0; submit.textContent = m === 'register' ? S.register : S.signIn; user.focus(); };
    form.onsubmit = async (e) => {
      e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); submit.disabled = true; err.textContent = '';
      try { await signIn(mode, user.value, pass.value, lang); } catch (x) { err.textContent = x.message; } finally { submit.disabled = false; }
    };
    for (const type of ['keydown', 'keyup', 'keypress']) form.addEventListener(type, (e) => e.stopPropagation()); // (the game's key handlers never see what is typed here)
    // (Google: a small window, the page stays — signIn's listeners run when it says so)
    const gErr = h('p', { class: 'gerr', role: 'alert' }), g = h('span', { class: 'g', 'aria-hidden': 'true' }); g.innerHTML = GOOGLE_G;
    const google = shell.google ? h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'google', onclick: async () => { gErr.textContent = ''; const r = await googleSignIn(lang); if (!r.ok) gErr.textContent = googleText(r, lang); } }, g, S.google) : null;
    who.append(svg('alert'), h('div', {}, h('p', {}, S.whoOff), h('div', { class: 'acts' },
      h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'primary', onclick: () => open('login') }, S.signIn),
      h('button', { type: 'button', onclick: () => open('register') }, S.register), google), gErr, form));
    shell.openSignIn = open;
  }
  onAccountChange(({ user }) => {
    const was = shell.account?.username; shell.account = user; renderWho(); renderSave();
    if (user && user.username !== was) { shell.toast(S.signedIn(user.username), 4000); o.onSignedIn?.(user); }
  });
  /** Who plays, asked of the server: { accounts, user }. */
  shell.ready = accountState().then((st) => { shell.accounts = st.accounts; shell.google = st.google; shell.account = st.user; renderWho(); renderSave(); return st; });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the mouse
  /** true: the game has the mouse (pointer lock), false: free, null: no game yet. */
  shell.setMouse = (locked) => {
    mouse.classList.toggle('on', locked === true); mouse.classList.toggle('wait', locked == null);
    mouse.querySelector('.ic').innerHTML = `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.9" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">${ICON[locked ? 'lock' : 'mouse']}</svg>`;
    mouseText.textContent = locked == null ? S.mouseWait : locked ? S.mouseLocked : S.mouseFree;
    mouse.title = locked == null ? S.mouseWaitTitle : locked ? S.mouseLockedTitle : S.mouseFreeTitle;
    mouse.setAttribute('aria-label', mouse.title);
  };
  shell.setMouse(null);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the game data loading in the background
  /**
   * A pill in the header while the game data loads in the background (src/vfs/data-client.js onProgress, every
   * runtime): { kind: 'ahead', done, total, finished } — the learned order —, { kind: 'whole', bytes, total, done } — the
   * whole game kept in this browser; gone once done.
   */
  const pills = {};
  let launching = false;
  shell.setData = (p) => {
    const kind = p.kind === 'whole' ? 'whole' : p.kind === 'launch' ? 'launch' : 'ahead';
    let pill = pills[kind];
    if (!pill) {
      pill = pills[kind] = h('span', { class: 'pill data', title: S[kind + 'Title'] }, h('span', {}, S[kind]), h('i', {}, h('u')), h('b'));
      extras.append(pill);
    }
    const frac = kind === 'whole' ? p.bytes / Math.max(1, p.total) : kind === 'launch' ? p.here / Math.max(1, p.bytes) : p.done / Math.max(1, p.total), pct = Math.min(100, Math.floor(frac * 100));
    pill.querySelector('u').style.width = pct + '%';
    pill.querySelector('b').textContent = kind === 'launch' ? S.launchLeft(p.seconds, p.wireLeft) : pct + ' %';
    if (kind === 'launch') {
      // (the way to playable said while it lasts: the learned order's own pill comes back after it)
      launching = !p.done && p.here < p.bytes;
      pill.hidden = !launching;
      if (pills.ahead) pills.ahead.hidden = launching || pills.ahead.dataset.over === '1';
      return;
    }
    if (kind === 'ahead') pill.dataset.over = p.finished || !p.total ? '1' : '';
    pill.hidden = kind === 'whole' ? !!p.done || p.stopped : !!p.finished || !p.total || launching;
  };
  mouse.onclick = () => o.onMouse?.();
  /** Follows the pointer lock of `doc` (the page's, or a frame's of the same origin). */
  shell.watchPointer = (doc = document) => {
    const upd = () => shell.setMouse(shell.running ? !!doc.pointerLockElement : null);
    doc.addEventListener('pointerlockchange', upd); upd();
    return upd;
  };

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the saves
  let saveState = { state: 'off' };
  const clock = (t) => new Date(t).toLocaleTimeString(lang, { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
  function renderSave() {
    const s = saveState, u = shell.account?.username ?? '';
    let cls = '', text = '', title = '', icon = 'cloud';
    if (shell.accounts === false) { text = S.saveLocal; title = S.saveLocalTitle; }
    else if (!shell.account) { cls = 'warn'; icon = 'alert'; text = S.saveOff; title = S.saveOffTitle; }
    else if (s.state === 'saving') { cls = 'busy'; text = S.saveSaving; title = S.saveSavingTitle; }
    else if (s.state === 'saved') { cls = 'ok'; icon = 'check'; text = S.saveSaved(clock(s.at)); title = S.saveSavedTitle(u, clock(s.at)); }
    else if (s.state === 'error') { cls = 'bad'; icon = 'alert'; text = S.saveError; title = S.saveErrorTitle(s.message ?? '?'); }
    else if (s.state === 'conflict') { cls = 'bad'; icon = 'alert'; text = S.saveConflict; title = S.saveConflictTitle; }
    else if (s.state === 'toobig') { cls = 'bad'; icon = 'alert'; text = S.saveTooBig; title = S.saveTooBigTitle; }
    else if (s.state === 'server') { cls = 'ok'; icon = 'check'; text = S.saveServer; title = S.saveServerTitle(u); }
    else { text = `${S.saveIdle} · ${u}`; title = S.saveIdleTitle(u); }
    save.className = 'pill save ' + cls; save.title = title; save.setAttribute('aria-label', title); saveText.textContent = text;
    save.querySelector('.ic').innerHTML = `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.9" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">${ICON[icon]}</svg>`;
  }
  /** A CloudSave status (cloud-sync.js), or the runtime's own: { state: off|idle|saving|saved|error|conflict|toobig, ... }. */
  shell.setSave = (status) => { saveState = status ?? { state: 'off' }; renderSave(); };
  save.onclick = async () => {
    const cloud = o.saves?.();
    if (!shell.account && shell.accounts) { shell.showLoaderSignIn?.(); return; }
    if (saveState.state === 'conflict' && cloud) { await shell.resolveConflict(cloud); return; }
    if (saveState.state === 'error' && cloud) cloud.push();
    else window.orthrosData?.open?.('cloud');
  };
  /** Not signed in, from the header: the account window (the loading screen's form is gone with it). */
  shell.showLoaderSignIn = () => { if (window.orthrosData?.open) window.orthrosData.open('account'); else if (!loader.classList.contains('hidden')) shell.openSignIn?.('login'); };
  /** The player chooses between the account's save and this browser's: the CloudSave settles it. */
  shell.resolveConflict = async (cloud) => {
    const choice = await shell.ask({ title: S.conflictTitle, text: S.conflictText(o.title), buttons: [{ value: 'account', label: S.conflictAccount, primary: true }, { value: 'device', label: S.conflictDevice }] });
    if (choice) await cloud.resolve(choice);
    return choice;
  };

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the frame rate
  /** samples: [{ fps, p99, max }] every ~0.5 s (the last two shown, the last minute drawn); mode: 'loading', 'paused' or 'running'. */
  shell.setFps = (samples, mode = 'running', extra = '') => {
    const ms = (v) => (v >= 1000 ? `${(v / 1000).toFixed(1)} s` : `${Math.round(v)} ms`);
    if (mode === 'loading') { fpsEl.textContent = '…'; fpsEl.className = 'fps'; sub.textContent = S.loadingShort + (extra ? '\n' + extra : ''); }
    else if (mode === 'paused') { fpsEl.textContent = '❚❚'; fpsEl.className = 'fps'; sub.textContent = S.paused; }
    else {
      const last = samples.slice(-2), f = last.reduce((a, s) => a + s.fps, 0) / Math.max(1, last.length);
      fpsEl.textContent = f.toFixed(0); fpsEl.className = 'fps ' + (f >= 29.5 ? 'good' : f >= 20 ? 'warn' : 'bad');
      sub.textContent = `p99 ${ms(Math.max(0, ...last.map((s) => s.p99 ?? 0)))}\nmax ${ms(Math.max(0, ...last.map((s) => s.max ?? 0)))}`;
    }
    drawGraph(graph, mode === 'running' ? samples : []);
  };
  shell.drawGraph = drawGraph;

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- passing messages, questions
  const toastEl = h('div', { id: 'toast', class: 'hidden' });
  let toastTimer = null;
  shell.toast = (text, ms = 5000) => {
    if (o.headless) return;
    toastEl.textContent = text; toastEl.classList.remove('hidden'); toastEl.style.opacity = '1';
    clearTimeout(toastTimer); toastTimer = setTimeout(() => { toastEl.style.opacity = '0'; setTimeout(() => toastEl.classList.add('hidden'), 700); }, ms);
  };
  const askEl = h('div', { id: 'ask', class: 'hidden', role: 'dialog', 'aria-modal': 'true' });
  /** A question: resolves to the value of the button chosen, null when dismissed (Escape, outside). */
  shell.ask = ({ title, text, buttons }) => new Promise((resolve) => {
    if (document.pointerLockElement) document.exitPointerLock();
    const done = (v) => { askEl.classList.add('hidden'); askEl.replaceChildren(); removeEventListener('keydown', onKey, true); resolve(v); };
    const onKey = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); done(null); } else if (!askEl.contains(e.target)) { e.stopImmediatePropagation(); } };
    addEventListener('keydown', onKey, true);
    const btns = buttons.map((b) => h('button', { type: 'button', class: b.primary ? 'primary' : b.danger ? 'danger' : '', onclick: () => done(b.value) }, b.label));
    askEl.replaceChildren(h('div', { class: 'card' }, h('h3', {}, title), text ? h('p', {}, text) : null, h('div', { class: 'acts' }, btns)));
    askEl.onclick = (e) => { if (e.target === askEl) done(null); };
    for (const type of ['mousedown', 'mouseup', 'click', 'keyup']) askEl.addEventListener(type, (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    askEl.classList.remove('hidden'); (btns.find((b) => b.classList.contains('primary')) ?? btns[0])?.focus();
  });
  const soundEl = h('button', { id: 'soundHint', type: 'button', class: 'hidden' }, svg('sound'), h('span', {}, S.soundOff));
  shell.sound = soundEl;

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- full screen, back to the games
  full.onclick = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (o.onFullscreen) return o.onFullscreen();
    try { await document.documentElement.requestFullscreen({ navigationUI: 'hide' }); } catch { return; }
    await lockKeys();
  };
  document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', () => { if (!document.fullscreenElement) navigator.keyboard?.unlock?.(); });
  let quitting = false;
  /** Back to the game list: asked first while a game runs; the runtime saves (onQuit) before the page goes. */
  shell.quit = async () => {
    if (quitting) return;
    if (shell.running && !o.headless) {
      const signedIn = !!shell.account;
      const ok = await shell.ask({ title: S.quitTitle(o.title), text: signedIn ? S.quitSaved : S.quitLocal, buttons: [{ value: true, label: S.quit, primary: true }, { value: false, label: S.stay }] });
      if (!ok) return;
    }
    quitting = true; games.disabled = true;
    try {
      shell.toast(S.quitSaving, 20000);
      const saved = await o.onQuit?.();
      if (saved === false && shell.account && !(await shell.ask({ title: S.quitTitle(o.title), text: S.quitFailed, buttons: [{ value: true, label: S.quit, danger: true }, { value: false, label: S.stay }] }))) { quitting = false; games.disabled = false; return; }
    } catch (e) { console.error(e); }
    location.href = '/?menu';
  };
  games.onclick = home.onclick = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); shell.quit(); };
  /** The runtime's save before the page goes, without the question nor the navigation: how the bench suite (bench-suite.js) leaves a game. */
  shell.save = async () => { try { return await o.onQuit?.(); } catch (e) { console.error(e); return false; } };
  globalThis.orthrosShell ??= shell; // (the page's shell, for the bench suite around it)
  // (out of full screen the browser keeps its shortcuts: a page left with Ctrl or ⌘ held while the game runs — Ctrl+W,
  // Ctrl+R in the middle of a fight — asks first; watchKeys(doc): a frame's document the game's keys go to)
  let held = false;
  shell.watchKeys = (doc) => {
    const note = (e) => { held = e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey; };
    doc.addEventListener('keydown', note, true); doc.addEventListener('keyup', note, true);
    doc.defaultView?.addEventListener('blur', () => { held = false; });
  };
  shell.watchKeys(document);
  addEventListener('beforeunload', (e) => { if (held && shell.running && !quitting && !o.headless) { e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; } });
  // (the header and its windows keep their clicks: the game under them never sees them)
  for (const type of ['mousedown', 'mouseup', 'click', 'contextmenu', 'wheel']) bar.addEventListener(type, (e) => e.stopPropagation());

  if (!o.headless) document.body.append(loader, bar, toastEl, askEl, soundEl);
  else document.body.classList.add('nobar');
  return shell;
}

/** The frame rate of the last minute (120 samples) against 30 fps, the frames over 50 ms marked in red above. */
export function drawGraph(cv, samples) {
  const g = cv.getContext('2d'), w = cv.width, ht = cv.height, top = 60, span = 120;
  const y = (v) => ht - 1 - Math.min(v, top) / top * (ht - 2);
  g.clearRect(0, 0, w, ht); g.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.04)'; g.fillRect(0, 0, w, ht);
  g.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.25)'; g.setLineDash([3, 3]); g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(0, y(30)); g.lineTo(w, y(30)); g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  const shown = samples.slice(-span), x0 = w - shown.length * (w / span);
  g.strokeStyle = '#8fd18f'; g.beginPath();
  shown.forEach((p, i) => { const x = x0 + i * (w / span); if (i) g.lineTo(x, y(p.fps)); else g.moveTo(x, y(p.fps)); });
  g.stroke();
  g.fillStyle = '#ff6b6b'; shown.forEach((p, i) => { if ((p.max ?? 0) > 50) g.fillRect(x0 + i * (w / span), 0, 2, 4); });
}
```

`src/host/web/snapshot-key.js`:

```js
// The key a snapshot of the machine is kept under (docs/snapshot.md): the page's own snapshot in OPFS and the server's
// shared one are used only by a session whose key is the same — Orthros' state-owning sources (/api/snapshot-sources),
// the game version's manifest and files, the game language and the page's options that change the machine. The debug
// flags that only measure the host (gpu-probe.js HOST_ONLY_DBG) are not among them: a ?bench page adds ORTHROS_GL_COUNT,
// and until 2026-10-27 that alone gave it a key no publishing session (tools/snapshot-publish.mjs, a plain page) could
// match — every shared-snapshot job a bench queued failed.
import { HOST_ONLY_DBG } from '../../gfx/gpu-probe.js';

/** `dbg` (the page's ?dbg=, "K=V,K=V") without the host-only flags, its order kept: the part a snapshot's key covers. */
export const machineDbg = (dbg) => String(dbg ?? '').split(',').filter((kv) => kv && !HOST_ONLY_DBG.includes(kv.split('=')[0])).join(',');

/**
 * The key of a snapshot of game `name` (a hex string, 32 digits): `sources` the state-owning sources' hash, `manifest`
 * and `tree` the version's, `opts` the worker's start options (main.js) — those that change the machine only.
 */
export async function snapshotKey(sources, name, manifest, tree, opts) {
  const machine = { lang: opts.gameLanguage, timeScale: opts.timeScale, interp: opts.interp, interpRange: opts.interpRange, dbg: machineDbg(opts.dbg), jitOpts: opts.jitOpts, noF32: opts.noF32, f32Off: opts.f32Off };
  const d = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ sources, name, manifest, tree, machine })));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(d).subarray(0, 16), (b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}
```
