```js
    if (!s || s.length > 400) return null;
    const t = s.trim(); if (!t) return null;
    let out = FR[t] ?? FR[s];
    if (out === undefined) { const p = STARTS.find(([a]) => t.startsWith(a)); if (p) out = p[1] + t.slice(p[0].length); }
    if (out === undefined) { const e = ENDS.find(([a]) => t.endsWith(a)); if (e) out = t.slice(0, -e[0].length) + e[1]; }
    if (out === undefined) return null;
    return FR[s] !== undefined ? out : s.replace(t, out);
  };
  const SKIP = new Set(['SCRIPT', 'STYLE', 'TEXTAREA', 'CANVAS', 'CODE', 'PRE']);
  const ATTRS = ['title', 'placeholder', 'aria-label', 'alt'];
  function node(n) {
    if (n.nodeType === 3) { if (n.parentNode && !SKIP.has(n.parentNode.nodeName)) { const o = tr(n.nodeValue); if (o !== null && o !== n.nodeValue) n.nodeValue = o; } return; }
    if (n.nodeType !== 1 || SKIP.has(n.nodeName)) return;
    for (const a of ATTRS) { const v = n.getAttribute(a); if (v) { const o = tr(v); if (o !== null && o !== v) n.setAttribute(a, o); } }
    if (n.nodeName === 'INPUT' && ['button', 'submit'].includes(n.type)) { const o = tr(n.value); if (o !== null) n.value = o; }
    for (const c of n.childNodes) node(c);
  }
  const start = () => {
    node(document.body);
    new MutationObserver((list) => {
      for (const m of list) {
        if (m.type === 'characterData') node(m.target);
        else if (m.type === 'attributes') node(m.target);

      }
    }).observe(document.body, { subtree: true, childList: true, characterData: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ATTRS });
    document.documentElement.lang = 'fr';
  };
  if (document.body) start(); else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', start);

```

`src/ports/openmw/view-grow.js`:

```js
// The OpenMW engine page's view distance on a link that is not fast: near first, far in the background. The engine
// starts with a short view distance (VIEW.start: about the cells around the player — distant terrain and object paging
// stay on as the page's quality tier says: they cannot be turned on once it runs), then the page raises it by
// VIEW.step up to the tier's own once the game data is quiet (GameData.quiet, src/vfs/data-client.js: no read waited
// for the network for a while, the learned order has nothing left for the game's current step) and the frames are
// short; the loads of a step read the light copies of their textures (GameData.prefer('light'): their files come after
// them, for their next loads). Through Orthros' PLAYER script in the engine (view.lua: the camera's view distance,
// never the settings), which tells the page the player's own setting — changed in Options, the growth stops — and
// exterior cell. Loaded by the engine page (src/host/openmw.js, withProgressiveView) before the engine starts.
import { linkRate } from '../../vfs/data-client.js';

export const VIEW = {
  /** the boot view distance on a link that is not fast (engine units: one exterior cell) */
  start: 8192,
  /** each raise */
  step: 2048,
  /** no read waited for the network this long before a raise (and after one: the step is loaded) */
  quietMs: 3000,
  /**
   * a frame longer than this, and than `longFactor` times the page's usual one (the median of the frame meter's p99 over
   * the last half minute, frame-meter.js: a slow machine's frames are all long), holds the next raise…
   */
  longFrameMs: 50, longFactor: 2.5,
  /** …for this long after it */
  holdMs: 3000,
  /** the page's look at the game data and the script's reports */
  pollMs: 500,
};
/** Orthros' content in the engine (its /resources/vfs, a data folder of the engine's own). */
const ROOT = '/resources/vfs';
export const CONTENT = 'orthros.omwscripts';
export const VIEW_FILE = `${ROOT}/orthros/view.txt`;

/** The script's report 'orthros.view' ("<view distance> <the player's setting>"): numbers, or null. */
export function parseView(text) {
  const m = /^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s+(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/.exec(String(text ?? ''));
  return m ? { live: Number(m[1]), base: Number(m[2]) } : null;
}

/**
 * The player is in the world (streamfs.js marks the session playable then): alone, the first report of Orthros'
 * script (view.lua, 'orthros.view'); in multiplayer — no Orthros script there, the world's content list is its own —
 * the multiplayer script's world joined and simulated (its 'simReady').
 */
export function inWorld(win) {
  const state = win.omw?.state ?? {};
  return state['orthros.view'] !== undefined || (!!win.__omwMPEnabled && state.state === 'Joined' && state.simReady === '1');
}

/**
 * One look of the growth `s` ({ phase: 'wait'|'loading'|'done'|'stopped', start, target, value, since }) at the game:
 * `report` (parseView: null before the player is in the world), `exterior`, `quiet`, `framesOk`, `now`. Changes `s`;
 * returns what to do: { write } the view distance for the script, { prefer } the loads' kind (GameData.prefer).
 */
export function growStep(s, { report, exterior, quiet, framesOk, now }) {
  const out = {};
  if (s.phase === 'done' || s.phase === 'stopped' || !report) return out;
  // (the player's own setting is not the page's boot value: theirs — saved earlier, or changed in Options — wins)
  if (Math.abs(report.base - s.start) >= 1) { if (s.phase === 'loading') out.prefer = null; s.phase = 'stopped'; return out; }
  if (s.phase === 'loading') {
    if (Math.abs(report.live - s.value) < 1 && quiet && now - s.since >= VIEW.quietMs) { out.prefer = null; s.phase = s.value >= s.target ? 'done' : 'wait'; }
    return out;
  }
  if (s.value >= s.target) { s.phase = 'done'; return out; }
  // (raised in an exterior only: inside, nothing far loads — the step would pass at once, the whole view loading on the
  // way out)
  if (exterior && quiet && framesOk) {
    s.value = Math.min(s.target, s.value + VIEW.step); s.phase = 'loading'; s.since = now;
    out.write = s.value; out.prefer = 'light';
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Into the engine page `win` before its engine starts (window.orthrosViewReady holds the engine's load): the hooks its
 * boot calls — orthrosViewBoot(tierDistance) the boot view distance (window.orthrosViewStart, orthrosViewTarget),
 * orthrosContent(FS, cfgLines) Orthros' script written and its content line added (single player only: a multiplayer
 * world's content list is the world's own) — and, on a link that is not fast, the growth (neither in multiplayer nor in
 * the baked example world, ?nomw). `o.lua`: the script's text (else fetched); `o.slow`: the link's kind (else linkRate, the last measure);
 * `o.now`, `o.setInterval`, `o.clearInterval`: a test's clock.
 */
export async function install(win = globalThis, o = {}) {
  const lua = o.lua ?? await fetch(new URL('./view.lua', import.meta.url)).then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`view.lua: HTTP ${r.status}`); return r.text(); });
  const slow = o.slow ?? !linkRate.fast(), now = o.now ?? (() => performance.now());
  const s = { phase: 'off', start: 0, target: 0, value: 0, since: 0, longAt: -Infinity, p99s: [] };
  let FS = null, timer = null;
  win.orthrosViewState = () => ({ ...s });
  win.orthrosViewBoot = (tierDistance) => {
    const target = Math.round(Number(tierDistance)) || 0;
    // (the page's own file streaming only: its game data says when it is quiet — never the baked example world, ?nomw,
    // which reads no game data over the network and writes no openmw.cfg to start the growth; never a multiplayer
    // world: its content list, the world's own, has no Orthros script to raise the view)
    const example = !!win.__FORCE_NOMW || /[?&]nomw\b/.test(win.location?.search ?? '');
    const grow = slow && !example && !win.__omwMPEnabled && target > VIEW.start && typeof win.StreamFS?.data === 'function';
    win.orthrosViewTarget = target; win.orthrosViewStart = grow ? VIEW.start : target;
    if (grow) Object.assign(s, { phase: 'wait', start: VIEW.start, target, value: VIEW.start });
    return String(win.orthrosViewStart);
  };
  const write = (v) => FS.writeFile(VIEW_FILE, `${v} ${s.start}`);
  const tick = () => {
    const data = win.StreamFS?.data?.(); if (!data) return;
    const t = now(), f = win.orthrosFrames, state = win.omw?.state ?? {}, report = parseView(state['orthros.view']);
    // (the frames of play only — the player in the world, frames drawn —: the half seconds of a boot or a load without
    // a frame (p99 0) made the usual frame 0 for the next 30 s, every frame of a 20 fps machine then a long one holding
    // the raise — an engine whose boot yields to the page (OpenMW r20, JSPI) gave this look its turns all along the
    // boot, one that holds the page's thread none: its raise 13 s later, 2026-10-30)
    if (report && f && Number.isFinite(f.p99) && f.p99 > 0) {
      s.p99s.push(f.p99); if (s.p99s.length > 60) s.p99s.shift();
      // (the usual frame once known — 5 s of samples —, else the fixed bound alone)
      const usual = s.p99s.length >= 10 ? [...s.p99s].sort((a, b) => a - b)[s.p99s.length >> 1] : 0;
      if (f.p99 > Math.max(VIEW.longFrameMs, VIEW.longFactor * usual)) s.longAt = t;
    }
    const r = growStep(s, { now: t, report, exterior: !!state['orthros.cell'], quiet: data.quiet(VIEW.quietMs), framesOk: t - s.longAt >= VIEW.holdMs });
    if (r.write !== undefined) write(r.write);
    if ('prefer' in r) data.prefer(r.prefer);
    if (s.phase === 'done' || s.phase === 'stopped') { (o.clearInterval ?? clearInterval)(timer); timer = null; }
  };
  win.orthrosContent = (fs, cfg) => {
    // (a multiplayer world checks the client's content list against its own — the native simulation's, which has no
    // orthros.omwscripts: an extra file is refused, BAD_CONTENT)
    if (win.__omwMPEnabled) return cfg;
    FS = fs;
    fs.mkdirTree(`${ROOT}/scripts/orthros`); fs.mkdirTree(`${ROOT}/orthros`);
    fs.writeFile(`${ROOT}/${CONTENT}`, 'PLAYER: scripts/orthros/view.lua\n');
    fs.writeFile(`${ROOT}/scripts/orthros/view.lua`, lua);
    if (s.phase === 'wait') write(s.value); else fs.writeFile(VIEW_FILE, '0 0');
    if (!cfg.includes(`content=${CONTENT}`)) cfg.push(`content=${CONTENT}`);
    if (s.phase === 'wait' && !timer) timer = (o.setInterval ?? setInterval)(tick, VIEW.pollMs);
    return cfg;
  };
  return { state: s, tick };
}
```

`src/ports/openmw/view.lua`:

```lua
-- Orthros' PLAYER script in the OpenMW engine (written into the engine's /resources/vfs before it starts by
-- src/ports/openmw/view-grow.js, loaded by orthros.omwscripts — always, alone or with friends: a save lists the same
-- content files whatever the link). Every half second of real time (paused too):
-- - the page's view distance, from orthros/view.txt ("<distance> <base>", rewritten by the page in the engine's
--   memory): set on the camera while the player's own setting is still the page's boot value <base> — never written to
--   the settings, so a save of the settings keeps the player's own; "0 0" leaves the camera alone;
-- - told to the page through the engine's page bridge (openmw.mp.set: window.omw.state, a string per key):
--   'orthros.view' "<view distance> <the player's setting>", 'orthros.cell' "<gridX> <gridY>" in an exterior cell,
--   "" elsewhere.
local camera = require('openmw.camera')
local core = require('openmw.core')
local vfs = require('openmw.vfs')
local mp = require('openmw.mp')
local self = require('openmw.self')

local POLL_SECONDS = 0.5
local nextAt = 0
local told = {}

local function tell(key, value)
    if told[key] ~= value then
        told[key] = value
        mp.set(key, value)
    end
end

local function wanted()
    local file = vfs.open('orthros/view.txt')
    if not file then return nil end
    local text = file:read('*a')
    file:close()
    local distance, base = string.match(text or '', '^%s*(%d+)%s+(%d+)')
    return tonumber(distance), tonumber(base)
end

local function poll()
    local ok, distance, base = pcall(wanted)
    local setting = camera.getBaseViewDistance()
    if ok and distance and distance > 0 and base and math.abs(setting - base) < 1
        and math.abs(camera.getViewDistance() - distance) >= 1 then
        camera.setViewDistance(distance)
    end
    tell('orthros.view', string.format('%d %d', math.floor(camera.getViewDistance() + 0.5), math.floor(setting + 0.5)))
    local cell = self.cell
    if cell and cell.isExterior then
        tell('orthros.cell', string.format('%d %d', cell.gridX, cell.gridY))
    else
        tell('orthros.cell', '')
    end
end

return {
    engineHandlers = {
        onFrame = function()
            local now = core.getRealTime()
            if now < nextAt then return end
            nextAt = now + POLL_SECONDS
            local ok, err = pcall(poll)
            if not ok then print('[orthros] view: ' .. tostring(err)) end
        end,
    },
}

```

`src/ports/openmw/wasm-code-cache.js`:

```js
// Put into the OpenMW engine's page by the Orthros server (src/host/openmw.js withWasmStream), ahead of the engine's
// Module literal and glue: the engine's module compiled in a worker (wasm-compile-worker.js) and instantiated here,
// through the engine glue's Module.instantiateWasm (docs/openmw.md "Chrome's code cache off the main thread"). Chrome
// keeps a WebAssembly code cache for a module streamed from a fetched answer, and works it on the thread that compiled
// it: read at the compile (wasm.Deserialize, 270-320 ms), then — each time V8 has ~1 MB of new optimized code — the
// whole module serialized again (20-50 ms on a thread-pool thread) and its 18-25 MB copy handed to the cache by that
// thread (OnMoreFunctionsCanBeSerialized: 21-57 ms measured on the page's main thread, a task with no script —
// "(program)" in a profile; six in the first 30 s of play on a first visit after a release, one or two on later
// visits). Compiled in the worker, all of that runs on the worker's thread; the module is the same (its code, its
// tier-up shared with the page's instance and the pthreads, which instantiate the module the page posts them, as before).
// The worker is started as this script runs (its script and its isolate ready while the glue downloads), told the
// module's URL when the glue asks. The worker failing: the module streamed here as the glue did. The instantiation
// failing, or the module unavailable here as well: the glue's abort (Module.onAbort, the page's fatal overlay).
// ?omwenv=OPENMW_ORTHROS_WASMWORKER=0: the glue's own path.
(() => {
  const env = /[?&]omwenv=([^&]*)/.exec(location.search);
  let off = false; try { off = !!env && decodeURIComponent(env[1]).split(',').includes('OPENMW_ORTHROS_WASMWORKER=0'); } catch { /* a malformed address: on */ }
  if (off || typeof Worker !== 'function' || typeof WebAssembly !== 'object' || typeof WebAssembly.compileStreaming !== 'function') return;
  let worker = null; // (kept for the page's life: the cache's later writes run on its thread)
  /** @type {Promise<WebAssembly.Module>} the worker's answer */
  let answer;
  try {
    const w = worker = new Worker('/src/ports/openmw/wasm-compile-worker.js');
    answer = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      w.onmessage = (e) => (e.data && e.data.module instanceof WebAssembly.Module ? resolve(e.data.module) : reject(new Error((e.data && e.data.error) || 'no module')));
      w.onerror = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); reject(new Error(e.message || 'worker failed')); };
    });
  } catch (e) { worker = null; answer = Promise.reject(e); }
  answer.catch(() => { /* reported when the glue asks */ });
  // (the glue's Module.instantiateWasm(imports, receive): receive(instance, module) once instantiated; its return unused)
  window.orthrosInstantiateWasm = function (imports, receive) {
    const M = window.Module, url = new URL(M && M.locateFile ? M.locateFile('openmw.wasm') : 'openmw.wasm', location.href).href;
    const here = () => WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(url, { credentials: 'same-origin' }), imports)
      .catch(() => fetch(url, { credentials: 'same-origin' }).then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()).then((b) => WebAssembly.instantiate(b, imports)));
    if (worker) worker.postMessage({ url });
    answer
      .then((module) => ({ module }), (e) => { console.warn('[orthros wasm] compiled here:', e && e.message); if (worker) worker.terminate(); worker = null; return null; })
      // (only the worker's failure falls back: an instantiation error would be the same here, so it is reported)
      .then((c) => (c ? WebAssembly.instantiate(c.module, imports).then((instance) => ({ instance, module: c.module })) : here()))
      .then((r) => receive(r.instance, r.module))
      .catch((e) => {
        // (as the glue's own path ends: its abort calls Module.onAbort, the page's fatal overlay, then throws)
        console.error('[orthros wasm] failed to prepare the module:', e);
        const m = window.Module;
        if (m && typeof m.onAbort === 'function') m.onAbort(e); else throw e;
      });
    return {};
  };
})();

```

`src/ports/openmw/wasm-compile-worker.js`:

```js
// The OpenMW engine module compiled off the page's main thread (src/ports/openmw/wasm-code-cache.js): streamed from its
// fetched answer here, so Chrome's WebAssembly code cache — read at the compile, written again each time V8 has more
// optimized code — works on this worker's thread, the page's main thread never. The compiled module goes to the page
// (one module: the page's instance and its pthreads share its code and its tier-up). Kept alive by the page for that.
self.onmessage = (e) => {
  WebAssembly.compileStreaming(fetch(e.data.url, { credentials: 'same-origin' }))
    .then((module) => self.postMessage({ module }), (err) => self.postMessage({ error: String((err && err.message) || err) }));
};
```

`src/ports/port-files.js`:

```js
// The game files of a browser port whose engine runs in the page (GoldSrc, re3 — CLAUDE.md "Standardization"): the
// game data every Orthros game reads (src/vfs/data-client.js: the data worker, the browser's OPFS copy, the learned
// order, the whole download) opened at the page's start, beside the engine's download (openPortData), then the copy an
// earlier page kept in IndexedDB handed over to it and the files mounted in the engine's file system
// (src/vfs/emscripten-files.js) once the engine is in (mountPortFiles), what earlier sessions read first loaded before
// the start; the loading indicator every game shows while it waits for its data (src/host/web/data-meter.js).
import '../host/web/data-meter.js'; // (the loading indicator, before the game data: attached to it — data-client.js)
import { GameData, PIECE } from '../vfs/data-client.js';
import { mountFiles } from '../vfs/emscripten-files.js';
import { eachStorage, removeStorage } from './goldsrc/storage.js';

/**
 * A port page's engine file addresses: `at(rel)` the URL of release path `rel` — by its content when the server gives it
 * (/api/manifest engineUrls, src/host/engine-content.js: a release's unchanged files keep their address, and the
 * browser's copy), else under the release (/engines/<release>/<rel>, encoded `encode`d).
 * @param {{ engineUrls?: Record<string, string> }} config the version's /api/manifest
 * @param {string} release the engine release's id
 */
export const engineUrls = (config, release, encode = false) => {
  const base = `/engines/${encodeURIComponent(release)}/`;
  return (rel) => config.engineUrls?.[rel] ?? base + (encode ? rel.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/') : rel);
};

/** Bytes per message to the data worker while an earlier copy is handed over. */
const BATCH = 16 << 20;

/**
 * The installation's game data opened now, as soon as the page knows its version — not after its engine: the data
 * worker, the version's store and the learned order's list ready while the engine downloads and compiles
 * (docs/slow-network.md "Opened early"). Returns the GameData at once (its `ready` settles once the worker answered);
 * mountPortFiles mounts it once the engine's file system exists.
 * @param {{ name: string, tree: object, manifest?: object, session: string, lang?: string, log: (text: string) => void }} o
 *   tree, manifest: the version's, as the page fetched them (not asked again: game-data.js openVersion)
 */
export function openPortData(o) {
  const data = new GameData({ name: o.name, tree: o.tree, manifest: o.manifest, session: o.session, lang: o.lang, prefetch: 'startup', orderAtOpen: true, log: o.log,
    // (the page's ?piecereuse=0: its pieces each a copy of its own, left to the collector — GameData's pieceReuse)
    pieceReuse: new URLSearchParams(globalThis.location?.search ?? '').get('piecereuse') !== '0' });
  data.ready.catch(() => {}); // (its failure told where the page waits for it: mountPortFiles)
  return data;
}

/**
 * The game data an openPortData opened, its files mounted under `root` once it is ready: { data, nodes }.
 * @param {GameData} data
 * @param {{ name: string, files: { path: string, at?: string }[], FS: object, root: string, log: (text: string) => void,
 *   db?: IDBDatabase, asyncReads?: boolean, rewritable?: boolean, onCopy?: (bytes: number) => void,
 *   onProgress?: (p: object) => void }} o
 *   files: the tree's files as the engine sees them (a language's view: languageFiles); db: the installation's IndexedDB,
 *   whose 'content' store an earlier page kept the game files in (handed over, then emptied)
 */
export async function mountPortFiles(data, o) {
  await data.ready;
  if (o.onProgress) data.onProgress(o.onProgress); // (the loading in the background: the shell's pill, shell.setData)
  if (o.db) await handOver(data, o.name, o.db, o.log, o.onCopy);
  const nodes = mountFiles(o.FS, o.root, data, o.name, o.files, { asyncReads: o.asyncReads, rewritable: o.rewritable, log: o.log });
  data.times.mounted = Math.round(performance.now());
  return { data, nodes };
}

/**
 * The game files an earlier page kept in IndexedDB ('content': `<path>\n<size>\n<mtime>` whole, `…\n#<piece>` 64 KiB
 * pieces) into the game data's store — those of the files as they are now —, then removed.
 */
async function handOver(data, name, db, log, onCopy = () => {}) {
  let batch = [], bytes = 0, moved = 0;
  const keys = [];
  const send = () => { if (batch.length) { data.migrate(batch); moved += bytes; onCopy(moved); } batch = []; bytes = 0; };
  try {
    await eachStorage(db, 'content', (key, value) => {
      keys.push(key);
      if (typeof key !== 'string' || !(value instanceof Uint8Array)) return;
      const cut = key.lastIndexOf('\n#'), file = cut < 0 ? key : key.slice(0, cut), [path, size, mtime] = file.split('\n');
      const h = data.file(name, path);
      if (!h || h.size !== Number(size) || h.mtime !== Number(mtime)) return; // (a file since changed: not handed over)
      batch.push({ name, path: h.path, at: cut < 0 ? 0 : Number(key.slice(cut + 2)) * PIECE, bytes: value }); bytes += value.length;
      if (bytes >= BATCH) send();
    });
    send();
    if (keys.length) await removeStorage(db, 'content', keys);
    if (moved) log(`Earlier copy of the game files handed over: ${Math.round(moved / 1048576)} MB`);
  } catch (error) { log('Earlier copy of the game files not handed over: ' + (error?.message ?? error)); }
}

```

`src/ports/re3/ini.js`:

```js
// The settings a game language puts in the engine's ini files (the manifest's re3.languages.<code>.ini,
// docs/browser-ports.md "re3 ports"): each key set in its section, everything else of the file kept byte for byte — its
// other lines, their order, comments, spacing and line endings. A file is edited as its bytes, one character each
// (latin1): the manifest's names and values are printable ASCII (src/host/re3.js), so what did not change is written
// back as it was read.

const BOM = '\xef\xbb\xbf'; // (UTF-8's, read as latin1)
const SECTION = /^\s*\[([^\]]*)\]/;
// (a key line: its indentation, name, separator with its spaces, value; a name never starts a comment nor a section)
const KEY = /^(\s*)([^\s=;#[][^=]*?)(\s*=[ \t]*)(.*)$/;

/** A file's bytes as text, one character per byte. */
export function bytesToText(bytes) {
  let s = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 0x8000) s += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));
  return s;
}
/** Text of one character per byte back to its bytes. */
export const textToBytes = (text) => Uint8Array.from(text, (c) => c.charCodeAt(0) & 0xff);

/**
 * `text` with each key of `sections` ({ <section>: { <key>: <value> } }) set: in place where the section has it (in
 * every section of that name, every line of that key: whichever one the engine reads), else added after the section's
 * last line, a missing section added at the end. Section and key names compare without case, as ini readers do; a
 * value is written and compared without the spaces around it, as they read it (the line's own spacing kept). Nothing to
 * change: `text` itself — the same settings set again change nothing.
 */
export function setIni(text, sections) {
  const bom = text.startsWith(BOM) ? BOM : '', body = text.slice(bom.length);
  const lines = body.match(/[^\n]*\n|[^\n]+$/g) ?? [];
  const eol = /\r\n/.test(body) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
  const wanted = new Map(Object.entries(sections).map(([name, keys]) => [name.toLowerCase(),
    { name, last: -1, keys: new Map(Object.entries(keys).map(([key, value]) => [key.toLowerCase(), { key, value: String(value).trim(), found: false }])) }]));
  let current = null;
  lines.forEach((line, i) => {
    const content = line.replace(/\r?\n$/, ''), end = line.slice(content.length);
    const s = SECTION.exec(content);
    if (s) { current = wanted.get(s[1].trim().toLowerCase()) ?? null; if (current) current.last = i; return; }
    if (!current) return;
    if (content.trim()) current.last = i; // (the section's last line that is not blank: added keys go after it)
    const k = KEY.exec(content), entry = k && current.keys.get(k[2].toLowerCase());
    if (!entry) return;
    entry.found = true;
    if (k[4].trimEnd() !== entry.value) lines[i] = k[1] + k[2] + k[3] + entry.value + end;
  });
  const added = (keys) => [...keys.values()].filter((e) => !e.found).map((e) => `${e.key}=${e.value}${eol}`);
  // (into the sections there, the last first: the earlier ones keep their place)
  for (const w of [...wanted.values()].filter((w) => w.last >= 0).sort((a, b) => b.last - a.last)) {
    const more = added(w.keys); if (!more.length) continue;
    if (!lines[w.last].endsWith('\n')) lines[w.last] += eol;
    lines.splice(w.last + 1, 0, ...more);
  }
  const missing = [...wanted.values()].filter((w) => w.last < 0 && w.keys.size);
  if (missing.length) {
    if (lines.length && !lines.at(-1).endsWith('\n')) lines[lines.length - 1] += eol;
    for (const w of missing) lines.push(...(lines.length && lines.at(-1).trim() ? [eol] : []), `[${w.name}]${eol}`, ...added(w.keys));
  }
  const out = bom + lines.join('');
  return out === text ? text : out;
}

/** `text`'s keys: section (lowercase) → key (lowercase) → value, without the spaces around; a key's last line wins. */
export function readIni(text) {
  const out = new Map(); let current = null;
  for (const line of text.replace(/^\xef\xbb\xbf/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const s = SECTION.exec(line);
    if (s) { const name = s[1].trim().toLowerCase(); current = out.get(name) ?? new Map(); out.set(name, current); continue; }
    const k = current && KEY.exec(line);
    if (k) current.set(k[2].toLowerCase(), k[4].trim());
  }
  return out;
}

/** The section where an ini file records the defaults it got (setIniDefaults): `<section>.<key>=<value>` each. */
export const DEFAULTS_SECTION = 'OrthrosDefaults';
/**
 * `text` with defaults ({ <section>: { <key>: <value> } }) set once: a key whose default the file has not got yet takes
 * it, and the file records it (DEFAULTS_SECTION, which the engine keeps as any section of its file); afterwards the
 * player's own choice stays. A default the manifest changes is set once more.
 */
export function setIniDefaults(text, defaults) {
  const got = readIni(text).get(DEFAULTS_SECTION.toLowerCase()) ?? new Map(), set = {}, marks = {};
  for (const [section, keys] of Object.entries(defaults)) {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(keys)) {
      const mark = `${section}.${key}`;
      if (got.get(mark.toLowerCase()) === String(value).trim()) continue;
      (set[section] ??= {})[key] = value; marks[mark] = value;
    }
  }
  return Object.keys(marks).length ? setIni(setIni(text, set), { [DEFAULTS_SECTION]: marks }) : text;
}

```

```js
// Async asset loading outlives the original click. Resume the engine's audio on the next user gesture.
const audioContexts = new Set(), NativeAudioContext = globalThis.AudioContext;
if (NativeAudioContext) globalThis.AudioContext = class extends NativeAudioContext {
  constructor(...args) { super(...args); audioContexts.add(this); }
};
// (the engine's output measured: its level the last seconds, for the "sound blocked" hint and the session's report)
const audioMeter = { peak: 0, heard: 0 };
const NativeConnect = AudioNode.prototype.connect;
AudioNode.prototype.connect = function (target, ...rest) {
  if (target instanceof AudioDestinationNode && !target.context.__meter) {
    const meter = target.context.__meter = target.context.createAnalyser(); meter.fftSize = 1024;
    NativeConnect.call(this, meter);
  } else if (target instanceof AudioDestinationNode) NativeConnect.call(this, target.context.__meter);
  return NativeConnect.call(this, target, ...rest);
};
setInterval(() => {
  const buf = new Float32Array(1024); let peak = 0;
  for (const context of audioContexts) { if (!context.__meter) continue; context.__meter.getFloatTimeDomainData(buf); for (const v of buf) peak = Math.max(peak, Math.abs(v)); }
  audioMeter.peak = Math.max(audioMeter.peak * 0.9, peak); if (peak > 0.01) audioMeter.heard = performance.now();
}, 250);
const audioState = () => ({ contexts: [...audioContexts].map((c) => c.state), heard: audioMeter.heard ? Math.round((performance.now() - audioMeter.heard) / 1000) : null });
const resumeAudio = () => {
  for (const context of audioContexts) if (context.state !== 'running' && context.state !== 'closed') context.resume().then(() => soundHint(), log);
  soundHint();
};
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', resumeAudio, { capture: true });
document.addEventListener('keydown', resumeAudio, { capture: true });
// (the browser keeps the sound off until the page is used: told, with a button, while it is)
function soundHint() {
  const blocked = session.state === 'running' && [...audioContexts].some((c) => c.state === 'suspended');
  shell?.sound.classList.toggle('hidden', !blocked);
}
setInterval(soundHint, 1000);

function log(line) { logs.push(String(line)); if (logs.length > 500) logs.shift(); shell?.log(String(line)); }
/** The engine's normal ways out: Emscripten's exit (ExitStatus) and the unwinding of its main loop. */
const isExit = (e) => e === 'unwind' || e?.name === 'ExitStatus';
window.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
  if (isExit(event.error) || (stopped && event.error === Infinity)) { event.preventDefault(); return; }
  log(`Page error: ${event.message}`); report('error', { message: String(event.message).slice(0, 300), where: 'page' });
});
window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (event) => {
  if (isExit(event.reason)) { event.preventDefault(); return; } // (the engine's glue rethrows its exit: the game ended)
  log(`Unhandled: ${event.reason?.message ?? event.reason}`); report('error', { message: String(event.reason?.message ?? event.reason).slice(0, 300), where: 'promise' });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what the server learns of a session (/api/telemetry)
// (its start, its errors with the end of the engine's log, its end with its length and frame rate; a few a session)
/** the passive session record (perf-page.js: every 2 min of play and at the end, docs/real-machine-bench.md) */
let perfRecord = null;
/** the browser's storage of the game data: persistent asked at the start, its state in the telemetry (storage-persist.js) */
const storage = pageStorage();
const telemetry = portEvents({ port: 're3', state: () => session.state, storage, bench: params.get('benchrun') });
const report = (event, data) => telemetry.report(event, data);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loading screen and passing messages
const toast = (text, ms = 5000) => shell?.toast(text, ms);
/** A status line: in the loading screen while it shows, then as a passing message over the game. */
const status = (text, error = false) => shell?.phase(text, error);
/** The start's steps (engine, files, game), each weighing its usual share of the wait; never going back. */
const progress = { weights: { engine: 0.2, files: 0.6, game: 0.2 }, parts: {} };
function step(k, state, value = '', fraction = undefined) {
  shell.step(k, state, value);
  progress.parts[k] = state === 'skip' ? null : fraction ?? (state === 'done' ? 1 : progress.parts[k] ?? 0);
  let weight = 0, done = 0;
  for (const [key, f] of Object.entries(progress.parts)) if (f !== null) { weight += progress.weights[key]; done += progress.weights[key] * f; }
  shell.progress(weight ? done / weight * 100 : 0);
}
function hideLoader() {
  if (!shell || shell.loader.classList.contains('hidden')) return;
  step('game', 'done');
  shell.hideLoader();
  gameData?.mark('playable'); // (the game shown: what it read until now is its launch set, src/vfs/launch-set.js)
  shell.running = true; shell.watchPointer(document);
  status(S.running);
}
/** The loading screen again, with its message and buttons (the end of the game, an error): the mouse given back. */
function showEnd(text, error, buttons) {
  shell.running = false; shell.showLoader(); status(text, error);
  if (document.pointerLockElement) document.exitPointerLock();
  const acts = Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { className: 'acts' });
  for (const { label, primary, onclick } of buttons) {
    const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.className = primary ? 'primary' : ''; b.textContent = label; b.onclick = onclick;
    acts.append(b);
  }
  shell.choices.replaceChildren(acts);
  acts.querySelector('button')?.focus();
}
const fail = (error) => {
  if (session.state === 'error') { log(error?.stack ?? error); return; } // (one report: an abort then its rejection)
  const crashed = profileReady; // (an engine that ran: its profile is kept; a new start reloads the page — a stopped engine cannot start again)
  session.state = 'error'; log(error?.stack ?? error); world?.link.close();
  report('crash', { message: String(error?.message ?? error).slice(0, 300), crashed, log: logs.slice(-30).map((l) => l.slice(0, 200)) });
  if (timer) clearInterval(timer); if (cloudTimer) clearInterval(cloudTimer);
  if (!shell) return;
  showEnd(S.failed + (error?.message ?? error), true, [{ label: S.restart, primary: true, onclick: restart }]);
  if (crashed) finalSave = saveAndPush();
};
/**
 * The game ended (the player quit it from its menu: main() returned, or the engine exited): the profile saved here and
 * on the account, then the loading screen with "the game has ended", to start it again or go back to the games.
 */
function ended(code) {
  if (session.state === 'ended' || session.state === 'error' || !shell) return;
  log(`The game ended (${code ?? 0})`);
  endReport();
  session.state = 'ended'; session.exitCode = code ?? 0; world?.link.close();
  if (timer) clearInterval(timer); if (cloudTimer) clearInterval(cloudTimer);
  if (document.fullscreenElement) document.exitFullscreen().catch(() => {});
  showEnd(S.ended, false, [{ label: S.restart, primary: true, onclick: restart }, { label: S.back, onclick: () => shell.quit() }]);
  finalSave = saveAndPush();
}
/** Start again: the page reloaded (an engine that ran cannot start again in it) once the profile's last save is done. */
async function restart(event) {
  if (event?.currentTarget) event.currentTarget.disabled = true;
  await finalSave;
  location.reload();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the game's place: the window under the header
// (SDL sizes the game's screen to the canvas' size on the page: the game renders at the size it is shown, without
// bars; a mouse position maps one to one)
function fit() {
  const stage = $('stage'), canvas = $('canvas'), w = Math.max(320, stage.clientWidth), h = Math.max(240, stage.clientHeight);
  if (canvas.style.width === w + 'px' && canvas.style.height === h + 'px') return;
  canvas.style.width = w + 'px'; canvas.style.height = h + 'px';
  // (SDL measures it again at the window's resize only: the header hidden or shown changes none)
  if (session.state === 'running') queueMicrotask(() => dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')));
}
addEventListener('resize', fit);
document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', fit);
// (the engine's glue resets the canvas' style when it sets its size: put back)
new MutationObserver(fit).observe($('canvas'), { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['style', 'width', 'height'] });
fit();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the mouse
// The engine captures the mouse itself when the game takes it (SDL's relative mode: pointer lock at the next input
// event) and tells the page (Module.orthrosMouse: true in the game, false in its menus — where it may draw its own
// cursor over a hidden one, so the canvas' CSS cursor tells nothing); for an engine that does not tell, its hidden
// cursor. A click captures it again only while the game wants it — after the browser released it (Esc) — never where the
// mouse must stay free.
let engineMouse = null;
const wantsMouse = () => session.state === 'running' && (engineMouse ?? $('canvas').style.cursor === 'none');
// (how to capture the mouse: told the first time the game wants it)
let captureTold = false;
function tellCapture() {
  if (captureTold || !wantsMouse() || document.pointerLockElement) return;
  captureTold = true; toast(S.capture, 7000);
}
new MutationObserver(tellCapture).observe($('canvas'), { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['style'] });
/** The engine took the mouse (the game) or freed it (a menu). */
function onMouseMode(relative) { engineMouse = relative; tellCapture(); }
escapeToGame(window); // (the first Escape to the game, the next frees the mouse)
$('canvas').addEventListener('pointerdown', () => { if (wantsMouse() && document.pointerLockElement !== $('canvas')) $('canvas').requestPointerLock()?.catch?.(() => {}); });
$('canvas').addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => event.preventDefault());
// (the engine may free the mouse a moment after the lock ends: only a release by the player is told)
document.addEventListener('pointerlockchange', () => setTimeout(() => { if (!document.pointerLockElement && wantsMouse() && !stopped) toast(S.released, 4000); }, 150));
/** The header's mouse indicator clicked: the game gets the mouse when it wants it, else the keys. */
function giveMouse() {
  $('canvas').focus();
  if (wantsMouse()) $('canvas').requestPointerLock()?.catch?.(() => {}); else toast(S.capture, 5000);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the header's frame rate
// (a frame is one the engine displayed: it calls Module.orthrosFrame after each)
const perf = { frames: [], samples: [], started: 0 };
function onFrame() {
  perfRecord?.shown();
  gameData?.progress(); // (the engine went on: the reads it asked for ahead are not waits — data-client.js holdCheck)
  perf.frames.push(performance.now());
  if (perf.frames.length > 400) perf.frames.splice(0, perf.frames.length - 400);
  if (session.state === 'running' && ++perf.started === 10) hideLoader(); // (its first images: the game is shown)
}
setInterval(() => {
  const now = performance.now(), recent = perf.frames.filter((t) => t > now - 500);
  const gaps = recent.slice(1).map((t, i) => t - recent[i]).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  perf.samples.push({ fps: recent.length * 2, max: gaps.at(-1) ?? 0, p99: gaps[Math.floor(gaps.length * 0.99)] ?? 0 });
  if (perf.samples.length > 120) perf.samples.shift();
  shell?.setFps(perf.samples, session.state !== 'running' || perf.started < 10 ? 'loading' : document.hidden ? 'paused' : 'running');
  const seed = seedWatch?.step(now, perf.started); if (seed) reportSeed(seed);
}, 500);
/** The session's end, once: its length and frame rate. */
function endReport() { perfRecord?.end(); telemetry.end({ frames: frameStats(), audio: audioState() }); }
/** The last minute's frame rate and slowest frames, for the session's report. */
function frameStats() {
  const a = perf.samples.filter((x) => x.fps > 0); if (!a.length) return null;
  return { fps: Math.round(a.reduce((t, x) => t + x.fps, 0) / a.length), p99: Math.round(Math.max(...a.map((x) => x.p99))) };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the profile, here and on the account (cloud-sync.js)
const name = decodeURIComponent(location.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)[2] ?? '');
const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '').slice(0, 24);
let config, tree, files, gameData;
/**
 * The profile now: the engine's tree once it is in place, else — before, or once saves of it stopped (the page goes, or
 * the account's copy replaced it) — the one kept in this browser.
 */
// (the profile's snapshot taken again only once the engine changed a file — a walk of the whole game folder, 1,500 files,
// a hitch in a frame: FS writes, removals and renames mark it)
let profileDirty = true, profileCache = null;
function snapshot() {
  if (profileDirty || !profileCache) { profileCache = profileSnapshot(FS, ROOT, gameNodes); profileDirty = false; }
  return profileCache;
}
function watchProfileWrites() {
  for (const op of ['write', 'unlink', 'rename', 'rmdir', 'mkdir', 'truncate', 'ftruncate', 'symlink']) {
    const original = FS[op]; if (typeof original !== 'function') continue;
    FS[op] = function (...a) { profileDirty = true; return original.apply(this, a); };
  }
}
const currentProfile = async () => (profileReady && !stopped ? snapshot() : (await readStorage(db, 'profile', 'files')) ?? []);
function newCloud(username) {
  return new CloudSave({
    game: name, user: username,
    // (the account's copy put in place while the game runs: recorded as in step, the page reloaded to start on it)
    onStatus: (s) => { if (!world?.link.joined()) shell.setSave(s); if (reloadWhenSaved && s.state === 'saved') location.reload(); },
    read: async () => toCloud(await currentProfile()),
    // The account's files in place of the profile, the previous one kept aside in the same store: before the engine
    // starts; or once it has, a conflict settled from the header — the engine's files are not replaced under it: no
    // more saves of them, and the page reloads to start on the account's (the game over: they wait for its restart).
    write: async (list) => {
      const replacing = profileReady && !stopped;
      if (replacing) stopped = true;
      try {
        const old = replacing ? snapshot() : await readStorage(db, 'profile', 'files');
        if (old?.length) await writeStorage(db, 'profile', `aside-${new Date().toISOString()}`, old);
        await writeStorage(db, 'profile', 'files', list.map((f) => ({ path: f.path, data: f.data })));
      } catch (error) { if (replacing) stopped = false; throw error; }
      if (replacing && session.state === 'running') reloadWhenSaved = true;
    },
  });
}
/**
 * Signed in while the game runs: its profile sent to the account, unless the account has another one — then the
 * player chooses: restart with the account's, or this browser's sent over it.
 */
async function lateSignIn(user) {
  if (cloud || !db) return;
  cloud = newCloud(user.username);
  const head = await cloud.remoteHead().catch(() => null);
  cloud.remoteHash = head;
  if (!head) { if (session.state === 'running') await save(); cloud.push(); return; }
  const choice = await shell.ask({ title: S.lateTitle, text: S.lateText(config.name), buttons: [{ value: 'account', label: S.lateAccount, primary: true }, { value: 'device', label: S.lateDevice }] });
  if (choice === 'account') { stopped = true; if (timer) clearInterval(timer); if (cloudTimer) clearInterval(cloudTimer); try { const remote = await cloud.fetchRemote(); if (remote) await cloud.applyRemote(remote); } finally { location.reload(); } }
  else if (choice === 'device') { await save(); cloud.resolve('device'); }
  else cloud.set({ state: 'conflict' });
}

let savedSnapshot = null;
async function save() {
  if (!db || !profileReady || saving || stopped) return saving; // (stopped: the page goes, or the account's copy replaces this one)
  const files = snapshot();
  if (files === savedSnapshot) return; // (nothing written since the last save)
  saving = writeStorage(db, 'profile', 'files', files);
  try { await saving; savedSnapshot = files; session.lastSaveAt = Date.now(); } finally { saving = null; }
}
session.save = save;
/** The profile saved as it is now — after a save in flight, whose snapshot may be older — then sent to the account. */
async function saveAndPush() {
  try {
    while (saving) await saving.catch(() => {});
    await save();
    const sent = cloud ? await cloud.push() : null;
    return !sent || !['error', 'toobig', 'conflict'].includes(sent.state);
  } catch (error) { log('Profile save failed: ' + (error?.message ?? error)); return false; }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the shared first-launch profile (profile-seed.js)
// A game's first start may write caches before the player does anything (a sound cache built by reading the header of
// every audio file: a long first start on a slow link). With the manifest's `profileSeed`, an empty profile gets the
// small files first sessions of the version wrote identical (the server's quorum), in place before the engine starts;
// else this session reports its own, taken at the player's first input, once it has gone on playing (SeedWatch). The
// ini files the version's languages and defaults name are left out: the player's settings, the screen's size among them.
let seedWatch = null, seedLanguage = null;
/** The files a seed may hold now: the profile's but its ini files. */
const seedFiles = (iniNames) => profileSnapshot(FS, ROOT, gameNodes).filter((f) => !iniNames.has(f.path.toLowerCase()));
/** The server's set put in the empty profile (true), or a watch of this first session set (false). */
async function seedProfile(language, iniNames) {
  const url = `/api/profile-seed/${encodeURIComponent(name)}?lang=${encodeURIComponent(language ?? '')}`;
  let files = [];
  try {
    const ac = new AbortController(), timer = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 3000); // (never holds the start long)
    const r = await fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal }).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
    const j = r.ok ? await r.json() : null;
    files = (Array.isArray(j?.files) ? j.files : []).map((f) => ({ path: f?.path, data: fromBase64(f?.data) })).filter((f) => f.data && seedPathOk(f.path) && !iniNames.has(f.path.toLowerCase()));
  } catch { /* none: learned below */ }
  if (files.length) { restoreProfile(FS, ROOT, files, log); log(`Profile: ${files.length} file(s) first sessions wrote put in place (shared first-launch profile)`); return true; }
  seedLanguage = language ?? '';
  seedWatch = new SeedWatch({ files: () => seedFiles(iniNames) });
  return false;
}
function reportSeed(files) {
  fetch(`/api/profile-seed/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ lang: seedLanguage, session: sessionId, files: files.map((f) => ({ path: f.path, data: toBase64(f.data) })) }) }).catch(() => {});
}
// (the player's first input: what the game wrote until then, before anything typed)
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => seedWatch?.input(performance.now(), perf.started, false), { capture: true });
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => seedWatch?.input(performance.now(), perf.started, event.key.length === 1), { capture: true });

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the shared world (docs/mmo.md, section 6)
// A version with `mmo` has a world on the server (src/host/mmo.js, /api/mmo/<version>/ws). The engine owns its rules and
// every record; the page gives it, as Module.orthrosNet, the shared link (mmo-link.js: open, close, state, refusal,
// send, drain, away…) and what only the page knows: user() the Orthros account's name ('' when none); signIn() the
// account window over the game; `testing` (a boolean: ?mmotest in the page's address); `testCommands` (strings the
// engine takes one a frame) and debug(json) (the engine's state, every 500 ms under test). The link opens when the
// engine asks — its main menu's Multiplayer —, never before. A sign-in, a sign-out or another account on this page
// renews it (link.renew()): a link in use connects again as the account now signed in — the engine says HELLO again
// and is accepted, or refused (a sign-out: REFUSED 1, the world left) —, a refused one (waiting on a sign-in) opens
// again; a closed one stays closed. window.orthrosMmo: { link, state (the engine's last
// debug object), updates, at, command(text) } — tools/re3/mmo-check.mjs drives two pages through it.
/** @type {{ link: ReturnType<typeof createMmoLink>, net: object } | null} */
let world = null, signInAsked = false, signInAsking = false;
function createWorld(versionId, username) {
  const url = new URL(`/api/mmo/${encodeURIComponent(versionId)}/ws`, location.href);
  url.protocol = location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss:' : 'ws:';
  let last = LINK.CLOSED, lostInWorld = false, shownJoined = false;
  const link = createMmoLink({ url, log: (line) => log(`Shared world: ${line}`), onState: (state, l) => {
    session.world = { state, refusal: l.refusal(), joined: l.joined() };
    if (state !== last) {
      if (state === LINK.WAITING && last === LINK.OPEN && l.joined()) { lostInWorld = true; toast(S.worldLost, 6000); }
      else if (state === LINK.OPEN && lostInWorld) { lostInWorld = false; toast(S.worldBack, 3000); }
      else if (state === LINK.CLOSED || state === LINK.REFUSED) lostInWorld = false;
      last = state;
    }
    // (the header's saves: the world's server keeps the character while one is in the world)
    if (l.joined() !== shownJoined) { shownJoined = l.joined(); shell?.setSave(shownJoined ? { state: 'server' } : cloud?.status ?? null); }
  } });
  link.away(document.hidden);
  const probe = { link, state: null, updates: 0, at: 0, command: (text) => net.testCommands.push(String(text)) };
  const net = {
    ...link,
    user: () => shell?.account?.username ?? '',
    signIn: () => askSignIn(),
    testing: params.has('mmotest'),
    testCommands: [],
    debug: (json) => {
      // (a C float printed as nan/inf is no JSON number: read as null, the rest of the state kept)
      try { probe.state = JSON.parse(json); } catch {
        try { probe.state = { ...JSON.parse(String(json).replace(/(?<=[:,\[])\s*-?(?:nan|inf(?:inity)?)\b/gi, 'null')), nonFinite: true }; }
        catch { probe.state = { error: 'not JSON', text: String(json).slice(0, 65536) }; }
      }
      probe.updates++; probe.at = performance.now();
    },
  };
  window.orthrosMmo = probe;
  let account = username;
  onAccountChange(({ user }) => {
    const now = user?.username ?? null;
    if (now === account) return;
    account = now;
    if (user && signInAsked) { signInAsked = false; window.orthrosData?.close?.(); $('canvas').focus(); } // (back to the game)
    link.renew();
  });
  return { link, net };
}
/**
 * The engine asks for a sign-in (its multiplayer needs an Orthros account; the server refused the link with 1): who is
 * signed in asked of the server again — the page's own idea may be stale (a session ended elsewhere) —; signed in
 * there after all: the link tried again; else the account window (data-manager.js) — a modal dialog, over the game in
 * full screen too (the top layer); the mouse freed; closed once signed in.
 */
async function askSignIn() {
  if (signInAsking) return; // (the server's answer on its way)
  if (document.pointerLockElement) document.exitPointerLock();
  signInAsking = true;
  const st = await accountState({ fresh: true }).catch(() => null);
  signInAsking = false;
  if (st && !st.accounts) return; // (a server without accounts: the engine shows the refusal)
  if (st?.user) { world?.link.renew(); return; }
  signInAsked = true;
  if (window.orthrosData?.open) window.orthrosData.open('account');
  else toast(S.worldSignIn, 9000);
}

/** The game's language: the one chosen on the home screen (?gameLang=, else remembered), among the version's. */
function gameLanguage(man) {
  const options = man.languages ?? [];
  let wanted = params.get('gameLang'); if (!options.includes(wanted)) { try { wanted = localStorage.getItem('orthros.gameLanguage.' + (man.gameId ?? name)); } catch { wanted = null; } }
  return options.includes(wanted) ? wanted : options.includes(lang) ? lang : options.includes('en') ? 'en' : options[0] ?? null;
}

const fmtMB = (bytes) => `${(bytes / 1048576).toFixed(bytes < 10485760 ? 1 : 0)} MB`;
/**
 * The game started: the account's saves first, then the engine, the files, the profile, the game's own start; `mode`:
 * one of the version's ways to play it (re3.modes: its arguments after re3.args), or none.
 */
async function start(mode = null) {
  session.state = 'starting'; session.mode = mode;
  storage.ask(); // (before the game data's first write: the store, the saves — storage-persist.js)
  perfRecord ??= portPerf({ runtime: 're3', storage, game: name, session: telemetry.session, version: config.version ?? null, bench: params.get('benchrun'), phase: () => session.state, data: () => portDataSummary(gameData, engine, { root: ROOT }), gl: () => canvasGl($('canvas')) });
  if (!crossOriginIsolated) throw new Error(S.isolated);
  if (typeof WebAssembly.Suspending !== 'function') throw new Error(S.noJspi);
  const r = config.re3, language = gameLanguage(config), own = r.languages?.[language] ?? {};
  if (!r.module) throw new Error(S.noModule);
  // (the game data opened now — its worker, the version's store, the learned order's list —, beside the account's saves
  // and the engine's download, ready by the time the engine's file system takes its files: openPortData)
  gameData ??= openPortData({ name, tree, manifest: config, session: sessionId, lang: language, log });
  step('engine', 'active'); step('files', ''); step('game', '');
  db = await openStorage(config.saveKey);
  const who = await shell.ready;
  if (who.user) {
    status(S.account);
    cloud = newCloud(who.user.username);
    const what = await cloud.pull().catch((e) => { log('Account saves: ' + e.message); return 'offline'; });
    if (what === 'conflict') await shell.resolveConflict(cloud);
  }
  world = config.mmo ? createWorld(name, who.user?.username ?? null) : null;
  status(S.init);
  // (the module's own files — its WebAssembly — beside it in the release; each by its content when the server gives it,
  // else under its release: engineUrls)
  const at = engineUrls(config, r.engine, true), moduleDir = r.module.slice(0, r.module.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
  const t = performance.now();
  const { default: createEngine } = await import(at(r.module));
  engine = session.engine = await createEngine({
    canvas: $('canvas'), print: log, printErr: log, locateFile: (file) => at(moduleDir + file), noInitialRun: true,
    onAbort: (reason) => fail(new Error(String(reason))), onExit: (code) => ended(code), orthrosFrame: onFrame, orthrosMouse: onMouseMode,
    ...(world ? { orthrosNet: world.net } : {}), // (the shared world: the engine's way to it)
    preRun: [envPreRun(own.env, log)], // (the language's environment, before the runtime copies it)
  });
  step('engine', 'done', `${((performance.now() - t) / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`);
  FS = engine.FS;
  FS.mkdirTree(ROOT);
  // (the game's files: its whole tree now — the release's own over the version's, as the server lists it —, what
  // earlier sessions read first loaded before the start, the rest later; a stream's next bytes read ahead; a game file
  // the engine writes anew, a file of the profile in its place)
  // (asyncReads: a read waiting for bytes suspends the engine — JSPI — instead of holding the page; rewritable: a game file
  // the engine writes anew, a file of the profile in its place)
  const t0 = performance.now();
  step('files', 'active', fmtMB(0), 0);
  let nodes;
  ({ nodes } = await mountPortFiles(gameData, { name, files, FS, root: ROOT, log, db, asyncReads: true, rewritable: true,
    onCopy: (bytes) => step('files', 'active', fmtMB(bytes), 0), onProgress: (progress) => shell.setData(progress) }));
  session.files = gameData; gameNodes = nodes;
  const loaded = await gameData.startup((p) => {
    const f = p.total ? p.bytes / p.total : 1, secs = (performance.now() - t0) / 1000;
    step('files', 'active', `${fmtMB(p.bytes)}${secs > 1 ? ` · ${(p.bytes / 1048576 / secs).toFixed(1)} MB/s` : ''}`, f); status(S.files(Math.round(f * 100)));
  });
  session.startup = { ...gameData.snapshot(), startupBytes: loaded.total, ms: Math.round(performance.now() - t0) };
  log(`Startup files: ${JSON.stringify(session.startup)}`);
  step('files', 'done', fmtMB(loaded.total));
  // (the profile in the game's folder, over the game's files it replaced; the language's settings — re3.languages.<code>,
  // the player's choice of the version's languages —, in every ini file a language names: a game's own copied into the
  // profile even when it has these settings, for the engine to write in)
  const kept = (await readStorage(db, 'profile', 'files')) ?? [];
  if (config.profileSeed && params.get('profileseed') !== '0' && !kept.length) {
    await seedProfile(language, new Set([...languageIni(r.languages, language).map(([file]) => file), ...Object.keys(r.defaults ?? {})].map((file) => file.toLowerCase())));
  }
  restoreProfile(FS, ROOT, kept, log);
  profileReady = true; watchProfileWrites();
  for (const [file, sections] of languageIni(r.languages, language)) {
    try { log(`${file}: ${setProfileIni(FS, ROOT, file, sections, gameNodes)} (${language})`); } catch (error) { log(`${file}: not set (${error.message})`); }
  }
  // (the version's defaults — re3.defaults —, set once in a profile: the player's later choice stays)
  for (const [file, sections] of Object.entries(r.defaults ?? {})) {
    try { log(`${file}: ${setProfileIni(FS, ROOT, file, sections, gameNodes, setIniDefaults)} (defaults)`); } catch (error) { log(`${file}: defaults not set (${error.message})`); }
  }
  FS.chdir(ROOT);
  step('game', 'active', '', 0.3); status(S.starting);
  gameData.start(); // (the reads are learned from the engine's start; the learned order loads in the data worker)
  session.state = 'running'; report('start', { engine: r.engine, mode, signedIn: !!shell.account });
  setTimeout(() => report('audio', audioState()), 60000); // (a minute in: is the game heard?)
  timer = setInterval(() => save().catch((error) => { log('Profile save failed: ' + error.message); status(S.saveFailed, true); }), 10000);
  // (the account's copy: a minute after a change at most — CloudSave sends only what changed)
  cloudTimer = setInterval(() => { if (cloud && session.state === 'running') cloud.push(); }, 60000);
  $('canvas').focus();
  // (main() runs until the player quits the game: its promise settles then — JSPI; an engine on a main loop returns at
  // once and ends through onExit)
  const run = engine.callMain([...(r.args ?? []), ...(r.modes?.[mode]?.args ?? [])]);
  if (typeof run?.then === 'function') run.then((code) => ended(code), (error) => (isExit(error) ? ended(error.status) : fail(error)));
}

/**
 * Back to the games: the profile kept here and on the account; false when it could not be sent. (The engine is not
 * asked to quit: the page goes.)
 */
async function quit() {
  if (session.state === 'ended' || session.state === 'error') return finalSave ?? true;
  if (session.state !== 'running') return true;
  return saveAndPush();
}

/**
 * The version's ways to play the game, on the loading screen: one button each (the last one chosen focused), its
 * note under them; the game starts on the one chosen (?mode= chooses at once).
 */
function chooseMode(modes) {
  session.state = 'choosing'; shell.showProgress(false);
  const key = 'orthros.re3Mode.' + name;
  let last = null; try { last = localStorage.getItem(key); } catch { /* none */ }
  const note = Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'note' }), acts = Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { className: 'acts' });
  const buttons = modes.map((m, i) => Object.assign(document.createElement('button'), {
    type: 'button', id: 'mode-' + m, className: (last ?? modes[0]) === m ? 'primary' : '', textContent: S.modes[m] ?? m,
    onfocus: () => { note.textContent = S.modeNotes[m] ?? ''; }, onmouseenter: () => { note.textContent = S.modeNotes[m] ?? ''; },
    onclick: () => {
      try { localStorage.setItem(key, m); } catch { /* not kept */ }
      shell.choices.replaceChildren(); shell.showProgress(true);
      start(m).catch((error) => fail(error));
    },
  }));
  acts.append(...buttons);
  shell.choices.replaceChildren(acts, note);
  (buttons[modes.indexOf(last)] ?? buttons[0]).focus();
}

async function fullscreen() {
  try { await document.documentElement.requestFullscreen({ navigationUI: 'hide' }); } catch (error) { status(error.message, true); return; }
  await lockKeys();
  $('canvas').focus();
  if (wantsMouse()) $('canvas').requestPointerLock()?.catch?.(() => {}); // (in the game: the mouse captured at once, as the Windows games')
}

try {
  const [manifestResponse, treeResponse] = await Promise.all([fetch(`/api/manifest/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`), fetch(`/api/tree/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`)]);
  if (!manifestResponse.ok || !treeResponse.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${manifestResponse.ok ? treeResponse.status : manifestResponse.status}`);
  config = session.config = await manifestResponse.json();
  if (config.runtime !== 're3') throw new Error('not an re3 installation');
  tree = await treeResponse.json(); files = treeFiles(tree);
  shell = createShell({
    title: config.name, version: config.version, gameLanguage: gameLanguage(config), cover: `/api/cover/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, subtitle: S.subtitle,
    steps: Object.entries(S.steps).map(([k, label]) => ({ k, label })), tips: S.tips,
    onQuit: quit, onFullscreen: fullscreen, onMouse: giveMouse, onSignedIn: lateSignIn, saves: () => cloud,
    onLoaderHidden: fit,
  });
  shell.sound.addEventListener('click', resumeAudio);
  const modes = Object.keys(config.re3.modes ?? {});
  if (modes.length > 1 && !modes.includes(params.get('mode'))) chooseMode(modes);
  else await start(modes.length ? (modes.includes(params.get('mode')) ? params.get('mode') : modes[0]) : null);
} catch (error) { if (shell) fail(error); else document.body.textContent = S.failed + (error.message ?? error); }

document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
  world?.link.away(document.hidden); // (the engine stops with the page's frames: the others are told, its entities go to them)
  if (document.hidden && session.state === 'running') save().then(() => cloud?.push()).catch(log);
});
window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
  world?.link.close();
  if (session.state === 'running') endReport();
  stopped = true; if (timer) clearInterval(timer); if (cloudTimer) clearInterval(cloudTimer); gameData?.close();
});
```

`src/ports/re3/profile.js`:

```js
// The player's profile of an re3 port (docs/browser-ports.md, "re3 ports"). The engine reads the game's files and
// writes its own — saves and settings (its "userfiles" folder), its ini file, maybe caches — in one folder, the game
// root, where the page mounted the game's files (../port-files.js). The profile is every regular file there that is
// not a mounted game file: created by the engine, or a game file it replaced. It is kept as { path relative to the
// root, data }, in IndexedDB and on the player's account, and put back before the engine starts.
import { bytesToText, textToBytes, setIni } from './ini.js';

/** A profile path: relative, '/'-separated, no empty, '.' or '..' part, no control character. */
export const profilePathOk = (p) => typeof p === 'string' && p.length > 0 && p.length <= 1024 && !p.startsWith('/') && !p.includes('\\') && !/[\x00-\x1f]/.test(p) && p.split('/').every((x) => x && x !== '.' && x !== '..');

const nodeAt = (FS, at) => { try { return FS.lookupPath(at, { follow: false }).node; } catch { return null; } };

/**
 * The profile's files under `root` ([{ path, data }], paths relative to it): every regular file but the mounted game
 * files (`game`: their nodes — never read: their bytes may not be here yet).
 */
export function profileSnapshot(FS, root, game) {
  const files = [];
  (function walk(dir, rel) {
    for (const name of FS.readdir(dir)) {
      if (name === '.' || name === '..') continue;
      const at = `${dir}/${name}`, node = nodeAt(FS, at);
      if (!node || game.has(node)) continue;
      if (FS.isDir(node.mode)) walk(at, `${rel}${name}/`);
      else if (FS.isFile(node.mode)) files.push({ path: rel + name, data: FS.readFile(at) });
    }
  })(root, '');
  return files;
}

/**
 * The profile's files put back under `root`, before the engine starts: each in place of a game file of the same path
 * (the engine had replaced it). A file that cannot be put back (its path a folder, an invalid path) is told and left out.
 */
export function restoreProfile(FS, root, files, log = () => {}) {
  for (const f of files ?? []) {
    if (!profilePathOk(f?.path) || !ArrayBuffer.isView(f.data)) { log(`Profile: ${String(f?.path).slice(0, 80)} left out (invalid)`); continue; }
    const at = `${root}/${f.path}`;
    try {
      FS.mkdirTree(at.slice(0, at.lastIndexOf('/')));
      const old = nodeAt(FS, at);
      if (old && FS.isDir(old.mode)) { log(`Profile: ${f.path} left out (a folder there)`); continue; }
      if (old) FS.unlink(at);
      FS.writeFile(at, f.data);
    } catch (e) { log(`Profile: ${f.path} left out (${e.message})`); }
  }
}

/**
 * `rel` under `root` spelled as what is there, whatever the case of its parts (the engine's own way: it lists folders):
 * `found`, the whole path is there; else its parts from the first missing one on as `rel` has them.
 */
export function casePath(FS, root, rel) {
  let dir = root, found = true;
  const parts = rel.split('/').map((part) => {
    let hit = null;
    if (found) {
      let names = null; try { names = FS.readdir(dir); } catch { /* not a folder */ }
      hit = names && (names.find((n) => n === part) ?? names.find((n) => n.toLowerCase() === part.toLowerCase()));
      if (!hit) found = false;
    }
    dir = `${dir}/${hit ?? part}`;
    return hit ?? part;
  });
  return { path: parts.join('/'), found };
}

/** The path under `root` that `rel` names, whatever the case of its parts, or null. */
export const findPath = (FS, root, rel) => { const p = casePath(FS, root, rel); return p.found ? p.path : null; };

/**
 * A language's settings put in the ini file `rel` of the profile (setIni: the rest of the file kept as it is): the
 * file the profile has under that name whatever its case; else the game's own, copied into the profile even when its
 * settings are already these — a mounted game file is read-only, and the engine writes its settings there; else a new
 * one, in the folders there whatever their case. Returns what was done: 'same', 'set', 'copied' or 'created'. `edit`:
 * how the settings go in (setIni; setIniDefaults: defaults set once).
 */
export function setProfileIni(FS, root, rel, sections, game, edit = setIni) {
  const { path: p, found } = casePath(FS, root, rel), at = `${root}/${p}`, node = found ? nodeAt(FS, at) : null;
  if (node && !FS.isFile(node.mode)) return 'same';
  const before = node ? bytesToText(FS.readFile(at)) : '', after = edit(before, sections);
  if (!node) {
    if (!after) return 'same';
    FS.mkdirTree(at.slice(0, at.lastIndexOf('/')));
    FS.writeFile(at, textToBytes(after));
    return 'created';
  }
  if (game.has(node)) FS.unlink(at); // (a game file: the profile's own copy from now on)
  else if (after === before) return 'same';
  FS.writeFile(at, textToBytes(after));
  return after === before ? 'copied' : 'set';
}

/**
 * The ini settings a game language puts in the profile ([file, sections]): for every file one of the version's
 * languages names (re3.languages.<code>.ini, file names without case), this language's sections, else none — the
 * game's own file then still copied into the profile (setProfileIni), whichever language the player chose.
 */
export function languageIni(languages, language) {
  const out = new Map();
  for (const own of Object.values(languages ?? {})) for (const file of Object.keys(own?.ini ?? {})) if (!out.has(file.toLowerCase())) out.set(file.toLowerCase(), [file, {}]);
  for (const [file, sections] of Object.entries(languages?.[language]?.ini ?? {})) out.set(file.toLowerCase(), [file, sections]);
  return [...out.values()];
}

/**
 * A language's environment variables (re3.languages.<code>.env) as the Module's preRun hook: set in its ENV before the
 * runtime starts — the C library copies the environment once, as its constructors run, before the Module is handed
 * over: set later, getenv() never sees it.
 */
export const envPreRun = (env, log = () => {}) => (M) => {
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(env ?? {})) { if (M.ENV) M.ENV[key] = value; else log(`${key}: the engine exposes no environment`); }
};

// What the account keeps of a profile (src/host/web/cloud-sync.js): its files less what the engine makes again —
// logs and screenshots.
const KEEP = (path) => !/(^|\/)(screenshots|logs)\//i.test(path) && !/\.log$/i.test(path);
/** A profile's files as the account keeps them. */
export const toCloud = (list) => (list ?? []).filter((f) => KEEP(f.path));

```

`src/vfs/data-client.js`:

```js
// The game data of an engine that runs in the page (GoldSrc, re3, OpenMW, the next ones — CLAUDE.md
// "Standardization"), the page's side: the data worker (data-worker.js: the Windows games' reader, the browser's copy,
// the learned order, the whole download) asked for bytes, kept here in 64 KiB pieces for the engine's many small reads.
// A read the engine waits for synchronously waits on shared memory (the page's thread spins: Atomics.wait is not
// allowed there); one it can wait for (JSPI: `ensure`) by message. The pieces the engine uses are told to the worker,
// which reports them to the server's learned order. Emscripten engines mount the files with emscripten-files.js.
// A texture's load reads its light copy (src/host/light-copies.js: the texture without its finest levels) on a thin link
// or one not measured yet, unless the file itself is here; the file comes in the background, for its next load. A page
// may say what its loads are for (prefer): 'light' — the far ring of a view that grows — or 'real'. A page whose engine
// loads a file again in place once it is here (reloads: a texture made sharp while it is shown) reads the light copies
// first on every link that is not fast, their files coming soon after them.
// The reads the engine waits for, as the worker counts them for the page's indicator (data-worker.js ctrl[6]): a
// synchronous read always (the page's thread is held); an asynchronous one (JSPI: `ensure`) when the engine has not gone
// on since it asked for it by the page's next task — an engine that suspends until its bytes are here gives the page its
// turn at once, having called nothing more; one that asked ahead and goes on (re3's streaming: a model, a sound not here
// yet shows a moment later) reads, asks for more or shows a frame first (progress) —, until it goes on; one fetched in
// the background (readable) never. A load made of many short waits counts as a wait all along.
// An engine that suspends while it waits (JSPI: OpenMW's Orthros build, orthros-r20.patch) asks `soon` before a read
// and wantWaitSoon before an announced wait: the page's thread waits a few ms first (SOON_SPIN_MS: the browser's copy
// answers most reads that fast — a suspension costs a round of the page's event loop each), then gives the request up
// to a message and the engine suspends until it lands (ctrl[16]: the request the page still waits for — the worker
// answers on shared memory only that one, claimed first; one given up comes by message).
// Announced reads (want, wantWait — docs/slow-network.md "Announced reads"): an engine that knows what its next load
// reads says so first; the worker fetches all of it in parallel, and the engine waits once (on shared memory: ctrl[12],
// the last batch settled) instead of a round trip per file. A big announced load of an engine that reloads in place
// (its batch's files would hold the link more than LOAD_BUDGET_S, a fast link included) reads the light copies first,
// the files after it (docs/slow-network.md "Big loads light first").
// Content files (game-tree.js isLightContent: a TES3 master's light copy keeps what the content load reads, every offset
// the file's): read light on every link while the engine says it loads its content (contentLoading), the file itself
// once it says its content is loaded (contentLoaded) — every read from then on, every handle, for good; never fetched
// whole after the copy; an engine that says nothing reads the file (docs/slow-network.md "Content files light before
// the menu").
import { treeFile, LIGHT_DIR, isLightContent, isWholeImage } from './game-tree.js';
import { FAST_BPS } from './net-link.js';

export const PIECE = 1 << 16;

/**
 * The player's choice, for every game (the settings' "offline copy"): each game kept whole in this browser, downloaded
 * in the background while it runs. Kept in this browser.
 */
// snapshot: no state — the page's preference, read from the browser's storage each time
export const offlineCopy = {
  get() { try { return localStorage.getItem('orthros.offlineCopy') === '1'; } catch { return false; } },
  set(on) { try { localStorage.setItem('orthros.offlineCopy', on ? '1' : '0'); } catch { /* storage off */ } },
};
/**
 * The rate this browser measured on its link to the server last time (bytes/s), for every game: the estimate a reader
 * starts with until it measures its own (src/vfs/net-link.js). Kept in this browser.
 */
// snapshot: no state — the browser's storage, read each time
export const linkRate = {
  get() { try { const v = Number(localStorage.getItem('orthros.netBw')); return v > 0 ? v : undefined; } catch { return undefined; } },
  set(bw) { if (bw > 0) try { localStorage.setItem('orthros.netBw', String(Math.round(bw))); } catch { /* storage off */ } },
  /** The link was fast last time (FAST_BPS, net-link.js): a page's choice before its game data opens — unknown is not fast. */
  fast() { return this.get() >= FAST_BPS; },
};
/** The most bytes one answer of the worker carries (its shared buffer). */
const SPAN = 16 << 20;
/** A read the engine waits for fails once the worker's heartbeat stopped this long (it died). */
const DEAD_MS = 30000;
/** How often the requests answered by message look at the worker's heartbeat while any is pending (watchAsks; ms). */
const ASK_WATCH_MS = 1000;
/**
 * How long the page's thread waits for bytes before an engine that can suspend does (soon, wantWaitSoon; ms): a read
 * the browser's copy answers takes ~0.3-3 ms, one over the network a round trip at least (tens of ms and more).
 */
export const SOON_SPIN_MS = 10;
const PER_FILE = 2 ** 21; // (a piece's key: file id × PER_FILE + piece)
/**
 * The most evicted pieces kept for the next ones (GameData.keep): a worker's answer's worth (SPAN), and no more than an
 * eighth of the budget (a small tier's: its memory is what it is short of) — those past it freed at once (release). Every
 * piece a buffer of its own otherwise, the evicted ones garbage — the page's external memory the collector is paced by:
 * its major collections came that often while the game streams.
 */
const freePiecesMax = (budget) => Math.min(SPAN / PIECE, Math.floor(budget / PIECE / 8));
/**
 * `bytes`, the only view of a buffer of the page's own that nothing uses any more (a worker's answer copied into the
 * pieces, an evicted piece), freed at once (ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer(0)) instead of left to the collector: dead
 * buffers count as the page's external memory, which starts its major collections, and each is freed in the
 * collection's pause (its array buffers' sweep: 17-25 ms of 50-65 ms collections while the game streamed). A shared
 * buffer, a view of part of one, or a browser without transfer: left as it is.
 */
function release(bytes) {
  const b = bytes.buffer;
  if (typeof b.transfer === 'function' && !b.detached && bytes.byteOffset === 0 && bytes.byteLength === b.byteLength) b.transfer(0);
}
/** A read at a file's start this long after its last read is a new load of it: light copy or file, chosen again. */
const LOAD_GAP_MS = 2000;
/** an announced choice (GameData.want: light copy or file) holds for the load that starts within this time (its waits, ~30 s at most) */
const PIN_MS = 60000;
/**
 * An announced load (GameData.want) whose batch's files that have a light copy would take the link longer than this (s,
 * at its measured rate) is a big load: an engine that reloads in place reads their light copies first, even on a fast
 * link — the player waits for ~15 MB instead of ~100 (a new device at a place of large textures: ~8 s frozen at 12 MB/s,
 * ~19 s at 5 MB/s) —, the files coming after the load, sharpened in place.
 */
export const LOAD_BUDGET_S = 2;
/**
 * The big load's state (GameData.bigLoadNow: the other loads of that moment — the engine's preloads, readable() — read
 * light too) holds this long after the engine's last wait for its batches ended (PIN_MS at most while it never waits).
 */
const BIG_HOLD_MS = 5000;
/**
 * Files made sharp in place delivered to the page's listeners (onReal) at most this many each 100 ms (a burst of reloads
 * is a hitch) — only those the page read light (the others reload nothing: not queued, the queue never outgrows them).
 */
const REAL_PER_TICK = 2;
/**
 * The files made sharp in place reach the listeners with their bytes in the page (realInPage, by default): each one
 * fetched from the worker in the background first, its listeners told once it is here — an engine's reload then reads
 * it without the page's thread waiting (OpenMW's reloads read their files through fetchSync, the worker's answer
 * waited for: ~90% of their time, 30-490 ms stretches in the first seconds in the world). At most this many files under
 * way at once, and 1/REAL_FETCH_SHARE of the page's bytes (always one: the others wait in realQ), and no new one while
 * the engine's reloads told and not done yet (o.realBacklog) and those under way are REAL_FETCHES or more — their bytes
 * stay in the page until the engine reads them, the next frames. Only the files a reload will read are fetched (an
 * engine that reloads in place, the file's last load read light): the others are told as they come. A reload's read
 * that waited all the same is counted (realMissed: its bytes left the page before it; realRaced: a load of the file
 * itself while its fetch was under way — realHere says it is here from the worker's word — read through fetchSync, as
 * before realInPage).
 */
const REAL_FETCHES = 8;
const REAL_FETCH_SHARE = 8;
/** The worker's word on the files here whole is held at most this long during an engine's load (GameData.heldReal). */
const HELD_MAX_MS = 60000;
```
