```js
  // in batches with their time since the epoch)
  if (o.trace) {
    const q = [];
    W.trace = (e) => { if (q.length < 5000) q.push({ t: performance.timeOrigin + performance.now(), ...e }); };
    for (const p of W.version.parts) p.files.traceAhead = W.trace;
    W.timers.push(setInterval(() => { if (q.length) postMessage({ trace: q.splice(0) }); }, 200));
  }
  // (the learned order's list asked now, its bytes not: here before the startup set or the engine's first read asks)
  if (o.orderAtOpen) order();
  W.timers.push(setInterval(monitor, 100), setInterval(report, REPORT_MS), setInterval(lightWatch, 1000));
  // (the files that have a light copy: those here whole the page reads themselves; the others watched — lightWatch —,
  // each by the name the page knows it under, through the part that reads it)
  const real = [];
  for (const p of W.version.parts) if (!p.shared) for (const f of treeFiles(p.tree)) {
    if (!f.light) continue;
    const r = route(p.name, f.path), k = lightKey(p.name, f.path);
    if (r.files.isWhole(f.path)) real.push(k); else W.light.set(k, { part: r, path: f.path, told: false });
  }
  // (the trees of the versions the page opened: a shared part's files are in them already)
  postMessage({ ready: { trees: Object.fromEntries(W.version.parts.filter((p) => !p.shared).map((p) => [p.name, p.tree])), kept, manifest: W.version.manifest, real } });
  lightWatch();
}

/** The part that reads the file `path` of version `name` as the page knows it (game-data.js partOf), or null. */
const route = (name, path) => (W.parts.has(name) ? partOf(W.version, name, path) : null);

/** The file `path` of version `name`, opened once (through the part that reads it). */
function handle(name, path) {
  const key = name + '\n' + path;
  let f = W.handles.get(key);
  if (!f) { f = route(name, path)?.files.open(path) ?? null; if (f) W.handles.set(key, f); }
  return f;
}

/** How far the bytes of `f` from `from` are here already (memory or store: no network), up to `limit`. */
function hereUntil(files, f, from, limit) {
  let pos = from;
  while (pos < limit) {
    const bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK), c = Math.floor(pos / CHUNK);
    if (files.peekBlockHere(f.path, f.len, f.mtime, bi)) pos = (bi + 1) * BLOCK;
    else if (files.pieceHere(f.path, f.len, f.mtime, c)) pos = (c + 1) * CHUNK;
    else break;
  }
  return Math.min(pos, limit);
}

/**
 * Bytes of `path` from `off`: at least `len` (fetched when missing — the reader's own planning: pieces, blocks, read
 * ahead, the link's measure), and on as far as they are here already, up to `want` in all. `ask`: the read, { held } —
 * whether the engine waits for it (counted among the waits while it waits for the network: waited()). Always a buffer
 * of their own (a copy, or a fetch's response), nothing the worker keeps: answerAsync hands it over to the page, which
 * frees it.
 */
async function bytesOf({ name, path, off, len, want, src }, ask = { held: true }) {
  if (src !== undefined) return sourceBytes(src, off, len);
  const part = route(name, path), f = handle(name, path);
  if (!part || !f) throw new Error(`${name}: ${path} not in the game's files`);
  const end = Math.min(f.len, off + len);
  if (end <= off) return new Uint8Array(0);
  W.readSeen = true; W.boot = false;
  if (W.prefetchAt === 'first-read' && !W.prefetching) prefetchAll();
  await adoptLegacy(name, path, part, f);
  const real = contentHere(name, path, f, off, end);
  if (real) {
    const stop = Math.max(end, hereUntil(real.files, real.f, Math.ceil(end / CHUNK) * CHUNK, Math.min(real.f.len, off + Math.max(len, want ?? 0))));
    return real.f.read(off, stop - off);
  }
  const wait = f.prepare(off, end - off);
  if (wait) {
    // (a media stream's read: a wait of the engine's, not of a load — see HttpFile.prepare)
    ask.media = !!part.files.isMedia?.(f.path);
    // (its file's whole fill first once the engine waits for it: waited, HttpBackend.noteWait)
    ask.files = part.files; ask.path = f.path;
    W.waits.add(ask); waited();
    try { await wait; } finally { W.waits.delete(ask); if (ask.tok) { W.version.net.waitEnd(ask.tok); ask.tok = null; } waited(); }
  }
  const stop = Math.max(end, hereUntil(part.files, f, Math.ceil(end / CHUNK) * CHUNK, Math.min(f.len, off + Math.max(len, want ?? 0))));
  W.trace?.({ k: 'wread', f: path, off, len: stop - off, held: ask.held ? 1 : 0, waited: wait ? 1 : 0 });
  return f.read(off, stop - off);
}

/**
 * A content file's light copy (game-tree.js isLightContent: every offset the file's, payloads zeroed) read where the
 * file's own bytes [off, end) are all here already (memory or store): the file's { files, f } to read them from — a
 * superset of the copy's, what an engine reading the file itself at its content load stored (a store from before its
 * engine read the copy) read as it is instead of fetched again light —, else null.
 */
function contentHere(name, path, f, off, end) {
  if (!path.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/') || !isLightContent(path)) return null;
  const rel = path.slice(LIGHT_DIR.length + 1), part = route(name, rel), r = part ? handle(name, rel) : null;
  return r && r.len === f.len && hereUntil(part.files, r, off, end) >= end ? { files: part.files, f: r } : null;
}

/**
 * The reads waiting for the network that the engine waits for, counted again (W.waiting; lastWait while there are);
 * each one a wait of the link's while it is held (NetLink.wait: the background keeps to a load's needs during a run of
 * them) — not a read fetched in the background, nor one the engine went on past, nor a media stream's.
 */
function waited() {
  const was = W.waiting, net = W.version.net;
  W.waiting = 0;
  for (const a of W.waits) {
    if (a.held) W.waiting++;
    // (once per ask: an ask the engine went on past never counts — a sample skipped while missing)
    if (a.held && !a.noted && a.files) { a.noted = true; a.files.noteWait?.(a.path); }
    if (a.held && !a.media && !a.tok) a.tok = net.wait(); else if (!a.held && a.tok) { net.waitEnd(a.tok); a.tok = null; }
  }
  if (W.waiting > 0 || was > 0) W.lastWait = performance.now();
}

/** The page says which of its asynchronous reads the engine waits for now ([id, 1 | 0]: data-client.js holdCheck, holdWatch). */
function hold(list) {
  for (const [id, on] of list) { const a = W.held.get(id); if (a) a.held = !!on; }
  waited();
}

async function answerSync(m) {
  let bytes = null, error = null;
  try { bytes = await bytesOf(m); } // (the page's thread waits for it)
  catch (err) { error = String(err?.message ?? err); postMessage({ log: `${m.path}: ${error}` }); }
  settleSync(m, bytes, error);
}

/**
 * A synchronous request's answer: on shared memory (its bytes in W.data, ctrl[1] their count or -1, ctrl[0] its number),
 * unless the page gave it up (late: ctrl[16] no longer its number — the page's engine suspended meanwhile): then by
 * message, as answerAsync's.
 */
function settleSync(m, bytes, error) {
  const { ctrl, data } = W;
  if (m.late !== undefined && Atomics.compareExchange(ctrl, 16, m.gen, -m.gen) !== m.gen) {
    if (bytes) postMessage({ id: m.late, bytes }, [bytes.buffer]); else postMessage({ id: m.late, error: error ?? 'read failed' });
    return;
  }
  if (bytes) { const n = Math.min(bytes.length, data.length); data.set(bytes.subarray(0, n), 0); ctrl[1] = n; } else ctrl[1] = -1;
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 0, m.gen);
  Atomics.notify(ctrl, 0);
}

/**
 * An asynchronous read answered: its bytes a buffer of their own (bytesOf), transferred — the page takes it over and
 * frees it once copied into its pieces (data-client.js fetchAsync, release). Never a view of what the worker keeps.
 */
async function answerAsync(m) {
  // (the engine waits for it once the page says so — held —, at once when it says so with the read)
  const ask = { held: !!m.held };
  W.held.set(m.id, ask);
  try { const bytes = await bytesOf(m, ask); postMessage({ id: m.id, bytes }, [bytes.buffer]); }
  catch (err) { postMessage({ id: m.id, error: String(err?.message ?? err) }); }
  finally { W.held.delete(m.id); }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- announced reads

/**
 * A batch of announced reads (GameData.want: `seq` its number, `from` the first batch of the page's current wait window,
 * `list` [[name, path, off, len]] — len -1: to the end of the file —, `label` what the load is for, e.g. 'meshes:-2,6'):
 * each version's entries to its reader (HttpBackend.wantList: fetched in parallel, kept), and as they land or fail, the
 * counters the page's wait reads (ctrl[12] — every batch of the window up to it settled —, ctrl[13], ctrl[14]). The
 * batch is registered whatever happens (an exception: its entries failed), so the window's count never stops at it.
 * `wait` false (GameData.want's: the engine waits for it through its own reads, never wantWait): no batch — its entries
 * counted in ctrl[13] and ctrl[14] only —, and no hold of the link's nor of the learned read-ahead (wantList `wait` false).
 */
function want({ seq, from, list, label, wait }) {
  const batch = wait !== false;
  W.wantLabel = typeof label === 'string' ? label.slice(0, 80) : null;
  const byPart = new Map();
  for (const [name, path, off, len] of list) {
    const part = route(name, String(path));
    const a = Math.max(0, Number(off) || 0), n = Number(len);
    if (!part) { W.wantFailed++; continue; }
    let e = byPart.get(part); if (!e) byPart.set(part, e = []);
    e.push([path, a, n < 0 || !Number.isFinite(n) ? -1 : a + n]);
  }
  const all = [];
  try { for (const [part, ranges] of byPart) all.push(...part.files.wantList(ranges, { label: W.wantLabel, wait: batch })); }
  catch { W.wantFailed += list.length - all.length; }
  if (batch) {
    W.wantMax = Math.max(W.wantMax, seq);
    if (Number.isInteger(from) && from > W.wantFrom) W.wantFrom = from;
    // (a settled batch leaves the map: a number up to wantMax not in it is settled)
    if (all.length) W.wants.set(seq, all.length);
  }
  W.wantLeft += all.length;
  const settle = (ok) => {
    W.wantLeft--; if (!ok) W.wantFailed++;
    if (batch) { const n = W.wants.get(seq) - 1; if (n > 0) W.wants.set(seq, n); else W.wants.delete(seq); }
    wantTell();
  };
  for (const p of all) p.then(settle, () => settle(false));
  wantTell();
}

/**
 * A predicted place's set (GameData.want `prio: 'place'`: `list` [[name, path, off, len]], `label` 'place:<key>'): each
 * version's entries to its reader at the place's priority (HttpBackend.wantList `prio: 'place'` — the link's idle time,
 * below the game's reads, a load's and the launch set); no batch, no counter the page waits on.
 */
function wantPlace({ list, label }) {
  const byPart = new Map();
  for (const [name, path, off, len] of Array.isArray(list) ? list : []) {
    const part = route(name, String(path)); if (!part) continue;
    const a = Math.max(0, Number(off) || 0), n = Number(len);
    let e = byPart.get(part); if (!e) byPart.set(part, e = []);
    e.push([path, a, n < 0 || !Number.isFinite(n) ? -1 : a + n]);
  }
  for (const [part, ranges] of byPart) try { part.files.wantList(ranges, { label: typeof label === 'string' ? label.slice(0, 80) : '', prio: 'place' }); } catch { /* a reader closed: nothing kept */ }
}

/**
 * The announced batches' counters to the page: the last batch settled with every one of the window before it (ctrl[12]:
 * from W.wantFrom — an older one still unsettled, its wait over, holds nothing), entries left, failed.
 */
function wantTell() {
  let done = W.wantFrom - 1;
  while (done < W.wantMax && !W.wants.has(done + 1)) done++;
  Atomics.store(W.ctrl, 13, W.wantLeft); Atomics.store(W.ctrl, 14, W.wantFailed);
  Atomics.store(W.ctrl, 12, done); Atomics.notify(W.ctrl, 12);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- files of elsewhere

/**
 * Files an engine reads that are not the game's (a file the player picked, a Blob the page keeps, a signed address):
 * { url } read by ranges (retried), { handle } (a FileSystemFileHandle) or { blob } sliced. Not kept, not learned.
 */
async function sourceBytes(id, off, len) {
  const s = W.sources.get(id); if (!s) throw new Error('unknown source');
  if (s.blob || s.handle) { s.file ??= s.blob ?? await s.handle.getFile(); return new Uint8Array(await s.file.slice(off, off + len).arrayBuffer()); }
  let last;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) {
    if (attempt) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400 * attempt * attempt));
    try {
      const r = await fetch(s.url, { headers: { Range: `bytes=${off}-${off + len - 1}` }, cache: 'no-store' });
      if (r.status === 206 || r.ok) { const b = new Uint8Array(await r.arrayBuffer()); return r.status === 206 ? b : b.subarray(off, off + len); }
      last = new Error('HTTP ' + r.status); if (r.status < 500 && r.status !== 408 && r.status !== 429) break;
    } catch (err) { last = err; }
  }
  throw last ?? new Error('read failed');
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what the engine read: the server's learned order

/** Pieces the engine used for the first time ([name, path, piece], told by the page): reported with their time. */
function used(list) {
  if (W.t0 === null) return;
  const t = Math.round(performance.now() - W.t0);
  for (const [name, path, c] of list) {
    if (name !== W.version.parts[0].name) continue; // (the learned order is the version's own)
    let s = W.seen.get(path); if (!s) W.seen.set(path, s = new Set());
    if (s.has(c)) continue;
    s.add(c);
    const f = handle(name, path); if (!f) continue;
    const a = c * CHUNK, b = Math.min(f.len, a + CHUNK), last = W.reads.at(-1);
    if (last && last[0] === path && last[2] === a && last[3] === t) last[2] = b; else W.reads.push([path, a, b, t]);
  }
}

function report(final = false, marked = null) {
  if ((!W.reads.length && !marked) || !W.session) return;
  // (a mark goes with every read before it, in one report: the server flags what the session had read by then)
  const reads = W.reads.splice(0, marked ? MARK_READS : 5000), name = W.version.parts[0].name;
  // (in order: a mark after the reports before it; the final one at once, keepalive while small enough — playable-watch.js)
  W.reports.send(name, W.session, reads, marked, final, W.phases);
}

/** The most phases a session tells (GameData.phase). */
const MAX_PHASES = 200;

/**
 * The page's game entered phase `name` (GameData.phase: a map, a level) `ago` ms ago: [name, t] (t: ms from the
 * session's start, the reads' times) goes with every report from now on — the server learns each read as its phase's.
 */
function phase({ name, ago }) {
  if (W.t0 === null || typeof name !== 'string' || !name || W.phases.length >= MAX_PHASES) return;
  const t = Math.max(0, Math.round(performance.now() - W.t0 - ago));
  if (W.phases.at(-1)?.[0] === name) return;
  W.phases.push([name, t]);
}

/**
 * The page's game reached a moment of its own (GameData.mark: 'playable' — it first draws in play): told to the server
 * once per kind, with the reads before it (the server learns the launch set from it: launch-set.js).
 */
function mark(m) {
  const kind = String(m.kind ?? ''); if (!/^[a-z-]{1,20}$/.test(kind) || W.marks.has(kind) || W.t0 === null) return;
  W.marks.add(kind);
  report(false, { kind, t: Math.round(performance.now() - W.t0), ...(W.lang ? { lang: W.lang } : {}) });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- loading ahead

/**
 * The learned order of the version, one list a part: what earlier sessions read first, the startup set its head — the
 * entries of files another version owns in that version's part's list (learnedOrders).
 */
const order = () => (W.learned ??= learnedOrders(W.version, W.lang));

/**
 * The startup set loaded (before the engine starts): every part's launch set — the version's, then those of the versions
 * it requires (the game reads them too), each from its own learned order —; progress { bytes, total, done } to the page.
 */
async function startup() {
  const lists = await order(), fast = W.version.net.fast();
  const heads = W.version.parts.map((p, i) => ({ p, head: launchSet(p.files, lists[i], fast), progress: { bytes: 0, blocks: 0, done: false } })).filter((h) => h.head.length);
  // (a fast link fetches the set's blocks whole: counted so; the progress never past its total all the same)
  const total = heads.reduce((n, h) => n + setBytes(h.p.files, h.head, fast).bytes, 0);
  const bytes = () => Math.min(total, heads.reduce((n, h) => n + h.progress.bytes, 0));
  if (!heads.length) { postMessage({ startup: { bytes: 0, total: 0, done: true } }); return; }
  const tick = setInterval(() => postMessage({ startup: { bytes: bytes(), total, done: false } }), 250);
  // (the pieces sessions read only: the rest of their blocks comes with the learned order, once the engine runs)
  try { for (const h of heads) { if (W.stop) break; await h.p.files.prefetch(h.head, h.progress, () => W.stop, { learnedOnly: true }); } }
  finally { clearInterval(tick); postMessage({ startup: { bytes: bytes(), total, done: true } }); }
}

/**
 * The learned order loaded now, before the engine's first read (GameData.prefetchNow: a page whose engine went quiet on
 * the link — OpenMW's once its package is in, its main() initialising for seconds before it reads a game file), only
 * on a cold store (less than LAUNCH_COLD of the launch set's bytes here: a new device, a store cleared, a version
 * updated): the link idle meanwhile fetches what the way to the menu reads first. A warm one, even missing part of the
 * set (another session's first place, entries learned since), starts at the first read as before
 * ('first-read': requests beside an engine's boot delay its first read — docs/openmw.md "Anticipated places" —, and
 * nothing there would be fetched). Its progress told to the page every BOOT_TELL_MS until that first read (boot).
 */
async function prefetchNow() {
  if (W.prefetching || W.stop) return;
  const lists = await order();
  if (W.prefetching || W.stop) return;
  // (judged on the set the home's card and "Prepare" call ready: the light one for an engine that reloads in place —
  // W.reloads, told by the page before its engine runs, read after the order's await; a store "Prepare" left at its
  // light stage is warm — and the files' own set on a fast link otherwise: lightLaunch)
  const fast = !lightLaunch(W.version.net.fast(), W.reloads);
  let bytes = 0, here = 0;
  W.version.parts.forEach((p, i) => { const s = setBytes(p.files, launchSet(p.files, lists[i], fast)); bytes += s.bytes; here += s.here; });
  if (!bytes || here >= bytes * LAUNCH_COLD) return;
  // (paced only before the engine's first read: one that came while the order was on its way ended the boot)
  W.boot = !W.readSeen;
  prefetchAll();
}

/**
 * The whole learned order, in the background from the game's position in it (HttpBackend.prefetch), every part's; its
 * progress to the page every second ({ ahead: { done, total, finished } }: entries of the order passed, of all).
 */
async function prefetchAll() {
  if (W.prefetching) return;
  W.prefetching = true;
  const lists = await order(), runs = [];
  W.version.parts.forEach((p, i) => {
    if (!lists[i].length) return;
    const progress = { bytes: 0, blocks: 0, done: false };
    // (its launch set first: a player waiting in the menu gets what the way to playable still needs first — launchFirst)
    const list = launchFirst(p.files, lists[i], W.version.net.fast());
    // (made again when the link's class changes: the rate this page started with was another page's — relist)
    runs.push({ p, progress, job: p.files.prefetch(list, progress, () => W.stop, { first: list.first, relist: (fast) => launchFirst(p.files, lists[i], fast) }).catch(() => {}) });
  });
  W.runs = runs;
  if (!runs.length) return;
  launchWatch(lists);
  const tell = () => {
    let done = 0, total = 0;
    for (const { p, progress } of runs) { const n = p.files.learned?.entries.length ?? 0; total += n; done += progress.done ? n : Math.min(n, Math.max(0, (progress.k ?? -1) + 1)); }
    postMessage({ ahead: { done, total, finished: runs.every((r) => r.progress.done) } });
  };
  // (paced while the engine boots: each post a task of the page's thread — and of the page around it — the boot shares)
  let told = -1e9;
  const tick = setInterval(() => { const now = performance.now(); if (W.boot && now - told < BOOT_TELL_MS) return; told = now; tell(); }, 1000);
  await Promise.all(runs.map((r) => r.job));
  clearInterval(tick); tell();
}

/**
 * The way to playable, told to the page every LAUNCH_TELL_MS while the game is not there yet ({ launch: { bytes, here,
 * wireLeft, seconds, done } }): the launch set of every part as this link reads it (launch-set.js: what earlier
 * sessions read before their game was playable — a new game's first load included), its bytes here already, the wire
 * bytes left (the link's measured ratio of wire to decoded bytes, else WIRE_RATIO) and the seconds they take at the
 * link's measured rate (null until measured). The set prefetchAll fetches first (launchFirst on this link's class), not
 * the light one the home announces for an engine that reloads in place (lightLaunch): counted on a set nothing fetches,
 * the pill would stay at its light copies' bytes while the link brings the files. Only for an order with flags (a
 * session marked the version playable); over once all of it is here or the game is playable (the page's mark).
 */
function launchWatch(lists) {
  if (!lists.some(flagged)) return;
  let sets = null, fastWas = null, timer = null, told = -1e9;
  const tell = () => {
    const now = performance.now();
    if (W.boot && now - told < BOOT_TELL_MS) return false;
    told = now;
    const net = W.version.net, fast = net.fast();
    if (fast !== fastWas) { fastWas = fast; sets = W.version.parts.map((p, i) => ({ p, set: launchSet(p.files, lists[i], fast) })); }
    let bytes = 0, here = 0;
    for (const { p, set } of sets) { const s = setBytes(p.files, set); bytes += s.bytes; here += s.here; }
    // (WIRE_RATIO at least: the session's own ratio so far is a game's master files', which compress far better than the
    // textures and models of a first load — measured at 85 KB/s, it said "< 1 min" for a load of 86 s)
    const ratio = Math.max(WIRE_RATIO, net.totals.rawBytes >= 1 << 20 ? net.ratio() : 0), wireLeft = Math.round(Math.max(0, bytes - here) * ratio);
    const seconds = net.measured && net.bw > 0 ? Math.ceil(wireLeft / net.bw) : null;
    const done = here >= bytes || W.marks.has('playable') || W.stop;
    postMessage({ launch: { bytes, here, wireLeft, seconds, done } });
    if (done && timer !== null) clearInterval(timer);
    return done;
  };
  if (!tell()) W.timers.push(timer = setInterval(tell, LAUNCH_TELL_MS));
}

/** The whole version (and the ones it requires) into the browser's copy, in the background, after the game's reads. */
async function wholeDownload() {
  if (W.whole && !W.whole.stop) return;
  const w = W.whole = { stop: false, bytes: 0, total: W.version.parts.reduce((n, p) => n + p.total, 0), done: false };
  const lists = await order();
  const tick = setInterval(() => postMessage({ whole: { bytes: w.bytes, total: w.total, done: false } }), 1000);
  try {
    for (const [i, p] of W.version.parts.entries()) {
      const progress = { bytes: 0, total: 0, done: false }, before = w.bytes;
      const watch = setInterval(() => { w.bytes = before + (progress.bytes ?? 0); }, 250); // (bytes: those stored before included)
      try { await p.files.downloadAll(progress, () => w.stop || W.stop, { order: lists[i] }); } finally { clearInterval(watch); }
      w.bytes = before + p.total;
      if (w.stop || !progress.done) return;
    }
    w.done = true;
  } finally { clearInterval(tick); postMessage({ whole: { bytes: w.bytes, total: w.total, done: w.done, stopped: w.stop } }); }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the indicator's counters

function monitor() {
  const { ctrl } = W, net = W.version.net, raw = net.totals.rawBytes;
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 2, raw % 0x7fffffff);
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 6, W.waiting);
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 7, net.fast() ? 1 : 0); Atomics.store(ctrl, 8, net.measured && net.bw > 0 ? Math.round(net.bw / 1024) : 0);
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 9, net.thin() ? 1 : 0);
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 15, Math.round(net.ratio() * 1000));
  const now = performance.now();
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 10, aheadIdle() ? 1 : 0);
  Atomics.store(ctrl, 11, W.waiting > 0 ? 0 : Math.min(0x7fffffff, Math.round(now - W.lastWait)));
  // (the current step: from the first wait after a pause, the bytes received, and those the learned order says remain)
  if (W.waiting > 0) {
    W.step ??= { base: raw };
    let rest = null;
    for (const p of W.version.parts) { const e = p.files.stepEstimate(); if (e) rest = (rest ?? 0) + e.bytes; }
    const done = raw - W.step.base;
    Atomics.store(ctrl, 4, Math.round(done / 1024)); Atomics.store(ctrl, 5, rest === null ? 0 : Math.round((done + rest) / 1024));
  } else if (W.step && now - W.lastWait > STEP_PAUSE_MS) { W.step = null; Atomics.store(ctrl, 4, 0); Atomics.store(ctrl, 5, 0); }
  // (the link's counters for the page's reports — GameData.snapshot's `net`: the background's bytes by producer —, every second)
  if (now - (W.netAt ?? -1e9) >= 1000) { W.netAt = now; postMessage({ net: net.snapshot() }); }
}

/**
 * The learned order's loading has nothing left for the game's current step: it does not run, it is over, or the
 * entries past the game's position up to its next pause are here (HttpBackend.stepEstimate) — every part's.
 */
function aheadIdle() {
  if (!W.prefetching) return true;
  if (!W.runs) return false; // (its order on its way)
  return W.runs.every(({ p, progress }) => progress.done || p.files.stepEstimate()?.bytes === 0);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- light copies: the files themselves after them

/** The key the page knows a file by (data-client.js). */
const lightKey = (name, path) => name + '\n' + path.toLowerCase();

/**
 * The engine read the light copy of `path`: the file itself in the background (HttpBackend.upgrade), told once here;
 * `soon` for an engine that loads it again in place (GameData.reloads: the player sees it sharpen).
 */
function upgrade(name, path, soon = false) {
  const part = route(name, path), r = part?.files.lookup(path); if (!r?.file) return;
  part.files.upgrade(r.path, { soon });
}

/**
 * The files that have a light copy, as they come (every second): one here whole now — upgraded, or brought by the
 * whole download, the learned order, a read — is told to the page (`real`: read itself from its next load); one whose
 * light copy is here whole (`lightHere`: read light even on a fast link — the learned order brought it before the link
 * was measured — until the file itself is here).
 */
function lightWatch() {
  const real = [], lightHere = [];
  for (const [k, e] of W.light) {
    if (e.part.files.isWhole(e.path)) { real.push(k); W.light.delete(k); }
    else if (!e.told && e.part.files.isWhole(`${LIGHT_DIR}/${e.path}`)) { e.told = true; lightHere.push(k); }
  }
  if (real.length || lightHere.length) postMessage({ real, lightHere });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- copies kept by earlier versions of the page

/**
 * A copy of a file an earlier version of the page kept elsewhere (told by the page: { name, path, module, args } — the
 * runtime's module that knows that copy, its `adopt(args, keep)` handing its bytes to keep(at, bytes)): taken into the
 * store before the file's first read, once.
 */
async function adoptLegacy(name, path, part, f) {
  const key = name + '\n' + path.toLowerCase(), rec = W.legacy.get(key);
  if (!rec) return;
  W.legacy.delete(key);
  try {
    let mod = W.adopters.get(rec.module);
    if (!mod) W.adopters.set(rec.module, mod = import(rec.module));
    await (await mod).adopt(rec.args, (at, bytes) => part.files.keep(f.path, f.len, f.mtime, at, bytes));
  } catch (err) { postMessage({ log: `${path}: an earlier copy not taken (${err?.message ?? err})` }); }
}

/**
 * Bytes the page kept elsewhere before (an earlier store of the page: { name, path, at, bytes } — whole blocks or 64 KiB
 * pieces of the file `path` from offset `at`), put into this store as if fetched.
 */
function migrate(list) {
  for (const { name, path, at, bytes } of list) {
    const part = route(name, path), f = handle(name, path);
    if (!part?.store || !f || at % CHUNK || at + bytes.length > f.len) continue;
    part.files.keep(f.path, f.len, f.mtime, at, bytes);
  }
  postMessage({ migrated: list.length });
}
```

`src/vfs/emscripten-files.js`:

```js
// The game's files in the file system of an Emscripten engine that runs in the page (GoldSrc, re3, OpenMW, the next
// ones — CLAUDE.md "Standardization"): a node per file, its size known at once, its bytes from the game data
// (data-client.js) as the engine reads them. Read-only; an engine that suspends while it waits (JSPI) asks for its
// bytes ahead (`node.orthrosStreamed`: whether it then waits for them or goes on, the game data tells by what the engine
// does meanwhile — data-client.js holdCheck); one that maps a file (mmap) gets it whole.

/** open()'s flags (Emscripten's, musl's values). */
const O_ACCMODE = 3, O_EXCL = 0o200, O_TRUNC = 0o1000;

/**
 * A node at `at` (an absolute path of the engine's file system) for the game file `h` (GameData.file).
 * @param {object} FS the engine's FS
 * @param {string} at
 * @param {import('./data-client.js').GameData} data
 * @param {object} h
 * @param {{ asyncReads?: boolean, mmap?: boolean, log?: (text: string) => void }} [o]
 *   asyncReads: the engine asks for missing bytes before reading (node.orthrosStreamed: missing, ensure, complete; soon —
 *   null when they are here within a few ms of the page's thread, else a promise: GameData.soon);
 *   mmap: false — the engine reads the file with read() only (its mmap fails: ENOSYS), as an engine that streams expects
 */
export function fileNode(FS, at, data, h, o = {}) {
  const slash = at.lastIndexOf('/'), dir = slash <= 0 ? '/' : at.slice(0, slash);
  FS.mkdirTree(dir);
  const node = FS.createFile(dir, at.slice(slash + 1), {}, true, false);
  Object.defineProperty(node, 'usedBytes', { get: () => h.size });
  Object.defineProperty(node, 'contents', { get: () => h.whole, set: () => {} }); // (whole once mapped: mmap reads it)
  const getattr = node.node_ops?.getattr;
  if (getattr) node.node_ops = { ...node.node_ops, getattr(n) { const a = getattr(n); a.size = h.size; return a; } };
  const ops = node.stream_ops, own = { ...ops };
  // (bytes that cannot be had: a read error for the engine (EIO), not an exception through its code)
  const fail = (e) => { if (e instanceof FS.ErrnoError) throw e; o.log?.(`${h.path}: ${e.message}`); throw new FS.ErrnoError(29); };
  const io = (fn) => { try { return fn(); } catch (e) { fail(e); } };
  own.llseek = (stream, off, whence) => {
    const p = whence === 1 ? stream.position + off : whence === 2 ? h.size + off : off;
    if (p < 0) throw new FS.ErrnoError(28);
    return p;
  };
  // (no closure a read: the engine reads thousands of times a second)
  own.read = (stream, buffer, offset, length, position) => { try { return data.read(h, buffer, offset, length, position); } catch (e) { fail(e); } };
  own.mmap = o.mmap === false ? () => { throw new FS.ErrnoError(52); } : (...a) => io(() => { data.whole(h); return ops.mmap(...a); });
  own.write = () => { throw new FS.ErrnoError(o.mmap === false ? 63 : 69); }; // (EROFS: the game files are read-only)
  node.stream_ops = own;
  if (o.asyncReads) {
    node.orthrosStreamed = { missing: (position, length) => data.missing(h, position, length), ensure: (position, length) => data.ensure(h, position, length),
      soon: (position, length, spinMs) => data.soon(h, position, length, spinMs), complete: () => data.wantWhole(h) };
  }
  return node;
}

/**
 * The game's phases told by its files (GameData.phase): a node among `nodes` whose path `phaseOf` names (a GoldSrc
 * map's .bsp: its map) starts that phase once an open of it has read at least half the file — a load, not a listing
 * that reads its header —, dated from that open's first read. Returns how many nodes are watched.
 * @param {object} FS the engine's FS
 * @param {Iterable<object>} nodes the game's file nodes (mountFiles)
 * @param {{ phase: (name: string, ago?: number) => void }} data
 * @param {(path: string) => string | null} phaseOf
 */
export function phaseOnRead(FS, nodes, data, phaseOf) {
  let n = 0;
  for (const node of nodes) {
    const name = phaseOf(FS.getPath(node)); if (!name) continue;
    const ops = node.stream_ops, read = ops.read, size = node.usedBytes;
    // (told before the read that reaches half the file: its own fetches, and those after it, are the phase's)
    node.stream_ops = { ...ops, read(stream, buffer, offset, length, position) {
      stream.orthrosFirstRead ??= performance.now();
      stream.orthrosRead = (stream.orthrosRead ?? 0) + Math.max(0, Math.min(length, size - position));
      if (!stream.orthrosPhase && stream.orthrosRead * 2 >= size) { stream.orthrosPhase = true; data.phase(name, performance.now() - stream.orthrosFirstRead); }
      return read(stream, buffer, offset, length, position);
    } };
    n++;
  }
  return n;
}

/**
 * The game's files (`files`: [{ path, at? }] of version `name` — `at`, where a language's file goes, languageFiles)
 * under `root`. `rewritable`: a game file the engine opens to write it anew (O_TRUNC: fopen's "w") replaced by an empty
 * file of the engine's own in its place, as in a game folder the player may write in (not when the open must create
 * it — O_EXCL — nor to change it in place: read-only). Returns the nodes.
 */
export function mountFiles(FS, root, data, name, files, o = {}) {
  const nodes = new Set();
  for (const f of files) {
    const h = data.file(name, f.path); if (!h) continue;
    nodes.add(fileNode(FS, `${root}/${f.at ?? h.path}`, data, h, o));
  }
  if (o.rewritable) {
    const open = FS.open;
    const anew = (flags) => (typeof flags === 'string' ? flags[0] === 'w' && !flags.includes('x') : (flags & O_TRUNC) && (flags & O_ACCMODE) && !(flags & O_EXCL));
    FS.open = function (at, flags, mode) {
      if (typeof at === 'string' && anew(flags)) {
        let node = null; try { node = FS.lookupPath(at, { follow: true }).node; } catch { /* not there */ }
        if (node && nodes.has(node)) { FS.unlink(at); FS.writeFile(at, new Uint8Array(0)); }
      }
      return open.call(this, at, flags, mode);
    };
  }
  return nodes;
}

/**
 * `fn(name)` once each of the engine's file_packager packages is in (its run dependency `datafile_<name>` removed: its
 * download and unpacking over — the engine's own download, before its main() and its first read of the game's files),
 * through `Module.removeRunDependency`, which the packager's code looks up on Module at that moment. Works installed
 * before the engine's script sets that function on Module (kept through an accessor) or after it. Returns an off().
 * @param {object} Module the engine's Module (the page's global, the engine's script not loaded yet or loaded)
 * @param {(name: string) => void} fn
 */
export function onPackageLoaded(Module, fn) {
  if (!Module || typeof Module !== 'object') return () => {};
  const wrap = (f) => (typeof f !== 'function' ? f : function (id) {
    const r = f.apply(this, arguments);
    if (live && typeof id === 'string' && id.startsWith('datafile_')) try { fn(id.slice('datafile_'.length)); } catch { /* the page's */ }
    return r;
  });
  let live = true, current = wrap(Module.removeRunDependency);
  Object.defineProperty(Module, 'removeRunDependency', { configurable: true, enumerable: true, get: () => current, set: (f) => { current = wrap(f); } });
  return () => { live = false; };
}
```

`src/vfs/file-alias-backend.js`:

```js
// A read-only view of a game folder with selected files served from other paths
// in that same folder. The guest keeps its original filenames; the source files
// and the underlying backend remain unchanged.
export class FileAliasBackend {
  /** `hidden`: paths the game does not see at all (a language's own files while another language is chosen). */
  constructor(backend, aliases = {}, hidden = []) {
    this.backend = backend;
    this.aliases = new Map(Object.entries(aliases).map(([from, to]) => [this.key(from), to]));
    this.hidden = new Set(hidden.map((p) => this.key(p)));
  }

  key(rel) { return rel.replaceAll('\\', '/').toLowerCase(); }
  source(rel) { return this.aliases.get(this.key(rel)) ?? rel; }
  stat(rel) { return this.hidden.has(this.key(rel)) ? null : this.backend.stat(this.source(rel)); }
  open(rel, opts = {}) {
    if (opts.write || opts.create || opts.truncate || this.hidden.has(this.key(rel))) return null;
    return this.backend.open(this.source(rel), opts);
  }
  readdir(rel) {
    const entries = this.backend.readdir(rel);
    if (!entries) return null;
    return entries.filter((entry) => !this.hidden.has(this.key(rel ? `${rel}/${entry.name}` : entry.name))).map((entry) => {
      const source = this.aliases.get(this.key(rel ? `${rel}/${entry.name}` : entry.name));
      return source ? { ...entry, ...this.backend.stat(source) } : entry;
    });
  }
  mkdir() { return false; }
  unlink() { return false; }
  rename() { return false; }
}
```

`src/vfs/game-data.js`:

```js
// A game version's data, the same for every runtime (CLAUDE.md "Standardization", docs/slow-network.md): its tree
// (/api/tree), the reader over the server's compressed ranges (HttpBackend, /gamez), the browser's copy of what it read
// (the OPFS block store orthros-files-<manifest>), the order earlier sessions read it in (/api/prefetch) and the
// versions it requires (manifest.extraMounts), all on one connection (NetLink). Opened by the Windows games' worker
// (src/host/web/worker.js), the data worker of the engines that run in the page (data-worker.js) and the whole-game
// download (src/host/web/download-worker.js).
// The files a version takes from one it requires (a port's underlays: the server marks them `owner`, game-files.js) are
// that version's: read through a part of its own (`shared`), its store orthros-files-<owner> and /gamez/<owner>/ —
// one copy in the browser for every version that reads them (docs/slow-network.md "Files of a required version").
import { HttpBackend } from './http-backend.js';
import { NetLink } from './net-link.js';
import { OpfsBlockStore } from './opfs-store.js';
import { treeBytes, treeOwner, splitOwners } from './game-tree.js';

const enc = encodeURIComponent;
async function json(url) {
  const r = await fetch(url);
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: HTTP ${r.status}`);
  return r.json();
}

/**
 * The browser's copy of a version's files (OPFS: one context at a time), or null when it cannot be opened. Opened under
 * the store's Web Lock (storeLocks): an open waits out the home's probe counting the store in this tab or another (a
 * moment), instead of failing and running the session without its store.
 */
export const openStore = (name) => storeLocks([name], () => openStoreNow(name));
/** openStore without the lock: the caller holds it (the home's probe, download-worker.js `probe`). */
export const openStoreNow = (name) => OpfsBlockStore.open('orthros-files-' + name);

/**
 * Runs `fn(got)` holding the Web Locks of the stores of `names` (navigator.locks, shared by every tab and worker of the
 * origin; held only while a store is opened — openStore — or opened, counted and closed — the probe). `o.ifAvailable`:
 * do not wait — `got` false when another context holds one of them (fn runs unlocked, to say so). Without Web Locks
 * (an old browser, a test): fn(true) at once. Taken in one order, by name, whoever asks (a version's store and its
 * owners' — a page of one edition and a probe or a page of another take the same locks —: no two contexts each wait
 * for the lock the other holds).
 * @template T @param {string[]} names @param {(got: boolean) => T|Promise<T>} fn @param {{ ifAvailable?: boolean }} [o]
 * @returns {Promise<T>}
 */
export async function storeLocks(names, fn, o = {}) {
  const locks = globalThis.navigator?.locks;
  if (!locks?.request || !names.length) return fn(true);
  const [n, ...rest] = [...new Set(names)].sort();
  return locks.request('orthros-store-' + n, { ifAvailable: !!o.ifAvailable }, (l) => (l || !o.ifAvailable ? lockedRest(rest, fn, o) : fn(false)));
}
// (the rest of storeLocks' names, already in order)
const lockedRest = (names, fn, o) => {
  if (!names.length) return fn(true);
  const [n, ...rest] = names;
  return navigator.locks.request('orthros-store-' + n, { ifAvailable: !!o.ifAvailable }, (l) => (l || !o.ifAvailable ? lockedRest(rest, fn, o) : fn(false)));
};

/**
 * The browser has a copy of a version's files: true when its OPFS directory exists (looked up without creating it —
 * openStore creates it), false when it does not, null when OPFS cannot say (no OPFS, an error).
 */
export async function storeExists(name) {
  let root; try { root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory(); } catch { return null; }
  try { await root.getDirectoryHandle('orthros-files-' + name); return true; } catch (e) { return e?.name === 'NotFoundError' ? false : null; }
}

/** The order earlier sessions read a version in (/api/prefetch: [path, block, pieces mask, ms]); [] when none. */
export const learnedOrder = (name, lang = null) => fetch(`/api/prefetch/${enc(name)}${lang ? `?lang=${enc(lang)}` : ''}`).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : [])).then((l) => (Array.isArray(l) ? l : [])).catch(() => []);

/**
 * The learned orders of an opened version's parts (openVersion), one list a part in its order: each version's own
 * (learnedOrder), its entries of files another version owns (treeOwner: a required version's, read by this one's
 * sessions — the version learns them as its own reads) moved to that owner's part, in their order; a shared part has
 * no order of its own (the owner's is its own players', not this game's reads).
 */
export async function learnedOrders(version, lang = null) {
  const lists = await Promise.all(version.parts.map((p) => (p.shared ? [] : learnedOrder(p.name, lang))));
  const at = new Map(version.parts.map((p, i) => [p.name, i]));
  version.parts.forEach((p, i) => {
    if (p.shared || !p.owned?.size) return;
    const keep = [];
    for (const e of lists[i]) {
      const owner = typeof e?.[0] === 'string' ? treeOwner(p.tree, e[0], p.name) : null, j = owner ? at.get(owner) : undefined;
      if (j !== undefined && j !== i) lists[j].push(e); else keep.push(e);
    }
    lists[i] = keep;
  });
  return lists;
}

/**
 * The part of an opened version (openVersion) that reads the file `path` of part `name` as the game sees it: that
 * part, or the part of the version owning the file (treeOwner) — remembered per path. Null for no such part.
 */
export function partOf(version, name, path) {
  const routes = version.routes ??= new Map(), key = name + '\n' + path;
  let p = routes.get(key);
  if (p === undefined) {
    const own = version.parts.find((q) => q.name === name && !q.shared) ?? null;
    const owner = own?.owned?.size ? treeOwner(own.tree, path, own.name) : null;
    p = (owner && version.parts.find((q) => q.name === owner)) || own;
    routes.set(key, p);
  }
  return p;
}

/**
 * One version's data: { name, tree, store, files (its HttpBackend), total (bytes) }.
 * @param {string} name the manifest
 * @param {{ tree?: object, store?: object|null|'opfs', net?: NetLink, link?: Set<HttpBackend>, session?: string,
 *   cacheBlocks?: number, encoded?: boolean, onFetch?: Function, onRetry?: Function, onRead?: Function }} [o]
 *   store: the block store, 'opfs' for the version's own, null for none; encoded: the compressed ranges (default);
 *   onRead: each read of the game (path, start, end), whatever answered it
 */
export async function openData(name, o = {}) {
  const tree = o.tree ?? await json(`/api/tree/${enc(name)}`);
  const store = o.store === 'opfs' ? await openStore(name) : o.store ?? null;
  const files = new HttpBackend(`/game/${name}/`, tree, { cacheBlocks: o.cacheBlocks, store, encoded: o.encoded ?? true, session: o.session ?? '',
    link: o.link, net: o.net, onFetch: o.onFetch, onRetry: o.onRetry, onRead: o.onRead });
  return { name, tree, store, files, total: treeBytes(tree) };
}

/**
 * A version and the versions it requires (manifest.extraMounts), on one connection: { net, manifest, parts:
 * [primary, ...dependencies, ...shared] } (openData's). Each part's `tree` is its tree as the game sees it, its `files`
 * read its own files only (`files.tree`, `total` their bytes); the files it takes from another version (the server's
 * `owner` marks, splitOwners) are read by a part of that version — one already opened, else a `shared` part (its tree
 * those files only, no session: the owner's order does not learn another game's reads), after the others. `owned`: a
 * part's owners. Route a read with partOf, a learned order with learnedOrders. `o.store`: a store option for every part,
 * or (name, primary, shared) => one — a shared part's null when the owner's store cannot be had (another tab's game
 * holds it): its files then kept where they were before the owners, the store of the parts that read them.
 * `o.kept(name)`: whether that version's store is the browser's (default: any store; the data worker's in memory are
 * not). A shared part's store is an UnderStore over the stores of the parts that read its files: what they kept of them
 * before (pages before the `owner` marks) is read there, and moved under the owner as it is read.
 * The manifest (`o.manifest`, the page's when it holds it: no request), the version's tree (`o.tree`, likewise) and its
 * store are had at once, then every required version's tree and store at once: one wait each instead of one after
 * another (a page that opens its data while its engine downloads — docs/slow-network.md "Opened early"). A failure
 * closes the stores that opened.
 */
export async function openVersion(name, o = {}) {
  const net = o.net ?? new NetLink({ bw: o.bw }), link = new Set();
  const storeOf = (n, primary, sh = false) => (typeof o.store === 'function' ? o.store(n, primary, sh) : o.store);
  const kept = (n, st) => !!st && typeof st === 'object' && (o.kept ? !!o.kept(n) : true);
  // (a version's tree and store, together; its store closed when its tree cannot be had. Each promise observed as it
  // is made — awaited later: a store that fails while the tree is in flight, or a tree while the manifest is, is not an
  // unhandled rejection — Node's process killed, the worker's "Uncaught (in promise)" before its clean failure)
  const both = async (n, primary, tree) => {
    const store = Promise.resolve(storeOf(n, primary));
    store.catch(() => {});
    try { return { n, tree: await (tree ?? json(`/api/tree/${enc(n)}`)), store: await store }; }
    catch (e) { store.then((st) => st?.close?.(), () => {}); throw e; }
  };
  const first = both(name, true, o.tree);
  first.catch(() => {});
  let manifest;
  try { manifest = await (o.manifest ?? json(`/api/manifest/${enc(name)}`)); }
  catch (e) { first.then((x) => x.store?.close?.(), () => {}); throw e; }
  const deps = [...new Set((Array.isArray(manifest.extraMounts) ? manifest.extraMounts.map((d) => d.manifest).filter(Boolean) : []))].filter((n) => n !== name);
  const got = await Promise.allSettled([first, ...deps.map((n) => both(n, false))]);
  const bad = got.find((g) => g.status === 'rejected');
  if (bad) { for (const g of got) if (g.status === 'fulfilled') g.value.store?.close?.(); throw bad.reason; }
  const names = [name, ...deps], parts = [], shared = new Map();
  for (const { value: { n, tree, store } } of got) {
    const { own, owners } = splitOwners(tree, n);
    const part = await openData(n, { ...o, net, link, store, tree: own });
    parts.push(Object.assign(part, { tree, owned: new Set(owners.keys()) }));
    for (const [owner, t] of owners) shared.set(owner, shared.has(owner) ? mergeTrees(shared.get(owner), t) : t);
  }
  for (const [owner, tree] of shared) {
    if (names.includes(owner)) continue; // (opened already: its tree has them)
    const top = await storeOf(owner, false, true);
    const below = parts.filter((p) => p.owned.has(owner) && kept(p.name, p.store)).map((p) => p.store);
    const store = !below.length ? top : new UnderStore(kept(owner, top) ? top : null, below);
    const part = await openData(owner, { ...o, net, link, store, tree, session: '' });
    parts.push(Object.assign(part, { shared: true, owned: new Set() }));
  }
  return { net, manifest, parts };
}

/**
 * A shared part's store (openVersion): the owner's store `top` over the stores of the versions that read its files
 * (`below`, each the browser's) — those kept their own copies of them before the server marked their owner. A block is
 * here when either has it; read from `below`, it is put into `top` and forgotten there (moved as it is read: no copy of
 * a whole store at the open — 1.5 GB of an offline copy before the page is ready —, nothing fetched again). New blocks
 * go to `top`; with no `top` (the owner's store held by another tab's game) or once it failed (the device full), to the
 * first of `below` that works — as before the owners: the files kept, not fetched again at each launch. A moved
 * block's bytes stay in the data file of the store it left until that store's cache is cleared (OpfsBlockStore appends
 * only). Closing it closes `top` only: each of `below` is its own part's.
 */
export class UnderStore {
  /** @param {object|null} top @param {object[]} below */
  constructor(top, below) {
    this.top = top; this.below = below;
    const has = (k) => !!top?.map.has(k) || below.some((b) => b.map.has(k));
    this.map = { has, get size() { return (top?.map.size ?? 0) + below.reduce((a, b) => a + b.map.size, 0); } };
    this.stats = top?.stats ?? below[0]?.stats ?? { hits: 0, puts: 0, bytes: 0 };
  }
  /** the store new blocks go to (null: none works) */
  get writer() { return this.top && !this.top.failed ? this.top : this.below.find((b) => !b.failed) ?? null; }
  get failed() { return !this.writer; }
  get(key) {
    const t = this.top && !this.top.failed ? this.top.get(key) : null; if (t) return t;
    for (const b of this.below) {
      if (!b.map.has(key)) continue;
      const bytes = b.get(key); if (!bytes) continue;
      const top = this.top;
      if (top && !top.failed) { top.put(key, bytes); if (top.map.has(key)) b.drop(key); }
      return bytes;
    }
    return null;
  }
  put(key, bytes) { if (!this.map.has(key)) this.writer?.put(key, bytes); }
  drop(key) { this.top?.drop(key); for (const b of this.below) b.drop(key); }
  flush(force = false) { this.top?.flush?.(force); for (const b of this.below) b.flush?.(force); }
  close() { this.top?.close?.(); }
}

/** Two trees' files together (`a` changed): those of `b` added. */
function mergeTrees(a, b) {
  Object.assign(a.files, b.files);
  for (const [n, d] of Object.entries(b.dirs)) a.dirs[n] = a.dirs[n] ? mergeTrees(a.dirs[n], d) : d;
  return a;
}
```

`src/vfs/game-tree.js`:

```js
// A game version's tree as the server lists it (/api/tree/<manifest>: { dirs, files: { name: { size, mtime } } }), for
// every runtime (CLAUDE.md "Standardization"): its files as a list, its size, a language's view of it.

/**
 * The light copies' folder in a version's paths (src/host/light-copies.js: a texture without its finest levels, for a
 * slow link — the tree tells a file's light size, `light`; read as `.light/<path>`).
 */
export const LIGHT_DIR = '.light';

/**
 * Media files by format (movies, music, long sounds), for every runtime: the server marks them in the tree (`media:
 * true`); on a link that is not fast they come after every other file the game reads (learned order, offline copy), are
 * left out of the startup set, and get no speculative fills unless the game is streaming them (src/vfs/http-backend.js,
 * data-worker.js). Their bytes are never faked: a read of one waits for the network as any other.
 */
const MEDIA = /\.(bik|bk2|mp3|ogg|avi|mpg|mpeg|wmv|smk|webm)$/i;
/** Movies among the media files: a game playing one is not playable yet (playable-watch.js). */
const VIDEO = /\.(bik|bk2|avi|mpg|mpeg|wmv|smk|webm)$/i;
/** The file `name` is a movie (by format). */
export const isVideoFile = (name) => VIDEO.test(name);
/** A .wav this large or larger is a media file (music, speech); smaller ones are a game's sound effects. */
export const MEDIA_WAV_BYTES = 512 << 10;
/** The file `name` of `size` bytes is a media file (see MEDIA). */
export function isMediaFile(name, size) { return MEDIA.test(name) || (/\.wav$/i.test(name) && size >= MEDIA_WAV_BYTES); }

/**
 * A file whose light copy is a picture rather than a texture, by format: src/host/light-copies.js lightens a TGA only
 * when it is a picture of a screen's size (TGA_LIGHT_FROM: a loading screen, a map) — shown a moment, often never again;
 * on a link that is not fast its file is not fetched after its light copy (HttpBackend.upgrade), it comes with the
 * offline copy, or read itself on a fast link.
 */
export const isLightPicture = (name) => /\.tga$/i.test(name);

/**
 * A content file whose light copy keeps only what an engine reads of it while it loads its content (src/host/light-
 * copies.js esmZeroRanges, by format: a TES3 file — Morrowind's masters and plugins, its LAND payloads and cell
 * references' details zeroed, every offset kept): read light only until the engine says its content is loaded
 * (data-client.js GameData.contentLoading / contentLoaded), on every link — the file itself from then on, by the ranges
 * its cells read; never fetched whole after its light copy (no upgrade), nor read light by an engine that does not say
 * so. docs/slow-network.md "Content files light before the menu".
 */
export const isLightContent = (name) => /\.(esm|esp|omwaddon|omwgame)$/i.test(name);

/**
 * An image file (a texture: DDS, TGA, PNG, JPEG, BMP, KTX), which an engine reads whole once it reads it: its first
 * missing piece is asked for to the file's end (data-client.js askedEnd, where the engine's page asks for it: wholeLoads).
 */
export const isWholeImage = (name) => /\.(dds|tga|png|jpe?g|bmp|ktx2?)$/i.test(name);

/** Native binaries of an installation: useless to a WebAssembly engine, never part of its files. */
const NATIVE = /\.(exe|dll|so|dylib)$/i;

/** Total bytes of a tree. */
export function treeBytes(node) {
  let n = 0;
  for (const f of Object.values(node.files ?? {})) n += f.size ?? 0;
  for (const d of Object.values(node.dirs ?? {})) n += treeBytes(d);
  return n;
}

/** The files of a tree ({ path, size, mtime, light?, media? }), dot files and native binaries left out. */
export function treeFiles(tree) {
  const files = [];
  (function walk(node, prefix) {
    for (const [dir, sub] of Object.entries(node.dirs ?? {})) if (!dir.startsWith('.')) walk(sub, prefix + dir + '/');
    for (const [file, st] of Object.entries(node.files ?? {})) if (!file.startsWith('.') && !NATIVE.test(file)) files.push({ path: prefix + file, size: st.size, mtime: st.mtime ?? 0, ...(st.light ? { light: st.light } : {}), ...(st.media ? { media: true } : {}) });
  })(tree, '');
  return files;
}

/**
 * The game's files as a language shows them (goldsrc.languages.<code>.overlays: { "valve_french": "valve" }): each file of
 * a language folder is mounted at the same place in the folder it translates (`at`), over the original of that path
 * (compared without case, as the engine finds files); the language folders themselves are not mounted otherwise.
 * Without overlays, the files as they are, the language folders left out of the engine's tree.
 */
export function languageFiles(files, overlays = {}, known = []) {
  const lower = (p) => p.toLowerCase(), top = (p) => lower(p.split('/')[0]);
  const over = new Map(Object.entries(overlays).map(([from, to]) => [lower(from), to]));
  const hidden = new Set([...known.map(lower)].filter((d) => !over.has(d)));
  const translated = new Map();
  for (const f of files) {
    const to = over.get(top(f.path)); if (!to) continue;
    const at = to + f.path.slice(f.path.indexOf('/'));
    translated.set(lower(at), { ...f, at });
  }
  const out = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    const t = top(f.path);
    if (over.has(t) || hidden.has(t)) continue;
    if (!translated.has(lower(f.path))) out.push(f);
  }
  return [...out, ...translated.values()];
}

/** The file at `rel` in a tree, found without case: { path (its real names), size, mtime, light? }, or null. */
export function treeFile(tree, rel) {
  let node = tree;
  const parts = rel.split('/').filter(Boolean), real = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
    const p = parts[i], low = p.toLowerCase();
    if (i < parts.length - 1) {
      const name = node.dirs?.[p] !== undefined ? p : Object.keys(node.dirs ?? {}).find((n) => n.toLowerCase() === low);
      if (name === undefined) return null;
      node = node.dirs[name]; real.push(name); continue;
    }
    const name = node.files?.[p] !== undefined ? p : Object.keys(node.files ?? {}).find((n) => n.toLowerCase() === low);
    if (name === undefined) return null;
    const f = node.files[name];
    return { path: [...real, name].join('/'), size: f.size, mtime: f.mtime ?? 0, ...(f.light ? { light: f.light } : {}), ...(f.owner ? { owner: f.owner } : {}) };
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * The version that owns the file `rel` of a tree when it is another version's (the server's `owner` mark: a file a
 * version takes from one it requires — its underlays, src/host/game-files.js listGameTree —, stored and fetched under
 * that version: docs/slow-network.md "Files of a required version"), else null. A light copy's (LIGHT_DIR/<path>): its
 * file's. `self`: the tree's own version (a mark of its own name is its own file).
 */
export function treeOwner(tree, rel, self = null) {
  const p = rel.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  const o = treeFile(tree, p.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/') ? p.slice(LIGHT_DIR.length + 1) : p)?.owner ?? null;
  return o && o !== self ? o : null;
}

/**
 * A version's tree split by owner (treeOwner): { own: the tree of its own files (the tree itself when no file is
 * another's), owners: Map(owner -> the tree of that version's files it takes, at the same paths) }.
 */
export function splitOwners(tree, self = null) {
  const owners = new Map();
  const marked = (node) => Object.values(node.files ?? {}).some((f) => f.owner && f.owner !== self) || Object.values(node.dirs ?? {}).some(marked);
  if (!marked(tree)) return { own: tree, owners };
  const split = (node, at) => {
    const own = { dirs: {}, files: {} };
    for (const [name, f] of Object.entries(node.files ?? {})) {
      if (!f.owner || f.owner === self) { own.files[name] = f; continue; }
      let o = owners.get(f.owner); if (!o) owners.set(f.owner, o = { dirs: {}, files: {} });
      for (const d of at) o = o.dirs[d] ??= { dirs: {}, files: {} };
      o.files[name] = f;
    }
    for (const [name, d] of Object.entries(node.dirs ?? {})) own.dirs[name] = split(d, [...at, name]);
    return own;
  };
  return { own: split(tree, []), owners };
}
```

`src/vfs/http-backend.js`:

```js
// Read-only VFS backend over HTTP range requests (synchronous XHR: the guest's ReadFile is
// synchronous and the emulator runs in a worker). The directory tree comes from the server's
// JSON listing so stat/readdir never hit the network; file data is fetched in blocks kept in a
// bounded LRU cache with read-ahead for sequential access.
import { acct, C as ACCT } from '../core/frame-acct.js';
import { NetLink, H1_CONNECTIONS, AHEAD_REQUESTS } from './net-link.js';
import { LIGHT_DIR, isVideoFile, isLightPicture } from './game-tree.js';
import { decodePcm, PCM_MAGIC } from './pcm-codec.js';

export const BLOCK = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB
/**
 * A random read that misses fetches only the 64 KiB pieces it covers (a round trip plus 64 KiB instead of a whole
 * block: ~10x less waiting over the Internet while the game waits); the whole block follows in the background.
 */
export const CHUNK = 1 << 16;
const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 << 20;
/** a read covering several whole blocks none of which is here fetches at most this many of them in one request */
const COALESCE_BLOCKS = 16;
/** sequential bytes after which a file is being read whole (whole blocks ahead) rather than streamed */
const STREAM_BYTES = 1 << 20;
/** sequential bytes and reads after which a file is a stream for the learned prefetch (see doneWith) */
const STREAM_SKIP = 256 << 10, STREAM_READS = 16;
/** at most this many bytes fetched ahead of a stream's read while the game waits (the rest comes in the background) */
const STREAM_WINDOW = 256 << 10; // pieces kept in memory (the blocks fetched behind them replace them)
/**
 * A file read whole (in sequence, past STREAM_BYTES): once fewer than READ_AHEAD_LOW bytes past its reader are here or on
 * their way, its next blocks are fetched asynchronously up to READ_AHEAD_HIGH bytes past it (see readAhead) — the reader
 * finds them here instead of waiting a round trip and a transfer every few blocks.
 */
const READ_AHEAD_LOW = 2 << 20, READ_AHEAD_HIGH = 4 << 20;
/** on a link that is not fast, a sequential reader gets this many seconds of the link ahead of it (see readAheadParts) */
const READ_AHEAD_SECONDS = 2;
/** a file read whole on a link that is not fast: this many whole blocks asked past its reader's (see readAheadParts) */
const WHOLE_AHEAD_BLOCKS = 2;
/** a run this long in sequence (from anywhere in the file) or STREAM_BYTES from the file's start: a file read whole (readAheadParts) */
const WHOLE_RUN = 4 << 20;
/**
 * A read that misses a block (needs pieces not here yet) also starts the download of the whole block, at most this many
 * such downloads in flight (else the block waits for the background fill, as before): see noteMiss.
 */
const MISSED_BLOCK_FLIGHTS = 2;
/**
 * The blocks this close to a missed one (before and after it) are wanted too, at the lowest priority: downloaded by the
 * background fill once the blocks the game touched are here and the network has been quiet for NEAR_QUIET_MS (the
 * game's next misses are often next to its last ones: the parts of an archive one scene needs). At most NEAR_MAX wanted.
 */
const NEAR_BLOCKS = 2, NEAR_QUIET_MS = 500, NEAR_MAX = 64;
/** The files whose latest wait laterNext remembers (the oldest forgotten), and the rank above any file wanted whole. */
const WAITED_FILES = 256, WAITED_RANK = 2 ** 40;
/**
 * Once the learned prefetch is over, a file in which the game keeps missing blocks — WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES distinct blocks
 * read at random, not as a stream — is an archive it reads here and there as it plays (a sound bank, models, textures
 * of what comes into view): the rest of it is wanted whole (wantWhole), last of the background downloads, on a fast link
 * with a block store. The learned order cannot hold those reads: they differ from one session to the next (BFME 1.08,
 * ten minutes of play: 42-47 reads on the network, 5 of them common to two sessions).
 */
const WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES = 3;
/**
 * the files whose light copy the game read (see upgrade): fetched once the game has read nothing for this long (ms) — the
 * player in an area loaded already, not between two reads of a load (an engine computes for seconds between them)
 */
const UPGRADE_QUIET_MS = 8000;
/**
 * …or this long for the files of an engine that loads them again in place (upgrade's `soon`: the player sees the file
 * replace its light copy at once, a benefit worth an earlier start)
 */
const UPGRADE_SOON_QUIET_MS = 1500;
const DEFAULT_CACHE_BLOCKS = 256; // 256 MiB
/**
 * learned pieces fetched ahead of the game (see pumpAhead): entries past its position, AHEAD_WINDOW at least and twice
 * the requests the link's budget allows (NetLink.aheadBudget)
 */
const AHEAD_WINDOW = 32;
/**
 * The game's position in the learned order is followed (L.tracked: what it reads next is what the order says — its
 * pieces ahead may go during a load, see pumpAhead) once TRACK_STEPS first touches of learned entries in a row went
 * forward by at most TRACK_WINDOW ranks each, and at least TRACK_SHARE of the last TRACK_SPAN blocks the game touched
 * first were in the order; a jump elsewhere, TRACK_MISSES blocks in a row touched outside the order (a place earlier
 * sessions did not load), or too few of them in it, and it is lost. A first touch at most TRACK_BACK ranks behind the
 * position (the engine's threads reading a few entries out of order) is neither a step nor a jump.
 */
const TRACK_STEPS = 2, TRACK_WINDOW = 64, TRACK_MISSES = 4, TRACK_SPAN = 8, TRACK_SHARE = 0.5, TRACK_BACK = 8;
/**
 * prefetch's list made again for the link's new class (see prefetch's relist) only once that class has held RELIST_HOLD_MS
 * (a rate near FAST_BPS goes back and forth), and RELISTS times at most
 */
const RELIST_HOLD_MS = 5000, RELISTS = 2;
/**
 * a media file streamed on a link that is not fast: its reader gets at most this many seconds of its own reading rate
 * ahead (MEDIA_AHEAD_MIN bytes at least), not READ_AHEAD_SECONDS of the link — a track of 20 KB/s took 4 MiB of the link
 * at once, a load's reads waiting behind it
 */
const MEDIA_AHEAD_SECONDS = 8, MEDIA_AHEAD_MIN = 256 << 10;
/** prefetch requests queued at once on a link that is not fast (see prefetch) */
const PREFETCH_PARTS = 6;
/**
 * prefetch requests in flight at once on a measured fast link while the game reads nothing from the network (one while it
 * does): one at a time left the link idle a round trip per request — BFME 1.08 through a 7 MB/s, 75 ms link (HTTP/2,
 * tools/net-proxy.mjs) carried 2.3-3 MB/s of learned blocks, and a game that read faster than that waited for them
 */
const FAST_PREFETCH_PARTS = 3;
/** a pause this long (ms) between two learned entries ends a step of the game (see stepEstimate) */
const STEP_GAP_MS = 5000;
/** the download of the whole game before playing, on a link that is not fast: a request carries about this much of the link (s) */
const ALONE_SECONDS = 8;
const RETRY_WAITS = [250, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000]; // ms before each new attempt of a failed range request
/** fetchBackground's answer for a download aborted because the game needed the network (fetched again later) */
const ABORTED = Symbol('aborted');
/** prefetchList's answer when the link's class changed from the one its list was made for (see prefetch's relist) */
const RELIST = Symbol('relist');
/**
 * Background download priorities on the shared link (NetLink.turn: lower first) and the quiet time (ms since the game's
 * last read) each waits for on a link that is not fast: the next blocks of a file read in sequence and the learned
 * pieces just ahead of the game first (its next reads), then the blocks the game touched, the learned order's launch set
 * (and a startup set), the place the page predicts the game loads next (wantList `prio: 'place'`), the rest of the
 * learned order (other places' reads), the blocks next to missed ones, the offline copy.
 */
const PRIO = { announced: [0, 0], readAhead: [1, 0], ahead: [2, 0], miss: [3, 100], fill: [4, 150], prefetch: [5, 300], place: [6, 300], learned: [7, 300], near: [8, 500], offline: [9, 500] };
/**
 * Announced reads (wantList: the ranges an engine says its next reads take, then waits for): unit requests in flight at
 * once at most — a load's few hundred small files fetched in parallel, not one round trip each (OpenMW, Ald'ruhn on a
 * 1.8 MB/s, 90 ms link: 340 serial reads, 37 s) —, fewer on a thin link (its bytes, not its round trips, are the wait).
 */
const WANT_REQUESTS = 32, WANT_REQUESTS_THIN = 8;
/**
 * The units of lists the engine waits for through its own reads (wantList `wait` false) in flight at once at most on an
 * HTTP/1.x origin (NetLink.h1): the browser's other connections left to the engine's reads and the learned read-ahead —
 * the window's units would hold all of them, and those reads wait behind them in the browser's queue (Half-Life's c1a0,
 * a taught map, at 8 MB/s, 85 ms: every request's first byte 400-690 ms instead of 90 during the announce, the load
 * 5.25 s instead of 4.05).
 */
const WANT_REQUESTS_H1_LOOSE = H1_CONNECTIONS - 2;
/**
 * A predicted place's set (wantList `prio: 'place'`: what a page expects the game to load next, fetched while the link
 * is idle — the OpenMW page asks it once its engine's boot is over, in the menu): its unit requests registered at once
 * at most — each still waits for its background turn (PRIO.place: NetLink's count and bytes rules bound them beside
 * the game's reads) —, and only while no announced unit waits for its request. (4 at once: Ald'ruhn's 8 MB took 13 s
 * at 1.8 MB/s, 90 ms — units of ~20 KB, the round trip their bound —; 8: NetLink.maxBackground on such a link.)
 */
const PLACE_REQUESTS = 8, PLACE_REQUESTS_THIN = 2;
/** an announced unit whose request failed on the network is asked again this many times (after retryWaits' pauses) */
const WANT_RETRIES = 2;
/** wire length of a response (its encoded body: what crossed the link), else the decoded length */
const wireOf = (len, header) => { const n = Number(header); return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : len; };

/**
 * Transport units (docs/slow-network.md "Precompressed units"): the server keeps some ranges of a file compressed ahead
 * at brotli's best (src/host/br-cache.js) — a whole block (the file's tail for its last one), or a single piece — and
 * answers a request of exactly that shape from them. unitOf: the unit [start, end) of a file of `size` bytes is (a
 * block first: a file or a tail of one piece is its block), or null.
 */
export function unitOf(start, end, size) {
  if (start % BLOCK === 0 && end === Math.min(size, start + BLOCK)) return { kind: 'b', index: start / BLOCK };
  if (start % CHUNK === 0 && end === Math.min(size, start + CHUNK)) return { kind: 'p', index: start / CHUNK };
  return null;
}
/**
 * On a link that is neither fast nor thin, a background run that is a whole block (every piece of it wanted, none here)
 * goes as the block — one request, one transport unit — when the link carries a block in this many seconds at most,
 * though that is more than backgroundBytes(): the server makes a block learned whole as a block unit (br-cache.js), and
 * the same bytes asked as pieces would miss it (measured, Morrowind at 1 MB/s: 82 % of the bytes the session asked were
 * of blocks the learned order makes as block units, asked as pieces). See wholeBlockFits.
 */
const WHOLE_BLOCK_SECONDS = 1.25;
/** a background request of more units than this goes as one (see rangeUnits) */
const MAX_UNIT_PARTS = 16;
/**
 * [start, end) of a file of `size` bytes cut at its units — whole blocks where they fit, else pieces —: [[a, b], ...],
 * or null when it is one unit, not aligned, or more than MAX_UNIT_PARTS of them (the last part may be no unit: a run
 * of pieces past `end`'s cut, as before).
 */
export function rangeUnits(start, end, size) {
  if (!(start < end) || end > size || start % CHUNK) return null;
  const out = [];
  for (let pos = start; pos < end;) {
    const e = pos % BLOCK === 0 && Math.min(size, pos + BLOCK) <= end ? Math.min(size, pos + BLOCK) : Math.min(end, pos + CHUNK);
    out.push([pos, e]); pos = e;
    if (out.length > MAX_UNIT_PARTS) return null;
  }
  return out.length > 1 ? out : null;
}
/**
 * Cutting a range at its units pays only when the server has them: a unit it lacks is compressed on the fly alone, and
 * independent 64 KiB pieces compress worse than the range whole (BFME2's archives, 384 KiB ranges: brotli-5 0.560 of
 * the raw bytes by pieces against 0.533 whole, zstd-3 0.586 against 0.557 — +5 %; a precompressed piece, brotli-11,
 * 0.519: -2.6 %), on as many more requests. So a backend cuts its background ranges while at least UNIT_HIT_MIN of the
 * parts it asked lately were answered from units (the server's X-Orthros-Unit; a moving share, UNIT_HIT_WEIGHT the
 * latest request's), and otherwise one request in UNIT_PROBE_EVERY only — a probe: the units it misses are made by the
 * server (br-cache.js `want`), the next probes find them.
 */
const UNIT_HIT_MIN = 0.66, UNIT_HIT_WEIGHT = 0.3, UNIT_PROBE_EVERY = 8;

/** Block the calling worker for `ms` (the reads are synchronous: nothing else can run meanwhile anyway). */
function pause(ms) {
  try { Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms); }
  catch { const t = performance.now() + ms; while (performance.now() < t) { /* no Atomics.wait here */ } }
}

export class HttpBackend {
  /**
   * @param {string} baseUrl e.g. "/game/bfme-vanilla/"
   * @param {{ dirs: Record<string, any>, files: Record<string, {size: number, mtime: number}> }} tree
   * @param {{ net?: NetLink, cacheBlocks?: number, store?: import('./opfs-store.js').OpfsBlockStore | null, onFetch?: (info: {url: string, start: number, end: number, ms: number}) => void, onRetry?: (info: {url: string, start: number, end: number, problem: string, attempt: number}) => void, retryWaits?: number[], encoded?: boolean, session?: string, link?: Set<HttpBackend> }} [opts]
   *   store: persistent block store (OPFS) consulted before the network and filled with every fetched block
   *   link: the backends sharing the player's connection (the game's folder and the games it requires, mounted beside
   *   it): the game's reads through any of them come first for the background downloads of all of them
   */
  constructor(baseUrl, tree, opts = {}) {
    this.base = baseUrl.endsWith('/') ? baseUrl : baseUrl + '/';
    this.tree = tree;
    this.link = opts.link ?? null; this.link?.add(this);
    /** the player's connection (shared by the backends of one link): bandwidth, demand first, background turns */
    this.net = opts.net ?? null;
    if (!this.net && this.link) for (const b of this.link) if (b !== this && b.net) { this.net = b.net; break; }
    this.net ??= new NetLink({ fixed: true }); // (no measure given: the local-network policies, as a test or a tool expects)
    this.cache = new Map(); // key "path#block" -> Uint8Array (insertion order = LRU)
    this.maxBlocks = opts.cacheBlocks ?? DEFAULT_CACHE_BLOCKS;
    this.onFetch = opts.onFetch ?? null;
    this.onRetry = opts.onRetry ?? null;
    this.retryWaits = opts.retryWaits ?? RETRY_WAITS;
    // the server's compressed ranges (/gamez/...?r=start-end: zstd/gzip Content-Encoding, decoded by the browser)
    this.encoded = !!opts.encoded;
    // (the audio units: a unit-shaped compressed range may come as a PCM transport container, decoded here before any
    // byte reaches the game — docs/slow-network.md "Audio units"; one that fails its check turns them off for this backend)
    this.pcm = this.encoded && opts.pcm !== false;
    // (a compressed background range cut at its transport units, see rangeUnits; false: one request as asked)
    this.unitRequests = opts.unitRequests ?? true;
    /** the share of the parts lately answered from the server's units (see UNIT_HIT_MIN), the cut requests since a probe */
    this.unitHitRate = 1; this.unitSkips = 0;
    /** session id sent with the compressed ranges (the server learns the order blocks are needed in, see prefetch) */
    this.session = opts.session ?? '';
    this.store = opts.store ?? null;
    this.stats = { requests: 0, bytes: 0, ms: 0 };
    /** the game's reads, whatever answered them (this browser's copy, memory, the network): bytes, those of movies */
    this.reads = { bytes: 0, videoBytes: 0 };
    /** each game read, as it happens: (path, start, end) — a page learning what its game read (worker.js, the mark) */
    this.onRead = opts.onRead ?? null;
    /** 64 KiB pieces of blocks not fetched whole yet: "path#chunk" -> bytes (insertion order = LRU) */
    this.chunks = new Map(); this.chunkBytes = 0;
    /** whole blocks wanted in the background (a random read touched them): "path#block" -> {path, size, mtime, index} */
    this.want = new Map(); this.filling = false;
    /** blocks next to missed ones, wanted at the lowest priority (see NEAR_BLOCKS): same entries as `want` */
    this.near = new Map();
    /** blocks of files the game wants whole (see wantWhole), after `want` and `near`: same entries (laterNext's order) */
    this.later = new Map();
    /** the files of `later` by rank (laterNext): path -> the turn of the latest wantWhole of it; path -> the turn of the
     * game's latest wait on it (a read it is blocked on that went to the network: fetchRange, HttpFile.prepare held, a page's
     * data worker's held ask — not a read the game went on past, a skipped sample: noteWait — at most WAITED_FILES) */
    this.wholeAt = new Map(); this.waitedAt = new Map(); this.fileTurn = 0;
    /** blocks of files whose light copy the game read (see upgrade), last of all: same entries, the latest last */
    this.upgrades = new Map();
    /** the latest upgrade was soon (an engine that reloads in place): the upgrades start after UPGRADE_SOON_QUIET_MS */
    this.upgradeSoon = false;
    /** the background downloads in flight (prefetch, block fill): their AbortControllers, aborted when the game
     * needs the network (see abortBackground) */
    this.bgAborts = new Set();
    /** the block fill's download in flight: { key, path, index, ctl, done, waiters } (waiters: parked reads waiting for it) */
    this.bgCur = null;
    /** asynchronous reads the game waits for, in flight (the background downloads wait for them to end) */
    this.fgPending = 0;
    /** learned pieces being fetched ahead of the game: "path#chunk" -> promise (see fetchPiecesAhead) */
    this.flights = new Map();
    /** whole blocks being fetched ahead of a sequential reader: "path#block" -> promise (see readAhead) */
    this.blockFlights = new Map(); this.readAheadPending = 0;
    /** the pieces a fetchAhead is fetching for a read (fetchForeground: `${path}#${piece}` → its job), joined by any other
     *  read of them meanwhile — a background ask and the forced read of the same bytes one wait limit later (data-worker
     *  bytesOf: both through fetchAhead), one request on the link instead of two */
    this.fgFlights = new Map();
    /** the latest read of any file (HttpFile.readNow): its path, end, and `runs` — counted up at each read that does not
     * continue the latest one (another file, or elsewhere in it); see readAheadParts */
    this.reader = { path: '', end: 0, runs: 0 };
    /** whole blocks downloading because a read missed them (see noteMiss) */
    this.missFlights = 0;
    /** the learned prefetch list and the game's position in it (see prefetch, noteBlock) */
    this.learned = null;
    /** open handles of the game per file: a file opened then closed again is done with for now (see doneWith) */
    this.opened = new Map();
    /** files the game reads as a stream (in sequence, past STREAM_SKIP bytes): fetched ahead of their reader only */
    this.streams = new Set();
    /** the learned prefetch pass is over (prefetch); then the blocks missed per file (path -> Set of blocks; true: wanted whole) */
    this.learnedDone = false; this.missedAfter = new Map();
    /** announced units waiting for a request (see wantList), in the order announced; the requests of them in flight */
    this.wantQ = []; this.wantInFlight = 0; this.wantLooseInFlight = 0;
    /** a predicted place's units waiting for a request (wantList `prio: 'place'`), in order; their requests in flight */
    this.placeQ = []; this.placeInFlight = 0;
    /** announced lists not all here yet (see wantList): meanwhile nothing is fetched ahead from the learned order (pumpAhead) */
```
