    this.wantLists = 0; this.wantHeld = 0;
    /** announced lists not all here yet that the engine waits for through its own reads (wantList `wait` false) */
    this.wantLoose = 0;
  }

  /**
   * Walk the tree case-insensitively; returns { node, dirNode, name, path } or null. A file's light copy (LIGHT_DIR/<path>,
   * src/host/light-copies.js) is a file of its own: its size the tree's `light`.
   */
  lookup(rel) {
    if (rel.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/')) {
      const r = this.lookup(rel.slice(LIGHT_DIR.length + 1));
      return r?.file?.light ? { file: { size: r.file.light, mtime: r.file.mtime ?? 0 }, name: r.name, path: `${LIGHT_DIR}/${r.path}` } : null;
    }
    const parts = rel.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean);
    let node = this.tree; const realParts = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
      const p = parts[i], last = i === parts.length - 1;
      const dirs = node.dirs ?? {}, files = node.files ?? {};
      let hit = dirs[p] !== undefined ? p : Object.keys(dirs).find((n) => n.toLowerCase() === p.toLowerCase());
      if (hit !== undefined) { node = dirs[hit]; realParts.push(hit); continue; }
      if (!last) return null;
      hit = files[p] !== undefined ? p : Object.keys(files).find((n) => n.toLowerCase() === p.toLowerCase());
      if (hit === undefined) return null;
      return { file: files[hit], name: hit, path: [...realParts, hit].join('/') };
    }
    return { dir: node, name: realParts[realParts.length - 1] ?? '', path: realParts.join('/') };
  }

  stat(rel) {
    const r = this.lookup(rel);
    if (!r) return null;
    return r.dir ? { size: 0, isDir: true, mtime: 0 } : { size: r.file.size, isDir: false, mtime: r.file.mtime ?? 0 };
  }
  readdir(rel) {
    const r = this.lookup(rel);
    if (!r || !r.dir) return null;
    const out = [];
    for (const n of Object.keys(r.dir.dirs ?? {})) out.push({ name: n, size: 0, isDir: true, mtime: 0 });
    for (const [n, f] of Object.entries(r.dir.files ?? {})) out.push({ name: n, size: f.size, isDir: false, mtime: f.mtime ?? 0 });
    return out;
  }
  open(rel, opts = {}) {
    const r = this.lookup(rel);
    if (!r || r.dir) return null;
    if (opts.write || opts.create || opts.truncate) return null; // read-only mount
    this.opened.set(r.path, (this.opened.get(r.path) ?? 0) + 1);
    const f = new HttpFile(this, r.path, r.file.size, r.file.mtime ?? 0);
    if (isVideoFile(r.path)) f.video = true;
    return f;
  }
  mkdir() { return false; }
  unlink() { return false; }
  rename() { return false; }

  /**
   * Fetch [start, end) of a file synchronously. A network error, an error status or a short answer (a connection
   * cut over the Internet) is retried after a pause, once per entry of retryWaits, before failing the read.
   */
  /** URL of [start, end) of a file: a compressed range, or the file itself (with a Range header) */
  rangeUrl(path, start, end, background = false, ahead = false, announced = false) {
    const rel = path.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');
    // (`ahead`: fetched ahead of the game but learned as its own read — the server counts it with the background;
    // `announced`: a background range the engine announced it reads next (wantList) — not learned either, queued by the
    // server between the game's reads and the background's)
    return this.encoded ? `${this.base.replace(/\/game\//, '/gamez/')}${rel}?r=${start}-${end}${background ? (announced ? '&w=1' : '&p=1') : this.session ? '&s=' + this.session : ''}${!background && ahead ? '&a=1' : ''}${this.pcm ? '&pc=1' : ''}` : this.base + rel;
  }
  /**
   * The bytes of an answer: `codec` its X-Orthros-Codec — pcm1: an audio unit, decoded (src/vfs/pcm-codec.js, its CRC
   * checked) —; null when it does not decode (the audio units off from then on: the request is made again without).
   * `want`: the range's length — an answer of another length that starts as a container is one whose header a proxy
   * dropped.
   */
  unitBody(data, codec, want) {
    if (codec !== 'pcm1' && !(this.pcm && data.length !== want && data.length >= 14 && (data[0] | (data[1] << 8) | (data[2] << 16) | (data[3] << 24)) === PCM_MAGIC)) return data;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    try { data = decodePcm(data); } catch { this.pcm = false; this.stats.pcmFailed = (this.stats.pcmFailed ?? 0) + 1; return null; }
    this.stats.pcmUnits = (this.stats.pcmUnits ?? 0) + 1; this.stats.pcmBytes = (this.stats.pcmBytes ?? 0) + data.length;
    this.stats.pcmMs = (this.stats.pcmMs ?? 0) + performance.now() - t0;
    return data;
  }

  /**
   * Background prefetch: download the listed blocks ([path, block index, pieces mask?], in the order earlier sessions
   * first needed them) that the store does not hold yet, one request at a time (two consecutive blocks at most),
   * yielding while the game reads from the network (its reads come first). The list is followed from the game's
   * position in it (see noteBlock): the blocks just past the last listed block the game touched first, then the rest
   * from the start — sessions of different speeds (and menu times) interleave phases in the learned order, so the head
   * of the list is often a phase this session has not reached, or has passed without needing it. Meanwhile the learned
   * pieces of the entries just past the game's position are fetched ahead (see pumpAhead). `progress` gets
   * { bytes, blocks, done, k }. `opts.learnedOnly`: the learned pieces only (not the rest of their blocks), on any link,
   * several requests at once, a block every piece of which is learned as one request (its transport unit) — what a page
   * waits for before the game starts, nothing of the game's own on the link. `opts.first`: the list's first entries are its launch
   * set (launch-set.js launchFirst): while one of them is missing, a position past them (a read the way to playable does
   * not need, e.g. a loading picture) does not send the pass on through the rest first.
   */
  async prefetch(list, progress, stop = () => false, opts = {}) {
    // (learnedOnly: its pieces kept in the store on a fast link too — that link otherwise keeps whole blocks only, and the
    // pass would fetch the pieces again and again, the memory's pieces trimmed)
    if (opts.learnedOnly) this.keepLearned = (this.keepLearned ?? 0) + 1;
    try {
      // (`opts.relist(fast)`: the list as a link of that class reads it — launch-set.js forLink: light copies or the files,
      // the media at the tail or not —, made again when the link's class changes from the one it was made for: a rate
      // kept from an earlier page said fast, the measure says otherwise)
      // (`carry`: the list it replaces — the game's position and the entries it touched kept, progress counted on)
      for (let relists = 0; ;) {
        if (await this.prefetchList(list, progress, stop, opts) !== RELIST) return;
        this.stats.relists = (this.stats.relists ?? 0) + 1;
        list = opts.relist(this.net.fast());
        opts = { ...opts, first: list.first ?? 0, carry: this.learned, relist: ++relists < RELISTS ? opts.relist : null };
      }
    } finally { if (opts.learnedOnly) this.keepLearned--; }
  }
  async prefetchList(list, progress, stop, opts) {
    const store = this.store; if (!store || typeof fetch !== 'function') return;
    if (!opts.carry) { progress.bytes = 0; progress.blocks = 0; }
    progress.done = false;
    /** @type {{path: string, size: number, mtime: number, index: number, mask: number, seen?: boolean, ahead?: boolean, skip?: boolean}[]} */
    const entries = [], rankOf = new Map();
    let first = 0; // (the launch set's entries kept: entries[0..first))
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      const [p, b, mask, t] = list[i];
      const r = this.lookup(p); if (!r || !r.file || !(b * BLOCK < r.file.size)) continue;
      const k = `${r.path}#${b}`; if (rankOf.has(k)) continue;
      rankOf.set(k, entries.length);
      if (i < (opts.first ?? 0)) first++;
      // (t: when the earliest session first needed it, ms from its start — absent from older servers)
      // (tail: a media file's entry on a link that is not fast — launch-set.js forLink put it after all the others, out of
      // the game's timeline: the game streaming it says nothing of where the game is — see noteBlock)
      entries.push({ path: r.path, size: r.file.size, mtime: r.file.mtime ?? 0, index: b, mask: typeof mask === 'number' ? mask & 0xffff : 0, t: Number.isFinite(t) ? t : null, tail: !!r.file.media && !this.net.fast() });
    }
    // (tracked, steps, misses: whether the game's position is followed — see noteBlock; fast: the link's class the list
    // was made for, see prefetch's relist)
    // (hist: the last TRACK_SPAN first touches, in the order or not; changed: since when the link's class differs from
    // fast, measured: the link's then)
    const L = this.learned = { entries, rankOf, first, pos: -1, inFlight: 0, inBytes: 0, stop, tracked: false, steps: 0, misses: 0, hist: [], fast: this.net.fast(), measured: this.net.measured, changed: null };
    // (a list made again for the link's new class: what the game did with the one it replaces)
    const C = opts.carry;
    if (C) {
      for (const e of C.entries) if (e.seen) { const r = rankOf.get(`${e.path}#${e.index}`); if (r !== undefined) entries[r].seen = true; }
      const p = C.entries[C.pos]; if (p) L.pos = rankOf.get(`${p.path}#${p.index}`) ?? -1;
      if (L.pos >= 0) Object.assign(L, { tracked: C.tracked, steps: C.steps, misses: C.misses, hist: C.hist });
      L.inFlight = C.inFlight; L.inBytes = C.inBytes; C.moved = L; // (its requests still on their way count in the new one's, see fetchPiecesAhead)
    }
    const skey = (e, i = e.index) => `${e.path}#${e.size}#${e.mtime}#${i}`;
    const stored = (e) => e.skip || store.map.has(skey(e)) || this.cache.has(`${e.path}#${e.index}`);
    // (the block the fill is downloading is left to it: it stores it too)
    // (nor one whose queued download the pieces ahead took (e.dropped, see pumpAhead) while those pieces are on their way)
    const flying = (e) => { for (let c = e.index * (BLOCK / CHUNK), z = c + BLOCK / CHUNK; c < z; c++) if (this.flights.has(`${e.path}#${c}`)) return true; return false; };
    const todo = (e) => !e.pending && !stored(e) && this.bgCur?.key !== `${e.path}#${e.index}` && !this.blockFlights.has(`${e.path}#${e.index}`) && !this.flights.has(`${e.path}#${e.index * (BLOCK / CHUNK)}`) && !(e.dropped && flying(e));
    // the entry to download next: the first one past the game's position not stored yet, else the first one — the
    // launch set's first when the position is past it (opts.first)
    const next = () => {
      if (L.pos >= L.first) for (let r = 0; r < L.first; r++) if (todo(entries[r])) return r;
      for (let r = L.pos + 1; r < entries.length; r++) if (todo(entries[r])) return r;
      for (let r = 0; r <= L.pos && r < entries.length; r++) if (todo(entries[r])) return r;
      return -1;
    };
    // a link that is not fast: the pieces the earlier sessions read first (the learned masks: what the game will read),
    // in the order they needed them from the game's position, then the rest of those blocks; in background requests
    // of the link's size (see NetLink), each piece kept as it comes
    const nextPart = () => {
      // (a thin link: the learned pieces only — whole blocks are for links that can afford them)
      for (const tier of this.net.thin() || opts.learnedOnly ? [1] : [1, 2]) {
        // (pass 0: the launch set while the position is past it — next's order)
        for (let pass = L.pos >= L.first ? 0 : 1; pass < 3; pass++) {
          const from = pass === 1 ? L.pos + 1 : 0, to = pass === 0 ? L.first : pass === 1 ? entries.length : Math.min(entries.length, L.pos + 1);
          for (let r = from; r < to; r++) {
            // (learnedOnly: an entry learned without its pieces — an older list — was read whole)
            const e = entries[r], mask = e.mask || (opts.learnedOnly ? 0xffff : 0);
            if (stored(e) || (tier === 1 && (!mask || e.maskDone)) || this.doneWith(e.path)) continue;
            // (learnedOnly — the game not started: nothing of its own on the link — a block whose learned pieces are all
            // of it goes whole on any link, the transport unit the server makes for it — br-cache.js: a block learned
            // whole is a block unit, its pieces are not —, as one request; a light copy's go by pieces, as made)
            const run = this.missingRun(e.path, e.size, e.mtime, e.index, tier === 1 ? mask : 0, !!opts.learnedOnly && !e.path.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/'));
            if (run) return { r, e, run, tier };
            if (tier === 1) { let fly = false; for (let c = e.index * 16; c < e.index * 16 + 16; c++) if (this.flights.has(`${e.path}#${c}`)) fly = true; if (!fly) { e.maskDone = true; progress.blocks++; } }
          }
        }
      }
      return null;
    };
    // (the launch set — and a startup set, learnedOnly — before a predicted place's set; the rest of the order, other
    // places' reads, after it: PRIO)
    const prioOf = (r) => (opts.learnedOnly || r < L.first ? PRIO.prefetch : PRIO.learned);
    const parts = new Set(); let failed = false, down = false;
    for (;;) {
      if (stop() || store.failed || down) return;
      if (opts.relist) {
        // (at once for a list made before the link was measured — a rate kept from another page —, else a class held
        // RELIST_HOLD_MS: not a rate near FAST_BPS going back and forth)
        if (this.net.fast() === L.fast) L.changed = null;
        else if (!L.measured || (L.changed ??= this.net.now()) <= this.net.now() - RELIST_HOLD_MS) return RELIST;
      }
      // (a measured fast link: requests side by side, the game's reads beside them — see FAST_PREFETCH_PARTS)
      const overlap = this.net.fast() && this.net.measured;
      // (the game's own reads first; the block fill, when it has blocks to fetch, runs beside this pass rather than
      // before it: a session whose game keeps touching new blocks keeps the fill busy for good, and waiting for it
      // starved this pass for whole sessions)
      if (!overlap) while (this.gameBusy(300)) { if (stop()) return; await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 100)); }
      // (learnedOnly on a fast link too: the learned pieces — the startup set a port's engine waits for, Prepare —, not
      // their whole blocks: Half-Life's startup set at 7 MB/s and 75 ms took 3.6 s, 61 serial requests for 5.9 MB where
      // its pieces are 2.7 MB; the rest of the blocks comes with the learned order later)
      if (!this.net.fast() || opts.learnedOnly) {
        // (up to PREFETCH_PARTS requests queued at once: each waits for its turn on the link, which lets several small
        // ones run together — a run of small files is latency-bound — within the link's background bytes)
        if (parts.size >= PREFETCH_PARTS) { await Promise.race(parts); continue; }
        const job = nextPart();
        if (!job) { if (parts.size || this.flights.size) { await (parts.size ? Promise.race(parts) : new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 200))); if (parts.size || next() >= 0 || nextPart()) continue; } break; }
        progress.k = job.r;
        // (learnedOnly: the set a page waits for before its game — what its first load needs —; else the learned order,
        // which waits for a load under way to end: the load's own next pieces go ahead of it, see pumpAhead)
        const pr = this.fetchPartBg(job.e.path, job.e.size, job.e.mtime, job.run[0], job.run[1], prioOf(job.r), stop, false, { reason: job.tier === 1 ? 'pf1' : 'pf2', forLoad: !!opts.learnedOnly }).then((r) => {
          if (r === null) failed = true;
          else if (r === undefined) job.e.skip = true;
          else if (r === true) {
            progress.bytes += Math.min(job.e.size, (job.run[1] + 1) * CHUNK) - job.run[0] * CHUNK;
            // (what came the store did not keep — full —: done with this entry, it would be asked again each time the
            // memory's copy is evicted)
            if (!this.keptInStore(job.e, job.run[0])) job.e.skip = true;
          }
        }).finally(() => parts.delete(pr));
        parts.add(pr);
        if (failed) { failed = false; if (stop()) return; await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 1000)); }
        continue;
      }
      if (overlap && parts.size >= (this.gameBusy(300) ? 1 : FAST_PREFETCH_PARTS)) { await Promise.race([...parts, new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 100))]); continue; }
      const k = next(); progress.k = k;
      if (k < 0) { if (parts.size) { await Promise.race(parts); continue; } break; }
      const e = entries[k], f = entries[k + 1];
      const n = f && f.path === e.path && f.index === e.index + 1 && todo(f) ? 2 : 1;
      const start = e.index * BLOCK, end = Math.min(e.size, (e.index + n) * BLOCK);
      e.pending = true; if (n === 2) f.pending = true;
      // (its blocks registered as on their way, as a sequential reader's read-ahead: a parked read or an announced list
      // joins the request and makes it go first rather than ask again (job.joined); the learned pieces ahead skip it once
      // it started, and take its blocks while it still waits for its turn — job.drop, see pumpAhead)
      const w = {}, keys = n === 2 ? [`${e.path}#${e.index}`, `${f.path}#${f.index}`] : [`${e.path}#${e.index}`];
      let dropped = false;
      const unregister = () => { for (const key of keys) if (this.blockFlights.get(key) === job) this.blockFlights.delete(key); };
      const job = this.fetchBackground(e.path, start, end, null, true, false, { prio: prioOf(k), stop: () => dropped || stop(), w, reason: 'pf' }).then((data) => {
        e.pending = false; if (n === 2) f.pending = false;
        unregister();
        if (data === ABORTED || dropped) return;
        if (data === null) { down = true; return; }
        if (!data) { e.skip = true; return; } // (an answer to skip: not asked again this session)
        // (a read joined it: the blocks in memory too — the store may drop them, full or failed, and the read would then
        // ask them again after waiting for this whole request)
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
          const b = data.subarray(i * BLOCK, Math.min(data.length, (i + 1) * BLOCK));
          if (job.joined && !this.cache.has(`${e.path}#${e.index + i}`)) this.installBlock(e.path, e.index + i, b, skey(e, e.index + i)); else store.put(skey(e, e.index + i), b);
        }
        if (job.joined) this.evict();
        // (done with, stored or not: a full store drops blocks silently, and the pass would fetch them again forever)
        e.skip = true; if (n === 2) f.skip = true;
        progress.bytes += data.length; progress.blocks += n;
      }, (err) => { unregister(); throw err; });
      job.w = w;
      // (still waiting for its turn: given up — its blocks to the pieces ahead —, true; else false)
      job.drop = () => {
        if (dropped || job.joined || !this.net.waiters.includes(w)) return false; // (a read waits for it: kept)
        dropped = true; unregister(); e.pending = false; e.dropped = true; if (n === 2) { f.pending = false; f.dropped = true; }
        this.net.kick(); // (out of the queue now: its stop holds)
        return true;
      };
      for (const key of keys) this.blockFlights.set(key, job);
      if (!overlap) { await job; continue; }
      parts.add(job); job.finally(() => parts.delete(job));
    }
    store.flush?.(true); // (a sync point: the prefetch is over)
    progress.done = true; this.learnedDone = true;
  }

  /**
   * The file bytes the game's current step still needs from the network, by the learned order: the entries past the
   * game's position up to the first pause of STEP_GAP_MS in the earliest sessions' timeline (a step: a run of reads —
   * a loading screen, a level — the pause: the game busy with something else), their learned pieces (the whole block
   * when not known) not here yet. Null without a learned list with times.
   */
  stepEstimate() {
    const L = this.learned; if (!L || !L.entries.length || L.entries[0].t === null) return null;
    let bytes = 0, prevT = L.pos >= 0 ? L.entries[L.pos].t : null;
    for (let r = L.pos + 1, n = 0; r < L.entries.length && n < 4096; r++, n++) {
      const e = L.entries[r];
      // (an earlier time: the order starts again — its launch set first, then the rest, launch-set.js launchFirst)
      if (e.t === null || (prevT !== null && (e.t - prevT > STEP_GAP_MS || e.t < prevT))) break;
      prevT = e.t;
      if (this.peekBlockHere(e.path, e.size, e.mtime, e.index)) continue;
      const P = BLOCK / CHUNK, c0 = e.index * P, pieces = Math.ceil((Math.min(e.size, (e.index + 1) * BLOCK) - e.index * BLOCK) / CHUNK);
      for (let i = 0; i < pieces; i++) if ((!e.mask || ((e.mask >>> i) & 1)) && !this.pieceHere(e.path, e.size, e.mtime, c0 + i)) bytes += Math.min(CHUNK, e.size - (c0 + i) * CHUNK);
    }
    return { bytes };
  }

  /**
   * The game touches block `index` of `path` (a read, from here or not): its first touch of a block of the learned
   * list moves the game's position in the list there, and the pieces learned for the next entries are fetched ahead.
   */
  noteBlock(path, index) {
    const L = this.learned; if (!L) return;
    const r = L.rankOf.get(`${path}#${index}`);
    const touch = (hit) => { L.hist.push(hit); if (L.hist.length > TRACK_SPAN) L.hist.shift(); };
    const share = () => L.hist.filter(Boolean).length >= TRACK_SHARE * L.hist.length;
    // (a block outside the order: a place earlier sessions did not load — after a few in a row, or too many among the
    // last ones, the position is lost)
    if (r === undefined) { touch(false); if (++L.misses >= TRACK_MISSES || !share()) { L.tracked = false; L.steps = 0; } return; }
    const e = L.entries[r]; if (e.seen) return;
    // (a media file's entry at the order's tail does not move the position: a menu's music, streamed while the player
    // waits, sent the background pass on through every movie and track of the tail before the rest of the way to playable)
    e.seen = true;
    if (!e.tail) {
      // (followed: first touches going forward within TRACK_WINDOW ranks, TRACK_STEPS of them in a row, most of the last
      // touches in the order; one a few ranks behind the position changes nothing)
      touch(true); L.misses = 0;
      const was = L.tracked;
      if (!(L.pos >= 0 && r < L.pos && L.pos - r <= TRACK_BACK)) {
        L.steps = L.pos >= 0 && r > L.pos && r - L.pos <= TRACK_WINDOW ? L.steps + 1 : 0;
        L.pos = r;
      }
      L.tracked = L.steps >= TRACK_STEPS && share();
      // (followed now: the ahead pieces queued before go during the load too — their forLoad is read at their turn)
      if (L.tracked && !was) this.net.kick();
    }
    this.pumpAhead();
  }

  /**
   * Fetch ahead the pieces earlier sessions read (the entry's mask of 64 KiB pieces) of the learned entries just past
   * the game's position (AHEAD_WINDOW entries, twice the budget's requests on a fast link), within the link's budget
   * (NetLink.aheadBudget: requests in flight, and their bytes on a fast HTTP/2 link — L.inBytes). While the game walks a run
   * of learned blocks reading a piece or two of each (a latency-bound chain of small reads, the link mostly idle
   * between them), its next reads are already here or on their way. While the game loads (NetLink.silenced) only when
   * its position is followed (L.tracked, see noteBlock): then they are the load's own next reads (forLoad). These requests are not aborted by the game's own
   * reads (they are predictions of those reads, and small); a parked read of a piece in flight waits for it
   * (fetchAhead). Entries whose mask is unknown (learned before masks) are left to the whole-block pass, as are the
   * blocks a download already started brings (blockFlights: their pieces were asked twice at once — Half Strike's first
   * map, 441 requests and 8.7 MB twice at 8 MB/s); one of that pass's still waiting for its turn is given up instead
   * (job.drop): queued behind the game's reads on a fast link, it would hold the load's next blocks back, a parked read
   * then waiting for its 1-2 MiB rather than a piece.
   */
  pumpAhead() {
    const L = this.learned; if (!L || L.stop() || this.store?.failed || typeof fetch !== 'function') return;
    // (a load at a place the order does not follow: nothing of it ahead — another place's next reads would take the
    // link from the load's own; the next touch of a learned entry pumps again)
    if (!L.tracked && this.net.silenced()) return;
    // (nor while the engine waits for what it announced (wantList): it said what its load reads — the learned order's
    // guesses would only take the link from it (measured: 0.8-1.1 MB of a 5 s announced wait); they go once it is here.
    // Not for a list announced with `wait` false: it holds files the load reads late too, and the order's next entries
    // — the reads it cannot predict — would each wait a round trip until its last unit came)
    if (this.wantLists > 0) return;
    const P = BLOCK / CHUNK, budget = this.net.aheadBudget();
    // (within the budget: its requests, and past AHEAD_REQUESTS of them its bytes — L.inBytes, see fetchPiecesAhead: whole
    // blocks stay at about main's three on a fast link, pieces go by the bandwidth-delay product)
    const room = () => L.inFlight < budget.requests && (L.inFlight < AHEAD_REQUESTS || (L.inBytes ?? 0) < budget.bytes);
    const span = Math.max(AHEAD_WINDOW, 2 * budget.requests);
    for (let r = L.pos + 1, lim = Math.min(L.entries.length, L.pos + 1 + span); r < lim && room(); r++) {
      const e = L.entries[r];
      // (nor a media file's entry at the order's tail: the game streams it, read ahead of its reader — readAhead)
      if (e.ahead || e.seen || !e.mask || e.tail || this.doneWith(e.path)) continue;
      // (nor a block a download started brings: a parked read joins that request — fetchAhead; the whole-block pass's
      // still queued is given up, its block's pieces go ahead — job.drop)
      const bf = this.blockFlights.get(`${e.path}#${e.index}`);
      if (bf && !(bf.w && this.net.waiters.includes(bf.w) && (!bf.drop || bf.drop()))) continue;
      if (e.pending && !bf) continue;
      e.ahead = true;
      if (this.cache.has(`${e.path}#${e.index}`) || this.store?.map.has(`${e.path}#${e.size}#${e.mtime}#${e.index}`)) continue;
      const c0 = e.index * P, pieces = Math.ceil((Math.min(e.size, (e.index + 1) * BLOCK) - e.index * BLOCK) / CHUNK);
      let all = true; for (let i = 0; i < pieces; i++) if (!((e.mask >>> i) & 1)) all = false;
      const want = (i) => ((e.mask >>> i) & 1) === 1 && !this.flights.has(`${e.path}#${c0 + i}`) && !this.hasPiece(e.path, e.size, e.mtime, c0 + i);
      // (every piece of the block learned: the block as one request when the link carries it soon enough — its unit, see
      // WHOLE_BLOCK_SECONDS)
      const most = all && this.wholeBlockFits() ? pieces : Math.max(1, this.net.requestBytes() / CHUNK);
      for (let i = 0; i < pieces; i++) {
        if (!want(i)) continue;
        let j = i; while (j + 1 < pieces && want(j + 1) && j + 1 - i < most) j++;
        // (every piece of the block wanted: the block itself, stored)
        this.fetchPiecesAhead(e, c0 + i, c0 + j, all && i === 0 && j === pieces - 1);
        i = j;
      }
    }
  }
  /** Pieces m0..m1 of a learned entry, fetched ahead (see pumpAhead); `whole`: they are the whole block. */
  fetchPiecesAhead(e, m0, m1, whole) {
    const L0 = this.learned, at = () => { let L = L0; while (L.moved) L = L.moved; return L; }; // (see prefetchList's carry)
    const start = m0 * CHUNK, stop = Math.min(e.size, (m1 + 1) * CHUNK);
    L0.inFlight++; L0.inBytes = (L0.inBytes ?? 0) + stop - start;
    this.stats.aheadRequests = (this.stats.aheadRequests ?? 0) + 1;
    // (the learned position followed (L.tracked): these are the load's next reads — they may go during it; read when the
    // turn is looked at, not when it was queued: tracking found or lost meanwhile)
    const w = { get forLoad() { return !e.tail && at().tracked; } };
    const done = this.fetchBackground(e.path, start, stop, null, false, false, { prio: PRIO.ahead, stop: L0.stop, w, reason: 'ahead' }).then((d) => {
      if (!(d instanceof Uint8Array) || this.cache.has(`${e.path}#${e.index}`)) return;
      this.stats.aheadBytes = (this.stats.aheadBytes ?? 0) + d.length;
      if (whole) { this.installBlock(e.path, e.index, d, `${e.path}#${e.size}#${e.mtime}#${e.index}`); this.evict(); } else this.addPieces(e.path, m0, m1, d, e);
    }).finally(() => {
      for (let c = m0; c <= m1; c++) if (this.flights.get(`${e.path}#${c}`) === done) this.flights.delete(`${e.path}#${c}`);
      const L = at(); L.inFlight--; L.inBytes = Math.max(0, (L.inBytes ?? 0) - (stop - start));
      this.pumpAhead();
    });
    done.w = w;
    for (let c = m0; c <= m1; c++) this.flights.set(`${e.path}#${c}`, done);
  }
  /**
   * Pieces c0..c1 of a file in one background request (after its turn on the link, priority `prio`), registered as on
   * their way (a parked read of one of them waits for it and makes it go first); they join the pieces here (a block
   * whose pieces are all here is installed whole). Resolves to true when they came, undefined for an answer to skip,
   * false when aborted (a synchronous read of the same bytes: try again later), null when the network failed or
   * `stop()` held. `tag`: { reason (NetLink.bgBy), forLoad (NetLink.mayStart) }.
   */
  fetchPartBg(path, size, mtime, c0, c1, prio, stop = () => false, learn = false, tag = {}) {
    const w = {};
    const done = this.fetchBackground(path, c0 * CHUNK, Math.min(size, (c1 + 1) * CHUNK), null, false, learn, { prio, stop, w, reason: tag.reason, forLoad: tag.forLoad }).then((d) => {
      if (d === ABORTED) return false;
      if (d === null) return null;
      if (!(d instanceof Uint8Array)) return undefined;
      this.stats.partBytes = (this.stats.partBytes ?? 0) + d.length;
      this.addPieces(path, c0, c1, d, { size, mtime });
      return true;
    }).finally(() => { for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (this.flights.get(`${path}#${c}`) === done) this.flights.delete(`${path}#${c}`); });
    done.w = w;
    for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) this.flights.set(`${path}#${c}`, done);
    return done;
  }
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- announced reads

  /**
   * Announced reads (docs/slow-network.md "Announced reads"): an engine says which ranges its next reads take, then
   * waits for them — a load's files fetched in parallel (WANT_REQUESTS unit requests in flight, in the list's order)
   * instead of one round trip each as the engine reads them. `list`: [[path, start, end]] (end exclusive, -1: the end of
   * the file — clamped to it). Each range's missing bytes go as transport units (unitOf: the whole block when the range
   * covers all of a block none of which is here, else its 64 KiB pieces), registered as on their way (a parked read of
   * them joins the request — and makes it go first — rather than ask again), kept like any background bytes (memory,
   * the store); what is here or on its way already (the learned pieces ahead, a block read ahead, the fill's block) is
   * not asked again. The requests are `forLoad` (they pass a load's silence, NetLink.mayStart) and urgent — the engine
   * waits for them next, as for a parked read: the window bounds them, not the background's count —; the server is told
   * they are announced (`w=1`: not learned as reads, queued between the game's reads and the background's). While any
   * of them is missing the game counts as waiting (NetLink.wait) and nothing is read ahead from the learned order
   * (pumpAhead); `opts.wait` false: neither — an engine that waits through its own reads, its list holding files read
   * late in the load too (GoldSrc's map loads): the learned order's next entries go meanwhile when it follows the load
   * (still a load under way, loadUnderWay). Returns one promise per entry: true once all its bytes are here, false when one of its units failed (the
   * engine's read then asks itself, and says what failed). `opts.label`: what the load is for (kept in stats.wantLabel).
   * `opts.prio` 'place': a list the page predicts (the place a saved game will load, fetched while the player sits in
   * the menu — docs/openmw.md "Anticipated places"), not one the engine waits for: the same units, deduplicated the same
   * way, but each a background turn of PRIO.place (after the game's reads, the load's, the launch set; never urgent nor
   * forLoad: a load's silence holds it), PLACE_REQUESTS at once and only while no announced unit waits for its
   * request, a flight on its way joined without promoting it, no wait of the link's, the learned read-ahead not paused,
   * asked as background (`p=1`: not learned); a parked read — or an announced list — of one of its units promotes it as
   * any. Counted as `place` (NetLink.bgBy, stats.place*).
   */
  wantList(list, opts = {}) {
    const place = opts.prio === 'place', loose = !place && opts.wait === false;
    if (opts.label) this.stats[place ? 'placeLabel' : 'wantLabel'] = String(opts.label).slice(0, 80);
    // (the queues pumped once the whole list is queued: a unit started as each is queued would empty the announced queue
    // between two — a predicted place's units then starting in its idle turn, the list's own among them)
    this.wantHeld = (this.wantHeld ?? 0) + 1;
    let ranges;
    try {
      ranges = list.map(([p, start, end]) => {
        const r = this.lookup(p);
        if (!r?.file) return false;
        const size = r.file.size, stop = end < 0 ? size : Math.min(size, end);
        this.stats[place ? 'placeEntries' : 'wantEntries'] = (this.stats[place ? 'placeEntries' : 'wantEntries'] ?? 0) + 1;
        return this.wantRange(r.path, size, r.file.mtime ?? 0, Math.max(0, start), stop, false, place, loose);
      });
    } finally { this.wantHeld--; }
    this.pumpWant();
    const missing = ranges.filter((x) => typeof x !== 'boolean');
    this.stats[place ? 'placeHere' : 'wantHere'] = (this.stats[place ? 'placeHere' : 'wantHere'] ?? 0) + ranges.length - missing.length;
    if (missing.length && !place) {
      // (one wait of the link's for the whole list, while any of it is missing: the rest of the background keeps quiet;
      // the learned pieces ahead too — pumpAhead —; neither for a list the engine waits for through its reads (wait false))
      const hold = opts.wait !== false, tok = hold ? this.net.wait() : null;
      if (hold) this.wantLists++; else this.wantLoose++;
      Promise.allSettled(missing).then(() => { if (tok !== null) this.net.waitEnd(tok); if (hold) this.wantLists--; else this.wantLoose--; this.pumpAhead(); });
    }
    return ranges.map((x) => (typeof x === 'boolean' ? Promise.resolve(x) : x));
  }
  /**
   * [start, end) of a file (`path` as listed) here: true when it is (no promise: nothing to wait for); else a promise of
   * true once its missing units came (false: one failed). A unit on its way already is joined, and goes first
   * (NetLink.promote, as for a parked read; `joined`: this range joined one already — its missing bytes are asked now,
   * not joined again; `place`: a predicted place's — see wantList —, a flight joined as it is, not promoted).
   */
  wantRange(path, size, mtime, start, end, joined, place = false, loose = false) {
    if (!(end > start)) return true;
    const waits = [], P = BLOCK / CHUNK;
    for (let bi = Math.floor(start / BLOCK); bi * BLOCK < end; bi++) {
      if (this.peekBlockHere(path, size, mtime, bi)) continue;
      const b0 = bi * BLOCK, b1 = Math.min(size, b0 + BLOCK), a = Math.max(start, b0), b = Math.min(end, b1);
      // (the whole block on its way: read ahead of a sequential reader, or the fill's)
      const bf = this.blockFlights.get(`${path}#${bi}`) ?? (this.bgCur?.key === `${path}#${bi}` ? this.bgCur.done : null);
      // (joined, and promoted as a parked read's (NetLink.promote): one still waiting for its turn would else stay queued
      // behind the very silence this list's wait makes — a background flight that is not forLoad — until the engine's
      // timeout)
      if (bf && !joined) { if (!place) this.net.promote(bf.w); bf.joined = true; waits.push(Promise.resolve(bf).then(() => this.wantRange(path, size, mtime, a, b, true, place, loose), () => this.wantRange(path, size, mtime, a, b, true, place, loose))); continue; }
      const c0 = Math.floor(a / CHUNK), c1 = Math.floor((b - 1) / CHUNK), first = bi * P, n = Math.ceil((b1 - b0) / CHUNK);
      const missing = [];
      for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) {
        if (this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c)) continue;
        const f = this.flights.get(`${path}#${c}`);
        // (a predicted place's unit still queued, now announced: an announced unit — moved to the announced queue in this
        // list's order, under its window (pumpWant) —, not promoted: promoted, every one of a place's queued units would
        // start at once past the window and the link's rules; only a parked read's goes past them)
        // (one started already, waiting for its turn on the link: a load's own from now — PLACE_REQUESTS of them at most)
        if (f && !joined && !place && f.job?.queued && f.job.place) this.adoptPlaceUnit(f.job);
        else if (f && !joined && !place && f.job?.place) this.net.forLoad(f.w, PRIO.announced);
        else if (f && !joined && !place) this.net.promote(f.w);
        if (f && !joined) { const again = () => this.wantRange(path, size, mtime, Math.max(a, c * CHUNK), Math.min(b, (c + 1) * CHUNK), true, place, loose); waits.push(f.then(again, again)); continue; }
        missing.push(c);
      }
      // (the range covers the whole block, none of it here nor on its way: the block, one unit)
      if (missing.length === n && n > 1) { waits.push(this.wantUnit(path, size, mtime, first, first + n - 1, true, place, loose)); continue; }
      for (const c of missing) waits.push(this.wantUnit(path, size, mtime, c, c, n === 1, place, loose));
    }
    if (!waits.length) return true;
    return Promise.all(waits).then((oks) => oks.every(Boolean));
  }
  /**
   * Pieces c0..c1 of a file (a unit: one piece, or `whole`, its whole block) queued for an announced request: registered
   * as on their way at once (flights: a parked read of them waits for it — and promotes it, NetLink.promote: it goes
   * before the queue); resolves to true once they are here, false when their request failed. `place`: a predicted
   * place's unit (wantList), queued apart (placeQ), not urgent nor forLoad until promoted.
   */
  wantUnit(path, size, mtime, c0, c1, whole, place = false, loose = false) {
    const self = this;
    // (the turn's mark: urgent once a parked read waits for it — the queue starts it first, past the window)
    const w = { forLoad: !place, u: false, get urgent() { return this.u; }, set urgent(v) { this.u = !!v; if (v && job.queued) self.pumpWant(); } };
    const job = { path, size, mtime, c0, c1, whole, w, place, loose, queued: true, resolve: null };
    const done = new Promise((res) => { job.resolve = res; });
    done.w = w; done.job = job;
    for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) this.flights.set(`${path}#${c}`, done);
    (place ? this.placeQ : this.wantQ).push(job);
    this.stats[place ? 'placeUnits' : 'wantUnits'] = (this.stats[place ? 'placeUnits' : 'wantUnits'] ?? 0) + 1;
    this.pumpWant();
    return done;
  }
  /**
   * A predicted place's unit still queued (placeQ) that an announced list names: an announced unit from now (forLoad,
   * PRIO.announced, the wantQ's window — WANT_REQUESTS, WANT_REQUESTS_THIN on a thin link —, after the list's units
   * queued before it), counted as announced.
   */
  adoptPlaceUnit(job) {
    const i = this.placeQ.indexOf(job);
    if (i < 0) return;
    this.placeQ.splice(i, 1);
    job.place = false; job.w.forLoad = true;
    this.wantQ.push(job);
    this.stats.placeAdopted = (this.stats.placeAdopted ?? 0) + 1;
    this.pumpWant();
  }
  /**
   * The announced units' requests started up to the window (WANT_REQUESTS), those a parked read waits for first and past
   * it; then a predicted place's, up to theirs (PLACE_REQUESTS), once no announced unit waits for its request.
   */
  pumpWant() {
    if (this.wantHeld) return; // (a list being queued: wantList pumps once it is)
    for (const q of [this.wantQ, this.placeQ]) for (let i = 0; i < q.length; i++) if (q[i].w.u) { const [job] = q.splice(i--, 1); this.runWant(job); }
    const max = this.net.thin() ? WANT_REQUESTS_THIN : WANT_REQUESTS, looseMax = this.net.h1() ? Math.min(max, WANT_REQUESTS_H1_LOOSE) : max;
    // (a unit of a list the engine waits for through its reads stays queued while its own window is full — the next
    // lists' units go past it)
    for (let i = 0; this.wantInFlight < max && i < this.wantQ.length; i++) {
      if (this.wantQ[i].loose && this.wantLooseInFlight >= looseMax) continue;
      const [job] = this.wantQ.splice(i--, 1); this.runWant(job);
    }
    if (this.wantQ.length) return;
    const pmax = this.net.thin() ? PLACE_REQUESTS_THIN : PLACE_REQUESTS;
    while (this.placeInFlight < pmax && this.placeQ.length) this.runWant(this.placeQ.shift());
  }
  /** An announced (or a predicted place's) unit's request (retried on a network failure): its pieces here, true; or false. */
  async runWant(job) {
    const { path, size, mtime, c0, c1, whole, w, place, loose } = job;
    job.queued = false;
    if (place) this.placeInFlight++; else this.wantInFlight++;
    if (loose) this.wantLooseInFlight++;
    if (!place) w.u = true; // (the engine waits for it next: urgent, as a parked read's turn)
    const P = BLOCK / CHUNK;
    const here = () => { for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (!this.peekBlockHere(path, size, mtime, Math.floor(c / P)) && !this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c)) return false; return true; };
    let ok = false;
    try {
      for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
        if (here()) { ok = true; break; }
        const d = typeof fetch === 'function' ? await this.fetchBackground(path, c0 * CHUNK, Math.min(size, (c1 + 1) * CHUNK), null, false, false, place ? { prio: PRIO.place, w, reason: 'place' } : { prio: PRIO.announced, w, reason: 'announced', forLoad: true }) : undefined;
        if (d instanceof Uint8Array) {
          const bi = Math.floor(c0 / P);
          if (whole && c0 % P === 0) { if (!this.cache.has(`${path}#${bi}`)) { this.installBlock(path, bi, d, `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${bi}`); this.evict(); } }
          else this.addPieces(path, c0, c1, d, { size, mtime });
          this.stats[place ? 'placeBytes' : 'wantBytes'] = (this.stats[place ? 'placeBytes' : 'wantBytes'] ?? 0) + d.length;
          ok = true; break;
        }
        // (aborted by a read of the same bytes: that read brought them; an answer refused, or the network still down: failed)
        if (here()) { ok = true; break; }
        if (d === undefined || attempt >= WANT_RETRIES) break;
        await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, this.retryWaits[attempt] ?? 1000));
      }
    } catch { ok = false; } finally {
      for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (this.flights.get(`${path}#${c}`)?.w === w) this.flights.delete(`${path}#${c}`);
      if (place) this.placeInFlight--; else this.wantInFlight--;
      if (loose) this.wantLooseInFlight--;
      if (!ok) this.stats[place ? 'placeFailed' : 'wantFailed'] = (this.stats[place ? 'placeFailed' : 'wantFailed'] ?? 0) + 1;
      job.resolve(ok);
      this.pumpWant();
    }
    return ok;
  }
  /**
   * The game opened `path` in this session and holds no handle on it now: what earlier sessions read further in it is
   * not fetched ahead (a movie skipped, a file parsed then closed) until the game opens it again. Nor, on a link that is
   * not fast, a file the game reads as a stream (a movie, music): its next bytes come ahead of its reader (readAhead),
   * and not at all once the game stops reading it — earlier sessions that played a movie through read all of it, this
   * one may skip it.
   */
  doneWith(path) { return this.opened.get(path) === 0 || (this.streams.has(path) && !this.net.fast()); }
  /** `path` is a media file (the tree's `media`, by format: src/vfs/game-tree.js isMediaFile — a movie, music). */
  isMedia(path) { return !!this.lookup(path)?.file?.media; }
  /**
   * Blocks of `path` may be fetched on a guess (the blocks near a missed one, the next ones of a read): not for a media
   * file the game is not streaming now — a movie skipped, a track probed — its bytes come when it is read (readAhead
   * while it is streamed), or with the offline copy, last.
   */
  speculate(path) { return this.streams.has(path) || !this.isMedia(path); }
  /** A handle of the game on `path` closed: when it was the last one, the background requests for the file go away. */
  noteClose(path) {
    const n = (this.opened.get(path) ?? 1) - 1;
    this.opened.set(path, Math.max(0, n));
    if (n <= 0 && !this.net.fast()) this.net.abortOverlap(this.base + path, 0, Infinity);
  }
  /** piece c is here or stored (not read back) */
  /** a learned entry's piece `c` (or its whole block) is in the persistent store */
  keptInStore(e, c) { return !!this.store && (this.store.map.has(`${e.path}#${e.size}#${e.mtime}#${e.index}`) || this.store.map.has(this.pieceKey(e.path, e.size, e.mtime, c))); }
  pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c) { return this.chunks.has(`${path}#${c}`) || !!this.store?.map.has(this.pieceKey(path, size, mtime, c)); }
  /**
   * The next run of pieces of block `index` to fetch in the background: missing, not on their way, among `mask` (bit i:
   * piece i of the block; 0: all), at most requestBytes() — [c0, c1], or null when none.
   */
  missingRun(path, size, mtime, index, mask = 0, whole = false) {
    const P = BLOCK / CHUNK, c0 = index * P, n = Math.ceil((Math.min(size, (index + 1) * BLOCK) - index * BLOCK) / CHUNK);
    const most = Math.max(1, this.net.requestBytes() / CHUNK);
    const need = (i) => (!mask || ((mask >>> i) & 1) === 1) && !this.flights.has(`${path}#${c0 + i}`) && !this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c0 + i);
    // (the whole block wanted, none of it here: the block itself, its unit, when the link carries it soon enough — or
    // `whole`: nothing of the game's own waits on the link, see prefetch's learnedOnly)
    if (n > most && (whole || this.wholeBlockFits())) { let all = true; for (let i = 0; i < n && all; i++) all = need(i); if (all) return [c0, c0 + n - 1]; }
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      if (!need(i)) continue;
      let j = i; while (j + 1 < n && need(j + 1) && j + 1 - i < most) j++;
      return [c0 + i, c0 + j];
    }
    return null;
  }
  /**
   * The game read from the network within the last `ms`, waits for an asynchronous read, or a sequential reader's next
   * blocks are on their way: background downloads wait.
   */
  gameBusy(ms) {
    if (!this.link) return this.ownBusy(ms);
    for (const b of this.link) if (b.ownBusy(ms)) return true;
    return false;
  }
  ownBusy(ms) { return this.fgPending > 0 || this.readAheadPending > 0 || performance.now() - (this.lastSyncFetchAt ?? -1e9) < ms; }
  /**
   * A load is under way, whatever the link: the game blocked on reads (NetLink.loading) or waiting for an announced list
   * (wantList) of this backend or one sharing its link — the upgrades of light copies wait for its end, on a fast link
   * too (a big load read light first, its files after it: GameData.bigBatch).
   */
  loadUnderWay() {
    if (this.net.loading()) return true;
    for (const b of this.link ?? [this]) if (b.wantLists > 0 || b.wantLoose > 0) return true;
    return false;
  }
  /** The game has read nothing for `ms` (from the network or not), through this backend nor those sharing its link. */
  gameQuiet(ms) {
    const now = performance.now();
    for (const b of this.link ?? [this]) if (b.fgPending > 0 || now - (b.lastReadAt ?? -1e9) < ms) return false;
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * A sequential reader of `path` (a file read whole) is at `end`: when fewer than READ_AHEAD_LOW bytes past it are here
   * (memory cache, store) or on their way, the next blocks up to READ_AHEAD_HIGH past it are fetched asynchronously
   * (consecutive missing blocks in one request). Not aborted by the game's other reads (they are its next reads); a
   * parked read of a block on its way waits for it (fetchAhead). A synchronous read of such a block fetches it again
   * (the worker cannot receive the asynchronous answer while it blocks): the bytes are the same either way.
   */
  // (`run`: the bytes its reader read in sequence so far, its first read included — `end` itself: from the file's start;
  // see readAheadParts)
  readAhead(path, size, mtime, end, rate = 0, reads = STREAM_READS, run = 0) {
    if (typeof fetch !== 'function' || end >= size) return;
    if (!this.net.fast()) { this.readAheadParts(path, size, mtime, end, rate, reads, run); return; }
    const have = (bi) => this.cache.has(`${path}#${bi}`) || this.blockFlights.has(`${path}#${bi}`) || !!this.store?.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${bi}`);
    let covered = end;
    while (covered < size && covered - end < READ_AHEAD_LOW && have(Math.floor(covered / BLOCK))) covered = (Math.floor(covered / BLOCK) + 1) * BLOCK;
    if (covered >= size || covered - end >= READ_AHEAD_LOW) return;
    const last = Math.min(Math.ceil(size / BLOCK), Math.ceil((end + READ_AHEAD_HIGH) / BLOCK)); // (exclusive)
    for (let b = Math.floor(covered / BLOCK); b < last; b++) {
      if (have(b)) continue;
      let e = b; while (e + 1 < last && !have(e + 1)) e++;
      this.fetchBlocksAhead(path, size, mtime, b, e);
      b = e;
    }
  }
  /**
   * readAhead on a link that is not fast: the pieces past the reader, up to what the link carries in READ_AHEAD_SECONDS
   * (at least 128 KiB, at most READ_AHEAD_HIGH), in background requests of the link's size at the read-ahead's priority
   * (the first of the background downloads: the reader comes for them next) — a stream (music, a movie) read while the
   * game plays finds its next bytes here instead of stopping the game a round trip and a transfer at a time. A file the
   * game loads goes on during a load (forLoad: its next reads); a media file gets MEDIA_AHEAD_SECONDS of its reader's
   * `rate` (bytes/s) only, and waits for a load to end. During a load, a reader of fewer than STREAM_READS reads in
   * sequence (`reads`: an archive's entry read in a few pieces, the bytes past it other entries the load may not read)
   * gets one request ahead of it, not two.
   *
   * A file read whole (not media, `reads` of STREAM_READS at least in sequence, its run past STREAM_BYTES from the file's
   * start or past WHOLE_RUN from anywhere: an engine reading its master file from start to end — a run of an archive's
   * adjacent entries rarely starts at offset 0 or lasts 4 MiB) takes whole blocks past its reader on any link — each
   * block one request, the server's block unit (precompressed at brotli 11 over 1 MiB: ~10 % fewer bytes than its
   * sixteen piece units, ~25 % fewer than pieces compressed on the fly). The blocks are counted from the first one past
   * the reader's (`end` on a block boundary: that block is the reader's own — the data worker's reads end where the
   * bytes here end): the reader's and WHOLE_AHEAD_BLOCKS more, one during a load. Only one of them waits for its turn at
   * a time (a 1 MiB request starts on a link that is not fast only when the link is free: NetLink.mayStart — a second
   * one queued would hold every later background request behind it, kick()'s strict priority), and a queued one is
   * dropped once its reader moved away (`reader`: a read elsewhere, in this file or another), so an archive's run that
   * ends leaves at most the block already on the link — kept (abortOverlap only): an abort throws its bytes away. The
   * rest of the block its reader is inside goes by pieces as before, and so does a block with a piece here or on its way
   * (its missing pieces); a block on its way whole (fetchBlocksAhead, the block fill) is counted, not asked again.
   * During a load this wins over requestBytes()'s two round trips: those keep a parked read of another file from waiting
   * behind a block it does not need, but this reader needs that block next, and the load's other reads queue behind
   * one block at most. Residual cost: the server learns these blocks as the game's reads (`a=1`) — the unread rest of a
   * block whose reader stopped inside it is learned too.
   */
  readAheadParts(path, size, mtime, end, rate = 0, reads = STREAM_READS, run = 0) {
    let want = Math.min(READ_AHEAD_HIGH, Math.max(128 << 10, Math.floor(this.net.secondsFor(1) > 0 ? READ_AHEAD_SECONDS / this.net.secondsFor(1) : READ_AHEAD_HIGH)));
    // (a media file: what its reader consumes in MEDIA_AHEAD_SECONDS — and not as part of a load: forLoad below)
    const media = this.isMedia(path), P = BLOCK / CHUNK;
    if (media) want = Math.min(want, Math.max(MEDIA_AHEAD_MIN, Math.floor(rate * MEDIA_AHEAD_SECONDS)));
    const whole = !media && reads >= STREAM_READS && (run >= STREAM_BYTES && run >= end || run >= WHOLE_RUN);
    const blocks = this.net.silenced() ? 1 : WHOLE_AHEAD_BLOCKS;
    let stop = Math.min(size, end + want);
    if (whole) stop = Math.min(size, Math.max(stop, (Math.floor(end / BLOCK) + 1 + blocks) * BLOCK));
    const last = Math.floor((stop - 1) / CHUNK), most = Math.max(1, this.net.requestBytes() / CHUNK);
    let inFlight = 0, queued = false;
    // (a file read whole: its requests counted once each — a block on its way is one request, not sixteen —, the
    // reader's block and the blocks past it)
    const ahead = whole ? 1 + blocks : !media && reads < STREAM_READS && this.net.silenced() ? 1 : 2, seen = new Set();
    /** block `bi` on its way whole outside the piece flights: the read-ahead's or a missed block's, the block fill's */
    const blockOnWay = (bi) => this.blockFlights.get(`${path}#${bi}`) ?? (this.bgCur?.key === `${path}#${bi}` ? this.bgCur.done ?? this.bgCur : null);
    /** every piece of block `bi` missing: none here, none on its way */
    const none = (bi) => { for (let k = bi * P, e = Math.min(Math.ceil(size / CHUNK), (bi + 1) * P); k < e; k++) if (this.flights.has(`${path}#${k}`) || this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, k)) return false; return true; };
    for (let c = Math.floor(end / CHUNK); c <= last; c++) {
      const bi = Math.floor(c * CHUNK / BLOCK), piece = this.flights.get(`${path}#${c}`), f = piece ?? blockOnWay(bi);
      if (f) {
        // (a whole block — this read-ahead's, or on its way outside the piece flights — still waiting for its turn)
        if (!whole || !seen.has(f)) { inFlight++; seen.add(f); if ((f.whole || !piece) && f.w && this.net.waiters.includes(f.w)) queued = true; }
        if (!piece) c = (bi + 1) * P - 1; // (a block on its way whole: none of its pieces asked)
        continue;
      }
      if (this.peekBlockHere(path, size, mtime, bi) || this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c)) continue;
      if (inFlight >= ahead) return; // (two requests on their way past the reader at most, one during a load: the link stays the game's)
      // (from a block's start, the whole block in one request — its unit — when the link carries it soon enough, or for a
      // file read whole a block starting at its reader or past it, nothing of that block here or on its way)
      const big = c % P === 0 && !this.wholeBlockFits() && whole && c * CHUNK >= end && none(bi);
      if (big && queued) return; // (one whole block waiting for its turn at a time: see above)
      const n = c % P === 0 && (this.wholeBlockFits() || big) ? P : most;
      let j = c; while (j + 1 <= last && j + 1 - c < n && Math.floor((j + 1) * CHUNK / BLOCK) === bi && !this.flights.has(`${path}#${j + 1}`) && !this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, j + 1)) j++;
      this.stats.readAheads = (this.stats.readAheads ?? 0) + 1;
      // (a whole block of a file read whole: dropped while it waits for its turn once its reader moved away — a read
      // elsewhere, or past this block — see `reader`; any other read-ahead but a media stream's too, once its reader
      // moved away, unless a read waits for it — a read-ahead queued behind a thin link's other requests went out long
      // after its reader left: a boot's, behind the boot's own reads, took the link 18 s in the middle of the next load
      // at 85 KB/s, its announced wait timing out — OpenMW, 2026-10-30, docs/openmw.md; nor a stream's read from inside
      // an archive, `streams` while it lasts — a read elsewhere in the file ends it —: two streams read in turn, music
      // and ambience from two archives, would else drop each other's on every read and play from synchronous reads)
      let halt = () => false, prw = null;
      const r = this.reader, runs = r.runs;
      if (big) {
        this.stats.wholeAheads = (this.stats.wholeAheads ?? 0) + 1;
        halt = () => r.path !== path || r.runs !== runs || r.end >= (bi + 1) * BLOCK;
      } else if (!media) {
        let dropped = false; // (counted once, however often the link asks)
        halt = () => {
          if (dropped) return true;
          if (prw?.urgent || this.streams.has(path) || (r.path === path && r.runs === runs)) return false;
          this.stats.aheadsDropped = (this.stats.aheadsDropped ?? 0) + 1;
          return (dropped = true);
        };
      }
      const pr = this.fetchPartBg(path, size, mtime, c, j, PRIO.readAhead, halt, true, { reason: media ? 'mediaAhead' : 'readAhead', forLoad: !media });
      prw = pr.w;
      // (a measuring harness's trace: the request, its reader — where it stood, how far it read in sequence —, whether whole)
      this.traceAhead?.({ k: 'ahead', f: path, off: c * CHUNK, len: (j + 1 - c) * CHUNK, end, run, reads, whole: big ? 1 : 0 });
      if (big) { pr.whole = true; if (pr.w && this.net.waiters.includes(pr.w)) queued = true; }
      inFlight++; c = j;
    }
  }
  /**
   * A whole block may go as one background request though it is more than backgroundBytes() (see WHOLE_BLOCK_SECONDS):
   * a measured link, not thin, that carries it in WHOLE_BLOCK_SECONDS at most, the game not loading.
   */
  // (not during a load — NetLink.silenced —: a parked read would wait for the whole block on its way)
  wholeBlockFits() { return this.net.bw > 0 && !this.net.thin() && !this.net.silenced() && this.net.secondsFor(BLOCK) <= WHOLE_BLOCK_SECONDS; }
  /**
   * How many blocks from `index` on lie whole within [index * BLOCK, end) and have nothing here (no block, no piece in
   * memory or stored, none on its way), up to COALESCE_BLOCKS: a read of them fetches them in one request (see readNow).
   */
  missingBlocks(path, size, mtime, index, end) {
    const P = BLOCK / CHUNK;
    let n = 0;
    for (let b = index; n < COALESCE_BLOCKS && b * BLOCK < size && Math.min(size, (b + 1) * BLOCK) <= end; b++, n++) {
      if (this.peekBlockHere(path, size, mtime, b) || this.blockFlights.has(`${path}#${b}`) || this.bgCur?.key === `${path}#${b}`) break;
      let any = false;
      for (let c = b * P; c < (b + 1) * P && c * CHUNK < size && !any; c++) any = this.pieceHere(path, size, mtime, c) || this.flights.has(`${path}#${c}`);
      if (any) break;
    }
    return n;
  }
  /** block `index` is in memory or stored (no read) */
  peekBlockHere(path, size, mtime, index) { return this.cache.has(`${path}#${index}`) || !!this.store?.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${index}`); }

  /**
   * A read of block `index` needs pieces from the network: the read fetches its pieces (the quickest answer), and the
   * whole block is downloaded beside them at once. Games read a block a little here and there (entries of an archive
   * one after the other, a file parsed piece by piece): measured over a 150 ms link, more than half the blocks missed
   * were missed again, up to 16 times, each miss a round trip the game waited for. The background block fill would
   * fetch the block too, but it waits while the game reads and gives way to each of its reads — the block came only
   * once the game had stopped reading it. The reads that follow wait for this download (fetchAhead) rather than each
   * for its own pieces. The bytes are the ones the fill would download anyway; only their priority changes.
   */
  noteMiss(path, size, mtime, index) {
    if (typeof fetch !== 'function' || this.net.thin()) return;
    const k = `${path}#${index}`, guess = this.speculate(path);
    for (let j = Math.max(0, index - NEAR_BLOCKS); guess && j <= index + NEAR_BLOCKS && j * BLOCK < size; j++) {
      const nk = `${path}#${j}`;
      if (j === index || this.near.has(nk) || this.cache.has(nk) || this.store?.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${j}`)) continue;
      this.near.set(nk, { path, size, mtime, index: j });
      if (this.near.size > NEAR_MAX) this.near.delete(this.near.keys().next().value); // (the oldest go)
    }
    // (on a link that is not fast the block waits for the background fill: it would hold the game's next reads up)
    if (!this.net.fast()) return;
    if (this.learnedDone && this.store && !this.isMedia(path) && !this.streams.has(path) && globalThis.ORTHROS_WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES === 1) this.noteMissAfter(path, index); // (off by default — measured: ~400 MB more per session for 0.6 → 0.3 frames over 100 ms a minute; ?dbg=ORTHROS_WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES=1: on)
    if (this.missFlights >= MISSED_BLOCK_FLIGHTS || this.blockFlights.has(k) || this.cache.has(k) || this.bgCur?.key === k || this.store?.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${index}`)) return;
    this.missFlights++;
    this.stats.missBlocks = (this.stats.missBlocks ?? 0) + 1;
    // (not learned as the game's own read: its pieces are, with the mask of what it read)
    this.fetchBlocksAhead(path, size, mtime, index, index, false).finally(() => { this.missFlights--; });
  }
  /** a block of `path` missed after the learned prefetch: the file wanted whole at its WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES-th distinct block */
  noteMissAfter(path, index) {
    let m = this.missedAfter.get(path);
    if (m === true) return;
    if (m === undefined) this.missedAfter.set(path, m = new Set());
    m.add(index);
    if (m.size < WHOLE_AFTER_MISSES) return;
    this.missedAfter.set(path, true);
    this.stats.wholeAfterMisses = (this.stats.wholeAfterMisses ?? 0) + 1;
    this.wantWhole(path);
  }
  /**
   * Blocks b0..b1 of a file fetched ahead of its sequential reader (see readAhead), resolved when done. `learn`: asked as
   * the game's own read (the server learns it for later sessions' prefetch).
   */
  fetchBlocksAhead(path, size, mtime, b0, b1, learn = true) {
    const start = b0 * BLOCK, end = Math.min(size, (b1 + 1) * BLOCK);
    this.readAheadPending++;
    this.stats.readAheads = (this.stats.readAheads ?? 0) + 1;
    // (a sequential reader's next blocks are asked as its own reads: the server learns them for later sessions' prefetch)
    const w = {};
    const done = this.fetchBackground(path, start, end, null, false, learn, { prio: learn ? PRIO.readAhead : PRIO.miss, w, reason: learn ? 'readAhead' : 'miss', forLoad: learn && !this.isMedia(path) }).then((d) => {
      if (!(d instanceof Uint8Array)) return;
      this.stats.readAheadBytes = (this.stats.readAheadBytes ?? 0) + d.length;
      for (let i = b0; i <= b1; i++) if (!this.cache.has(`${path}#${i}`)) this.installBlock(path, i, d.subarray((i - b0) * BLOCK, Math.min(d.length, (i - b0 + 1) * BLOCK)), `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`);
      this.evict();
    }).finally(() => {
      this.readAheadPending--;
      for (let i = b0; i <= b1; i++) if (this.blockFlights.get(`${path}#${i}`) === done) this.blockFlights.delete(`${path}#${i}`);
    });
    done.w = w;
    for (let i = b0; i <= b1; i++) this.blockFlights.set(`${path}#${i}`, done);
    return done;
  }
  /**
   * The game needs the network: every background download in flight goes away (fetched again later), except the
   * block fill's when a parked read waits for it (`spareWaited`) — on a link not measured (the local policies). On a
   * measured link only those whose rest would hold the game's read up long (NetLink.abortLong): on a fast one with a
   * real round trip an abort threw away bytes mostly arrived, to fetch them again a round trip later, for a read that
   * shares the link with them for a few milliseconds (7 MB/s: a 2 MiB block, ~1 MB on the wire, in ~150 ms).
   */
  abortBackground(spareWaited = false) {
    if (!this.net.fast() || this.net.measured) { this.net.abortLong(); return; }
    if (this.link) { for (const b of this.link) b.abortOwn(spareWaited); } else this.abortOwn(spareWaited);
  }
  abortOwn(spareWaited) {
    for (const ctl of this.bgAborts) {
      if (spareWaited && this.bgCur?.ctl === ctl && this.bgCur.waiters > 0) continue;
      this.bgAborts.delete(ctl); ctl.abort();
    }
  }
  /**
   * [start, end) with fetch(), for the background downloads: the bytes, undefined for an answer to skip, ABORTED when
   * the game needed the network (try again later), null when the network failed. `onStart` gets the AbortController.
   */
  fetchBackground(path, start, end, onStart, abortable = true, learn = false, turn = null, reason = turn?.reason ?? 'other') {
    // (its turn on the shared link first: the game's reads come first, see NetLink; `turn`: { prio: [order, quiet ms],
    // stop, w, reason, forLoad } — w.urgent set meanwhile by a parked read waiting for this download lets it go at once;
    // forLoad: what a load under way needs, it may go during the load (NetLink.mayStart); a turn free now starts the
    // request now)
    // (the bytes a read's foreground fetch is bringing already — fgFlights —: that request joined, before any turn on the
    // link; the link asked only when it did not bring them all)
    if (turn && this.fgFlights.size) {
      const joined = this.joinForeground(path, start, end);
      if (joined) return joined.then((d) => d ?? this.fetchBackground(path, start, end, onStart, abortable, learn, turn, reason));
    }
    if (turn) {
      const quiet = this.net.fast() ? 0 : turn.prio[1], w = turn.w ?? {};
      if (turn.forLoad) w.forLoad = true;
      if (!this.net.tryTurn(quiet, w, end - start)) return this.net.turn(turn.prio[0], quiet, turn.stop, w, end - start).then((go) => (go ? this.fetchBackgroundNow(path, start, end, onStart, abortable, learn, reason) : null));
    }
    return this.fetchBackgroundNow(path, start, end, onStart, abortable, learn, reason);
  }
  async fetchBackgroundNow(path, start, end, onStart, abortable, learn, reason = 'other') {
    // (the converse of fetchAhead's join: a background ask — an announced read, a preload's, the learned order — of bytes
    // a read's fetchAhead is fetching waits for that request instead of asking them again on the link; validation3's
    // glide at 85 KB/s, 2026-10-31: the demand read's 1 MiB blocks first, the preload's announced ask of the same
    // blocks 6-8 s later, both on the link at once)
    const joined = this.joinForeground(path, start, end);
    if (joined) { const d = await joined; if (d) return d; }
    const ctl = typeof AbortController === 'function' ? new AbortController() : null;
    if (ctl && abortable) this.bgAborts.add(ctl);
    onStart?.(ctl);
    // (any background request may be aborted by a synchronous read of the same bytes, see NetLink.abortOverlap; only the
    // abortable ones by a demand read elsewhere)
    const tok = this.net.begin('bg', end - start, ctl ? () => ctl.abort() : null, { key: this.base + path, start, end }, reason);
    if (!abortable) tok.keep = true;
    const announced = reason === 'announced'; // (wantList's: the server's `w=1`)
    let wire = 0, ok = false;
    try {
      // (compressed ranges: one request per transport unit the range covers, in parallel — each answered from the
      // server's precompressed units when it has them, see rangeUnits; the parts all here or the download fails)
      // — while the server has them: see UNIT_HIT_MIN)
      let parts = this.encoded && this.unitRequests ? rangeUnits(start, end, this.lookup(path)?.file?.size ?? 0) : null;
      if (parts && this.unitHitRate < UNIT_HIT_MIN) { if (++this.unitSkips < UNIT_PROBE_EVERY) parts = null; else this.unitSkips = 0; }
      if (parts) {
        let first = true;
        const ress = await Promise.all(parts.map(([a, b]) => fetch(this.rangeUrl(path, a, b, !learn, learn, announced), { signal: ctl?.signal }).then((r) => { if (first) { first = false; this.net.firstByte(tok); } return r; })));
        if (ress.some((r) => r.status !== 206 && r.status !== 200)) return undefined;
        const bodies = await Promise.all(ress.map((r) => r.arrayBuffer()));
        const data = new Uint8Array(end - start);
        for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
          let d = new Uint8Array(bodies[i]);
          wire += wireOf(d.length, ress[i].headers?.get?.('content-length'));
          d = this.unitBody(d, ress[i].headers?.get?.('x-orthros-codec'), parts[i][1] - parts[i][0]);
          if (!d || d.length !== parts[i][1] - parts[i][0]) return undefined;
          data.set(d, parts[i][0] - start);
        }
        const hits = ress.filter((r) => ['hit', 'raw'].includes(r.headers?.get?.('x-orthros-unit'))).length;
        this.unitHitRate += UNIT_HIT_WEIGHT * (hits / parts.length - this.unitHitRate);
        ok = true;
        return data;
      }
      const res = await fetch(this.rangeUrl(path, start, end, !learn, learn, announced), { ...(this.encoded ? {} : { headers: { Range: `bytes=${start}-${end - 1}` } }), signal: ctl?.signal });
      this.net.firstByte(tok);
      if (res.status !== 206 && res.status !== 200) return undefined;
      let data = new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer());
      wire = wireOf(data.length, res.headers?.get?.('content-length'));
      data = this.unitBody(data, res.headers?.get?.('x-orthros-codec'), end - start);
      if (!data) return undefined;
      if (res.status === 200 && !this.encoded) data = data.subarray(start, end);
      ok = data.length === end - start;
      return ok ? data : undefined;
    } catch { return ctl?.signal.aborted ? ABORTED : null; } finally {
      // (a failed path — a part refused, one fetch failed, a body short — cancels the requests still running: their
      // bodies would hold the link while it counts as free)
      if (ctl) { if (!ok) ctl.abort(); this.bgAborts.delete(ctl); }
      this.net.end(tok, wire, end - start, ok);
    }
  }

  fetchRange(path, start, end) {
    this.noteWait(path);
    const ap = acct.enter(ACCT.net); // (frame accounting: the game thread waits for the network)
    try { return this.fetchRangeNow(path, start, end); } finally { acct.leave(ap); }
  }
  fetchRangeNow(path, start, end) {
    // (a background download shares the connection: it goes away while the game waits, and is fetched again later — on
    // a fast link; on a slower one only those that would hold the game up long, see NetLink.abortLong)
    this.abortBackground();
    // (the game is blocked on this read: a wait, see NetLink.loading — not a media stream's, see HttpFile.prepare)
    const waitTok = this.isMedia(path) ? null : this.net.wait();
    try { return this.fetchRangeTry(path, start, end); } finally { this.net.waitEnd(waitTok); }
  }
  fetchRangeTry(path, start, end) {
    for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
      // (made at each attempt: an audio unit that failed to decode turned the codec off — asked again without it)
      const url = this.rangeUrl(path, start, end);
      const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
      xhr.open('GET', url, false);
      xhr.responseType = 'arraybuffer';
      if (!this.encoded) xhr.setRequestHeader('Range', `bytes=${start}-${end - 1}`);
      const t0 = performance.now();
      this.net.abortOverlap(this.base + path, start, end);
      const tok = this.net.begin('demand', end - start);
      let problem = null;
      try { xhr.send(); } catch (e) { problem = e.message; }
      const ms = performance.now() - t0;
      this.lastSyncFetchAt = performance.now(); // (a background download yields to the game's own reads)
      let data = null;
      if (!problem && xhr.status !== 206 && xhr.status !== 200) problem = `status ${xhr.status}`;
      if (!problem) {
        data = this.unitBody(new Uint8Array(xhr.response), xhr.getResponseHeader?.('X-Orthros-Codec'), end - start);
        if (!data) problem = 'audio unit not decoded';
        else if (xhr.status === 200 && !this.encoded) data = data.subarray(start, end);
        if (data && data.length !== end - start) problem = `${data.length} bytes of ${end - start}`;
      }
      this.net.end(tok, problem ? 0 : wireOf(xhr.response?.byteLength ?? 0, xhr.getResponseHeader?.('Content-Length')), end - start, !problem);
      if (!problem) {
        this.stats.requests++; this.stats.bytes += data.length; this.stats.ms += ms;
        this.onFetch?.({ url, path, start, end, ms });
        return data;
      }
      this.stats.retries = (this.stats.retries ?? 0) + 1;
      this.onRetry?.({ url, start, end, problem, attempt });
      if (attempt >= this.retryWaits.length) throw new Error(`range request failed (${problem}) ${url} ${start}-${end}`);
      pause(this.retryWaits[attempt]);
    }
  }

  /** Block `index` from the memory cache or the persistent store, or null (no network). */
  peekBlock(path, size, index, mtime = 0) {
    const key = `${path}#${index}`;
    let b = this.cache.get(key);
    if (b) { this.cache.delete(key); this.cache.set(key, b); return b; }
    // persistent store (the key names the file version: size and mtime of the listing)
    const skey = `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${index}`;
    b = this.store?.get(skey);
    // (a stored block must have the block's length: the whole block, or the file's tail for the last one)
    if (b && b.length === Math.min(BLOCK, size - index * BLOCK)) { this.cache.set(key, b); this.evict(); return b; }
    if (b) this.store.drop?.(skey);
    return null;
  }

  block(path, size, index, readAhead, mtime = 0) {
    const b0 = this.peekBlock(path, size, index, mtime);
    if (b0) return b0;
    const skey = (i) => `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`;
    // fetch this block plus up to `readAhead` following blocks in one request
    const start = index * BLOCK;
    const n = Math.max(1, Math.min(readAhead, Math.ceil((size - start) / BLOCK)));
    const end = Math.min(size, start + n * BLOCK);
    const data = this.fetchRange(path, start, end);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) this.installBlock(path, index + i, data.subarray(i * BLOCK, Math.min(data.length, (i + 1) * BLOCK)), skey(index + i));
    this.evict();
    // (the block itself, not a cache lookup: a cache smaller than the read-ahead has already evicted it)
    return data.subarray(0, Math.min(data.length, BLOCK));
  }
  /** A whole block arrived: memory cache, persistent store; its pieces and its background request are dropped. */
  installBlock(path, index, bytes, skey) {
    const k = `${path}#${index}`;
    this.cache.set(k, bytes);
    this.store?.put(skey, bytes);
    this.want.delete(k); this.near.delete(k); this.later.delete(k); this.upgrades.delete(k);
    const pk = skey.slice(0, skey.lastIndexOf('#')) + '#c';
    for (let c = (index * BLOCK) / CHUNK, e = c + BLOCK / CHUNK; c < e; c++) {
      const ck = `${path}#${c}`, p = this.chunks.get(ck); if (p) { this.chunks.delete(ck); this.chunkBytes -= p.length; }
      if (this.store?.map.has(pk + c)) this.store.drop?.(pk + c); // (the pieces kept from a slow link: the block replaces them)
    }
  }

  /** key of a 64 KiB piece kept in the persistent store (a slow link fetches pieces, not always whole blocks) */
  pieceKey(path, size, mtime, c) { return `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#c${c}`; }
  /**
   * Piece `c` of a file is here: in memory, or kept in the persistent store by an earlier session (then brought back
   * into memory).
   */
  hasPiece(path, size, mtime, c) {
    const ck = `${path}#${c}`;
    if (this.chunks.has(ck)) return true;
    const st = this.store; if (!st) return false;
    const key = this.pieceKey(path, size, mtime, c);
    if (!st.map.has(key)) return false;
    const b = st.get(key);
    if (!b || b.length !== Math.min(CHUNK, size - c * CHUNK)) { if (b) st.drop?.(key); return false; }
    this.chunks.set(ck, b); this.chunkBytes += b.length;
    this.trimPieces();
    return true;
  }
  trimPieces() { while (this.chunkBytes > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES) { const [k, v] = this.chunks.entries().next().value; this.chunks.delete(k); this.chunkBytes -= v.length; } }
  /** pieces fetched are kept in the persistent store too: on a link that is not fast (whole blocks may never come) */
  keepPieces() { return !!this.store && (!this.net.fast() || this.keepLearned > 0); }
  /** Every piece of block `index` is here: the block is assembled from them and installed (memory, store). */
  assemble(path, size, mtime, index) {
    const k = `${path}#${index}`;
    if (this.cache.has(k)) return;
    const b0 = index * BLOCK, len = Math.min(BLOCK, size - b0), c0 = b0 / CHUNK, n = Math.ceil(len / CHUNK);
    for (let c = c0; c < c0 + n; c++) if (!this.chunks.has(`${path}#${c}`)) return;
    const out = new Uint8Array(len);
    for (let c = c0; c < c0 + n; c++) out.set(this.chunks.get(`${path}#${c}`), (c - c0) * CHUNK);
    this.installBlock(path, index, out, `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${index}`);
    this.evict();
  }

  /** Pieces m0..m1 of a file from `data` (fetched from piece m0), those not here yet; the piece cache stays bounded. */
  addPieces(path, m0, m1, data, file = null) {
    const keep = file && this.keepPieces(), added = [];
    for (let c = m0; c <= m1; c++) {
      const ck = `${path}#${c}`, piece = data.subarray((c - m0) * CHUNK, Math.min(data.length, (c - m0 + 1) * CHUNK));
      if (this.chunks.has(ck)) continue;
      if (this.cache.has(`${path}#${Math.floor(c * CHUNK / BLOCK)}`)) continue; // (its block is here whole)
      this.chunks.set(ck, piece); this.chunkBytes += piece.length;
      if (keep) added.push([c, piece]);
    }
    // (a block whose pieces are all here becomes a whole block: kept as such, its background download not needed)
    if (file) {
      const P = BLOCK / CHUNK;
      for (let bi = Math.floor(m0 / P); bi <= Math.floor(m1 / P); bi++) {
        const c0 = bi * P, n = Math.ceil((Math.min(file.size, (bi + 1) * BLOCK) - bi * BLOCK) / CHUNK);
        let all = true; for (let c = c0; c < c0 + n && all; c++) if (!this.hasPiece(path, file.size, file.mtime, c)) all = false;
        if (all) this.assemble(path, file.size, file.mtime ?? 0, bi);
      }
    }
    // (kept once their blocks are known: a piece whose block it just completed is in the store as that block — the
    // store appends, a piece put and then dropped would keep its bytes for good)
    for (const [c, piece] of added) if (!this.cache.has(`${path}#${Math.floor(c * CHUNK / BLOCK)}`)) this.store.put(this.pieceKey(path, file.size, file.mtime, c), piece);
    this.trimPieces();
  }

  /**
   * Bytes [pos, end) of one block that is neither cached nor stored (a random read): the missing 64 KiB pieces are
   * fetched in one request, the whole block is queued for the background.
   */
  readPieces(path, size, mtime, index, pos, end, out, outOff, ahead = 0, extra = 0) {
    const c0 = Math.floor(pos / CHUNK), c1 = Math.floor((end - 1) / CHUNK);
    let m0 = -1, m1 = -1;
    for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (!this.hasPiece(path, size, mtime, c)) { if (m0 < 0) m0 = c; m1 = c; }
    // (a stream: the request also covers the `extra` bytes that follow, within the block — the window grows with the
