```js
    // stream, as few round trips as whole blocks would take for a file read from start to end)
    if (m0 >= 0 && extra > 0) { const last = Math.min(Math.floor((Math.min(size, (index + 1) * BLOCK) - 1) / CHUNK), Math.floor((end - 1 + extra) / CHUNK)); while (m1 < last && !this.hasPiece(path, size, mtime, m1 + 1)) m1++; }
    if (m0 >= 0) {
      this.noteMiss(path, size, mtime, index);
      const start = m0 * CHUNK, stop = Math.min(size, (m1 + 1) * CHUNK);
      const data = this.fetchRange(path, start, stop);
      this.addPieces(path, m0, m1, data, { size, mtime });
      // (all of the block's pieces here: assembled, installed whole)
      const whole = this.cache.get(`${path}#${index}`);
      if (whole) { out.set(whole.subarray(pos - index * BLOCK, end - index * BLOCK), outOff); this.fillBackground(); return true; }
    }
    for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) {
      const ck = `${path}#${c}`, piece = this.chunks.get(ck);
      if (!piece) return false; // (evicted at once: a read larger than the piece cache — the caller fetches the block)
      this.chunks.delete(ck); this.chunks.set(ck, piece); // (LRU)
      const a = Math.max(pos, c * CHUNK), b = Math.min(end, c * CHUNK + piece.length);
      out.set(piece.subarray(a - c * CHUNK, b - c * CHUNK), outOff + (a - pos));
    }
    // the block, and for a stream the next ones, in the background (not on a thin link: there the bandwidth goes to
    // what the game reads and what earlier sessions read next — a whole block for a piece read is 16 times the bytes;
    // not the next ones of a media file the game is not streaming: see speculate)
    if (ahead && !this.speculate(path)) ahead = 0;
    for (let i = index; i <= index + ahead && i * BLOCK < size && !this.net.thin(); i++) {
      const wk = `${path}#${i}`;
      if (!this.want.has(wk) && (i === index || !this.peekBlock(path, size, i, mtime))) this.want.set(wk, { path, size, mtime, index: i });
    }
    this.fillBackground();
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Fetch asynchronously what a read of [pos, end) would fetch (the missing pieces of the blocks it touches, or whole
   * blocks for a bulk read), so that the read that follows finds everything here: the reading guest thread waits
   * parked while the others run (see ReadFile). Resolves when done (failures resolve too: the read then fetches
   * synchronously and reports the error itself).
   */
  async fetchAhead(path, size, mtime, pos, end, bulk, extra = 0) {
    // pieces of the read already on their way (fetched ahead from the learned list): waited for, not asked again
    // (and whole blocks fetched ahead of a sequential reader, see readAhead); one still waiting for its turn on the link
    // goes first now (the game waits for it)
    // (and the pieces another read's fetchAhead is fetching: fgFlights — joined, never asked twice at once)
    if (this.flights.size || this.blockFlights.size || this.fgFlights.size) {
      const flying = new Set();
      if (this.flights.size) for (let c = Math.floor(pos / CHUNK); c * CHUNK < end; c++) { const f = this.flights.get(`${path}#${c}`); if (f) flying.add(f); }
      if (this.blockFlights.size) for (let bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK); bi * BLOCK < end; bi++) { const f = this.blockFlights.get(`${path}#${bi}`); if (f) flying.add(f); }
      if (this.fgFlights.size) for (let c = Math.floor(pos / CHUNK); c * CHUNK < end; c++) { const f = this.fgFlights.get(`${path}#${c}`); if (f) { flying.add(f); this.stats.fgJoined = (this.stats.fgJoined ?? 0) + 1; } }
      for (const f of flying) { if (f.w) this.net.promote(f.w); f.joined = true; }
      if (flying.size) await Promise.all(flying);
    }
    const jobs = [];
    // a block of the read is being downloaded in the background (a stream's read-ahead): wait for it rather than
    // abort it (marked before any fetch below aborts the background downloads)
    const cur = this.bgCur;
    const waited = cur && cur.path === path && cur.index >= Math.floor(pos / BLOCK) && cur.index * BLOCK < end && !this.peekBlock(path, size, cur.index, mtime) ? cur : null;
    if (waited) { waited.waiters++; jobs.push(waited.done); }
    for (let bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK); bi * BLOCK < end; bi++) {
      if (this.peekBlock(path, size, bi, mtime)) continue;
      const b0 = bi * BLOCK, b1 = Math.min(size, b0 + BLOCK);
      if (waited?.index === bi) continue;
      if (bulk) {
        // (the blocks the read covers, up to 4, not past one on its way: the reader waits for these only — the ones
        // after them follow asynchronously once it has read, see readAhead)
        let n = 1; while (n < 4 && b0 + n * BLOCK < Math.min(size, end) && !this.blockFlights.has(`${path}#${bi + n}`)) n++;
        const e = Math.min(size, b0 + n * BLOCK);
        jobs.push(this.fgFlight(path, b0, e, this.fetchForeground(path, b0, e).then((d) => { if (d) for (let i = 0; b0 + i * BLOCK < e; i++) if (!this.cache.has(`${path}#${bi + i}`)) this.installBlock(path, bi + i, d.subarray(i * BLOCK, Math.min(d.length, (i + 1) * BLOCK)), `${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${bi + i}`); this.evict(); })));
        break;
      }
      const c0 = Math.floor(Math.max(pos, b0) / CHUNK), c1 = Math.floor((Math.min(end, b1) - 1) / CHUNK);
      let m0 = -1, m1 = -1;
      for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (!this.hasPiece(path, size, mtime, c)) { if (m0 < 0) m0 = c; m1 = c; }
      if (m0 < 0) continue;
      // (a stream: the `extra` bytes past the read too, within the block, as readPieces does)
      if (extra > 0 && Math.min(end, b1) === end) { const last = Math.min(Math.floor((b1 - 1) / CHUNK), Math.floor((end - 1 + extra) / CHUNK)); while (m1 < last && !this.hasPiece(path, size, mtime, m1 + 1) && !this.flights.has(`${path}#${m1 + 1}`)) m1++; }
      this.noteMiss(path, size, mtime, bi);
      const start = m0 * CHUNK, stop = Math.min(size, (m1 + 1) * CHUNK);
      jobs.push(this.fgFlight(path, start, stop, this.fetchForeground(path, start, stop).then((d) => {
        if (d && !this.cache.has(`${path}#${bi}`)) this.addPieces(path, m0, m1, d, { size, mtime });
      })));
    }
    try { await Promise.all(jobs); } finally { if (waited) waited.waiters--; }
  }
  /**
   * Every piece of [start, end) of `path` is on its way in a read's foreground fetch (fgFlights): a promise of those
   * bytes once the fetches settled — read back from memory (memoryRange) —, null then when they did not bring them all (a
   * request failed, or evicted already); null at once when some piece is not on its way (the caller fetches the range).
   */
  joinForeground(path, start, end) {
    if (!this.fgFlights.size || !(end > start)) return null;
    const flying = new Set();
    for (let c = Math.floor(start / CHUNK); c * CHUNK < end; c++) { const f = this.fgFlights.get(`${path}#${c}`); if (!f) return null; flying.add(f); }
    this.stats.bgJoinedFg = (this.stats.bgJoinedFg ?? 0) + 1;
    return Promise.allSettled([...flying]).then(() => {
      const d = this.memoryRange(path, start, end);
      if (!d) this.stats.bgJoinedFgMissed = (this.stats.bgJoinedFgMissed ?? 0) + 1;
      return d;
    });
  }
  /** [start, end) of `path` from the memory cache — its whole blocks, else its pieces —, a copy; null when some byte is not there. */
  memoryRange(path, start, end) {
    const out = new Uint8Array(end - start);
    for (let pos = start; pos < end;) {
      const bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK), b = this.cache.get(`${path}#${bi}`);
      let src = b, at = pos - bi * BLOCK;
      if (!src) { const c = Math.floor(pos / CHUNK); src = this.chunks.get(`${path}#${c}`); at = pos - c * CHUNK; }
      const n = src ? Math.min(end - pos, src.length - at) : 0;
      if (!(n > 0)) return null;
      out.set(src.subarray(at, at + n), pos - start);
      pos += n;
    }
    return out;
  }
  /** `job` (fetching [start, end) of `path` for a read, its bytes installed once it settles) in fgFlights while it runs. */
  fgFlight(path, start, end, job) {
    const c0 = Math.floor(start / CHUNK), c1 = Math.floor((end - 1) / CHUNK);
    const done = job.finally(() => { for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) if (this.fgFlights.get(`${path}#${c}`) === done) this.fgFlights.delete(`${path}#${c}`); });
    for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) this.fgFlights.set(`${path}#${c}`, done);
    return done;
  }
  /** [start, end) with fetch() for a read the game waits for (counted as the game's own reads; not aborted). */
  async fetchForeground(path, start, end) {
    const t0 = performance.now();
    this.abortBackground(true);
    this.fgPending++;
    const tok = this.net.begin('demand', end - start);
    let wire = 0, ok = false;
    try {
      const url = this.rangeUrl(path, start, end);
      const res = await fetch(url, this.encoded ? {} : { headers: { Range: `bytes=${start}-${end - 1}` } });
      this.net.firstByte(tok);
      if (res.status !== 206 && res.status !== 200) return null;
      let data = new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer());
      wire = wireOf(data.length, res.headers?.get?.('content-length'));
      data = this.unitBody(data, res.headers?.get?.('x-orthros-codec'), end - start);
      if (!data) return null;
      if (res.status === 200 && !this.encoded) data = data.subarray(start, end);
      if (data.length !== end - start) return null;
      ok = true;
      const ms = performance.now() - t0;
      this.stats.requests++; this.stats.bytes += data.length; this.stats.ms += ms; this.stats.asyncReads = (this.stats.asyncReads ?? 0) + 1;
      this.onFetch?.({ url, path, start, end, ms, async: true });
      return data;
    } catch { return null; } finally { this.fgPending--; this.lastSyncFetchAt = performance.now(); this.net.end(tok, wire, end - start, ok); }
  }

  /**
   * The game reads `path` at random as it goes (a streaming archive, a sound bank): all of its blocks wanted, downloaded
   * by the background fill last — after the blocks the game touched and those near them, the link quiet for NEAR_QUIET_MS
   * (not on a thin link: the game's reads alone there).
   */
  wantWhole(path) {
    const r = this.lookup(path); if (!r?.file) return;
    const size = r.file.size, mtime = r.file.mtime ?? 0;
    this.wholeAt.set(r.path, ++this.fileTurn);
    for (let i = 0; i * BLOCK < size; i++) {
      const k = `${r.path}#${i}`;
      if (!this.cache.has(k) && !this.store?.map.has(`${r.path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`)) this.later.set(k, { path: r.path, size, mtime, index: i });
    }
    this.fillBackground();
  }

  /**
   * The game is blocked on the network for a read of `path` (a synchronous read, a held one — HttpFile.prepare, a page's
   * data worker once the engine waits for its ask): its whole fill goes first (laterNext). Never for a read the game went
   * on past (an ask ahead, readable(), a sample skipped while missing): one would put a bank its engine skips before the
   * archive whose reads wait.
   */
  noteWait(path) {
    this.waitedAt.delete(path); this.waitedAt.set(path, ++this.fileTurn);
    if (this.waitedAt.size > WAITED_FILES) this.waitedAt.delete(this.waitedAt.keys().next().value); // (the oldest go)
  }

  /**
   * The `later` block the fill takes next ([key, entry] or undefined), file by file, each file's blocks in their order:
   * the file the game waited on latest this session first (its next reads wait on the network again while the file is
   * not whole — reVC's gta3.img, read at random as the player moves), else the file wanted whole latest (a bank wanted
   * whole at the engine's start before an archive wanted at a new game's: the archive's streaming reads wait, a bank's
   * missing sample is skipped — measured, docs/slow-network.md "Whole files in order").
   */
  laterNext() {
    let best, bestRank = -1;
    const ranks = new Map();
    for (const e of this.later) {
      const path = e[1].path;
      let r = ranks.get(path);
      if (r === undefined) { const w = this.waitedAt.get(path); r = w !== undefined ? WAITED_RANK + w : this.wholeAt.get(path) ?? 0; ranks.set(path, r); }
      if (r > bestRank) { best = e; bestRank = r; }
    }
    return best;
  }

  /** Every block of `path` is here (memory, store): its reads need no network. */
  isWhole(path) {
    const r = this.lookup(path); if (!r?.file) return false;
    const size = r.file.size, mtime = r.file.mtime ?? 0;
    for (let i = 0; i * BLOCK < size; i++) if (!this.cache.has(`${r.path}#${i}`) && !this.store?.map.has(`${r.path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`)) return false;
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * The tree's bytes and those of its blocks here whole (memory or store): { bytes, total } — downloadAll's count of
   * what it skips (a block here by pieces only is fetched whole again).
   */
  storedBytes() {
    let bytes = 0, total = 0;
    const walk = (node, rel) => {
      for (const [n, f] of Object.entries(node.files ?? {})) {
        const path = rel ? `${rel}/${n}` : n, size = f.size ?? 0, mtime = f.mtime ?? 0; total += size;
        for (let i = 0; i * BLOCK < size; i++) if (this.cache.has(`${path}#${i}`) || this.store?.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`)) bytes += Math.min(size, (i + 1) * BLOCK) - i * BLOCK;
      }
      for (const [n, d] of Object.entries(node.dirs ?? {})) walk(d, rel ? `${rel}/${n}` : n);
    };
    walk(this.tree, '');
    return { bytes, total };
  }

  /**
   * The game read `path`'s light copy (a link that is not fast: src/vfs/data-client.js): the file itself downloaded in
   * the background for its next load, last of all — after every other background download, the link quiet for
   * UPGRADE_QUIET_MS (UPGRADE_SOON_QUIET_MS when `soon`: an engine that loads it again in place), a thin link too (by
   * pieces) —, the latest files first (the player is near them: loaded again soonest). Not a picture's on a link that
   * is not fast (isLightPicture), and none while the game loads, on any link (fillBackground, loadUnderWay).
   */
  upgrade(path, { soon = false } = {}) {
    const r = this.lookup(path); if (!r?.file) return;
    // (a picture's light copy — a loading screen, a map: game-tree.js isLightPicture — on a link that is not fast: the
    // file comes with the offline copy, or read itself on a fast link; seconds of the link for a picture shown a moment)
    if (!this.net.fast() && isLightPicture(r.path)) { this.stats.pictureKept = (this.stats.pictureKept ?? 0) + 1; return; }
    const size = r.file.size, mtime = r.file.mtime ?? 0;
    for (let i = 0; i * BLOCK < size; i++) {
      const k = `${r.path}#${i}`;
      if (this.cache.has(k) || this.store?.map.has(`${r.path}#${size}#${mtime}#${i}`)) continue;
      this.upgrades.delete(k); this.upgrades.set(k, { path: r.path, size, mtime, index: i, soon });
      this.upgradeSoon = soon; // (the latest file's: the next one fetched)
    }
    this.fillBackground();
  }

  /**
   * Bytes of a file kept elsewhere before (a store an earlier page used), from offset `at` (a piece's start), into the
   * store as if downloaded: whole blocks as blocks, the rest as 64 KiB pieces (whole, or the file's tail).
   */
  keep(path, size, mtime, at, bytes) {
    const store = this.store; if (!store || at % CHUNK) return;
    const end = Math.min(size, at + bytes.length);
    for (let pos = at; pos < end;) {
      const bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK), bEnd = Math.min(size, (bi + 1) * BLOCK);
      if (pos === bi * BLOCK && end >= bEnd) { store.put(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${bi}`, bytes.subarray(pos - at, bEnd - at)); pos = bEnd; continue; }
      const c = pos / CHUNK, cEnd = Math.min(size, pos + CHUNK);
      if (end < cEnd) break; // (a piece cut short: not kept)
      if (!store.map.has(`${path}#${size}#${mtime}#${bi}`)) store.put(this.pieceKey(path, size, mtime, c), bytes.subarray(pos - at, cEnd - at));
      pos = cEnd;
    }
  }

  /** Download the wanted blocks, one at a time, while the game is not reading synchronously. */
  async fillBackground() {
    if (this.filling || typeof fetch !== 'function') return;
    this.filling = true;
    try {
      while (this.want.size || this.near.size || this.later.size || this.upgrades.size) {
        // (the blocks next to missed ones, then those of files wanted whole, after a longer quiet time, then the files
        // whose light copy the game read, after a longer one still)
        const quiet = () => (this.want.size ? 150 : this.near.size || this.later.size ? NEAR_QUIET_MS : 0);
        const reasonOf = (q) => (q === this.want ? 'want' : q === this.near ? 'near' : q === this.later ? 'later' : 'upgrade');
        const queued = () => this.want.size || this.near.size || this.later.size || this.upgrades.size;
        // (the next upgrade, the latest file's: soon or not)
        const upgradeQuiet = () => (this.upgradeSoon ? UPGRADE_SOON_QUIET_MS : UPGRADE_QUIET_MS);
        // (and none while the game loads — NetLink.loading: a dense run of reads it waits for, its engine's work between
        // them no pause —, whichever queue is next; the upgrades not during a load on a fast link either — loadUnderWay:
        // an engine waiting for its announced batch reads nothing meanwhile, the game would look quiet)
        while (queued() && (this.net.silenced() || (quiet() ? this.gameBusy(quiet()) : this.loadUnderWay() || !this.gameQuiet(upgradeQuiet())))) await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 50));
        const q = this.want.size ? this.want : this.near.size ? this.near : this.later.size ? this.later : this.upgrades;
        if (!q.size) continue; // (fetched whole meanwhile by a sequential read)
        const [k, w] = q === this.upgrades ? [...q].at(-1) : q === this.later ? this.laterNext() : q.entries().next().value;
        // (here already: fetched whole by a read, or stored by the learned prefetch)
        // (or on its way, fetched ahead of a sequential reader)
        if (this.cache.has(k) || this.blockFlights.has(k) || this.store?.map.has(`${w.path}#${w.size}#${w.mtime}#${w.index}`)) { q.delete(k); continue; }
        // (queued before the link was measured thin — the files whose light copy the game read stay: by pieces, below)
        if (this.net.thin() && q !== this.upgrades) { this.want.clear(); this.near.clear(); this.later.clear(); continue; }
        if (!this.net.fast()) {
          // (a link that is not fast: the block's missing pieces, a background request of the link's size at a time —
          // what came is kept whatever happens next, and the block is installed whole once all its pieces are here)
          const run = this.missingRun(w.path, w.size, w.mtime, w.index);
          if (!run) { if (this.flights.size) await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 50)); else q.delete(k); continue; }
          const r = await this.fetchPartBg(w.path, w.size, w.mtime, run[0], run[1], q === this.want ? PRIO.fill : q === this.near ? PRIO.near : PRIO.offline, undefined, false, { reason: reasonOf(q) });
          if (r === null) break; // (network down: the next random read queues it again)
          if (r === false) continue;
          if (r === undefined) q.delete(k);
          if (this.cache.has(k)) this.stats.bgBlocks = (this.stats.bgBlocks ?? 0) + 1;
          continue;
        }
        const start = w.index * BLOCK, end = Math.min(w.size, start + BLOCK);
        const cur = { key: k, path: w.path, index: w.index, ctl: null, done: null, waiters: 0 };
        const pr = this.fetchBackground(w.path, start, end, (ctl) => { cur.ctl = ctl; }, true, false, null, reasonOf(q));
        cur.done = pr.then(() => {});
        this.bgCur = cur;
        const data = await pr;
        this.bgCur = null;
        if (data === ABORTED) continue;
        if (data === null) break; // (network down: the next random read queues it again)
        q.delete(k);
        if (!data) continue;
        this.installBlock(w.path, w.index, data, `${w.path}#${w.size}#${w.mtime}#${w.index}`);
        this.evict();
        this.stats.bgBlocks = (this.stats.bgBlocks ?? 0) + 1;
      }
    } finally { this.filling = false; }
  }
  /**
   * Offline copy: fetch every block of every file of the listing that the store does not hold yet, in the background,
   * yielding to the game's reads (its turn on the link like the other background downloads, after them). The blocks of
   * the learned list `opts.order` ([path, block, ...], the order earlier sessions needed them) come first, then the
   * rest file by file; the media files' blocks (isMedia: movies, music) after all the others, in the same order. Requests carry up to 4 blocks when the game is not running (`opts.alone`: the page downloads the
   * game before playing) or the link is fast, else the link's background size (pieces, assembled into blocks). A
   * download stopped (page closed) resumes where it was: the stored blocks are skipped. `progress` is updated
   * ({ bytes, total, stored (bytes already here at the start), done }); stops at `stop()` or when the store fails (quota).
   */
  async downloadAll(progress, stop = () => false, opts = {}) {
    const store = this.store; if (!store || typeof fetch !== 'function') return;
    const files = [], byPath = new Map();
    const walk = (node, rel) => {
      for (const [n, f] of Object.entries(node.files ?? {})) { const e = { path: rel ? `${rel}/${n}` : n, size: f.size, mtime: f.mtime ?? 0, media: !!f.media }; files.push(e); byPath.set(e.path, e); }
      for (const [n, d] of Object.entries(node.dirs ?? {})) walk(d, rel ? `${rel}/${n}` : n);
    };
    walk(this.tree, '');
    const key = (f, i) => `${f.path}#${f.size}#${f.mtime}#${i}`;
    const blockBytes = (f, i) => Math.min(f.size, (i + 1) * BLOCK) - i * BLOCK;
    // the blocks in download order: learned ones first, then every other one; media files' after all of those
    const main = [], media = [], queued = new Set();
    for (const it of opts.order ?? []) {
      const r = Array.isArray(it) && typeof it[0] === 'string' ? this.lookup(it[0]) : null, f = r?.file ? byPath.get(r.path) : null;
      if (!f || !Number.isInteger(it[1]) || it[1] < 0 || it[1] * BLOCK >= f.size || queued.has(key(f, it[1]))) continue;
      queued.add(key(f, it[1])); (r.file.media ? media : main).push([f, it[1]]);
    }
    for (const f of files) for (let i = 0; i * BLOCK < f.size; i++) if (!queued.has(key(f, i))) (f.media ? media : main).push([f, i]);
    const jobs = main.concat(media);
    progress.total = files.reduce((a, f) => a + f.size, 0); progress.done = false;
    progress.bytes = 0; for (const [f, i] of jobs) if (store.map.has(key(f, i))) progress.bytes += blockBytes(f, i);
    progress.stored = progress.bytes;
    let failures = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < jobs.length; k++) {
      if (stop() || store.failed) return;
      const [f, b] = jobs[k];
      if (store.map.has(key(f, b))) continue;
      if (!opts.alone) while (this.gameBusy(500)) { if (stop()) return; await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200)); }
      if (opts.alone || this.net.backgroundBytes() >= BLOCK) {
        // (consecutive missing blocks of the file in one request, up to 4: those next in the order)
        // (alone on a link that is not fast: about ALONE_SECONDS of the link per request, one block until measured — a
        // 4 MiB request takes 50 s at 85 KB/s: the progress would move by jumps, and a pause would lose it)
        let n = 1; const most = this.net.fast() ? 4 : opts.alone ? Math.max(1, Math.min(4, Math.floor((this.net.bw ?? 0) * ALONE_SECONDS / this.net.ratio() / BLOCK))) : Math.max(1, Math.floor(this.net.backgroundBytes() / BLOCK));
        while (n < most && k + n < jobs.length && jobs[k + n][0] === f && jobs[k + n][1] === b + n && !store.map.has(key(f, b + n))) n++;
        const start = b * BLOCK, end = Math.min(f.size, (b + n) * BLOCK);
        const data = await this.fetchBackground(f.path, start, end, null, !opts.alone, false, { prio: PRIO.offline, stop, reason: 'offline' });
        if (data === ABORTED) { k--; continue; }
        if (data === null) { if (stop() || ++failures > 8) return; await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000)); k--; continue; }
        failures = 0;
        if (data) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) store.put(key(f, b + i), data.subarray(i * BLOCK, Math.min(data.length, (i + 1) * BLOCK)));
        progress.bytes += end - start; k += n - 1;
      } else {
        // (a thin link while the game runs: the block by pieces, a background request of the link's size at a time)
        const run = this.missingRun(f.path, f.size, f.mtime, b);
        if (!run) { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100)); if (!store.map.has(key(f, b)) && !this.cache.has(`${f.path}#${b}`)) k--; else progress.bytes += blockBytes(f, b); continue; }
        const r = await this.fetchPartBg(f.path, f.size, f.mtime, run[0], run[1], PRIO.offline, stop, false, { reason: 'offline' });
        if (r === null) { if (stop() || ++failures > 8) return; await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 2000)); }
        else failures = 0;
        if (r !== undefined && !store.map.has(key(f, b)) && !this.cache.has(`${f.path}#${b}`)) k--; // (the block's other pieces next)
        else progress.bytes += blockBytes(f, b);
      }
    }
    store.flush(true);
    progress.done = true;
  }
  evict() { while (this.cache.size > this.maxBlocks) { const first = this.cache.keys().next().value; this.cache.delete(first); } }
}

class HttpFile {
  constructor(backend, path, size, mtime) { this.b = backend; this.path = path; this.len = size; this.mtime = mtime; this.lastEnd = -1; this.run = 0; }
  size() { return this.len; }
  /**
   * Debugging (?dbg=ORTHROS_VERIFY_READS=1): the bytes a read returned compared with the same range fetched straight
   * from the server, past every cache; the first difference, or null.
   */
  verify(off, bytes) {
    if (!bytes.length) return null;
    const ref = this.b.fetchRange(this.path, off, off + bytes.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) if (bytes[i] !== ref[i]) return { at: i, got: bytes[i], want: ref[i] };
    return null;
  }
  /** The blocks of [off, end) are touched: the game's position in the learned prefetch list (see noteBlock). */
  note(off, end) {
    this.b.lastReadAt = performance.now(); // (the game reads: see gameQuiet)
    if (!this.b.learned) return;
    for (let bi = Math.floor(off / BLOCK), e = Math.floor((end - 1) / BLOCK); bi <= e; bi++) if (bi !== this.noted) { this.noted = bi; this.b.noteBlock(this.path, bi); }
  }
  /**
   * A read of [off, off + len) would need the network: a promise fetching it asynchronously (resolved when the data
   * is here), else null. Leaves the read state (sequence detection) alone. `held`: the game waits for it (see below).
   */
  // (`held`: the game is blocked until it is here — a parked read: a wait for NetLink.loading; a page's data worker counts
  // its waits itself, data-worker.js waited)
  prepare(off, len, held = false) {
    const p = this.prepareNow(off, len);
    // (nor a media stream's: its reader's misses are no load — counted as one, they silenced its own read-ahead, the
    // movie read a round trip at a time)
    if (p && held) this.b.noteWait(this.path); // (a wait for the file's whole fill too: laterNext)
    if (!p || !held || this.b.isMedia(this.path)) return p;
    const tok = this.b.net.wait();
    return p.finally(() => this.b.net.waitEnd(tok));
  }
  prepareNow(off, len) {
    const end = Math.min(off + len, this.len);
    if (off >= end || typeof fetch !== 'function') return null;
    this.note(off, end);
    // (on a link that is not fast a file read whole goes by pieces too, its next bytes fetched past the read by the
    // link's measure: whole blocks of 1-4 MiB would hold the game up for seconds)
    const fast = this.b.net.fast(), sequential = off === this.lastEnd, bulk = fast && sequential && this.run + (end - off) >= STREAM_BYTES;
    let missing = false;
    for (let bi = Math.floor(off / BLOCK); bi * BLOCK < end && !missing; bi++) {
      if (this.b.peekBlock(this.path, this.len, bi, this.mtime)) continue;
      if (bulk) { missing = true; break; }
      for (let c = Math.floor(Math.max(off, bi * BLOCK) / CHUNK), e = Math.floor((Math.min(end, (bi + 1) * BLOCK) - 1) / CHUNK); c <= e; c++) if (!this.b.hasPiece(this.path, this.len, this.mtime, c)) { missing = true; break; }
    }
    const extra = !fast && sequential ? this.b.net.demandExtra(Math.min(this.run + (end - off), BLOCK)) : 0;
    return missing ? this.b.fetchAhead(this.path, this.len, this.mtime, off, end, bulk, extra) : null;
  }
  read(off, len) {
    const ap = acct.enter(ACCT.io); // (frame accounting: a game file read — its network part is `net`)
    try { return this.readNow(off, len); } finally { acct.leave(ap); }
  }
  readNow(off, len) {
    const end = Math.min(off + len, this.len);
    if (off >= end) return new Uint8Array(0);
    this.note(off, end);
    this.b.reads.bytes += end - off; if (this.video) this.b.reads.videoBytes += end - off;
    this.b.onRead?.(this.path, off, end);
    const out = new Uint8Array(end - off);
    const sequential = off === this.lastEnd;
    this.lastEnd = end;
    // bytes read in sequence so far: a bulk read (loading a file whole) fetches whole blocks ahead synchronously; a
    // stream read a little at a time (audio, video while playing) goes by pieces, its next blocks in the background
    this.run = sequential ? this.run + (end - off) : 0;
    if (!sequential) { this.runT0 = performance.now(); this.runFrom = off; } // (the run's start: its reading rate and offset, see readAhead)
    // (a stream: many reads in sequence — a movie, music; an archive entry loaded in one go is not, and a read elsewhere
    // in the file ends it)
    this.runReads = sequential ? (this.runReads ?? 0) + 1 : 0;
    // (the backend's latest reader: a queued whole block of a file read whole drops once it moved away, see readAheadParts)
    const rd = this.b.reader; if (rd.path !== this.path || !sequential) rd.runs++; rd.path = this.path; rd.end = end;
    if (this.run >= STREAM_SKIP && this.runReads >= STREAM_READS) this.b.streams.add(this.path);
    else if (!sequential && this.b.streams.size) this.b.streams.delete(this.path);
    const fast = this.b.net.fast(), bulk = sequential && this.run >= STREAM_BYTES;
    let pos = off;
    while (pos < end) {
      const bi = Math.floor(pos / BLOCK), bo = pos - bi * BLOCK;
      // (one read that covers several whole blocks none of which is here — a file read whole in one call, as a program
      // image is loaded —: those blocks in one request, as the game waits for all of them anyway; one round trip instead
      // of one per block — BFME 1.08's 16 MB executable through a 75 ms link: 16 requests, 2.6 s before)
      if (bo === 0) {
        const n = this.b.missingBlocks(this.path, this.len, this.mtime, bi, end);
        if (n >= 2) { this.b.block(this.path, this.len, bi, n, this.mtime); this.b.stats.coalesced = (this.b.stats.coalesced ?? 0) + 1; }
      }
      // a random read of a block not here yet: only its pieces now (the block follows in the background); on a link
      // that is not fast a file read whole too, with what the link carries in a moment past it (see prepare)
      if ((!bulk || !fast) && !this.b.peekBlock(this.path, this.len, bi, this.mtime)) {
        const stop = Math.min(end, (bi + 1) * BLOCK);
        const extra = !sequential ? 0 : fast ? Math.min(this.run, STREAM_WINDOW) : this.b.net.demandExtra(Math.min(this.run, BLOCK));
        if (this.b.readPieces(this.path, this.len, this.mtime, bi, pos, stop, out, pos - off, sequential ? 2 : 0, extra)) { pos = stop; continue; }
      }
      const blk = this.b.block(this.path, this.len, bi, sequential && fast ? 4 : 1, this.mtime);
      const n = Math.min(end - pos, blk.length - bo);
      if (n <= 0) break;
      out.set(blk.subarray(bo, bo + n), pos - off);
      pos += n;
    }
    // (a file read whole: its next blocks on their way before the reader gets there)
    if (pos === end && (bulk || (!fast && sequential && this.run >= CHUNK))) this.b.readAhead(this.path, this.len, this.mtime, end, this.run / Math.max(0.25, (performance.now() - this.runT0) / 1000), this.runReads, end - this.runFrom);
    return pos === end ? out : out.subarray(0, pos - off);
  }
  write() { return 0; }
  truncate() {}
  close() { if (this.closed) return; this.closed = true; this.b.noteClose(this.path); }
}

```

`src/vfs/launch-set.js`:

```js
// The launch set of a game version, the same for every runtime (CLAUDE.md "Standardization", docs/slow-network.md
// "Playable after"): the entries of its learned order (/api/prefetch: [path, block, pieces mask, ms, flags?]) a session
// reads before its game is playable, as a link reads them (forLink). The server's learned order says which: a page marks
// the moment its game first draws in play (GameData.mark('playable')), the server flags the entries the sessions that
// marked it had read by then (bit PRE_PLAYABLE of the fifth element, present once a session marked the version); an
// order without flags is cut at its first pause instead (STARTUP_GAP_MS). One implementation for the data worker (the
// startup set a page waits for), the download worker (the home's "Prepare") and the server (the home's "playable after
// X MB": /api/manifests `launch`). `files`: an HttpBackend over the version's tree (lookup, isWhole, pieceHere,
// peekBlockHere) — the server's has no store.
import { BLOCK, CHUNK } from './http-backend.js';
import { LIGHT_DIR, isLightContent } from './game-tree.js';

/** An order without flags: its startup set up to its first pause this long. */
export const STARTUP_GAP_MS = 2000;
/** Flags bit: earlier sessions read the entry before their game was playable (in at least half the marked sessions). */
export const PRE_PLAYABLE = 1;
/**
 * Flags bit: a content file's block (game-tree.js isLightContent) that sessions whose engine reads it light at its
 * content load (CONTENT_EXPORT) read as the file itself before their game was playable (in at least half of those that
 * marked it): their first cells' land and references, after the content load (whose reads are learned under the light
 * copy's path: data-client.js) — the file's own bytes, not its light copy (contentLight). The server's
 * (src/host/server.js prefetchList); an order learned before such sessions has none.
 */
export const CONTENT_REAL = 2;
/** The wire bytes of a decoded byte, when the server does not know them (its compressed units: br-cache.js). */
export const WIRE_RATIO = 0.75;

const PIECES = BLOCK / CHUNK;

/**
 * The export of an engine that loads a file again in place once it is here (its release.json `exports`: OpenMW's,
 * streamfs.js; GameData.reloads): its big loads read light copies first on every link (data-client.js), so its launch
 * set is the light one on every link too (lightLaunch).
 */
export const RELOAD_EXPORT = 'orthros_file_updated';
/**
 * The export of an engine that reads its content files light while it loads its content and says when it is done
 * (game-tree.js isLightContent; OpenMW's Orthros build from orthros-r13: globalThis.orthrosContentLoading /
 * orthrosContentLoaded, data-client.js): only its versions' trees mark those files' light copies (src/host/game-files.js
 * listGameTree `contentLight`) — another engine reads them as they are, nothing light listed or fetched for them.
 */
export const CONTENT_EXPORT = 'orthros_content_light';
/**
 * An entry of a learned order of the content file `path` (isLightContent) stands for its light copy — on every link —
 * when sessions read it before their game was playable (`flags` PRE_PLAYABLE), or in an order without flags: the
 * content load reads the copy (orders learned before it did read the file there — the same pieces, light now; since,
 * learned under the copy's path); the file's own reads after it stay the file's: in play, or before playable by the
 * sessions whose engine reads the copy (CONTENT_REAL: their first cells' land and references — a block an older
 * engine's content load read too stays the file's then, not dropped from the launch set as a copy of what it has).
 */
export const contentLight = (path, flags) => isLightContent(path) && (flags === undefined || ((flags & PRE_PLAYABLE) !== 0 && (flags & CONTENT_REAL) === 0));
/**
 * The launch set read as on a link that is not fast (light copies, no media: launchSet(..., false)) — on such a link, and
 * on any link for a version whose engine reloads in place (/api/manifests launch.reloads): what its game reads before it
 * plays without waiting (a new game's big load reads the light copies even on a fast link), the files themselves
 * coming after as upgrades. One rule for the home's card (launchStatus), "Prepare" and the probe (download-worker.js)
 * and the page's cold-store test (data-worker.js prefetchNow; not its pill, launchWatch: counted on the set its prefetch
 * fetches).
 */
export const lightLaunch = (fast, reloads = false) => !fast || !!reloads;

/** The order carries the server's flags (a session marked the version playable). */
export const flagged = (list) => list.some((e) => typeof e[4] === 'number');

/**
 * A learned order as this link reads it: on a link that is not fast, a texture's light copy (whole, once) in place of
 * the file — unless the file is here; a copy of the file's own size (redrawn in place: a WAD's, light-copies.js) by the
 * same pieces; a content file's (a TES3 file's) by the same pieces on every link, for the entries read before playable
 * (contentLight) —, and the media files' entries (the tree's `media`: movies, music — game-tree.js)
 * after all the others, in their order (a movie earlier sessions watched while this one may skip it, a track the engine
 * streams itself: not ahead of what the game waits for); on a fast one, the files themselves in place of light copies
 * earlier sessions read. An entry's flags go with what replaces it.
 */
export function forLink(files, list, fast) {
  const out = [], tail = [], seen = new Set();
  const add = (path, block, mask, t, flags) => { const k = path + '#' + block; if (!seen.has(k)) { seen.add(k); out.push(flags === undefined ? [path, block, mask, t] : [path, block, mask, t, flags]); } };
  for (const e of list) {
    const [path, , , t, flags] = e, light = path.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/');
    const r = files.lookup(light ? path.slice(LIGHT_DIR.length + 1) : path);
    if (!fast && !light && r?.file?.media) { const k = path + '#' + e[1]; if (!seen.has(k)) { seen.add(k); tail.push(e); } continue; }
    if (!r?.file?.light) { if (!light) add(...e); continue; }
    if (r.file.light === r.file.size) { // (a copy redrawn in place — a WAD's —, its offsets the file's: the same pieces of the one read)
      // (a content file's — a TES3 file's, payloads zeroed in place —: its copy on every link for the content load, the
      // file's own entries in play the file's — contentLight)
      const real = files.isWhole(r.path) || (isLightContent(r.path) ? !light && !contentLight(r.path, flags) : fast);
      add(real ? r.path : `${LIGHT_DIR}/${r.path}`, e[1], e[2], t, flags);
      continue;
    }
    if (fast || files.isWhole(r.path)) {
      if (!light) add(...e); else for (let b = 0; b * BLOCK < r.file.size; b++) add(r.path, b, 0, t, flags);
    } else {
      for (let b = 0; b * BLOCK < r.file.light; b++) {
        const n = Math.ceil((Math.min(BLOCK, r.file.light - b * BLOCK)) / CHUNK);
        add(`${LIGHT_DIR}/${r.path}`, b, n >= 16 ? 0xffff : (1 << n) - 1, t, flags);
      }
    }
  }
  return tail.length ? out.concat(tail) : out;
}

/**
 * The startup set of a learned order as this link reads it (forLink's): its entries flagged PRE_PLAYABLE when the order
 * has flags, else those up to its first pause of STARTUP_GAP_MS — on a link that is not fast, without the media files
 * (they are not needed to start the game).
 */
export function startupHead(files, list, fast) {
  if (!fast) list = list.filter(([path]) => !files.lookup(path)?.file?.media);
  if (flagged(list)) return list.filter((e) => (e[4] & PRE_PLAYABLE) !== 0);
  let end = list.length;
  for (let i = 1; i < list.length; i++) if (list[i][3] - list[i - 1][3] > STARTUP_GAP_MS) { end = i; break; }
  return list.slice(0, end);
}

/** The launch set of a learned order (as received) on this link: startupHead(forLink(...)). */
export const launchSet = (files, list, fast) => startupHead(files, forLink(files, list, fast), fast);

/**
 * A learned order as this link reads it (forLink's), its launch set first when it has flags: the entries earlier
 * sessions read before their game was playable, then the others, each part in its order (the media files last still,
 * on a link that is not fast). Followed from the game's position (HttpBackend.prefetch), a session that waits in its
 * menu loads what the rest of the way to playable needs (a new game's first load) before what sessions read later.
 * The list's `first` (when it has flags): how many of its entries are the launch set (HttpBackend.prefetch's opts.first).
 */
export function launchFirst(files, list, fast) {
  const all = forLink(files, list, fast);
  if (!flagged(all)) return all;
  const first = [], rest = [];
  for (const e of all) ((e[4] & PRE_PLAYABLE) !== 0 && (fast || !files.lookup(e[0])?.file?.media) ? first : rest).push(e);
  // (`first`: the launch set's length — HttpBackend.prefetch's opts.first)
  return Object.assign(first.concat(rest), { first: first.length });
}

/**
 * The 64 KiB pieces an entry stands for: { path (the tree's), size, mtime, block, pieces: [chunk index] } — its learned
 * ones (all of the block's when its mask is unknown) —, or null (not in the tree).
 */
export function entryPieces(files, [path, block, mask]) {
  const r = files.lookup(path); if (!r?.file || !(block * BLOCK < r.file.size)) return null;
  const n = Math.ceil(Math.min(BLOCK, r.file.size - block * BLOCK) / CHUNK), all = n >= PIECES ? 0xffff : (1 << n) - 1;
  const m = (mask & all) || all, pieces = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) if (m & (1 << i)) pieces.push(block * PIECES + i);
  return { path: r.path, size: r.file.size, mtime: r.file.mtime ?? 0, block, pieces, whole: m === all };
}
const pieceBytes = (size, c) => Math.min(CHUNK, size - c * CHUNK);

/**
 * The bytes of a set (decoded), and those of them here already (files' memory or store): { bytes, here }. `whole`: its
 * blocks counted whole (what a fast link fetches of them: HttpBackend.prefetch), not their learned pieces. The set as
 * this link reads it (forLink): on a link that is not fast a file here whole is listed itself, not its light copy;
 * on a fast one a light copy here does not count for its file — the game's startup fetches the file's own pieces.
 */
export function setBytes(files, list, whole = false) {
  let bytes = 0, here = 0;
  for (const e of list) {
    const p = entryPieces(files, e); if (!p) continue;
    const block = p.block, blockHere = files.peekBlockHere?.(p.path, p.size, p.mtime, block);
    // (a content file's light copy: its file's pieces here count — the bytes its reads take where they are, data-worker.js
    // contentHere: a store filled when the engine read the file itself)
    const real = p.path.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/') && isLightContent(p.path) ? p.path.slice(LIGHT_DIR.length + 1) : null;
    const realBlock = real !== null && files.peekBlockHere?.(real, p.size, p.mtime, block);
    const pieces = whole ? Array.from({ length: Math.ceil(Math.min(BLOCK, p.size - block * BLOCK) / CHUNK) }, (_, i) => block * PIECES + i) : p.pieces;
    for (const c of pieces) {
      const n = pieceBytes(p.size, c); bytes += n;
      if (blockHere || files.pieceHere?.(p.path, p.size, p.mtime, c) || realBlock || (real !== null && files.pieceHere?.(real, p.size, p.mtime, c))) here += n;
    }
  }
  return { bytes, here };
}

/**
 * What a version's launch costs, from its learned order (as the server lists it): { bytes, lightBytes, wire, lightWire,
 * entries } — decoded and wire bytes of the launch set on a fast link (the files themselves) and on one that is not
 * (light copies, no media: the one a version whose engine reloads in place announces on every link, lightLaunch — the
 * server adds `reloads`) —, or null when no session marked it playable (no flags). `wireOf(path, unit, raw)`: the wire
 * bytes of a transport unit ({ kind: 'b' | 'p', index }, br-cache.js's: a block whose pieces are all learned, or one
 * piece; a light copy by pieces, one block when it is one piece), else raw × WIRE_RATIO.
 */
export function launchSummary(files, list, wireOf = null) {
  if (!flagged(list)) return null;
  const wire = (path, unit, raw) => { const w = wireOf?.(path, unit, raw); return Number.isFinite(w) ? w : raw * WIRE_RATIO; };
  const cost = (fast) => {
    const set = launchSet(files, list, fast);
    let bytes = 0, wired = 0;
    for (const e of set) {
      const p = entryPieces(files, e); if (!p) continue;
      const light = p.path.startsWith(LIGHT_DIR + '/');
      const n = p.pieces.reduce((a, c) => a + pieceBytes(p.size, c), 0);
      bytes += n;
      if (light ? p.size <= CHUNK : p.whole) wired += wire(p.path, { kind: 'b', index: p.block }, n);
      else for (const c of p.pieces) wired += wire(p.path, { kind: 'p', index: c }, pieceBytes(p.size, c));
    }
    return { bytes, wire: Math.round(wired), entries: set.length };
  };
  const full = cost(true), light = cost(false);
  return { bytes: full.bytes, lightBytes: light.bytes, wire: full.wire, lightWire: light.wire, entries: full.entries };
}
```

`src/vfs/net-link.js`:

```js
// The player's connection to the server, as the game file downloads share it (docs/slow-network.md): the
// bandwidth it delivers (measured from the transfers themselves), the game's own reads in flight, and the turns of the
// background downloads (prefetch, read-ahead, block fill, offline copy). One per page: the game's folder and the games
// it requires share it.
//
// Rules (generic: they depend on the measured link only):
// - the game's reads (demand) come first: on a thin link (below THIN_BPS) a background download starts only while no
//   demand read is in flight and the link has been quiet for the download's own delay; between thin and fast it goes
//   beside them, the bytes in flight (the game's and the background's) within about BG_SECONDS of the link; a fast
//   link (FAST_BPS and more) keeps the local-network policies. The background requests in flight carry at most about
//   BG_SECONDS of the link together (several small ones at once — a latency-bound run of small files fills the link —
//   or one larger one), and at most maxBackground() of them;
// - a background request carries at most backgroundBytes() (about BG_SECONDS of the link): a demand read that comes
//   while it is on its way waits for it at most that long, and nothing needs to be aborted (an abort throws away what
//   the request had already received);
// - a demand read asks for what the game reads plus at most demandExtra() bytes past it (DEMAND_SECONDS of the
//   link): a thin link fetches what the game needs, a fast one rounds up generously (fewer round trips).
// - a load (docs/slow-network.md "Silence during a load"): while the game is blocked in a dense run of reads it really
//   waits for (wait/waitEnd: a parked read, a synchronous one — not a read fetched ahead that nothing waits for), a link
//   that is not fast carries only what that load needs: the turns promoted by a parked read (urgent) and those flagged
//   forLoad; the others stay queued until the load is over (loading()), and an allowed one is small (requestBytes()).

/** a background request carries about this much of the link's time (s) */
export const BG_SECONDS = 0.35;
/** a demand read rounds up by at most this much of the link's time (s) */
export const DEMAND_SECONDS = 0.25;
/** at or above this rate (bytes/s, measured) the link is "fast": the earlier policies (whole blocks, block fill, aborts) apply — measured at 5 MB/s with a 50 ms round trip, they reach the menu and the game sooner there (round trips cost more than bytes) */
export const FAST_BPS = 3 << 20;
/** below this rate (bytes/s) the link is "thin": no speculative whole blocks in the background (see thin()) */
export const THIN_BPS = 384 << 10;
const MIN_BG = 64 << 10, MAX_BG = 4 << 20;
/** request size bound while the link is not measured yet */
const UNKNOWN_BG = 256 << 10;
/** answers at most this large (wire bytes) time the round trip */
const RTT_BYTES = 16 << 10;
/** the rate is measured over the answers that ended within this much time (ms, see sample) */
const HORIZON_MS = 20000;
/**
 * A load (see loading): at least LOAD_WAITS reads the game waited for began within LOAD_WINDOW_MS, the last of them
 * ended less than loadGap() ago (LOAD_GAP_MS at least, LOAD_GAP_RTTS round trips) — one wait in play alone silences
 * nothing past its own end
 */
export const LOAD_WAITS = 3, LOAD_WINDOW_MS = 4000, LOAD_GAP_MS = 500, LOAD_GAP_RTTS = 4;
/**
 * a run of waits that has lasted LOAD_LONG_MS (a load, not a few reads in play) ends only after a pause of LOAD_HOLD_MS:
 * its engine's own work between two reads (a save parsed, a scene built) can last longer than loadGap()'s few round
 * trips, and each such pause released every queued download, whole blocks too, into the load's next reads
 */
export const LOAD_LONG_MS = 4000, LOAD_HOLD_MS = 2000;
/** while loading, a background request carries at most this many round trips of the link (see requestBytes) */
const LOAD_REQUEST_RTTS = 2;
/** requests a browser runs at once to an HTTP/1.x origin (Chrome: six connections per host; see h1) */
export const H1_CONNECTIONS = 6;
/**
 * The learned read-ahead's requests in flight (HttpBackend.pumpAhead, see aheadBudget): AHEAD_REQUESTS on a thin link or
 * an HTTP/1.x origin (its six connections are the game's reads' too), AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID otherwise — small files are
 * latency-bound —, and on a measured fast link over HTTP/2 or 3 as many as keep AHEAD_BDP times the link's
 * bandwidth-delay product in flight, AHEAD_REQUESTS_MAX at most: a GoldSrc map's first load reads ~750 learned entries,
 * most of them 64 KiB or less, and 3 requests of ~86 KB each round trip carried 0.2-0.9 MB/s of an 8 MB/s, 85 ms link
 * (Half Strike de_dust2, 814 waits for 15 s of a 17 s load, tools/goldsrc/maps.mjs --proxy 8m:85)
 */
export const AHEAD_REQUESTS = 3, AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID = 8, AHEAD_REQUESTS_MAX = 24, AHEAD_BDP = 2;
/** the fast link's ahead bytes at least: AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID pieces of 64 KiB (a short round trip: no fewer than a mid link's) */
export const AHEAD_BYTES_MIN = AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID * 65536;

export class NetLink {
  /**
   * @param {{ now?: () => number, bw?: number, fixed?: boolean, setTimer?: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => any, clearTimer?: (t: any) => void, protocol?: string }} [opts]
   *   bw: the rate measured on this link last time (bytes/s), the estimate until this session measures its own;
   *   protocol: the origin's HTTP version, as nextHopProtocol says it (else found by h1)
   */
  constructor(opts = {}) {
    this.now = opts.now ?? (() => performance.now());
    this.setTimer = opts.setTimer ?? ((fn, ms) => setTimeout(fn, ms));
    this.clearTimer = opts.clearTimer ?? ((t) => clearTimeout(t));
    /** bandwidth estimate (bytes/s on the wire), null until measured (nor given) */
    this.bw = Number.isFinite(opts.bw) && opts.bw > 0 ? opts.bw : null;
    /** fixed: never measured (the estimate stays as given: null keeps the local-network policies) */
    this.fixed = !!opts.fixed;
    this.measured = false;
    /** shortest request seen (ms): the round trip, about */
    this.rtt = null;
    this.inflight = { demand: 0, bg: 0 };
    this.lastDemandEnd = -1e9;
    /** totals: wire bytes received, requests, ms the game's reads were on their way */
    this.totals = { demandBytes: 0, demandRequests: 0, demandMs: 0, bgBytes: 0, bgRequests: 0, abortedRequests: 0, rawBytes: 0, waits: 0, waitMs: 0 };
    // bandwidth window: bytes received and link busy time since the last sample
    // (bandwidth window: the transfer intervals of the answers that ended in it — from their first byte, else from their
    // start plus a round trip, to their end — and their wire bytes; see sample)
    this.winStart = this.now(); this.winIntervals = []; this.winBytes = 0;
    /** the answers ended within HORIZON_MS: [transfer start, end, wire bytes] (see sample) */
    this.hist = [];
    /** background downloads waiting for their turn: { prio, quietMs, resolve, urgent } */
    this.waiters = []; this.timer = null;
    /** background requests in flight: Set of { bytes, t0, abort } */
    this.bgFlights = new Set();
    /** turns given to background downloads that have not begun their request yet (times given) */
    this.reserved = [];
    /** the game's reads in flight (their tokens) */
    this.demandFlights = new Set();
    /** the reads the game waits for now (wait's tokens), the times the latest ones began, when the last one ended */
    this.waitsNow = new Set(); this.waitStarts = []; this.lastWaitEnd = -1e9;
    /** when the current run of waits began (its first wait after a pause of loadGap(): see loadGap) */
    this.runT0 = -1e9;
    /**
     * the background bytes by producer (begin's `reason`: pf1/pf2 learned pieces / rest of their blocks, pf whole learned
     * blocks, ahead, readAhead, mediaAhead, miss, want, near, later, upgrade, offline): { requests, wire, raw, inLoad —
     * wire bytes of the requests begun during a load }
     */
    this.bgBy = {};
    /**
     * the origin's HTTP version as the browser negotiated it (PerformanceResourceTiming.nextHopProtocol: 'http/1.1', 'h2',
     * 'h3'), null until one of its answers tells it (see h1); `protocol` given: fixed (tests)
     */
    this.protocol = typeof opts.protocol === 'string' ? opts.protocol : null;
  }

  /**
   * The origin speaks HTTP/1.x (a local server, `make serve`; the production front speaks HTTP/2): the browser runs
   * H1_CONNECTIONS requests to it at once, the others queued in the order they came — not the link's priorities: a
   * request beyond them waits behind every one started before it, the game's reads too. Known from the first answer the
   * browser's resource timing lists (this context's own requests); false until then.
   */
  h1() {
    if (this.protocol === null && typeof performance !== 'undefined' && typeof performance.getEntriesByType === 'function') {
      for (const e of performance.getEntriesByType('resource')) if (e.nextHopProtocol) { this.protocol = e.nextHopProtocol; break; }
    }
    return /^http\/1/i.test(this.protocol ?? '');
  }

  /**
   * The game is blocked on a read (a parked read, a synchronous one, a page's read its engine waits for): its token for
   * waitEnd. Not a request: what feeds loading() — a read fetched ahead that nothing waits for is no wait.
   */
  wait() {
    const t = { t0: this.now() };
    // (the first wait after a pause: a new run)
    if (!this.waitsNow.size && t.t0 - this.lastWaitEnd >= this.loadGap()) this.runT0 = t.t0;
    this.waitsNow.add(t); this.waitStarts.push(t.t0); this.totals.waits++;
    if (this.waitStarts.length > 64) this.waitStarts.shift();
    return t;
  }
  /** The read of wait token `t` is here (or failed): the game goes on. */
  waitEnd(t) {
    if (!t || !this.waitsNow.delete(t)) return;
    this.lastWaitEnd = this.now(); this.totals.waitMs += this.lastWaitEnd - t.t0;
    this.kick();
  }
  /**
   * after a dense run of waits, a pause this long (ms) ends the load: a few round trips, LOAD_GAP_MS at least —
   * LOAD_HOLD_MS once the run has lasted LOAD_LONG_MS
   */
  loadGap() {
    const g = Math.max(LOAD_GAP_MS, LOAD_GAP_RTTS * (this.rtt ?? 0));
    return this.lastWaitEnd - this.runT0 >= LOAD_LONG_MS ? Math.max(g, LOAD_HOLD_MS) : g;
  }
  /**
   * The game is loading: a read it waits for is in flight, or a dense run of them (LOAD_WAITS within LOAD_WINDOW_MS)
   * ended less than loadGap() ago — the engine's work between two reads of a load is no pause.
   */
  loading() {
    if (this.waitsNow.size) return true;
    const now = this.now();
    if (now - this.lastWaitEnd >= this.loadGap()) return false;
    let n = 0; for (let i = this.waitStarts.length - 1; i >= 0 && now - this.waitStarts[i] < LOAD_WINDOW_MS; i--) n++;
    return n >= LOAD_WAITS;
  }
  /** The background keeps to the load's own needs now: a load on a link that is not fast (a fast one keeps its policies). */
  silenced() { return !this.fast() && this.loading(); }
  /**
   * File bytes one background request may carry now: backgroundBytes(), and while silenced() at most LOAD_REQUEST_RTTS
   * round trips of the link — a parked read that waits for a request on its way waits about that long, not a block's time.
   */
  requestBytes() {
    const b = this.backgroundBytes();
    if (!this.bw || !this.silenced()) return b;
    return Math.max(MIN_BG, Math.min(b, Math.floor(this.bw * LOAD_REQUEST_RTTS * (this.rtt ?? 0) / 1000 / this.ratio() / MIN_BG) * MIN_BG));
  }
  /** background requests in flight or about to be (turns given within the last 500 ms) */
  bgCount() { const now = this.now(); while (this.reserved.length && now - this.reserved[0].t > 500) this.reserved.shift(); return this.inflight.bg + this.reserved.length; }
  /** file bytes of the game's reads in flight */
  demandBytes() { let n = 0; for (const t of this.demandFlights) n += t.bytes; return n; }
  /** file bytes of the background requests in flight or about to be */
  bgBytes() { let n = 0; for (const t of this.bgFlights) n += t.bytes; for (const r of this.reserved) n += r.bytes; return n; }

  /** wire bytes per file byte so far (compressed ranges: below 1), 1 until known */
  ratio() { const t = this.totals; return t.rawBytes >= 256 << 10 ? Math.max(0.15, Math.min(1, (t.demandBytes + t.bgBytes) / t.rawBytes)) : 1; }
  /** seconds the link takes to carry `bytes` of file (0 when unknown: no limit) */
  secondsFor(bytes) { return this.bw ? bytes * this.ratio() / this.bw : 0; }
  /** the link is fast enough for the local-network policies (or not measured yet and nothing says otherwise) */
  // (not measured yet: careful until the first answers measure it — a thin link's first seconds are when a 2 MiB
  // background block hurts most; a fixed link without a measure keeps the local-network policies, as tests expect)
  fast() { return this.bw === null ? this.fixed : this.bw >= FAST_BPS; }
  /** a thin link (measured below THIN_BPS): the background downloads keep to what the game is known to need */
  thin() { return this.bw !== null && this.bw < THIN_BPS; }
  /** file bytes a background request may carry (a multiple of 64 KiB) */
  backgroundBytes() {
    if (this.bw === null) return this.fixed ? MAX_BG : UNKNOWN_BG;
    return Math.max(MIN_BG, Math.min(MAX_BG, Math.floor(this.bw * BG_SECONDS / this.ratio() / MIN_BG) * MIN_BG));
  }
  /**
   * The learned read-ahead's budget (HttpBackend.pumpAhead): { requests, bytes } — requests in flight at most, and the
   * file bytes in flight past which only AHEAD_REQUESTS requests go (whatever their size: a learned whole block is one).
   * A thin link: AHEAD_REQUESTS; between thin and fast (or not measured yet, nor fixed): AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID; a fast link
   * measured over HTTP/2 or 3, its round trip known: up to AHEAD_REQUESTS_MAX requests while their bytes stay under
   * AHEAD_BDP bandwidth-delay products, AHEAD_BYTES_MIN at least (8 MB/s × 85 ms: ~1.4 MB on the wire, ~24 requests of
   * a map's learned pieces, three whole blocks — as before; a demand read that misses the order waits behind about
   * AHEAD_BDP round trips, a block more at most) — it had AHEAD_REQUESTS, fewer than a slower link; a fast link
   * otherwise (HTTP/1.x: six connections shared with the game's reads; a fixed one, not measured): AHEAD_REQUESTS.
   */
  aheadBudget() {
    if (this.thin()) return { requests: AHEAD_REQUESTS, bytes: Infinity };
    if (!this.fast()) return { requests: AHEAD_REQUESTS_MID, bytes: Infinity };
    if (this.h1() || !this.measured || !this.bw || !this.rtt) return { requests: AHEAD_REQUESTS, bytes: Infinity };
    return { requests: AHEAD_REQUESTS_MAX, bytes: Math.max(AHEAD_BYTES_MIN, Math.round(AHEAD_BDP * this.bw * this.rtt / 1000 / this.ratio())) };
  }
  /** background requests at once at most (within the bytes of backgroundBytes(), see mayStart) */
  maxBackground() { return this.bw === null && !this.fixed ? 2 : this.fast() ? 64 : 8; }
  /** bytes a demand read may fetch past what the game asked for (`cap`: the caller's own limit) */
  demandExtra(cap) { return this.bw === null ? (this.fixed ? cap : Math.min(cap, UNKNOWN_BG)) : Math.min(cap, Math.floor(this.bw * DEMAND_SECONDS / this.ratio())); }

  /**
   * A request starts: `kind` 'demand' (the game waits for it) or 'bg' — `reason` the background producer's (counted in
   * bgBy: which of them carried what). Returns its token for end().
   */
  begin(kind, bytes = 0, abort = null, range = null, reason = 'other') {
    const t = { kind, t0: this.now(), bytes, abort, range, tx: null, reason };
    this.inflight[kind]++;
    if (kind === 'bg' && this.loading()) t.inLoad = true; // (started during a load: see bgBy's inLoad)
    if (kind === 'bg') { this.reserved.shift(); this.bgFlights.add(t); } else this.demandFlights.add(t);
    return t;
  }
  /** The answer of request `t` began to arrive (its headers): its time to the first byte, the round trip (about). */
  firstByte(t) {
    const now = this.now(), ms = now - t.t0;
    if (t.tx === null) t.tx = now;
    if (ms >= 0) this.rtt = this.rtt === null ? ms : Math.min(this.rtt, ms);
  }
  /**
   * A request ended: `wire` bytes received (the encoded body), `raw` the bytes they decode to; ok false: failed or
   * aborted (its bytes are not counted).
   */
  end(t, wire, raw = wire, ok = true) {
    if (t.ended) return; t.ended = true;
    const now = this.now(), ms = now - t.t0;
    this.inflight[t.kind]--;
    if (t.kind === 'bg') this.bgFlights.delete(t); else this.demandFlights.delete(t);
    if (t.kind === 'demand') { this.lastDemandEnd = now; this.totals.demandMs += ms; }
    if (ok) {
      if (t.kind === 'demand') { this.totals.demandBytes += wire; this.totals.demandRequests++; } else {
        this.totals.bgBytes += wire; this.totals.bgRequests++;
        const r = (this.bgBy[t.reason] ??= { requests: 0, wire: 0, raw: 0, inLoad: 0 });
        r.requests++; r.wire += wire; r.raw += raw; if (t.inLoad) r.inLoad += wire;
      }
      this.totals.rawBytes += raw;
      // (the round trip from small answers only: a large one's time is mostly its transfer)
      if (wire <= RTT_BYTES) this.rtt = this.rtt === null ? ms : Math.min(this.rtt, ms);
      this.winBytes += wire;
      const a = t.tx ?? Math.min(now, t.t0 + (this.rtt ?? 0));
      this.winIntervals.push([a, now]);
      this.hist.push([a, now, wire]);
      this.sample(now);
    } else if (t.kind === 'bg') this.totals.abortedRequests++;
    this.kick();
  }
  /**
   * A bandwidth sample once the window (the answers ended since the last sample) holds enough: the wire bytes of the
   * answers ended within HORIZON_MS over the time bytes were arriving (the union of their transfer intervals: concurrent
   * answers count once, the waits for a first byte not at all). The time since the first answer still on its way began
   * to arrive is left out, and an answer that began before the horizon counts with its part inside it only (its bytes
   * pro rata): an answer still arriving shares the link without its bytes counted yet, and a long one that ends brings
   * its whole time back — either way the rate of a thin link carrying a long game read beside small background answers
   * read 4 times too low (85 KB/s measured as 20-35).
   */
  sample(now) {
    if (this.fixed) return;
    const busyOf = (iv) => {
      iv.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);
      let busy = 0, cs = -Infinity, ce = -Infinity;
      for (const [a, b] of iv) { if (a > ce) { if (ce > cs) busy += ce - cs; cs = a; ce = b; } else if (b > ce) ce = b; }
      if (ce > cs) busy += ce - cs;
      return busy;
    };
    const busy = busyOf(this.winIntervals.map(([a, b]) => [Math.max(a, this.winStart), b]));
    // (when nothing else is on its way — an answer ending now would count without its bytes — or the window is long)
    const idle = this.inflight.demand + this.inflight.bg === 0;
    const enough = busy >= 2000 || (idle && (busy >= 400 || (!this.measured && this.winBytes >= 48 << 10 && busy >= 20)));
    if (!enough) return;
    this.winBytes = 0; this.winIntervals = []; this.winStart = now;
    const lo = now - HORIZON_MS;
    while (this.hist.length && this.hist[0][1] <= lo) this.hist.shift();
    let hi = now;
    for (const set of [this.demandFlights, this.bgFlights]) for (const t of set) if (!t.ended) hi = Math.min(hi, t.tx ?? t.t0 + (this.rtt ?? 0));
    let bytes = 0; const iv = [];
    for (const [a, b, w] of this.hist) {
      const ca = Math.max(a, lo), cb = Math.min(b, hi);
      if (cb <= ca) continue;
      bytes += b > a ? w * (cb - ca) / (b - a) : w;
      iv.push([ca, cb]);
    }
    const span = busyOf(iv);
    if (span < (this.measured ? 300 : 20) || bytes <= 0) return;
    const s = bytes / span * 1000;
    this.bw = this.measured && this.bw ? this.bw * 0.6 + s * 0.4 : s;
    this.measured = true;
  }

  /**
   * Background requests in flight whose rest would hold a demand read up longer than BG_SECONDS (sized before the link
   * was measured, or the link slowed down) are aborted; the others finish (their bytes are not thrown away).
   */
  abortLong() {
    if (!this.bw) return;
    const now = this.now();
    for (const t of this.bgFlights) {
      if (!t.abort || !t.bytes || t.keep) continue;
      const left = this.secondsFor(t.bytes) - (now - t.t0) / 1000;
      if (left > BG_SECONDS * 1.5) { this.bgFlights.delete(t); t.abort(); }
    }
  }

  /**
   * A synchronous read of [start, end) of `key` (a file) is about to fetch it: background requests in flight for bytes
   * of that range are aborted (the worker cannot receive their answers while it waits: they would carry the same bytes
   * twice over the link at the same time).
   */
  abortOverlap(key, start, end) {
    for (const t of this.bgFlights) {
      const r = t.range;
      if (!t.abort || !r || r.key !== key || r.end <= start || r.start >= end) continue;
      this.bgFlights.delete(t); t.abort();
    }
  }

  /**
   * True when a background download of priority `quietMs` may start now: `urgent` (a parked read waits for it) at once;
   * while silenced() (a load) only one `forLoad` (what the load needs), by the same rules as outside a load.
   */
  mayStart(quietMs, urgent = false, bytes = 0, forLoad = false) {
    if (urgent) return true;
    const quiet = this.silenced();
    if (quiet && !forLoad) return false;
    const n = this.bgCount();
    if (n >= this.maxBackground()) return false;
    // (together the background requests carry about BG_SECONDS of the link: one at least)
    if (n > 0 && !this.fast() && this.bgBytes() + bytes > this.backgroundBytes()) return false;
    if (this.fast()) return quietMs <= 0 || this.inflight.demand === 0 && this.now() - this.lastDemandEnd >= quietMs;
    // (a thin link: the game's reads alone on it, then a quiet time; between thin and fast: beside them, the bytes in
    // flight — the game's and the background's — within about BG_SECONDS of the link: a game read waits at most that
    // long more, and the round trips of a run of small reads no longer leave the link idle)
    if (this.thin()) return this.inflight.demand === 0 && this.now() - this.lastDemandEnd >= quietMs;
    // (a load's own download larger than the bytes rule — queued before the load, at the size of a link then free —
    // goes when nothing else is on the link, or it would wait for the load to end, the load's next pieces behind it;
    // those queued during a load are small: requestBytes)
    return n + this.inflight.demand === 0 || this.bgBytes() + this.demandBytes() + bytes <= this.backgroundBytes();
  }
  /**
   * Wait for a background download's turn: `prio` orders the waiting ones (lower first), `quietMs` the time since the
   * game's last read it waits for (0 on a fast link: no wait). `w.urgent` set meanwhile (a parked read waits for this
   * download) lets it start at once. Resolves to true, or false once `stop()` holds.
   */
  // (`w.forLoad`: the download is what a load under way needs — it may start during the load, see mayStart)
  turn(prio, quietMs, stop = () => false, w = {}, bytes = 0) {
    w.bytes = bytes;
    if (this.tryTurn(quietMs, w)) return Promise.resolve(true);
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      Object.assign(w, { prio, quietMs, resolve, stop });
      this.waiters.push(w);
      this.waiters.sort((a, b) => (b.urgent ? 1 : 0) - (a.urgent ? 1 : 0) || a.prio - b.prio);
      this.kick();
    });
  }
  /** The turn of a background download that may start now (none waits before it): taken, true; else false. */
  tryTurn(quietMs, w = {}, bytes = w.bytes ?? 0) {
    if (this.waiters.length || !this.mayStart(quietMs, w.urgent, bytes, w.forLoad)) return false;
    this.reserved.push({ t: this.now(), bytes });
    return true;
  }
  /** Let the waiting downloads whose turn has come start (in priority order); wake up again when a quiet delay ends. */
  kick() {
    if (this.timer !== null) { this.clearTimer(this.timer); this.timer = null; }
    // (the stopped ones go first, wherever they wait)
    for (let i = 0; i < this.waiters.length; i++) { const w = this.waiters[i]; if (w.stop?.()) { this.waiters.splice(i--, 1); w.resolve(false); } }
    const quiet = this.silenced();
    for (let i = 0; i < this.waiters.length; i++) {
      const w = this.waiters[i];
      // (a load: the ones it does not need stay queued, out of the priority order meanwhile — the timer looks again)
      if (quiet && !w.urgent && !w.forLoad) continue;
      // (the request starts after this resolves: counted as in flight now so the next ones see it)
      if (this.mayStart(w.quietMs, w.urgent, w.bytes ?? 0, w.forLoad)) { this.waiters.splice(i--, 1); this.reserved.push({ t: this.now(), bytes: w.bytes ?? 0 }); w.resolve(true); continue; }
      if (!w.urgent) break; // (strict priority: a later one does not pass one that waits)
    }
    if (this.waiters.length) {
      const w = this.waiters[0];
      const due = Math.max(20, w.quietMs - (this.now() - this.lastDemandEnd));
      this.timer = this.setTimer(() => { this.timer = null; this.kick(); }, Math.min(due, 250));
    }
  }
  /**
   * The download `w` (see turn) is now what a load under way needs (an announced list names a predicted place's): it may
   * pass the load's silence and ranks at `prio` among the waiting ones — by the count and bytes rules still (mayStart),
   * not urgent as promote's.
   */
  forLoad(w, prio) {
    if (!w || w.forLoad) return;
    w.forLoad = true;
    if (this.waiters.includes(w)) { if (Number.isFinite(prio)) w.prio = Math.min(w.prio, prio); this.waiters.sort((a, b) => (b.urgent ? 1 : 0) - (a.urgent ? 1 : 0) || a.prio - b.prio); this.kick(); }
  }
  /** The waiting download `w` (see turn) is now waited for by the game: it goes first. */
  promote(w) {
    if (!w || w.urgent) return;
    w.urgent = true;
    if (this.waiters.includes(w)) { this.waiters.sort((a, b) => (b.urgent ? 1 : 0) - (a.urgent ? 1 : 0) || a.prio - b.prio); this.kick(); }
  }
  /** A snapshot for the page and the reports. */
  snapshot() {
    return { bw: this.bw === null ? null : Math.round(this.bw), measured: this.measured, rtt: this.rtt === null ? null : Math.round(this.rtt), demandInFlight: this.inflight.demand, bgInFlight: this.inflight.bg, waiting: this.waiters.length, loading: this.loading(), ...this.totals, bgBy: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(this.bgBy).map(([k, v]) => [k, { ...v }])) };
  }
}
```
