`src/vfs/node-backend.js`:

```js
// Node backend: a host directory exposed with case-insensitive lookup (Linux hosts are
// case-sensitive; Windows programs are not). Used by the Node test harness and the server.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

export class NodeBackend {
  /** @param {string} root @param {{ readOnly?: boolean }} [opts] */
  constructor(root, opts = {}) {
    this.root = path.resolve(root);
    this.readOnly = !!opts.readOnly;
    /** dir (host path) -> Map(lowercase name -> real name) */
    this.dirCache = new Map();
  }

  listDir(hostDir) {
    let m = this.dirCache.get(hostDir);
    if (m) return m;
    m = new Map();
    try { for (const n of fs.readdirSync(hostDir)) m.set(n.toLowerCase(), n); } catch { /* not a dir */ }
    this.dirCache.set(hostDir, m);
    return m;
  }

  /** Resolve a relative guest path (forward slashes) to a host path, case-insensitively. */
  hostPath(rel, { forCreate = false } = {}) {
    let cur = this.root;
    const segs = rel.split('/').filter(Boolean);
    for (let i = 0; i < segs.length; i++) {
      const m = this.listDir(cur);
      const real = m.get(segs[i].toLowerCase());
      if (real === undefined) {
        if (forCreate && i === segs.length - 1) return path.join(cur, segs[i]);
        return null;
      }
      cur = path.join(cur, real);
    }
    return cur;
  }

  stat(rel) {
    const hp = this.hostPath(rel);
    if (!hp) return null;
    try {
      const st = fs.statSync(hp);
      return { size: st.size, isDir: st.isDirectory(), mtime: st.mtimeMs };
    } catch { return null; }
  }

  readdir(rel) {
    const hp = this.hostPath(rel);
    if (!hp) return null;
    try {
      return fs.readdirSync(hp).map((name) => {
        try { const st = fs.statSync(path.join(hp, name)); return { name, size: st.size, isDir: st.isDirectory(), mtime: st.mtimeMs }; }
        catch { return { name, size: 0, isDir: false, mtime: 0 }; }
      });
    } catch { return null; }
  }

  open(rel, opts = {}) {
    let hp = this.hostPath(rel);
    if (!hp) {
      if (!opts.create || this.readOnly) return null;
      hp = this.hostPath(rel, { forCreate: true });
      if (!hp) return null;
      this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(hp));
    }
    const write = !!(opts.write || opts.create || opts.truncate) && !this.readOnly;
    try {
      const flags = write ? (fs.existsSync(hp) ? (opts.truncate ? 'w+' : 'r+') : 'w+') : 'r';
      const fd = fs.openSync(hp, flags);
      return new NodeFile(fd, write);
    } catch { return null; }
  }

  mkdir(rel) {
    if (this.readOnly) return false;
    const hp = this.hostPath(rel, { forCreate: true });
    if (!hp || fs.existsSync(hp)) return false;
    try { fs.mkdirSync(hp); this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(hp)); return true; } catch { return false; }
  }

  unlink(rel) {
    if (this.readOnly) return false;
    const hp = this.hostPath(rel);
    if (!hp) return false;
    try { fs.unlinkSync(hp); this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(hp)); return true; } catch { return false; }
  }

  /** Removes an empty folder (false otherwise). */
  rmdir(rel) {
    if (this.readOnly || !rel) return false;
    const hp = this.hostPath(rel);
    if (!hp || hp === this.root) return false;
    try { fs.rmdirSync(hp); this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(hp)); this.dirCache.delete(hp); return true; } catch { return false; }
  }

  rename(from, to) {
    if (this.readOnly) return false;
    const a = this.hostPath(from), b = this.hostPath(to, { forCreate: true });
    if (!a || !b) return false;
    try { fs.renameSync(a, b); this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(a)); this.dirCache.delete(path.dirname(b)); return true; } catch { return false; }
  }
}

class NodeFile {
  constructor(fd, write) { this.fd = fd; this.writable = write; }
  size() { return fs.fstatSync(this.fd).size; }
  read(off, len) {
    const buf = new Uint8Array(len);
    const n = fs.readSync(this.fd, buf, 0, len, off);
    return n === len ? buf : buf.subarray(0, n);
  }
  write(off, bytes) {
    if (!this.writable) return -1;
    return fs.writeSync(this.fd, bytes, 0, bytes.length, off);
  }
  truncate(len) { if (this.writable) fs.ftruncateSync(this.fd, len); }
  close() { try { fs.closeSync(this.fd); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
}

```

`src/vfs/opfs-store.js`:

```js
// Persistent block store for the HTTP game backend: file blocks fetched once are kept in the origin
// private file system (OPFS) and read back synchronously on later runs, so a game folder served over the
// network is downloaded once instead of at every launch (and a block needed in the middle of a match is a
// local read, not a synchronous round trip). One append-only data file plus an append-only index log, both through
// synchronous access handles (dedicated workers only). Keys carry the file size and mtime of the server
// listing: a changed file simply misses. Any storage error (quota, a second tab holding the handles)
// disables the store; the backend then keeps fetching over HTTP.
//
// Index format 3 (index.bin): an 8-byte header ('OBSI', u32 3) then records, each
//   u16 key length, u8 kind (1: block stored, 2: block dropped), u8 0, u32 offset low, u32 offset high, u32 length,
//   u32 block checksum, the key's UTF-8 bytes, u32 checksum of the record's previous bytes
// (little-endian). A later record of a key replaces the earlier one. Records are appended, never rewritten: the earlier
// format (index.json, { v: 2, entries: [[key, offset, length, checksum]] }) rewrote and synced the whole index every 16
// blocks — 2.7 s of the game thread over a BFME2 first launch. Records wait in memory and are written (and the index
// flushed) at a sync point: once >= 2 s passed since the last one or >= 256 records wait, and when the caller forces it
// (prefetch end, stop, close). A crash loses at most the records of the last sync interval: those blocks are fetched
// again. Reading stops at the first incomplete or damaged record (the log is cut there).
// The data file is flushed only at close: its flush writes back every block written since the last one (~4 ms of the
// game thread per MiB, 2.2 s over a first launch's prefetch, whatever the cadence). An indexed block whose bytes a
// crash lost is caught by its checksum at read (or lies past the end of the data file) and fetched again.
const INDEX_MAGIC = 0x4953424f; // 'OBSI'
const INDEX_VERSION = 3;
const HEADER_BYTES = 8, RECORD_FIXED = 20;
const REC_PUT = 1, REC_DROP = 2;
/** sync cadence of the index: at most every SYNC_MS (unless forced), sooner once SYNC_BLOCKS records wait */
export const SYNC_MS = 2000, SYNC_BLOCKS = 256;

/**
 * A 32-bit checksum of a block (multiply-xor over 32-bit words, then the tail bytes, then the length): ~1 ms for 1 MiB,
 * to catch a stored block that does not read back as written.
 */
export function blockHash(bytes) {
  let h = 0x811c9dc5 ^ bytes.length;
  const words = bytes.byteOffset % 4 === 0 ? new Uint32Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.length >>> 2) : new Uint32Array(bytes.slice(0, bytes.length & ~3).buffer);
  for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i++) { h = Math.imul(h ^ words[i], 0x9e3779b1); h ^= h >>> 15; }
  for (let i = bytes.length & ~3; i < bytes.length; i++) { h = Math.imul(h ^ bytes[i], 0x85ebca6b); h ^= h >>> 13; }
  return (h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0;
}

const enc = new TextEncoder(), dec = new TextDecoder();

/** The index log's bytes for `records` ([kind, key, offset, length, checksum]), preceded by the header when `header`. */
export function encodeIndex(records, header = false) {
  const keys = records.map((r) => enc.encode(r[1]));
  let n = header ? HEADER_BYTES : 0;
  for (const k of keys) n += RECORD_FIXED + k.length + 4;
  const out = new Uint8Array(n), dv = new DataView(out.buffer);
  let p = 0;
  if (header) { dv.setUint32(0, INDEX_MAGIC, true); dv.setUint32(4, INDEX_VERSION, true); p = HEADER_BYTES; }
  for (let i = 0; i < records.length; i++) {
    const [kind, , off, len, h] = records[i], k = keys[i], at = p;
    dv.setUint16(p, k.length, true); out[p + 2] = kind; out[p + 3] = 0;
    dv.setUint32(p + 4, off >>> 0, true); dv.setUint32(p + 8, Math.floor(off / 0x100000000), true);
    dv.setUint32(p + 12, len >>> 0, true); dv.setUint32(p + 16, h >>> 0, true);
    out.set(k, p + RECORD_FIXED); p += RECORD_FIXED + k.length;
    dv.setUint32(p, blockHash(out.subarray(at, p)), true); p += 4;
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Replay an index log into `map` (key -> [offset, length, checksum]). Returns the byte length of its valid part (up to
 * the last complete, undamaged record), or -1 when the header is not this format's.
 */
export function decodeIndex(buf, map) {
  if (buf.length < HEADER_BYTES) return -1;
  const dv = new DataView(buf.buffer, buf.byteOffset, buf.length);
  if (dv.getUint32(0, true) !== INDEX_MAGIC || dv.getUint32(4, true) !== INDEX_VERSION) return -1;
  let p = HEADER_BYTES;
  while (p + RECORD_FIXED + 4 <= buf.length) {
    const kl = dv.getUint16(p, true), kind = buf[p + 2], end = p + RECORD_FIXED + kl;
    if (end + 4 > buf.length) break;
    if (dv.getUint32(end, true) !== blockHash(buf.subarray(p, end))) break;
    const key = dec.decode(buf.subarray(p + RECORD_FIXED, end));
    if (kind === REC_PUT) map.set(key, [dv.getUint32(p + 4, true) + dv.getUint32(p + 8, true) * 0x100000000, dv.getUint32(p + 12, true), dv.getUint32(p + 16, true)]);
    else if (kind === REC_DROP) map.delete(key);
    else break;
    p = end + 4;
  }
  return p;
}

export class OpfsBlockStore {
  /**
   * @param {FileSystemSyncAccessHandle} data
   * @param {FileSystemSyncAccessHandle} index the index log (format 3), its valid part `indexEnd` bytes long
   * @param {Map<string, [number, number, number]>} map key -> [offset, length, checksum]
   */
  constructor(data, index, map, indexEnd = index.getSize()) {
    this.data = data; this.indexHandle = index; this.map = map;
    this.end = data.getSize();
    this.indexEnd = indexEnd;
    /** @type {Array<[number, string, number, number, number]>} index records not written yet */
    this.pending = [];
    this.lastSync = performance.now();
    this.failed = false;
    this.stats = { hits: 0, puts: 0, bytes: 0 };
  }

  /** Index records waiting for the next sync point. */
  get dirty() { return this.pending.length; }

  /** Open (or create) the store in OPFS directory `name`; null when OPFS or sync handles are unavailable. */
  static async open(name) {
    try {
      const root = await navigator.storage.getDirectory();
      const dir = await root.getDirectoryHandle(name, { create: true });
      const data = await (await dir.getFileHandle('blocks.bin', { create: true })).createSyncAccessHandle();
      let index;
      try { index = await (await dir.getFileHandle('index.bin', { create: true })).createSyncAccessHandle(); } catch (e) { data.close(); throw e; }
      try {
        const map = new Map();
        let reset = null, migrated = false, end = -1, cut = 0;
        // an index of the earlier format (index.json): read once (when there is no log yet), rewritten as a log, removed
        let old = null;
        try { old = await dir.getFileHandle('index.json'); } catch { /* none */ }
        const n = index.getSize();
        if (n > 0) {
          const buf = new Uint8Array(n); index.read(buf, { at: 0 });
          end = decodeIndex(buf, map);
          if (end < 0) reset = 'unreadable index'; else cut = n - end;
        } else if (old) {
          const h = await old.createSyncAccessHandle();
          try {
            const m = h.getSize();
            const buf = new Uint8Array(m); if (m) h.read(buf, { at: 0 });
            if (!m) { if (data.getSize() > 0) reset = 'no index'; } // (created, never written)
            else try {
              const j = JSON.parse(dec.decode(buf));
              if (j && j.v === 2 && Array.isArray(j.entries)) { for (const [k, off, len, hh] of j.entries) map.set(k, [off, len, hh]); migrated = true; }
              else reset = 'an earlier format without block checksums';
            } catch { reset = 'unreadable index'; }
          } finally { h.close(); }
        } else if (data.getSize() > 0) reset = 'no index';
        // a store of an earlier format (no checksums) or with an unreadable index starts over, its data file emptied
        if (reset) { map.clear(); data.truncate(0); }
        // entries past the end of the data file (its tail lost in a crash while their index records were synced) are
        // dropped — and the log rewritten without them: blocks appended later fill that range again, where the stale
        // records would come back as entries pointing into other blocks' bytes
        const size = data.getSize();
        let pastEnd = 0;
        for (const [k, [off, len]] of map) if (off + len > size) { map.delete(k); pastEnd++; }
        if (end < 0 || reset || migrated || pastEnd) {
          // a new log: the header and every entry, as one write
          const bytes = encodeIndex([...map].map(([k, [off, len, h]]) => [REC_PUT, k, off, len, h]), true);
          index.truncate(0); index.write(bytes, { at: 0 }); index.flush(); end = bytes.length;
        } else if (cut > 0) { index.truncate(end); index.flush(); } // (an incomplete or damaged tail: the log is cut there)
        if (old) { try { await dir.removeEntry('index.json'); } catch { /* left behind: ignored once the log exists */ } }
        const store = new OpfsBlockStore(data, index, map, end);
        store.resetReason = reset;
        store.migrated = migrated;
        store.indexCut = cut;
        store.pastEnd = pastEnd;
        return store;
      } catch (e) { data.close(); index.close(); throw e; }
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  /**
   * The stored bytes of `key`, or null. Their checksum is verified: a block that does not match what was written (a
   * damaged or misplaced write, whatever the cause) is dropped and reported (stats.corrupt, onCorrupt), the caller then
   * fetches it again.
   */
  get(key) {
    if (this.failed) return null;
    const e = this.map.get(key);
    if (!e) return null;
    const out = new Uint8Array(e[1]);
    try { if (this.data.read(out, { at: e[0] }) !== e[1]) return null; } catch { this.fail(); return null; }
    if (blockHash(out) !== e[2]) {
      this.drop(key);
      this.stats.corrupt = (this.stats.corrupt ?? 0) + 1;
      this.onCorrupt?.(key);
      return null;
    }
    this.stats.hits++;
    return out;
  }

  /** Append `bytes` under `key` (ignored when the store has failed). */
  put(key, bytes) {
    if (this.failed || this.map.has(key)) return;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    try {
      const n = this.data.write(bytes, { at: this.end });
      if (n !== bytes.length) { this.fail(); return; }
      const h = blockHash(bytes);
      this.map.set(key, [this.end, n, h]);
      this.pending.push([REC_PUT, key, this.end, n, h]);
      this.end += n;
      this.stats.puts++; this.stats.bytes += n;
      this.flush();
    } catch { this.fail(); }
    this.stats.putMs = (this.stats.putMs ?? 0) + performance.now() - t0;
  }

  /**
   * A sync point: the waiting index records appended and the index flushed — when `force`, once SYNC_MS passed since the
   * last one, or once SYNC_BLOCKS records wait; otherwise nothing (cheap to call often). The data file is not flushed
   * (see the top of this file).
   */
  flush(force = false) {
    if (this.failed || !this.pending.length) return;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    if (!force && this.pending.length < SYNC_BLOCKS && t0 - this.lastSync < SYNC_MS) return;
    this.stats.flushes = (this.stats.flushes ?? 0) + 1;
    try {
      const bytes = encodeIndex(this.pending);
      if (this.indexHandle.write(bytes, { at: this.indexEnd }) !== bytes.length) this.fail();
      else {
        this.indexHandle.flush();
        this.indexEnd += bytes.length;
        this.pending = [];
      }
    } catch { this.fail(); }
    this.lastSync = performance.now();
    this.stats.flushMs = (this.stats.flushMs ?? 0) + this.lastSync - t0;
  }

  /** Forget `key` (a block found unusable by the reader): fetched and stored again. */
  drop(key) {
    const e = this.map.get(key);
    if (!e) return;
    this.map.delete(key);
    this.pending.push([REC_DROP, key, e[0], e[1], e[2]]);
  }

  fail() { this.failed = true; }

  close() { try { this.data.flush(); this.flush(true); this.data.close(); this.indexHandle.close(); } catch { /* already closed */ } }
}

/**
 * The block store's interface in memory, up to `maxBytes` (then new blocks are dropped): pages without OPFS and
 * harness runs measuring the prefetch without a persistent profile.
 */
export class MemBlockStore {
  constructor(maxBytes = 1 << 30) { this.map = new Map(); this.bytes = 0; this.max = maxBytes; this.failed = false; this.stats = { hits: 0, puts: 0, bytes: 0 }; }
  get(key) { const b = this.map.get(key); if (b) this.stats.hits++; return b ?? null; }
  put(key, bytes) { if (this.map.has(key) || this.bytes + bytes.length > this.max) return; this.map.set(key, bytes.slice()); this.bytes += bytes.length; this.stats.puts++; this.stats.bytes += bytes.length; }
  drop(key) { const b = this.map.get(key); if (b) { this.map.delete(key); this.bytes -= b.length; } }
  flush() {}
  close() {}
}
```

`src/vfs/overlay-backend.js`:

```js
// Read-only union of installed game layers, in priority order.
import { NodeBackend } from './node-backend.js';

export class OverlayBackend {
  constructor(roots) { this.layers = roots.map((root) => new NodeBackend(root, { readOnly: true })); }
  stat(rel) { for (const layer of this.layers) { const st = layer.stat(rel); if (st) return st; } return null; }
  readdir(rel) {
    const entries = new Map(); let found = false;
    for (const layer of this.layers) {
      const list = layer.readdir(rel);
      if (!list) continue;
      found = true;
      for (const entry of list) if (!entries.has(entry.name.toLowerCase())) entries.set(entry.name.toLowerCase(), entry);
    }
    return found ? [...entries.values()] : null;
  }
  open(rel, opts = {}) {
    if (opts.write || opts.create || opts.truncate) return null;
    for (const layer of this.layers) { const file = layer.open(rel); if (file) return file; }
    return null;
  }
  mkdir() { return false; }
  unlink() { return false; }
  rename() { return false; }
}
```

`src/vfs/pcm-codec.js`:

```js
// Lossless PCM transport codec (docs/slow-network.md "Audio units"): a range of a game file whose bytes are, wholly or
// in part, uncompressed PCM sound (8-bit unsigned or 16-bit signed little-endian, mono or stereo), coded by linear
// prediction and Rice codes of the residuals — what brotli cannot see in sampled sound (it finds repeated strings, a
// waveform has almost none: sounds at 0.88-0.95 of their bytes) —, byte-exact. The server makes such units in the
// background beside its brotli ones (src/host/br-cache.js, src/host/pcm-units.js) and sends one to a request that says
// it decodes them; the shared reader decodes it (HttpBackend.decodeUnit, src/vfs/http-backend.js) before any byte
// reaches the game. Written from scratch for Orthros.
//
// Container (little-endian): 'OPC1', u32 decoded length, u32 CRC-32 of the decoded bytes, u16 segment count, then per
// segment u8 kind (0 bytes as they are, 1 PCM), u8 bits (8 | 16), u8 channels (1 | 2), u8 log2 of its frame (PCM; 0),
// u32 decoded length; then
// each segment's payload: the bytes themselves, or u32 coded length + the coded samples. A PCM segment's length is a
// whole number of sample frames.
//
// Coded samples (bits read most significant first): frames of the segment's sample frames (the last one shorter); a stereo
// frame starts with 2 bits — 0 left/right, 1 left/side, 2 side/right, 3 mid/side (side = left − right, mid = (left +
// right) >> 1) —; then one subframe per channel, its samples `w` bits wide (the segment's bits, one more for the side):
// 6 bits of type — 0-4 fixed polynomial predictor of that order, 5 verbatim, 6 constant, 8 + n − 1 linear predictor of
// order n (1-32) —; constant: one w-bit value; verbatim: every sample in w bits; a predictor: its first `order` samples
// in w bits, for a linear one 4 bits (coefficients' precision − 1), 5 bits (shift) and its coefficients (signed, that
// precision), then the residuals: 4 bits of partition order p (2^p partitions, the first one `order` samples shorter),
// per partition 5 bits of Rice parameter k — or 31: 5 bits of width then each residual in that width — and its
// residuals zigzagged (0, −1, 1, −2 … → 0, 1, 2, 3 …), each as q = u >> k zeros, a one, and u's k low bits.
// A prediction is floor(Σ cᵢ·xₙ₋ᵢ / 2^shift), the sum exact (below 2^53: doubles).

import { crc32 } from '../core/crc32.js';

export const PCM_MAGIC = 0x3143504f; // 'OPC1'
/** sample frames per frame (by default: a segment says its own, as the log2 of it, 64-65536) */
export const FRAME = 2048;
const MAX_LPC = 12;
const T_VERBATIM = 5, T_CONSTANT = 6, T_LPC = 8;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ bits
class BitWriter {
  constructor(n = 1 << 16) { this.buf = new Uint8Array(n); this.len = 0; this.acc = 0; this.nacc = 0; }
  grow(n) { if (this.len + n > this.buf.length) { const b = new Uint8Array(Math.max(this.buf.length * 2, this.len + n + 1024)); b.set(this.buf.subarray(0, this.len)); this.buf = b; } }
  /** the n low bits of v (n ≤ 24) */
  put(v, n) {
    if (n === 0) return;
    this.acc = (this.acc << n) | (v & ((1 << n) - 1)); this.nacc += n;
    if (this.nacc >= 8) {
      this.grow(4);
      while (this.nacc >= 8) { this.nacc -= 8; this.buf[this.len++] = (this.acc >>> this.nacc) & 0xff; }
      this.acc &= (1 << this.nacc) - 1;
    }
  }
  /** n bits of v, n ≤ 32 */
  putLong(v, n) { if (n > 24) { this.put(Math.floor(v / 0x10000) & 0xffff, n - 16); this.put(v & 0xffff, 16); } else this.put(v, n); }
  zeros(q) { while (q >= 24) { this.put(0, 24); q -= 24; } this.put(0, q); }
  /** the bytes, the last one padded with zero bits */
  end() { if (this.nacc) { this.grow(1); this.buf[this.len++] = (this.acc << (8 - this.nacc)) & 0xff; this.acc = 0; this.nacc = 0; } return this.buf.subarray(0, this.len); }
}

class BitReader {
  /** b: padded with 8 zero bytes past `end` */
  constructor(b, end) { this.b = b; this.pos = 0; this.end = end * 8; }
  /** the 32 bits from pos */
  peek() {
    const b = this.b, i = this.pos >>> 3, s = this.pos & 7;
    const hi = (b[i] << 24) | (b[i + 1] << 16) | (b[i + 2] << 8) | b[i + 3];
    return s ? ((hi << s) | (b[i + 4] >>> (8 - s))) >>> 0 : hi >>> 0;
  }
  /** n bits unsigned (1 ≤ n ≤ 32) */
  bits(n) { const v = this.peek() >>> (32 - n); this.pos += n; if (this.pos > this.end) throw new Error('pcm: coded samples cut short'); return n === 32 ? v >>> 0 : v; }
  /** n bits two's complement (1 ≤ n ≤ 32) */
  signed(n) { const v = this.peek(); this.pos += n; if (this.pos > this.end) throw new Error('pcm: coded samples cut short'); return (v | 0) >> (32 - n); }
}

const zig = (r) => (r >= 0 ? 2 * r : -2 * r - 1);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ prediction
/** residuals of fixed predictor `order` over x[order, n) into r (r[i] for sample i) */
function fixedResidual(x, n, order, r) {
  switch (order) {
    case 0: for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) r[i] = x[i]; break;
    case 1: for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) r[i] = x[i] - x[i - 1]; break;
    case 2: for (let i = 2; i < n; i++) r[i] = x[i] - 2 * x[i - 1] + x[i - 2]; break;
    case 3: for (let i = 3; i < n; i++) r[i] = x[i] - 3 * x[i - 1] + 3 * x[i - 2] - x[i - 3]; break;
    case 4: for (let i = 4; i < n; i++) r[i] = x[i] - 4 * x[i - 1] + 6 * x[i - 2] - 4 * x[i - 3] + x[i - 4]; break;
  }
}
function fixedRestore(x, n, order, r) {
  switch (order) {
    case 0: for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] = r[i]; break;
    case 1: for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) x[i] = r[i] + x[i - 1]; break;
    case 2: for (let i = 2; i < n; i++) x[i] = r[i] + 2 * x[i - 1] - x[i - 2]; break;
    case 3: for (let i = 3; i < n; i++) x[i] = r[i] + 3 * x[i - 1] - 3 * x[i - 2] + x[i - 3]; break;
    case 4: for (let i = 4; i < n; i++) x[i] = r[i] + 4 * x[i - 1] - 6 * x[i - 2] + 4 * x[i - 3] - x[i - 4]; break;
  }
}
function lpcResidual(x, n, c, order, shift, r) {
  const k = 2 ** -shift;
  for (let i = order; i < n; i++) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < order; j++) s += c[j] * x[i - 1 - j];
    r[i] = x[i] - Math.floor(s * k);
  }
}
function lpcRestore(x, n, c, order, shift, r) {
  const k = 2 ** -shift;
  if (order === 12) { // (the encoder's usual order: unrolled)
    const c0 = c[0], c1 = c[1], c2 = c[2], c3 = c[3], c4 = c[4], c5 = c[5], c6 = c[6], c7 = c[7], c8 = c[8], c9 = c[9], c10 = c[10], c11 = c[11];
    for (let i = 12; i < n; i++) {
      const s = c0 * x[i - 1] + c1 * x[i - 2] + c2 * x[i - 3] + c3 * x[i - 4] + c4 * x[i - 5] + c5 * x[i - 6] + c6 * x[i - 7] + c7 * x[i - 8] + c8 * x[i - 9] + c9 * x[i - 10] + c10 * x[i - 11] + c11 * x[i - 12];
      x[i] = r[i] + Math.floor(s * k);
    }
    return;
  }
  for (let i = order; i < n; i++) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < order; j++) s += c[j] * x[i - 1 - j];
    x[i] = r[i] + Math.floor(s * k);
  }
}

/** linear prediction coefficients of orders 1..maxOrder (Levinson-Durbin over a Welch-windowed autocorrelation): lpc[o-1] */
function lpcCoefs(x, n, maxOrder) {
  const w = new Float64Array(n), h = (n - 1) / 2;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const t = (i - h) / (h + 1); w[i] = x[i] * (1 - t * t); }
  const R = new Float64Array(maxOrder + 1);
  for (let l = 0; l <= maxOrder; l++) { let s = 0; for (let i = l; i < n; i++) s += w[i] * w[i - l]; R[l] = s; }
  if (!(R[0] > 0)) return null;
  R[0] *= 1 + 1e-9; // (a little white noise: a stable recursion on pure tones)
  const out = [], a = new Float64Array(maxOrder + 1), tmp = new Float64Array(maxOrder + 1);
  let err = R[0];
  for (let o = 1; o <= maxOrder; o++) {
    let acc = R[o];
    for (let j = 1; j < o; j++) acc -= a[j] * R[o - j];
    const k = acc / err;
    tmp.set(a);
    a[o] = k;
    for (let j = 1; j < o; j++) a[j] = tmp[j] - k * tmp[o - j];
    err *= 1 - k * k;
    out.push(Array.from(a.subarray(1, o + 1)));
    if (!(err > 0)) break;
  }
  return out;
}
/** coefficients quantized to `precision` bits: { c: Int32 array, shift } or null */
function quantize(a, precision) {
  let max = 0; for (const v of a) max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(v));
  if (!(max > 0)) return null;
  const lim = 2 ** (precision - 1) - 1;
  let shift = precision - 1 - Math.ceil(Math.log2(max + 1e-12));
  shift = Math.max(0, Math.min(31, shift));
  while (shift > 0 && Math.round(max * 2 ** shift) > lim) shift--;
  const c = new Int32Array(a.length);
  let e = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { // (the rounding error carried: FLAC's way)
    const v = a[i] * 2 ** shift + e, q = Math.max(-lim - 1, Math.min(lim, Math.round(v)));
    e = v - q; c[i] = q;
  }
  return { c, shift };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ residual coding
const PARTITION_MAX = 6;
/** bits of the best Rice coding of r[from, to) and its parameter (31: escape) */
function riceBest(r, from, to) {
  const n = to - from; if (n <= 0) return { bits: 5, k: 0 };
  let sum = 0, maxU = 0;
  for (let i = from; i < to; i++) { const u = zig(r[i]); sum += u; if (u > maxU) maxU = u; }
  const mean = sum / n;
  let k0 = mean > 1 ? Math.floor(Math.log2(mean)) : 0, best = null;
  for (let k = Math.max(0, k0 - 1); k <= Math.min(30, k0 + 1); k++) {
    let bits = 5 + n * (k + 1);
    const d = 2 ** k;
    for (let i = from; i < to; i++) bits += Math.floor(zig(r[i]) / d);
    if (!best || bits < best.bits) best = { bits, k };
  }
  const width = maxU ? 32 - Math.clz32(maxU) + 1 : 1; // (two's complement of the residual: one bit more than |r|)
  const esc = 10 + n * Math.min(32, width);
  return esc < best.bits ? { bits: esc, k: 31, width: Math.min(32, width) } : best;
}
/** the best partitioning of residuals r[order, n): { bits, p, parts: [{ k, width }] } */
function residualPlan(r, n, order) {
  let best = null;
  for (let p = 0; p <= PARTITION_MAX; p++) {
    if (n % (1 << p) || (n >> p) <= order) break;
    const size = n >> p, parts = [];
    let bits = 4;
    for (let i = 0; i < 1 << p; i++) {
      const from = i === 0 ? order : i * size, b = riceBest(r, from, (i + 1) * size);
      bits += b.bits; parts.push(b);
    }
    if (!best || bits < best.bits) best = { bits, p, parts };
  }
  return best;
}
function writeResidual(bw, r, n, order, plan) {
  bw.put(plan.p, 4);
  const size = n >> plan.p;
  for (let i = 0; i < 1 << plan.p; i++) {
    const { k, width } = plan.parts[i], from = i === 0 ? order : i * size, to = (i + 1) * size;
    bw.put(k, 5);
    if (k === 31) { bw.put(width - 1, 5); for (let j = from; j < to; j++) bw.putLong(r[j] >>> 0, width); continue; }
    const d = 2 ** k;
    for (let j = from; j < to; j++) {
      const u = zig(r[j]), q = Math.floor(u / d);
      bw.zeros(q); bw.put(1, 1);
      if (k) bw.putLong(u - q * d, k);
    }
  }
}
function readResidual(br, r, n, order) {
  const p = br.bits(4), size = n >> p;
  if (n % (1 << p) || size < order) throw new Error('pcm: bad partition');
  for (let i = 0; i < 1 << p; i++) {
    const from = i === 0 ? order : i * size, to = (i + 1) * size, k = br.bits(5);
    if (k === 31) { const w = br.bits(5) + 1; for (let j = from; j < to; j++) r[j] = br.signed(w); continue; }
    // (the hot loop: the reader's state in locals, its 32-bit window read inline)
    const b = br.b, end = br.end, ks = 32 - k;
    let pos = br.pos;
    for (let j = from; j < to; j++) {
      let q = 0, w;
      for (;;) {
        const i = pos >>> 3, s = pos & 7;
        w = (b[i] << 24) | (b[i + 1] << 16) | (b[i + 2] << 8) | b[i + 3];
        if (s) w = (w << s) | (b[i + 4] >>> (8 - s));
        if (w !== 0) break;
        q += 32; pos += 32;
        if (pos > end) throw new Error('pcm: coded samples cut short');
      }
      const z = Math.clz32(w); q += z; pos += z + 1;
      // (u below 2^31 in a valid stream: the encoder escapes larger residuals; a corrupt one fails the CRC)
      let u = q;
      if (k) {
        const i = pos >>> 3, s = pos & 7;
        let v = (b[i] << 24) | (b[i + 1] << 16) | (b[i + 2] << 8) | b[i + 3];
        if (s) v = (v << s) | (b[i + 4] >>> (8 - s));
        u = (q << k) | (v >>> ks); pos += k;
      }
      r[j] = (u >>> 1) ^ -(u & 1);
    }
    if (pos > end) throw new Error('pcm: coded samples cut short');
    br.pos = pos;
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ subframes
/** the cheapest coding of x[0, n) at width w: { bits, write(bw) } */
function planSubframe(x, n, w, r) {
  let constant = true; for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) if (x[i] !== x[0]) { constant = false; break; }
  if (constant) return { bits: 6 + w, write: (bw) => { bw.put(T_CONSTANT, 6); bw.putLong(x[0] >>> 0, w); } };
  let best = { bits: 6 + n * w, write: (bw) => { bw.put(T_VERBATIM, 6); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) bw.putLong(x[i] >>> 0, w); } };
  // fixed predictors: the one with the smallest residual magnitude, then coded exactly
  let fo = 0, fs = Infinity;
  for (let o = 0; o <= 4 && o < n; o++) {
    fixedResidual(x, n, o, r);
    let s = 0; for (let i = o; i < n; i++) s += Math.abs(r[i]);
    s /= Math.max(1, n - o);
    if (s < fs) { fs = s; fo = o; }
  }
  {
    const o = fo;
    fixedResidual(x, n, o, r);
    const plan = residualPlan(r, n, o);
    if (plan) {
      const bits = 6 + o * w + plan.bits;
      if (bits < best.bits) { const rr = r.slice(0, n); best = { bits, write: (bw) => { bw.put(o, 6); for (let i = 0; i < o; i++) bw.putLong(x[i] >>> 0, w); writeResidual(bw, rr, n, o, plan); } }; }
    }
  }
  // linear predictors
  if (n > 32) {
    const sets = lpcCoefs(x, n, Math.min(MAX_LPC, n >> 3));
    const precision = w <= 9 ? 12 : 14;
    if (sets) for (const o of [2, 4, 8, 12]) {
      if (o > sets.length) break;
      const q = quantize(sets[o - 1], precision); if (!q) continue;
      lpcResidual(x, n, q.c, o, q.shift, r);
      let ok = true; for (let i = o; i < n; i++) if (Math.abs(r[i]) >= 2 ** 30) { ok = false; break; }
      if (!ok) continue;
      const plan = residualPlan(r, n, o); if (!plan) continue;
      const bits = 6 + o * w + 9 + o * precision + plan.bits;
      if (bits < best.bits) {
        const rr = r.slice(0, n), { c, shift } = q;
        best = { bits, write: (bw) => { bw.put(T_LPC + o - 1, 6); for (let i = 0; i < o; i++) bw.putLong(x[i] >>> 0, w); bw.put(precision - 1, 4); bw.put(shift, 5); for (let i = 0; i < o; i++) bw.putLong(c[i] >>> 0, precision); writeResidual(bw, rr, n, o, plan); } };
      }
    }
  }
  return best;
}
function readSubframe(br, x, n, w, r) {
  const t = br.bits(6);
  if (t === T_CONSTANT) { const v = br.signed(w); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] = v; return; }
  if (t === T_VERBATIM) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] = br.signed(w); return; }
  if (t <= 4) {
    if (t > n) throw new Error('pcm: bad order');
    for (let i = 0; i < t; i++) x[i] = br.signed(w);
    readResidual(br, r, n, t); fixedRestore(x, n, t, r); return;
  }
  if (t < T_LPC) throw new Error('pcm: bad subframe');
  const o = t - T_LPC + 1; if (o > n) throw new Error('pcm: bad order');
  for (let i = 0; i < o; i++) x[i] = br.signed(w);
  const precision = br.bits(4) + 1, shift = br.bits(5), c = new Float64Array(o);
  for (let i = 0; i < o; i++) c[i] = br.signed(precision);
  readResidual(br, r, n, o); lpcRestore(x, n, c, o, shift, r);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ segments
/** the samples of PCM bytes b[at, at + len): one Float64Array per channel (8-bit unsigned centred on 0) */
function samplesOf(b, at, len, bits, ch) {
  const bps = bits >> 3, frames = Math.floor(len / (bps * ch)), out = [];
  for (let c = 0; c < ch; c++) out.push(new Float64Array(frames));
  for (let f = 0, p = at; f < frames; f++) for (let c = 0; c < ch; c++, p += bps) out[c][f] = bits === 8 ? b[p] - 128 : (b[p] | (b[p + 1] << 8)) << 16 >> 16;
  return out;
}

/** PCM bytes coded (see the header) */
function encodeSamples(b, at, len, bits, ch, FRAME) {
  const chans = samplesOf(b, at, len, bits, ch), frames = chans[0].length, bw = new BitWriter(len + 64);
  const r = new Float64Array(FRAME), xs = [new Float64Array(FRAME), new Float64Array(FRAME), new Float64Array(FRAME), new Float64Array(FRAME)];
  for (let f0 = 0; f0 < frames; f0 += FRAME) {
    const n = Math.min(FRAME, frames - f0);
    if (ch === 1) { xs[0].set(chans[0].subarray(f0, f0 + n)); planSubframe(xs[0], n, bits, r).write(bw); continue; }
    const L = chans[0].subarray(f0, f0 + n), R = chans[1].subarray(f0, f0 + n);
    const [l, rr, s, m] = xs;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { l[i] = L[i]; rr[i] = R[i]; s[i] = L[i] - R[i]; m[i] = Math.floor((L[i] + R[i]) / 2); }
    const pl = planSubframe(l, n, bits, r), pr = planSubframe(rr, n, bits, r), ps = planSubframe(s, n, bits + 1, r), pm = planSubframe(m, n, bits, r);
    const modes = [[pl, pr], [pl, ps], [ps, pr], [pm, ps]];
    let bi = 0; for (let i = 1; i < 4; i++) if (modes[i][0].bits + modes[i][1].bits < modes[bi][0].bits + modes[bi][1].bits) bi = i;
    bw.put(bi, 2); modes[bi][0].write(bw); modes[bi][1].write(bw);
  }
  return bw.end();
}
function decodeSamples(coded, out, at, len, bits, ch, FRAME) {
  const pad = new Uint8Array(coded.length + 8); pad.set(coded);
  const br = new BitReader(pad, coded.length), bps = bits >> 3, frames = len / (bps * ch);
  const r = new Float64Array(FRAME), a = new Float64Array(FRAME), b2 = new Float64Array(FRAME);
  for (let f0 = 0; f0 < frames; f0 += FRAME) {
    const n = Math.min(FRAME, frames - f0);
    let L = a, R = b2;
    if (ch === 1) readSubframe(br, a, n, bits, r);
    else {
      const mode = br.bits(2);
      readSubframe(br, a, n, mode === 2 ? bits + 1 : bits, r);
      readSubframe(br, b2, n, mode === 0 ? bits : mode === 2 ? bits : bits + 1, r);
      if (mode === 1) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) b2[i] = a[i] - b2[i]; // left, side → left, right
      else if (mode === 2) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = a[i] + b2[i]; // side, right → left, right
      else if (mode === 3) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const s = b2[i], mm = a[i] * 2 + (s & 1); a[i] = (mm + s) / 2; b2[i] = (mm - s) / 2; }
      L = a; R = b2;
    }
    let p = at + f0 * bps * ch;
    if (ch === 1 && bits === 16) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++, p += 2) { const v = L[i]; out[p] = v; out[p + 1] = v >> 8; }
    else if (ch === 1) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out[p++] = L[i] + 128;
    else if (bits === 16) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++, p += 4) { const v = L[i], w = R[i]; out[p] = v; out[p + 1] = v >> 8; out[p + 2] = w; out[p + 3] = w >> 8; }
    else for (let i = 0; i < n; i++, p += 2) { out[p] = L[i] + 128; out[p + 1] = R[i] + 128; }
  }
}

/**
 * Bytes b coded: `regions` [{ at, len, bits: 8 | 16, ch: 1 | 2 }] the PCM parts (sorted, not overlapping, inside b);
 * the rest goes as it is. Returns the container.
 */
export function encodePcm(b, regions, { frame: fl = FRAME } = {}) {
  const segs = [], payloads = [];
  let pos = 0;
  const raw = (to) => { if (to > pos) { segs.push([0, 0, 0, to - pos, 0]); payloads.push(b.subarray(pos, to)); pos = to; } };
  for (const g of regions) {
    const frame = (g.bits >> 3) * g.ch, at = Math.max(g.at, pos), len = Math.floor((Math.min(b.length, g.at + g.len) - at) / frame) * frame;
    if (len < frame * 64 || (at - g.at) % frame) continue; // (too short to gain anything, or cut inside a frame)
    raw(at);
    const coded = encodeSamples(b, at, len, g.bits, g.ch, fl);
    if (coded.length + 4 >= len) { raw(at + len); continue; } // (not predictable: as it is)
    segs.push([1, g.bits, g.ch, len, 31 - Math.clz32(fl)]);
    const p = new Uint8Array(4 + coded.length); new DataView(p.buffer).setUint32(0, coded.length, true); p.set(coded, 4);
    payloads.push(p); pos = at + len;
  }
  raw(b.length);
  const head = 14 + segs.length * 8, total = head + payloads.reduce((a, p) => a + p.length, 0);
  const out = new Uint8Array(total), dv = new DataView(out.buffer);
  dv.setUint32(0, PCM_MAGIC, true); dv.setUint32(4, b.length, true); dv.setUint32(8, crc32(b), true); dv.setUint16(12, segs.length, true);
  segs.forEach(([kind, bits, ch, len, lf], i) => { out[14 + i * 8] = kind; out[15 + i * 8] = bits; out[16 + i * 8] = ch; out[17 + i * 8] = lf; dv.setUint32(18 + i * 8, len, true); });
  let o = head; for (const p of payloads) { out.set(p, o); o += p.length; }
  return out;
}

/** how many of the container's decoded bytes are coded samples (0: none — not worth sending as such) */
export function pcmCodedBytes(c) {
  const dv = new DataView(c.buffer, c.byteOffset, c.byteLength), n = dv.getUint16(12, true);
  let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) if (c[14 + i * 8] === 1) s += dv.getUint32(18 + i * 8, true);
  return s;
}

/** the bytes of a container (throws on anything not one, or not whole, or whose bytes do not match their CRC) */
export function decodePcm(c) {
  if (c.length < 14) throw new Error('pcm: not a container');
  const dv = new DataView(c.buffer, c.byteOffset, c.byteLength);
  if (dv.getUint32(0, true) !== PCM_MAGIC) throw new Error('pcm: not a container');
  const size = dv.getUint32(4, true), crc = dv.getUint32(8, true), n = dv.getUint16(12, true);
  let o = 14 + n * 8, at = 0;
  if (o > c.length) throw new Error('pcm: cut short');
  const out = new Uint8Array(size);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const kind = c[14 + i * 8], bits = c[15 + i * 8], ch = c[16 + i * 8], lf = c[17 + i * 8], len = dv.getUint32(18 + i * 8, true);
    if (at + len > size) throw new Error('pcm: segments past the end');
    if (kind === 0) { if (o + len > c.length) throw new Error('pcm: cut short'); out.set(c.subarray(o, o + len), at); o += len; }
    else if (kind === 1) {
      if ((bits !== 8 && bits !== 16) || (ch !== 1 && ch !== 2) || len % ((bits >> 3) * ch) || lf < 6 || lf > 16) throw new Error('pcm: bad segment');
      if (o + 4 > c.length) throw new Error('pcm: cut short');
      const cl = dv.getUint32(o, true); o += 4;
      if (o + cl > c.length) throw new Error('pcm: cut short');
      decodeSamples(c.subarray(o, o + cl), out, at, len, bits, ch, 1 << lf); o += cl;
    } else throw new Error('pcm: bad segment');
    at += len;
  }
  if (at !== size || o !== c.length) throw new Error('pcm: bad length');
  if (crc32(out) !== crc) throw new Error('pcm: CRC mismatch');
  return out;
}

```

`src/vfs/playable-watch.js`:

```js
// When a game whose page cannot tell it is playable reaches that point (a Windows game: the page knows nothing of its
// menus): the launch set's mark (GameData.mark('playable') for the engines that run in the page; launch-set.js), the
// same for every Windows game — no per-game rule. The game is taken as playable at the end of its first stretch of
// `quietMs` that looks like a menu or a game in play, not like a loading or a movie:
//   - it presents frames, at least `minFps` a second (a loading that blocks on its reads presents few or none);
//   - none of its reads waited for the network (a loading over a slow link, its frames drawn by another thread);
//   - it read little of its files, `maxReadBps` at most on average (a loading from this browser's copy reads megabytes a
//     second; music streamed from an archive tens of KB a second), and nothing of a movie (an intro playing);
//   - it paces itself, `minPacing` of the time at least (its threads waiting for their timers — frame-acct.js `wait`
//     and `sleep`: a menu waits for its next frame; a loading that computes draws its splash screen between steps of
//     work without waiting).
// Seen on BFME's first start (headless, 2026-10-21): with 5 s at 10 fps it marked its splash screen (69 MB read, two
// minutes of computation before its menu): a splash fading at 10-23 fps, idle half the time, for 5-10 s — hence 10 s at
// 20 fps; its menu draws at 30 fps, waiting 50-80 % of each frame (the worker's pump itself is busy all along: not a
// measure of it).
// ReadLog keeps what the game reads, by 64 KiB pieces, as the server learns reads (`[path, start, end, t]`, t: ms from
// the session's first read): reported every so often, as the engines that run in the page do (data-worker.js) — the
// server sees only the reads that reach the network, not those this browser's copy or the learned prefetch answered —,
// the reads before the mark with it: the server flags them (server.js learnMark).
import { CHUNK } from './http-backend.js';

export class PlayableWatch {
  /** @param {{ quietMs?: number, minFps?: number, maxReadBps?: number, minPacing?: number }} [o] */
  constructor({ quietMs = 10000, minFps = 20, maxReadBps = 96 * 1024, minPacing = 0.2 } = {}) {
    this.quietMs = quietMs; this.minFps = minFps; this.maxReadBps = maxReadBps; this.minPacing = minPacing;
    this.samples = []; // ({ at, frames, bytes, videoBytes, requests, pacingMs }: the last quietMs of steps)
    this.done = false;
  }
  /**
   * Each step of the page (every few hundred ms): true once, when the game is playable. `s`: { frames (presented so
   * far), bytes (read of its files so far), videoBytes (of movies), requests (reads that went to the network so far),
   * pacingMs (ms the game spent pacing itself so far: its threads waiting for their timers) }.
   */
  step(now, s) {
    if (this.done) return false;
    // (the last `quietMs`, sliding: its first sample the latest at least that old)
    const w = this.samples; w.push({ at: now, ...s });
    while (w.length > 1 && w[1].at <= now - this.quietMs) w.shift();
    const a = w[0], b = w.at(-1);
    if (now - a.at < this.quietMs || s.bytes === 0) return false;
    // (each half too: a stretch that only averages out — the end of a loading, then a menu — is not one yet)
    const mid = w.find((x) => x.at >= a.at + (now - a.at) / 2) ?? b;
    if (!this.quiet(a, b) || !this.quiet(a, mid) || !this.quiet(mid, b)) return false;
    this.done = true; this.samples = [];
    return true;
  }
  /** From sample `a` to `b`: frames at minFps, no read waited for the network, no movie, few bytes read, pacing. */
  quiet(a, b) {
    const ms = b.at - a.at; if (ms <= 0) return true;
    return b.requests === a.requests && b.videoBytes === a.videoBytes && b.bytes - a.bytes <= (ms / 1000) * this.maxReadBps
      && b.frames - a.frames >= (ms / 1000) * this.minFps && (b.pacingMs ?? ms) - (a.pacingMs ?? 0) >= ms * this.minPacing;
  }
}

/**
 * The reads of a session's game, per version: by 64 KiB pieces, the first time each was read (whatever answered it:
 * this browser's copy, memory, the network — the server sees only the last), taken by the reports to the server.
 */
export class ReadLog {
  constructor(max = 200000) { this.max = max; this.t0 = null; this.parts = new Map(); this.count = 0; }
  /** A read of [start, end) of `path` in version `name`. */
  add(name, path, start, end, now) {
    if (this.count >= this.max || end <= start) return;
    this.t0 ??= now;
    let v = this.parts.get(name); if (!v) this.parts.set(name, v = { seen: new Map(), reads: [] });
    let s = v.seen.get(path); if (!s) v.seen.set(path, s = new Set());
    const t = Math.round(now - this.t0);
    for (let c = Math.floor(start / CHUNK), e = Math.floor((end - 1) / CHUNK); c <= e; c++) {
      if (s.has(c)) continue;
      if (++this.count > this.max) return;
      s.add(c);
      // (pieces of one file in sequence: one range, at its first piece's time)
      const last = v.reads.at(-1), a = c * CHUNK;
      if (last && last[0] === path && last[2] === a) { last[2] = a + CHUNK; continue; }
      v.reads.push([path, a, a + CHUNK, t]);
    }
  }
  /** The reads of version `name` not taken yet, at most `n`: [path, start, end, t], ends within `size(path)`. */
  take(name, size, n = 40000) {
    const v = this.parts.get(name);
    return v ? v.reads.splice(0, n).map(([p, a, b, t]) => [p, a, Math.min(b, size(p) ?? b), t]).filter((r) => r[2] > r[1]) : [];
  }
  get names() { return [...this.parts.keys()]; }
}

/** Chrome refuses a keepalive request once the keepalive bodies in flight pass 64 KiB (the page's, all requests). */
export const KEEPALIVE_BYTES = 60000;
/** reads in one body of a final report (~50 bytes each: a body well under KEEPALIVE_BYTES) */
export const FINAL_PIECE = 1000;

/**
 * The reports of a page's reads to the server's learned order (POST /api/prefetch/<version> { session, reads, mark? }),
 * the same for the Windows worker and the data worker of the engines that run in the page:
 *   - in order: each waits for the earlier ones to be answered — a playable mark is never handled before the reads that
 *     came before it (server.js learnMark flags what the session had read by then);
 *   - a final one (the page leaving) at once, keepalive so that it outlives the page — split into bodies of FINAL_PIECE
 *     reads, keepalive only while the keepalive bodies in flight stay under KEEPALIVE_BYTES (over it Chrome fails the
 *     request at once and the reads, taken from the log, are lost), the rest as plain requests (they complete when the
 *     worker lives on, after a stop).
 */
export class ReadReports {
  constructor(o = {}) {
    this.fetch = o.fetch ?? ((url, init) => fetch(url, init));
    this.chain = Promise.resolve();
    this.keepaliveBytes = 0; // (keepalive bodies in flight)
    this.enc = new TextEncoder();
  }
  /**
   * Send `reads` (and `mark`) of version `name` for `session` — and the session's `phases` so far ([name, t], every
   * report: GameData.phase); the promise of the chain (tests).
   */
  send(name, session, reads, mark = null, final = false, phases = null) {
    const ph = phases?.length ? { phases } : {};
    const url = `/api/prefetch/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`;
    const init = (body, keepalive) => ({ method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, keepalive, body });
    if (!final) {
      const body = JSON.stringify({ session, reads, ...(mark ? { mark } : {}), ...ph });
      this.chain = this.chain.then(() => this.fetch(url, init(body, false))).catch(() => {}).then(() => {});
      return this.chain;
    }
    const sent = [];
    for (let i = 0; i === 0 || i < reads.length; i += FINAL_PIECE) {
      const last = i + FINAL_PIECE >= reads.length;
      const body = JSON.stringify({ session, reads: reads.slice(i, i + FINAL_PIECE), ...(mark && last ? { mark } : {}), ...(last ? ph : {}) });
      const bytes = this.enc.encode(body).length, keepalive = this.keepaliveBytes + bytes <= KEEPALIVE_BYTES;
      if (keepalive) this.keepaliveBytes += bytes;
      let r; try { r = Promise.resolve(this.fetch(url, init(body, keepalive))); } catch (e) { r = Promise.reject(e); }
      sent.push(r.catch(() => {}).then(() => { if (keepalive) this.keepaliveBytes -= bytes; }));
    }
    return Promise.all(sent).then(() => {});
  }
}
```

`src/vfs/profile-moves.js`:

```js
// Player profile moves declared by a manifest ("profileMoves"): files a game kept at one place of the player's profile
// (C:\Users\Player) and keeps at another since its manifest changed — e.g. a registry value the installer writes added
// to the manifest, which moves the game's user-data folder — put at the new place at every start, before the game
// sees its profile, so a player keeps their settings and saves. Generic: any VFS backend with the usual interface
// (stat, readdir, mkdir, rename, rmdir: MemBackend — the page's profile, the OPFS copy and the account's copy go
// through it —, NodeBackend — the Node runner's save folder), no game named here.
//
// A move { from, to, names? } takes every entry of the folder `from` (only those named in `names`, compared without
// case, when given; never the folder holding `to` when `to` is beneath `from`) to `to/<name>`, folders merged
// recursively. A file whose new place already holds one stays where it was (the new place's is the game's own, newer:
// nothing is overwritten, nothing lost). Idempotent: once moved there is nothing left to move, a later start changes
// nothing — no marker needed, so the profile the game sees (and a snapshot's check of it) is the files alone.

const SEGMENT = /^[^\x00-\x1f<>:"\\|?*/]+$/;
const MAX_MOVES = 8, MAX_NAMES = 64, MAX_PATH = 240, MAX_DEPTH = 32;

const segOk = (s) => SEGMENT.test(s) && s !== '.' && s !== '..' && !/[ .]$/.test(s);
/** A profile path as a manifest gives it: '/'-separated, relative, without '.', '..' or Windows-forbidden characters. */
export const profilePathOk = (p) => typeof p === 'string' && p.length > 0 && p.length <= MAX_PATH && p.split('/').every(segOk);

/** What is wrong with a manifest's profileMoves (undefined: none declared), or null when it is valid. */
export function profileMovesProblem(moves) {
  if (moves === undefined) return null;
  if (!Array.isArray(moves) || moves.length > MAX_MOVES) return `profileMoves doit être une liste de ${MAX_MOVES} déplacements au plus`;
  for (const mv of moves) {
    if (!mv || typeof mv !== 'object' || Array.isArray(mv)) return 'profileMoves : déplacement invalide';
    for (const k of Object.keys(mv)) if (!['from', 'to', 'names'].includes(k)) return `profileMoves : champ inconnu ${k}`;
    if (!profilePathOk(mv.from) || !profilePathOk(mv.to)) return 'profileMoves : from et to doivent être des chemins relatifs du profil (séparés par /)';
    const from = mv.from.toLowerCase(), to = mv.to.toLowerCase();
    if (from === to || from.startsWith(to + '/')) return 'profileMoves : to ne peut être from ni le contenir';
    if (mv.names !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(mv.names) || !mv.names.length || mv.names.length > MAX_NAMES || !mv.names.every(segOk))) return 'profileMoves : names doit lister des noms d\'entrées';
  }
  return null;
}

const join = (a, b) => (a ? a + '/' + b : b);
const parentOf = (p) => (p.includes('/') ? p.slice(0, p.lastIndexOf('/')) : '');

/** The folders of `dir` made down from the root (the existing ones left as they are); false when one is a file. */
function ensureDir(backend, dir) {
  const parts = dir.split('/').filter(Boolean);
  for (let i = 1; i <= parts.length; i++) {
    const p = parts.slice(0, i).join('/'), st = backend.stat(p);
    if (st?.isDir) continue;
    if (st || !backend.mkdir(p)) return false;
  }
  return true;
}

function moveEntry(backend, src, dst, isDir, out, depth = 0) {
  const there = backend.stat(dst);
  if (!isDir) {
    if (there || !ensureDir(backend, parentOf(dst)) || !backend.rename(src, dst)) { out.kept.push(src); return; }
    out.moved.push([src, dst]);
    return;
  }
  if ((there && !there.isDir) || depth >= MAX_DEPTH) { out.kept.push(src); return; } // (deeper than a profile goes: left)
  if (!there && !ensureDir(backend, dst)) { out.kept.push(src); return; }
  for (const e of backend.readdir(src) ?? []) moveEntry(backend, join(src, e.name), join(dst, e.name), e.isDir, out, depth + 1);
  if (!(backend.readdir(src) ?? []).length && backend.rmdir?.(src)) out.moved.push([src, dst]);
}

/**
 * Applies a manifest's profile moves to a backend holding the player's profile at its root.
 * @returns {{ moved: Array<[string, string]>, kept: string[] }} the entries moved (files, then each emptied folder) and
 *   the files left at their old place because the new one holds a file already.
 */
export function applyProfileMoves(backend, moves) {
  const out = { moved: [], kept: [] };
  if (!Array.isArray(moves) || profileMovesProblem(moves)) return out;
  for (const { from, to, names } of moves) {
    if (!backend.stat(from)?.isDir) continue;
    const lower = from.toLowerCase(), target = to.toLowerCase();
    // (the folder holding `to`, when `to` is beneath `from`: where the entries go, not one to move)
    const skip = target.startsWith(lower + '/') ? target.slice(lower.length + 1).split('/')[0] : null;
    const only = names ? new Set(names.map((n) => n.toLowerCase())) : null;
    for (const e of backend.readdir(from) ?? []) {
      const n = e.name.toLowerCase();
      if (n === skip || (only && !only.has(n))) continue;
      moveEntry(backend, join(from, e.name), join(to, e.name), e.isDir, out);
    }
  }
  return out;
}
```

`src/vfs/profile-opfs.js`:

```js
// The player's profile (C:\Users\Player: settings, saves) kept in the browser's OPFS between sessions: what the page
// worker writes there as the game changes it (flushProfileOpfs), and the profile as the headless harness takes it
// (profileDumpOf, profileGone: --profile-dir).

/**
 * Write what changed in `profile` (a MemBackend: files dated after `since`, the keys in `profile.changes` — renamed,
 * removed, folders made) into the OPFS directory `dir`. The files first, then the removals, and only once every write
 * succeeded: a file moved to a new place (a manifest's profileMoves, a rename by the game) is never gone from both
 * places — a worker killed during the writes, or a write that fails, leaves its old entry. What failed stays in
 * `profile.changes` and is written (or removed) again at the next flush.
 * @param {FileSystemDirectoryHandle | any} dir
 * @param {any} profile
 * @param {number} since the previous flush's date (ms)
 * @param {{ log?: (msg: string) => void }} [o]
 * @returns {Promise<{ written: number, removed: number, failed: number, changed: boolean }>}
 */
export async function flushProfileOpfs(dir, profile, since, o = {}) {
  const changes = profile.changes ? [...profile.changes] : []; profile.changes?.clear();
  const dirty = new Map([...profile.files].filter(([, f]) => f.mtime > since));
  for (const k of changes) if (profile.files.has(k)) dirty.set(k, profile.files.get(k)); // (renamed: same date)
  const out = { written: 0, removed: 0, failed: 0, changed: dirty.size > 0 || changes.length > 0 };
  const dirOf = async (parts, create) => { let d = dir; for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) d = await d.getDirectoryHandle(profile.names.get(parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/')) ?? parts[i], { create }); return d; };
  const gone = [];
  // (folders made: before the files they hold)
  for (const k of changes) {
    if (profile.files.has(k)) continue;
    if (profile.dirs.has(k)) { try { await dirOf(k.split('/'), true); } catch { /* already so */ } } else gone.push(k);
  }
  for (const [key, f] of dirty) {
    try {
      const parts = key.split('/');
      const d = await dirOf(parts.slice(0, -1), true);
      const fh = await d.getFileHandle(profile.names.get(key) ?? parts[parts.length - 1], { create: true });
      const w = await fh.createWritable();
      await w.write(f.data.subarray(0, f.len));
      await w.close();
      out.written++;
    } catch (e) { out.failed++; profile.changes?.add(key); o.log?.(`OPFS write failed for ${key}: ${e.message}`); }
  }
  // (files removed or renamed away, folders removed: the browser's copy follows — a deleted save must not come back —
  // once the new copies are there; else at a later flush)
  if (out.failed) { for (const k of gone) profile.changes?.add(k); return out; }
  for (const k of gone) {
    const parts = k.split('/');
    try { await (await dirOf(parts.slice(0, -1), false)).removeEntry(profile.names.get(k) ?? parts[parts.length - 1]); out.removed++; }
    catch { /* already so */ }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Every profile file as { path (original case, '/'-separated), data (base64) } for the headless harness — null while
 * the profile is not complete yet (`ready` false: the worker still loading it, or its start failed before), so that the
 * harness never takes a profile it has not seen whole for one the game emptied.
 * @param {any} profile
 * @param {boolean} ready
 * @param {(p: any) => { path: string, data: Uint8Array }[]} list
 * @param {(d: Uint8Array) => string} toBase64
 */
export function profileDumpOf(profile, ready, list, toBase64) {
  if (!profile || !ready) return null;
  return list(profile).map((f) => ({ path: f.path, data: toBase64(f.data) }));
}

/**
 * The files the harness loaded into the profile that its dump no longer has (the game deleted them, a manifest's
 * profileMoves moved them): removed from the host folder too. None when there is no dump (null: not ready).
 * @param {string[]} loaded
 * @param {{ path: string }[] | null | undefined} files
 */
export function profileGone(loaded, files) {
  if (!Array.isArray(files)) return [];
  const now = new Set(files.map((f) => f.path.toLowerCase()));
  return loaded.filter((p) => !now.has(p.toLowerCase()));
}
```

`src/vfs/vfs.js`:

```js
// Virtual file system: Windows paths (drive letters, backslashes, case-insensitive) mapped onto
// mounted backends. Backends implement a small synchronous interface (the guest's file API is
// synchronous, see DECISIONS.md D007).
//
// Backend interface:
//   stat(rel) -> { size, isDir, mtime } | null
//   readdir(rel) -> [{ name, size, isDir, mtime }]
//   open(rel, { write, create, truncate }) -> File | null
//   mkdir(rel), unlink(rel), rename(relFrom, relTo)
// File interface: size(), read(off, len) -> Uint8Array, write(off, bytes), truncate(len), close()

export class Vfs {
  constructor() {
    /** @type {Array<{prefix: string, backend: any}>} sorted longest-prefix first */
    this.mounts = [];
    this.opens = 0; // (files opened: the host watches the game's loading — a snapshot is taken once it settles)
    /** @type {Map<string, {type: number, label: string, fs: string, serial: number}>} drives besides C: (letter -> Windows drive type, volume) */
    this.drives = new Map();
  }

  /** A whole drive (e.g. a CD-ROM: type 5, file system CDFS) served by `backend`. */
  mountDrive(letter, backend, { type = 5, label = '', fs = 'CDFS', serial = 0 } = {}) {
    const L = String(letter).charAt(0).toUpperCase();
    this.mount(`${L}:\\`, backend);
    this.drives.set(L, { type, label, fs, serial: serial >>> 0 });
  }

  /** @param {string} winPath e.g. 'C:\\Game' @param {any} backend */
  mount(winPath, backend) {
    const prefix = normalizeWin(winPath);
    this.mounts.push({ prefix, lower: prefix.toLowerCase(), backend }); // (paths match their mount whatever their case)
    this.mounts.sort((a, b) => b.prefix.length - a.prefix.length);
  }

  /** @returns {{ backend: any, rel: string, prefix: string } | null} */
  resolve(winPath) {
    const p = normalizeWin(winPath), lp = p.toLowerCase();
    for (const m of this.mounts) {
      if (lp === m.lower) return { backend: m.backend, rel: '', prefix: m.prefix };
      if (lp.startsWith(m.lower + '\\') || m.lower.endsWith('\\') && lp.startsWith(m.lower)) {
        const rel = p.slice(m.prefix.length).replace(/^\\+/, '').split('\\').join('/');
        return { backend: m.backend, rel, prefix: m.prefix };
      }
    }
    return null;
  }

  stat(winPath) { const r = this.resolve(winPath); return r ? r.backend.stat(r.rel) : null; }
  readdir(winPath) { const r = this.resolve(winPath); return r ? r.backend.readdir(r.rel) : null; }
  open(winPath, opts = {}) { this.opens++; const r = this.resolve(winPath); return r ? r.backend.open(r.rel, opts) : null; }
  mkdir(winPath) { const r = this.resolve(winPath); return r ? r.backend.mkdir(r.rel) : false; }
  unlink(winPath) { const r = this.resolve(winPath); return r ? r.backend.unlink(r.rel) : false; }
  rename(from, to) {
    const a = this.resolve(from), b = this.resolve(to);
    if (!a || !b || a.backend !== b.backend) return false;
    return a.backend.rename(a.rel, b.rel);
  }
  /** Read a whole file (or null). */
  readFile(winPath) {
    const f = this.open(winPath, {});
    if (!f) return null;
    try { return f.read(0, f.size()); } finally { f.close(); }
  }
}

/**
 * The manifest's `cdrom` (generic compat option: games checking for their disc): the game's own files are also a
 * CD-ROM drive. `"cdrom": "D"` or `{ "drive": "D", "label": "<volume label>", "serial": <number> }`.
 */
export function mountGameCdrom(vfs, manifest, gameBackend) {
  const cd = manifest?.cdrom;
  if (!cd) return;
  const spec = typeof cd === 'string' ? { drive: cd } : cd;
  const L = String(spec.drive ?? 'D').charAt(0).toUpperCase();
  if (!/[D-Z]/.test(L)) throw new Error(`manifest cdrom: invalid drive ${spec.drive}`);
  const label = String(spec.label ?? '').slice(0, 32);
  let serial = spec.serial ?? 0;
  if (!serial) for (const ch of label + L) serial = (Math.imul(serial, 31) + ch.charCodeAt(0)) >>> 0; // (stable per label)
  vfs.mountDrive(L, gameBackend, { type: 5, label, fs: 'CDFS', serial });
}

/** Normalize a Windows path: uppercase drive, backslashes, resolve . and .., no trailing slash. */
export function normalizeWin(p, cwd = 'C:\\') {
  let s = String(p).replace(/\//g, '\\');
  const literal = /^\\\\\?\\/.test(s); // (\\?\ paths are taken as they are)
  if (literal) s = s.slice(4);
  // Win32 path normalization: the trailing spaces and periods of a path not ending with a separator are removed
  // ("data\file.ide " opens "data\file.ide"); not in a wildcard pattern (FindFirstFile's "*." has its own meaning)
  else {
    const last = s.slice(s.lastIndexOf('\\') + 1);
    if (/[ .]$/.test(last) && !/^\.+$/.test(last) && !/[*?]/.test(last)) s = s.slice(0, s.length - last.length) + last.replace(/[ .]+$/, '');
  }
  if (!/^[A-Za-z]:/.test(s)) {
    // relative or rooted-without-drive
    if (s.startsWith('\\')) s = cwd.slice(0, 2) + s;
    else s = cwd.replace(/\\$/, '') + '\\' + s;
  }
  const drive = s[0].toUpperCase() + ':';
  const parts = [];
  for (const seg of s.slice(2).split('\\')) {
    if (seg === '' || seg === '.') continue;
    if (seg === '..') { parts.pop(); continue; }
    parts.push(seg);
  }
  return drive + '\\' + parts.join('\\');
}

/** What a machine saw of a path of a persistent mount (MemBackend.seen): whether it is there, its listing, its bytes. */
export const SEEN = Object.freeze({ STAT: 1, LIST: 2, DATA: 4 });

/** In-memory backend (writable). */
export class MemBackend {
  constructor() {
    /** @type {Map<string, {data: Uint8Array, len: number, mtime: number}>} lowercase path -> file */
    this.files = new Map();
    /** @type {Set<string>} lowercase dir paths */
    this.dirs = new Set(['']);
    this.names = new Map(); // lowercase -> original name path
    // A persistent mount (the player's profile: the host keeps it across sessions, the machine does not own it) records
    // what the machine saw of each path (SEEN bits): a snapshot goes on only from a profile as its machine saw it
    // (seenFingerprint, docs/snapshot.md). null: not recorded.
    /** @type {Map<string, number>|null} */
    this.seen = null;
    // Entries made, removed or renamed since a mirror last took them (a mirror of the backend replays them: the profile's
    // copy in the browser's storage, which file writes alone would leave with empty folders lost, deleted files back).
    /** @type {Set<string>|null} */
    this.changes = null;
  }
  key(rel) { return rel.toLowerCase(); }
  saw(k, bit) { if (this.seen) this.seen.set(k, (this.seen.get(k) ?? 0) | bit); return k; }
  stat(rel) {
    const k = this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.STAT);
    if (this.dirs.has(k)) return { size: 0, isDir: true, mtime: 0 };
    const f = this.files.get(k);
    return f ? { size: f.len, isDir: false, mtime: f.mtime } : null;
  }
  readdir(rel) { return this.listing(this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.LIST)); }
  /** The entries of directory `k` (a lowercase path), or null. */
  listing(k) {
    if (!this.dirs.has(k)) return null;
    const out = [];
    const prefix = k ? k + '/' : '';
    for (const d of this.dirs) if (d && d.startsWith(prefix) && !d.slice(prefix.length).includes('/')) out.push({ name: this.names.get(d) ?? d.slice(prefix.length), size: 0, isDir: true, mtime: 0 });
    for (const [p, f] of this.files) if (p.startsWith(prefix) && !p.slice(prefix.length).includes('/')) out.push({ name: this.names.get(p) ?? p.slice(prefix.length), size: f.len, isDir: false, mtime: f.mtime });
    return out;
  }
  open(rel, opts = {}) {
    const k = this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.DATA);
    let f = this.files.get(k);
    if (!f) {
      if (!opts.create) return null;
      const parent = k.includes('/') ? k.slice(0, k.lastIndexOf('/')) : '';
      if (!this.dirs.has(parent)) return null;
      f = { data: new Uint8Array(0), len: 0, mtime: Date.now() };
      this.files.set(k, f);
      this.names.set(k, rel.split('/').pop());
      this.changes?.add(k);
    } else if (opts.truncate) { f.len = 0; }
    return new MemFile(f);
  }
  mkdir(rel) {
    const k = this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.STAT);
    const parent = k.includes('/') ? k.slice(0, k.lastIndexOf('/')) : '';
    if (!this.dirs.has(parent) || this.dirs.has(k) || this.files.has(k)) return false;
    this.dirs.add(k); this.names.set(k, rel.split('/').pop()); this.changes?.add(k);
    return true;
  }
  unlink(rel) { const k = this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.DATA), r = this.files.delete(k); if (r) this.changes?.add(k); return r; }
  /** Removes an empty folder (false: not a folder, the root, or not empty). */
  rmdir(rel) {
    const k = this.saw(this.key(rel), SEEN.STAT), prefix = k + '/';
    if (!k || !this.dirs.has(k)) return false;
    for (const d of this.dirs) if (d.startsWith(prefix)) return false;
    for (const p of this.files.keys()) if (p.startsWith(prefix)) return false;
    this.dirs.delete(k); this.changes?.add(k); // (its name kept: the mirror removes it by its original case)
    return true;
  }
  rename(from, to) {
    this.saw(this.key(from), SEEN.DATA); this.saw(this.key(to), SEEN.DATA);
    const f = this.files.get(this.key(from));
    if (!f) return false;
    this.files.delete(this.key(from)); this.files.set(this.key(to), f); this.names.set(this.key(to), to.split('/').pop());
    this.changes?.add(this.key(from)); this.changes?.add(this.key(to));
    return true;
  }
}

class MemFile {
  constructor(f) { this.f = f; }
  size() { return this.f.len; }
  read(off, len) {
    const end = Math.min(off + len, this.f.len);
    return off >= end ? new Uint8Array(0) : this.f.data.slice(off, end);
  }
  write(off, bytes) {
    const need = off + bytes.length;
    if (need > this.f.data.length) {
      const nd = new Uint8Array(Math.max(need, this.f.data.length * 2, 4096));
      nd.set(this.f.data.subarray(0, this.f.len));
      this.f.data = nd;
    }
    if (off > this.f.len) this.f.data.fill(0, this.f.len, off);
    this.f.data.set(bytes, off);
    this.f.len = Math.max(this.f.len, need);
    this.f.mtime = Date.now();
    return bytes.length;
  }
  truncate(len) { this.f.len = Math.min(len, this.f.len); if (len > this.f.len) { this.write(this.f.len, new Uint8Array(len - this.f.len)); } }
  close() {}
}

/**
 * What `backend` holds now at the paths in `seen` (lowercase path -> SEEN bits), as far as those bits go: kind, size,
 * listing (names and sizes), bytes (a hash). Equal fingerprints: a machine that saw those paths sees them alike now.
 * Modification times are left out (a profile loaded from the browser's storage gets new ones each session).
 */
export function seenFingerprint(backend, seen) {
  const out = {};
  for (const k of [...seen.keys()].sort()) {
    const bits = seen.get(k);
    let v;
    if (backend.dirs.has(k)) v = bits & SEEN.LIST ? 'd:' + (backend.listing(k) ?? []).map((e) => `${e.name.toLowerCase()}${e.isDir ? '/' : ':' + e.size}`).sort().join('|') : 'd';
    else { const f = backend.files.get(k); v = !f ? '-' : bits & SEEN.DATA ? `f:${f.len}:${hashBytes(f.data.subarray(0, f.len))}` : `f:${f.len}`; }
    out[k] = [bits, v];
  }
  return out;
}

/** A 64-bit hash of `b` (two 32-bit FNV-style lanes): change detection, not security. */
export function hashBytes(b) {
  let h1 = 0x811c9dc5, h2 = 0x9747b28c ^ b.length;
  for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i++) { h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ b[i], 0x01000193); h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ b[i], 0x5bd1e995); h2 ^= h2 >>> 15; }
  return (h1 >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0') + (h2 >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0');
}
```

`src/vfs/wad3.js`:

```js
// WAD3: GoldSrc's texture archives — a 12-byte header ('WAD3', its lumps' count, its directory's offset), the lumps, then
// the directory (32 bytes a lump: offset, size in the file, size, type, compression, two pad bytes, a 16-byte name).
// Its textures (miptex): a 16-byte name, width, height, the offsets of four levels, each half the last's size, of 8-bit
// palette indices.
// One reader for every place that reads one: the server's light copies (src/host/light-copies.js: a texture's finest
// level redrawn) and a GoldSrc page that announces the textures a map's load reads (src/ports/goldsrc/bsp-reads.js).
// Pure: bytes in (a Uint8Array or a Buffer), values out — Node and the browser alike.

/** WAD3 lump type of a texture with its mip levels (miptex) */
export const WAD_MIPTEX = 0x43;
/** Bytes of a directory entry. */
export const WAD_ENTRY = 32;

/**
 * A WAD3's header (its first 12 bytes at least) in a file of `size` bytes: { n, dir } — its lumps' count and its
 * directory's offset —, or null: not a WAD3, or a directory that does not fit in the file.
 * @param {Uint8Array} head
 * @param {number} size
 */
export function wadHeader(head, size) {
  if (head.length < 12 || head[0] !== 0x57 || head[1] !== 0x41 || head[2] !== 0x44 || head[3] !== 0x33) return null;
  const v = new DataView(head.buffer, head.byteOffset, head.byteLength), n = v.getInt32(4, true), dir = v.getInt32(8, true);
  return n > 0 && n < 1 << 20 && dir >= 12 && dir + n * WAD_ENTRY <= size ? { n, dir } : null;
}

/**
 * The directory's entries (`bytes`: its n × 32 bytes) of a WAD3 of `size` bytes: [{ name, pos, disk, size, type, comp }]
 * — name lower case (the engine finds a texture by its name without case), up to its first NUL —, those whose bytes
 * lie in the file (after the header) only.
 * @param {Uint8Array} bytes
 * @param {number} n
 * @param {number} size
 */
export function wadEntries(bytes, n, size) {
  const v = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength), out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n && (i + 1) * WAD_ENTRY <= bytes.length; i++) {
    const at = i * WAD_ENTRY, pos = v.getInt32(at, true), disk = v.getInt32(at + 4, true);
    if (!(pos >= 12 && disk >= 0 && pos + disk <= size)) continue;
    let name = '';
    for (let k = at + 16; k < at + 32 && bytes[k]; k++) name += String.fromCharCode(bytes[k]);
    out.push({ name: name.toLowerCase(), pos, disk, size: v.getInt32(at + 8, true), type: bytes[at + 12], comp: bytes[at + 13] });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Bytes of a miptex's header (name, width, height, four level offsets). */
export const MIPTEX_HEADER = 40;
/** A texture's finest level is redrawn (a light copy) from this many pixels on: 64 × 64 (smaller ones save nothing worth their detail). */
export const MIP_LIGHT_FROM = 64 * 64;

/**
 * The two finest levels of a miptex whose header (`mt`, its MIPTEX_HEADER bytes) lies at file offset `pos`, `span` bytes
 * of the file from there being its own (a WAD's lump): [level 0's file offset, width,
 * height, level 1's file offset] — or null: no pixels here (offsets 0), under
 * MIP_LIGHT_FROM pixels, odd sides, or levels not as the format lays them (level 1 past level 0, both inside the span).
 * @param {Uint8Array} mt
 * @param {number} pos
 * @param {number} span
 */
export function miptexLevels(mt, pos, span) {
  if (mt.length < MIPTEX_HEADER) return null;
  const v = new DataView(mt.buffer, mt.byteOffset, mt.byteLength);
  const w = v.getUint32(16, true), h = v.getUint32(20, true), o0 = v.getUint32(24, true), o1 = v.getUint32(28, true);
  if (!w || !h || w % 2 || h % 2 || w > 4096 || h > 4096 || w * h < MIP_LIGHT_FROM) return null;
  if (o0 < MIPTEX_HEADER || o1 < o0 + w * h || o1 + (w / 2) * (h / 2) > span) return null;
  return [pos + o0, w, h, pos + o1];
}

/**
 * A miptex's finest level redrawn from the next one (each pixel of level 1 twice as wide and high: half the detail) over
 * the bytes of `buf` that hold the file's [start, end) from index `base`: level 0 at file offset `d0` (`w` × `h`), its
 * pixels inside the range only, level 1 read at index `l1` of `buf` (it lies after level 0: the caller read that far).
 * @param {Uint8Array} buf
 * @param {number} base
 * @param {number} start
 * @param {number} end
 * @param {number} d0
 * @param {number} w
 * @param {number} h
 * @param {number} l1
 */
export function redrawFinest(buf, base, start, end, d0, w, h, l1) {
  const hw = w / 2, a = Math.max(start, d0), b = Math.min(end, d0 + w * h);
  for (let p = a; p < b; p++) { const i = p - d0, y = (i / w) | 0, x = i - y * w; buf[base + p - start] = buf[l1 + (y >> 1) * hw + (x >> 1)]; }
}
```
