`src/win32/api.js`:

```js
// Win32 API registry: builtin DLL modules whose exports are host (JS) functions reached through
// thunk addresses. Calling a thunk makes the executor exit to the dispatcher (EXIT.THUNK, see
// DECISIONS.md D004), which runs the handler and performs the callee/caller stack cleanup.
import { THUNK_BASE, THUNK_END, THUNK_SIZE } from '../cpu/memory.js';

export const CC_STDCALL = 0, CC_CDECL = 1;

/** pseudo-DLLs of Orthros' own (no module image) */
const INTERNAL_DLLS = new Set(['com.dll', 'orthros.dll']);
/** free slots of a module image for functions it does not export (unknown imports); then header-less pages */
const SLACK_SLOTS = 64;
const CHUNK_SIZE = 0x1000;
/** size of the headers (MZ, PE, one section header) and alignment of the image's section: the export directory and
 * the thunks follow at once (a small-alignment image, mapped as one region as Windows maps such images) */
const HDR = 0x200;
const alignUp = (v, a) => (v + a - 1) & ~(a - 1);

/** @typedef {{ dll: string, base: number, end: number, chunk: { next: number, end: number } }} ThunkWindow */

/**
 * Layout of a builtin DLL's image: headers, the export directory (at HDR), then the thunk slots (16-byte aligned, at
 * headerSize). funcs: the export address table (function name per ordinal - 1, null for an unused
 * ordinal); names: [name, EAT index] sorted by name (the order a binary search of the name table expects).
 * @param {string} dllName
 * @param {{ funcs: Map<string, any>, ordinals: Map<number, string> } | undefined} d
 */
export function buildExportImage(dllName, d) {
  /** @type {(string|null)[]} */
  const funcs = [];
  if (d) {
    const index = new Map();
    let maxOrd = 0;
    for (const ord of d.ordinals.keys()) if (ord > maxOrd && ord < 0x10000) maxOrd = ord;
    for (let i = 0; i < maxOrd; i++) funcs.push(null);
    for (const [ord, name] of [...d.ordinals].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0])) if (ord >= 1 && ord < 0x10000 && !index.has(name)) { funcs[ord - 1] = name; index.set(name, ord - 1); }
    for (const name of d.funcs.keys()) if (!index.has(name) && !name.startsWith('#')) { index.set(name, funcs.length); funcs.push(name); }
  }
  const names = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < funcs.length; i++) if (funcs[i] !== null && !funcs[i].startsWith('#')) names.push([funcs[i], i]);
  names.sort((a, b) => (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0));
  let strBytes = dllName.length + 1;
  for (const [n] of names) strBytes += n.length + 1;
  const exportSize = 40 + 4 * funcs.length + 6 * names.length + strBytes;
  return { funcs, names, exportSize, headerSize: alignUp(HDR + exportSize, 16) };
}

/** Write a builtin DLL's MZ/PE headers and export directory at its base (eat: function RVA per ordinal - 1). */
function writeExportImage(mem, base, size, dllName, img, eat) {
  mem.fill(base, img.headerSize, 0);
  const pe = base + 0x40;
  mem.write16(base, 0x5a4d); // MZ
  mem.write32(base + 0x3c, 0x40); // e_lfanew
  mem.write32(pe, 0x4550); // PE\0\0
  // file header: i386, one section, optional header size, DLL | 32-bit machine | executable image
  mem.write16(pe + 4, 0x14c); mem.write16(pe + 6, 1); mem.write16(pe + 20, 0xe0); mem.write16(pe + 22, 0x2102);
  const oh = pe + 24;
  mem.write16(oh, 0x10b); // PE32
  mem.write32(oh + 4, size - HDR); // SizeOfCode
  mem.write32(oh + 20, HDR); // BaseOfCode
  mem.write32(oh + 28, base); // ImageBase
  mem.write32(oh + 32, HDR); mem.write32(oh + 36, HDR); // section / file alignment (equal: below a page)
  mem.write16(oh + 40, 5); mem.write16(oh + 42, 1); // OS version 5.1
  mem.write16(oh + 48, 5); mem.write16(oh + 50, 1); // subsystem version 5.1
  mem.write32(oh + 56, size); // SizeOfImage
  mem.write32(oh + 60, HDR); // SizeOfHeaders
  mem.write16(oh + 68, 3); // subsystem: Windows CUI (as system DLLs)
  mem.write32(oh + 72, 0x40000); mem.write32(oh + 76, 0x1000); mem.write32(oh + 80, 0x100000); mem.write32(oh + 84, 0x1000); // stack / heap
  mem.write32(oh + 92, 16); // NumberOfRvaAndSizes
  mem.write32(oh + 96, HDR); mem.write32(oh + 100, img.exportSize); // export directory
  const sh = oh + 0xe0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) mem.write8(sh + i, '.text'.charCodeAt(i));
  mem.write32(sh + 8, size - HDR); mem.write32(sh + 12, HDR); // VirtualSize, VirtualAddress
  mem.write32(sh + 16, size - HDR); mem.write32(sh + 20, HDR); // SizeOfRawData, PointerToRawData
  mem.write32(sh + 36, 0x60000020); // code | execute | read
  // export directory
  const ed = base + HDR, nf = img.funcs.length, nn = img.names.length;
  const eatRva = HDR + 40, namesRva = eatRva + 4 * nf, ordsRva = namesRva + 4 * nn;
  let str = ordsRva + 2 * nn;
  const putStr = (s) => { for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) mem.write8(base + str + i, s.charCodeAt(i) & 0xff); str += s.length + 1; };
  mem.write32(ed + 12, str); putStr(dllName); // Name
  mem.write32(ed + 16, 1); // ordinal base
  mem.write32(ed + 20, nf); mem.write32(ed + 24, nn);
  mem.write32(ed + 28, eatRva); mem.write32(ed + 32, namesRva); mem.write32(ed + 36, ordsRva);
  for (let i = 0; i < nf; i++) mem.write32(base + eatRva + 4 * i, eat[i]);
  img.names.forEach(([name, i], k) => { mem.write32(base + namesRva + 4 * k, str); mem.write16(base + ordsRva + 2 * k, i); putStr(name); });
}

/**
 * @typedef {object} ApiDef
 * @property {string} name
 * @property {number} argc number of 32-bit stack arguments
 * @property {number} cc
 * @property {(ctx: import('./ctx.js').Ctx) => (number|undefined)} fn returns EAX (undefined: unchanged)
 * @property {string} dll
 * @property {boolean} [stub] auto-generated tracing stub
 * @property {boolean} [noreturn] handler manages EIP/ESP itself (thread switches, exits)
 */

export class ApiRegistry {
  /** @param {import('../cpu/memory.js').GuestMemory|null} [mem] guest memory (the module images are written there) */
  constructor(mem = null) {
    this.mem = mem;
    /** @type {Map<string, ThunkWindow>} canonical DLL name -> thunk window */
    this.windows = new Map();
    /** @type {ThunkWindow[]} the windows holding a module image, by address */
    this.windowList = [];
    this.windowTop = THUNK_BASE; // module images grow upwards from THUNK_BASE...
    this.chunkFloor = THUNK_END; // ...header-less pages downwards from THUNK_END
    /** @type {Map<string, {name: string, funcs: Map<string, ApiDef>, ordinals: Map<number, string>, aliasOf?: string}>} */
    this.dlls = new Map();
    /**
     * by thunk index (module headers and free slots: null). Allocated whole: the internal pages are taken from the top of
     * the thunk region, so a table grown by assignment would be sparse — V8 then keeps it as a dictionary, and every API
     * call (dispatch, the deferred queue) paid a hash lookup to find its thunk.
     * @type {Array<{dll: string, name: string, def: ApiDef|null, addr: number}|null>}
     */
    this.thunks = new Array((THUNK_END - THUNK_BASE) / THUNK_SIZE).fill(null);
    /** dll!name -> thunk index */
    this.thunkIndex = new Map();
    /** Signature database for unknown imports (name -> argc), so stubs can clean the stack. */
    this.signatures = new Map();
    this.unknown = new Map(); // "dll!name" -> call count
    this.onThunk = null; // (idx, 'dll!name', def) callback when a thunk slot is created
    /** DLL -> (name) => def: handlers a module defines as the game reaches them (COM methods), defined by name instead
     *  — a restored Vm's (core/vm-snapshot.js) */
    this.lazyDefs = new Map();
    /** default return value of tracing stubs per DLL (GpStatus GenericError for gdiplus, E_NOTIMPL for COM-style DLLs) */
    this.stubReturns = new Map([['gdiplus.dll', 1], ['ole32.dll', 0x80004001], ['oleaut32.dll', 0x80004001], ['d3d8.dll', 0], ['dsound.dll', 0x80004001], ['ddraw.dll', 0x80004001], ['dinput8.dll', 0x80004001], ['quartz.dll', 0x80004001], ['avifil32.dll', 0x80004001]]);
  }

  /** Normalize a DLL name: lowercase, ensure .dll suffix, strip path. */
  static norm(dll) {
    let n = dll.toLowerCase();
    const slash = Math.max(n.lastIndexOf('\\'), n.lastIndexOf('/'));
    if (slash >= 0) n = n.slice(slash + 1);
    if (!n.includes('.')) n += '.dll';
    return n;
  }

  /** Register a builtin DLL. */
  dll(name, aliases = []) {
    const n = ApiRegistry.norm(name);
    let d = this.dlls.get(n);
    if (!d) { d = { name: n, funcs: new Map(), ordinals: new Map() }; this.dlls.set(n, d); }
    for (const a of aliases) this.dlls.set(ApiRegistry.norm(a), d);
    return d;
  }

  has(dll) { return this.dlls.has(ApiRegistry.norm(dll)); }

  /**
   * Define functions. specs: { Name: [argc, fn] | [argc, fn, opts] | fn (argc from signatures) }
   * @param {string} dll
   * @param {Record<string, any>} specs
   * @param {{ cc?: number }} [opts]
   */
  define(dll, specs, opts = {}) {
    const d = this.dll(dll);
    const cc = opts.cc ?? CC_STDCALL;
    for (const [name, spec] of Object.entries(specs)) {
      let argc, fn, o = {};
      if (Array.isArray(spec)) { [argc, fn, o = {}] = spec; }
      else { fn = spec; argc = this.signatures.get(name); if (argc === undefined) throw new Error(`no signature for ${dll}!${name}`); }
      d.funcs.set(name, { name, argc, cc: o.cc ?? cc, fn, dll: d.name, noreturn: !!o.noreturn, com: o.com ?? null });
      if (o.ordinal !== undefined) d.ordinals.set(o.ordinal, name);
    }
  }

  /** Register ordinal -> name mappings for a DLL. */
  ordinals(dll, map) {
    const d = this.dll(dll);
    for (const [ord, name] of Object.entries(map)) d.ordinals.set(+ord, name);
  }

  lookup(dll, name) {
    const d = this.dlls.get(ApiRegistry.norm(dll));
    return d ? d.funcs.get(name) ?? null : null;
  }

  /** Thunk address for dll!name (creates a stub entry for unknown functions). */
  thunkFor(dll, name) {
    const n = ApiRegistry.norm(dll);
    const cn = this.dlls.get(n)?.name ?? n; // (aliases share their DLL's thunks)
    const idx = this.thunkIndex.get(`${cn}!${name}`);
    if (idx !== undefined) return this.thunks[idx].addr;
    return this.newThunk(this.window(cn), cn, name);
  }

  /** @param {ThunkWindow} w */
  newThunk(w, dll, name) {
    let c = w.chunk;
    if (c.next >= c.end) c = w.chunk = this.allocChunk();
    const addr = c.next;
    c.next += THUNK_SIZE;
    const idx = (addr - THUNK_BASE) / THUNK_SIZE;
    const key = `${dll}!${name}`;
    const def = this.lookup(dll, name);
    this.thunks[idx] = { dll, name, def, addr };
    this.thunkIndex.set(key, idx);
    if (this.onThunk) this.onThunk(idx, key, def);
    return addr;
  }

  /** A page of thunk slots without a module header (internal pseudo-DLLs, full images), from the top down. */
  allocChunk() {
    const base = this.chunkFloor - CHUNK_SIZE;
    if (base < this.windowTop) throw new Error('thunk table exhausted');
    this.chunkFloor = base;
    return { next: base, end: base + CHUNK_SIZE };
  }

  /**
   * The thunk window of a DLL (created on first use). A builtin DLL's window is an in-memory PE image, as a loaded DLL
   * is on Windows: MZ/PE headers and an export directory at its base (the module handle), whose functions are the
   * thunk slots that follow, inside the image. Software finding a module from one of its function addresses (scanning
   * down for the MZ header, VirtualQuery's allocation base) or resolving functions from the export table instead of
   * GetProcAddress then sees what it would on Windows. Orthros' internal pseudo-DLLs (COM methods, its own return
   * thunks) have header-less pages.
   * @returns {ThunkWindow}
   */
  window(dll) {
    const n = ApiRegistry.norm(dll);
    const d = this.dlls.get(n);
    const cn = d?.name ?? n;
    let w = this.windows.get(cn);
    if (w) return w;
    if (INTERNAL_DLLS.has(cn)) {
      w = { dll: cn, base: 0, end: 0, chunk: { next: 0, end: 0 } };
      this.windows.set(cn, w);
      return w;
    }
    const img = buildExportImage(cn, d);
    const base = this.windowTop;
    const size = alignUp(img.headerSize + (img.funcs.length + SLACK_SLOTS) * THUNK_SIZE, 0x1000);
    if (base + size > this.chunkFloor) throw new Error('thunk table exhausted');
    this.windowTop = base + size;
    w = { dll: cn, base, end: base + size, chunk: { next: base + img.headerSize, end: base + size } };
    this.windows.set(cn, w);
    this.windowList.push(w);
    // the slots of the exported functions first (their addresses go into the export table)
    const eat = img.funcs.map((f) => (f === null ? 0 : this.newThunk(w, cn, f) - base));
    if (this.mem) writeExportImage(this.mem, base, size, cn, img, eat);
    return w;
  }

  /** Module handle (image base) of a builtin DLL. */
  moduleBase(dll) { return this.window(dll).base; }

  /** The builtin DLL image containing an address, or null. */
  windowAt(addr) {
    addr >>>= 0;
    if (addr < THUNK_BASE || addr >= this.windowTop) return null;
    for (const w of this.windowList) if (addr >= w.base && addr < w.end) return w;
    return null;
  }

  thunkForOrdinal(dll, ordinal) {
    const d = this.dlls.get(ApiRegistry.norm(dll));
    const name = d?.ordinals.get(ordinal) ?? `#${ordinal}`;
    return this.thunkFor(dll, name);
  }

  /** Thunk entry by index (from EXIT_ARG). */
  thunk(idx) { return this.thunks[idx]; }

  /** Address -> "dll!name" if it is a thunk. */
  nameOf(addr) {
    if (addr < THUNK_BASE || addr >= THUNK_END) return null;
    const t = this.thunks[((addr - THUNK_BASE) / THUNK_SIZE) | 0];
    return t ? `${t.dll}!${t.name}` : null;
  }
}
```

`src/win32/authenticode.js`:

```js
// Authenticode (signed PE files) for wintrust.dll!WinVerifyTrust: synchronous, from scratch — the guest's call is
// synchronous and WebCrypto is not.
//
// What is checked, as Windows does: the file carries a PKCS#7 SignedData in its certificate table whose
// SpcIndirectDataContent digest equals the file's Authenticode image digest (MD5 / SHA-1 / SHA-256), whose signer's
// messageDigest attribute is the digest of that content, and whose signer's RSA signature over the authenticated
// attributes verifies with the signer's certificate (PKCS#1 v1.5). Not checked: the certificate chain up to a trusted
// root, revocation and validity periods (there is no Windows root store here; a file signed by its publisher and left
// intact verifies as it does on a Windows machine that trusts that publisher's root).

export const TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE = 0x800b0100, TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST = 0x80096010, TRUST_E_SUBJECT_FORM_UNKNOWN = 0x800b0003, CRYPT_E_SECURITY_SETTINGS = 0x80092026;
export const TRUST_E_NO_SIGNER_CERT = 0x80096002, TRUST_E_FAIL = 0x800b010b;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- hashes
const K256 = new Uint32Array([
  0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5, 0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
  0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da, 0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
  0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85, 0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
  0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3, 0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2]);
const MD5_S = [7, 12, 17, 22, 5, 9, 14, 20, 4, 11, 16, 23, 6, 10, 15, 21];
const MD5_K = new Uint32Array(64).map((_, i) => Math.floor(Math.abs(Math.sin(i + 1)) * 2 ** 32) >>> 0);

/** Incremental hash over 64-byte blocks: update(bytes) any number of times, then digest(). */
class BlockHash {
  constructor(kind) {
    this.kind = kind; this.buf = new Uint8Array(64); this.n = 0; this.len = 0; this.w = new Uint32Array(kind === 'sha256' ? 64 : kind === 'sha1' ? 80 : 16);
    this.h = new Uint32Array(kind === 'sha256' ? [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19]
      : kind === 'sha1' ? [0x67452301, 0xefcdab89, 0x98badcfe, 0x10325476, 0xc3d2e1f0] : [0x67452301, 0xefcdab89, 0x98badcfe, 0x10325476]);
  }
  update(d) {
    let i = 0; this.len += d.length;
    if (this.n) { const k = Math.min(64 - this.n, d.length); this.buf.set(d.subarray(0, k), this.n); this.n += k; i = k; if (this.n < 64) return this; this.block(this.buf, 0); this.n = 0; }
    for (; i + 64 <= d.length; i += 64) this.block(d, i);
    if (i < d.length) { this.buf.set(d.subarray(i), 0); this.n = d.length - i; }
    return this;
  }
  digest() {
    const bits = this.len * 8, le = this.kind === 'md5';
    const pad = new Uint8Array(((this.n + 9 + 63) & ~63) - this.n); pad[0] = 0x80;
    const dv = new DataView(pad.buffer), at = pad.length - 8;
    dv.setUint32(at + (le ? 0 : 4), bits >>> 0, le); dv.setUint32(at + (le ? 4 : 0), Math.floor(bits / 2 ** 32), le);
    this.update(pad);
    const out = new Uint8Array(this.h.length * 4), ov = new DataView(out.buffer);
    this.h.forEach((v, j) => ov.setUint32(j * 4, v, le));
    return out;
  }
  block(d, o) {
    const w = this.w, h = this.h;
    if (this.kind === 'md5') {
      for (let j = 0; j < 16; j++) w[j] = d[o + j * 4] | d[o + j * 4 + 1] << 8 | d[o + j * 4 + 2] << 16 | d[o + j * 4 + 3] << 24;
      let [a, b, c, e] = h;
      for (let j = 0; j < 64; j++) {
        let f, g;
        if (j < 16) { f = (b & c) | (~b & e); g = j; } else if (j < 32) { f = (e & b) | (~e & c); g = (5 * j + 1) & 15; } else if (j < 48) { f = b ^ c ^ e; g = (3 * j + 5) & 15; } else { f = c ^ (b | ~e); g = (7 * j) & 15; }
        const s = MD5_S[(j >> 4) * 4 + (j & 3)], t = (a + f + MD5_K[j] + w[g]) | 0;
        a = e; e = c; c = b; b = (b + ((t << s) | (t >>> (32 - s)))) | 0;
      }
      h[0] += a; h[1] += b; h[2] += c; h[3] += e;
      return;
    }
    for (let j = 0; j < 16; j++) w[j] = d[o + j * 4] << 24 | d[o + j * 4 + 1] << 16 | d[o + j * 4 + 2] << 8 | d[o + j * 4 + 3];
    if (this.kind === 'sha1') {
      for (let j = 16; j < 80; j++) { const x = w[j - 3] ^ w[j - 8] ^ w[j - 14] ^ w[j - 16]; w[j] = (x << 1) | (x >>> 31); }
      let [a, b, c, e, f] = h;
      for (let j = 0; j < 80; j++) {
        const k = j < 20 ? ((b & c) | (~b & e)) + 0x5a827999 : j < 40 ? (b ^ c ^ e) + 0x6ed9eba1 : j < 60 ? ((b & c) | (b & e) | (c & e)) + 0x8f1bbcdc : (b ^ c ^ e) + 0xca62c1d6;
        const t = (((a << 5) | (a >>> 27)) + k + f + w[j]) | 0;
        f = e; e = c; c = (b << 30) | (b >>> 2); b = a; a = t;
      }
      h[0] += a; h[1] += b; h[2] += c; h[3] += e; h[4] += f;
      return;
    }
    for (let j = 16; j < 64; j++) {
      const x = w[j - 15], y = w[j - 2];
      w[j] = (((x >>> 7) | (x << 25)) ^ ((x >>> 18) | (x << 14)) ^ (x >>> 3)) + w[j - 7] + (((y >>> 17) | (y << 15)) ^ ((y >>> 19) | (y << 13)) ^ (y >>> 10)) + w[j - 16];
    }
    let [a, b, c, e, f, g, k, l] = h;
    for (let j = 0; j < 64; j++) {
      const t1 = (l + (((f >>> 6) | (f << 26)) ^ ((f >>> 11) | (f << 21)) ^ ((f >>> 25) | (f << 7))) + ((f & g) ^ (~f & k)) + K256[j] + w[j]) | 0;
      const t2 = ((((a >>> 2) | (a << 30)) ^ ((a >>> 13) | (a << 19)) ^ ((a >>> 22) | (a << 10))) + ((a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c))) | 0;
      l = k; k = g; g = f; f = (e + t1) | 0; e = c; c = b; b = a; a = (t1 + t2) | 0;
    }
    h[0] += a; h[1] += b; h[2] += c; h[3] += e; h[4] += f; h[5] += g; h[6] += k; h[7] += l;
  }
}

/** @param {'md5'|'sha1'|'sha256'} kind */
export function createHash(kind) { return new BlockHash(kind); }
export function hash(kind, bytes) { return new BlockHash(kind).update(bytes).digest(); }

const DIGEST_OIDS = { '1.2.840.113549.2.5': 'md5', '1.3.14.3.2.26': 'sha1', '2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1': 'sha256' };

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- DER
/** One DER element at `o`: { tag, start (of the header), hdr (header length), len (content length), end }. */
export function derAt(b, o) {
  if (o + 2 > b.length) throw new Error('DER: truncated');
  const tag = b[o]; let len = b[o + 1], hdr = 2;
  if (len === 0x80) throw new Error('DER: indefinite length');
  if (len & 0x80) { const n = len & 0x7f; if (n > 4) throw new Error('DER: length too long'); len = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) len = len * 256 + b[o + 2 + i]; hdr += n; }
  if (o + hdr + len > b.length) throw new Error('DER: element past its container');
  return { tag, start: o, hdr, len, end: o + hdr + len, body: o + hdr };
}
/** The children of a constructed element. */
export function derChildren(b, e) { const out = []; for (let o = e.body; o < e.end;) { const c = derAt(b, o); out.push(c); o = c.end; } return out; }
function oid(b, e) {
  if (e.tag !== 6) throw new Error('DER: OID expected');
  const out = [], first = b[e.body]; out.push(Math.floor(first / 40), first % 40);
  let v = 0; for (let i = e.body + 1; i < e.end; i++) { v = v * 128 + (b[i] & 0x7f); if (!(b[i] & 0x80)) { out.push(v); v = 0; } }
  return out.join('.');
}
const bytesEq = (a, b) => a.length === b.length && a.every((v, i) => v === b[i]);
const toBig = (u8) => { let x = 0n; for (const v of u8) x = (x << 8n) | BigInt(v); return x; };
function modPow(base, exp, m) { let r = 1n; base %= m; while (exp > 0n) { if (exp & 1n) r = (r * base) % m; base = (base * base) % m; exp >>= 1n; } return r; }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- PE
/** The certificate table and the Authenticode digest's holes of a PE file, or null when it is not a PE file. */
export function peLayout(f) {
  if (f.length < 0x40 || f[0] !== 0x4d || f[1] !== 0x5a) return null;
  const dv = new DataView(f.buffer, f.byteOffset, f.byteLength);
  const pe = dv.getUint32(0x3c, true);
  if (pe + 26 > f.length || dv.getUint32(pe, true) !== 0x4550) return null;
  const opt = pe + 24, magic = dv.getUint16(opt, true);
  const dirs = opt + (magic === 0x20b ? 112 : 96), checksum = opt + 64, secEntry = dirs + 4 * 8;
  if (secEntry + 8 > f.length) return null; // (a truncated or malformed header: not a PE file — never a read past the buffer)
  const nDirs = dv.getUint32(dirs - 4, true);
  const certOff = nDirs > 4 ? dv.getUint32(secEntry, true) : 0, certLen = nDirs > 4 ? dv.getUint32(secEntry + 4, true) : 0;
  return { checksum, secEntry, certOff, certLen };
}
/** Authenticode image digest: every byte of the file except the checksum, the certificate table's directory entry and the table. */
export function imageDigest(f, kind, L = peLayout(f)) {
  const h = createHash(kind), end = L.certLen ? L.certOff : f.length;
  h.update(f.subarray(0, L.checksum)); h.update(f.subarray(L.checksum + 4, L.secEntry)); h.update(f.subarray(L.secEntry + 8, end));
  if (L.certLen && L.certOff + L.certLen < f.length) h.update(f.subarray(L.certOff + L.certLen));
  // (data between the end of the image and the table, not a multiple of 8 bytes, is padded with zeros by signing tools)
  return h.digest();
}

/**
 * WinVerifyTrust's answer for a file's contents (WINTRUST_ACTION_GENERIC_VERIFY_V2 on a file).
 * @param {Uint8Array} f the file, or its first bytes (the headers) with `size` its whole size: then answered only
 * when the certificate table is absent or does not fit in the file
 * @param {number} [size] @returns {{ status: number, why: string }}
 */
export function verifyAuthenticode(f, size = f.length) {
  const L = peLayout(f);
  if (!L) return { status: TRUST_E_SUBJECT_FORM_UNKNOWN, why: 'not a PE file' };
  if (!L.certLen || !L.certOff) return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'no certificate table' };
  if (L.certOff + L.certLen > size || L.certLen < 8) return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'certificate table past the end of the file' }; // (no signature can be read)
  if (L.certOff + L.certLen > f.length) return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'certificate table not in the bytes given (the whole file is needed)' };
  const dv = new DataView(f.buffer, f.byteOffset, f.byteLength);
  // WIN_CERTIFICATE entries (8-byte aligned): the first PKCS#7 one (revision 0x200, type 2) is the signature
  let pk = null;
  for (let o = L.certOff; o + 8 <= L.certOff + L.certLen;) {
    const len = dv.getUint32(o, true), type = dv.getUint16(o + 6, true);
    if (len < 8) break;
    if (type === 2) { pk = f.subarray(o + 8, Math.min(o + len, f.length)); break; }
    o += (len + 7) & ~7;
  }
  if (!pk) return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'no PKCS#7 certificate' };
  try {
    const ci = derAt(pk, 0), [ctype, ctx] = derChildren(pk, ci);
    if (oid(pk, ctype) !== '1.2.840.113549.1.7.2') return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'not SignedData' };
    const sd = derChildren(pk, derAt(pk, ctx.body));
    const content = derChildren(pk, sd[2]);
    if (oid(pk, content[0]) !== '1.3.6.1.4.1.311.2.1.4') return { status: TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE, why: 'not SpcIndirectDataContent' };
    const spc = derAt(pk, content[1].body), [, digestInfo] = derChildren(pk, spc);
    const [alg, dig] = derChildren(pk, digestInfo), kind = DIGEST_OIDS[oid(pk, derChildren(pk, alg)[0])];
    if (!kind) return { status: TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST, why: 'unknown digest algorithm' };
    const want = pk.subarray(dig.body, dig.end), got = imageDigest(f, kind, L);
    if (!bytesEq(want, got)) return { status: TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST, why: `${kind} image digest differs` };
    // the signer: certificates [0], signerInfos SET (last element)
    let certs = [], signerSet = sd[sd.length - 1];
    for (const e of sd.slice(3)) if (e.tag === 0xa0) certs = derChildren(pk, e);
    const signers = derChildren(pk, signerSet);
    if (!signers.length) return { status: TRUST_E_NO_SIGNER_CERT, why: 'no signer' };
    const si = derChildren(pk, signers[0]);
    // version, issuerAndSerialNumber, digestAlgorithm, [0] authenticatedAttributes, digestEncryptionAlgorithm, encryptedDigest
    const ias = derChildren(pk, si[1]), siKind = DIGEST_OIDS[oid(pk, derChildren(pk, si[2])[0])];
    const attrs = si[3]?.tag === 0xa0 ? si[3] : null, sig = si[attrs ? 5 : 4];
    if (!siKind || !sig) return { status: TRUST_E_FAIL, why: 'malformed signer' };
    let signed;
    if (attrs) {
      let md = null;
      for (const a of derChildren(pk, attrs)) { const [t, vals] = derChildren(pk, a); if (oid(pk, t) === '1.2.840.113549.1.9.4') { const v = derChildren(pk, vals)[0]; md = pk.subarray(v.body, v.end); } }
      // (the content's digest: the SpcIndirectDataContent's value without its own tag and length)
      if (!md || !bytesEq(md, hash(siKind, pk.subarray(spc.body, spc.end)))) return { status: TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST, why: 'messageDigest attribute differs' };
      const enc = pk.slice(attrs.start, attrs.end); enc[0] = 0x31; // (signed as a SET OF)
      signed = hash(siKind, enc);
    } else signed = hash(siKind, pk.subarray(spc.body, spc.end));
    // the signer's certificate: the one with that issuer and serial number
    let key = null;
    for (const c of certs) {
      if (c.tag !== 0x30) continue;
      const tbs = derChildren(pk, derChildren(pk, c)[0]), off = tbs[0].tag === 0xa0 ? 1 : 0;
      const serial = tbs[off], issuer = tbs[off + 2];
      const ser2 = ias[1], iss2 = ias[0];
      if (!bytesEq(pk.subarray(serial.start, serial.end), pk.subarray(ser2.start, ser2.end)) || !bytesEq(pk.subarray(issuer.start, issuer.end), pk.subarray(iss2.start, iss2.end))) continue;
      const spki = derChildren(pk, tbs[off + 5]);
      if (oid(pk, derChildren(pk, spki[0])[0]) !== '1.2.840.113549.1.1.1') return { status: TRUST_E_FAIL, why: 'signer key is not RSA' };
      const bits = spki[1], rsa = derChildren(pk, derAt(pk, bits.body + 1));
      key = { n: toBig(pk.subarray(rsa[0].body, rsa[0].end)), e: toBig(pk.subarray(rsa[1].body, rsa[1].end)), bytes: rsa[0].len - (pk[rsa[0].body] === 0 ? 1 : 0) };
      break;
    }
    if (!key) return { status: TRUST_E_NO_SIGNER_CERT, why: 'signer certificate not found' };
    // RSA PKCS#1 v1.5: 00 01 FF.. 00 DigestInfo
    const m = modPow(toBig(pk.subarray(sig.body, sig.end)), key.e, key.n);
    const em = new Uint8Array(key.bytes); let x = m; for (let i = em.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { em[i] = Number(x & 0xffn); x >>= 8n; }
    if (em[0] !== 0 || em[1] !== 1) return { status: TRUST_E_FAIL, why: 'signature does not verify' };
    let i = 2; while (i < em.length && em[i] === 0xff) i++;
    if (em[i] !== 0 || i < 10) return { status: TRUST_E_FAIL, why: 'signature does not verify' };
    const di = derChildren(em, derAt(em, i + 1)), d2 = em.subarray(di[1].body, di[1].end);
    if (DIGEST_OIDS[oid(em, derChildren(em, di[0])[0])] !== siKind || !bytesEq(d2, signed)) return { status: TRUST_E_FAIL, why: 'signature does not verify' };
    return { status: 0, why: `signed (${kind})` };
  } catch (e) {
    return { status: TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST, why: `malformed signature (${e.message})` };
  }
}
```

`src/win32/com.js`:

```js
// COM plumbing: interfaces are vtables of API thunks living in guest memory; objects are small
// guest blocks [vtable, marker, id] whose methods dispatch to JS implementations. Unimplemented
// methods are traced (once per method) and return E_NOTIMPL so the caller keeps going.
import { snapshotClass } from '../core/snapshot.js';
import { E } from './errors.js';
import { COM_MARKER, COM_REFS } from '../cpu/jit/runtime.js';
/** 'comx' log kind: the COM trace without the per-draw state setters, draws, buffer locks and reference counting */
const COM_SITE_MAX = 20; // 'comx': calls logged per (method, call site)
const COM_QUIET = /^(Set(RenderState|TextureStageState|SamplerState|Texture|Transform|StreamSource|Indices|FVF|VertexShader|PixelShader|VertexDeclaration|Material|Light|VertexShaderConstantF|PixelShaderConstantF|Viewport|SoftwareVertexProcessing|ClipPlane|ScissorRect)|LightEnable|Draw\w*|Get(Transform|RenderState|TextureStageState|Desc|LevelDesc|LevelCount|DeviceCaps|DisplayMode|Direct3D|Type|CurrentPosition|Status|DeviceData|DeviceState)|AddRef|Release|QueryInterface|Lock|Unlock|TestCooperativeLevel|BeginScene|EndScene|Present|Clear)$/;

export const S_OK = 0, S_FALSE = 1, E_NOTIMPL = 0x80004001, E_NOINTERFACE = 0x80004002, E_POINTER = 0x80004003, E_FAIL = 0x80004005, E_INVALIDARG = 0x80070057, E_OUTOFMEMORY = 0x8007000e, CLASS_E_NOAGGREGATION = 0x80040110, REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG = 0x80040154;
export const IID_IUnknown = '00000000-0000-0000-c000-000000000046';
const MARKER = COM_MARKER; // '!COM'

/**
 * GUID in guest memory -> canonical lowercase string. The strings of the GUIDs met are kept by their four words (a
 * QueryInterface asks for the same few IIDs again and again: no string built per call); GUIDs past GUID_CACHE_MAX
 * distinct ones are formatted each time.
 */
export function readGuid(mem, a) {
  const u8 = mem.u8, p = a >>> 0;
  if (!u8 || p + 16 > u8.length) return formatGuid(mem, a);
  const w0 = (u8[p] | (u8[p + 1] << 8) | (u8[p + 2] << 16) | (u8[p + 3] << 24)) | 0, w1 = (u8[p + 4] | (u8[p + 5] << 8) | (u8[p + 6] << 16) | (u8[p + 7] << 24)) | 0;
  const w2 = (u8[p + 8] | (u8[p + 9] << 8) | (u8[p + 10] << 16) | (u8[p + 11] << 24)) | 0, w3 = (u8[p + 12] | (u8[p + 13] << 8) | (u8[p + 14] << 16) | (u8[p + 15] << 24)) | 0;
  let list = GUID_CACHE.get(w0);
  if (list !== undefined) for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i += 4) if (list[i] === w1 && list[i + 1] === w2 && list[i + 2] === w3) return list[i + 3];
  const s = formatGuid(mem, a);
  if (guidCached < GUID_CACHE_MAX) { if (list === undefined) GUID_CACHE.set(w0, (list = [])); list.push(w1, w2, w3, s); guidCached++; }
  return s;
}
const GUID_CACHE = new Map(), GUID_CACHE_MAX = 4096;
let guidCached = 0; // snapshot: cache of formatted GUID strings (a pure function of the bytes)
function formatGuid(mem, a) {
  const h = (v, n) => v.toString(16).padStart(n, '0');
  const b = mem.bytes(a, 16);
  return `${h(mem.read32(a), 8)}-${h(mem.read16(a + 4), 4)}-${h(mem.read16(a + 6), 4)}-${h(b[8], 2)}${h(b[9], 2)}-${Array.from(b.subarray(10, 16), (x) => h(x, 2)).join('')}`;
}
export function writeGuid(mem, a, s) {
  const p = s.toLowerCase().split('-');
  mem.write32(a, parseInt(p[0], 16)); mem.write16(a + 4, parseInt(p[1], 16)); mem.write16(a + 6, parseInt(p[2], 16));
  const tail = p[3] + p[4];
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) mem.write8(a + 8 + i, parseInt(tail.slice(2 * i, 2 * i + 2), 16));
}

/**
 * The JavaScript side of a guest COM object. One class (one shape, the reference count's accessors on the prototype):
 * an object literal with its own getter / setter closures gave every object a map of its own, and the Direct3D
 * setters' AddRef / Release of the textures and buffers they bind went through megamorphic property accesses.
 */
class ComObject {
  constructor(mem, ptr, iface, impl, id, proc) {
    this.mem = mem; this.ptr = ptr; this.iface = iface; this.impl = impl; this.id = id; this.proc = proc;
    /** @type {any[]|null} methods resolved by index (Com.dispatch) */
    this.fns = null;
    /** impl.iids as lowercase IIDs (Com.supports), and the array they were made from */
    this.iidsNorm = undefined; this.iidsOf = undefined;
  }
  /** the reference count, in guest memory (the JIT's AddRef / Release fast path updates it there) */
  get refs() { return this.mem.read32(this.ptr + COM_REFS) | 0; }
  set refs(v) { this.mem.write32(this.ptr + COM_REFS, v >>> 0); }
}
snapshotClass(ComObject, { skip: ['fns'], init: (o) => { o.fns = null; } }); // (snapshots, core/vm-snapshot.js: fns a cache)

export class Com {
  /** @param {import('../core/vm.js').Vm} vm */
  constructor(vm) {
    this.failedOnce = new Set(); // interface::method=hresult already reported
    /** (the same by method descriptor and code, for a quick check: transient, not in snapshots) */
    this.failedSeen = new Map();
    this.comSites = new Map(); // 'comx' trace: calls logged per method@site
    this.vm = vm;
    this.mem = vm.mem;
    this.api = vm.api;
    /** @type {Map<string, Interface>} name -> interface */
    this.interfaces = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<string, Interface>} iid -> interface */
    this.byIid = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<number, ComObject>} guest pointer -> object */
    this.objects = new Map();
    /** @type {Map<string, (ctx, iid) => number|null>} clsid -> factory returning an object pointer */
    this.classes = new Map();
    this.nextId = 1;
    this.tracedMissing = new Set();
    this.interface('IUnknown', IID_IUnknown, null, [['QueryInterface', 2], ['AddRef', 0], ['Release', 0]]);
    // (a method's handler is defined when its interface first gets a vtable: a restored Vm defines it by name)
    this.api.lazyDefs?.set('com.dll', (fname) => {
      const [name, method] = fname.split('::'), iface = this.interfaces.get(name), i = iface?.methods.findIndex((m) => m.name === method) ?? -1;
      if (i >= 0) this.defineMethod(iface, i);
      return this.api.lookup('com', fname);
    });
  }

  /** The API handler of method `i` of `iface` (its thunk dispatches to the object's implementation). */
  defineMethod(iface, i) {
    const m = iface.methods[i], fname = `${iface.name}::${m.name}`;
    if (!this.api.lookup('com', fname)) this.api.define('com', { [fname]: [m.argc + 1, (c) => this.dispatch(c, iface, i), { com: { iface, index: i } }] });
    return fname;
  }

  /**
   * Declare an interface. `methods`: [name, argc] in vtable order (after the parent's methods).
   * @returns {Interface}
   */
  interface(name, iid, parent, methods) {
    const p = parent ? this.interfaces.get(parent) : null;
    const all = [...(p ? p.methods : []), ...methods.map(([n, argc]) => ({ name: n, argc }))];
    const iface = { name, iid: iid?.toLowerCase() ?? null, parent: p, methods: all, vtable: 0 };
    this.interfaces.set(name, iface);
    if (iface.iid) this.byIid.set(iface.iid, iface);
    return iface;
  }

  /** Register a CoCreateInstance class. factory(ctx, iid) -> guest object pointer (or null to fail). */
  registerClass(clsid, factory) { this.classes.set(clsid.toLowerCase(), factory); }
  /** 'comx' trace: true once method@site has been logged COM_SITE_MAX times */
  comSiteSeen(name, site) { const k = `${name}@${site}`, n = this.comSites.get(k) ?? 0; this.comSites.set(k, n + 1); return n >= COM_SITE_MAX; }

  /** Allocate the vtable of an interface once: one API thunk per method. */
  vtableOf(proc, iface) {
    if (iface.vtable) return iface.vtable;
    const n = iface.methods.length;
    const vt = proc.processHeap.alloc(n * 4);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) this.mem.write32(vt + 4 * i, this.api.thunkFor('com', this.defineMethod(iface, i)));
    iface.vtable = vt;
    return vt;
  }

  /**
   * Create a guest object exposing `iface` (an Interface or its name), implemented by `impl`.
   * `impl` may list extra interface names it answers to in `impl.iids` (array of IIDs or names).
   * @returns {number} guest pointer (refcount 1)
   */
  create(proc, iface, impl, extra = 0) {
    if (typeof iface === 'string') iface = this.interfaces.get(iface);
    // [vtable, marker, id, a word for the object's fast paths (runtime.js: effect handle block, device state shadow,
    // surface description), reference count, an effect's commit list] — the count in guest memory: AddRef/Release run
    // on the JIT's fast path (runtime.js FID_ADDREF); `extra` bytes after them for the implementation (freed with it)
    const ptr = proc.processHeap.alloc(24 + extra);
    this.mem.write32(ptr, this.vtableOf(proc, iface));
    this.mem.write32(ptr + 4, MARKER);
    this.mem.write32(ptr + 8, this.nextId);
    this.mem.write32(ptr + 12, 0);
    this.mem.write32(ptr + COM_REFS, 1);
    this.mem.write32(ptr + 20, 0); // (runtime.js COMMIT_LIST: an effect's)
    const obj = new ComObject(this.mem, ptr, iface, impl, this.nextId++, proc);
    this.objects.set(ptr, obj);
    impl.comObject = obj;
    return ptr;
  }

  /** JS object behind a guest interface pointer (null if unknown). */
  objectAt(ptr) { return this.objects.get(ptr >>> 0) ?? null; }
  implAt(ptr) { return this.objects.get(ptr >>> 0)?.impl ?? null; }

  addRef(obj) { return ++obj.refs; }
  release(obj) {
    if (--obj.refs > 0) return obj.refs;
    // (an object another one owns — a device's back buffers, a texture's levels — stays valid at the same address
    // without references while its owner lives, as Direct3D's do: software keeps such pointers after Release)
    if (obj.impl.keepAlive) { obj.refs = 0; return 0; }
    this.dispose(obj);
    return 0;
  }
  /** The owner of a kept-alive object is gone: the object is destroyed now if nothing references it. */
  unpin(impl) {
    const obj = impl?.comObject;
    if (obj && this.objects.get(obj.ptr) === obj && obj.refs <= 0) this.dispose(obj);
  }
  dispose(obj) {
    this.objects.delete(obj.ptr);
    this.mem.write32(obj.ptr + 4, 0); // (no longer an object for the fast paths)
    // (debugging, ?dbg=ORTHROS_RELEASE_WATCH=1: the guest memory of a released object is reused only 4096 releases later —
    // a call through a pointer kept after the release then reaches no object, reported, instead of the next object)
    try { obj.impl.destroy?.(obj); } finally {
      // (the words the fast paths follow — runtime.js: +12 an effect's handle block, a device's shadow, a surface's
      // description; +20 an effect's commit list — no longer lead to the blocks the implementation freed)
      this.mem.write32(obj.ptr + 12, 0); this.mem.write32(obj.ptr + 20, 0);
      if (globalThis.ORTHROS_RELEASE_WATCH) { (this.quarantine ??= []).push(obj); if (this.quarantine.length > 4096) { const o = this.quarantine.shift(); o.proc.processHeap.free_(o.ptr); } }
      else obj.proc.processHeap.free_(obj.ptr);
    }
    return 0;
  }

  /** Does `obj` implement the interface with this IID? (its own chain, plus impl.iids) */
  supports(obj, iid) {
    if (iid === IID_IUnknown) return true;
    for (let i = obj.iface; i; i = i.parent) if (i.iid === iid) return true;
    const iids = obj.impl.iids;
    if (!iids) return false;
    // impl.iids normalized once per array (the implementations assign a new array when it changes)
    let norm = obj.iidsNorm;
    if (norm === undefined || obj.iidsOf !== iids || norm.length !== iids.length) { norm = obj.iidsNorm = iids.map((x) => (x.includes('-') ? x.toLowerCase() : this.interfaces.get(x)?.iid)); obj.iidsOf = iids; }
    for (let k = 0; k < norm.length; k++) if (norm[k] === iid) return true;
    return false;
  }

  dispatch(ctx, iface, index) {
    const m = iface.methods[index];
    const self = ctx.arg(0);
    const obj = this.objects.get(self);
    if (!obj) { const dead = this.quarantine?.find((o) => o.ptr === self); this.vm.warn(`COM: ${iface.name}::${m.name} on unknown object ${self.toString(16)} from ${ctx.proc.symbolize(ctx.retAddr)}${dead ? ` (released: ${dead.iface.name} #${dead.id})` : ''} [t${ctx.thread.id}]`); return E_POINTER; }
    switch (index) {
      case 0: { // QueryInterface(riid, ppv)
        const riid = readGuid(this.mem, ctx.arg(1)), ppv = ctx.arg(2);
        if (!ppv) return E_POINTER;
        if (this.supports(obj, riid)) { this.mem.write32(ppv, self); this.addRef(obj); return S_OK; }
        const custom = obj.impl.queryInterface?.(ctx, riid, obj);
        if (custom) { this.mem.write32(ppv, custom); return S_OK; }
        this.mem.write32(ppv, 0);
        this.vm.log('com', `${iface.name}::QueryInterface(${this.byIid.get(riid)?.name ?? riid}) -> E_NOINTERFACE`);
        return E_NOINTERFACE;
      }
      case 1: return this.addRef(obj);
      case 2: return this.release(obj);
    }
    // the method resolved once per object (a property lookup by name is megamorphic across implementations)
    const fns = obj.fns ?? (obj.fns = []);
    let fn = fns[index];
    if (fn === undefined) fn = fns[index] = obj.impl[m.name] ?? null;
    if (typeof fn !== 'function') {
      const key = `${iface.name}::${m.name}`;
      if (!this.tracedMissing.has(key)) { this.tracedMissing.add(key); this.vm.warn(`COM: ${key} not implemented (called from ${ctx.proc.symbolize(ctx.retAddr)})`); }
      const args = []; for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(m.argc, 8); i++) args.push('0x' + ctx.arg(1 + i).toString(16));
      this.vm.log('com', `${key}(${args.join(', ')}) -> E_NOTIMPL`);
      return obj.impl.notImpl ?? E_NOTIMPL;
    }
    if (this.vm.traceCom && !(this.vm.traceComQuiet && (COM_QUIET.test(m.name) || this.comSiteSeen(m.name, ctx.retAddr)))) { const args = []; for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(m.argc, 8); i++) args.push('0x' + ctx.arg(1 + i).toString(16)); this.vm.logFn('com', `${iface.name}::${m.name}(${args.join(', ')}) from ${ctx.proc.symbolize(ctx.retAddr)}`); }
    const r = fn.call(obj.impl, ctx, obj);
    if (typeof r === 'number' && (r >>> 0) >= 0x80000000) this.failed(ctx, iface, m, r);
    return r === undefined ? S_OK : r;
  }
  /** a failed HRESULT: traced once per method/value (fidelity diagnostics) */
  failed(ctx, iface, m, r) {
    // (a method that keeps failing — thousands of times per second — is checked without building its key: the result
    // codes seen per method, transient, `failedSeen`)
    // (by interface, then method: an inherited method's descriptor is shared by every interface derived from its parent)
    let byM = this.failedSeen.get(iface);
    if (byM === undefined) this.failedSeen.set(iface, byM = new Map());
    let seen = byM.get(m);
    if (seen === undefined) byM.set(m, seen = new Set());
    else if (seen.has(r >>> 0)) return;
    seen.add(r >>> 0);
    const k = `${iface.name}::${m.name}=${(r >>> 0).toString(16)}`;
    if (!this.failedOnce.has(k)) { this.failedOnce.add(k); this.vm.log('gfx', `com: ${iface.name}::${m.name} -> 0x${(r >>> 0).toString(16)} (first from ${ctx.proc.symbolize(ctx.retAddr)})`); }
  }
  /**
   * A call the JIT queued (Vm.drainDeferred), on the object `self`: its method resolved before, called directly; anything
   * else (an unknown object, a method not resolved yet or missing, COM tracing on) through dispatch. The result is not
   * returned: a queued call's caller already received D3D_OK.
   */
  callQueued(ctx, self, iface, index) {
    const obj = this.objects.get(self);
    const fn = obj !== undefined && !this.vm.traceCom ? obj.fns?.[index] : undefined;
    if (typeof fn !== 'function') { this.dispatch(ctx, iface, index); return; }
    const r = fn.call(obj.impl, ctx, obj);
    if (typeof r === 'number' && (r >>> 0) >= 0x80000000) this.failed(ctx, iface, iface.methods[index], r);
  }

  /** CoCreateInstance backend. */
  createInstance(ctx, clsid, iid, ppv) {
    const f = this.classes.get(clsid.toLowerCase());
    if (!f) return undefined; // not registered: the caller reports it
    const ptr = f(ctx, iid.toLowerCase());
    if (!ptr) return REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG;
    const obj = this.objects.get(ptr);
    if (obj && !this.supports(obj, iid)) { this.release(obj); this.mem.write32(ppv, 0); return E_NOINTERFACE; }
    this.mem.write32(ppv, ptr);
    return S_OK;
  }
}

/**
 * @typedef {{ name: string, iid: string|null, parent: Interface|null, methods: {name: string, argc: number}[], vtable: number }} Interface
 * @typedef {{ ptr: number, iface: Interface, impl: any, refs: number, id: number, proc: any }} ComObject
 */
export { E };
```

```js
// Call context handed to API handlers: argument access, string helpers, return conventions.
import { R } from '../cpu/state.js';

export class Ctx {
  /** @param {import('../core/vm.js').Vm} vm */
  constructor(vm) {
    this.vm = vm;
    this.mem = vm.mem;
    this.proc = vm.proc;
    /** @type {import('./process.js').Thread} */
    this.thread = null;
    this.cpu = null;
    /** address of the return address slot (ESP at thunk entry) */
    this.sp = 0;
    this.def = null;
  }

  bind(thread, def) {
    this.thread = thread;
    this.cpu = thread.cpu;
    this.sp = thread.cpu.esp;
    this.def = def;
    this.proc = this.vm.proc;
    return this;
  }

  /** i-th 32-bit stack argument. */
  arg(i) { return this.mem.read32(this.sp + 4 + 4 * i); }
  /** i-th argument as signed int32 */
  sarg(i) { return this.mem.readS32(this.sp + 4 + 4 * i); }
  /** i-th argument as a 64-bit value (two slots) */
  arg64(i) { return this.mem.read64(this.sp + 4 + 4 * i); }
  /** i-th argument as f64 (two slots) / f32 (one slot) */
  argF64(i) { return this.mem.readF64(this.sp + 4 + 4 * i); }
  argF32(i) { return this.mem.readF32(this.sp + 4 + 4 * i); }
  /** ANSI string argument (null -> null) */
  str(i, max = 0x10000) { const a = this.arg(i); return a ? this.mem.readCString(a, max) : null; }
  /** Wide string argument */
  wstr(i, max = 0x10000) { const a = this.arg(i); return a ? this.mem.readWString(a, max) : null; }
  /** Return address of the call */
  get retAddr() { return this.mem.read32(this.sp); }

  // Registers (for handlers implementing register conventions or __fastcall)
  get eax() { return this.cpu.eax; } set eax(v) { this.cpu.eax = v; }
  get ecx() { return this.cpu.ecx; } set ecx(v) { this.cpu.ecx = v; }
  get edx() { return this.cpu.edx; } set edx(v) { this.cpu.edx = v; }

  /** Set the Win32 last error for the calling thread. */
  setLastError(code) { this.thread.lastError = code >>> 0; }
  /** Return value helper: 0 with last error set. */
  fail(code) { this.setLastError(code); return 0; }

  /** Write an out parameter (pointer arg i) if non-null. */
  out32(i, v) { const a = this.arg(i); if (a) this.mem.write32(a, v >>> 0); }
  out16(i, v) { const a = this.arg(i); if (a) this.mem.write16(a, v & 0xffff); }
  out64(i, v) { const a = this.arg(i); if (a) this.mem.write64(a, BigInt.asUintN(64, BigInt(v))); }

  /** Return a double in ST(0) (cdecl/stdcall functions returning double/float). */
  retDouble(v) {
    const cpu = this.cpu;
    cpu.fpuTop = (cpu.fpuTop - 1) & 7;
    cpu.setSt(0, v);
    cpu.fpuTw |= 1 << cpu.fpuTop;
  }
  /** Pop the x87 stack (for functions taking their argument in ST(0)). */
  popFpu() {
    const cpu = this.cpu;
    cpu.fpuTw &= ~(1 << cpu.fpuTop);
    cpu.fpuTop = (cpu.fpuTop + 1) & 7;
  }

  /** Log helper (API trace). */
  log(...a) { this.vm.log('api', ...a); }
}
```

```js
export function noteState(dev, group, s, v) {
  // (numeric keys: this runs for every state change — group name and state number joined only for the report)
  const gid = STATE_GROUPS.get(group) ?? STATE_GROUPS.set(group, STATE_GROUP_NAMES.push(group) - 1).get(group);

  let set = m.get(k); if (!set) m.set(k, (set = new Set()));
  if (set.size < 12) set.add(v >>> 0);
}
const STATE_GROUPS = new Map(), STATE_GROUP_NAMES = [];

/**
 * The tokens of a shader in guest memory, up to its end token: comment blocks (constant tables, preshaders — whose
 * data may contain 0x0000FFFF) are skipped as a whole, instructions by their length (SM 2+) or their parameter tokens
 * (SM 1.x: bit 31 set; DEF's four values taken as such).
 */
export function readShaderTokens(mem, addr, max = 65536) {
  const out = [mem.read32(addr)];
  const major = (out[0] >> 8) & 0xff;
  let p = addr + 4;
  while (out.length < max) {
    const t = mem.read32(p);
    out.push(t); p += 4;
    if (t === 0x0000ffff) break;
    if ((t & 0xffff) === 0xfffe) { const n = t >>> 16; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out.push(mem.read32(p + 4 * i)); p += 4 * n; continue; }
    if (major >= 2) { const n = (t >> 24) & 0xf; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out.push(mem.read32(p + 4 * i)); p += 4 * n; continue; }
    if ((t & 0xffff) === 81) { for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) out.push(mem.read32(p + 4 * i)); p += 20; continue; } // (def: register + 4 floats)
    while (out.length < max) { const q = mem.read32(p); if (!(q & 0x80000000)) break; out.push(q); p += 4; }
  }
  return out;
}

}

export function surfacePitch(fmt, w) {
  switch (fmt) {
    case FMT.DXT1: return Math.max(1, (w + 3) >> 2) * 8;
    case FMT.DXT2: case FMT.DXT3: case FMT.DXT4: case FMT.DXT5: return Math.max(1, (w + 3) >> 2) * 16;
    case FMT.R8G8B8: return w * 3;
    case FMT.A8: case FMT.L8: case FMT.P8: case FMT.A4L4: case FMT.R3G3B2: return w;
    case FMT.A16B16G16R16: return w * 8;
    case FMT.L16: case FMT.R5G6B5: case FMT.X1R5G5B5: case FMT.A1R5G5B5: case FMT.A4R4G4B4: case FMT.A8L8: case FMT.D16: case FMT.D16_LOCKABLE: case FMT.D15S1: case FMT.V8U8: case FMT.L6V5U5: case FMT.A8R3G3B2: case FMT.X4R4G4B4: case FMT.INDEX16: case FMT.UYVY: case FMT.YUY2: return w * 2;
    default: return w * 4;
  }
}
export function surfaceBytes(fmt, w, h) {
  const rows = fmt === FMT.DXT1 || fmt === FMT.DXT2 || fmt === FMT.DXT3 || fmt === FMT.DXT4 || fmt === FMT.DXT5 ? Math.max(1, (h + 3) >> 2) : h;
  return surfacePitch(fmt, w) * rows;
}

/**
 * Shared Direct3D core (resources in guest memory, device state model, adapter helpers) used by

export function d3dCore(vm) {
  if (vm.d3dCore) return vm.d3dCore;

  const displayMode = () => { const d = vm.host?.display; return { width: d?.width ?? 1024, height: d?.height ?? 768, refresh: 60, format: FMT.X8R8G8B8 }; };
  const writeMode = (a, m) => { mem.write32(a, m.width); mem.write32(a + 4, m.height); mem.write32(a + 8, m.refresh); mem.write32(a + 12, m.format); };

    w32(36, 0x1 | 0x10 | 0x80 | 0x100 | 0x2000 | 0x4000 | 0x10000 | 0x20000 | 0x100000 | 0x200000 | 0x400000); // RasterCaps

    const filt = 0x100 | 0x200 | 0x400 | 0x10000 | 0x20000 | 0x1000000 | 0x2000000 | 0x4000000;

    w32(76, 0x3f); w32(80, 0x3f); // TextureAddressCaps, Volume

    w32(136, 0xff); // StencilCaps

    SetPrivateData(c) { const g = readGuid(mem, c.arg(1)), p = c.arg(2), n = c.arg(3), flags = c.arg(4); this.privateData.set(g, flags & 1 ? { iunknown: mem.read32(p) } : { data: mem.bytes(p, n).slice() }); return D3D_OK; }
    GetPrivateData(c) { const g = readGuid(mem, c.arg(1)), p = c.arg(2), ps = c.arg(3); const d = this.privateData.get(g); if (!d) return D3DERR_NOTFOUND; const bytes = d.data ?? new Uint8Array(4); const size = mem.read32(ps); mem.write32(ps, bytes.length); if (size < bytes.length) return D3DERR_MOREDATA; if (d.data) mem.writeBytes(p, d.data); else mem.write32(p, d.iunknown); return D3D_OK; }

      for (const f of this.faces ?? []) for (const l of f) com.unpin?.(l);
```
