`tests/opfs-store.test.js`:

```js
// The OPFS block store's index log (format 3): records appended at sync points (every 2 s or 256 blocks, or forced),
// replayed at open up to the last complete undamaged record; a v2 JSON index migrated once. Synchronous access handles
// are faked in memory (counting their writes and flushes).
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { OpfsBlockStore, SYNC_BLOCKS, SYNC_MS, blockHash } from '../src/vfs/opfs-store.js';

class FakeHandle {
  constructor() { this.b = new Uint8Array(0); this.writes = 0; this.flushes = 0; this.truncates = 0; }
  getSize() { return this.b.length; }
  read(out, { at }) { const n = Math.max(0, Math.min(out.length, this.b.length - at)); out.set(this.b.subarray(at, at + n)); return n; }
  write(src, { at }) { this.writes++; if (at + src.length > this.b.length) { const nb = new Uint8Array(at + src.length); nb.set(this.b); this.b = nb; } this.b.set(src, at); return src.length; }
  truncate(n) { this.truncates++; const nb = new Uint8Array(n); nb.set(this.b.subarray(0, Math.min(n, this.b.length))); this.b = nb; }
  flush() { this.flushes++; } close() {}
}

/** a fake OPFS (one directory) around `fn(files)` */
async function withFakeOpfs(fn) {
  const files = new Map();
  const dir = {
    getFileHandle: async (name, o) => { if (!o?.create && !files.has(name)) throw new Error('NotFoundError'); return { createSyncAccessHandle: async () => { if (!files.has(name)) files.set(name, new FakeHandle()); return files.get(name); } }; },
    removeEntry: async (name) => { if (!files.delete(name)) throw new Error('NotFoundError'); },
  };
  const realNav = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, 'navigator');
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'navigator', { value: { storage: { getDirectory: async () => ({ getDirectoryHandle: async () => dir }) } }, configurable: true });
  try { await fn(files); } finally { if (realNav) Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'navigator', realNav); else delete globalThis.navigator; }
}

const block = (i, n = 1000 + i) => Uint8Array.from({ length: n }, (_, k) => (k * 31 + i * 7) & 0xff);
const key = (i) => `Data/file é ${i}.big#123456#0#${i}`; // (a non-ASCII key: UTF-8 bytes in the record)

test('block store: put / sync / reopen roundtrip, drops replayed, a key stored again after its drop', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.resetReason, null);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.drop(key(3));
    s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.resetReason, null);
    assert.equal(s.indexCut, 0);
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 9);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(i)), i === 3 ? null : block(i));
    s.put(key(3), block(3)); s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(3)), block(3), 'stored again at the end of the data file');
    assert.equal(s.map.get(key(3))[0] > s.map.get(key(9))[0], true);
    assert.equal(files.has('index.json'), false);
  });
});

test('block store: a truncated tail record is cut; the blocks before it stay', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.close();
    const idx = files.get('index.bin'), full = idx.getSize();
    idx.b = idx.b.slice(0, full - 7); // (the last record's write lost its end)
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 3);
    assert.ok(s.indexCut > 0);
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(2)), block(2));
    assert.equal(s.get(key(3)), null, 'not indexed: fetched again');
    // the log was cut at the last complete record: later appends are readable
    s.put(key(3), block(3)); s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.indexCut, 0);
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 4);
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(3)), block(3));
  });
});

test('block store: a damaged record ends the log there (its block and the later ones fetched again)', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.flush(true);
    const mid = files.get('index.bin').getSize();
    for (let i = 3; i < 6; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.close();
    files.get('index.bin').b[mid + 6] ^= 1; // (the 4th record's offset)
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.deepEqual([...s.map.keys()], [key(0), key(1), key(2)]);
    assert.equal(s.get(key(3)), null);
    assert.equal(files.get('index.bin').getSize(), mid);
  });
});

test('block store: a record pointing past the data file is dropped; a damaged block is dropped durably', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.close();
    const d = files.get('blocks.bin');
    d.b = d.b.slice(0, d.getSize() - 10); // (the data file's tail lost)
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 2);
    d.b[5] ^= 0xff; // (the first block damaged on disk)
    const bad = []; s.onCorrupt = (k) => bad.push(k);
    assert.equal(s.get(key(0)), null);
    assert.deepEqual(bad, [key(0)]);
    s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.deepEqual([...s.map.keys()], [key(1)], 'the drop was recorded');
  });
});

test('block store: a v2 JSON index is read once and rewritten as a log; v1 and unreadable indexes empty the store', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    // a store written by the earlier format
    const data = new FakeHandle(), blocks = [block(0), block(1, 4096)];
    const entries = []; let off = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { data.write(blocks[i], { at: off }); entries.push([key(i), off, blocks[i].length, blockHash(blocks[i])]); off += blocks[i].length; }
    entries.push([key(2), off, 100, 0]); // (past the end of the data file)
    const json = new FakeHandle(); json.write(new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ v: 2, entries })), { at: 0 });
    files.set('blocks.bin', data); files.set('index.json', json);
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.resetReason, null);
    assert.equal(s.migrated, true);
    assert.equal(files.has('index.json'), false, 'the JSON index removed');
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(0)), blocks[0]);
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(1)), blocks[1]);
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 2);
    s.put(key(5), block(5)); s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.migrated, false);
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 3);
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(5)), block(5));
    // v1 (no checksums)
    files.delete('index.bin'); files.set('index.json', new FakeHandle()); files.get('index.json').write(new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify([[key(0), 0, 1000]])), { at: 0 });
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.resetReason, 'an earlier format without block checksums');
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 0);
    assert.equal(files.get('blocks.bin').getSize(), 0);
    // a log whose header is not this format's
    s.put(key(1), block(1)); s.close();
    files.get('index.bin').b[0] ^= 1;
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.resetReason, 'unreadable index');
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 0);
    s.put(key(1), block(1)); s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(1)), block(1), 'usable again after the reset');
  });
});

test('block store: index sync cadence — every 256 blocks or 2 s, at once when forced; nothing written in between', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    const s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    const idx = files.get('index.bin'), data = files.get('blocks.bin');
    const w0 = idx.writes, f0 = idx.flushes, small = new Uint8Array(16);
    for (let i = 0; i < SYNC_BLOCKS - 1; i++) { s.put(key(i), small); s.flush(); }
    assert.equal(idx.writes, w0, 'no index write before the cadence');
    assert.equal(idx.flushes, f0);
    assert.equal(data.flushes, 0);
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes ?? 0, 0);
    s.put(key(SYNC_BLOCKS - 1), small);
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes, 1, 'synced at 256 blocks');
    assert.equal(idx.writes, w0 + 1, 'one append');
    assert.equal(idx.flushes, f0 + 1);
    assert.equal(data.flushes, 0, 'the data file is not flushed at a sync point (checksums catch a lost block)');
    assert.equal(idx.truncates, 1, 'no rewrite (the one truncate is the new log at open)');
    // time-based: the next put syncs once SYNC_MS passed
    s.put(key(1000), small);
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes, 1);
    s.lastSync -= SYNC_MS;
    s.flush();
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes, 2);
    // forced (prefetch end, close): at once; with nothing waiting: nothing
    s.put(key(1001), small);
    s.flush(true);
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes, 3);
    s.flush(true);
    assert.equal(s.stats.flushes, 3);
    assert.equal(s.dirty, 0);
    assert.equal(data.flushes, 0);
    s.close();
    assert.equal(data.flushes, 1, 'the data file flushed at close');
    const again = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(again.map.size, SYNC_BLOCKS + 2);
  });
});

test('block store: a record dropped at open (past the data file) does not come back once later blocks fill that range', async () => {
  await withFakeOpfs(async (files) => {
    let s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) s.put(key(i), block(i));
    s.close();
    const d = files.get('blocks.bin');
    d.b = d.b.slice(0, d.getSize() - 10); // (a crash lost the data file's tail; the index record of key 2 survived)
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    assert.equal(s.map.has(key(2)), false);
    s.put(key(7), block(7, 3000)); // (appended where key 2's bytes were: its old record now lies inside the file)
    s.close();
    s = await OpfsBlockStore.open('x');
    const bad = []; s.onCorrupt = (k) => bad.push(k);
    assert.equal(s.map.has(key(2)), false, 'the stale record stays dropped');
    assert.equal(s.get(key(2)), null);
    assert.deepEqual(bad, []);
    assert.deepEqual(s.get(key(7)), block(7, 3000));
    assert.equal(s.map.size, 3);
  });
});
```

`tests/pcm-codec.test.js`:

```js
// The lossless PCM transport codec (src/vfs/pcm-codec.js) and the server's sound finder (src/host/pcm-units.js,
// docs/slow-network.md "Audio units"): every container decodes to exactly the bytes it was made from (checked by hash),
// whatever they are; sampled sound codes smaller than brotli; a damaged container throws.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import zlib from 'node:zlib';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { encodePcm, decodePcm, pcmCodedBytes } from '../src/vfs/pcm-codec.js';
import { parseWave, scanWaves, regionsIn, trialLayouts, estimateCoded } from '../src/host/pcm-units.js';

const sha = (b) => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
const rng = (seed) => () => { seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) >>> 0; return seed / 2 ** 32; };
/** a sound: a few decaying partials plus noise, as `bits` / `ch` PCM bytes */
function sound(frames, bits, ch, seed = 1) {
  const r = rng(seed), b = new Uint8Array(frames * ch * (bits >> 3)), amp = bits === 8 ? 100 : 20000;
  const parts = Array.from({ length: 4 }, () => [r() * 0.2, r() * 6.28, 0.3 + r() * 0.5]);
  let p = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < frames; i++) for (let c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
    let v = 0; for (const [f, ph, a] of parts) v += a * Math.sin(i * f * (1 + c * 0.01) + ph);
    v = Math.round(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, v * Math.exp(-i / (frames * 2)) / 2 + (r() - 0.5) * 0.01)) * amp);
    if (bits === 8) b[p++] = v + 128; else { b[p++] = v & 0xff; b[p++] = (v >> 8) & 0xff; }
  }
  return b;
}
const roundTrip = (b, regions, opts) => { const c = encodePcm(b, regions, opts), d = decodePcm(c); assert.equal(sha(d), sha(b)); return c; };
const wave = (pcm, bits, ch, rate = 22050, tag = 1) => {
  const h = Buffer.alloc(44);
  h.write('RIFF', 0, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(36 + pcm.length, 4); h.write('WAVEfmt ', 8, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(16, 16);
  h.writeUInt16LE(tag, 20); h.writeUInt16LE(ch, 22); h.writeUInt32LE(rate, 24); h.writeUInt32LE(rate * ch * (bits >> 3), 28); h.writeUInt16LE(ch * (bits >> 3), 32); h.writeUInt16LE(bits, 34);
  h.write('data', 36, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(pcm.length, 40);
  return Buffer.concat([h, Buffer.from(pcm)]);
};

test('codec: every layout round-trips byte-exact, and sound codes well under brotli', () => {
  for (const [bits, ch] of [[16, 1], [16, 2], [8, 1], [8, 2]]) {
    const b = sound(20000, bits, ch, bits + ch), c = roundTrip(b, [{ at: 0, len: b.length, bits, ch }]);
    const br = zlib.brotliCompressSync(b, { params: { [zlib.constants.BROTLI_PARAM_QUALITY]: 9 } }).length;
    assert.ok(c.length < br * 0.8, `${bits}-bit ${ch} ch: ${c.length} against brotli ${br}`);
    assert.equal(pcmCodedBytes(c), b.length);
  }
});

test('codec: any bytes — noise, constants, silence, extremes, odd lengths, short frames — come back exact', () => {
  const r = rng(7);
  const noise = Uint8Array.from({ length: 70001 }, () => Math.floor(r() * 256));
  const c = roundTrip(noise, [{ at: 0, len: noise.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]);
  assert.ok(c.length <= noise.length + 64, 'unpredictable bytes: kept as they are');
  roundTrip(new Uint8Array(50000), [{ at: 0, len: 50000, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
  roundTrip(new Uint8Array(50000).fill(0x80), [{ at: 0, len: 50000, bits: 8, ch: 1 }]);
  // full-scale square waves and clicks: the widest residuals (escape codes, side channel 17 bits)
  const sq = new Uint8Array(40000); for (let i = 0; i < sq.length; i += 2) { const v = (i >> 6) & 1 ? 32767 : -32768; sq[i] = v & 0xff; sq[i + 1] = (v >> 8) & 0xff; }
  roundTrip(sq, [{ at: 0, len: sq.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]);
  roundTrip(sq, [{ at: 0, len: sq.length, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
  const lr = new Uint8Array(40000); for (let i = 0; i < lr.length; i += 4) { lr[i] = 0x00; lr[i + 1] = 0x80; lr[i + 2] = 0xff; lr[i + 3] = 0x7f; } // (left −32768, right 32767)
  roundTrip(lr, [{ at: 0, len: lr.length, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
  for (let i = 0; i < 4000; i += 97) noise[i] = 0;
  const s = sound(3001, 16, 1, 3); // (odd frame count, a last frame of 3001 % 2048)
  roundTrip(s, [{ at: 0, len: s.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]);
  for (const frame of [64, 256, 1024, 4096, 65536]) roundTrip(s, [{ at: 0, len: s.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }], { frame });
  roundTrip(new Uint8Array(0), []);
  roundTrip(Uint8Array.of(1, 2, 3), [{ at: 0, len: 3, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]);
});

test('codec: sound regions inside other bytes (headers, other members), cut ones skipped', () => {
  const a = sound(9000, 16, 1, 5), b8 = sound(12000, 8, 1, 6), text = Buffer.from('not a sound at all '.repeat(300));
  const all = Buffer.concat([text, a, text.subarray(0, 77), b8, text]);
  const at1 = text.length, at2 = at1 + a.length + 77;
  const c = roundTrip(all, [{ at: at1, len: a.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }, { at: at2, len: b8.length, bits: 8, ch: 1 }]);
  assert.equal(pcmCodedBytes(c), a.length + b8.length);
  // a region past the end, overlapping ones, one too short: still exact
  roundTrip(all, [{ at: at1, len: a.length + 10, bits: 16, ch: 1 }, { at: at1 + 100, len: 5000, bits: 16, ch: 1 }, { at: at2, len: 20, bits: 8, ch: 1 }, { at: all.length - 1000, len: 9000, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
});

test('codec: a damaged, cut or foreign container throws (never wrong bytes)', () => {
  const b = sound(8000, 16, 1, 9), c = encodePcm(b, [{ at: 0, len: b.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]);
  assert.throws(() => decodePcm(c.subarray(0, c.length - 1)));
  assert.throws(() => decodePcm(c.subarray(0, 10)));
  assert.throws(() => decodePcm(new Uint8Array(100)));
  let caught = 0;
  for (let i = 30; i < c.length; i += Math.max(1, c.length >> 6)) {
    const d = c.slice(); d[i] ^= 0x10;
    try { const out = decodePcm(d); assert.equal(sha(out), sha(b), 'a flip the CRC let through must not change the bytes'); } catch { caught++; }
  }
  assert.ok(caught > 0);
});

test('sound finder: RIFF WAVE PCM found in a file or inside an archive, other formats not', () => {
  const a = sound(5000, 8, 1, 2), s = sound(4000, 16, 2, 3), adpcm = wave(sound(3000, 16, 1, 4), 4, 1, 22050, 0x11);
  const w1 = wave(a, 8, 1), w2 = wave(s, 16, 2);
  assert.deepEqual(parseWave(w1, 0, w1.length), { start: 44, end: 44 + a.length, bits: 8, ch: 1, next: w1.length });
  assert.equal(parseWave(adpcm, 0, adpcm.length), null, 'IMA ADPCM: not PCM');
  const junk = Buffer.from('RIFF....junk'), arch = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('BIGF header'), w1, junk, adpcm, Buffer.alloc(3), w2, Buffer.from('tail')]);
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'orthros-pcm-')), f = path.join(dir, 'a.big');
  try {
    fs.writeFileSync(f, arch);
    const at1 = 11, at2 = at1 + w1.length + junk.length + adpcm.length + 3;
    const waves = scanWaves(f);
    assert.deepEqual(waves, [{ start: at1 + 44, end: at1 + 44 + a.length, bits: 8, ch: 1 }, { start: at2 + 44, end: at2 + 44 + s.length, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
    // a unit cut inside the stereo sound starts on its next sample frame
    const cut = at2 + 44 + 1001, rs = regionsIn(waves, cut, cut + 4096);
    assert.deepEqual(rs, [{ at: 3, len: 4092, bits: 16, ch: 2 }]);
    const unit = arch.subarray(cut, cut + 4096);
    assert.equal(sha(decodePcm(encodePcm(unit, rs))), sha(unit));
  } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
});

test('trial layouts: a raw 16-bit bank estimates well under its bytes, noise does not', () => {
  const s = sound(30000, 16, 1, 11), r = rng(3), noise = Uint8Array.from({ length: 60000 }, () => Math.floor(r() * 256));
  const est = (b) => Math.min(...trialLayouts(b.length).map((l) => estimateCoded(b, l)));
  assert.ok(est(s) < s.length * 0.7, `sound ${est(s)} of ${s.length}`);
  assert.ok(est(noise) > noise.length * 0.9, `noise ${est(noise)} of ${noise.length}`);
});
```

`tests/pcm-units.test.js`:

```js
// Audio units (docs/slow-network.md "Audio units"): the server makes a unit's PCM transport form beside its brotli one —
// for RIFF WAVE sound found in a file or an archive, for a raw sample bank by trial — and sends it to a request that
// says it decodes them (&pc=1); the shared reader decodes it before the game sees a byte; the bytes are the file's
// (checked by hash); other requests, light copies and data that is not sound are as before.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import http from 'node:http';
import zlib from 'node:zlib';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { HttpBackend, BLOCK, CHUNK } from '../src/vfs/http-backend.js';
import { createServer } from '../src/host/server.js';
import { createBrCache } from '../src/host/br-cache.js';
import { encodePcm, decodePcm } from '../src/vfs/pcm-codec.js';

const QUIET = { loadLimit: Infinity, diskLimit: 1, idleMs: 50 };
const sha = (b) => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
/** 16-bit mono sound bytes: partials and a little noise */
function sound(frames, seed = 1) {
  let s = seed; const r = () => { s = (s * 1103515245 + 12345) >>> 0; return s / 2 ** 32; };
  const b = Buffer.alloc(frames * 2), f = [0.01 + r() * 0.05, 0.07 + r() * 0.1, 0.2 + r() * 0.1];
  for (let i = 0; i < frames; i++) b.writeInt16LE(Math.round((Math.sin(i * f[0]) * 0.5 + Math.sin(i * f[1]) * 0.25 + Math.sin(i * f[2]) * 0.1 + (r() - 0.5) * 0.02) * 20000), i * 2);
  return b;
}
const wave = (pcm) => {
  const h = Buffer.alloc(44);
  h.write('RIFF', 0, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(36 + pcm.length, 4); h.write('WAVEfmt ', 8, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(16, 16);
  h.writeUInt16LE(1, 20); h.writeUInt16LE(1, 22); h.writeUInt32LE(22050, 24); h.writeUInt32LE(44100, 28); h.writeUInt16LE(2, 32); h.writeUInt16LE(16, 34);
  h.write('data', 36, 'latin1'); h.writeUInt32LE(pcm.length, 40);
  return Buffer.concat([h, pcm]);
};
const get = (url, enc = 'gzip, br') => new Promise((res, rej) => http.get(url, { headers: { 'accept-encoding': enc } }, async (r) => { const parts = []; for await (const d of r) parts.push(d); res({ r, body: Buffer.concat(parts) }); }).on('error', rej));
const plain = ({ r, body }) => (r.headers['content-encoding'] === 'br' ? zlib.brotliDecompressSync(body) : body);

test('server: audio units made for sound (a .wav, an archive member, a raw bank), sent to &pc=1 only, the bytes exact', async () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'orthros-pcmunits-'));
  const w = wave(sound(BLOCK / 2 + 5000, 3)); // (a block and a tail)
  const text = Buffer.from('member text, compressible '.repeat(2000));
  const arch = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('BIGF....'), text, wave(sound(30000, 4)), text]);
  const bank = Buffer.concat([sound(40000, 5), sound(30000, 6)]); // (no header: the trial layouts)
  const noise = crypto.randomBytes(CHUNK);
  for (const [n, b] of [['s.wav', w], ['a.big', arch], ['sfx.raw', bank], ['noise.bin', noise]]) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, n), b);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(dir, 'man')); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'man', 'g.json'), JSON.stringify({ name: 'g', folder: dir, exe: 'x.exe' }));
  const brDir = path.join(dir, 'brcache');
  const server = createServer({ manifests: path.join(dir, 'man'), brCacheDir: brDir, brCacheOptions: QUIET, brCacheLog: () => {} });
  await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r));
  const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`;
  const units = [['s.wav', 0, BLOCK, w], ['s.wav', BLOCK, w.length, w], ['a.big', 0, arch.length, arch], ['sfx.raw', 0, bank.length, bank], ['noise.bin', 0, CHUNK, noise]];
  try {
    for (const [f, a, e, b] of units) assert.equal(sha(plain(await get(`${base}/gamez/g/${f}?r=${a}-${e}&pc=1`))), sha(b.subarray(a, e)), 'a miss: the dynamic way');
    await server.brCache.drain();
    const st = server.brCache.stats();
    assert.equal(st.units, 5); assert.equal(st.pcmUnits, 4, 'the sound units, not the noise');
    for (const [f, a, e, b] of units) {
      const want = sha(b.subarray(a, e));
      const p = await get(`${base}/gamez/g/${f}?r=${a}-${e}&p=1&pc=1`);
      if (f === 'noise.bin') { assert.equal(p.r.headers['x-orthros-codec'], undefined); assert.equal(sha(p.body), want); continue; }
      assert.equal(p.r.headers['x-orthros-codec'], 'pcm1', f);
      assert.equal(p.r.headers['content-encoding'], 'br');
      assert.equal(p.r.headers['x-orthros-unit'], 'hit');
      assert.equal(sha(decodePcm(zlib.brotliDecompressSync(p.body))), want, `${f} ${a}-${e}: decoded to the file's bytes`);
      const q = await get(`${base}/gamez/g/${f}?r=${a}-${e}&p=1`);
      assert.equal(q.r.headers['x-orthros-codec'], undefined, 'without &pc=1: the brotli unit');
      assert.equal(sha(plain(q)), want);
      assert.ok(p.body.length < q.body.length * 0.95, `${f}: ${p.body.length} against brotli's ${q.body.length}`);
    }
    assert.ok(JSON.parse((await get(`${base}/api/netstats`, '')).body).pcmHits >= 4);
    // the index rebuilt from the disk keeps them (and the files' waves); a unit's audio form gone: made again
    server.brCache.close();
    const again = createBrCache({ dir: brDir, ...QUIET });
    await again.ready;
    assert.equal(again.stats().pcmUnits, 4);
    const f = path.join(dir, 's.wav'), sz = fs.statSync(f);
    assert.ok(again.lookupPcm(f, sz, null, { kind: 'b', index: 0 }));
    assert.ok(again.size(f, sz, null, { kind: 'b', index: 0 }) < again.lookup(f, sz, null, { kind: 'b', index: 0 }).bytes, 'its wire size: the audio form\'s');
    again.close();
  } finally { server.close(); fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
});

test('cache: units made before audio units get their audio form later; none for light copies', async () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'orthros-pcmunits-'));
  const f = path.join(dir, 's.wav'); fs.writeFileSync(f, wave(sound(20000, 8)));
  try {
    const old = createBrCache({ dir: path.join(dir, 'c'), ...QUIET, pcm: false });
    const st = fs.statSync(f), unit = { kind: 'b', index: 0 };
    old.want(f, st, null, unit); await old.drain();
    assert.ok(old.lookup(f, st, null, unit)); assert.equal(old.lookupPcm(f, st, null, unit), null);
    old.close();
    const made = [], c = createBrCache({ dir: path.join(dir, 'c'), ...QUIET, onMade: (file, u) => made.push(u) });
    await c.ready;
    c.want(f, st, null, unit); await c.drain();
    assert.equal(made.length, 1, 'the audio form only');
    assert.ok(c.lookupPcm(f, st, null, unit));
    assert.equal(c.lookupPcm(f, st, { copy: { size: 10, from: 0, head: [] } }, unit), null);
    c.close();
  } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
});

test('backend: an audio unit is decoded before the reader keeps it; a bad one turns them off and is asked again', async () => {
  const FILE = Buffer.concat([sound(BLOCK / 2, 9), sound(BLOCK / 2, 10)]);
  const tree = { dirs: {}, files: { 'a.raw': { size: FILE.length, mtime: 1 } } };
  const realFetch = globalThis.fetch, asked = [];
  let corrupt = false, dropHeader = false;
  globalThis.fetch = async (url) => {
    const [, a, e] = /\?r=(\d+)-(\d+)/.exec(url), pc = /&pc=1(&|$)/.test(url); asked.push([+a, +e, pc]);
    let body = new Uint8Array(FILE.subarray(+a, +e)), codec = null;
    if (pc) { body = encodePcm(body, [{ at: 0, len: body.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]); codec = dropHeader ? null : 'pcm1'; if (corrupt) body[body.length >> 1] ^= 0x55; }
    return { status: 200, headers: { get: (h) => (h === 'x-orthros-codec' ? codec : h === 'content-length' ? String(body.length) : null) }, arrayBuffer: async () => body.slice().buffer };
  };
  try {
    const b = new HttpBackend('/game/g/', tree, { encoded: true });
    const d = await b.fetchBackground('a.raw', 0, 2 * BLOCK, null);
    assert.equal(sha(d), sha(FILE));
    assert.deepEqual(asked.map((x) => x[2]), [true, true], 'asked with &pc=1, one request per unit');
    assert.equal(b.stats.pcmUnits, 2);
    const fg = await b.fetchForeground('a.raw', CHUNK, 2 * CHUNK);
    assert.equal(sha(fg), sha(FILE.subarray(CHUNK, 2 * CHUNK)));
    dropHeader = true; // (a proxy that drops X-Orthros-Codec: the container told by its length and magic)
    assert.equal(sha(await b.fetchBackground('a.raw', BLOCK, 2 * BLOCK, null)), sha(FILE.subarray(BLOCK)));
    dropHeader = false;
    corrupt = true; asked.length = 0;
    assert.equal(await b.fetchBackground('a.raw', 0, BLOCK, null), undefined, 'a bad unit: no bytes');
    assert.equal(b.pcm, false);
    corrupt = false;
    assert.equal(sha(await b.fetchBackground('a.raw', 0, BLOCK, null)), sha(FILE.subarray(0, BLOCK)));
    assert.deepEqual(asked.map((x) => x[2]), [true, false], 'asked again without');
    const off = new HttpBackend('/game/g/', tree, { encoded: true, pcm: false });
    assert.ok(!off.rangeUrl('a.raw', 0, BLOCK).includes('pc=1'));
    assert.ok(!new HttpBackend('/game/g/', tree, {}).rangeUrl('a.raw', 0, BLOCK).includes('pc=1'), 'not the compressed ranges: never');
  } finally { globalThis.fetch = realFetch; }
});

test('backend: a synchronous read whose audio unit does not decode is asked again without the codec', () => {
  const FILE = Buffer.from(sound(CHUNK, 4));
  const tree = { dirs: {}, files: { 'a.raw': { size: FILE.length, mtime: 1 } } };
  const Real = globalThis.XMLHttpRequest, urls = [];
  globalThis.XMLHttpRequest = class {
    open(m, url) { this.url = url; }
    setRequestHeader() {}
    getResponseHeader(h) { return /x-orthros-codec/i.test(h) ? this.codec : null; }
    send() {
      urls.push(this.url);
      const [, a, e] = /\?r=(\d+)-(\d+)/.exec(this.url), body = new Uint8Array(FILE.subarray(+a, +e));
      this.status = 200;
      if (/&pc=1(&|$)/.test(this.url)) { const enc = encodePcm(body, [{ at: 0, len: body.length, bits: 16, ch: 1 }]); enc[enc.length >> 1] ^= 0x55; this.codec = 'pcm1'; this.response = enc.buffer; }
      else { this.codec = null; this.response = body.slice().buffer; }
    }
  };
  try {
    const b = new HttpBackend('/game/g/', tree, { encoded: true, retryWaits: [0, 0, 0] });
    assert.equal(sha(b.fetchRange('a.raw', 0, CHUNK)), sha(FILE.subarray(0, CHUNK)));
    assert.equal(b.pcm, false);
    assert.deepEqual(urls.map((u) => /&pc=1/.test(u)), [true, false], 'the retry without &pc=1');
  } finally { globalThis.XMLHttpRequest = Real; }
});

test('cache: a restart pins a launch set\'s audio units with its brotli ones before anything is made (pinNow)', async () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'orthros-pcmpin-'));
  const unit = { kind: 'p', index: 0 };
  const file = (n, b) => { const f = path.join(dir, n); fs.writeFileSync(f, b); return { file: f, st: fs.statSync(f), light: null, unit }; };
  const s = file('s.wav', wave(sound(CHUNK, 7)));
  const [a0, m1, m2] = ['a0', 'm1', 'm2'].map((n) => file(n, Buffer.from(`${n} compressible text `.repeat(3000)).subarray(0, CHUNK)));
  const cdir = path.join(dir, 'cache');
  try {
    // an earlier process: the launch unit s (brotli and audio forms) made long ago, two live misses lately
    const first = createBrCache({ dir: cdir, ...QUIET });
    for (const u of [s, m1, m2]) { first.want(u.file, u.st, null, u.unit); await first.drain(); }
    const now = Date.now() / 1000, pcm = first.lookupPcm(s.file, s.st, null, unit);
    assert.ok(pcm, 'the audio form made');
    for (const [p, age] of [[first.lookup(s.file, s.st, null, unit).path, 3000], [pcm.path, 3000], [first.lookup(m1.file, m1.st, null, unit).path, 100], [first.lookup(m2.file, m2.st, null, unit).path, 50]]) fs.utimesSync(p, now - age, now - age);
    const before = first.stats().bytes; first.close();
    // (a0's unit: what making it adds)
    const probe = createBrCache({ dir: path.join(dir, 'probe'), ...QUIET });
    probe.want(a0.file, a0.st, null, unit); await probe.drain(); const add = probe.stats().bytes; probe.close();
    // restarted with one unit's room too few: making A's missing unit evicts one unit — a live miss, not B's audio form
    const max = before + add - 1;
    const cache = createBrCache({ dir: cdir, maxBytes: max, lowBytes: max, pinShare: 0.9, ...QUIET,
      sources: () => [{ name: 'A', units: () => [a0] }, { name: 'B', units: () => [s] }] });
    await cache.ready; await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20)); await cache.drain();
    assert.ok(cache.lookup(a0.file, a0.st, null, unit), 'the missing launch unit made');
    assert.ok(cache.stats().evicted >= 1);
    // (before, B's audio unit — the oldest, not pinned until the walk reached it — went out and the walk made it again)
    assert.equal(cache.stats().generated, 1, 'nothing made twice'); assert.equal(cache.stats().pcmMade, 0);
    assert.ok(cache.lookupPcm(s.file, s.st, null, unit), 'B\'s audio unit kept');
    assert.ok(cache.lookup(s.file, s.st, null, unit), 'B\'s brotli unit kept');
    assert.equal(cache.lookup(m1.file, m1.st, null, unit), null, 'a live miss out instead');
    cache.close();
  } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
});
```

`tests/pe.test.js`:

```js
// M2: PE loader + Win32 bootstrap. Runs CRT-free test programs built by tools/pe/build.sh.
import { TimerResolution } from '../src/core/timer-res.js';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { Vm } from '../src/core/vm.js';
import { Vfs, MemBackend } from '../src/vfs/vfs.js';
import { VirtualClock } from '../src/core/clock.js';
import { HeadlessHost } from '../src/host/display.js';
import { wmOf } from '../src/win32/user32.js';
import { FAST_STATS } from '../src/cpu/jit/runtime.js';

const PE_DIR = new URL('../build/pe/', import.meta.url).pathname;

/** Boot a test exe in a fresh VM with a writable C:\Test holding the exe. */
function boot(exeName, opts = {}) {
  const vfs = new Vfs();
  const test = new MemBackend();
  vfs.mount('C:\\', new MemBackend());
  vfs.mount('C:\\Test', test);
  test.open(exeName, { create: true }).write(0, fs.readFileSync(PE_DIR + exeName));
  for (const [name, path] of Object.entries(opts.files ?? {})) test.open(name, { create: true }).write(0, fs.readFileSync(path));
  const clock = new VirtualClock();
  const host = new HeadlessHost({ clock, width: 800, height: 600 });
  const vm = new Vm({ vfs, clock, host, jit: opts.jit, apiHist: opts.apiHist, nullPage: opts.nullPage, timerRes: opts.timerRes, logKinds: opts.logKinds ?? ['warn', 'crash'] });
  vm.createProcess({ exePath: 'C:\\Test\\' + exeName });
  return { vm, host, clock };
}

const skip = (name) => !fs.existsSync(PE_DIR + name) && `build/pe/${name} missing (make pe-tests)`;

test('hello.exe: PE load, imports, heap, TLS, VirtualAlloc, files, exit code', { skip: skip('hello.exe') }, () => {
  const { vm } = boot('hello.exe');
  const code = vm.run();
  const out = vm.stdout.join('');
  assert.equal(code, 42);
  assert.equal(out,
    'hello from guest\n' +
    'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\n' +
    'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\n' +
    '1234\n' +
    '42\n' +
    '"C:\\Test\\hello.exe"\n' +
    'C:\\Test\\hello.exe\n' +
    'read back: written by guest\n' +
    '16\n' +
    '1234\n' +
    '8\n');
  assert.equal(vm.proc.unknownImports.size, 0);
});

test('window.exe: RegisterClass/CreateWindow, WM_PAINT via GDI, timers, input, message loop', { skip: skip('window.exe') }, () => {
  const { vm, host } = boot('window.exe');
  // scripted input: a key press and a click inside the client area (window at 100,100; client offset by frame/caption)
  host.at(25, { type: 'keydown', vk: 0x41, scan: 0x1e });
  host.at(26, { type: 'keyup', vk: 0x41, scan: 0x1e });
  host.at(35, { type: 'mousedown', button: 0, x: 100 + 4 + 12, y: 100 + 4 + 19 + 7 });
  host.at(36, { type: 'mouseup', button: 0, x: 100 + 4 + 12, y: 100 + 4 + 19 + 7 });
  const code = vm.run();
  // exit code = result(7) + paints*10 + keys*1000 + clicks*100000; clicks = x + y in client coords
  assert.equal(code % 10, 7, 'GetPixel readbacks (red rect, blue pixel)');
  const paints = Math.floor(code / 10) % 100;
  assert.ok(paints >= 2, `expected >= 2 paints, got ${paints}`);
  assert.equal(Math.floor(code / 1000) % 100, 0x41, 'WM_KEYDOWN delivered with VK_A');
  assert.equal(Math.floor(code / 100000), 12 + 7, 'WM_LBUTTONDOWN delivered with client coordinates');
  // the last presented frame shows the client surface with the red rectangle and blue pixel
  const d = host.display;
  assert.ok(d.frames > 0, 'frames presented');
  const cx = d.last.x, cy = d.last.y;
  assert.equal(d.pixelAt(cx + 50, cy + 30), 0xff0000, 'red rect presented');
  assert.equal(d.pixelAt(cx + 200, cy + 100), 0x0000ff, 'blue pixel presented');
  assert.equal(d.pixelAt(cx + 5, cy + 5), 0xffffff, 'class background brush (COLOR_WINDOW) erased');
  assert.equal(vm.proc.unknownImports.size, 0);
});

// a failure exit (non-zero code) leaves a report for the host: the exiting thread, the recent API calls and the last
// exceptions raised, a C++ exception with its thrown type's name (MSVC ThrowInfo chain, built here in guest memory)
test('hello.exe: a non-zero exit code leaves a failure report with the last exceptions raised', { skip: skip('hello.exe') }, () => {
  const { vm } = boot('hello.exe');
  const m = vm.mem, a = vm.proc.processHeap.alloc(64);
  const ti = a, cta = a + 16, ct = a + 24, td = a + 36;
  m.write32(ti + 12, cta); m.write32(cta, 1); m.write32(cta + 4, ct); m.write32(ct + 4, td); m.writeCString(td + 8, '.?AVFailure@@');
  vm.seh.remember(vm.proc.threads[0], 0xe06d7363, vm.proc.exe.entry, [0x19930520, 0, ti]);
  assert.equal(vm.run(), 42);
  assert.match(vm.exitReport, /process exit with code 42 in thread/);
  assert.match(vm.exitReport, /kernel32\.dll!ExitProcess/);
  assert.match(vm.exitReport, /exceptions raised: 1, the last ones:\n  t\d+ 0xe06d7363 \.\?AVFailure@@ at /);
});

test('seh.exe: frame-based SEH dispatch, fault continuation, RtlUnwind, execution faults at bad addresses, an exception raised in a handler, null-page data accesses', { skip: skip('seh.exe') }, () => {
  for (const jit of [true, false]) {
    const { vm } = boot('seh.exe', { jit, nullPage: true }); // (its null-page cases read: faults on reads too)
    const code = vm.run();
    const exec = (a) => `exec code 0xc0000005\nexec addr 0x${a}\nexec info 0x${a}\n`;
    const h8 = (v) => '0x' + (v >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0');
    const av = (w, a, ecx) => `av code 0xc0000005\nav info ${h8(w)}\nav addr ${h8(a)}\nav at insn 0x00000001\nav ecx ${h8(ecx)}\n`;
    assert.equal(vm.stdout.join(''), 'div result 0x0000004d\ninner code 0xc0000094\ninner hits after unwind 0x00000065\ntop is outer 0x00000001\n' +
      exec('00000000') + exec('fffffff0') + exec('ffffffff') +
      'nested inner 0x0000004d\nnested inner code 0xc0000094\nnested outer 0x00000037\n' +

      // (ECX kept), [null-4] past the user address space, then LEA (no access)

      'av code 0x00000000\nav info 0xeeeeeeee\nav addr 0xeeeeeeee\nav at insn 0x00000001\nav ecx 0x00000000\n' +
      'av faults 0x000005dc\nav faults per round 0x00000005\n', `jit=${jit}`);
    assert.equal(code, 0);
  }
});

test('dx.exe: DirectSound buffers/cursors, DirectInput keyboard+mouse, Direct3D 8 device/resources', { skip: skip('dx.exe') }, () => {
  // (exact sleeps — no clock-interrupt rounding, core/timer-res.js: the scripted events and the play cursors below are
  // timed on the program's Sleep durations)
  const { vm, host } = boot('dx.exe', { jit: true, timerRes: new TimerResolution(0) });
  const base = 2850; // virtual ms consumed by the DirectSound sleeps before the DirectInput part
  host.at(base + 20, { type: 'keydown', vk: 0x41, scan: 0x1e });
  host.at(base + 50, { type: 'mousemove', x: 100, y: 100 });
  host.at(base + 80, { type: 'mousemove', x: 110, y: 105 });
  host.at(base + 81, { type: 'mousedown', button: 0, x: 110, y: 105 });
  const code = vm.run();
  assert.equal(code, 0);
  const out = Object.fromEntries(vm.stdout.join('').trim().split('\n').map((l) => l.split('=')));
  // DirectSound: 44.1 kHz 16-bit stereo, play cursor follows the virtual clock
  for (const k of ['dscreate', 'coop', 'primary', 'setformat', 'secondary', 'lock', 'unlock', 'play', 'playloop', 'setfreq', 'stop', 'setvol']) assert.equal(out[k], '0x00000000', k);
  assert.equal(out.lockbytes, '176400');
  assert.deepEqual([out.pos250, out.status250], ['44100', '0x00000011'], '250 ms of playback');

  for (const k of ['checktype', 'checkfmt', 'device', 'tex', 'lockrect', 'unlockrect', 'surflevel', 'vb', 'vblock', 'vbunlock', 'begin', 'clear', 'rs', 'settex', 'stream', 'fvf', 'draw', 'end', 'present', 'backbuffer']) assert.equal(out[k], '0x00000000', k);

// Host input: a mouse release waits until the game presented a frame after the press (at most 250 ms), so a game
// sampling the button once per frame sees a click shorter than one of its frames; GetAsyncKeyState bit 0 reports
// a press since its previous call.
test('input: a click shorter than a frame still shows the button down for one frame; GetAsyncKeyState bit 0', { skip: skip('window.exe') }, () => {
  const { vm, host, clock } = boot('window.exe');
  const wm = wmOf(vm);
  vm.d3dDevice = { frames: 5, lost: 0 };
  host.inputQueue.push({ type: 'mousedown', button: 0, x: 10, y: 10 }, { type: 'mouseup', button: 0, x: 10, y: 10 }, { type: 'mousemove', x: 20, y: 20 });
  wm.pump();
  assert.equal(wm.keyState[1] & 0x80, 0x80, 'button down seen, release held');
  assert.equal(wm.cursor.x, 10, 'the move after the held release waits too');
  wm.pump();
  assert.equal(wm.keyState[1] & 0x80, 0x80, 'no frame yet: still held');
  vm.d3dDevice.frames = 6;
  wm.pump();
  assert.equal(wm.keyState[1] & 0x80, 0, 'released after a frame');
  assert.equal(wm.cursor.x, 20);
  // without a frame, the release goes after 250 ms
  host.inputQueue.push({ type: 'mousedown', button: 0, x: 1, y: 1 }, { type: 'mouseup', button: 0, x: 1, y: 1 });
  wm.pump(); assert.equal(wm.keyState[1] & 0x80, 0x80);
  clock.sleep(300); wm.pump(); assert.equal(wm.keyState[1] & 0x80, 0, 'released after 250 ms without a frame');
  vm.d3dDevice = null;
  // GetAsyncKeyState: bit 0 once after a press (here a tap already over), then 0
  host.inputQueue.push({ type: 'keydown', vk: 0x41, scan: 0x1e }, { type: 'keyup', vk: 0x41, scan: 0x1e });
  wm.pump();
  assert.equal(wm.asyncPressed[0x41], 1, 'pressed since the last call');
});

// The cursor shows when ShowCursor's count is >= 0 and a shape is set: SetCursor(NULL) hides it until the next
// SetCursor with a cursor (it used to stay hidden for good), independently of the count.
test('cursor: SetCursor(NULL) hides until the next SetCursor; ShowCursor counts independently', { skip: skip('window.exe') }, () => {
  const { vm } = boot('window.exe');

  shown.length = 0;
  call('ShowCursor', 0); call('SetCursor', 0); call('SetCursor', h); call('ShowCursor', 1);

// Winsock (D061): UDP and TCP inside the process, then over the virtual LAN with a machine played by the test (it
// answers the program's broadcast on port 8086, then accepts its TCP connection on 8100 and replies "ok" to "data").
import { LAN } from '../src/host/lan-proto.js';
test('net.exe: Winsock inside the process and over the virtual LAN', { skip: skip('net.exe') }, () => {
  const inside = boot('net.exe', { jit: true });
  assert.equal(inside.vm.run(), 0);
  const want = 'startup=0\nme=127.0.0.1\nbind1=0\nbind2=0\nbind_inuse=10048\nsendto=4\nrecvfrom=4\nfrom_port=9001\ndata_ping=1\nwouldblock=10035\nbcast_own=5\n' +
    'listen=0\nconnect=0\naccept_ready=1\naccepted=1\nsend=5\nrecv=5\ndata_hello=1\nreadable=1\nrecv2=3\nrecv3=3\ndata_world=1\npeer_closed=0\nrefused=10061\n';
  assert.equal(inside.vm.stdout.join(''), want);

  const { vm, host } = boot('net.exe', { jit: true });
  const other = { ip: 0x09004d0a, frames: [] }; // 10.77.0.9
  host.lan = {
    ip: '10.77.0.2',
    send(type, src, dst, payload) {
      other.frames.push(type);
      const back = (t, data = null) => vm.lanDeliver(t, dst.ip === 0xffffffff ? { ip: other.ip, port: dst.port } : dst, src, data);
      if (type === LAN.UDP && dst.port === 8086) back(LAN.UDP, new TextEncoder().encode('hello'));
      else if (type === LAN.SYN && dst.ip === other.ip && dst.port === 8100) back(LAN.ACCEPT);
      else if (type === LAN.DATA && new TextDecoder().decode(payload) === 'data') back(LAN.DATA, new TextEncoder().encode('ok'));
    },
  };
  assert.equal(vm.run(), 0);
  const out = vm.stdout.join('');
  assert.ok(out.startsWith('startup=0\nme=10.77.0.2\n'), out);
  assert.ok(out.endsWith('lan_reply=5\nlan_from=10.77.0.9\nlan_data=1\nlan_connect=0\nlan_recv=2\nlan_ok=1\n'), out);
  assert.deepEqual(other.frames, [LAN.UDP, LAN.UDP, LAN.SYN, LAN.DATA, LAN.FIN], 'both broadcasts leave the machine, then the connection');
});
```

`tests/peek-idle.test.js`:

```js
// PeekMessage polling (user32.js peekIdle): a thread calling PeekMessage with nothing to get, over and over, waits in
// short steps instead of spinning, and spins again around the time its previous bouts of polling ended, so that a
// frame limiter polling its clock is not made late. Driven on the virtual clock (outside the dispatcher the waits are
// nested: the clock sleeps through them): a guest frame loop — some API calls, then PeekMessage + a clock read until
// its deadline — with each polling iteration costing 1 µs.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { PARK } from '../src/core/sched.js';
import { VirtualClock } from '../src/core/clock.js';
import { Vm } from '../src/core/vm.js';
import { Vfs, MemBackend } from '../src/vfs/vfs.js';
import { HeadlessHost } from '../src/host/display.js';
import { Ctx } from '../src/win32/ctx.js';

const EXE = new URL('../build/pe/hello.exe', import.meta.url).pathname;
const skip = !fs.existsSync(EXE) && 'build/pe/hello.exe missing (make pe-tests)';

function setup() {
  const vfs = new Vfs(); const b = new MemBackend();
  vfs.mount('C:\\', new MemBackend()); vfs.mount('C:\\Test', b);
  b.open('hello.exe', { create: true }).write(0, fs.readFileSync(EXE));
  const clock = new VirtualClock();
  const vm = new Vm({ vfs, clock, host: new HeadlessHost({ clock, width: 64, height: 64 }), logKinds: [] });
  vm.createProcess({ exePath: 'C:\\Test\\hello.exe' });
  const mem = vm.mem, frame = vm.proc.processHeap.alloc(64, true), msg = vm.proc.processHeap.alloc(64, true), th = vm.proc.threads[0];
  const call = (dll, name, ...args) => {
    args.forEach((a, i) => mem.write32(frame + 4 + 4 * i, a >>> 0));
    th.apiCalls++; vm.apiCalls++; // (as the dispatcher counts them)
    const c = new Ctx(vm); c.thread = th; c.cpu = th.cpu; c.sp = frame;
    const r = vm.api.lookup(dll, name).fn(c); return r === PARK || r === undefined ? r : r >>> 0;
  };
  const peek = () => call('user32.dll', 'PeekMessageA', msg, 0, 0, 0, 1);
  return { vm, clock, th, call, peek };
}

/**
 * `frames` frames of a limiter: `work` ms of other calls (8 API calls), then PeekMessage until the clock reaches the
 * deadline (`rel`: the previous frame's start + period, else the next multiple of the period); returns the frame start
 * times and the PeekMessage calls of each frame. `period` may be a function of the frame index.
 */
function limiter(env, frames, period, work = 12, rel = true) {
  const { clock, call, peek } = env, starts = [], peeks = [];
  let start = clock.now();
  for (let f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
    starts.push(start);
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { call('kernel32.dll', 'GetLastError'); clock.t += work / 8; }
    const p = typeof period === 'function' ? period(f) : period;
    const deadline = rel ? start + p : (Math.floor(start / p) + 1) * p;
    let n = 0;
    while (clock.now() < deadline) { peek(); n++; clock.t += 0.001; }
    peeks.push(n);
    start = clock.now();
  }
  return { starts, peeks };
}

test('PeekMessage polling waits, and frames start on time once the polling rate is known', { skip }, () => {
  const env = setup();
  const { starts, peeks } = limiter(env, 40, 100 / 3);
  const st = env.th.peekIdle;
  assert.ok(st.parks > 0, 'the polling waited');
  // without waits each frame polls ~21 ms at 1 µs per call: ~21 000 calls
  for (let f = 6; f < 40; f++) assert.ok(peeks[f] < 1500, `frame ${f}: ${peeks[f]} PeekMessage calls`);
  // the frame intervals: as without waits (the deadline plus at most one polling iteration) once learned
  for (let f = 6; f < 39; f++) { const d = starts[f + 1] - starts[f] - 100 / 3; assert.ok(d >= 0 && d < 0.01, `frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(4)} ms late`); }
  // before the estimate (the first frames), late by at most one short wait
  for (let f = 0; f < 39; f++) assert.ok(starts[f + 1] - starts[f] - 100 / 3 < 0.3, `frame ${f}`);
});

test('PeekMessage polling: an absolute deadline rule and a higher rate are followed', { skip }, () => {
  const env = setup();
  const a = limiter(env, 30, 25, 10, false);
  for (let f = 6; f < 29; f++) { const d = a.starts[f + 1] % 25; assert.ok(d < 0.01 || d > 24.99, `frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(4)}`); }
  // the rate goes up (25 -> 12.5 ms): a few frames late at most by a long wait, then on time again
  const b = limiter(env, 40, 12.5, 4, true);
  let late = 0;
  for (let f = 0; f < 39; f++) { const d = b.starts[f + 1] - b.starts[f] - 12.5; if (d > 0.01) late++; if (f > 12) assert.ok(d < 0.01, `frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(4)} ms late`); assert.ok(d < 4.5, `frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(3)}`); }
  assert.ok(late <= 6, `${late} late frames`);
});

test('PeekMessage polling: waits that last longer than asked (a coarse host timer) widen the margin', { skip }, () => {
  const env = setup();
  // every wait ends at the next whole millisecond after its deadline, plus 0.5 ms
  env.vm.host.waitEvent = (ms) => { const c = env.clock; c.sleepUntil(Math.ceil(c.now() + ms) + 0.5); };
  const { starts } = limiter(env, 60, 100 / 3);
  let late = 0;
  for (let f = 10; f < 59; f++) { const d = starts[f + 1] - starts[f] - 100 / 3; if (d > 0.01) late++; assert.ok(d < 2, `frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(3)} ms late`); }
  assert.ok(late <= 2, `${late} frames late after the first ten`);
  assert.ok(env.th.peekIdle.over > 0.5, 'the overshoot is known');
  // a 15.625 ms system timer: the first frames late, then on time (spinning where a wait would overshoot)
  const env2 = setup();
  env2.vm.host.waitEvent = (ms) => { const c = env2.clock; c.sleepUntil(Math.ceil((c.now() + ms) / 15.625) * 15.625); };
  const r = limiter(env2, 80, 100 / 3);
  for (let f = 30; f < 79; f++) { const d = r.starts[f + 1] - r.starts[f] - 100 / 3; assert.ok(d < 0.01, `15.625 ms timer, frame ${f}: ${d.toFixed(3)} ms late`); }
});

test('PeekMessage: no wait with ORTHROS_PEEK_IDLE_MS=0, nor when other calls come between, nor with a message', { skip }, () => {
  globalThis.ORTHROS_PEEK_IDLE_MS = 0;
  try {
    const env = setup();
    const t0 = env.clock.now();
    for (let i = 0; i < 5000; i++) { env.peek(); env.clock.t += 0.001; }
    assert.ok(Math.abs(env.clock.now() - t0 - 5) < 1e-6, 'the clock moved by the polling only');
    assert.equal(env.th.peekIdle, null);
  } finally { globalThis.ORTHROS_PEEK_IDLE_MS = undefined; }
  { // two other API calls between the polls: not message-loop polling
    const env = setup(), t0 = env.clock.now();
    for (let i = 0; i < 5000; i++) { env.peek(); env.call('kernel32.dll', 'GetLastError'); env.call('kernel32.dll', 'GetLastError'); env.clock.t += 0.001; }
    assert.ok(Math.abs(env.clock.now() - t0 - 5) < 1e-6);
    assert.equal(env.th.peekIdle.parks, 0);
  }
  { // a message is returned at once
    const env = setup();
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { env.peek(); env.clock.t += 0.001; }
    assert.ok(env.th.peekIdle.parks > 0);
    env.call('user32.dll', 'PostThreadMessageA', env.vm.proc.threads[0].id, 0x400, 7, 9);
    const t0 = env.clock.now();
    assert.equal(env.peek(), 1);
    assert.equal(env.clock.now(), t0);
  }
});

test('PeekMessage: a loop pumping messages between small chunks of guest work (no API call) is not slowed down', { skip }, () => {
  for (const [chunkMs, insns] of [[0.005, 5000], [0.02, 20000], [0.049, 50000]]) {
    const env = setup(), t0 = env.clock.now(), n = 20000;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { env.peek(); env.clock.t += chunkMs; env.vm.guestInsns += insns; }
    assert.ok(Math.abs(env.clock.now() - t0 - n * chunkMs) < 1e-6, `${chunkMs} ms chunks: ${(env.clock.now() - t0).toFixed(1)} ms for ${(n * chunkMs).toFixed(1)}`);
    assert.equal(env.th.peekIdle.parks, 0);
  }
  // a polling loop of ~100 guest instructions per call still waits
  const env = setup();
  for (let i = 0; i < 2000; i++) { env.peek(); env.clock.t += 0.001; env.vm.guestInsns += 100; }
  assert.ok(env.th.peekIdle.parks > 0);
});
```

`tests/perf-record.test.js`:

```js
// Passive session records (src/host/perf-record.js, src/host/web/perf-page.js, docs/real-machine-bench.md "Passive
// session records"): the recording per minute and per phase, hidden time left out, the counters' differences, the
// bounds, the server's validation and the /api/telemetry route, the page side with a fake window (frames, the
// engine's work, the GPU timer, the end), what a port's data waits were for (portDataSummary, compactDataSum), its
// session events (portEvents), the --perf report.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { PerfRecorder, sanitizePerfRecord, fitRecord, compactProbe, compactDataSum, MAX_RECORDS, MAX_ENTRIES, PERF_MAX_BYTES, PATH_MAX } from '../src/host/perf-record.js';
import { PerfSession, timerContext, portDataSummary, portEvents } from '../src/host/web/perf-page.js';
import { GameData } from '../src/vfs/data-client.js';
import { createServer } from '../src/host/server.js';
import { perfSessions, perfReport, formatPerf, gpuLabel, buildSessions } from '../tools/telemetry-report.mjs';
import { HIST_N, histBucket } from '../src/core/frame-acct.js';

const IRIS = 'ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (0x00009A49) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)';
const header = { session: 'abcd1234', game: 'g1', runtime: 'goldsrc', version: '1.0', build: 'b1', tier: null };

/** `seconds` of play at `dt` ms frames (every `slowEvery`th frame `slowMs` long), the clock every second. */
function play(rec, t0, seconds, { dt = 33.3, slowEvery = 0, slowMs = 120, work = 20, visible = true, phase = 'running', data = 0 } = {}) {
  let t = t0, next = t0 + 1000, i = 0;
  while (t < t0 + seconds * 1000) {
    const d = slowEvery && ++i % slowEvery === 0 ? slowMs : dt; t += d;
    if (visible) rec.frame(d, work, d === slowMs ? data : 0);
    while (t >= next) { rec.clock(next, visible, phase); next += 1000; }
  }
  return t;
}

test('frames per minute: fps, percentiles, slow frames, work and wait; a record every 2 min with the totals', () => {
  const r = new PerfRecorder({ header });
  r.clock(0, true, 'running');
  play(r, 0, 125, { slowEvery: 30, slowMs: 120 });
  const rec = r.take(125000);
  assert.ok(rec, 'a record after 2 min');
  assert.equal(rec.event, 'perf'); assert.equal(rec.seq, 0); assert.equal(rec.final, false); assert.equal(rec.session, 'abcd1234');
  assert.equal(rec.mins.length, 2, 'two whole minutes');
  const m = rec.mins[0];
  assert.equal(m.t, 0); assert.equal(m.ph, 'running');
  assert.ok(Math.abs(m.s - 60) <= 1, `visible seconds ${m.s}`);
  assert.ok(m.fps > 25 && m.fps < 30, `fps ${m.fps}`);
  assert.equal(m.p50, 34); // (the bucket's upper bound of 33.3 ms)
  assert.ok(m.p99 >= 120, `p99 ${m.p99}`);
  assert.ok(m.f40 >= 50 && m.f40 <= 70, `f40 ${m.f40}`); assert.equal(m.f40, m.f100);
  assert.equal(m.work, 20);
  assert.ok(m.wait > 13 && m.wait < 20, `wait ${m.wait}`);
  assert.ok(m.slow.work > 0 && m.slow.other > 0, 'the slow frames by cause');
  assert.equal(rec.tot.n, rec.mins[0].n + rec.mins[1].n + (rec.tot.n - rec.mins[0].n - rec.mins[1].n));
  assert.ok(Array.isArray(rec.tot.h) && rec.tot.h.length > 0);
  assert.equal(r.take(126000), null, 'not due again');
});

test('hidden time is counted apart and its frames left out; a hidden tab sends nothing', () => {
  const r = new PerfRecorder({ header });
  r.clock(0, true, 'running');
  let t = play(r, 0, 30);
  r.clock(30000, false, 'running');
  // (frames while hidden: ignored)
  for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) r.frame(16, 5, 0);
  for (let s = 31; s <= 90; s++) r.clock(s * 1000, false, 'running');
  r.clock(91000, true, 'running');
  t = play(r, 91000, 40);
  const rec = r.take(131000);
  assert.ok(rec);
  const hid = rec.mins.reduce((a, e) => a + e.hid, 0), vis = rec.mins.reduce((a, e) => a + e.s, 0);
  assert.ok(hid >= 58 && hid <= 62, `hidden ${hid}`);
  assert.ok(vis >= 57 && vis <= 61, `visible in the two minutes closed ${vis}`);
  assert.ok(rec.vis >= 68 && rec.vis <= 72, `visible in the session ${rec.vis}`);
  assert.ok(rec.tot.fps > 28 && rec.tot.fps < 31, `the totals' fps over the visible time: ${rec.tot.fps}`);
  assert.ok(rec.tot.p50 >= 33 && rec.tot.p50 <= 34, `no 16 ms frame counted: p50 ${rec.tot.p50}`);
  assert.ok(Math.abs(rec.hid - 61) <= 2 && rec.len === 131);
  // a long hidden stretch: no record without entries
  const h = new PerfRecorder({ header });
  h.clock(0, false, 'running');
  for (let s = 1; s <= 400; s++) h.clock(s * 1000, false, 'running');
  assert.equal(h.take(400000), null);
});

test('a phase change starts a new entry (a short one takes the new phase)', () => {
  const r = new PerfRecorder({ header });
  r.clock(0, true, 'starting');
  r.clock(2000, true, 'loading'); // (2 s: the entry takes the new phase)
  play(r, 2000, 20, { phase: 'loading' });
  play(r, 22000, 20, { phase: 'running' });
  const rec = r.take(42000, true);
  assert.deepEqual(rec.mins.map((e) => e.ph), ['loading', 'running']);
  assert.equal(rec.final, true);
  assert.equal(r.take(500000, true), null, 'nothing after the end');
});

test('Win32 intervals: frame accounting counts, categories, slow categories', () => {
  const r = new PerfRecorder({ header: { ...header, runtime: 'win32' } });
  r.clock(0, true, 'running');
  for (let i = 1; i <= 120; i++) {
    r.interval({ frames: 15, h: [33, 14, 120, 1], s40: 1, s100: 1, max: 121, w: 18, c: { guest: 12, draw: 6, wait: 15 }, sc: { guest: 80, wait: 40 } }, 15 * 33);
    if (i % 2 === 0) r.clock(i * 500, true, 'running');
  }
  const rec = r.take(60000, true);
  const m = rec.mins[0];
  assert.equal(m.n, 1800); assert.equal(m.f40, 120); assert.equal(m.f100, 120);

  assert.equal(m.slow.guest, 9600); assert.equal(m.slow.wait, 4800);
  assert.equal(m.p50, 34); assert.equal(m.max, 121);
});

test('GPU timer and data waits: differences per entry, totals over the session', () => {
  const r = new PerfRecorder({ header });
  const hist = new Array(HIST_N).fill(0);
  r.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 0, ms: 0, hist }, data: { waits: 0, ms: 0 } });
  r.clock(0, true, 'running');
  play(r, 0, 59);
  hist[histBucket(8.5)] += 120;
  r.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 120, ms: 1020, hist }, data: { waits: 3, ms: 450 } });
  play(r, 59000, 2);
  play(r, 61000, 58);
  hist[histBucket(12.5)] += 60;
  r.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 180, ms: 1770, hist }, data: { waits: 4, ms: 500 } });
  play(r, 119000, 3);
  const rec = r.take(122000);
  assert.deepEqual(rec.mins[0].gpu, { n: 120, mean: 8.5, p50: 9, p90: 9, p99: 9 });
  assert.deepEqual(rec.mins[0].data, { n: 3, ms: 450 });
  assert.deepEqual(rec.mins[1].gpu, { n: 60, mean: 12.5, p50: 13, p90: 13, p99: 13 });
  assert.deepEqual(rec.mins[1].data, { n: 1, ms: 50 });
  assert.equal(rec.tot.gpu.n, 180); assert.equal(rec.tot.data.ms, 500);
  // a browser without the timer: its state
  const u = new PerfRecorder({ header }); u.counters({ gpu: { state: 'unavailable' } }); u.clock(0, true, 'x'); play(u, 0, 10, { phase: 'x' });
  assert.deepEqual(u.take(10000, true).mins[0].gpu, { state: 'unavailable' });
  // queries lost (no result), and a frame past the histogram's last bound
  const l = new PerfRecorder({ header }); l.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 0, ms: 0, lost: 0, hist: new Array(HIST_N).fill(0) } }); l.clock(0, true, 'x'); play(l, 0, 10, { phase: 'x' });
  const big = new Array(HIST_N).fill(0); big[histBucket(9000)] = 1;
  l.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 0, ms: 0, lost: 7, hist: big.map(() => 0) } });
  assert.deepEqual(l.take(10000, true).mins[0].gpu, { n: 0, lost: 7 });
  const o = new PerfRecorder({ header }); o.clock(0, true, 'x'); o.counters({ gpu: { state: 'on', frames: 1, ms: 9000, hist: big } }); play(o, 0, 10, { phase: 'x' });
  assert.equal(o.take(10000, true).mins[0].gpu.p99, 5000);
});
```
