`tools/input-latency.mjs`:

```mjs
// tools/input-latency.mjs: input latency as the player feels it, from a Chrome trace — shared by the ports' tools
// (tools/openmw/place-load.mjs --input-trace; tests/input-latency.test.js; checked on a deliberately blocked page,
// tools/input-latency-check.mjs).
//
// Why from the trace: a page's own handler sees only the events it is handed. While its thread is held the browser
// coalesces the mouse moves queued for it into one (rAF-aligned input), so a probe in the page counts 3 moves over a
// 5 s block where the user made 100, and its percentiles compare different sets of events between two builds (the
// fourth validation of r20: 3-4 received moves against 14-16). Here every event the harness generates is counted.
//
// The events: generateInputs() sends mouse moves at a fixed cadence (default every 50 ms) and a key press now and then
// through CDP's Input domain without waiting for the page (a dispatch's answer waits for the renderer: an awaited
// generator stops while the page is held — place-load's 250 ms jiggler did). Chrome records one `EventLatency` (trace
// categories 'input'/'benchmark') for every one of them, coalesced or not: its begin is the event's own timestamp
// (when the harness made it), its stages tell how it ended — `RendererMainProcessing` when the page's thread
// dispatched it, `RendererCompositorFinishedToTermination` alone when it was coalesced into a move already queued (or
// dropped by the compositor), `SubmitCompositorFrameToPresentationCompositorFrame` when Chrome attributed a presented
// frame to it.
//
// The measure (inputLatency), per event in the window:
// - its carrier: the event itself when the page's thread dispatched it; a coalesced one's, the last move before it that
//   the page's thread dispatched at or after this one reached the renderer (still queued then: the one it merged into;
//   the queue coalesces into its tail only); none such — the next dispatch of its kind after it.
// - answered at: the earliest frame presented by the same renderer that committed a main frame after the carrier's
//   dispatch ended (a `PipelineReporter` presented, its `SendBeginMainFrameToCommit` ending at or after the dispatch's
//   end: the first picture that could show the handler's effect) — Chrome's own presentation stage when the carrier
//   has one, if earlier; no such frame in the trace: the dispatch's end (counted apart: `byDispatch`).
// - latency: answered at − the event's timestamp. Never answered (no carrier, the trace ended): its latency is the
//   window's end − its timestamp, a lower bound (counted apart: `unanswered`).
// p50/p95/max over every event whose timestamp is in [from, to] (trace clock, µs; traceClock() maps the page's).

/** The trace categories inputLatency needs (Chrome's input path, frames' reports, the page's console.timeStamp marks). */
export const INPUT_TRACE_CATEGORIES = ['input', 'latencyInfo', 'devtools.timeline', 'benchmark'];

const MOVE = new Set(['MOUSE_MOVED_EVENT', 'MOUSE_DRAGGED_EVENT']);
const PRESENTED = new Set(['STATE_PRESENTED_ALL', 'STATE_PRESENTED_PARTIAL']);
const idOf = (e) => (e.id2 ? JSON.stringify(e.id2) : e.id !== undefined ? String(e.id) : null);

/**
 * Chrome's nested async slices named `top` (EventLatency, PipelineReporter) with their stages: Chrome writes a
 * report's begin, its stages and its end together, on one thread, under one id (ids are reused once a report ended):
 * read in the trace's order, per thread and id. → [{ pid, ts, end, args, stages: { name: [begin, end] } }]
 */
export function asyncReports(events, top) {
  const open = new Map(), out = [];
  for (const e of events) {
    if (e.ph !== 'b' && e.ph !== 'e') continue;
    const id = idOf(e); if (id === null) continue;
    const k = `${e.pid}/${e.tid}/${id}`;
    if (e.name === top) {
      if (e.ph === 'b') { const r = { pid: e.pid, ts: e.ts, end: null, args: e.args ?? {}, stages: {} }; open.set(k, r); }
      else { const r = open.get(k); if (r) { r.end = e.ts; out.push(r); open.delete(k); } }
      continue;
    }
    const r = open.get(k); if (!r) continue;
    if (e.ph === 'b') r.stages[e.name] = [e.ts, null];
    else if (r.stages[e.name]) r.stages[e.name][1] = e.ts;
  }
  return out;
}

/** The trace's events: Chrome's JSON trace (an object with traceEvents, or the bare array). */
export const traceEvents = (trace) => (Array.isArray(trace) ? trace : trace?.traceEvents ?? []);

/**
 * The page's clock to the trace's: console.timeStamp(label) marks (devtools.timeline `TimeStamp`, args.data.message)
 * against `marks` { label: page ms (performance.now() taken at the call) }. → (pageMs) => trace µs, or null without a
 * mark found (several: their median offset).
 */
export function traceClock(events, marks) {
  const offs = [];
  for (const e of events) {
    if (e.name !== 'TimeStamp' || e.ph === 'M') continue;
    const m = e.args?.data?.message ?? e.args?.data?.name; if (m === undefined || !(m in marks)) continue;
    offs.push(e.ts - marks[m] * 1000);
  }
  if (!offs.length) return null;
  offs.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const off = offs[Math.floor(offs.length / 2)];
  return (ms) => ms * 1000 + off;
}

const q = (a, f) => (a.length ? Math.round(a[Math.min(a.length - 1, Math.floor(a.length * f))]) : null);

/**
 * Every generated input's latency from a trace (the module's header): `from`/`to` the window (trace µs; default the
 * trace's whole span), `types` the events counted (default every type: moves and keys; e.g. ['MOUSE_MOVED_EVENT']),
 * `pids` the renderers counted (default all). → { events, p50Ms, p95Ms, maxMs, byKind, byType, carriers, byDispatch,
 * unanswered, list: [[t µs, latency ms, how]] } (how: 'self'|'coalesced'|'next' + '/frame'|'/chrome'|'/dispatch', or 'none').
 */
export function inputLatency(trace, { from = -Infinity, to = Infinity, types = null, pids = null, list = false } = {}) {
  const ev = traceEvents(trace);
  const lat = asyncReports(ev, 'EventLatency').map((r) => {
    const s = r.stages, main = s.RendererMainProcessing, arrive = s.RendererCompositorProcessing?.[1] ?? s.BrowserMainToRendererCompositor?.[1] ?? r.ts;
    const pres = s.SubmitCompositorFrameToPresentationCompositorFrame?.[1] ?? null;
    return { pid: r.pid, t: r.ts, end: r.end, type: r.args?.event_latency?.event_type ?? 'UNKNOWN', arrive, main: main && main[1] !== null ? main : null, pres };
  }).filter((r) => !pids || pids.includes(r.pid)).sort((a, b) => a.t - b.t);
  const frames = new Map();
  for (const r of asyncReports(ev, 'PipelineReporter')) {
    const st = r.args?.frame_reporter?.state, c = r.stages.SendBeginMainFrameToCommit;
    if (!PRESENTED.has(st) || !c || c[1] === null || r.end === null) continue;
    if (!frames.has(r.pid)) frames.set(r.pid, []);
    frames.get(r.pid).push([c[1], r.end]);
  }
  for (const f of frames.values()) f.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);
  const ts = lat.map((r) => r.t);
  const lastT = ev.reduce((m, e) => (e.ts !== undefined && e.ph !== 'M' && e.ts > m ? e.ts : m), -Infinity);
  const winEnd = Number.isFinite(to) ? to : lastT;
  /** The earliest presentation of a frame of `pid` that committed at or after `t`. */
  const presentedAfter = (pid, t) => {
    const f = frames.get(pid); if (!f) return null;
    let lo = 0, hi = f.length; while (lo < hi) { const m = (lo + hi) >> 1; if (f[m][0] < t) lo = m + 1; else hi = m; }
    let best = null; for (let i = lo; i < f.length; i++) { if (best !== null && f[i][0] > best) break; if (best === null || f[i][1] < best) best = f[i][1]; }
    return best;
  };
  const kindOf = (type) => (MOVE.has(type) ? 'move' : /KEY|CHAR/.test(type) ? 'key' : type.toLowerCase());
  const out = [], carriers = { self: 0, coalesced: 0, next: 0, none: 0 };
  let byDispatch = 0;
  lat.forEach((r, i) => {
    if (r.t < from || r.t > to || (types && !types.includes(r.type))) return;
    const kind = kindOf(r.type);
    let carrier = null, how = 'none';
    if (r.main) { carrier = r; how = 'self'; }
    else {
      // (merged into the tail of the page's queue: the last earlier event of its kind still undispatched when it arrived)
      for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
        const c = lat[j]; if (c.pid !== r.pid || kindOf(c.type) !== kind || !c.main) continue;
        if (c.main[0] >= r.arrive) { carrier = c; how = 'coalesced'; }
        break;
      }
      if (!carrier) for (let j = i + 1; j < lat.length; j++) { const c = lat[j]; if (c.pid === r.pid && kindOf(c.type) === kind && c.main) { carrier = c; how = 'next'; break; } }
    }
    let at = null;
    if (carrier) {
      const f = presentedAfter(carrier.pid, carrier.main[1]);
      const c = carrier.pres;
      if (f !== null && (c === null || f <= c)) { at = f; how += '/frame'; }
      else if (c !== null) { at = c; how += '/chrome'; }
      else { at = carrier.main[1]; how += '/dispatch'; byDispatch++; }
      carriers[how.split('/')[0]]++;
    } else carriers.none++;
    const ms = ((at ?? Math.max(winEnd, r.t)) - r.t) / 1000;
    out.push({ t: r.t, ms, how, kind, type: r.type });
  });
  const all = out.map((x) => x.ms).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const sum = (a) => { const s = a.map((x) => x.ms).sort((x, y) => x - y); return { events: s.length, p50Ms: q(s, 0.5), p95Ms: q(s, 0.95), maxMs: s.length ? Math.round(s.at(-1)) : null }; };
  const byKind = {}, byType = {};
  for (const k of new Set(out.map((x) => x.kind))) byKind[k] = sum(out.filter((x) => x.kind === k));
  for (const x of out) byType[x.type] = (byType[x.type] ?? 0) + 1;
  return {
    events: all.length, p50Ms: q(all, 0.5), p95Ms: q(all, 0.95), maxMs: all.length ? Math.round(all.at(-1)) : null,
    byKind, byType, carriers, byDispatch, unanswered: carriers.none,
    ...(list ? { list: out.map((x) => [x.t, Math.round(x.ms), x.how]) } : {})
  };
}

/**
 * Inputs at a fixed cadence on `page` (Playwright) through CDP, never waiting for the page: a mouse move every
 * `moveMs` (alternating between two points `dx`,`dy` apart from `x`,`y`: no net movement), a key press (`key`, default
 * F13 — bound to nothing in a game, a key all the same: keydown, keyup `keyUpMs` later) every `keyMs` (0: none).
 * → { stop(): counts } (the counts sent).
 */
export async function generateInputs(page, { moveMs = 50, keyMs = 1000, x = 200, y = 200, dx = 40, dy = 30, key = 'F13', keyCode = 124, keyUpMs = 50 } = {}) {
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  const sent = { moves: 0, keys: 0, failed: 0 };
  const fail = () => { sent.failed++; };
  let k = 0;
  const mv = setInterval(() => { const a = ++k % 2; sent.moves++; cdp.send('Input.dispatchMouseEvent', { type: 'mouseMoved', x: x + a * dx, y: y + a * dy }).catch(fail); }, moveMs);
  const kk = keyMs > 0 ? setInterval(() => {
    sent.keys++;
    const d = { key, code: key, windowsVirtualKeyCode: keyCode, nativeVirtualKeyCode: keyCode };
    cdp.send('Input.dispatchKeyEvent', { type: 'rawKeyDown', ...d }).catch(fail);
    setTimeout(() => cdp.send('Input.dispatchKeyEvent', { type: 'keyUp', ...d }).catch(fail), keyUpMs);
  }, keyMs) : null;
  return {
    sent,
    async stop() { clearInterval(mv); if (kk) clearInterval(kk); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, keyUpMs + 20)); await cdp.detach().catch(() => {}); return { ...sent }; }
  };
}

/** A console.timeStamp mark in `frame` (Playwright page or frame) and the page's clock at it: traceClock's input. */
export const markClock = (frame, label) => frame.evaluate((label) => { const a = performance.now(); console.timeStamp(label); return (a + performance.now()) / 2; }, label);

/** The trace times (µs) of the console.timeStamp marks named `label`, in order. */
export const stampsOf = (trace, label) => traceEvents(trace).filter((e) => e.name === 'TimeStamp' && e.ph !== 'M' && (e.args?.data?.message ?? e.args?.data?.name) === label).map((e) => e.ts).sort((a, b) => a - b);

/**
 * The measure checked on a known block (the page's thread held from `start` to `end`, trace µs, by a busy loop): every
 * event made during it cannot be answered before the block ends, and should be soon after — its latency minus the rest
 * of the block (`end` − its timestamp) is the residual, ≥ 0 and small (a frame or two). → { events, blockMs, firstMs
 * (the first event's latency: ~ the block), residual: { min, p50, max } ms, list: [[ms into the block, latency ms, how]] }.
 */
export function blockCheck(trace, { start, end, types = ['MOUSE_MOVED_EVENT'] }) {
  const r = inputLatency(trace, { from: start, to: end, types, list: true });
  const res = r.list.map(([t, ms]) => ms - (end - t) / 1000).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  return {
    events: r.events, blockMs: Math.round((end - start) / 1000), firstMs: r.list[0]?.[1] ?? null, carriers: r.carriers,
    residual: { min: q(res, 0), p50: q(res, 0.5), max: res.length ? Math.round(res.at(-1)) : null },
    list: r.list.map(([t, ms, how]) => [Math.round((t - start) / 1000), ms, how])
  };
}

```

`tools/jit-dump.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Translated code listing: the WASM instructions the JIT emits for each guest instruction of a region, as a
// pseudo-WAT trace of the emitter calls (locals by name), with per-instruction counts and the block structure — to
// judge the code quality of common x86 patterns without a WASM disassembler (src/cpu/jit/listing.js; the page worker
// lists live regions of a running game the same way: harness input `jitlist:<hex eip>`).
// Usage: node tools/jit-dump.mjs <hex bytes | preset> [--cw 0x7f] [--quiet]
//   presets: prologue (frame setup, loads/stores, call, epilogue), xform (x87 float transform), loop (integer loop)
import { GuestMemory } from '../src/cpu/memory.js';
import { CpuState, THREAD_STATES_BASE, ST } from '../src/cpu/state.js';
import { listRegion } from '../src/cpu/jit/listing.js';
import '../src/cpu/jit/translate-x87.js'; // (the translators register their handlers on import, as jit.js does)
import '../src/cpu/jit/translate-sse-float.js';
import '../src/cpu/jit/translate-sse-int.js';

const CODE = 0x20000000;
const PRESETS = {
  // push ebp ; mov ebp, esp ; sub esp, 16 ; push esi ; mov esi, [ebp+8] ; mov eax, [esi+4] ; test eax, eax ; jz L ;
  // mov ecx, [eax+0x10] ; add [esi+8], ecx ; L: mov eax, [ebp-4] ; pop esi ; mov esp, ebp ; pop ebp ; ret 4
  prologue: '55 8bec 83ec10 56 8b7508 8b4604 85c0 7406 8b4810 014e08 8b45fc 5e 8be5 5d c20400',
  // fld [esi] ; fmul [edi] ; fld [esi+4] ; fmul [edi+4] ; faddp ; fld [esi+8] ; fmul [edi+8] ; faddp ; fadd [edi+12] ; fstp [ebx] ; ret
  xform: 'd906 d80f d94604 d84f04 dec1 d94608 d84f08 dec1 d8470c d91b c3',
  // xor eax, eax ; L: add eax, [esi+ecx*4] ; inc ecx ; cmp ecx, edx ; jl L ; ret
  loop: '31c0 03048e 41 39d1 7cf8 c3',
};
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = PRESETS[args[0]] ?? args.filter((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && !/^0x/.test(a) && args[i - 1] !== '--opts' && args[i - 1] !== '--cw').join('');
const cwArg = args.indexOf('--cw');
const cw = cwArg >= 0 ? parseInt(args[cwArg + 1], 16) : 0x027f;
const bytes = Uint8Array.from(src.replace(/\s+/g, '').match(/../g).map((h) => parseInt(h, 16)));

const mem = new GuestMemory();
const cpu = new CpuState(mem, THREAD_STATES_BASE);
cpu.reset();
mem.writeBytes(CODE, bytes);
mem.write16(cpu.base + ST.FPU_CW, cw);
// --opts <json>: translation options (e.g. '{"ifcvt":true}')
const optsArg = args.indexOf('--opts');
const extra = optsArg >= 0 ? JSON.parse(args[optsArg + 1]) : {};
console.log(listRegion(mem, CODE, { fpcAssume: cw & 0xf00, smc: true, ...extra }, { ops: !args.includes('--quiet') }).text);

```

`tools/jit-mix.mjs`:

```mjs
// Dynamic instruction mix of the translated code (diagnostics for the code generator): every live region translated
// with block counters (Jit opts.blockCounts) has its blocks decoded again and weighted by their execution counts —
// which instructions run, how many stores are checked for self-modifying code (not addressed by ESP), how long the
// blocks are, how often the code leaves its region. Used by tools/startbench.mjs --mix.
import { decode, OP, OP_NAMES, OT } from '../src/cpu/decoder.js';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { translateRegion, buildRegionModule, touchesFpu } from '../src/cpu/jit/translate.js';

const READS_FIRST = new Set(['CMP', 'TEST', 'BT', 'JMP', 'CALL', 'PUSH', 'FLD', 'FILD', 'FBLD', 'FCOM', 'FCOMP', 'FICOM', 'FICOMP', 'FUCOM', 'FUCOMP',
  'FADD', 'FSUB', 'FSUBR', 'FMUL', 'FDIV', 'FDIVR', 'FIADD', 'FISUB', 'FISUBR', 'FIMUL', 'FIDIV', 'FIDIVR', 'FLDCW', 'FLDENV', 'FRSTOR', 'FXRSTOR',
  'COMISS', 'UCOMISS', 'COMISD', 'UCOMISD', 'PREFETCH', 'CLFLUSH', 'LDMXCSR', 'NOP']);
const TERM_NAMES = ['fallthrough', 'jmp', 'jcc', 'call', 'ret', 'indirect', 'exit', 'loop'];

/**
 * @param {import('../src/cpu/jit/jit.js').Jit} jit
 * @returns {string} report
 */
export function jitMix(jit) {
  const mem = jit.mem;
  const ops = new Map(), stores = { esp: 0, ebp: 0, other: 0, abs: 0 }, terms = new Map();
  let insns = 0, blocks = 0, regionsCounted = 0, regionEntries = 0;
  const regionInsns = [];
  for (const r of jit.regions) {
    const counts = jit.blockCounts(r);
    if (!counts) continue;
    regionsCounted++;
    let ri = 0;
    r.blocks.forEach((b, k) => {
      const n = counts[b.index];
      if (!n) return;
      blocks += n;
      let a = b.eip;
      let last = null;
      while (a < b.end) {
        let insn;
        try { insn = decode(mem, a); } catch { break; }
        const name = OP_NAMES[insn.op];
        ops.set(name, (ops.get(name) ?? 0) + n);
        insns += n; ri += n;
        const m = insn.ops[0];
        if (m && m.t === OT.MEM && !READS_FIRST.has(name)) {
          if (m.base === 4 && m.index < 0) stores.esp += n;
          else if (m.base === 5) stores.ebp += n;
          else if (m.base < 0 && m.index < 0) stores.abs += n;
          else stores.other += n;
        }
        last = insn;
        a = insn.next;
      }
      void last;
    });
    regionInsns.push([r.entry, ri]);
    void regionEntries;
  }
  // checked stores per block that could share one check made before the first of them: stores whose address registers
  // no instruction between them writes (a register operand written, or any instruction with implicit writes)
  let checked = 0, groups = 0;
  for (const r of jit.regions) {
    const counts = jit.blockCounts(r);
    if (!counts) continue;
    r.blocks.forEach((b, k) => {
      const n = counts[b.index]; if (!n) return;
      let a = b.eip, open = null; // open group: Set of address registers
      while (a < b.end) {
        let insn; try { insn = decode(mem, a); } catch { break; }
        const name = OP_NAMES[insn.op], m = insn.ops[0];
        const isStore = m && m.t === OT.MEM && !READS_FIRST.has(name) && !(m.base === 4 && m.index < 0);
        if (isStore) {
          checked += n;
          const regsOf = new Set([m.base, m.index].filter((x) => x >= 0));
          if (!open) { groups += n; open = regsOf; } else for (const x of regsOf) open.add(x);
        }
        // writes ending the group: a register destination among the group's address registers, or an implicit writer
        const d = insn.ops[0];
        const writesReg = d && d.t === OT.REG ? (d.size === 1 && d.r >= 4 ? d.r - 4 : d.r) : -1;
        if (open && ((writesReg >= 0 && open.has(writesReg)) || ['CALL', 'RET', 'PUSHA', 'POPA', 'MOVS', 'STOS', 'CMPS', 'SCAS', 'LODS', 'XCHG', 'XADD', 'CMPXCHG', 'MUL', 'IMUL', 'DIV', 'IDIV', 'CDQ', 'CWD', 'LEAVE', 'POP'].includes(name))) open = null;
        a = insn.next;
      }
    });
  }
  const pct = (x) => (100 * x / Math.max(1, insns)).toFixed(1) + '%';
  void 0;
  const lines = [];
  lines.push(`[mix] ${regionsCounted} regions with counters, ${(insns / 1e6).toFixed(0)} M guest instructions in ${(blocks / 1e6).toFixed(0)} M block executions (${(insns / Math.max(1, blocks)).toFixed(2)} per block)`);
  lines.push(`[mix] stores: esp ${pct(stores.esp)}, ebp ${pct(stores.ebp)}, absolute ${pct(stores.abs)}, other ${pct(stores.other)} (checked: ${pct(stores.ebp + stores.abs + stores.other)})`);
  lines.push(`[mix] checked stores (executed) ${(checked / 1e6).toFixed(0)} M in ${(groups / 1e6).toFixed(0)} M groups sharing their address registers (x${(checked / Math.max(1, groups)).toFixed(2)} per group)`);
  lines.push(`[mix] top: ${[...ops].sort((x, y) => y[1] - x[1]).slice(0, 30).map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${pct(v)}`).join(', ')}`);
  regionInsns.sort((x, y) => y[1] - x[1]);
  let acc = 0; const cum = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < regionInsns.length; i++) { acc += regionInsns[i][1]; if ([10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000].includes(i + 1)) cum.push(`${i + 1}: ${pct(acc)}`); }
  lines.push(`[mix] instructions in the hottest regions: ${cum.join(', ')}`);
  lines.push(`[mix] hottest: ${regionInsns.slice(0, 12).map(([e, v]) => `${e.toString(16)} ${pct(v)}`).join(', ')}`);
  void terms; void TERM_NAMES; void OP;
  return lines.join('\n');
}

/**
 * ORTHROS_X87_DUMP=<dir> (with --mix): every live x87 region's module written to <dir>/new (as translated now) and to
 * <dir>/old (the same region translated with the x87 options of the earlier code: cold paths inline, rotating exits,
 * separate exit tails) — the game's own x87 regions, compiled afterwards by tools/x87-size.mjs --modules <dir> for
 * their machine code.
 */
const X87_DUMP = globalThis.process?.env?.ORTHROS_X87_DUMP ?? null;
const X87_OLD = { x87Cold: 'inline', x87ExitRotate: true, exitShare: false };
function dumpX87Region(jit, r, code) {
  const name = `x_${(r.entry >>> 0).toString(16)}_${r.fpc ?? 'g'}_${r.fnIdx}`; // (unique: versions share their entry)
  for (const [sub, c] of [['new', code], ['old', null]]) {
    const d = path.join(X87_DUMP, sub); fs.mkdirSync(d, { recursive: true });
    let body = c;
    if (!body) { try { body = translateRegion(jit.mem, r.entry, { ...jit.translateOpts(r.fnIdx, r.fpc), blockCounts: false, ...X87_OLD }).code; } catch { return; } }
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(d, name + '.wasm'), buildRegionModule([body], [name]));
  }
}

/**
 * The x87 regions among every live region (a region holding an x87 instruction caches the register stack: translate.js
 * usesX87), not only the first ones jitShape lists: count, WASM body bytes, guest instructions, operations by part, the
 * x87 arithmetic's share (FADD..FDIVR, FIADD..FIDIVR and their popping forms) — static, and weighted by the block
 * executions (translations with counters) — and the static operations per instruction of the most executed mnemonics.
 * With ORTHROS_X87_DUMP each region's module is written both ways (dumpX87Region).
 */
function x87Shape(jit, listRegion, over) {
  const ARITH = /^f(i?add|i?mul|i?sub|i?subr|i?div|i?divr|addp|mulp|subp|subrp|divp|divrp)$/;
  const x = { regions: 0, bytes: 0, insns: 0, ops: 0, arith: 0, arithN: 0, prologue: 0, epilogue: 0, blockEnd: 0, dynInsns: 0, dynOps: 0, dynArith: 0, dynArithOps: 0 };
  const byOp = new Map();
  for (const r of jit.regions) {
    let fpu = false;
    for (const b of r.blocks) {
      for (let a = b.eip; a < b.end && !fpu;) { let insn; try { insn = decode(jit.mem, a); } catch { break; } if (touchesFpu(insn)) fpu = true; a = insn.next; }
      if (fpu) break;
    }
    if (!fpu) continue;
    let L;
    try { L = listRegion(jit.mem, r.entry, { ...jit.translateOpts(r.fnIdx, r.fpc), blockCounts: false, ...over }, { counts: jit.blockCounts(r), ops: false }); } catch { continue; }
    if (X87_DUMP && over && over !== X87_OLD) dumpX87Region(jit, r, L.result.code);
    const counts = jit.blockCounts(r);
    x.regions++; x.bytes += L.result.code.length;
    for (const g of L.groups) {
      if (g.head) continue;
      const n = g.ops.length, w = counts && g.block >= 0 ? counts[g.block] ?? 0 : 0;
      x.ops += n;
      if (g.block < 0) { if (/prologue/.test(g.label)) x.prologue += n; else x.epilogue += n; continue; }
      x.dynOps += n * w;
      if (g.tail) { x.blockEnd += n; continue; }
      const m = g.label.trim().split(/\s+/)[1] ?? '';
      x.insns++; x.dynInsns += w;
      const e = byOp.get(m) ?? { n: 0, ops: 0, dyn: 0 }; e.n++; e.ops += n; e.dyn += w; byOp.set(m, e);
      if (ARITH.test(m)) { x.arith += n; x.arithN++; x.dynArith += w; x.dynArithOps += n * w; }
    }
  }
  if (!x.regions) return [];
  const pct = (a, b) => (100 * a / Math.max(1, b)).toFixed(1);
  const lines = [`[shape] x87 regions: ${x.regions} of ${jit.regions.length}, ${(x.bytes / 1024).toFixed(0)} KiB WASM bodies (${(x.bytes / x.regions / 1024).toFixed(1)} KiB each), ${x.insns} guest instructions, ${(x.ops / x.insns).toFixed(1)} operations per instruction; x87 arithmetic ${x.arithN} instructions, ${(x.arith / Math.max(1, x.arithN)).toFixed(1)} operations each, ${pct(x.arith, x.ops)} % of the operations; prologues ${pct(x.prologue, x.ops)} %, epilogues ${pct(x.epilogue, x.ops)} %, block ends ${pct(x.blockEnd, x.ops)} %`];
  if (x.dynInsns) lines.push(`[shape] x87 regions executed: ${(x.dynInsns / 1e6).toFixed(0)} M guest instructions, x87 arithmetic ${pct(x.dynArith, x.dynInsns)} % of them and ${pct(x.dynArithOps, x.dynOps)} % of the operations executed (weighted by block executions)`);
  const top = [...byOp].sort((a, b) => (b[1].dyn || b[1].n) - (a[1].dyn || a[1].n)).slice(0, 16);
  lines.push(`[shape] x87 regions by instruction (static operations per instruction${x.dynInsns ? ', share of executed instructions' : ''}): ${top.map(([k, e]) => `${k} ${(e.ops / e.n).toFixed(0)}${x.dynInsns ? ` ${pct(e.dyn, x.dynInsns)}%` : ''}`).join(', ')}`);
  return lines;
}

/**
 * Static shape of the translated code: every live region translated again under the listing (src/cpu/jit/listing.js),
 * its WASM operations counted per guest instruction kind and per part (prologue, block ends, epilogue: exits, chaining)
 * — with `counts`, weighted by the block executions too. What the code generator spends its operations on.
 * @param {import('../src/cpu/jit/jit.js').Jit} jit
 * @param {(mem: any, entry: number, opts: any, how: any) => any} listRegion
 */
export function jitShape(jit, listRegion, max = 4000, over = null) {
  // (with ORTHROS_X87_DUMP, the same report for the earlier x87 options follows, its lines tagged [shape-old])
  if (X87_DUMP && !over) return jitShape(jit, listRegion, max, {}) + '\n' + jitShape(jit, listRegion, max, X87_OLD).replace(/\[shape\]/g, '[shape-old]');
  const byOp = new Map(), parts = { insn: 0, blockEnd: 0, prologue: 0, epilogue: 0 }, dyn = { insn: 0, blockEnd: 0 };
  let insns = 0, regions = 0, bytes = 0, dynInsns = 0;
  for (const r of jit.regions.slice(0, max)) {
    let L;
    try { L = listRegion(jit.mem, r.entry, { ...jit.translateOpts(r.fnIdx, r.fpc), blockCounts: false, ...over }, { counts: jit.blockCounts(r), ops: false }); } catch { continue; }
    regions++; bytes += L.result.code.length;
    const counts = jit.blockCounts(r);
    for (const g of L.groups) {
      const n = g.ops.length, w = counts && g.block >= 0 ? counts[g.block] ?? 0 : 0;
      if (g.head) continue;
      if (g.block < 0) { if (/prologue/.test(g.label)) parts.prologue += n; else parts.epilogue += n; continue; }
      if (g.tail) { parts.blockEnd += n; dyn.blockEnd += n * w; continue; }
      const m = g.label.split(/\s+/)[1];
      const e = byOp.get(m) ?? { n: 0, ops: 0, dyn: 0, dynOps: 0 };
      e.n++; e.ops += n; e.dyn += w; e.dynOps += n * w; byOp.set(m, e);
      parts.insn += n; dyn.insn += n * w; insns++; dynInsns += w;
    }
  }
  const total = parts.insn + parts.blockEnd + parts.prologue + parts.epilogue;
  const lines = [];
  const x87Lines = x87Shape(jit, listRegion, over);
  // duplication: the same guest code translated in several regions (callees and shared paths copied into each region
  // reaching them)
  { const seen = new Set(); let all = 0; for (const r of jit.regions) for (const b of r.blocks) { all += b.end - b.eip; for (let a = b.eip; a < b.end; a++) seen.add(a); }
    lines.push(`[shape] duplication: ${jit.regions.length} live regions translate ${(all / 1024).toFixed(0)} KiB of guest code, ${(seen.size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KiB distinct (x${(all / Math.max(1, seen.size)).toFixed(2)})`); }
  lines.push(`[shape] ${regions} regions, ${insns} guest instructions, ${(bytes / insns).toFixed(1)} body bytes and ${(total / insns).toFixed(1)} operations per instruction: instructions ${(100 * parts.insn / total).toFixed(0)}%, block ends ${(100 * parts.blockEnd / total).toFixed(0)}%, prologues ${(100 * parts.prologue / total).toFixed(0)}%, epilogues ${(100 * parts.epilogue / total).toFixed(0)}%`);
  lines.push(...x87Lines);
  if (dynInsns) lines.push(`[shape] executed: ${((dyn.insn + dyn.blockEnd) / dynInsns).toFixed(1)} operations per instruction (block ends ${(100 * dyn.blockEnd / (dyn.insn + dyn.blockEnd)).toFixed(0)}%)`);
  const top = [...byOp].sort((a, b) => (b[1].dynOps || b[1].ops) - (a[1].dynOps || a[1].ops)).slice(0, 25);
  lines.push(`[shape] by instruction (static ops/insn, executed share of operations): ${top.map(([k, e]) => `${k} ${(e.ops / e.n).toFixed(1)}${dynInsns ? ` ${(100 * e.dynOps / Math.max(1, dyn.insn + dyn.blockEnd)).toFixed(1)}%` : ''}`).join(', ')}`);
  return lines.join('\n');
}
```

`tools/jit-suite.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Run one generated conformance suite through the JIT and report native/fallback statistics.
//
//   node tools/jit-suite.mjs <suite> [--modules a.js,b.js] [--only REGEX] [--show N]
//
// Same harness as tests/cpu-jit.test.js (tests/conformance/runner.js runSuite, one region per
// case bounded at `end`, maxInsns 100000, x87 stack-fault cases skipped). `--modules` imports
// extra ES modules before running (e.g. a translator module registering HANDLERS that is not
// yet wired into jit.js). `--only` keeps only the cases whose asm matches the regex. Prints the
// total, the failures (up to --show N, default 20), jit.stats native/fallback/fallbackSteps and
// the interpreter-fallback histogram by mnemonic.
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { runSuite, isStackFaultCase } from '../tests/conformance/runner.js';
import { Interp } from '../src/cpu/interp.js';
import '../src/cpu/interp-x87.js';
import '../src/cpu/interp-sse.js';
import { Jit } from '../src/cpu/jit/jit.js';
import { OP_NAMES } from '../src/cpu/decoder.js';

const DIR = new URL('../tests/generated/', import.meta.url).pathname;

function parseArgs(argv) {
  const o = { suite: null, modules: [], only: null, show: 20 };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    const a = argv[i];
    if (a === '--modules') o.modules = argv[++i].split(',').filter(Boolean);
    else if (a === '--only') o.only = new RegExp(argv[++i]);
    else if (a === '--show') o.show = +argv[++i];
    else if (a.startsWith('--')) { console.error(`unknown option ${a}`); process.exit(2); }
    else if (!o.suite) o.suite = a;
    else { console.error(`unexpected argument ${a}`); process.exit(2); }
  }
  if (!o.suite) { console.error('usage: node tools/jit-suite.mjs <suite> [--modules a.js,b.js] [--only REGEX] [--show N]'); process.exit(2); }
  return o;
}

const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
for (const m of args.modules) {
  const url = pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.cwd(), m)).href;
  await import(url);
}

let jit;
const t0 = performance.now();
const res = runSuite(DIR, args.suite, (mem, cpu) => {
  const I = new Interp(mem, cpu);
  jit = new Jit(mem, I, { fallbackHist: true });
  return {
    run(end) {
      jit.reset();
      I.cache.clear();
      jit.boundaries = new Set([end]);
      jit.cpu = cpu;
      const r = jit.run({ stopAt: end, maxInsns: 100000 });
      this.lastFault = jit.lastFault;
      return r;
    },
  };
}, {
  skip: (i, c) => isStackFaultCase(i, c) || (args.only !== null && !args.only.test(c.meta[i].asm)),
});
const ms = performance.now() - t0;

const s = jit.stats;
console.log(`${args.suite}: ${res.total} cases, ${res.failures.length} failures, ${res.skipped} skipped, ${ms.toFixed(0)} ms`);
console.log(`jit stats: regions ${s.regions} blocks ${s.blocks} native ${s.native} fallback ${s.fallback} fallbackSteps ${s.fallbackSteps}`);
const hist = [...jit.fallbackHist.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
console.log(`fallback histogram (${hist.length} mnemonics): ${hist.map(([op, n]) => `${OP_NAMES[op]} ${n}`).join(', ') || '(none)'}`);
if (res.failures.length) {
  console.log(`failures (showing ${Math.min(args.show, res.failures.length)} of ${res.failures.length}):`);
  for (const f of res.failures.slice(0, args.show)) console.log(`#${f.i} ${f.asm}\n    ${f.diff}`);
}
process.exit(res.failures.length ? 1 : 0);
```

`tools/learn-prune.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Learned prefetch orders without the mask-less entries that are provably stale (docs/slow-network.md "Learned order").
// An entry learned before masks existed ([path#block, t, n], no fourth element) stands for a whole 1 MiB block: a link
// that is not fast fetches the learned pieces only (its mask), so on a thin link the learned pass skips such an entry
// altogether, and on a between link it fetches the whole block.
//
// A mask-less entry is NOT a block "no recent session read": it is also the only record of a phase no recent session
// reached (a map load after sessions that stopped at the menu). The prune of 2026-10-21, which dropped every mask-less
// entry of an order that had enough masked ones, took BFME II's map load out of its order (docs/startup.md "Why RotWK
// 2.02 and BFME II waited"). So an entry is dropped only when one of two rules proves it stale:
//
//   masked-duplicate  the same block (path compared case-insensitively, '\' as '/') has a masked entry in the order:
//                     a session re-learned it since masks exist (the server ORs the pieces into the entry it reads), the
//                     mask-less record adds nothing but a whole-block fetch.
//   passed-unread     at least --sessions N (default 3) of the --recent K (default 10) latest sessions provably went
//                     through the entry's phase / time without reading the block. Needs a per-session record of reads
//                     (sessions-<manifest>.json, below). The server keeps none on disk (its sessions' read sets live in
//                     memory, phases-<manifest>.json counts phase starts, not reads): without that file the rule
//                     refuses, and drops nothing.
//
// A session "passed" an entry when its record reached the entry's time (`reached` ≥ t) without reading the block, and
// it went through the entry's phase: one of the entry's phases (`ph`) is among the session's, or — an entry without
// phases — the session read at least half of the order's masked entries learned within --window ms (default 5000) of
// the entry's time, with at least --min-neighbors (default 3) such entries: a phase none of the recent sessions
// reached has no masked neighbours, so its entries stay.
//
// sessions-<manifest>.json (not written by the server today; a later server or an operator's export):
//   [{ "id": "…", "reached": <ms from the session's first read>, "phases": [["map", 41000], …], "read": ["path#block", …] }, …]
//   oldest first.
//
// Usage: node tools/learn-prune.mjs <learn dir> [--only <manifest>]... [--sessions N] [--recent K] [--window MS]
//          [--min-neighbors N] [--list] [--write]
//   Without --write (the default): a dry run — each prefetch-<manifest>.json, its entries, mask-less ones and what each
//   rule would drop (entries, whole-block MB), what stays and why; --list prints every mask-less entry with its verdict.
//   With --write the entries the rules drop go (the file first copied to <file>.bak-<time>). The server keeps the orders
//   in memory and writes them back: run it while the server is stopped (or just before its restart), on a copy first.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const BLOCK = 1 << 20, CHUNK = 64 << 10;
const bits = (m) => { let n = 0; for (let x = m >>> 0; x; x &= x - 1) n++; return n; };
const isMaskless = (e) => Array.isArray(e) && (e[3] === undefined || e[3] === null);
/** A block's key as the game's files are matched (case-insensitively, either separator). */
export const blockKey = (k) => String(k).replace(/\\/g, '/').toLowerCase();

/** An order's entries split: { all, maskless: [...], masked: [...], masklessBytes, maskedBytes }. */
export function splitOrder(entries) {
  const maskless = [], masked = [];
  for (const e of entries) (isMaskless(e) ? maskless : masked).push(e);
  return { all: entries.length, maskless, masked, masklessBytes: maskless.length * BLOCK, maskedBytes: masked.reduce((n, e) => n + (e[3] ? bits(e[3]) * CHUNK : BLOCK), 0) };
}

/** A session record checked: { id, reached, phases: Set, read: Set(blockKey) } or null. */
function sessionRecord(s) {
  if (!s || typeof s !== 'object' || !Number.isFinite(s.reached) || !Array.isArray(s.read)) return null;
  return { id: String(s.id ?? ''), reached: s.reached, phases: new Set((Array.isArray(s.phases) ? s.phases : []).filter(Array.isArray).map((p) => String(p[0]))),
    read: new Set(s.read.map(blockKey)) };
}

/**
 * The verdict on each mask-less entry of `entries`: { drops: Map(entry -> rule), kept: Map(entry -> reason),
 * rules: { 'masked-duplicate': { entries, bytes }, 'passed-unread': { entries, bytes, refused? } } }.
 * `sessions`: the per-session records, oldest first (null: none kept — the passed-unread rule refuses).
 */
export function planPrune(entries, { sessions = null, need = 3, recent = 10, windowMs = 5000, minNeighbors = 3 } = {}) {
  const s = splitOrder(entries), drops = new Map(), kept = new Map();
  const maskedKeys = new Set(s.masked.filter(Array.isArray).map((e) => blockKey(e[0])));
  const recs = sessions ? sessions.map(sessionRecord).filter(Boolean).slice(-recent) : null;
  const masked = s.masked.filter((e) => Array.isArray(e) && Number.isFinite(e[1])).sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
  const neighbours = (t) => { // (the masked entries learned within windowMs of t)
    let lo = 0, hi = masked.length;
    while (lo < hi) { const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; if (masked[mid][1] < t - windowMs) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; }
    const out = []; for (let i = lo; i < masked.length && masked[i][1] <= t + windowMs; i++) out.push(blockKey(masked[i][0]));
    return out;
  };
  const passed = (r, e, key) => {
    if (r.read.has(key) || !(r.reached >= e[1])) return false;
    const ph = e[6] && typeof e[6] === 'object' ? Object.keys(e[6]) : [];
    if (ph.length) return ph.some((p) => r.phases.has(p));
    const nb = neighbours(e[1]);
    return nb.length >= minNeighbors && nb.filter((k) => r.read.has(k)).length * 2 >= nb.length;
  };
  for (const e of s.maskless) {
    const key = blockKey(e[0]);
    if (maskedKeys.has(key)) { drops.set(e, 'masked-duplicate'); continue; }
    if (!recs) { kept.set(e, 'no per-session record (passed-unread refused)'); continue; }
    const n = recs.filter((r) => passed(r, e, key)).length;
    if (n >= need && recs.length) drops.set(e, 'passed-unread');
    else kept.set(e, `${n} of ${recs.length} recent sessions passed it unread (${need} needed)`);
  }
  const rule = (name) => { const n = [...drops.values()].filter((v) => v === name).length; return { entries: n, bytes: n * BLOCK }; };
  return { ...s, drops, kept, rules: { 'masked-duplicate': rule('masked-duplicate'), 'passed-unread': { ...rule('passed-unread'), ...(recs ? { sessions: recs.length } : { refused: true }) } } };
}

/** The per-session records kept beside an order (sessions-<manifest>.json), null when there are none. */
export function readSessions(file) {
  const f = file.replace(/prefetch-([^/\\]+)\.json$/, 'sessions-$1.json');
  if (f === file || !fs.existsSync(f)) return null;
  const j = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));
  if (!Array.isArray(j)) throw new Error(`${f}: not a list of session records`);
  return j;
}

/** The order of `file` with the entries planPrune drops taken out (only with `write`): the plan and `written`. */
export function pruneFile(file, { write = false, now = new Date(), sessions, ...opts } = {}) {
  const entries = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
  if (!Array.isArray(entries)) throw new Error(`${file}: not a learned order`);
  const plan = planPrune(entries, { sessions: sessions === undefined ? readSessions(file) : sessions, ...opts });
  let written = false;
  if (write && plan.drops.size) {
    fs.copyFileSync(file, `${file}.bak-${now.toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')}`);
    fs.writeFileSync(file + '.tmp', JSON.stringify(entries.filter((e) => !plan.drops.has(e)))); fs.renameSync(file + '.tmp', file);
    written = true;
  }
  return { ...plan, written };
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  const VAL = ['--only', '--sessions', '--recent', '--window', '--min-neighbors'];
  const args = process.argv.slice(2), dir = args.find((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && !VAL.includes(args[i - 1]));
  const usage = 'usage: node tools/learn-prune.mjs <learn dir> [--only <manifest>]... [--sessions N] [--recent K] [--window MS] [--min-neighbors N] [--list] [--write]';
  if (args.includes('--min-masked')) { console.error('--min-masked is gone: a count of masked entries does not prove a mask-less one stale (docs/slow-network.md)'); process.exit(2); }
  if (!dir) { console.error(usage); process.exit(2); }
  const num = (flag, d) => { if (!args.includes(flag)) return d; const v = Number(args[args.indexOf(flag) + 1]); if (!(v >= 0)) { console.error(`${flag}: a number`); process.exit(2); } return v; };
  const opts = { need: Math.max(1, num('--sessions', 3)), recent: num('--recent', 10), windowMs: num('--window', 5000), minNeighbors: Math.max(1, num('--min-neighbors', 3)) };
  const only = args.flatMap((a, i) => (a === '--only' ? [args[i + 1]] : [])), write = args.includes('--write'), list = args.includes('--list');
  const MB = (b) => (b / 1048576).toFixed(0);
  if (!write) console.log('dry run (--write to drop)');
  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => /^prefetch-.+\.json$/.test(n)).sort()) {
    const name = f.slice('prefetch-'.length, -'.json'.length);
    if (only.length && !only.includes(name)) continue;
    const r = pruneFile(path.join(dir, f), { write, ...opts });
    const md = r.rules['masked-duplicate'], pu = r.rules['passed-unread'];
    console.log(`${name.padEnd(40)} ${String(r.all).padStart(6)} entries, ${String(r.maskless.length).padStart(5)} mask-less (${MB(r.masklessBytes)} MB whole blocks), masked ${MB(r.maskedBytes)} MB${r.written ? ` -> ${r.drops.size} dropped` : ''}`);
    if (!r.maskless.length) continue;
    console.log(`  masked-duplicate: ${md.entries} (${MB(md.bytes)} MB)   passed-unread: ${pu.refused ? 'refused (no sessions-' + name + '.json: the server keeps no per-session reads)' : `${pu.entries} (${MB(pu.bytes)} MB) over ${pu.sessions} recent sessions`}   kept: ${r.kept.size}`);
    if (list) for (const e of r.maskless) console.log(`    ${String(e[0]).padEnd(60)} t ${String(Math.round(e[1])).padStart(8)} ms  ${r.drops.has(e) ? 'drop: ' + r.drops.get(e) : 'keep: ' + r.kept.get(e)}`);
  }
}

```

`tools/learn-unflag.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// A learned launch set taken back for some files (docs/slow-network.md "Launch set after an engine change"): the
// entries of a version's learned order (prefetch-<manifest>.json) whose file is one of --path lose their `pre` count
// (the marking sessions that had read them before playable, the 5th element, and its per-language counts, the 6th) —
// out of the launch set at once, flagged again only if new sessions read them before playable as often as the version's
// marks ask (half of them: server.js prefetchList). They also move to the END of the order: their time becomes later
// than every other entry's, their phases go (the order is sorted by time — the earliest across sessions —, so an entry
// left at its early time would still be the first thing fetched after the launch set: measured on reVC r3 at 1.8 MB/s,
// the 11 MB sound bank downloaded during the menu ahead of the new game's gta3.img blocks, ~20 more serial demand reads
// in its load). A session that reads them earlier again teaches its own time. The version's marks
// (playable-<manifest>.json), the entries' counts and piece masks stay.
//
// What it is for: an engine release that no longer reads a file before playable (reVC r3: sound bank 0 read sample by
// sample on first play, no longer whole at the audio's start) leaves that file flagged by the sessions of the release
// before — with 19 marks, about 20 sessions of the new release before the server would stop flagging it alone.
// And --tail: an engine release that no longer reads a file's first blocks in play (reVC r4: a streamed MP3/ADF seeks
// to its byte estimate, no longer reading every frame from the file's start up to it) leaves those blocks early in the
// order, counted by the older release's sessions, never flagged (read after playable): fetched by every new device in
// the new game's load. With --tail the entries of the files and blocks named move to the end of the order whether
// counted before playable or not (those counted lose that count as above). The move lasts only for blocks the new
// release no longer reads early: the server keeps a block's earliest time over every session and sorts the order by it
// alone, so one session that reads a moved block early (an ambience started at a random position: its target block)
// puts it back — resetting its count would not help (docs/slow-network.md "How long the move lasts").
//
// Usage: node tools/learn-unflag.mjs <learn dir> --only <manifest>... --path <game file>[#<blocks>]... [--tail] [--write]
//   --path: a game file as the order names it (case-insensitively, either separator: 'Audio/sfx.RAW'); every block of it,
//   or the 1 MiB blocks given after '#': one ('#3'), a range ('#1-8'), or from one to the file's end ('#1-').
//   --tail: the entries named move to the end of the order even when no session counted them before playable.
//   Without --write (the default): a dry run — per order, the entries and bytes (whole 1 MiB blocks, or their learned
//   pieces) that are flagged today and would leave the launch set. With --write the counts go (the file first copied to
//   <file>.bak-<time>). The server keeps the orders in memory and writes them back: run it while the server is stopped,
//   after tools/backup.sh snapshot, on a copy first.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const BLOCK = 1 << 20, CHUNK = 64 << 10;
const bits = (m) => { let n = 0; for (let x = m >>> 0; x; x &= x - 1) n++; return n; };
/** A file's key as the game's files are matched (case-insensitively, either separator). */
const fileKey = (p) => String(p).replace(/\\/g, '/').toLowerCase();
/** An entry's file (its key "path#block"). */
const entryFile = (k) => { const s = String(k), i = s.lastIndexOf('#'); return i < 0 ? s : s.slice(0, i); };
/** An entry's block (its key's number after '#'), null without one. */
const entryBlock = (k) => { const m = /#(\d+)$/.exec(String(k)); return m ? Number(m[1]) : null; };

/**
 * A --path as a selector: { key, lo, hi } — the file's key and its blocks [lo, hi] (every one without '#<blocks>').
 * A path whose own name holds '#' followed by anything but a block range is taken whole.
 */
export function parsePath(p) {
  const m = /^(.*)#(\d+)(?:(-)(\d*))?$/.exec(String(p));
  if (!m) return { key: fileKey(p), lo: 0, hi: Infinity };
  const lo = Number(m[2]), hi = m[3] ? (m[4] === '' ? Infinity : Number(m[4])) : lo;
  if (hi < lo) throw new Error(`${p}: empty block range`);
  return { key: fileKey(m[1]), lo, hi };
}

/**
 * An entry without its `pre` counts nor its phases, at time `t` (the order's end), in the row form the server writes
 * (server.js armLearnTimer): [k, t, n, mask], or [k, t, n] (no mask learned).
 */
export function unflagEntry(e, t = e[1]) {
  return e[3] === undefined || e[3] === null ? [e[0], t, e[2]] : [e[0], t, e[2], e[3]];
}

/**
 * The plan for an order (`entries`, `marks`: the version's marking sessions, playable-<manifest>.json): the entries of
 * `paths` (files, or blocks of them: parsePath) that carry a `pre` count — `hit`, a Set — and of them those flagged
 * today (`flagged`, `flaggedBytes`: whole blocks, or their learned pieces), and the order with them unflagged
 * (`entries`). `tail`: the entries of `paths` without a `pre` count move to the end too (`moved`, a Set, with `hit`'s).
 */
export function planUnflag(entries, paths, marks = 0, { tail = false } = {}) {
  const sel = paths.map(parsePath), hit = new Set(), moved = new Set();
  const named = (k) => { const f = fileKey(entryFile(k)), b = entryBlock(k); return sel.some((x) => x.key === f && (b === null ? x.lo === 0 && x.hi === Infinity : b >= x.lo && b <= x.hi)); };
  let flagged = 0, flaggedBytes = 0;
  // (after every other entry, in their own order: their time past the order's latest by their rank)
  const end = entries.reduce((m, e) => (Array.isArray(e) && Number.isFinite(e[1]) ? Math.max(m, e[1]) : m), 0) + 1;
  let rank = 0;
  const out = entries.map((e) => {
    if (!Array.isArray(e) || !named(e[0])) return e;
    if (!(e[4] > 0)) { if (!tail) return e; moved.add(e); return unflagEntry(e, end + rank++); }
    hit.add(e); moved.add(e);
    if (marks && e[4] * 2 >= marks) { flagged++; flaggedBytes += e[3] ? bits(e[3]) * CHUNK : BLOCK; }
    return unflagEntry(e, end + rank++);
  });
  return { hit, moved, flagged, flaggedBytes, entries: out };
}

/** The order of `file` with planUnflag's entries unflagged (only with `write`): the plan and `written`. */
export function unflagFile(file, paths, { write = false, now = new Date(), tail = false } = {}) {
  const entries = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
  if (!Array.isArray(entries)) throw new Error(`${file}: not a learned order`);
  let marks = 0;
  try { marks = Number(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file.replace(/prefetch-([^/\\]+)\.json$/, 'playable-$1.json'), 'utf8')).marks) || 0; } catch { /* never marked */ }
  const plan = planUnflag(entries, paths, marks, { tail });
  let written = false;
  if (write && plan.moved.size) {
    fs.copyFileSync(file, `${file}.bak-${now.toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')}`);
    fs.writeFileSync(file + '.tmp', JSON.stringify(plan.entries)); fs.renameSync(file + '.tmp', file);
    written = true;
  }
  return { ...plan, marks, written };
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  const VAL = ['--only', '--path'];
  const args = process.argv.slice(2), dir = args.find((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && !VAL.includes(args[i - 1]));
  const many = (flag) => args.flatMap((a, i) => (a === flag ? [args[i + 1]] : []));
  const only = many('--only'), paths = many('--path'), write = args.includes('--write'), tail = args.includes('--tail');
  // (--only required: a file name shared by several games is never unflagged everywhere by mistake)
  if (!dir || !only.length || !paths.length) {
    console.error('usage: node tools/learn-unflag.mjs <learn dir> --only <manifest>... --path <game file>[#<blocks>]... [--tail] [--write]'); process.exit(2);
  }
  if (!write) console.log('dry run (--write to unflag)');
  for (const name of only) {
    const f = path.join(dir, `prefetch-${name.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, '_')}.json`);
    if (!fs.existsSync(f)) { console.log(`${name}: no learned order (${f})`); continue; }
    const r = unflagFile(f, paths, { write, tail });
    console.log(`${name.padEnd(30)} ${String(r.hit.size).padStart(5)} entries counted before playable, ${r.flagged} flagged of ${r.marks} marks (${(r.flaggedBytes / 1048576).toFixed(2)} MB) out of the launch set${tail ? `; ${r.moved.size} entries to the order's end` : ''}${r.written ? ' -> written' : ''}`);
  }
}
```

`tools/loop-bench.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Tight integer loop microbenchmark: a strlen byte loop (movzx / inc / test / jnz) over a 4 KB string, repeated;
// ns per inner iteration under the JIT. With `node --no-liftoff --print-wasm-code` it shows V8's code for the loop.
// Usage: node tools/loop-bench.mjs [repetitions]
import { GuestMemory } from '../src/cpu/memory.js';
import { CpuState, THREAD_STATES_BASE, EXIT, F } from '../src/cpu/state.js';
import { Interp } from '../src/cpu/interp.js';
import { Jit } from '../src/cpu/jit/jit.js';

const CODE = 0x20000000, DATA = 0x10000000, LEN = 4095;
const REPS = +(process.argv[2] ?? 4000);
// outer: xor ecx, ecx ; L: movzx edx, byte [esi+ecx] ; inc ecx ; test dl, dl ; jne L ; dec edi ; jne outer ; hlt
const code = Uint8Array.from([0x31, 0xc9, 0x0f, 0xb6, 0x14, 0x0e, 0x41, 0x84, 0xd2, 0x75, 0xf7, 0x4f, 0x75, 0xf2, 0xf4]);
let best = Infinity;
for (let rep = 0; rep < 5; rep++) {
  const mem = new GuestMemory();
  const cpu = new CpuState(mem, THREAD_STATES_BASE);
  cpu.reset();
  mem.writeBytes(CODE, code);
  mem.fill(DATA, LEN, 0x61); mem.write8(DATA + LEN, 0);
  cpu.eip = CODE; cpu.esp = DATA + 0x10000; cpu.esi = DATA; cpu.edi = REPS; cpu.eflags = F.RESERVED1 | F.IF;
  const jit = new Jit(mem, new Interp(mem, cpu), { smc: true }); jit.cpu = cpu;
  const end = CODE + code.length - 1;
  const t0 = performance.now();
  let r; do r = jit.run({ stopAt: end, maxInsns: 2e9 }); while (r === EXIT.TIMESLICE);
  best = Math.min(best, performance.now() - t0);
  if (r !== EXIT.HALT) throw new Error('exit ' + r);
}
console.log(`strlen loop: ${(best * 1e6 / (REPS * (LEN + 1))).toFixed(2)} ns per byte (4 instructions)`);
```

```mjs
// Checks the browser-side parts of the DirectShow path in headless Chromium against ffmpeg:
// - MPEG audio layer III (MP3) decoded through WebCodecs (src/media/mpeg-source.js AsyncAudio), compared with ffmpeg's
//   decoding;
// - the video layer's VideoFrame path (BrowserDisplay.presentVideoYuv): an I420 picture drawn on an OffscreenCanvas
//   compared with the RGBA conversion of src/media/yuv.js.
// Usage: tools/with-browser-slot.sh node tools/media-browser-check.mjs   (needs ffmpeg with libmp3lame)
import { chromium } from 'playwright';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';

const root = new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname;
const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'orthros-media-'));
const ff = (...a) => execFileSync('ffmpeg', ['-nostdin', '-loglevel', 'error', '-y', ...a]);
const cases = [['44100', '2', '128k'], ['22050', '1', '64k'], ['48000', '2', '320k']];
for (const [rate, ch, br] of cases) {
  ff('-f', 'lavfi', '-i', `anoisesrc=d=2:c=pink:r=${rate}:a=0.3`, '-ac', ch, '-ar', rate, '-c:a', 'libmp3lame', '-b:a', br, path.join(dir, `a${rate}.mp3`));
  ff('-c:a', 'mp3float', '-i', path.join(dir, `a${rate}.mp3`), '-f', 'f32le', path.join(dir, `a${rate}.f32`));
}
const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-unsafe-swiftshader', '--ignore-gpu-blocklist', '--use-angle=swiftshader'] });
let failed = 0;
try {
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  await page.route('http://localhost:9/**', (r) => {
    const u = new URL(r.request().url()).pathname;
    const file = u.startsWith('/m/') ? path.join(dir, u.slice(3)) : path.join(root, u);
    if (u === '/') return r.fulfill({ body: '<!doctype html><title>media</title>', contentType: 'text/html' });
    if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return r.fulfill({ status: 404 });
    r.fulfill({ body: fs.readFileSync(file), contentType: file.endsWith('.js') || file.endsWith('.mjs') ? 'text/javascript' : 'application/octet-stream' });
  });
  page.on('console', (m) => console.log('[page]', m.text()));
  await page.goto('http://localhost:9/'); // (localhost: a secure context, where WebCodecs exists)
  for (const [rate, ch] of cases) {
    const pcm = await page.evaluate(async (name) => {
      const { openMedia } = await import('/src/media/open.js');
      const data = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch(name)).arrayBuffer());
      const s = openMedia({ size: () => data.length, read: (o, n) => data.subarray(o, o + n) }, { log: (m) => console.log(m) });
      const chunks = []; let t = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < 2000 && !s.audioDone; i++) { t += 0.05; s.audioUntil(t, (smp, start) => chunks.push({ start, smp: smp.map((a) => Array.from(a)) })); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2)); }
      return { kind: s.kind, async: !!s.audioAsync, rate: s.audioRate, done: s.audioDone, chunks };
    }, `/m/a${rate}.mp3`);
    const refb = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, `a${rate}.f32`)), ref = new Float32Array(refb.buffer.slice(refb.byteOffset, refb.byteOffset + refb.length));
    const n = Number(ch);
    // (ffmpeg drops the encoder's delay and padding announced by the LAME header, and the header frame itself; the
    // browser's decoder — as Windows' MPEG layer-3 decoder — plays every frame: compared at the best offset)
    const all = Array.from({ length: n }, () => []);
    let contiguous = true, expect = 0;
    for (const c of pcm.chunks) { const at = Math.round(c.start * pcm.rate); if (at !== expect) contiguous = false; for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) all[k].push(...c.smp[k]); expect = at + c.smp[0].length; }
    const total = all[0].length;
    let best = -Infinity, lag = 0;
    for (let d = 0; d <= 4000; d++) {
      let se = 0, sp = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < ref.length / n; i += 7) for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) { const x = all[k][i + d]; if (x === undefined) continue; const y = ref[i * n + k]; se += (x - y) ** 2; sp += y * y; }
      const v = 10 * Math.log10(sp / se); if (v > best) { best = v; lag = d; }
    }
    const snr = best;
    const ok = pcm.async && pcm.done && contiguous && total >= ref.length / n && snr > 60;
    if (!ok) failed++;
    console.log(`${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'} mp3 ${rate} Hz ${ch} ch: WebCodecs ${pcm.async}, ${total} samples (ffmpeg ${ref.length / n}), contiguous ${contiguous}, SNR ${snr.toFixed(1)} dB at an offset of ${lag} samples`);
  }
  // the VideoFrame path's colors against the RGBA conversion
  const diff = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const { yuv420ToRgba } = await import('/src/media/yuv.js');
    const W = 64, H = 48, y = new Uint8Array(W * H), cb = new Uint8Array(W * H / 4), cr = new Uint8Array(W * H / 4);
    for (let j = 0; j < H; j++) for (let i = 0; i < W; i++) y[j * W + i] = 16 + ((i * 219) / (W - 1) | 0);
    for (let j = 0; j < H / 2; j++) for (let i = 0; i < W / 2; i++) { cb[j * W / 2 + i] = 16 + (j * 224 / (H / 2 - 1) | 0); cr[j * W / 2 + i] = 240 - (i * 224 / (W / 2 - 1) | 0); }
    const buf = new Uint8Array(W * H * 3 / 2); buf.set(y); buf.set(cb, W * H); buf.set(cr, W * H * 5 / 4);
    const vf = new VideoFrame(buf, { format: 'I420', codedWidth: W, codedHeight: H, timestamp: 0, colorSpace: { primaries: 'smpte170m', transfer: 'smpte170m', matrix: 'smpte170m', fullRange: false } });
    const c = new OffscreenCanvas(W, H), ctx = c.getContext('2d'); ctx.drawImage(vf, 0, 0); vf.close();
    const got = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, W, H).data, want = yuv420ToRgba({ y, cb, cr, stride: W, cstride: W / 2 }, 0, 0, W, H, new Uint8ClampedArray(W * H * 4));
    let max = 0, sum = 0; for (let i = 0; i < got.length; i++) { if ((i & 3) === 3) continue; const d = Math.abs(got[i] - want[i]); max = Math.max(max, d); sum += d; }
    return { max, mean: sum / (W * H * 3) };
  });
  const vok = diff.mean < 3; // (the canvas samples the chroma planes bilinearly where the RGBA conversion repeats them)
  if (!vok) failed++;
  console.log(`${vok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'} VideoFrame I420 colors vs yuv.js: mean difference ${diff.mean.toFixed(2)}, max ${diff.max}`);
} finally {
  await browser.close();
  fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
```

`tools/mem-check.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# The server's memory, for the project's heavy jobs (CLAUDE.md "Shared server budget": incident of 2026-10-30 — test
# browsers, an engine compile and other projects together filled the 62 GB and swap, the server froze and rebooted).
# Usage: tools/mem-check.sh            prints the available memory in GB (MemAvailable)
#        tools/mem-check.sh -w|--wait <GB>  waits (every 20 s, a line on stderr each minute) until at least <GB> GB are
#                                      available, then exits 0
#        tools/mem-check.sh -q|--quiet <GB> exits 0 if at least <GB> GB are available now, 1 otherwise (no wait)
set -u
avail() { awk '/^MemAvailable:/ { printf "%d", $2 / 1048576 }' /proc/meminfo; }
case "${1:-}" in
  -w|--wait)
    need=${2:?GB}; n=0
    while [ "$(avail)" -lt "$need" ]; do
      [ $((n % 3)) -eq 0 ] && echo "mem-check: $(avail) GB available, waiting for $need GB" >&2
      n=$((n + 1)); sleep 20
    done ;;
  -q|--quiet) [ "$(avail)" -ge "${2:?GB}" ] ;;
  *) avail; echo ;;
esac
```

`tools/memop-bench.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Memory-operand / stack microbenchmark: ns per iteration of small integer loops, each case differing from a
// reference loop by one kind of memory access (loads, MOVZX, stores and their SMC check, read-modify-write ALU ops,
// PUSH/POP runs, a call/return with a frame inside the region, LEA), so that the difference between a case and
// its reference is the cost of that access as the JIT emits it. With --nosmc the translations skip the SMC check
// on stores (unsafe; to measure what the check costs). Loops run 8 copies of the measured instruction group.
// WASM branch hints are turned on (as Chrome ships them; Node 24 keeps them behind a flag): the translations mark
// their cold paths (SMC exits, budget exits) unlikely, which decides V8's block layout; --no-hints leaves them off.
// Usage: node tools/memop-bench.mjs [iterations] [--runs 7] [--nosmc] [--no-hints] [--only <substring>]
import v8 from 'node:v8';
if (!process.argv.includes('--no-hints')) v8.setFlagsFromString('--experimental-wasm-branch-hinting');
const { GuestMemory } = await import('../src/cpu/memory.js'); // (after the flag: dynamic imports)
const { CpuState, THREAD_STATES_BASE, EXIT, F } = await import('../src/cpu/state.js');
const { Interp } = await import('../src/cpu/interp.js');
const { Jit } = await import('../src/cpu/jit/jit.js');

const CODE = 0x20000000, DATA = 0x10000000;
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const N = +(args.find((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && args[i - 1] !== '--runs' && args[i - 1] !== '--only') ?? 5e6);
const opt = (k, d) => { const i = args.indexOf(k); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : d; };
const RUNS = +opt('--runs', 7);
const ONLY = opt('--only', null);
const SMC = !args.includes('--nosmc');
const hex = (s) => s.replace(/\s+/g, '');
const rep = (s, n = 8) => hex(s).repeat(n);

// every case: L: <body> ; dec ecx ; jnz L ; hlt  (ecx = N, esi/edi -> data, esp -> a stack page, ebp = esp)
// 49 = dec ecx ; 0f85 rel32 = jnz (filled in), f4 = hlt
const CASES = [
  ['empty loop', ''],
  ['8x mov eax, [esi+4]', rep('8b4604')],
  ['8x mov eax, [esi+ebx*4+8]', rep('8b449e08')],
  ['8x movzx eax, byte [esi+5]', rep('0fb64605')],
  ['8x mov [edi+4], eax', rep('894704')],
  ['8x mov byte [edi+5], al', rep('884705')],
  ['8x mov [edi+4*k], eax', '894704 894708 89470c 894710 894714 894718 89471c 894720'.replace(/ /g, '')],
  ['8x (mov [edi+4],eax ; mov edx,[esi+0x100])', rep('894704 8b9600010000')],
  ['8x (mov [esp+8],eax ; mov edx,[esi+0x100])', rep('89442408 8b9600010000')],
  ['8x mov [ebp-8], eax', rep('8945f8')],
  ['8x mov [esp+8], eax', rep('89442408')],
  ['8x add [edi+8], eax', rep('014708')],
  ['8x movups [edi+16], xmm0', rep('0f114710')],
  ['8x fst dword [edi+4]', rep('d95704')],
  ['8x add eax, [esi+8]', rep('034608')],
  ['8x (cmp dword [esi+8], 0 ; jz +0)', rep('837e0800 7400')],
  ['8x (cmp eax, [esi+8] ; jne +0)', rep('3b4608 7500')],
  ['8x (test byte [esi+5], 1 ; jnz +0)', rep('f6460501 7500')],
  ['8x (movzx edx, byte [esi+5] ; test edx, edx ; jz +0)', rep('0fb65605 85d2 7400')],
  ['8x lea eax, [esi+ebx*4+8]', rep('8d449e08')],
  ['8x (push eax ; pop edx)', rep('50 5a')],
  ['8x (push 4 regs ; pop 4)', rep('50 53 56 57 5f 5e 5b 5a')],
  ['8x (push 3 ; add esp, 12)', rep('50 53 6a01 83c40c')],
  ['8x (push [esi+4] ; pop edx)', rep('ff7604 5a')],
];
// call/return within the region: body = 4x (push eax ; push ebx ; call F ; add esp, 8), F after the hlt:
// F: push ebp ; mov ebp, esp ; mov eax, [ebp+8] ; add eax, [ebp+12] ; pop ebp ; ret
const CALLF = { name: '4x call F(a,b) with frame', body: 4 };

function build(body, call) {
  const b = [];
  const bytes = (h) => { for (const x of h.match(/../g) ?? []) b.push(parseInt(x, 16)); };
  const calls = [];
  if (call) for (let k = 0; k < call.body; k++) { bytes('50 53'.replace(/ /g, '')); calls.push(b.length); bytes('e800000000'); bytes('83c408'); }
  else bytes(body);
  b.push(0x49, 0x0f, 0x85, 0, 0, 0, 0);
  const jEnd = b.length; const rel = -jEnd;
  b[jEnd - 4] = rel & 0xff; b[jEnd - 3] = (rel >> 8) & 0xff; b[jEnd - 2] = (rel >> 16) & 0xff; b[jEnd - 1] = (rel >>> 24) & 0xff;
  const end = b.length; b.push(0xf4);
  const f = b.length;
  bytes('55 8bec 8b4508 03450c 5d c3'.replace(/ /g, ''));
  for (const at of calls) { const r = f - (at + 5); for (let k = 0; k < 4; k++) b[at + 1 + k] = (r >> (8 * k)) & 0xff; }
  return { bytes: Uint8Array.from(b), end: CODE + end };
}

async function once(p) {
  const mem = new GuestMemory();
  const cpu = new CpuState(mem, THREAD_STATES_BASE);
  cpu.reset();
  mem.writeBytes(CODE, p.bytes);
  const reset = () => {
    cpu.eip = CODE; cpu.ecx = N; cpu.eax = 1; cpu.ebx = 2; cpu.edx = 0;
    cpu.esi = DATA; cpu.edi = DATA + 0x1000; cpu.esp = DATA + 0x10000; cpu.ebp = DATA + 0x10000;
    cpu.eflags = F.RESERVED1 | F.IF;
  };
  const jit = new Jit(mem, new Interp(mem, cpu), { smc: SMC, ...JSON.parse(process.env.ORTHROS_JIT_OPTS ?? '{}') }); jit.cpu = cpu; // (ORTHROS_JIT_OPTS: translation options, e.g. '{"maxBlocks":64}')
  let r;
  reset();
  do r = jit.run({ stopAt: p.end, maxInsns: 2e9 }); while (r === EXIT.TIMESLICE); // warm-up: translation, then
  await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 100)); // V8's background tier-up of the region to optimized code
  reset();
  const t0 = performance.now();
  do r = jit.run({ stopAt: p.end, maxInsns: 2e9 }); while (r === EXIT.TIMESLICE);
  const ms = performance.now() - t0;
  if (r !== EXIT.HALT) throw new Error('exit ' + r);
  if (cpu.ecx !== 0) throw new Error('did not run to the end');
  return (ms * 1e6) / N;
}

const all = [...CASES.map(([n, h]) => [n, build(h)]), [CALLF.name, build('', CALLF)]].filter(([n]) => !ONLY || n.includes(ONLY) || n === 'empty loop');
for (const [, p] of all) await once(p); // discarded round (the JS dispatcher and translator still being optimized)
let base = 0;
for (const [name, p] of all) {
  const t = [];
  for (let k = 0; k < RUNS; k++) t.push(await once(p));
  t.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const med = t[t.length >> 1];
  if (name === 'empty loop') base = med;
  console.log(`${name.padEnd(32)} ${med.toFixed(3)} ns/iter  (+${((med - base) / 8).toFixed(3)} per group; min ${t[0].toFixed(3)}, max ${t[t.length - 1].toFixed(3)})`);
}
```

`tools/mpa-window-fit.mjs`:

```mjs
// Recovers the synthesis window D[0..511] of MPEG audio layers I / II (ISO/IEC 11172-3 table B.3, a constant of the
// standard) from a reference decoding, and writes src/media/mpeg-audio-window.js.
//
// Each output sample j of a 32-sample block is sum_i D[j + 32 i] * U[j + 32 i] (16 terms), with U computed by the
// decoder of src/media/mpeg-audio.js before windowing: given a stream and its reference decoding (32-bit float PCM),
// D is the least-squares solution of 32 independent 16-unknown systems. The table of the standard is in units of 2^-16;
// the tool checks that every fitted value is within 1e-4 of such a multiple (else something else in the decoder is
// wrong) and that the second half mirrors the first.
//
// Usage: node tools/mpa-window-fit.mjs <stream.mp2> <reference.f32le> [--write]
//   e.g. ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anoisesrc=d=6:c=pink:r=48000 -ac 2 -c:a mp2 -b:a 384k n.mp2
//        ffmpeg -c:a mp2float -i n.mp2 -f f32le n.f32
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { MpegAudioDecoder } from '../src/media/mpeg-audio.js';

const [file, refFile] = process.argv.slice(2).filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
const data = readFileSync(file), ref = new Float32Array(readFileSync(refFile).buffer.slice(0));
const ata = Array.from({ length: 32 }, () => new Float64Array(256)), atb = Array.from({ length: 32 }, () => new Float64Array(16));
const u = new Float64Array(16);
const dec = new MpegAudioDecoder();
let block = 0, nch = 2, rows = 0;
dec.emit = function (ch, out, o) {
  this.synth[ch].run(this.sb[ch], this.pcm, 0, new Float64Array(512));
  const t = block + o / 32;
  for (let j = 0; j < 32; j++) {
    const y = ref[(t * 32 + j) * nch + ch];
    if (y === undefined) return;
    this.synth[ch].inputs(j, u);
    const A = ata[j], B = atb[j];
    for (let a = 0; a < 16; a++) { B[a] += u[a] * y; for (let b = 0; b < 16; b++) A[a * 16 + b] += u[a] * u[b]; }
    rows++;
  }
};
for (let i = 0; i + 4 < data.length;) {
  const f = dec.decodeFrame(data, i);
  if (!f) { i++; continue; }
  nch = f.channels; block += f.samples[0].length / 32; i += dec.header.bytes;
}
function solve(A, b, n) { // Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting
  const M = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, r) => [...A.subarray(r * n, r * n + n), b[r]]);
  for (let c = 0; c < n; c++) {
    let p = c; for (let r = c + 1; r < n; r++) if (Math.abs(M[r][c]) > Math.abs(M[p][c])) p = r;
    [M[c], M[p]] = [M[p], M[c]];
    for (let r = 0; r < n; r++) if (r !== c) { const k = M[r][c] / M[c][c]; for (let k2 = c; k2 <= n; k2++) M[r][k2] -= k * M[c][k2]; }
  }
  return M.map((row, r) => row[n] / row[r]);
}
// (the matrixing makes V[16 + 64 m] zero: the window values applied to those inputs never matter — left out of the fit,
// and taken from their mirror)
const D = new Float64Array(512), free = new Uint8Array(512);
for (let j = 0; j < 32; j++) {
  const A = ata[j], keep = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) if (A[i * 16 + i] > 1e-9 * rows) keep.push(i); else free[j + 32 * i] = 1;
  const n = keep.length, As = new Float64Array(n * n), bs = new Float64Array(n);
  keep.forEach((a, r) => { bs[r] = atb[j][a]; keep.forEach((b, c) => { As[r * n + c] = A[a * 16 + b]; }); });
  const x = solve(As, bs, n);
  keep.forEach((i, r) => { D[j + 32 * i] = x[r]; });
}
const mirror = (i) => (i % 64 === 0 ? 1 : -1);
for (let i = 1; i < 512; i++) if (free[i] && !free[512 - i]) D[i] = mirror(i) * D[512 - i];
console.log(`window values never used by the matrixing: ${[...free.keys()].filter((i) => free[i]).join(' ')}`);
let worst = 0, asym = 0;
const ints = Array.from(D, (v) => Math.round(v * 65536));
for (let i = 0; i < 512; i++) if (!free[i]) worst = Math.max(worst, Math.abs(D[i] * 65536 - ints[i]));
for (let i = 1; i < 256; i++) if (!free[i] && !free[512 - i]) asym = Math.max(asym, Math.abs(ints[512 - i] - mirror(i) * ints[i]));
if (process.argv.includes("--dump")) for (const i of [1,2,31,32,33,63,64,65,96,127,128,129,160,192,224,255,256]) console.log(i, ints[i], ints[512 - i]);
console.log(`${rows} equations; largest distance to a multiple of 2^-16: ${worst.toFixed(6)} units; asymmetry ${asym}; D[256] = ${ints[256]} / 65536`);
if (worst > 1e-4 * 65536 || asym) { console.log('not a clean fit: the table is not written'); process.exit(1); }
if (process.argv.includes('--write')) {
  const half = ints.slice(0, 257), lines = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < half.length; i += 16) lines.push('  ' + half.slice(i, i + 16).join(', ') + ',');
  writeFileSync(new URL('../src/media/mpeg-audio-window.js', import.meta.url), `// The polyphase synthesis window of MPEG audio layers I and II (ISO/IEC 11172-3 table B.3), D[0..256] in units of
// 2^-16 (the other half follows by symmetry, see mpeg-audio.js). Produced by tools/mpa-window-fit.mjs.
export const SYNTH_WINDOW_HALF = new Int32Array([
${lines.join('\n')}
]);
`);
  console.log('src/media/mpeg-audio-window.js written');
}
```
