+#ifndef OPENMW_MWLUA_MAINTHREAD_H
+#define OPENMW_MWLUA_MAINTHREAD_H
+
+// Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUATHREAD): Lua bindings' calls that must run on the page's thread on the web.
+//
+// LuaManager::update() may run on the Lua thread (mwlua/worker.cpp), in parallel with the frame's cull and draw. On the
+// desktop a few bindings call engine subsystems directly from there (OpenAL Soft being thread safe); on the web some of
+// them live in the page's JavaScript (the OpenAL library, its EM_JS extensions, the engine's EM_ASM hooks), which a Web
+// Worker does not have, and a few others mutate state the frame's cull reads (MyGUI's message boxes and cursor, the
+// post-processor's technique list). Those calls go through a queue of their own — not Emscripten's system proxy
+// queue, which the page's thread serves wherever it waits on a lock (mid-cull included, and inside a proxied task that
+// does not serve it again) — that the page's thread runs only in Worker::finishUpdate, after the frame's drawing, in
+// call order: exactly where the inline update() ran them.
+//   mainThreadPost(f): f queued, the Lua thread goes on (calls whose result Lua does not read: play, stop, show).
+//   onMainThread(f):   f queued and waited for (its result returned, its exception thrown again on the Lua thread);
+//                      being behind the calls posted before it, it sees their effects as inline.
+// On the page's thread itself (the switch at 0, synchronizedUpdate, the menu) and off the web: f called directly.
+
+#include <chrono>
+#include <condition_variable>
+#include <deque>
+#include <exception>
+#include <functional>
+#include <mutex>
+#include <optional>
+#include <type_traits>
+#include <utility>
+
+#include <components/debug/debuglog.hpp>
+
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+#include <emscripten/threading.h>
+#endif
+
+namespace MWLua
+{
+    class MainThreadCalls
+    {
+    public:
+        static MainThreadCalls& get()
+        {
+            static MainThreadCalls sCalls;
+            return sCalls;
+        }
+
+        // True on a thread that must queue its calls (the Lua thread, on the web).
+        static bool mustQueue()
+        {
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+            return !emscripten_is_main_runtime_thread();
+#else
+            return false;
+#endif
+        }
+
+        void post(std::function<void()> call)
+        {
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mMutex);
+                mCalls.push_back(std::move(call));
+            }
+            mCV.notify_all();
+        }
+
+        // The Lua thread: `call` run on the page's thread, waited for.
+        void runAndWait(const std::function<void()>& call)
+        {
+            bool done = false;
+            post([&] {
+                runOne(call);
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mMutex);
+                done = true;
+            });
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk(mMutex);
+            mCV.wait(lk, [&] { return done; });
+        }
+
+        // The page's thread: runs the queued calls, in order, until finished() is true with none pending (whoever
+        // makes it true calls wake() after). A posted call's exception is logged: it has nobody to be thrown to.
+        // onIdle() is called after each `slice` spent waiting with nothing to do.
+        template <class Finished, class OnIdle, class Rep, class Period>
+        void serveUntil(Finished&& finished, OnIdle&& onIdle, std::chrono::duration<Rep, Period> slice)
+        {
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk(mMutex);
+            while (true)
+            {
+                if (!mCalls.empty())
+                {
+                    std::function<void()> call = std::move(mCalls.front());
+                    mCalls.pop_front();
+                    lk.unlock();
+                    runOne(call);
+                    mCV.notify_all(); // a runAndWait's done set
+                    lk.lock();
+                    continue;
+                }
+                if (finished())
+                    return;
+                if (mCV.wait_for(lk, slice) == std::cv_status::timeout && mCalls.empty() && !finished())
+                {
+                    lk.unlock();
+                    onIdle();
+                    lk.lock();
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        // The page's thread: runs whatever is queued now.
+        void drain()
+        {
+            serveUntil([] { return true; }, [] {}, std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
+        }
+
+        // After serveUntil's condition became true.
+        void wake()
+        {
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(mMutex);
+            }
+            mCV.notify_all();
+        }
+
+    private:
+        static void runOne(const std::function<void()>& call)
+        {
+            try
+            {
+                call();
+            }
+            catch (const std::exception& e)
+            {
+                Log(Debug::Error) << "Lua: a call queued for the page's thread failed: " << e.what();
+            }
+            catch (...)
+            {
+                Log(Debug::Error) << "Lua: a call queued for the page's thread failed (non-C++ exception)";
+            }
+        }
+
+        std::mutex mMutex;
+        std::condition_variable mCV;
+        std::deque<std::function<void()>> mCalls;
+    };
+
+    // f run on the page's thread after the frame's drawing (see above), the caller going on: f must own what it uses.
+    template <class F>
+    void mainThreadPost(F&& f)
+    {
+        if (!MainThreadCalls::mustQueue())
+        {
+            f();
+            return;
+        }
+        MainThreadCalls::get().post(std::function<void()>(std::forward<F>(f)));
+    }
+
+    // f run on the page's thread and waited for: its result returned, its exception thrown again here.
+    template <class F>
+    auto onMainThread(F&& f) -> std::decay_t<std::invoke_result_t<F&>>
+    {
+        using Result = std::decay_t<std::invoke_result_t<F&>>;
+        if (!MainThreadCalls::mustQueue())
+            return static_cast<Result>(f());
+        std::exception_ptr error;
+        std::conditional_t<std::is_void_v<Result>, bool, std::optional<Result>> result{};
+        MainThreadCalls::get().runAndWait([&] {
+            try
+            {
+                if constexpr (std::is_void_v<Result>)
+                    f();
+                else
+                    result.emplace(f());
+            }
+            catch (...)
+            {
+                error = std::current_exception();
+            }
+        });
+        if (error)
+            std::rethrow_exception(error);
+        if constexpr (!std::is_void_v<Result>)
+            return std::move(*result);
+    }
+}
+
+#endif // OPENMW_MWLUA_MAINTHREAD_H

+        // The Lua thread's calls for the page's thread run here, in order, until its update() ended. Never a silent
+        // endless wait: past 10 s (a Lua update reading much over a slow link may take that long), a log line every
+        // 10 s says what the page waits for.

         constexpr uint64_t maxDepth = 250;
 
+        // Orthros (orthros-luauidiff.patch): LuaUtil::getFieldOrNil(table, field) — the same object — without the
+        // registry references of the table's copy and its lua_table view, when the table has no metatable
+        // (lua_rawget, what safeGet's raw_get does then); a table with a metatable takes getFieldOrNil itself.
+        // Only called when OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUAUIDIFF is on (properties.hpp); its callers keep the original statements
+        // for "0".
+        template <typename Ref>
+        sol::object orthrosFieldOrNil(const Ref& table, std::string_view field)
+        {
+            const int ref = table.registry_index();
+            if (ref == LUA_REFNIL || ref == LUA_NOREF)
+                return sol::nil;
+            lua_State* L = table.lua_state();
+            const int top = lua_gettop(L);
+            table.push();
+            if (lua_type(L, -1) != LUA_TTABLE)
+            {
+                lua_settop(L, top);
+                return sol::nil;
+            }
+            if (lua_getmetatable(L, -1))
+            {
+                lua_settop(L, top);
+                return LuaUtil::getFieldOrNil(table, field);
+            }
+            lua_pushlstring(L, field.data(), field.size());
+            lua_rawget(L, -2);
+            sol::object value(L, -1);
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            return value;

+    // Orthros (orthros-luauidiff.patch): OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUAUIDIFF, read once (util.cpp; absent or anything but "0":

+    bool orthrosLuaUiDiff();

+    // Orthros (orthros-luauidiff.patch): parseValue<T>(sol::object(table), field, errorPrefix) — the same result and
+    // the same errors — without its registry references (the table's copy, its lua_table view, the field's object:
+    // a luaL_ref and a luaL_unref each, per read). parseValue reads through LuaUtil::getFieldOrNil: nil unless
+    // `table` is a Lua table; when the table's metatable has a callable __index, that call; else the raw field. Here a
+    // table with no metatable is read with lua_rawget; a table with a metatable, or a value of the wrong type (the
+    // error and its message), takes parseValue itself. The value is checked and read with the sol::stack::check /
+    // sol::stack::get that sol::object::is / as use.
+    template <typename T, typename Ref>
+    sol::optional<T> orthrosParseValue(const Ref& table, std::string_view field, std::string_view errorPrefix)
+    {
+        using LuaT = std::conditional_t<isMyGuiVector<T>(), osg::Vec2f,
+            std::conditional_t<isMyGuiColor<T>(), Misc::Color, T>>;
+        const int ref = table.registry_index();
+        if (ref == LUA_REFNIL || ref == LUA_NOREF)
+            return sol::nullopt; // (nil: not a table, getFieldOrNil's nil)
+        lua_State* L = table.lua_state();
+        const int top = lua_gettop(L);
+        table.push();
+        if (lua_type(L, -1) != LUA_TTABLE)
+        {
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            return sol::nullopt;
+        }
+        if (lua_getmetatable(L, -1))
+        {
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            return parseValue<T>(sol::object(table), field, errorPrefix);
+        }
+        lua_pushlstring(L, field.data(), field.size());
+        lua_rawget(L, -2);
+        if (lua_type(L, -1) == LUA_TNIL)
+        {
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            return sol::nullopt;
+        }
+        if (!sol::stack::check<LuaT>(L, -1, &sol::no_panic))
+        {
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            return parseValue<T>(sol::object(table), field, errorPrefix); // (throws its error)
+        }
+        struct Restore
+        {
+            lua_State* L;
+            int top;
+            ~Restore() { lua_settop(L, top); }
+        } restore{ L, top };
+        LuaT luaT = sol::stack::get<LuaT>(L, -1);
+        if constexpr (isMyGuiIntVector<T>())
+            return T(static_cast<int>(luaT.x()), static_cast<int>(luaT.y()));
+        else if constexpr (isMyGuiVector<T>())
+            return T(luaT.x(), luaT.y());
+        else if constexpr (isMyGuiColor<T>())
+            return T(luaT.r(), luaT.g(), luaT.b(), luaT.a());
+        else
+            return luaT;
+    }
+
+    // Orthros (orthros-luauidiff.patch): parseProperty through orthrosParseValue — the props read first, then the
+    // template's (whose errors are thrown even when the props hold the field), as parseProperty does.
+    template <typename T>
+    T orthrosParseProperty(const sol::main_object& props, const sol::main_object& templateProps,
+        std::string_view field, const T& defaultValue)
+    {
+        auto propOptional = orthrosParseValue<T>(props, field, "Property");
+        auto templateOptional = orthrosParseValue<T>(templateProps, field, "Template property");
+
+        if (propOptional.has_value())
+            return propOptional.value();
+        else if (templateOptional.has_value())
+            return templateOptional.value();
+        else
+            return defaultValue;
+    }
+

+    template <typename T>
+    T orthrosParseExternal(const sol::main_object& external, std::string_view field, const T& defaultValue)
+    {
+        auto optional = orthrosParseValue<T>(external, field, "External value");
+
+        return optional.value_or(defaultValue);
+    }

+    bool PostProcessor::orthrosGammaUnchanged(Fx::Technique& technique, float gamma)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosGammaEnabled() || !isEnabled())
+            return false;
+        Fx::Types::UniformBase* uniform = orthrosGammaUniform(technique);
+        if (uniform == nullptr)
+            return false;
+        // (weak: a uniform freed since, and another allocated at its address, never matches)
+        const std::shared_ptr<Fx::Types::UniformBase> last = mOrthrosGammaUniform.lock();
+        if (last.get() != uniform || !(mOrthrosGamma == gamma)
+            || mOrthrosGammaWrites
+                != Settings::ShaderManager::get().orthrosWatch(uniform->mTechniqueName, uniform->mName))
+            return false;
+        const auto& value = std::get<Fx::Types::Uniform<float>>(uniform->mData).mValue;
+        return value.has_value() && *value == gamma;
+    }

+    {

+        if (uniform != nullptr)

+    void PostProcessor::orthrosGammaWritten(
+        Fx::Technique& technique, float gamma, Fx::Types::UniformBase* watched, unsigned long long before)
+    {
+        mOrthrosGammaUniform.reset();
+        if (watched == nullptr || orthrosGammaUniform(technique) != watched)
+            return;

+        // processing off, the settings not loaded — is made again next frame, as before)
+        const unsigned long long after
+            = Settings::ShaderManager::get().orthrosWatch(watched->mTechniqueName, watched->mName);
+        if (after != before + 1)
+            return;
+        for (const auto& candidate : technique.getUniformMap())
+        {
+            if (candidate.get() == watched)
+            {
+                mOrthrosGammaUniform = candidate;
+                break;
+            }
+        }
+        mOrthrosGamma = gamma;
+        mOrthrosGammaWrites = after;

+// Orthros (unattributed.patch): the clock's glue (Emscripten 6.0.1: src/lib/libcore.js emscripten_get_now,
+// src/lib/libwasi.js clock_time_get) in this MEMORY64 + pthreads + ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH build, on every thread.
+// OpenMW reads the clock a few hundred times a frame (osg::Timer::tick: every ScopedProfile, the viewer, the cull/draw
+// stats; std::chrono::steady_clock::now: the terrain preload's time slices, the Lua scripts' real-time clock, mods
+// calling it from every onFrame). Profiled on r13 (Vanilla+ FR, Seyda Neen, tools/openmw/perf.mjs --profile): the
+// clock's JS 0.26 ms a frame, of which emscripten_get_now's own time 0.17 and performance.now() 0.03.
+// Linked after the system libraries (--js-library, link-openmw.sh): its entries replace theirs of the same name, whose
+// __sig, __i53abi, __proxy and __nothrow stay (deps are only added to).
+//
+// Switch: OPENMW_ORTHROS_CLOCK, read once per thread, at its first call once it can be read (a call before that takes
+// the library's path and decides nothing). "0": the library's own bodies, kept below as orthrosClockOrig_<name>;
+// absent or anything else: the paths below. On the page's thread: ENV, once the runtime is initialized (the page fills
+// ENV in preRun, before initRuntime). On a pthread (the OSG pager, the preload and async threads, the whole engine
+// under OMW_PROXY), whose JS ENV is empty: the C environment (getenv), in the shared memory, built from the page's ENV
+// by the constructors on the page's thread before any pthread exists, read once the thread runs (its stack set up):
+// every thread follows the switch, so "0" is the previous code path everywhere.
+//
+// - emscripten_get_now (pthreads): performance.timeOrigin + performance.now(). timeOrigin is a getter into the
+//   browser (a Performance attribute, not a fast API call) and the time origin of a global never changes (High
+//   Resolution Time: it is fixed when the global is created), so it is read once and kept: the same double added to
+//   the same performance.now(), the same result. Headless Chromium, 2,000,000 calls: 430 → 236 ns a call.
+// - clock_time_get: wrote its nanoseconds through (growMemViews(), HEAP64)[ptime / 8] = BigInt(nsec): the shared
+//   memory's buffer getter and a BigInt allocated every call. Now the two 32-bit halves of the same integer, through
+//   a view of the heap kept by this glue (a view of a SharedArrayBuffer stays valid when the memory grows: growth gives
+//   a longer buffer, never a detached one; the current one is taken when a write reaches past its end). nsec is an
+//   integer-valued double in [0, 2^64) there (Math.round of a positive time): hi = floor(nsec / 2^32) and
+//   lo = nsec - hi * 2^32 are exact (a power of two scales exactly; the difference is a multiple of nsec's ulp below
+//   2^32, so representable), the same eight bytes BigInt64Array would store, modulo 2^64 as it stores them (checked on
+//   2.2 million values, the edges included). A pointer not 8-aligned (the library wrote nothing there), an unknown
+//   clock or a monotonic clock missing take the library's own body; a NaN or negative time its write (BigInt). The
+//   same calls through a test program linked with and without this file, its clocks made deterministic, print the same
+//   values (clock_gettime of each clock, std::chrono::steady_clock, emscripten_get_now). Headless Chromium: 522 → 273
+//   ns a call.
+
+(() => {
+  // The library's own bodies, kept under $orthrosClockOrig_<name> (no __sig: they take the arguments already
+  // converted); the replaced entries' deps gain their kept body and the switch. (libwasi.js keeps its functions as
+  // their source text, wrapSyscallFunction's: a string the jsifier emits as a function.)
+  const lib = LibraryManager.library;
+  const kept = {};
+  for (const name of ['emscripten_get_now', 'clock_time_get']) {
+    const body = lib[name];
+    if (typeof body != 'function' && !(typeof body == 'string' && /^\s*(\([^)]*\)\s*=>|function\b)/.test(body))) {
+      throw new Error(`orthros-clock.js: no library function ${name}`);
+    }
+    kept['$orthrosClockOrig_' + name] = lib[name];
+    kept['$orthrosClockOrig_' + name + '__deps'] = lib[name + '__deps'] || [];
+    kept[name + '__deps'] = (lib[name + '__deps'] || []).concat(['$orthrosClockOrig_' + name, '$orthrosClockOrigin']);
+  }
+  addToLibrary(kept);
+})();
+
+addToLibrary({
+  // undefined until chosen (the first call once the runtime is initialized); then the page's time origin, kept (on),
+  // or null ("0").
+  $orthrosClockOrigin: undefined,
+  $orthrosClockOrigin__deps: ['$ENV',
+#if PTHREADS
+    'getenv', 'pthread_self', '$stackSave', '$stackRestore', '$stringToUTF8OnStack', '$UTF8ToString',
+#endif
+  ],
+  $orthrosClockOrigin__postset: `
+    // the glue's view of the heap for clock_time_get (see the header); an empty one until the first write
+    var orthrosClockHeapU32 = new Uint32Array(0);
+    var orthrosClockChoose = () => {
+      if (!runtimeInitialized) return orthrosClockOrigin;
+      var off;
+#if PTHREADS
+      if (ENVIRONMENT_IS_PTHREAD) {
+        // (before the worker runs a thread — no thread pointer, no stack of its own — nothing is decided)
+        if (!_pthread_self()) return orthrosClockOrigin;
+        var sp = stackSave();
+        try {
+          var name = stringToUTF8OnStack('OPENMW_ORTHROS_CLOCK');
+#if MEMORY64
+          // (the toolchain gives no signature conversion to a native export only a JS library depends on: the
+          // pointers cross as BigInt; Number/BigInt also accept an already converted value)
+          var value = Number(_getenv(BigInt(name)));
+#else
+          var value = _getenv(name);
+#endif
+          off = !!value && UTF8ToString(value) === '0';
+        } finally {
+          stackRestore(sp);
+        }
+      } else
+#endif
+      off = ENV['OPENMW_ORTHROS_CLOCK'] === '0';
+      orthrosClockOrigin = off ? null : performance.timeOrigin;
+      return orthrosClockOrigin;
+    };
+  `,
+
+  emscripten_get_now: () => {
+    var origin = orthrosClockOrigin;
+    if (origin === undefined) origin = orthrosClockChoose();
+    if (origin == null) return orthrosClockOrig_emscripten_get_now();
+    return origin + performance.now();
+  },
+
+  // (i53abi: ignored_precision and ptime arrive as Numbers)
+  clock_time_get: (clk_id, ignored_precision, ptime) => {
+    var origin = orthrosClockOrigin;
+    if (origin === undefined) origin = orthrosClockChoose();
+    if (origin == null || ptime % 8 !== 0) return orthrosClockOrig_clock_time_get(clk_id, ignored_precision, ptime);
+    var now;
+    // the library's order and results: EINVAL for an unknown clock, Date.now() for the realtime one, the monotonic
+    // clock for the others (nowIsMonotonic: always with performance.now())
+    if (!checkWasiClock(clk_id)) return orthrosClockOrig_clock_time_get(clk_id, ignored_precision, ptime);
+    if (clk_id === 0 /* __WASI_CLOCKID_REALTIME */) now = _emscripten_date_now();
+    else if (nowIsMonotonic) now = _emscripten_get_now();
+    else return orthrosClockOrig_clock_time_get(clk_id, ignored_precision, ptime);
+    var nsec = Math.round(now * 1000 * 1000);
+    if (!(nsec >= 0 && nsec < 18446744073709551616)) {
+      // (the library's write of the same value: BigInt's RangeError for a NaN as before)
+      HEAP64[ptime / 8] = BigInt(nsec);
+      return 0;
+    }
+    var i = ptime / 4, heap = orthrosClockHeapU32;
+    // (the toolchain reads every HEAPxx of library code as (growMemViews(), HEAPxx): the current view)
+    if (i + 2 > heap.length) heap = orthrosClockHeapU32 = HEAPU32;
+    var hi = Math.floor(nsec / 4294967296);
+    heap[i] = nsec - hi * 4294967296;
+    heap[i + 1] = hi;
+    return 0;
+  },
+});

+// Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_STATEGRAPHS; absent or anything but "0": on, read once): the cull's StateGraph tree keeps a
+// graph left without leaves for fewer than sOrthrosStateGraphKeep prunes in a row instead of erasing it at the first.
+// OSG's prune() at the end of every cull erases each graph whose subtree drew nothing, so a StateSet seen every other
+// cull -- r11's light list StateSets alternate between two a list, one an update's parity -- or an object culled for a
+// frame had its graph deleted and made again: a map erase, a destructor, an allocation and a map insert each time
+// (~0.1 ms a frame in Vanilla+). The draw never walks the tree (RenderBin's StateGraph lists hold the graphs given
+// leaves this cull, in the order the cull gave them, as before), and a kept graph reached again by find_or_insert takes
+// a new one's state (orthrosRevive), so the same leaves are drawn with the same states in the same order. A kept graph
+// holds its StateSet (ref_ptr) until it is erased: at most sOrthrosStateGraphKeep prunes of the same tree later -- the
+// tree of one camera (a render-to-texture camera's is pruned only when that camera is culled), not frames. A graph
+// whose StateSet nothing else references any more (its node unloaded) is erased at once: find_or_insert can never be
+// given that StateSet again, so keeping it would only hold the StateSet and its textures. "0": OSG's prune.
+static const unsigned int sOrthrosStateGraphKeep = 3;
+
+static bool orthrosReadStateGraphsSwitch()
+{
+    const char* value = getenv("OPENMW_ORTHROS_STATEGRAPHS");
+    const bool enabled = !(value && strcmp(value, "0") == 0);
+    if (enabled)
+    {
+        OSG_NOTICE << "Orthros: StateGraphs kept through " << sOrthrosStateGraphKeep << " prunes without leaves: on" << std::endl;
+    }
+    else
+    {
+        OSG_NOTICE << "Orthros: StateGraphs kept through prunes without leaves: off (OPENMW_ORTHROS_STATEGRAPHS=0)" << std::endl;
+    }
+    return enabled;
+}
+
+static bool orthrosStateGraphsEnabled()
+{
+    static const bool enabled = orthrosReadStateGraphsSwitch();
+    return enabled;
+}
+
+bool StateGraph::orthrosPrune(unsigned int keep)
+{
+    bool live = !_leaves.empty();
+    ChildList::iterator citr=_children.begin();
+    while(citr!=_children.end())
+    {
+        StateGraph* child = citr->second.get();
+        if (child->orthrosPrune(keep))
+        {
+            child->_orthrosIdlePrunes = 0;
+            live = true;
+            ++citr;
+        }
+        else if (++child->_orthrosIdlePrunes >= keep
+                 || (child->_stateset.valid() && child->_stateset->referenceCount() == 1))
+        {
+            ChildList::iterator ditr= citr++;
+            _children.erase(ditr);
+        }
+        else ++citr;
+    }
+    return live;
+}

+// Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE): every live Program, so that the ones not linked yet can be compiled before a
+// frame draws with them (osg::orthrosCompileUnlinkedPrograms, called by the engine while its loading screen is up and
+// at the first frame after it). Without it the first draw that applies a program compiles and links it, reading the
+// statuses synchronously: in a browser each status read waits for the GPU process to finish that compile and link
+// (100-380 ms for the big ones on SwiftShader), in the world's first frames.
+// A Program registers itself in its constructors and leaves first thing in its destructor, under the registry's
+// mutex. ~Program may run on another thread than the GL one (a postprocessing Shader userdata collected by Lua's GC on
+// the Lua thread, r14), so the compile pass holds the mutex while it uses a program: a Program being destroyed
+// elsewhere waits until the pass is done with it, and the pass passes over a program whose last reference is already
+// gone (referenceCount 0: its destructor is running or about to). The mutex is recursive and the pass walks a copy of
+// the list, checking each entry is still registered, so a Program made or destroyed on the GL thread inside a compile
+// can neither deadlock nor invalidate the walk. Order: by registration (a serial), the same from run to run.
+namespace
+{
+    bool orthrosReadPrecompileSwitch()
+    {
+        const char* value = getenv("OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE");
+        if (value && value[0] == '0' && value[1] == 0)
+        {
+            OSG_NOTICE << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE=0: a program is compiled at the first draw that applies it" << std::endl;
+            return false;
+        }
+        // (OPENMW_WORKQUEUE_THREADED: worker threads build programs while the pass would read them; off, as before)
+        if (getenv("OPENMW_WORKQUEUE_THREADED") != nullptr)
+        {
+            OSG_NOTICE << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE off with OPENMW_WORKQUEUE_THREADED" << std::endl;
+            return false;
+        }
+        return true;
+    }
+
+    struct OrthrosProgramRegistry
+    {
+        std::recursive_mutex mutex;
+        unsigned long long nextSerial = 1;
+        std::unordered_map<const Program*, unsigned long long> serials;
+        std::map<unsigned long long, const Program*> bySerial;
+        // (GL thread only, under the mutex) compiled by a pass and not applied by a draw since
+        std::unordered_set<const Program*> precompiledUnapplied;
+        // (its size, read by Program::apply without the lock)
+        std::atomic<size_t> unappliedSize{ 0 };
+        // the serial given last when the latest Finish pass ran (0: none yet)
+        unsigned long long finishSerial = 0;
+        // counters (published to the page)
+        unsigned int compiled = 0, finishCompiled = 0, passes = 0, offThread = 0;
+        double ms = 0.0, finishMs = 0.0;
+        int left = 0, withDefines = 0, skippedDying = 0;
+        unsigned int lateBefore = 0, lateOld = 0, lateNew = 0, appliedAfter = 0;
+        std::thread::id glThread;
+        bool glThreadKnown = false;
+    };
+
+    OrthrosProgramRegistry& orthrosProgramRegistry()
+    {
+        // (never destroyed: Programs may outlive static destruction order)
+        static OrthrosProgramRegistry* registry = new OrthrosProgramRegistry;
+        return *registry;
+    }
+
+    void orthrosNoteThread(OrthrosProgramRegistry& r)
+    {
+        // (a counter only: a Program made or destroyed off the GL thread, e.g. by Lua's GC; safe, see above)
+        if (r.glThreadKnown && std::this_thread::get_id() != r.glThread) ++r.offThread;
+    }
+
+    void orthrosRegisterProgram(const Program* program)
+    {
+        if (!osg::orthrosPrecompileEnabled()) return;
+        OrthrosProgramRegistry& r = orthrosProgramRegistry();
+        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(r.mutex);
+        orthrosNoteThread(r);
+        const unsigned long long serial = r.nextSerial++;
+        r.serials[program] = serial;
+        r.bySerial[serial] = program;
+    }
+
+    void orthrosUnregisterProgram(const Program* program)
+    {
+        if (!osg::orthrosPrecompileEnabled()) return;
+        OrthrosProgramRegistry& r = orthrosProgramRegistry();
+        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(r.mutex);
+        orthrosNoteThread(r);
+        auto it = r.serials.find(program);
+        if (it != r.serials.end())
+        {
+            r.bySerial.erase(it->second);
+            r.serials.erase(it);
+        }
+        r.precompiledUnapplied.erase(program);
+        r.unappliedSize.store(r.precompiledUnapplied.size(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+
+    void orthrosPublish(OrthrosProgramRegistry& r)
+    {
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+        // (the counters, for the page's measurements; posted to the page's thread, which is this one in the build
+        // without OMW_PROXY and the page's otherwise; no comma inside the code: EM_ASM is a macro)
+        // clang-format off
+        MAIN_THREAD_ASYNC_EM_ASM({
+            var p = globalThis.__omwPrecompile || (globalThis.__omwPrecompile = {});
+            p.compiled = $0; p.ms = $1; p.finishCompiled = $2; p.finishMs = $3; p.left = $4; p.withDefines = $5;
+            p.passes = $6; p.registered = $7; p.unapplied = $8; p.lateBefore = $9; p.lateOld = $10; p.lateNew = $11;
+            p.skippedDying = $12; p.offThread = $13; p.appliedAfter = $14;
+        }, r.compiled, r.ms, r.finishCompiled, r.finishMs, r.left, r.withDefines, r.passes, (int)r.serials.size(),
+            (int)r.precompiledUnapplied.size(), r.lateBefore, r.lateOld, r.lateNew, r.skippedDying, r.offThread,
+            r.appliedAfter);
+        // clang-format on
+#else
+        (void)r;
+#endif
+    }
+
+    // Program::apply: the program drawn compiled by a pass (counted once), or compiled at this draw after all (late:
+    // before any Finish pass, or registered before the latest one — a define variant, a relink, a program the pass
+    // passed over — or registered since).
+    inline void orthrosNoteApply(const Program* program, bool late)
+    {
+        if (!osg::orthrosPrecompileEnabled()) return;
+        OrthrosProgramRegistry& r = orthrosProgramRegistry();
+        // (the usual case, a draw of a linked program once every precompiled one has been drawn: one atomic read)
+        if (!late && r.unappliedSize.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == 0) return;
+        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(r.mutex);
+        const bool wasUnapplied = r.precompiledUnapplied.erase(program) != 0;
+        r.unappliedSize.store(r.precompiledUnapplied.size(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        if (!late)
+        {
+            if (wasUnapplied) { ++r.appliedAfter; orthrosPublish(r); }
+            return;
+        }
+        auto it = r.serials.find(program);
+        if (r.finishSerial == 0) ++r.lateBefore;
+        else if (it != r.serials.end() && it->second < r.finishSerial) ++r.lateOld;
+        else ++r.lateNew;
+        orthrosPublish(r);
+    }
+}

+namespace osg
+{
+    /** Orthros: OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE read once (the page sets ENV before the engine starts); absent = on, 0 = off,
+     * off as well with OPENMW_WORKQUEUE_THREADED. Off: no Program is registered, nothing is precompiled. */
+    bool orthrosPrecompileEnabled()
+    {
+        static const bool enabled = orthrosReadPrecompileSwitch();
+        return enabled;
+    }
+
+    /** Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE): compiles and links, on the State's context, the Programs that a draw would
+     * compile at its first apply: those with shaders whose per-context program is not linked yet (and not tried: a
+     * failed link is not tried again, as at a draw), in registration order. Only a program none of whose imported
+     * defines (#pragma import_defines / requires) is current in the State, so that the per-context program made is
+     * the one a draw without those defines selects; a program drawn with them (FORCE_OPAQUE, DISTORTION) is still
+     * compiled at its draw. budgetMs < 0: all of them; otherwise none is started once budgetMs have passed (one that
+     * has started runs to its end). finish: the pass at the first frame after a loading (counted apart; programs
+     * registered after it and compiled at a draw count as lateNew). Must run on the context's thread, between draws
+     * (compiling and linking leave the current program alone). Returns the number compiled. Not declared in an OSG
+     * header (the caller declares it), so that the change touches no header. */
+    unsigned int orthrosCompileUnlinkedPrograms(State& state, double budgetMs, bool finish)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosPrecompileEnabled()) return 0;
+        const GLExtensions* extensions = state.get<GLExtensions>();
+        if (!extensions || !extensions->isGlslSupported) return 0;
+        const Timer_t start = Timer::instance()->tick();
+        unsigned int compiled = 0;
+        int notStarted = 0, passedOver = 0;
+        OrthrosProgramRegistry& r = orthrosProgramRegistry();
+        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(r.mutex);
+        r.glThread = std::this_thread::get_id();
+        r.glThreadKnown = true;
+        std::vector<std::pair<unsigned long long, const Program*>> order(r.bySerial.begin(), r.bySerial.end());
+        for (const auto& entry : order)
+        {
+            const Program* program = entry.second;
+            // (still registered: not destroyed by a compile of this pass)
+            auto it = r.serials.find(program);
+            if (it == r.serials.end() || it->second != entry.first) continue;
+            if (program->getNumShaders() == 0) continue;
+            // (multiview programs: built by the engine but never drawn in WebGL — no OVR_multiview2 — and not valid
+            // GLSL ES; compiling them ahead only logged a failure)
+            bool multiview = false;
+            for (unsigned int i = 0; i < program->getNumShaders() && !multiview; ++i)
+                multiview = program->getShader(i) && program->getShader(i)->getName().find("multiview") != std::string::npos;
+            if (multiview) continue;
+            if (program->referenceCount() <= 0)
+            {
+                ++r.skippedDying;
+                continue;
+            }
+            // (the program's imported defines are the union of its shaders': an empty string for it is an empty
+            // string for each of them, so the per-context shaders compiled are the ones that draw will use too)
+            if (!program->getShaderDefines().empty() && !state.getDefineString(program->getShaderDefines()).empty())
+            {
+                ++passedOver;
+                continue;
+            }
+            const Program::PerContextProgram* pcp = program->getPCP(state);
+            if (!pcp || !pcp->needsLink()) continue;
+            if (budgetMs >= 0 && Timer::instance()->delta_m(start, Timer::instance()->tick()) >= budgetMs)
+            {
+                ++notStarted;
+                continue;
+            }
+            program->compileGLObjects(state);
+            r.precompiledUnapplied.insert(program);
+            ++compiled;
+        }
+        r.unappliedSize.store(r.precompiledUnapplied.size(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const double ms = Timer::instance()->delta_m(start, Timer::instance()->tick());
+        ++r.passes;
+        r.compiled += compiled;
+        r.ms += ms;
+        if (finish)
+        {
+            r.finishCompiled += compiled;
+            r.finishMs += ms;
+            r.finishSerial = r.nextSerial;
+        }
+        r.left = notStarted;
+        r.withDefines = passedOver;
+        orthrosPublish(r);
+        return compiled;
+    }

+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+    // Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUAGCINC, components/lua/luastate.cpp): Lua's incremental collector, stopped, its work
+    // paid here alone, in update() -- on the Lua thread beside the frame's cull and draw (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUATHREAD;
+    // inline, after the drawing, without it). Measured before: left running, the collector was stepped by whichever
+    // thread allocated, the page's thread included (synchronizedUpdate's userdata and UI layers: 36-89 ms of luaC_step
+    // per 30 s there, stretches of 18-25 ms in the frame); and one LUA_GCSTEP(steps) pays its whole debt at once (100 KB
+    // a frame: 20-30 ms of marking in each frame of a cycle). So, Lua's own pacing, kept by hand (LUAI_GCPAUSE 200 %,
+    // step multiplier 100: 1 KB of marking for each KB allocated):
+    //   - each call counts the heap's net growth since the previous one (on every thread: what Lua's debt counts) plus
+    //     upstream's forced `steps` KB ([Lua] gc steps per frame) as owed;
+    //   - between cycles (Lua's pause) nothing runs until the owed KB reach the heap left at the last cycle's end
+    //     (the heap twice that, but for the forced KB); then a cycle starts;
+    //   - during a cycle, the owed KB are paid as LUA_GCSTEP(1) calls (1 KB of debt each: one 1 KB step every other
+    //     call), until a cycle ends or the steps took sOrthrosGcBudgetMs (checked after each step: the step that
+    //     ends the mark phase, the atomic one, is indivisible and can take 15-20 ms). What is left is carried to the
+    //     next frame. Behind (the heap at 4 times the last cycle's, a load's allocations), the budget is
+    //     sOrthrosGcBehindBudgetMs, so that the heap stays bounded.
+    // LUA_GCSTEP runs the collector while it is stopped (lapi.c restores the stop after the step); a stopped
+    // collector's allocation checks only reset its debt (luaC_step), so no other thread ever runs a step.
+    void LuaManager::orthrosGcStep(int steps)
+    {
+        constexpr double sOrthrosGcBudgetMs = 2.0;
+        constexpr double sOrthrosGcBehindBudgetMs = 12.0;
+        lua_State* const L = mLua.unsafeState();
+        OrthrosGcPacer& pacer = mOrthrosGc;
+        const double start = emscripten_get_now();
+        const int countKb = lua_gc(L, LUA_GCCOUNT, 0);
+        if (!pacer.mStopped)
+        {
+            // Whatever Lua's collector was doing (a cycle under way, or its pause): a cycle paid from now on.
+            lua_gc(L, LUA_GCSTOP, 0);
+            pacer.mStopped = true;
+            pacer.mInCycle = false;
+            pacer.mPauseKb = 0;
+            pacer.mLastKb = countKb;
+        }
+        pacer.mOwedKb += static_cast<double>(countKb - pacer.mLastKb) + steps;
+        if (!pacer.mInCycle)
+        {
+            if (pacer.mOwedKb < pacer.mPauseKb)
+            {
+                pacer.mLastKb = countKb;
+                return;
+            }
+            // A cycle starts (Lua's own debt set to 0 by a basic step: from now on each 1 KB of debt is a step).
+            pacer.mOwedKb -= pacer.mPauseKb;
+            pacer.mInCycle = true;
+            if (lua_gc(L, LUA_GCSTEP, 0) > 0)
+                pacer.mInCycle = false;
+        }
+        // (A cycle's work is at most a mark and sweep of the heap: no more debt carried than that.)
+        pacer.mOwedKb = std::min<double>(pacer.mOwedKb, countKb);
+        const double budgetMs = pacer.mPauseKb > 0 && countKb >= 4 * pacer.mPauseKb ? sOrthrosGcBehindBudgetMs
+                                                                                      : sOrthrosGcBudgetMs;
+        while (pacer.mInCycle && pacer.mOwedKb > 0)
+        {
+            const int ended = lua_gc(L, LUA_GCSTEP, 1);
+            pacer.mOwedKb -= 1;
+            if (ended < 0) // (-1: the collector is running a finalizer, never so here)
+                break;
+            if (ended > 0)
+            {
+                // A cycle ended: Lua's pause, the next one at twice the heap left (setpause: LUAI_GCPAUSE 200 %).
+                pacer.mInCycle = false;
+                pacer.mOwedKb = 0;
+                pacer.mPauseKb = lua_gc(L, LUA_GCCOUNT, 0);
+                break;
+            }
+            if (emscripten_get_now() - start >= budgetMs)
+                break;
+        }
+        pacer.mLastKb = lua_gc(L, LUA_GCCOUNT, 0);
+    }
+
+    // A full collection made elsewhere (clear()): Lua's pause, the next cycle at twice the heap left.
+    void LuaManager::orthrosGcCollected()
+    {
+        if (!mOrthrosGc.mStopped)
+            return;
+        mOrthrosGc.mInCycle = false;
+        mOrthrosGc.mOwedKb = 0;
+        mOrthrosGc.mLastKb = lua_gc(mLua.unsafeState(), LUA_GCCOUNT, 0);
+        mOrthrosGc.mPauseKb = mOrthrosGc.mLastKb;
+    }

+    void PostProcessor::orthrosPrecompile(const std::shared_ptr<Fx::Technique>& technique)
+    {
+        // Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_FXPROGRAMS): a technique a Lua script loads (postprocessing.load) and enables later,
+        // e.g. at the first sprint, had its programs compiled and linked at the first frame drawing it - a frame of
+        // several hundred milliseconds on WebGL. Its passes' programs (the ones prepareStateSet will give: Fx::Pass
+        // keeps them) go to the incremental compile operation now, which compiles them on this (GL) thread within its
+        // per-frame budget, or all at once under the loading screen. Linking a program draws nothing. "0": compiled at
+        // the first draw, as before.
+        if (!technique || !Fx::Pass::orthrosKeepsPrograms() || !technique->isValid()
+            || technique->getGLSLVersion() > mGLSLVersion)
+            return;
+        osgUtil::IncrementalCompileOperation* ico = mViewer->getIncrementalCompileOperation();
+        if (!ico)
+            return;
+        osg::ref_ptr<osg::Group> group = new osg::Group;
+        const std::string name = technique->getName();
+        for (const auto& pass : technique->getPasses())
+        {
+            osg::ref_ptr<osg::Group> node = new osg::Group;
+            node->getOrCreateStateSet()->setAttribute(pass->getProgram(name));
+            group->addChild(node);
+        }
+        osgUtil::StateToCompile stateToCompile(osgUtil::GLObjectsVisitor::COMPILE_STATE_ATTRIBUTES, nullptr);
+        group->accept(stateToCompile);
+        if (stateToCompile.empty())
+            return;
+        osg::ref_ptr<osgUtil::IncrementalCompileOperation::CompileSet> compileSet
+            = new osgUtil::IncrementalCompileOperation::CompileSet(group);
+        compileSet->buildCompileMap(ico->getContextSet(), stateToCompile);
+        ico->add(compileSet.get(), false);
+    }

+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+        // Orthros: OPENMW_ORTHROS_GUIONEBUFFER (read once with the drawable, made at startup; absent or anything but
+        // "0": on; "0": the per-batch loop above, as before). The frame's batches drawn from one vertex buffer, the
+        // GUI's own: each batch's vertices copied at its place in it (the batches in their order, each right after the
+        // one before), the three attribute pointers set once, then per batch its StateSet and texture as before and
+        // glDrawArrays from its first vertex. Before, every batch bound its own buffer and pointed the three
+        // attributes at it: a HUD of ~190 batches (Vanilla+'s: mostly window borders of nine pieces, one quad and
+        // one texture each) cost ~1,150 WebGL calls a frame, 760 of them buffer binds and attribute pointers. The
+        // same vertices, textures, states and order: the same picture.
+        // Two such buffers, used in turn (a frame's writes never go into the buffer the frame before drew from).
+        // Uploads: a batch's bytes compared with those its place holds (orthrosSameBytes) and copied only when they
+        // differ; each run of changed bytes uploaded with one glBufferSubData (runs closer than sOrthrosRunGap
+        // merged), nothing when nothing changed. A buffer grows (a new one, uploaded whole by OSG's first compile)
+        // when the frame needs more room, never shrinks. Its bytes are written behind OSG's back (the array is never
+        // dirty()-ed): OSG uploads it at its first compile only, when its bytes are the frame's. The batches' own
+        // buffers are then never bound, so never made on the GPU. Returns false (the per-batch loop runs as before)
+        // when buffer objects are not supported (or the buffer's GL object cannot be had: then before any byte of
+        // the arena changed). Relies on nothing the drawable's vertex array state believes: the buffer is bound
+        // explicitly before its runs go up and its pointers are set.
+        static constexpr size_t sOrthrosRunGap = 16 * 1024;
+
+        bool orthrosDrawOneBuffer(osg::State* state, const std::vector<Batch>& vec, unsigned int posLoc,
+            unsigned int colLoc, unsigned int uvLoc) const
+        {
+            if (!state->isVertexBufferObjectSupported())
+                return false;
+            const size_t stride = sizeof(MyGUI::Vertex);
+            size_t total = 0;
+            for (const Batch& batch : vec)
+                total += batch.mVertexCount * stride;
+
+            mOrthrosArenaIndex = (mOrthrosArenaIndex + 1) % 2;
+            osg::ref_ptr<osg::UByteArray>& arenaArray = mOrthrosArena[mOrthrosArenaIndex];
+            osg::ref_ptr<osg::VertexBufferObject>& arenaVbo = mOrthrosArenaVbo[mOrthrosArenaIndex];
+            if (!arenaArray || arenaArray->size() < total)
+            {
+                // (room to grow: a text window opening adds a few thousand vertices; 64 KiB at least)
+                size_t capacity = std::max<size_t>(total + total / 2, 64 * 1024);
+                capacity = (capacity + stride - 1) / stride * stride;
+                arenaArray = new osg::UByteArray(static_cast<unsigned int>(capacity));
+                arenaVbo = new osg::VertexBufferObject;
+                arenaVbo->setDataVariance(osg::Object::DYNAMIC);
+                arenaVbo->setUsage(GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW);
+                arenaVbo->setArray(0, arenaArray.get());
+            }
+
+            // (its GL object fetched before any byte of the arena changes: when there is none, the per-batch loop
+            // draws and the arena still mirrors its GL buffer)
+            osg::GLBufferObject* bufferobject = arenaVbo->getOrCreateGLBufferObject(state->getContextID());
+            if (!bufferobject)
+                return false;
+            // (a fresh arena's buffer object is a new one: dirty)
+            const bool uploaded = bufferobject->isDirty();
+
+            // The vertices at their places; mOrthrosRuns the [begin, end) spans of bytes that changed.
+            unsigned char* arena = &(*arenaArray)[0];
+            mOrthrosRuns.clear();
+            size_t offset = 0;
+            for (const Batch& batch : vec)
+            {
+                const size_t bytes = batch.mVertexCount * stride;
+                const osg::Array* array = batch.mArray.get();
+                // (a batch whose array holds fewer bytes than its count: the old path's draw read past its buffer --
+                // a WebGL error, nothing drawn; here its place is left as it is and its draw skipped below)
+                if (bytes != 0 && array && array->getTotalDataSize() >= bytes)
+                {
+                    const unsigned char* src = static_cast<const unsigned char*>(array->getDataPointer());
+                    if (uploaded || !orthrosSameBytes(arena + offset, src, bytes))
+                    {
+                        std::memcpy(arena + offset, src, bytes);
+                        if (!mOrthrosRuns.empty() && offset <= mOrthrosRuns.back().second + sOrthrosRunGap)
+                            mOrthrosRuns.back().second = offset + bytes;
+                        else
+                            mOrthrosRuns.emplace_back(offset, offset + bytes);
+                    }
+                }
+                offset += bytes;
+            }
+
+            // The arena's bytes always equal its GL buffer's (or its GL buffer is dirty: uploaded whole at its bind):
+            // the bytes are changed only past this point, where nothing returns before they are uploaded.
+            // (a dirty buffer object -- a fresh arena's, or a new one after its GL objects were released -- is
+            // compiled at its bind: the whole array goes up, the frame's bytes; otherwise it is bound explicitly,
+            // whatever the drawable's vertex array state believes is bound, and the changed runs go up through that
+            // binding)
+            if (uploaded)
+                state->bindVertexBufferObject(bufferobject);
+            else
+            {
+                bufferobject->bindBuffer();
+                state->setCurrentVertexBufferObject(bufferobject);
+            }
+            if (!uploaded)
+                for (const std::pair<size_t, size_t>& run : mOrthrosRuns)
+                    glBufferSubData(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, static_cast<GLintptr>(run.first),
+                        static_cast<GLsizeiptr>(run.second - run.first), arena + run.first);
+
+            const GLsizei glStride = static_cast<GLsizei>(stride);
+            glEnableVertexAttribArray(posLoc);
+            glVertexAttribPointer(posLoc, 3, GL_FLOAT, GL_FALSE, glStride, reinterpret_cast<char*>(0));
+            glEnableVertexAttribArray(colLoc);
+            glVertexAttribPointer(colLoc, 4, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, GL_TRUE, glStride, reinterpret_cast<char*>(12));
+            glEnableVertexAttribArray(uvLoc);
+            glVertexAttribPointer(uvLoc, 2, GL_FLOAT, GL_FALSE, glStride, reinterpret_cast<char*>(16));
+
+            size_t first = 0;
+            for (const Batch& batch : vec)
+            {
+                if (batch.mStateSet)
+                {
+                    state->pushStateSet(batch.mStateSet);
+                    state->apply();
+                }
+
+                osg::Texture2D* texture = batch.mTexture;
+                if (texture)
+                    state->applyTextureAttribute(0, texture);
+                else
+                    state->applyTextureAttribute(0, mDummyTexture);
+
+                const osg::Array* array = batch.mArray.get();
+                const size_t bytes = batch.mVertexCount * stride;
+                if (bytes == 0 || (array && array->getTotalDataSize() >= bytes))
+                    glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, static_cast<GLint>(first), static_cast<GLsizei>(batch.mVertexCount));
+                first += batch.mVertexCount;
+
+                if (batch.mStateSet)
+                {
+                    state->popStateSet();
+                    state->apply();
+                }
+            }
+
+            glDisableVertexAttribArray(posLoc);
+            glDisableVertexAttribArray(colLoc);
+            glDisableVertexAttribArray(uvLoc);
+            return true;
+        }
+#endif

+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+    void LuaState::orthrosCompileFactory(const VFS::Path::Normalized& path, const std::string& source)
+    {
+        // The source as the body of a vararg function, its first line kept on line 1 (error lines unchanged). The
+        // function's only possible upvalue is the factory's local _ENV: one fresh per call, so each instance and the
+        // closures it makes share their own environment, as with a main chunk loaded anew; sol::set_environment finds
+        // it by its name, _ENV. Compiled only after the source compiled as itself, so no source that is invalid alone
+        // runs; one that compiles only alone keeps its bytecode re-read per instance (no factory recorded).
+        std::string wrapped;
+        wrapped.reserve(source.size() + 64);
+        wrapped.append("local _ENV = ...; return function(...) ");
+        wrapped.append(source);
+        wrapped.append("\nend");
+        sol::load_result factory = mSol.load(wrapped, path.value(), sol::load_mode::text);
+        if (!factory.valid())
+        {
+            Log(Debug::Warning) << "Orthros: " << path.value()
+                                << " not compiled as a factory, its bytecode re-read per instance (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUACHUNKS)";
+            return;
+        }
+        mOrthrosFactories[path] = sol::main_function(factory.get<sol::function>());
+    }
+
+    bool LuaState::orthrosInstantiate(const VFS::Path::Normalized& path, sol::function& out)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosChunkFactories())
+            return false;
+        auto it = mOrthrosFactories.find(path);
+        if (it == mOrthrosFactories.end())
+            return false;
+        lua_State* L = mSol.lua_state();
+        // Pushed on the main state, as lua_load did; when this is a `require` run from a coroutine, the main state's
+        // LUA_MINSTACK guarantee belongs to the C function that is running, not to us: make room (else the undump).
+        if (!lua_checkstack(L, 3))
+            return false;
+        // factory(_G): the new closure's _ENV starts at the globals, as lua_load sets a loaded chunk's first upvalue.
+        // The factory runs a few instructions on the main state: a memory error, or the instruction watchdog
+        // (countHook) firing there instead of in the script's first instructions, fails the script's start with the
+        // same "Lua error" as before.
+        const int top = lua_gettop(L);
+        sol::stack::push(L, it->second);
+        lua_pushglobaltable(L);
+        if (lua_pcall(L, 1, 1, 0) != LUA_OK)
+        {
+            std::string message = lua_isstring(L, -1) ? lua_tostring(L, -1) : "error in a script factory";
+            lua_settop(L, top);
+            throw std::runtime_error("Lua error: " + message);
+        }
+        out = sol::stack::pop<sol::function>(L);
+        lua_settop(L, top);
+        return true;
+    }
+#endif

+        }();
+        return on;
+#else
+        return false;

+        double mMs = 0;
+    };
+
+    /// Orthros (texahead.patch): at most this many ms of uploads ahead in one tick; past it, the rest of the tick's
+    /// textures are left to their next draw (the previous path). A tick that reloads a large set never adds more than
+    /// this to its decode, and the reloads' pacing (their decoded bytes, ImageManager::reloadImage's return) is
+    /// unchanged: no light copy stays longer.
+    constexpr double sOrthrosAheadTickMs = 8.0;
+
+    /// Orthros (texahead.patch): `image` was just updated in place (ImageManager::reloadImage, between frames, on the
+    /// thread that renders: a light copy replaced by the file itself). Its textures that hold an older upload are
+    /// uploaded again now, as their next apply would have, instead of by the first draw that shows them: shown, that
+    /// is this frame's draw anyway — the same work, a little earlier —; not shown (behind the camera, under a roof),
+    /// a later draw used to upload them all at once (the local map's first render of a cell drew a dozen such
+    /// textures, 25 MB, in one frame; a camera turn the same). Within sOrthrosAheadTickMs a tick. A texture never
+    /// uploaded is left to the incremental compile or its first draw, as before. A texture alive but never drawn
+    /// again (only an expiring cache holds it) is uploaded too: it had a GL object already, the cost is its upload
+    /// once, inside the tick's cap. Requires: called between frames on the GL thread (EmscriptenLoop::tick calls
+    /// reloadUpdated before viewer->advance/frame — keep it there).
+    void orthrosUploadAhead(osgViewer::Viewer& viewer, osg::Image& image, OrthrosAheadTick& tick)
+    {
+        std::vector<osg::ref_ptr<osg::Texture2D>> textures;
+        osg::orthrosTexture2DsOfImage(&image, textures);
+        if (textures.empty())
+            return;
+        osg::GraphicsContext* gc = viewer.getCamera()->getGraphicsContext();
+        osg::State* state = gc != nullptr ? gc->getState() : nullptr;
+        if (state == nullptr || viewer.getFrameStamp() == nullptr)
+            return;
+        const unsigned int frame = viewer.getFrameStamp()->getFrameNumber();
+        if (tick.mFrame != frame)
+        {
+            tick.mFrame = frame;
+            tick.mMs = 0;
+        }
+        const unsigned int contextID = state->getContextID();
+        const double start = emscripten_get_now();
+        int uploaded = 0, deferred = 0;
+        double bytes = 0;
+        for (const osg::ref_ptr<osg::Texture2D>& texture : textures)
+        {
+            if (texture->getImage() != &image || texture->getSubloadCallback() != nullptr
+                || texture->getTextureObject(contextID) == nullptr
+                || texture->getModifiedCount(contextID) == image.getModifiedCount())
+                continue;
+            if (tick.mMs + (emscripten_get_now() - start) >= sOrthrosAheadTickMs)
+            {
+                ++deferred; // (its next draw uploads it, as before)
+                continue;
+            }
+            texture->apply(*state);
+            ++uploaded;
+            bytes += image.getTotalSizeInBytesIncludingMipmaps();
+        }
+        if (uploaded == 0 && deferred == 0)
+            return;
+        // (the texture unit's binding changed behind the State's back: its next apply binds again)
+        if (uploaded != 0)
+            state->haveAppliedTextureAttribute(state->getActiveTextureUnit(), osg::StateAttribute::TEXTURE);
+        const double ms = emscripten_get_now() - start;
+        tick.mMs += ms;
+        // clang-format off
+        EM_ASM({
+            var s = globalThis.__orthrosTexAhead || (globalThis.__orthrosTexAhead = { textures: 0, bytes: 0, deferred: 0, ms: 0, max: 0, maxTick: 0 });
+            s.textures += $0; s.bytes += $1; s.deferred += $2; s.ms += $3;
+            if ($3 > s.max) s.max = $3;
+            if ($4 > s.maxTick) s.maxTick = $4;
+        }, uploaded, bytes, deferred, ms, tick.mMs);
+        // clang-format on
+    }
+}
+#endif

+    {

+    std::streamsize ConstrainedFileStreamBuf::xsgetn(char_type* s, std::streamsize count)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosWholeReads() || count < static_cast<std::streamsize>(sizeof(mBuffer)))
+            return std::streambuf::xsgetn(s, count);
+        std::streamsize done = 0;
+        // (what the buffer holds first, then the rest from the file in one read — File::read may return less: again
+        // until the region's end)
+        const std::streamsize held = std::min<std::streamsize>(egptr() - gptr(), count);
+        if (held > 0)
+        {
+            std::memcpy(s, gptr(), static_cast<std::size_t>(held));
+            done = held;
+        }
+        setg(nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
+        while (done < count)
+        {
+            const std::size_t left = (mOrigin + mSize) - File::tell(mFile);
+            const std::size_t toRead = std::min(left, static_cast<std::size_t>(count - done));
+            if (toRead == 0)
+                break;
+            const std::size_t got = File::read(mFile, s + done, toRead);
+            if (got == 0)
+                break;
+            done += static_cast<std::streamsize>(got);
+        }
+        return done;
+    }

+    /// Orthros (nifparse.patch): the bytes the stream reads, owned by it (first base: built before MemBuf points
+    /// at them).
+    struct OwnedBytes
+    {
+        std::vector<char> mBytes;
+    };
+
+    /// @brief Orthros (nifparse.patch): a std::istream over a buffer it owns — a file read whole once, then parsed
+    /// (and hashed) from memory.
+    struct IOwnedMemStream : private OwnedBytes, MemBuf, std::istream
+    {
+        explicit IOwnedMemStream(std::vector<char>&& bytes)
+            : OwnedBytes{ std::move(bytes) }
+            , MemBuf(mBytes.data(), mBytes.size())
+            , std::istream(static_cast<std::streambuf*>(static_cast<MemBuf*>(this)))
+        {
+        }
+    };
+
+    /// Orthros (nifparse.patch): the rest of `stream` (from its position to its end) into `out`, in one read. False
+    /// (the stream back at its position): its size unknown, or fewer bytes than that read.
+    inline bool orthrosReadRest(std::istream& stream, std::vector<char>& out)
+    {
+        const std::istream::pos_type start = stream.tellg();
+        if (start == std::istream::pos_type(-1))
+        {
+            stream.clear();
+            return false;
+        }
+        stream.seekg(0, std::ios_base::end);
+        const std::istream::pos_type end = stream.tellg();
+        stream.clear();
+        stream.seekg(start);
+        if (end == std::istream::pos_type(-1) || std::streamoff(end) < std::streamoff(start))
+        {
+            stream.clear();
+            return false;
+        }
+        out.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(std::streamoff(end) - std::streamoff(start)));
+        if (!out.empty())
+            stream.read(out.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(out.size()));
+        if (static_cast<std::size_t>(stream.gcount()) != out.size() && !out.empty())
+        {
+            stream.clear();
+            stream.seekg(start);
+            out.clear();
+            return false;
+        }
+        return true;
+    }

+    /// Orthros (nifparse.patch): NIF parses run on a thread of their own (the web's cooperative WorkQueue runs the
+    /// preloads on the page's thread, where a whole NIF or .kf parse is one indivisible step of 20-250 ms). The page's
+    /// thread reads the file's bytes (from the page, once they are there: no FS read ever happens on the thread — the
+    /// web proxies those to the page's thread) and hands them over; the thread parses them from memory (Nif::Reader
+    /// on an IOwnedMemStream: the same parse, the same hash) and keeps the result until taken (get(),
+    /// orthrosTakeParsed()) or unused for kResultLife; a readiness check only peeks at it (orthrosPeekParsed), so a
+    /// mesh put off for its textures keeps its parse. A failed parse stays recorded (orthrosParsedReady true, never
+    /// queued again) until kResultLife: the caller's own parse reports the error, as before. Nothing on the page's
+    /// thread ever waits for it (but ~NifFileManager, for a parse under way).
+    struct OrthrosNifParses
+    {
+        struct Job
+        {
+            VFS::Path::Normalized mPath;
+            std::vector<char> mBytes;
+        };
+        struct Result
+        {
+            Nif::NIFFilePtr mFile; // (null: the parse failed — the caller parses it again and reports the error)
+            std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point mAt;
+        };
+
+        static constexpr std::chrono::seconds kResultLife{ 30 };
+        static constexpr std::size_t kMaxResults = 256;
+        static constexpr std::size_t kThreadStack = 1024 * 1024;
+
+        const ToUTF8::StatelessUtf8Encoder* mEncoder = nullptr;
+        std::mutex mMutex;
+        std::condition_variable mWake;
+        std::condition_variable mIdle;
+        std::deque<Job> mQueue;
+        std::set<std::string, std::less<>> mPending; // (queued or being parsed)
+        std::map<std::string, Result, std::less<>> mResults;
+        bool mStop = false;
+        bool mBusy = false;
+        bool mStarted = false;
+        bool mNoThread = false;
+        bool mWarnedThread = false;
+        // (counters, logged every kLogEvery parses, at an unfinished preload's abort, and published to the page:
+        // globalThis.__omwNifThreadStats — Resource::nifStatAdd's Parse stage counts the page's thread's parses only)
+        std::size_t mParsed = 0;
+        std::size_t mFailed = 0;
+        std::size_t mTaken = 0;
+        std::size_t mUnused = 0;
+        std::size_t mBytes = 0;
+        double mParseMs = 0;
+        double mReadMs = 0;
+        std::size_t mCancelled = 0; // (queued, then parsed on the page's thread first: dropped unparsed)
+        std::size_t mHereParsed = 0; // (parsed on the page's thread while the switch is on: get(), a .kf)
+        double mHereMs = 0;
+        std::size_t mLoggedAt = 0;
+        static constexpr std::size_t kLogEvery = 10;
+
+        void run()
+        {
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+            while (true)
+            {
+                mWake.wait(lock, [&] { return mStop || !mQueue.empty(); });
+                if (mStop)
+                    break;
+                Job job = std::move(mQueue.front());
+                mQueue.pop_front();
+                mBusy = true;
+                lock.unlock();
+                const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+                Nif::NIFFilePtr file;
+                try
+                {
+                    auto parsed = std::make_shared<Nif::NIFFile>(job.mPath);
+                    Nif::Reader reader(*parsed, mEncoder);
+                    reader.parse(std::make_unique<Files::IOwnedMemStream>(std::move(job.mBytes)));
+                    file = std::move(parsed);
+                }
+                catch (...)
+                {
+                    // (anything: reported by the parse on the page's thread, as before — never out of the thread)
+                    file = nullptr;
+                }
+                const double ms
+                    = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+                lock.lock();
+                mBusy = false;
+                mPending.erase(std::string(job.mPath.value()));
+                ++mParsed;
+                if (!file)
+                    ++mFailed;
+                mResults[std::string(job.mPath.value())] = Result{ std::move(file), std::chrono::steady_clock::now() };
+                mParseMs += ms;
+                mIdle.notify_all();
+            }
+            mBusy = false;
+            mIdle.notify_all();
+        }
+
+        /// (results unused for kResultLife, or the oldest past kMaxResults, dropped; mMutex held)
+        void prune()
+        {
+            const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+            for (auto it = mResults.begin(); it != mResults.end();)
+            {
+                if (now - it->second.mAt > kResultLife)
+                {
+                    it = mResults.erase(it);
+                    ++mUnused;
+                }
+                else
+                    ++it;
+            }
+            while (mResults.size() > kMaxResults)
+            {
+                auto oldest = mResults.begin();
+                for (auto it = mResults.begin(); it != mResults.end(); ++it)
+                    if (it->second.mAt < oldest->second.mAt)
+                        oldest = it;
+                mResults.erase(oldest);
+                ++mUnused;
+            }
+        }
+
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+        static void* threadMain(void* arg)
+        {
+            auto* self = static_cast<std::shared_ptr<OrthrosNifParses>*>(arg);
+            std::shared_ptr<OrthrosNifParses> parses = std::move(*self);
+            delete self;
+            parses->run();
+            return nullptr;
+        }
+#endif
+
+        /// (the thread, started at the first job; false: none — the callers parse as before; mMutex held)
+        bool start(const std::shared_ptr<OrthrosNifParses>& me)
+        {
+            if (mStarted || mNoThread)
+                return mStarted;
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+            pthread_attr_t attr;
+            pthread_attr_init(&attr);
+            pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, kThreadStack);
+            pthread_t thread;
+            auto* arg = new std::shared_ptr<OrthrosNifParses>(me);
+            if (pthread_create(&thread, &attr, &OrthrosNifParses::threadMain, arg) == 0)
+            {
+                pthread_detach(thread);
+                mStarted = true;
+                Log(Debug::Info) << "Orthros: NIF parses on a thread of their own (OPENMW_ORTHROS_NIFTHREAD)";
+            }
+            else
+            {
+                delete arg;
+                mNoThread = true;
+                Log(Debug::Warning) << "Orthros: no thread for NIF parses: on the page's thread, as before";
+            }
+            pthread_attr_destroy(&attr);
+#else
+            (void)me;
+            mNoThread = true;
+#endif
+            return mStarted;
+        }
+
+        /// (the counters as one line, and published to the page; mMutex held — the caller logs it after)
+        std::string counters()
+        {
+            mLoggedAt = mParsed;
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+            if (emscripten_is_main_runtime_thread())
+            {
+                // (no comma inside the EM_ASM block: one statement a field, as nifstats.cpp)
+                EM_ASM({
+                    var s = {};
+                    s.parsed = $0;
+                    s.failed = $1;
+                    s.parseMs = $2;
+                    s.taken = $3;
+                    s.unused = $4;
+                    s.cancelled = $5;
+                    s.queued = $6;
+                    s.readMs = $7;
+                    s.hereParsed = $8;
+                    s.hereMs = $9;
+                    globalThis.__omwNifThreadStats = s;
+                },
+                    static_cast<double>(mParsed), static_cast<double>(mFailed), mParseMs, static_cast<double>(mTaken),
+                    static_cast<double>(mUnused), static_cast<double>(mCancelled), static_cast<double>(mQueue.size()),
+                    mReadMs, static_cast<double>(mHereParsed), mHereMs);
+            }
+#endif
+            return "Orthros: NIF parses on their thread: " + std::to_string(mParsed) + " (" + std::to_string(mFailed)
+                + " failed, " + std::to_string(static_cast<int>(mParseMs)) + " ms there; "
+                + std::to_string(mBytes >> 10) + " KB read for them in " + std::to_string(static_cast<int>(mReadMs))
+                + " ms here), " + std::to_string(mTaken) + " taken, " + std::to_string(mUnused) + " unused, "
+                + std::to_string(mCancelled) + " cancelled, " + std::to_string(mQueue.size()) + " queued; "
+                + std::to_string(mHereParsed) + " parsed on the page's thread meanwhile ("
+                + std::to_string(static_cast<int>(mHereMs)) + " ms)";
+        }
+    };

+    Nif::NIFFilePtr NifFileManager::orthrosTakeParsed(VFS::Path::NormalizedView name)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return nullptr;
+        OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+        const auto found = parses.mResults.find(name.value());
+        if (found == parses.mResults.end() || found->second.mFile == nullptr)
+            return nullptr; // (none, or a failed parse: kept, so that orthrosParsedReady never queues it again)
+        Nif::NIFFilePtr file = std::move(found->second.mFile);
+        parses.mResults.erase(found);
+        ++parses.mTaken;
+        return file;
+    }

+    Nif::NIFFilePtr NifFileManager::orthrosPeekParsed(VFS::Path::NormalizedView name, bool* failed)
+    {
+        if (failed != nullptr)
+            *failed = false;
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return nullptr;
+        OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+        const auto found = parses.mResults.find(name.value());
+        if (found == parses.mResults.end())
+            return nullptr;
+        if (failed != nullptr)
+            *failed = found->second.mFile == nullptr;
+        return found->second.mFile;
+    }

+    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point NifFileManager::orthrosCancelParse(VFS::Path::NormalizedView name)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return {};
+        OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+        if (parses.mPending.contains(name.value()))
+        {
+            // (still queued: dropped. Under way: its result comes, unused — kResultLife)
+            const auto queued = std::find_if(parses.mQueue.begin(), parses.mQueue.end(),
+                [&](const OrthrosNifParses::Job& job) { return job.mPath.value() == name.value(); });
+            if (queued != parses.mQueue.end())
+            {
+                parses.mQueue.erase(queued);
+                parses.mPending.erase(std::string(name.value()));
+                ++parses.mCancelled;
+            }
+        }
+        return std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    }

+    void NifFileManager::orthrosParsedHere(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point start)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return;
+        const double ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+        OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+        ++parses.mHereParsed;
+        parses.mHereMs += ms;
+    }

+    void NifFileManager::orthrosLogCounters()
+    {
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return;
+        std::string line;
+        {
+            OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+            if (!parses.mStarted)
+                return;
+            line = parses.counters();
+        }
+        Log(Debug::Info) << line;

+    bool NifFileManager::orthrosParsedReady(VFS::Path::NormalizedView name)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosParseOffThread())
+            return true;
+        OrthrosNifParses& parses = *mOrthrosParses;
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+        // (the page's thread only: the one the cooperative WorkQueue runs on. Under the OMW_PROXY spike
+        // (PROXY_TO_PTHREAD) the engine runs on a pthread: the switch is then a no-op — said once)
+        if (!emscripten_is_main_runtime_thread())
+        {
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+            if (!parses.mWarnedThread)
+            {
+                parses.mWarnedThread = true;
+                Log(Debug::Warning) << "Orthros: OPENMW_ORTHROS_NIFTHREAD unused: the engine is not on the page's "
+                                       "thread (NIF parses there, as before)";
+            }
+            return true;
+        }
+#endif
+        if (mCache->getRefFromObjectCache(name) != nullptr)
+            return true;
+        {
+            std::string line;
+            bool ready = false;
+            bool pending = false;
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+                if (parses.mStarted && parses.mParsed >= parses.mLoggedAt + OrthrosNifParses::kLogEvery)
+                    line = parses.counters();
+                // (a failed parse among the results as well: final until kResultLife)
+                ready = parses.mNoThread || parses.mResults.contains(name.value());
+                pending = parses.mPending.contains(name.value());
+            }
+            if (!line.empty())
+                Log(Debug::Info) << line;
+            if (ready)
+                return true;
+            if (pending)
+                return false;
+        }
+        if (!mVFS->exists(name))
+            return true; // (the caller's own error)
+        if (!mVFS->orthrosDataReady(name))
+            return false; // (on its way)
+        const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        std::vector<char> bytes;
+        try
+        {
+            Files::IStreamPtr stream = mVFS->get(name);
+            if (!Files::orthrosReadRest(*stream, bytes))
+                return true; // (its size unknown: parsed by the caller, as before)
+        }
+        catch (const std::exception&)
+        {
+            return true; // (the caller's read reports it)
+        }
+        const double ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(parses.mMutex);
+        if (!parses.start(mOrthrosParses))
+            return true;
+        parses.prune();
+        parses.mReadMs += ms;
+        parses.mBytes += bytes.size();
+        parses.mPending.insert(std::string(name.value()));
+        parses.mQueue.push_back(OrthrosNifParses::Job{ VFS::Path::Normalized(name), std::move(bytes) });
+        parses.mWake.notify_one();
+        return false;
+    }

+    bool LuaFlex::orthrosSkipChildCoord(std::size_t index, WidgetExtension* child)
+    {
+        // Left out: the child's pass in updateChildren changed nothing in its tree — the state it left is a fixpoint of
+        // its layout for what it read from outside its tree — and those inputs are the same now: its forced coord (its
+        // size and position ignore its parent's while forced: every child of a Flex is), its MyGUI parent's inherited
+        // visibility (updateVisible; this Flex's own may have changed since, in WidgetExtension::updateCoord), and its
+        // coord as it left it. Then laying it out again changes nothing either.
+        if (!mOrthrosPassesValid || index >= mOrthrosPasses.size())
+            return false;
+        OrthrosLayoutStats& stats = orthrosLayoutStats();
+        ++stats.mSecondPasses;
+        const OrthrosChildPass& pass = mOrthrosPasses[index];
+        if (!pass.mClean || !(child->orthrosForced() == pass.mForced) || child->widget()->getCoord() != pass.mCoord)
+            return false;
+        MyGUI::Widget* parent = child->widget()->getParent();
+        if ((parent == nullptr || parent->getInheritedVisible()) != pass.mParentVisible)
+            return false;
+        ++stats.mSecondPassesSkipped;
+        if (orthrosLuaUiLayout() == 2)
+        {
+            // (checked: laid out anyway — any change it makes is a pass wrongly left out)
+            const std::uint64_t before = stats.mMutations;
+            child->updateCoord();
+            if (stats.mMutations != before)
+            {
+                ++stats.mSkipMismatches;
+                if (stats.mSkipMismatches <= 20)
+                    Log(Debug::Warning) << "Orthros: Lua UI Flex second pass left out would have changed "
+                                        << child->diagnosticName() << " (" << (stats.mMutations - before)
+                                        << " changes)";
+            }
+            return true;
+        }
+        return true;
     }
