+// Orthros (drawthread.patch, OPENMW_ORTHROS_DRAWTHREAD; the engine selects DrawThreadPerContext with it, and only with
+// it, on the web — this file only reacts to that threading model). The web build's graphics thread owns its own WebGL
+// context (an OffscreenCanvas of the pthread, components/sdlutil/sdlgraphicswindow.cpp) and the page thread has none
+// once threading started: stopThreading() cannot hand the context back to the page thread and a new graphics thread
+// would be a new pthread with an empty context. So, with DrawThreadPerContext on the web:
+// - stopThreading() only waits until every frame the page thread dispatched has been drawn and swapped and every
+//   draw-thread job (below) has run (nothing in flight while its caller changes shared state, the reason OpenMW calls
+//   it), the graphics thread kept; startThreading() is then a no-op (_threadsRunning stays true);
+// - the graphics thread waits between frames in a gate of its own (OrthrosFrameGate, before the frame's draws) and not
+//   in the Renderer's draw queue: there it runs the jobs the page thread hands it (orthrosDrawThreadRun: WebGL work
+//   between frames — the uploads ahead, the global map's read), at once, a frame dispatched or not; a page thread
+//   waiting for a job never waits for a frame it has not dispatched. (A GraphicsContext::add operation, after the swap
+//   in the graphics thread's queue, would wait for the next frame.)
+// - the graphics thread is event-driven (OrthrosGraphicsThread, below): once its context is current it returns to its
+//   worker's event loop (emscripten_exit_with_live_runtime) and never blocks there between frames; its operations
+//   (the gate, the frame's draws, the swap) run in tasks — a frame dispatched, a job queued or the page's kick wakes it
+//   with one task proxied to it (orthrosDrawThreadWake: emscripten_proxy_async on the system queue, from any thread,
+//   through Atomics.waitAsync on the worker: no step of the page's event loop), and each task draws at most one frame,
+//   the next frame's in the worker's next task (a MessageChannel self-post: no timer clamp). A task may still block
+//   inside, as the draws wait for the frame's culls. Why: Chrome releases a transferred ImageBitmap's GPU memory through
+//   a task on the worker that made it — a worker that never returns to its event loop leaks every frame it posts
+//   (~4 MB each at 1280x800).
+// The threading model is fixed for the session (setThreadingModel) and the web build never destroys its viewer
+// (~Viewer's close would cancel a graphics thread that is never in its loop).

+// Module.orthrosDrawWorker): 1 when ready and its context's attributes are the page context's
+// (components/sdlutil/sdlgraphicswindow.cpp compared them); 0 — none asked for, -1 — not made (refused, or no
+// answer), -2 — attributes that differ
+// clang-format off
+EM_JS(int, orthros_drawthread_prepared, (), {
+    var p = Module['orthrosDrawWorker'];
+    if (!p || !p.worker) return p && p.state == 'failed' ? -1 : 0;
+    if (p.state != 'ready') return -1;
+    if (p.claimed) return -3;
+    return p.compatible === false ? -2 : 1;
+});

+    p.claimed = true;
+    PThread.unusedWorkers.push(p.worker);
+    return 1;

+// an abort) told to the page as the thread's crash: its notice (components/sdlutil/sdlgraphicswindow.cpp's `crashed`)
+// and Emscripten's crashed-thread flag, which unwinds the page thread out of its waits for this thread (a task run from

+// proxied to this thread would be relayed through the page thread's event loop, which a page thread waiting for this

+    // The frames' timeline (tlPage / tlDraw below) is a measuring probe: recorded and published only with

+    // from there and waited for would never run: orthrosDrawThreadRun refuses a waited job then.

+    // The only place that clears the queued flag — before the pump looks at the work: a wake after this point proxies
+    // another task, one before it is seen by this pump. (The pump's next turn, a MessageChannel task, leaves the flag
+    // alone: a task proxied meanwhile is still on its way.)
+    void orthrosPumpTask(void*)
+    {
+        sOrthrosPumpQueued.store(false);
+        orthros_drawthread_pump_js();
+    }

+    // (any thread) the graphics thread has work — a frame dispatched, a job queued, the page's kick: one pump task
+    // proxied to it, unless one is queued and not run yet. Never waits: the proxied task reaches the worker through
+    // Atomics.waitAsync (Emscripten's mailbox), no step of the page's event loop — a page thread then waiting for the
+    // draw thread does not deadlock. False when the task could not be proxied (sOrthrosWakeFailed set).
+    bool orthrosDrawThreadWake()
+    {
+        const pthread_t thread = sOrthrosDrawPthread.load();
+        if (thread == 0 || sOrthrosPumpQueued.exchange(true))
+            return true;
+        ++sOrthrosWakes;
+        if (!emscripten_proxy_async(emscripten_proxy_get_system_queue(), thread, orthrosPumpTask, nullptr))
+        {
+            sOrthrosPumpQueued.store(false);
+            if (!sOrthrosWakeFailed.exchange(true))
+                OSG_FATAL << "Orthros: the draw thread could not be woken (emscripten_proxy_async failed): the session ends"
+                          << std::endl;
+            return false;
+        }
+        return true;
+    }

+    // Never waits: pass() is false when there is nothing to do (no frame dispatched, no job) — the graphics thread then
+    // returns to its event loop until a wake (OrthrosGraphicsThread::pump)
+    struct OrthrosFrameGate : public osg::GraphicsOperation
+    {
+        OrthrosFrameGate() : osg::GraphicsOperation("OrthrosFrameGate", true) {}
+        // (only a stock GraphicsThread's OperationThread::run calls this — OrthrosGraphicsThread::pump calls pass(),
+        // startThreading always installs it: never expected. r8v's blocking wait then, rather than a busy loop.)
+        void operator()(osg::GraphicsContext* context) override
+        {
+            static std::atomic<bool> told{ false };
+            if (!told.exchange(true))
+                OSG_WARN << "Orthros: the frame gate runs outside OrthrosGraphicsThread::pump: it blocks between frames"
+                         << std::endl;
+            OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+            while (!pass(context))
+            {
+                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+                if (c.mDispatched == c.mSwapped && c.mJobs.empty())
+                    c.mChanged.wait(lock);
+            }
+        }
+        bool pass(osg::GraphicsContext* context)
+        {
+            OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+            while (true)
+            {
+                // (a frame dispatched first: the page thread waits for its dynamic draw, _endDynamicDrawBlock — the
+                // jobs queued meanwhile run after its swap, at the next pass here; once only: a page dispatching faster
+                // than this thread draws would starve them, so jobs passed over once run before the next frame)
+                if (c.mDispatched > c.mSwapped && (c.mJobs.empty() || !c.mJobsYielded))
+                {
+                    if (!c.mJobs.empty())
+                    {
+                        c.mJobsYielded = true;
+                        ++c.mJobsDeferred;
+                    }
+                    break;
+                }
+                if (!c.mJobs.empty())
+                {
+                    c.mJobsYielded = false;
+                    double ms = 0;
+                    {
+                        osg::ref_ptr<osg::GraphicsOperation> job = std::move(c.mJobs.front());
+                        c.mJobs.pop_front();
+                        c.mJobRunning = true;
+                        lock.unlock();
+                        const double t0 = emscripten_get_now();
+                        (*job)(context);
+                        ms = emscripten_get_now() - t0;
+                    }
+                    lock.lock();
+                    c.mJobRunning = false;
+                    ++c.mJobsRun;
+                    c.mJobsMs += ms;
+                    c.mChanged.notify_all();
+                    continue;
+                }
+                // (nothing to do: the newest frame held back posted if the page showed the previous one meanwhile —
+                // orthros_drawthread_kick wakes this thread then —, and back to the event loop)
+                lock.unlock();
+                orthros_drawthread_flush_held();
+                lock.lock();
+                if (c.mDispatched > c.mSwapped || !c.mJobs.empty())
+                    continue;
+                return false;
+            }
+            c.mGateExit = emscripten_get_now();
+            c.mCompletedAt = 0;
+            c.mCompletions = 0;
+            const int width = c.mSizes[c.mSwapped % 64][0], height = c.mSizes[c.mSwapped % 64][1];
+            lock.unlock();
+            orthros_drawthread_resize(width, height);
+            return true;
+        }
+    };
+
+    // SwapBuffersOperation, then the frame counted as swapped (the graphics thread)
+    struct OrthrosCountedSwap : public osg::GraphicsOperation
+    {
+        OrthrosCountedSwap() : osg::GraphicsOperation("OrthrosCountedSwap", true) {}
+        void operator()(osg::GraphicsContext* context) override
+        {
+            if (context)
+            {
+                context->swapBuffersImplementation();
+                context->clear();
+            }
+            const double now = emscripten_get_now();
+            OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+                const double culled = c.mCulledTimes[c.mSwapped % 64];
+                const double start = culled > c.mGateExit ? culled : c.mGateExit;
+                if (c.mDrawMs.size() < 4096) c.mDrawMs.push_back(static_cast<float>(now - start));
+                if (orthrosTimelineOn() && c.mDrawTl.size() < 7 * 4096)
+                    c.mDrawTl.insert(c.mDrawTl.end(), { static_cast<double>(c.mSwapped + 1), c.mPumpT0, c.mGateExit,
+                        culled, c.mCompletedAt, now, static_cast<double>(c.mCompletions) });
+                ++c.mSwapped;
+            }
+            c.mChanged.notify_all();
+        }
+    };
+
+    // The graphics thread of DrawThreadPerContext on the web: event-driven (the file's head). run() makes the context
+    // current, says so (startThreading's wait), then returns to the worker's event loop for good
+    // (emscripten_exit_with_live_runtime: the pthread stays, isRunning() stays true; no C++ object alive across it).
+    // Each pump() — a task of that event loop — runs the thread's operation queue as OperationThread::run would (the
+    // gate, the frame's draws, the swap, and any operation added to the queue, in order), but stops at the gate when
+    // it has nothing to do, and after one frame swapped: the next frame's operations run in the worker's next task
+    // (orthros_drawthread_defer), so the worker returns to its event loop between any two frames and Chrome frees the
+    // bitmaps the page has replaced. A frame dispatched while this thread draws the previous one waits for that turn
+    // only (no frame of latency added). Operations run with no queue lock held, as in OperationThread::run.
+    class OrthrosGraphicsThread : public osg::GraphicsThread
+    {
+    public:
+        void run() override
+        {
+            bool ready = false;
+            {
+                osg::GraphicsContext* context = dynamic_cast<osg::GraphicsContext*>(getParent());
+                if (context)
+                {
+                    context->makeCurrent();
+                    context->getState()->initializeExtensionProcs();
+                }
+                // (makeCurrent's failure is ignored, as GraphicsThread::run does: a context current on this thread is
+                // the proof it was made)
+                ready = emscripten_webgl_get_current_context() != 0;
+                if (ready && !orthros_drawthread_event_setup())
+                {
+                    // (never here in Chrome: orthros-gl.js gives no draw thread without Atomics.waitAsync)
+                    OSG_FATAL << "Orthros: no Atomics.waitAsync for the draw thread's wakes" << std::endl;
+                    ready = false;
+                }
+                if (ready)
+                    sOrthrosDrawPthread.store(pthread_self());
+                (ready ? sOrthrosContextReady : sOrthrosContextFailed).store(true);
+                OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+                c.mChanged.notify_all();
+            }
+            OSG_INFO << "Orthros: the graphics thread returns to its event loop (OPENMW_ORTHROS_DRAWTHREAD"
+                     << (ready ? "" : ", no context") << ")" << std::endl;
+            // (no context: the thread stays idle — nothing is dispatched to it, renderingTraversals ends the session)
+            emscripten_exit_with_live_runtime();
+        }
+
+        void pump()
+        {
+            // (a frame drawn in this task already, or a pump inside a pump: this one in the next task)
+            if (mInPump || orthros_drawthread_turn_busy())
+            {
+                defer();
+                return;
+            }
+            // (reset however the pump ends; a throw out of it is the thread's crash anyway: orthros_drawthread_event_setup)
+            struct InPump
+            {
+                bool& mFlag;
+                explicit InPump(bool& flag) : mFlag(flag) { mFlag = true; }
+                ~InPump() { mFlag = false; }
+            } inPump(mInPump);
+            const double t0 = emscripten_get_now();
+            if (mDeferredAt > 0)
+            {
+                // (the next turn's delay: from its post to this pump)
+                const double turn = t0 - mDeferredAt;
+                mDeferredAt = 0;
+                sOrthrosTurnMs.store(sOrthrosTurnMs.load() + turn);
+                if (turn > sOrthrosTurnMax.load()) sOrthrosTurnMax.store(turn);
+                ++sOrthrosTurnRuns;
+            }
+            ++sOrthrosPumps;
+            orthrosDrawThreadCounters().mPumpT0 = t0; // (this thread's own: the timeline)
+            osg::Object* parent = getParent();
+            osg::GraphicsContext* context = dynamic_cast<osg::GraphicsContext*>(parent);
+            osg::OperationQueue* queue = getOperationQueue();
+            bool drew = false, ran = false;
+            while (queue != nullptr)
+            {
+                osg::ref_ptr<osg::Operation> operation;
+                if (mGate.valid())
+                    operation.swap(mGate);
+                else
+                    operation = queue->getNextOperation(false);
+                if (!operation.valid())
+                    break;
+                if (OrthrosFrameGate* gate = dynamic_cast<OrthrosFrameGate*>(operation.get()))
+                {
+                    // (stopped here: the gate passed again at the next pump)
+                    if (drew || !gate->pass(context))
+                    {
+                        mGate = operation;
+                        break;
+                    }
+                    ran = true;
+                    continue;
+                }
+                (*operation)(parent);
+                ran = true;
+                if (dynamic_cast<OrthrosCountedSwap*>(operation.get()) != nullptr)
+                    drew = true;
+            }
+            if (!ran) ++sOrthrosEmptyPumps;
+            sOrthrosPumpMs.store(sOrthrosPumpMs.load() + (emscripten_get_now() - t0));
+            if (drew)
+                defer();
+        }
+
+    private:
+        void defer()
+        {
+            if (mDeferredAt == 0) mDeferredAt = emscripten_get_now();
+            orthros_drawthread_defer();
+        }
+
+        osg::ref_ptr<osg::Operation> mGate; // (the gate where the last pump stopped, passed first at the next)
+        bool mInPump = false;
+        double mDeferredAt = 0; // (the next turn's post, for its delay)
+    };
+
+    std::atomic<OrthrosGraphicsThread*> sOrthrosGraphicsThread{ nullptr };
+
+    void OrthrosEndOfDynamicDrawBlock::completed(osg::State* state)
+    {
+        OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+        {
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+            c.mCompletedAt = emscripten_get_now();
+            ++c.mCompletions;
+        }
+        osg::EndOfDynamicDrawBlock::completed(state);
+    }
+}
+
+// (the graphics thread, a task of its event loop: orthros_drawthread_event_setup's pump) its operations, until the gate
+// has nothing to do or one frame is swapped
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE void orthros_drawthread_pump()
+{
+    if (OrthrosGraphicsThread* thread = sOrthrosGraphicsThread.load())
+        thread->pump();
+}
+
+// (the page thread) the page showed (or dropped) the draw thread's frame: its gate looks again at the frame it holds back
+// (components/sdlutil/sdlgraphicswindow.cpp: Module.orthrosDrawThreadFrame calls it)
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE void orthros_drawthread_kick()
+{
+    OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+    {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+        c.mChanged.notify_all();
+    }
+    orthrosDrawThreadWake();
+}
+
+namespace osgViewer
+{
+    /// Orthros (drawthread.patch): 0 — no draw thread (SingleThreaded, the default); 1 — a draw thread whose WebGL
+    /// context is not made yet (no frame drawn, no job run: a page-thread wait for either would wait for ever); 2 — the
+    /// draw thread draws; 3 — its context could not be made, or it could not be woken. Any thread.
+    int orthrosDrawThreadState()
+    {
+        if (!sOrthrosDrawThreadInUse.load()) return 0;
+        if (sOrthrosContextFailed.load() || sOrthrosWakeFailed.load()) return 3;
+        return sOrthrosContextReady.load() ? 2 : 1;
+    }
+
+    /// Orthros (drawthread.patch): `job` run on the draw thread with its context current, between two frames' draws —
+    /// at once if it waits for a frame, else after the frame it draws. Only while orthrosDrawThreadState() is 2 (false
+    /// otherwise, `job` not queued). A caller that waits for its end says so (`wait`): it never waits for a frame, except
+    /// on the page thread between renderingTraversals' dispatch and the end of its culls (the graphics thread may then
+    /// wait for this thread's cull) — a waited job is refused there (false, not queued).
+    bool orthrosDrawThreadRun(osg::GraphicsOperation* job, bool wait)
+    {
+        if (job == nullptr || orthrosDrawThreadState() != 2) return false;
+        if (wait && tOrthrosInCull)
+        {
+            OSG_WARN << "Orthros: a draw-thread job waited for from inside the culls refused (it would never run)"
+                     << std::endl;
+            return false;
+        }
+        OrthrosDrawThreadCounters& c = orthrosDrawThreadCounters();
+        {
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+            c.mJobs.emplace_back(job);
+        }
+        c.mChanged.notify_all();
+        if (!orthrosDrawThreadWake())
+        {
+            // (the thread unreachable: the job taken back if it is still queued — its caller does not wait then)
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(c.mMutex);
+            for (auto it = c.mJobs.begin(); it != c.mJobs.end(); ++it)
+                if (it->get() == job)
+                {
+                    c.mJobs.erase(it);
+                    return false;
+                }
+        }
+        return true;
+    }
+}

+    // Orthros (orthros-r3.patch, drawthread.patch): the overlay texture `texture` (a WebGL name of the calling
+    // thread's context) read into `out` (width x height RGBA8, rows unpadded) through a framebuffer of its own, the
+    // previous bindings restored. 1 when read, 0 when this thread has no context, or no such texture, or the
+    // framebuffer was incomplete. (No comma outside parentheses in the JavaScript: the macro would split there.)
+    int orthrosReadOverlayTexture(unsigned int texture, int width, int height, void* out)
+    {
+        // clang-format off
+        return EM_ASM_INT({
+            var gl = GLctx;
+            var tex = GL.textures[$0];
+            if (!gl || !tex) return 0;
+            var read = gl.getParameter(gl.READ_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING);
+            var pack = gl.getParameter(gl.PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER_BINDING);
+            var fb = gl.createFramebuffer();
+            gl.bindFramebuffer(gl.READ_FRAMEBUFFER, fb);
+            gl.bindBuffer(gl.PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER, null);
+            gl.framebufferTexture2D(gl.READ_FRAMEBUFFER, gl.COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, gl.TEXTURE_2D, tex, 0);
+            var ok = gl.checkFramebufferStatus(gl.READ_FRAMEBUFFER) == gl.FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE;
+            if (ok)
+                gl.readPixels(0, 0, $1, $2, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, HEAPU8.subarray($3, $3 + $1 * $2 * 4));
+            gl.bindFramebuffer(gl.READ_FRAMEBUFFER, read);
+            gl.bindBuffer(gl.PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER, pack);
+            gl.deleteFramebuffer(fb);
+            return ok ? 1 : 0;
+        }, texture, width, height, static_cast<double>(reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(out)));
+        // clang-format on
+    }
+
+    /// Orthros (drawthread.patch, OPENMW_ORTHROS_DRAWTHREAD): the read above on the draw thread — its context owns
+    /// the texture (WebGL names are a thread's own) —, a job between two frames' draws (osgViewer::
+    /// orthrosDrawThreadRun: run after the frame in flight, never waiting for another); the page thread waits for it.
+    struct OrthrosReadOverlayOperation : public osg::GraphicsOperation
+    {
+        OrthrosReadOverlayOperation(osg::Texture2D* texture, int width, int height, osg::Image* image)

+            , mTexture(texture)
+            , mWidth(width)
+            , mHeight(height)

+        }

+        {
+            int ok = 0;
+            if (gc != nullptr && gc->getState() != nullptr)
+                if (osg::Texture::TextureObject* texture
+                    = mTexture->getTextureObject(gc->getState()->getContextID()))
+                    ok = orthrosReadOverlayTexture(texture->id(), mWidth, mHeight, mImage->data());
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+            mResult = ok;
+            mDone.notify_all();
+        }
+
+        /// 1 when read; 0 otherwise
+        int wait()
+        {
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+            mDone.wait(lock, [this] { return mResult >= 0; });
+            return mResult;
+        }

+        int mWidth, mHeight;

+// (the graphics thread) its context registered at the first call, then made current: 2 — the context made before
+// main() (wasm-build/orthros-gl.js: this worker's globalThis.__omwDrawThreadPrepared) —, 1 — one made now (no such
+// context: a worker's context waits for the page thread's event loop, the frames wait meanwhile:

+// glueOff: OPENMW_ORTHROS_GLGLUE=0 in the engine's environment (wasm-build/orthros-gl.js decides its glue from the JS
+// ENV at a realm's first registerContext, and a pthread's JS ENV is empty: the page's switch passed on here).
+EM_JS(int, orthros_drawthread_make_current, (double attrsJson, int width, int height, int discard, int glueOff), {
+    var s = globalThis.__omwDrawThreadGL;
+    if (!s) {
+        var attrs = {};

+        // a loss while no frame is dispatched is told at once; the check at each swap, orthros_drawthread_present,
+        // stays as a backstop. No preventDefault: that would let the browser restore the context, every GL object
+        // gone, and the thread draw on with it — a restore that happens anyway is told as the loss as well.)

+        // OSG's GLExtensions bridges on the context it was made on: OES_draw_buffers_indexed, GLctx.__omwDBI)
+        ['EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic', 'EXT_color_buffer_float', 'EXT_color_buffer_half_float',

+            var disable = gl.disable;

+        var told = false;
+        var crashed = function(what) {
+            if (told) return;
+            told = true;
+            try { self.postMessage({ cmd: 9, handler: 'orthrosDrawThreadCrashed', args: [String(what)] }); } catch (e) {}
+        };

+        s.crashed = crashed;
+        // (the worker's own error events, now that it returns to its event loop between frames: a crash only when
+        // the thread can no longer run — a wasm trap or abort (WebAssembly.RuntimeError), or anything before its pump
+        // is set up (its entry point). Anything else — a stray error or rejection from a browser API or Emscripten's
+        // glue between pumps — is logged, the session goes on.)

+            try { if (x instanceof WebAssembly.RuntimeError) return true; } catch (e) {}

+        };

+            if (fatal(x)) crashed(what);
+            else try { console.warn('[drawthread] an error on the draw worker, not a crash: ' + what); } catch (e) {}
+        };
+        self.addEventListener('error', function(e) { report(e && e.error, (e && (e.message || e.error)) || 'error'); });
+        self.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', function(e) { report(e && e.reason, (e && e.reason) || 'unhandled rejection'); });
+    }

+// (the graphics thread) the frame drawn handed to the page thread (shared: sOrthrosPresentShared's address; a bitmap
+// held while the page has not shown the previous one, replaced by a newer one, posted at the first swap after the page
+// showed it — or by the gate, osgViewer/ViewerBase.cpp, once the page woke it: s.flushHeld). The drawing buffer is
+// sized before each frame's draws (the gate: orthros_drawthread_resize), not here.
+EM_JS(void, orthros_drawthread_present, (double sharedAddress, int loseAt), {
+    var s = globalThis.__omwDrawThreadGL;
+    if (!s) return;
+    var shared = sharedAddress / 4;
+    var heap = function() {
+        var h = HEAP32;
+        try { if (wasmMemory.buffer !== h.buffer) h = new Int32Array(wasmMemory.buffer); } catch (e) {}
+        return h;
+    };
+    // (9: Emscripten 6.0.1's CMD_CALL_HANDLER, src/lib/libpthread.js: the page thread runs Module[handler](...args);
+    // checked when the page prepares this thread's worker, wasm-build/orthros-gl.js)
+    var post = function(bitmap, seq) {
+        Atomics.add(heap(), shared, 1);
+        s.posted++;
+        self.postMessage({ cmd: 9, handler: 'orthrosDrawThreadFrame', args: [bitmap, s.posted, s.dropped, seq] }, [bitmap]);
+    };
+    if (!s.flushHeld) {
+        s.flushHeld = function() {
+            var h = heap();
+            if (!s.held || Atomics.load(h, shared) > 0) return;
+            var bitmap = s.held, seq = s.heldSeq;
+            s.held = null;
+            Atomics.store(h, shared + 2, 0);
+            post(bitmap, seq);
+        };
+    }
+    if (loseAt > 0 && s.posted == loseAt && !s.lostOnPurpose) {
+        s.lostOnPurpose = true;
+        try { var x = s.gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context'); if (x) x.loseContext(); } catch (e) {}
+    }
+    // (a lost context told to the page at the first swap after — isContextLost read here, at each swap, as the
+    // canvas's webglcontextlost event waits for the end of this thread's task)
+    if (!s.lostTold && s.gl.isContextLost()) {
+        s.lostTold = true;
+        self.postMessage({ cmd: 9, handler: 'orthrosDrawThreadLost', args: [] });
+    }
+    var seq = ++s.swaps;
+    var h = heap();
+    Atomics.store(h, shared + 1, seq);
+    var bitmap = null;
+    try { bitmap = s.canvas.transferToImageBitmap(); } catch (e) {}
+    if (bitmap && s.held) { s.held.close(); s.held = null; s.dropped++; }
+    if (!bitmap) { bitmap = s.held || null; seq = s.heldSeq; s.held = null; }
+    if (bitmap && Atomics.load(h, shared) > 0) {
+        s.held = bitmap;
+        s.heldSeq = seq;
+        Atomics.store(h, shared + 2, 1);
+        return;
+    }
+    Atomics.store(h, shared + 2, 0);
+    if (bitmap) post(bitmap, seq);
+});

+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+// Orthros (screenshot.patch): WebGL2's readPixels accepts only GL_RGBA/GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE on a normalized colour buffer
+// (plus the one implementation-chosen pair of GL_IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_FORMAT/TYPE); another unsigned byte format
+// (GL_RGB: the screen capture handler of a window without alpha — F12 — or a RenderStage image attachment without a
+// format) fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and writes nothing, leaving the image's fresh allocation as it was (black, or
+// noise). Those formats are read as RGBA and converted; an image whose read fails is left zeroed (a failed WebGL read
+// writes nothing: the zeroing before it is enough, no glGetError — a synchronous call — on the plain RGBA reads).
+namespace
+{
+    // the bytes per pixel of an unsigned byte format converted from RGBA here, 0 if not converted
+    unsigned int orthrosChannelsFromRGBA(GLenum format)
+    {
+        switch (format)
+        {
+            case GL_RGB: case GL_BGR: return 3;
+            case GL_BGRA: return 4;
+            case GL_RED: case GL_ALPHA: return 1;
+#ifdef GL_RG
+            case GL_RG: return 2;
+#endif
+            default: return 0;
+        }
+    }
+
+    void orthrosConvertFromRGBA(GLenum format, const unsigned char* src, unsigned char* dst, int width)
+    {
+        for (int i = 0; i < width; ++i, src += 4)
+        {
+            switch (format)
+            {
+                case GL_RGB: *dst++ = src[0]; *dst++ = src[1]; *dst++ = src[2]; break;
+                case GL_BGR: *dst++ = src[2]; *dst++ = src[1]; *dst++ = src[0]; break;
+                case GL_BGRA: *dst++ = src[2]; *dst++ = src[1]; *dst++ = src[0]; *dst++ = src[3]; break;
+                case GL_RED: *dst++ = src[0]; break;
+                case GL_ALPHA: *dst++ = src[3]; break;
+                default: *dst++ = src[0]; *dst++ = src[1]; break; // (GL_RG)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+#endif

+// Orthros (tools/openmw/patches/orthros-r2.patch): the GLES rewriting of OpenMW's shaders without std::regex.
+// adjustSourceForGLES (shadermanager.cpp) ran about 40 std::regex constructions and passes over each merged shader
+// source, on the page's thread, whenever a shader variant was first asked for (a 213 ms frame measured for the rain's).
+// The same rewrites as plain scans, each giving the bytes its regex gave (tools/openmw/gles-rewrite-check.sh compares
+// them over every shader of the engine and generated sources): `\b` is a boundary between a word character
+// ([A-Za-z0-9_], the "C" locale's) and anything else, `\s` one of " \t\n\v\f\r".
+#ifndef OPENMW_COMPONENTS_SHADER_GLESREWRITE_H
+#define OPENMW_COMPONENTS_SHADER_GLESREWRITE_H
+
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+
+namespace Shader::GlesRewrite
+{
+    inline bool isWord(char c)
+    {
+        return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_';
+    }
+
+    inline bool isSpace(char c)
+    {
+        return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\n' || c == '\v' || c == '\f' || c == '\r';
+    }
+
+    inline std::size_t skipSpace(std::string_view s, std::size_t i)
+    {
+        while (i < s.size() && isSpace(s[i]))
+            ++i;
+        return i;
+    }
+
+    /// The end of a match starting at `at` (npos: none). `boundaryBefore`: `\b` before it.
+    template <class Matcher>
+    std::string replaceAll(const std::string& source, std::string_view first, bool boundaryBefore, Matcher matchRest,
+        std::string_view replacement, bool* found = nullptr)
+    {
+        std::string out;
+        std::size_t copied = 0, from = 0;
+        bool any = false;
+        while (true)
+        {
+            const std::size_t at = source.find(first, from);
+            if (at == std::string::npos)
+                break;
+            std::size_t end = std::string::npos;
+            if (!boundaryBefore || at == 0 || !isWord(source[at - 1]))
+                end = matchRest(std::string_view(source), at + first.size());
+            if (end == std::string::npos)
+            {
+                from = at + 1;
+                continue;
+            }
+            if (!any)
+                out.reserve(source.size() + source.size() / 8);
+            any = true;
+            out.append(source, copied, at - copied);
+            out.append(replacement);
+            copied = from = end;
+        }
+        if (found)
+            *found = any;
+        if (!any)
+            return source;
+        out.append(source, copied, std::string::npos);
+        return out;
+    }
+
+    /// `\bword\b` (a word of word characters) by `replacement`; `found`: whether there was one.
+    inline std::string replaceWord(
+        const std::string& source, std::string_view word, std::string_view replacement, bool* found = nullptr)
+    {
+        return replaceAll(
+            source, word, true,
+            [](std::string_view s, std::size_t i) { return i == s.size() || !isWord(s[i]) ? i : std::string::npos; },
+            replacement, found);
+    }
+
+    inline bool hasWord(const std::string& source, std::string_view word)
+    {
+        for (std::size_t at = source.find(word); at != std::string::npos; at = source.find(word, at + 1))
+        {
+            const std::size_t end = at + word.size();
+            if ((at == 0 || !isWord(source[at - 1])) && (end == source.size() || !isWord(source[end])))
+                return true;
+        }
+        return false;
+    }
+
+    /// `\bftransform\s*\(\s*\)`
+    inline std::string replaceFtransform(const std::string& source, std::string_view replacement)
+    {
+        return replaceAll(
+            source, "ftransform", true,
+            [](std::string_view s, std::size_t i) {
+                i = skipSpace(s, i);
+                if (i == s.size() || s[i] != '(')
+                    return std::string::npos;
+                i = skipSpace(s, i + 1);
+                if (i == s.size() || s[i] != ')')
+                    return std::string::npos;
+                return i + 1;
+            },
+            replacement);
+    }
+
+    /// `gl_TextureMatrix\[[0-9]+\]` (no boundary before)
+    inline std::string replaceTextureMatrix(const std::string& source, std::string_view replacement)
+    {
+        return replaceAll(
+            source, "gl_TextureMatrix[", false,
+            [](std::string_view s, std::size_t i) {
+                const std::size_t digits = i;
+                while (i < s.size() && s[i] >= '0' && s[i] <= '9')
+                    ++i;
+                if (i == digits || i == s.size() || s[i] != ']')
+                    return std::string::npos;
+                return i + 1;
+            },
+            replacement);
+    }
+
+    /// `\bstruct\s*\.\s*member\b` (gl_FrontMaterial.diffuse, gl_Fog . color)
+    inline std::string replaceMember(
+        const std::string& source, std::string_view structName, std::string_view member, std::string_view replacement)
+    {
+        return replaceAll(
+            source, structName, true,
+            [member](std::string_view s, std::size_t i) {
+                i = skipSpace(s, i);
+                if (i == s.size() || s[i] != '.')
+                    return std::string::npos;
+                i = skipSpace(s, i + 1);
+                if (s.substr(i, member.size()) != member)
+                    return std::string::npos;
+                i += member.size();
+                return i == s.size() || !isWord(s[i]) ? i : std::string::npos;
+            },
+            replacement);
+    }
+
+    /// A `$link` statement (what follows "$link" on its line) as the regex
+    /// `\s*"([^"]+)"\s*(if\s+(!)?\s*([_a-zA-Z0-9]+)?)?\s*` matched whole: false when it does not match.
+    inline bool parseLinkStatement(std::string_view s, std::string& target, bool& hasCondition, bool& negated,
+        std::string& conditionExpression)
+    {
+        std::size_t i = skipSpace(s, 0);
+        if (i == s.size() || s[i] != '"')
+            return false;
+        const std::size_t nameStart = ++i;
+        while (i < s.size() && s[i] != '"')
+            ++i;
+        if (i == s.size() || i == nameStart)
+            return false;
+        const std::string_view name = s.substr(nameStart, i - nameStart);
+        i = skipSpace(s, i + 1);
+        bool condition = false, bang = false;
+        std::string_view expression;
+        if (s.substr(i, 2) == "if" && i + 2 < s.size() && isSpace(s[i + 2]))
+        {
+            condition = true;
+            i = skipSpace(s, i + 2);
+            if (i < s.size() && s[i] == '!')
+            {
+                bang = true;
+                i = skipSpace(s, i + 1);
+            }
+            const std::size_t e = i;
+            while (i < s.size() && isWord(s[i]))
+                ++i;
+            expression = s.substr(e, i - e);
+            i = skipSpace(s, i);
+        }
+        if (i != s.size())
+            return false;
+        target = std::string(name);
+        hasCondition = condition;
+        negated = bang;
+        conditionExpression = std::string(expression);
+        return true;
+    }
+}
+
+#endif

+    void orthrosRunDebugAsks()

+// Orthros (orthros-r20.patch, JSPI): the engine's waits for the game's files suspend it (WebAssembly JSPI, -sJSPI,
+// link-openmw.sh) while the page fetches the bytes, instead of the page's thread spinning on shared memory (Orthros'
+// src/vfs/data-client.js fetchSync, wantWait): the page answers input, draws its own indicator and presents what the
+// engine drew so far. Linked after the system library (--js-library): fd_read and fd_sync replace libwasi's.
+//
+// Where it may suspend: only under the engine's promising exports — omw_pump_frame (a load's frame) and main() (the
+// boot) —, which say so (orthros_jspi_enter / orthros_jspi_leave, engine.cpp, main.cpp), one suspension at a time.
+// A frame of play is the plain export (omw_pump_frame_plain: the page's own stack, nothing suspends — as before r20);
+// the page pumps the promising one only for a load: one put off to the next frame by the engine (orthros_jspi_defer: a
+// save's load, a new game, the debug COE asked in a plain frame), or the frame of a loading screen still on. A load
+// that starts in a frame of play by itself — a door, an exterior crossing — runs synchronously there, as r16's. Why: a
+// frame in play gained nothing from suspending (docs/openmw.md), and a JSPI stack is exposed to Chromium's native stack
+// walker (base::debug::TraceStackFramePointers, its heap profiler's on a sampled allocation): from that stack's first
+// frame it scans 8 KB further for a frame pointer, past the stack's end — the renderer's crash (2026-10-29/30, the
+// kernel's log: the same instruction each time; at every run with the heap profiler forced on every renderer, never
+// with r16). The promising exports' stacks are made deep first (engine.cpp orthros_jspi_deep: 1,024 plain wasm frames
+// at their base), so that walker, which stops at 255 frames, never reaches the end. An import that suspends (WebAssembly.Suspending) throws SuspendError when called outside
+// a promising export even when it returns a value at once (V8, measured): the engine calls the suspending imports
+// (orthros_fd_read_async, orthros_fd_sync_async, Emscripten's emscripten_sleep — through engine.cpp's --wrap'd C
+// library functions —, present, breathe, settle, gl_settle, read_wait) only when orthros_jspi_may() says so (under a
+// promising export, not suspended), the plain ones otherwise (fd_read, fd_sync: as a build without JSPI).
+//
+// A read first waits a few ms on the page's thread (ENV OPENMW_ORTHROS_JSPI_SPIN_MS, 10 by default; play/index.html
+// ?jspispin=N): the page's store answers most of the boot's reads that fast, and a suspension costs a round of the
+// page's event loop each — the spike that suspended at once took 2 s more to the menu over ~1,700 store hits. That
+// short wait holds during the boot (main) and the engine's loads — its loading screen on (orthros_jspi_loading,
+// mwgui/loadingscreen.cpp: a save's load, a COE, a door, an exterior cell's) —, where the page's thread is what the
+// player has. In play, outside them, a read never suspends: it waits on the page's thread as before r20 (ENV
+// OPENMW_ORTHROS_JSPI_PLAY_SPIN_MS unset or negative; ?jspiplay=N: it may, after N ms there): a frame that suspends
+// presents nothing more meanwhile, and in play each suspension cost the frame its short wait, then the round to the page
+// and back, the page's thread having nothing to show for it — with 100 ms first, 2-3 of 3 measured minutes still had a
+// frame gap of 400-900 ms that r14's synchronous reads did not (2026-10-30, docs/openmw.md). A read
+// whose file is one the page streams (its node's `orthrosStreamed`: Orthros' src/vfs/emscripten-files.js, asyncReads)
+// asks `soon(position, length, spinMs)`: null when its bytes are in the page by then — read at once —, else a promise
+// the engine suspends on, the read itself then Emscripten's (doReadv: the page's pieces). The announced wait
+// (orthros_read_wait, components/vfs/manager.cpp orthrosReadWait) asks the page's globalThis.orthrosReadWaitSoon the
+// same way (its answer, or a promise of it), else calls orthrosReadWait as before — in play too, after the short wait: it
+// is a load's (a cell change's read-ahead comes before its loading screen). ENV OPENMW_ORTHROS_JSPI=0 (?jspi=0):
+// never suspends — every read as before r20. A build without JSPI (ASYNCIFY != 2) never returns a promise.
+//
+// A worker thread's read (Lua's update on its own thread, orthros-r14.patch: proxied to the page's thread) is the plain
+// fd_read, answered at once, synchronously, as before: the page's thread may serve it inside a wait for that very
+// thread (Worker::finishUpdate's futex wait runs the proxied calls), where no promise could settle — the read waits on
+// the page's thread when its bytes are missing (counted: proxied). Never a suspension there, never a deadlock.
+//
+// While the frame or the boot is suspended, nothing else enters the engine's state from the page: the page's calls
+// (Module._omw_*, Module._orthros_*, Module.ccall / cwrap's — but omw_save_settings, which reads no game file and
+// which the page's leaving persists at once after) and the engine's WebSocket events (multiplayer, MWMP::WebSocket:
+// "callbacks never interleave with a frame"; one whose socket was deleted or handler replaced by then dropped) are put
+// off, in order, to just after its end (a microtask once it returned: before any other task), 0 returned meanwhile
+// (Module.orthrosEngineBusy, Module.orthrosAfterEngine(fn)). Input events still reach SDL's queue at once (the html5
+// callbacks answer synchronously): the next frame reads them. The debug COE and teleport (engine.cpp) run at the next
+// frame's start, inside it.
+//
+// A loading screen's frame (orthros_jspi_present, mwgui/loadingscreen.cpp LoadingScreen::draw) is presented: the engine
+// suspends until the browser's next rendering update has run (a task posted from requestAnimationFrame: the engine

+//

 #include <osgUtil/TransformAttributeFunctor>
 
+#include <cmath>

 using namespace osgUtil;
 
+// Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_OSGFAST): Vec3f * Matrixd (Matrixd::preMult) divides every vertex by its w, the dot product
+// of the vertex with the matrix's last column. For an affine matrix -- last column exactly (0, 0, 0, 1), every
+// transform OpenMW's optimizer flattens -- and a finite vertex that w is exactly 1: each 0 * x is +-0, their sum +-0,
+// plus 1 is 1, and 1 / 1 is 1, so the multiply by it changes no bit either. The fast path skips those operations and
+// keeps the others in preMult's order, in double, with the same rounding to float: the same bits out. A vertex with a
+// NaN or infinite coordinate, or any other matrix, takes preMult as before. "0": preMult for every vertex.
+// The exactness needs IEEE arithmetic without contraction into fused multiply-adds (wasm has none outside
+// relaxed-simd) and a real std::isfinite: a build with -ffast-math / -ffinite-math-only keeps preMult always.
+#if defined(__FAST_MATH__) || defined(__FINITE_MATH_ONLY__) && __FINITE_MATH_ONLY__
+#define ORTHROS_OSGFAST_VERTICES 0
+#else
+#define ORTHROS_OSGFAST_VERTICES 1
+#endif
+static bool orthrosOsgFastEnabled()
+{
+    static const bool enabled = [] {
+        const char* value = getenv("OPENMW_ORTHROS_OSGFAST");
+        return !(value && strcmp(value, "0") == 0);
+    }();
+    return enabled;
+}

+        // Orthros (c4.patch): at most this many candidates for one levelled item list of a record, its nested lists'
+        // included (an AllLevels list at a high level would bring many meshes into the preload for one item shown),
+        // and at most this many lists visited for it (a list naming itself, or deeply nested ones, as mods may have).
+        constexpr std::size_t orthrosMaxItemCandidates = 4;
+        constexpr int orthrosMaxListVisits = 16;
+
+        // The items getLevelledItem may pick from this list at this level (as ContainerStore::addInitialItem draws a
+        // record's list: the highest level not above it, or every level not above it with AllLevels; nested lists
+        // followed) — the dice left out, a list that never gives anything (chance none 100) skipped — until `limit`
+        // items are listed or `visits` lists visited.
+        void orthrosItemCandidates(const ESM::ItemLevList& list, int level, const MWWorld::ESMStore& store,
+            std::vector<ESM::RefId>& items, std::size_t limit, int& visits)
+        {
+            if (--visits < 0 || list.mChanceNone >= 100)
+                return;
+            int highestLevel = 0;
+            for (const auto& item : list.mList)
+                if (item.mLevel > highestLevel && item.mLevel <= level)
+                    highestLevel = item.mLevel;
+            const bool allLevels = (list.mFlags & ESM::ItemLevList::AllLevels) != 0;
+            for (const auto& item : list.mList)
+            {
+                if (items.size() >= limit || visits <= 0)
+                    return;
+                if (level < item.mLevel || !(allLevels || item.mLevel == highestLevel))
+                    continue;
+                if (const ESM::ItemLevList* nested = store.get<ESM::ItemLevList>().search(item.mId))
+                    orthrosItemCandidates(*nested, level, store, items, limit, visits);
+                else
+                    items.push_back(item.mId);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    void orthrosCreatureRecordModels(const ESM::Creature& creature, const MWWorld::ESMStore& store,
+        std::vector<std::string_view>& shields, std::vector<std::string_view>* weapons)
+    {
+        if ((creature.mFlags & ESM::Creature::Weapon) == 0)
+            return;
+        const bool armed
+            = weapons != nullptr && (creature.mAiData.mServices & (ESM::NPC::Weapon | ESM::NPC::MagicItems)) == 0;
+        std::vector<ESM::RefId> items;

+                    shield = a;

+            }
+            if (!model.empty())

+    void LuaState::orthrosBuildCommon()
+    {

+    void LuaState::orthrosVerifyLoaded(
+        const sol::table& loaded, const std::map<std::string, sol::main_object>& packages, const std::string& envName)
+    {
+        // The previous code's table, rebuilt beside `loaded`: the same sets in the same order, with the previous
+        // code's own loader test made now; a loader's result is taken from `loaded` (a loader runs once per sandbox).
+        // Then both tables compared entry by entry (raw equality, both ways), and the kept common list checked against
+        // mCommonPackages (names, values, loader tests). So this checks the keys, the plain values and which packages
+        // are taken as loaders -- not a loader's result itself (a loader runs once): that, and the loaders' call order
+        // and arguments, are what the native harness (round 14, luainst.cpp) compares. Diagnosis only: it logs from
+        // the Lua thread; never in a measured run.
+        std::uint64_t diffs = 0;
+        auto differ = [&](const std::string& what) {
+            ++diffs;
+            Log(Debug::Error) << "Orthros: OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUAINST verify: " << envName << ": " << what;
+        };
+        if (!mOrthrosCommon)
+            orthrosBuildCommon(); // (dropped by an addCommonPackage during this sandbox's loaders)
+        const std::vector<OrthrosCommonPackage>& common = *mOrthrosCommon;
+        if (common.size() != mCommonPackages.size())
+            differ("common package count");
+        auto kept = common.begin();
+        for (const auto& [name, package] : mCommonPackages)
+        {
+            if (kept == common.end())
+                break;
+            const bool loader = package.is<sol::function>();
+            if (!kept->mKey.is<std::string>() || kept->mKey.as<std::string>() != name)
+                differ("common package name " + name);
+            if (loader != kept->mLoader.has_value())
+                differ("loader test of " + name);
+            kept->mValue.push();
+            package.push();
+            const bool sameValue = lua_rawequal(mSol.lua_state(), -1, -2) != 0;
+            lua_pop(mSol.lua_state(), 2);
+            if (!sameValue)
+                differ("common package value " + name);
+            ++kept;
+        }
+        sol::table reference(mSol, sol::create);
+        auto expected = [&](const std::string& name, const sol::object& package) -> sol::object {
+            if (package.is<sol::function>())
+                return loaded.raw_get<sol::object>(name);
+            return package;
+        };
+        for (const auto& [name, package] : mCommonPackages)
+            reference[name] = expected(name, package);
+        for (const auto& [name, package] : packages)
+            reference[name] = expected(name, package);
+        lua_State* L = mSol.lua_state();
+        std::uint64_t inReference = 0, inLoaded = 0;
+        auto count = [&](const sol::table& t, const sol::table& other, std::uint64_t& n, const char* side) {
+            t.push();
+            lua_pushnil(L);
+            while (lua_next(L, -2) != 0)
+            {
+                ++n;
+                other.push();
+                lua_pushvalue(L, -3);
+                lua_rawget(L, -2);
+                const bool same = lua_rawequal(L, -1, -3) != 0;
+                std::string key = lua_type(L, -4) == LUA_TSTRING ? lua_tostring(L, -4) : "(not a string)";
+                lua_pop(L, 3); // (other's value, other, the value: the key stays for lua_next)
+                if (!same)
+                    differ(std::string(side) + " entry " + key);
+            }
+            lua_pop(L, 1);
+        };
+        count(reference, loaded, inReference, "previous code's");
+        count(loaded, reference, inLoaded, "new");
+        if (inReference != inLoaded)
+            differ("entry counts");
+        ++mOrthrosVerifySandboxes;
+        mOrthrosVerifyEntries += inLoaded;
+        mOrthrosVerifyDiffs += diffs;
+        const std::uint64_t n = mOrthrosVerifySandboxes;
+        if (n <= 3 || n % 250 == 0 || diffs != 0)
+            Log(Debug::Info) << "Orthros: OPENMW_ORTHROS_LUAINST verify: " << n << " sandboxes, "
+                             << mOrthrosVerifyEntries << " entries compared, " << mOrthrosVerifyDiffs
+                             << " differences (last: " << envName << ", " << inLoaded << " entries)";
+    }

+        bool orthrosSameRef(const PagedCellRef& a, const PagedCellRef& b)
+        {
+            // (bits, not values: a NaN kept is the same NaN)
+            return a.mRefId == b.mRefId && a.mRefNum == b.mRefNum
+                && std::memcmp(a.mPosition.ptr(), b.mPosition.ptr(), sizeof(float) * 3) == 0
+                && std::memcmp(a.mRotation.ptr(), b.mRotation.ptr(), sizeof(float) * 3) == 0

+    struct ObjectPaging::OrthrosKeptRefs
+    {
+        using Refs = std::map<ESM::RefNum, PagedCellRef>;
+        static constexpr std::size_t kMaxChunks = 256;
+        static constexpr std::size_t kMaxRefs = 262144; // (about 25 MB at most)
+        struct Entry
+        {
+            Refs mRefs;
+            std::list<ChunkId>::iterator mOrder;
+            bool mFromFiles; // (listed by orthrosChunkFiles(), not chunkReady())
+        };
+        std::mutex mMutex;
+        std::map<ChunkId, Entry> mByChunk;
+        std::list<ChunkId> mOrder; // (oldest first)
+        std::size_t mRefs = 0;
+        std::uint64_t mKept = 0, mTaken = 0, mRead = 0, mDropped = 0, mChecked = 0, mCheckedFromFiles = 0,
+                      mDiffer = 0, mBuilds = 0;
+
+        void eraseLocked(std::map<ChunkId, Entry>::iterator it)
+        {
+            mRefs -= it->second.mRefs.size();
+            mOrder.erase(it->second.mOrder);
+            mByChunk.erase(it);
+        }
+
+        void keep(const ChunkId& id, Refs&& refs, bool fromFiles)
+        {
+            const std::lock_guard lock(mMutex);
+            if (const auto found = mByChunk.find(id); found != mByChunk.end())
+                eraseLocked(found); // (listed again: the same references, read anew)
+            if (refs.size() > kMaxRefs)
+            {
+                ++mDropped;
+                return;
+            }
+            while (!mOrder.empty() && (mByChunk.size() >= kMaxChunks || mRefs + refs.size() > kMaxRefs))
+            {
+                eraseLocked(mByChunk.find(mOrder.front()));
+                ++mDropped;
+            }
+            mOrder.push_back(id);
+            mRefs += refs.size();
+            mByChunk.emplace(id, Entry{ std::move(refs), std::prev(mOrder.end()), fromFiles });
+            ++mKept;
+        }
+
+        bool take(const ChunkId& id, Refs& refs, bool& fromFiles)
+        {
+            const std::lock_guard lock(mMutex);
+            const auto found = mByChunk.find(id);
+            if (found == mByChunk.end())
+            {
+                ++mRead;
+                return false;
+            }
+            fromFiles = found->second.mFromFiles;
+            Refs taken = std::move(found->second.mRefs);
+            found->second.mRefs = Refs();
+            mOrder.erase(found->second.mOrder);
+            mRefs -= taken.size();
+            mByChunk.erase(found);
+            refs = std::move(taken);
+            ++mTaken;
+            return true;
+        }
+
+        void check(const Refs& kept, const Refs& read, bool fromFiles)
+        {
+            const std::lock_guard lock(mMutex);
+            ++mChecked;
+            if (fromFiles)
+                ++mCheckedFromFiles;
+            bool same = kept.size() == read.size();
+            for (auto a = kept.begin(), b = read.begin(); same && a != kept.end(); ++a, ++b)
+                same = a->first == b->first && orthrosSameRef(a->second, b->second);
+            if (!same && ++mDiffer <= 5)
+                Log(Debug::Warning) << "Orthros: chunk references check: the references kept differ from those read ("
+                                    << kept.size() << " kept, " << read.size() << " read)";
+        }
+
+        void built()
+        {
+            const std::lock_guard lock(mMutex);
+            if (++mBuilds % 256 == 0)
+                Log(Debug::Info) << "Orthros: chunk references: " << mBuilds << " chunks built, " << mTaken
+                                 << " from their listing, " << mRead << " read, " << mKept << " kept, " << mDropped
+                                 << " dropped, " << mByChunk.size() << " held (" << mRefs << " references), "
+                                 << mChecked << " checked (" << mCheckedFromFiles << " listed by orthrosChunkFiles), "
+                                 << mDiffer << " different";
+        }
+
+        void clear()
+        {
+            const std::lock_guard lock(mMutex);
+            mByChunk.clear();
+            mOrder.clear();
+            mRefs = 0;
+        }
+    };

+// Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS, components/shader/shadermanager.cpp): a program compiled in play — by the
+// incremental compile operation or at a draw, after the first Finish pass and outside every pass — is reported to the
+// engine through this hook (set once by the engine), which learns it so that the next sessions make it before their
+// first loading screen and the passes compile it there. The hook runs on the GL thread before the compile.
+// Only a program's first link in play is reported: not a relink (a setGlobalDefines in play — a settings change —
+// re-sources every shader and every program drawn relinks; those were compiled before, they are not new materials),
+// and not a compile under a loading screen (an incremental compile operation's while a door's or a crossing's loading
+// screen is up: cheap there, and the loading screens' passes compile what is left anyway).
+namespace
+{
+    std::atomic<void (*)(const Program*)> orthrosLateCompileHook{ nullptr };
+    std::atomic<bool> orthrosFinishedOnce{ false };
+    // (GL thread: set while orthrosCompileUnlinkedPrograms compiles)
+    thread_local bool orthrosInPass = false;
+    // the frame number of the latest loading pass (a loading screen's frame) since the latest Finish pass; -2: none
+    std::atomic<long long> orthrosLoadingFrame{ -2 };
+
+    // (a loading screen up: a loading pass ran at this frame or the one before — a compile that runs before the pass
+    // in the frame is counted under the previous frame's — and no Finish pass since; a loading too short to show its
+    // screen runs no pass, and its window ends one frame after the last)
+    bool orthrosUnderLoading(const State& state)
+    {
+        const long long last = orthrosLoadingFrame.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const FrameStamp* stamp = state.getFrameStamp();
+        return last >= 0 && stamp && static_cast<long long>(stamp->getFrameNumber()) <= last + 1;
+    }
+
+    // (true the first time the program is compiled for a link, on any path; GL thread)
+    bool orthrosFirstLink(const Program* program)
+    {
+        OrthrosProgramRegistry& r = orthrosProgramRegistry();
+        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(r.mutex);
+        return r.linkedOnce.insert(program).second;
+    }

+namespace
+{
+    // Orthros (OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS; absent = on, 0 = off, off as well without OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE): the
+    // programs a session had to compile in play are made at the next sessions' start.
+    //
+    // A program made after the loading screens (a new material's define combination met by a cell or a distant chunk
+    // the cooperative preload builds while the player moves on) is compiled by the incremental compile operation or at
+    // its first draw: in a browser, reading its statuses waits for the GPU process to execute everything queued before
+    // them and then to compile it (120-270 ms on our SwiftShader server, where the GPU process is always a few frames
+    // behind, so no moment in play is cheap; WebGL there has no KHR_parallel_shader_compile, and a compile issued
+    // ahead is not started before its status is read). Its define combination cannot be told before its mesh is
+    // loaded, but it can be remembered: osg::Program::compileGLObjects reports each program linked for the first time
+    // in play (after the first loading screen's last pass, outside the passes, not under a loading screen, not a
+    // relink; orthrosOnLateCompile); a program ShaderManager made from a template with the default program template
+    // is identified by that template's name and its defines, one line in the page's localStorage (see below: the
+    // browser's, per origin, as the IndexedDB user config; not a file of the player's profile, so neither the
+    // account's copy of the profile, cloud.js, nor a profile backup ever sees it, and no sync is asked). At the next
+    // start the first setGlobalDefines (RenderingManager's constructor, before the
+    // first loading screen) makes each line's program through getProgram, the same call ShaderVisitor makes: the same
+    // shaders, sources and Program object the session would make later, made earlier; the loading screens' passes
+    // (OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE) then compile it, and the preload that meets the material later gets that program,
+    // already linked. Nothing drawn changes: no program, source or state is different, only when the compile is done.
+    // At most kMaxLines lines (the oldest dropped first); a line whose shaders cannot be made is dropped. Counters:
+    // globalThis.__omwLatePrograms.
+    constexpr std::size_t kMaxLines = 64;
+    // (the lines are kept in the page's localStorage under 'orthros.openmw.latePrograms.1' — written out in the two
+    // EM_ASM below, which stringify their code —: the lines, oldest first, each ended by '\n')
+
+    struct OrthrosLearnedPrograms
+    {
+        std::mutex mutex;
+        // the programs getProgram(templateName, defines) made with no program template: their line
+        std::unordered_map<const osg::Program*, std::string> lineOf;
+        // programs some caller asked for with its own program template: never learned
+        std::unordered_set<const osg::Program*> templated;
+        // the stored lines, oldest first, and the lines learned in play not stored yet
+        std::vector<std::string> lines, pending;
+        std::set<std::string> known;
+        std::atomic<bool> dirty{ false };
+        bool prepared = false;
+        // counters
+        int made = 0, failed = 0, late = 0, lateOther = 0, learned = 0, writes = 0;
+        double prepareMs = 0;
+    };
+
+    OrthrosLearnedPrograms& orthrosLearned()
+    {
+        // (never destroyed: programs may be compiled while statics are destroyed)
+        static OrthrosLearnedPrograms* learned = new OrthrosLearnedPrograms;
+        return *learned;
+    }
+
+    bool orthrosReadLateProgramsSwitch()
+    {
+        const char* value = getenv("OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS");
+        if (value && value[0] == '0' && value[1] == 0)
+        {
+            Log(Debug::Info) << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS=0: the programs compiled in play are neither learned nor made ahead";
+            return false;
+        }
+        if (!osg::orthrosPrecompileEnabled())
+        {
+            Log(Debug::Info) << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS off: it needs OPENMW_ORTHROS_PRECOMPILE";
+            return false;
+        }
+        return true;
+    }
+
+    bool orthrosLateProgramsEnabled()
+    {
+        static const bool enabled = orthrosReadLateProgramsSwitch();
+        return enabled;
+    }
+
+    bool orthrosLineSafe(std::string_view text, bool templateName)
+    {
+        if (text.empty())
+            return false;
+        for (char c : text)
+        {
+            const bool ok = templateName ? ((c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
+                                               || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '.' || c == '/')
+                                         : (c >= 0x20 && c < 0x7f && c != '=');
+            if (!ok)
+                return false;
+        }
+        return !templateName || (text.find("..") == std::string_view::npos && text.front() != '/');
+    }
+
+    // "<templateName>\t<define>=<value>\t..." in the DefineMap's order; empty: not representable
+    std::string orthrosLine(const std::string& templateName, const Shader::ShaderManager::DefineMap& defines)
+    {
+        if (!orthrosLineSafe(templateName, true))
+            return {};
+        std::string line = templateName;
+        for (const auto& [name, value] : defines)
+        {
+            if (!orthrosLineSafe(name, false) || (!value.empty() && !orthrosLineSafe(value, false)))
+                return {};
+            line += '\t';
+            line += name;
+            line += '=';
+            line += value;
+        }
+        return line;
+    }
+
+    bool orthrosParseLine(const std::string& line, std::string& templateName, Shader::ShaderManager::DefineMap& defines)
+    {
+        std::size_t start = 0, end = line.find('\t');
+        templateName = line.substr(0, end);
+        if (!orthrosLineSafe(templateName, true))
+            return false;
+        while (end != std::string::npos)
+        {
+            start = end + 1;
+            end = line.find('\t', start);
+            const std::string field = line.substr(start, end == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : end - start);
+            const std::size_t eq = field.find('=');
+            if (eq == std::string::npos || eq == 0)
+                return false;
+            defines[field.substr(0, eq)] = field.substr(eq + 1);
+        }
+        // (the canonical form only: what orthrosLine writes for these)
+        return orthrosLine(templateName, defines) == line;
+    }
+
+    // (the counters, copied under the mutex by the caller: the GL thread changes them, DRAWTHREAD)
+    struct OrthrosLearnedCounters
+    {
+        int lines, made, failed, late, lateOther, learned, writes;
+        double prepareMs;
+    };
+
+    OrthrosLearnedCounters orthrosCountersLocked(const OrthrosLearnedPrograms& l)
+    {
+        return { static_cast<int>(l.lines.size()), l.made, l.failed, l.late, l.lateOther, l.learned, l.writes,
+            l.prepareMs };
+    }
+
+    void orthrosPublishLearned(const OrthrosLearnedCounters& c)
+    {
+        // clang-format off
+        MAIN_THREAD_ASYNC_EM_ASM({
+            var p = globalThis.__omwLatePrograms || (globalThis.__omwLatePrograms = {});
+            p.lines = $0; p.made = $1; p.failed = $2; p.late = $3; p.lateOther = $4; p.learned = $5; p.writes = $6;
+            p.prepareMs = $7;
+        }, c.lines, c.made, c.failed, c.late, c.lateOther, c.learned, c.writes, c.prepareMs);
+        // clang-format on
+    }
+
+    // (osg::Program::compileGLObjects, GL thread: a program compiled in play)
+    void orthrosOnLateCompile(const osg::Program* program)
+    {
+        OrthrosLearnedPrograms& l = orthrosLearned();
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(l.mutex);
+        auto it = l.lineOf.find(program);
+        if (it == l.lineOf.end() || l.templated.count(program))
+        {
+            ++l.lateOther;
+            return;
+        }
+        ++l.late;
+        if (!l.known.insert(it->second).second)
+            return;
+        l.pending.push_back(it->second);
+        ++l.learned;
+        l.dirty.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
+    }
+
+    // (getProgram(templateName, defines, programTemplate): the line of a program made from a template)
+    void orthrosNoteProgram(const osg::Program* program, const std::string& templateName,
+        const Shader::ShaderManager::DefineMap& defines, bool withTemplate)
+    {
+        OrthrosLearnedPrograms& l = orthrosLearned();
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(l.mutex);
+        if (withTemplate)
+        {
+            l.templated.insert(program);
+            return;
+        }
+        if (l.lineOf.count(program))
+            return;
+        std::string line = orthrosLine(templateName, defines);
+        if (!line.empty())
+            l.lineOf.emplace(program, std::move(line));
+    }
+
+    // (ShaderManager::update, the engine's main thread: the lines learned since, stored; the text built under the
+    // mutex, stored after it — the GL thread's hook and getProgram's notes never wait on the page)
+    void orthrosWriteLearned(OrthrosLearnedPrograms& l)
+    {
+        std::string text;
+        OrthrosLearnedCounters counters;
+        {
+            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(l.mutex);
+            for (std::string& line : l.pending)
+                l.lines.push_back(std::move(line));
+            l.pending.clear();
+            while (l.lines.size() > kMaxLines)
+            {
+                l.known.erase(l.lines.front());
+                l.lines.erase(l.lines.begin());
+            }
+            for (const std::string& line : l.lines)
+            {
+                text += line;
+                text += '\n';
+            }
+            ++l.writes;
+            counters = orthrosCountersLocked(l);
+        }
+        // (a few KB at most, set once per program learned: rare. Synchronous, the text lives on this stack)
+        // clang-format off
+        const int stored = MAIN_THREAD_EM_ASM_INT({
+            try { localStorage.setItem('orthros.openmw.latePrograms.1', UTF8ToString($0)); return 1; } catch (e) { return 0; }
+        }, text.c_str());
+        // clang-format on
+        if (!stored)
+            Log(Debug::Warning) << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS: localStorage refused the learned programs";
+        orthrosPublishLearned(counters);
+    }
+
+    // (the stored lines; empty: none, or no localStorage)
+    std::string orthrosReadStored()
+    {
+        // clang-format off
+        char* text = static_cast<char*>(MAIN_THREAD_EM_ASM_PTR({
+            try { var t = localStorage.getItem('orthros.openmw.latePrograms.1'); return t ? stringToNewUTF8(t) : 0; }
+            catch (e) { return 0; }
+        }));
+        // clang-format on
+        if (!text)
+            return {};
+        std::string out(text);
+        std::free(text);
+        return out;
+    }
+
+    // (the first setGlobalDefines: every line's program made now, before the first loading screen)
+    void orthrosPrepareLearned(Shader::ShaderManager& manager)
+    {
+        OrthrosLearnedPrograms& l = orthrosLearned();
+        if (l.prepared)
+            return;
+        l.prepared = true;
+        const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        std::vector<std::string> lines;
+        {
+            std::istringstream in(orthrosReadStored());
+            std::string line;
+            std::set<std::string> seen;
+            while (std::getline(in, line))
+                if (!line.empty() && line[0] != '#' && seen.insert(line).second)
+                    lines.push_back(line);
+        }
+        std::vector<std::string> kept;
+        for (const std::string& line : lines)
+        {
+            std::string templateName;
+            Shader::ShaderManager::DefineMap defines;
+            bool ok = orthrosParseLine(line, templateName, defines);
+            if (ok)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    // (records the line itself, orthrosNoteProgram)
+                    ok = manager.getProgram(templateName, defines) != nullptr;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception& e)
+                {
+                    Log(Debug::Warning) << "OPENMW_ORTHROS_LATEPROGRAMS: " << templateName << ": " << e.what();
+                    ok = false;
+                }
+            }

+    void WorkQueue::runCooperative(double budgetMs)
+    {
+        if (!mCooperative)
+            return;
+        const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now()
+            + std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::steady_clock::duration>(
+                std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(budgetMs));
+        do
+        {
+            osg::ref_ptr<WorkItem> item;
+            {
+                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+                if (mQueue.empty())
+                    return;
+                item = std::move(mQueue.front());
+                mQueue.pop_front();
+            }
+            // (the item off the queue while it runs: its work may queue others, or wait for others, finishNow)
+            item->mCooperativeQueue = nullptr;
+            const bool done = item->doWorkSlice(deadline);
+            if (done)
+            {
+                item->signalDone();
+                continue;
+            }
+            // (part done: first again at the next frame, waitTillDone() still finishing it if asked)
+            item->mCooperativeQueue = this;
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+            mQueue.push_front(std::move(item));
+            return;
+        } while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline);
+    }
+
+    void WorkQueue::finishNow(WorkItem* item)
+    {
+        osg::ref_ptr<WorkItem> held(item);
+        {
+            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mMutex);
+            const auto found = std::find_if(
+                mQueue.begin(), mQueue.end(), [&](const osg::ref_ptr<WorkItem>& queued) { return queued == item; });
+            if (found == mQueue.end())
+                return;
+            mQueue.erase(found);
+        }
+        item->mCooperativeQueue = nullptr;
+        while (!item->doWorkSlice(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point::max()))
+        {
+        }
+        item->signalDone();
+    }

+        std::atomic<bool>& abort, Loading::Reporter& reporter, std::size_t& next,

+    {
+        // Orthros (orthros-r3.patch): preload() a few chunks at a time. `next`: 0 before the traversal, then 1 + the
+        // next entry to load.

+            if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() >= deadline)

+                break;
+        }
+        return next - 1 >= vd->getNumEntries() || abort;
+    }

+    bool SceneManager::orthrosTemplateReady(VFS::Path::NormalizedView path)
+    {
+        if (mCache->getRefFromObjectCache(path))
+            return true;
+        if (!mVFS->exists(path))
+            return true; // (the error marker: getTemplate's own answer)
+        if (!mVFS->orthrosDataReady(path))
+            return false;

+        if (path.extension() != nif)
+            return true;
+        Nif::NIFFilePtr file;
+        try
+        {
+            file = mNifFileManager->get(path);
+        }
+        catch (const std::exception&)
+        {
+            return true; // (getTemplate reports it)
+        }
+        // (every texture the file names, each asked: the missing ones all on their way at once)
+        bool ready = true;
+        for (const auto& record : file->mRecords)
+        {
+            if (!record || record->mRecordType != Nif::RC_NiSourceTexture)
+                continue;
+            const auto* texture = static_cast<const Nif::NiSourceTexture*>(record.get());
+            if (!texture->mExternal || texture->mFile.empty())
+                continue;
+            const VFS::Path::Normalized image
+                = Misc::ResourceHelpers::correctTexturePath(VFS::Path::toNormalized(texture->mFile), *mVFS);
+            if (!mImageManager->orthrosCached(image) && !mVFS->orthrosDataReady(image))
+                ready = false;
+        }
+        return ready;
+    }
