`tools/pe/priority.c`:

```c
// Test program: thread priorities. A THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL thread (an audio mixer's) wakes up and does work
// spanning several time slices while a normal-priority thread is ready (it spins): as on Windows, the normal thread
// does not run before the high-priority work is done — it never observes that work half done. Then a normal thread
// that waits for a lower-priority one with Sleep(0) still gets it to run (priorities do not starve it forever).
#include "win.h"

#define INFINITE 0xffffffff
#define THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL 15
#define THREAD_PRIORITY_IDLE (-15)
DLLIMPORT BOOL WINAPI SetThreadPriority(HANDLE, int);
DLLIMPORT DWORD WINAPI ResumeThread(HANDLE);
DLLIMPORT int WINAPI GetThreadPriority(HANDLE);

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static HANDLE out;
static void put(const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(out, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void putnum(unsigned v) {
  char buf[12]; int i = 11; buf[i] = 0;
  if (v == 0) buf[--i] = '0';
  while (v) { buf[--i] = '0' + v % 10; v /= 10; }
  put(buf + i);
}
static void report(const char* name, unsigned v) { put(name); put("="); putnum(v); put("\n"); }

static volatile int inWork, stop, spins, seenMidWork, workDone, idleRan;
static volatile unsigned sink;

static DWORD WINAPI mixer(void* p) {
  Sleep(10); // (the normal thread spins meanwhile)
  inWork = 1;
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 60000; i++) sink += i * 7; // (several time slices of work)
  inWork = 0;
  workDone = 1;
  return 0;
}
static DWORD WINAPI spinner(void* p) {
  while (!stop) { spins++; if (inWork) seenMidWork++; }
  return 0;
}
static DWORD WINAPI idler(void* p) { idleRan = 1; return 0; }

void __stdcall start(void) {
  out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  HANDLE s = CreateThread(0, 0, spinner, 0, 0, 0);
  HANDLE m = CreateThread(0, 0, mixer, 0, 0, 0);
  SetThreadPriority(m, THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL);
  WaitForSingleObject(m, INFINITE);
  stop = 1;
  WaitForSingleObject(s, INFINITE);
  report("work_done", workDone); report("spinner_ran", spins > 0); report("seen_mid_work", seenMidWork);
  // a lower-priority thread the main thread waits for by polling
  HANDLE i = CreateThread(0, 0, idler, 0, 4 /* CREATE_SUSPENDED */, 0);
  SetThreadPriority(i, THREAD_PRIORITY_IDLE);
  ResumeThread(i);
  unsigned polls = 0;
  while (!idleRan && polls < 10000000) { polls++; Sleep(0); }
  report("idle_ran", idleRan);
  // values outside the priority levels are rejected (THREAD_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN is accepted for the calling thread
  // without changing its level: stored, it would have outranked every thread)
  HANDLE self = (HANDLE)-2;
  int bad = SetThreadPriority(self, 99) || SetThreadPriority(self, -16) || !SetThreadPriority(self, 0x10000)
    || GetThreadPriority(self) != 0 || !SetThreadPriority(self, 0x20000) || !SetThreadPriority(self, 2) || GetThreadPriority(self) != 2;
  report("bad_levels_rejected", !bad);
  ExitProcess(seenMidWork || !workDone || !idleRan || bad ? 1 : 0);
}

```

`tools/pe/quartz.c`:

```c
// Test program: DirectShow movie playback through the filter graph manager (quartz.dll), as games play their movies:
// CoCreateInstance(CLSID_FilterGraph), IGraphBuilder::RenderFile, IVideoWindow over an owner window, IMediaControl::Run,
// the end reported through IMediaEventEx (event handle + GetEvent) and IMediaEvent::WaitForCompletion, IMediaSeeking.
// Files (C:\Test): movie.mpg (an MPEG-1 system stream), notmedia.bin (anything else).
#include "win.h"

typedef long HRESULT;
typedef struct { DWORD a; WORD b, c; BYTE d[8]; } GUID;
typedef long long LONGLONG;
#define VT(o) (*(void***)(o))
typedef HRESULT (WINAPI *F0)(void*);
typedef HRESULT (WINAPI *F1)(void*, DWORD);
typedef HRESULT (WINAPI *F2)(void*, DWORD, DWORD);
typedef HRESULT (WINAPI *F3)(void*, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD);
typedef HRESULT (WINAPI *F4)(void*, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD);
#define C0(o, i) ((F0)VT(o)[i])(o)
#define C1(o, i, a) ((F1)VT(o)[i])(o, (DWORD)(a))
#define C2(o, i, a, b) ((F2)VT(o)[i])(o, (DWORD)(a), (DWORD)(b))
#define C3(o, i, a, b, c) ((F3)VT(o)[i])(o, (DWORD)(a), (DWORD)(b), (DWORD)(c))
#define C4(o, i, a, b, c, d) ((F4)VT(o)[i])(o, (DWORD)(a), (DWORD)(b), (DWORD)(c), (DWORD)(d))
#define RELEASE(o) C0(o, 2)

DLLIMPORT HRESULT WINAPI CoInitialize(void*);
DLLIMPORT void WINAPI CoUninitialize(void);
DLLIMPORT HRESULT WINAPI CoCreateInstance(const GUID*, void*, DWORD, const GUID*, void**);

int _fltused = 1;
static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static HANDLE out;
static void put(const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(out, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void puthex(unsigned v) { char b[11] = "0x"; for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) b[2 + i] = "0123456789abcdef"[(v >> (28 - 4 * i)) & 15]; b[10] = 0; put(b); }
static void putnum(unsigned v) { char buf[12]; int i = 11; buf[i] = 0; if (v == 0) buf[--i] = '0'; while (v) { buf[--i] = '0' + v % 10; v /= 10; } put(buf + i); }
static void hex(const char* k, unsigned v) { put(k); put("="); puthex(v); put("\n"); }
static void num(const char* k, unsigned v) { put(k); put("="); putnum(v); put("\n"); }
static void pump(void) { MSG m; while (PeekMessageA(&m, 0, 0, 0, 1)) { TranslateMessage(&m); DispatchMessageA(&m); } }
static int notified;
#define WM_GRAPHNOTIFY 0x8001
static LRESULT WINAPI wndproc(HWND h, UINT m, WPARAM w, LPARAM l) { if (m == WM_GRAPHNOTIFY && l == 0x1234) notified++; return DefWindowProcA(h, m, w, l); }

#define G(a, b, c, d0, d1) { a, b, c, { d0 >> 8, d0 & 255, (d1 >> 40) & 255, (d1 >> 32) & 255, (d1 >> 24) & 255, (d1 >> 16) & 255, (d1 >> 8) & 255, d1 & 255 } }
static const GUID CLSID_FilterGraph = G(0xe436ebb3, 0x524f, 0x11ce, 0x9f53, 0x0020af0ba770LL);
static const GUID IID_IGraphBuilder = G(0x56a868a9, 0x0ad4, 0x11ce, 0xb03a, 0x0020af0ba770LL);
```

`tools/pe/seh.c`:

```c
// Test program: structured exception handling without a CRT (hand-rolled registration records),
// RaiseException, faults (division by zero, access violation), RtlUnwind, nested frames.
#include "win.h"
typedef struct _EXCEPTION_RECORD { DWORD ExceptionCode; DWORD ExceptionFlags; struct _EXCEPTION_RECORD* ExceptionRecord; void* ExceptionAddress; DWORD NumberParameters; DWORD ExceptionInformation[15]; } EXCEPTION_RECORD;
typedef struct { DWORD ContextFlags; DWORD Dr[6]; BYTE FloatSave[112]; DWORD SegGs, SegFs, SegEs, SegDs; DWORD Edi, Esi, Ebx, Edx, Ecx, Eax; DWORD Ebp, Eip, SegCs, EFlags, Esp, SegSs; } CONTEXT;
typedef struct _REG { struct _REG* prev; void* handler; DWORD code; DWORD hits; } REG;
DLLIMPORT void WINAPI RaiseException(DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, const DWORD*);
DLLIMPORT void WINAPI RtlUnwind(void*, void*, EXCEPTION_RECORD*, DWORD);

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static void put(HANDLE h, const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(h, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void puthex(HANDLE h, unsigned v) { char b[12]; b[0]='0'; b[1]='x'; for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) { unsigned d = (v >> (28 - 4 * i)) & 15; b[2 + i] = d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10; } b[10] = '\n'; b[11] = 0; put(h, b); }

static HANDLE out;
static volatile int marker = 0;

// Handler 1: records the code, skips the faulting instruction for #DE (continue execution)
static int __cdecl handler_skip(EXCEPTION_RECORD* rec, void* frame, CONTEXT* ctx, void* disp) {
  REG* r = (REG*)frame;
  if (rec->ExceptionFlags & 2) { r->hits += 100; return 1; } // unwinding
  r->code = rec->ExceptionCode; r->hits++;
  if (rec->ExceptionCode == 0xC0000094) { ctx->Eip += 2; ctx->Eax = 77; return 0; } // skip 'div ecx' (2 bytes)
  return 1; // continue search
}
static int __cdecl handler_search(EXCEPTION_RECORD* rec, void* frame, CONTEXT* ctx, void* disp) {
  REG* r = (REG*)frame;
  if (rec->ExceptionFlags & 2) { r->hits += 100; return 1; }
  r->code = rec->ExceptionCode; r->hits++;
  return 1;
}

// Handler 3: an execution fault (a call through a bad pointer): records the exception, resumes at the caller (the
// return address the call pushed)
static DWORD exec_code, exec_addr, exec_info1;
static int __cdecl handler_exec(EXCEPTION_RECORD* rec, void* frame, CONTEXT* ctx, void* disp) {
  if (rec->ExceptionFlags & 2) return 1;
  exec_code = rec->ExceptionCode; exec_addr = (DWORD)rec->ExceptionAddress; exec_info1 = rec->ExceptionInformation[1];
  ctx->Eip = *(DWORD*)ctx->Esp; ctx->Esp += 4;
  return 0;
}

// Handler 4: an exception raised while it runs (a nested dispatch): it installs a frame of its own, divides by zero
// (skipped by handler_skip, eax = 77), removes the frame, then continues the first exception with eax = 55
static void install(REG* r, void* handler);
static void uninstall(REG* r);
static DWORD nested_q, nested_code;
static int __cdecl handler_nested(EXCEPTION_RECORD* rec, void* frame, CONTEXT* ctx, void* disp) {
  if (rec->ExceptionFlags & 2) return 1;
  REG r2; install(&r2, handler_skip);
  unsigned q2;
  __asm__ volatile("xorl %%ecx, %%ecx; movl $10, %%eax; xorl %%edx, %%edx; divl %%ecx" : "=a"(q2) : : "ecx", "edx");
  uninstall(&r2);
  nested_q = q2; nested_code = r2.code;
  ctx->Eip += 2; ctx->Eax = 55;
  return 0;
}

// Handler 5: a data access in the null page (or past the user address space): records the exception and resumes after
// the faulting instruction (av_skip bytes, measured by the case)
static DWORD av_code, av_info0, av_info1, av_addr, av_ecx, av_faults, av_skip;
static int __cdecl handler_av(EXCEPTION_RECORD* rec, void* frame, CONTEXT* ctx, void* disp) {
  if (rec->ExceptionFlags & 2) return 1;
  av_code = rec->ExceptionCode; av_info0 = rec->ExceptionInformation[0]; av_info1 = rec->ExceptionInformation[1];
  av_addr = (DWORD)rec->ExceptionAddress == ctx->Eip ? ctx->Eip : 0; av_ecx = ctx->Ecx; av_faults++;
  ctx->Eip += av_skip;
  return 0;
}

static void install(REG* r, void* handler) {
  r->handler = handler; r->code = 0; r->hits = 0;
  __asm__ volatile("movl %%fs:0, %%eax; movl %%eax, (%0); movl %0, %%fs:0" : : "r"(r) : "eax", "memory");
}
static void uninstall(REG* r) { __asm__ volatile("movl (%0), %%eax; movl %%eax, %%fs:0" : : "r"(r) : "eax", "memory"); }

void __stdcall start(void) {
  out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  REG outer, inner;
  install(&outer, handler_search);
  install(&inner, handler_skip);
  // 1. division by zero, handled by the inner handler (continue execution with eax = 77)
  unsigned q;
  __asm__ volatile("xorl %%ecx, %%ecx; movl $10, %%eax; xorl %%edx, %%edx; divl %%ecx" : "=a"(q) : : "ecx", "edx");
  put(out, "div result "); puthex(out, q);
  put(out, "inner code "); puthex(out, inner.code);
  // 2. RaiseException with a custom code: inner returns search, outer returns search -> unhandled filter not set... use RtlUnwind from the outer? Instead test RaiseException with continuable flag handled via hits.
  // Both handlers continue search, so we need someone to handle it: register a third handler that unwinds.
  // 3. explicit RtlUnwind to `outer`: inner must receive an unwind notification (hits += 100) and be popped
  RtlUnwind(&outer, 0, 0, 0);
  put(out, "inner hits after unwind "); puthex(out, inner.hits);
  REG* top; __asm__ volatile("movl %%fs:0, %0" : "=r"(top));
  put(out, "top is outer "); puthex(out, top == &outer);
  uninstall(&outer);
  // 4. calls through bad pointers (null, past the address space, the last byte): access violations at the target
  REG ex; install(&ex, handler_exec);
  static const DWORD targets[3] = { 0, 0xfffffff0, 0xffffffff };
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    void (*volatile fp)(void) = (void (*)(void))targets[i];
    exec_code = 0; fp();
    put(out, "exec code "); puthex(out, exec_code); put(out, "exec addr "); puthex(out, exec_addr); put(out, "exec info "); puthex(out, exec_info1);
  }
  uninstall(&ex);
  // 5. nested dispatch: the handler of a division by zero raises and handles another one before continuing the first
  REG n; install(&n, handler_nested);
  unsigned qn;
  __asm__ volatile("xorl %%ecx, %%ecx; movl $10, %%eax; xorl %%edx, %%edx; divl %%ecx" : "=a"(qn) : : "ecx", "edx");
  uninstall(&n);
  put(out, "nested inner "); puthex(out, nested_q); put(out, "nested inner code "); puthex(out, nested_code); put(out, "nested outer "); puthex(out, qn);
  // 6. data accesses through null pointers: read, write, a call through a null vtable, a string copy from null, a
  // negative offset from null (past the user address space), and LEA (no access). Repeated so that the JIT translates
  // the code (the last round printed): each faults at the instruction (EIP and ExceptionAddress at its label, ECX as
  // before it) with [0 read / 1 write, address].
  REG av; install(&av, handler_av);
  DWORD at[6], ecxs[6], codes[6], i0[6], i1[6], pc[6], faults0 = 0;
  static DWORD buf[4];
  for (int round = 0; round < 300; round++) {
    DWORD e, x, y;
#define AV_BEGIN() av_code = 0; av_addr = 1; av_info0 = av_info1 = 0xeeeeeeee; e = 0
#define AV_END(k) codes[k] = av_code; i0[k] = av_info0; i1[k] = av_info1; pc[k] = av_addr; ecxs[k] = e
#define AV_ASM(text) "movl $2f-1f, %[skip]\n\tmovl $1f, %[at]\n1:\t" text "\n2:"
    AV_BEGIN(); __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("movl 8(%%ecx), %%eax") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[0]), "+c"(e), "=a"(x) : : "memory"); AV_END(0);
    AV_BEGIN(); __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("movl %%eax, 0x7ffc(%%ecx)") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[1]), "+c"(e) : "a"(5) : "memory"); AV_END(1);
    AV_BEGIN(); __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("call *0x10(%%ecx)") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[2]), "+c"(e) : : "eax", "edx", "memory"); AV_END(2);
    AV_BEGIN(); e = 4; __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("rep movsl") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[3]), "+c"(e), "=S"(x), "=D"(y) : "S"(0), "D"(buf) : "memory"); AV_END(3);
    AV_BEGIN(); __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("movl -4(%%ecx), %%eax") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[4]), "+c"(e), "=a"(x) : : "memory"); AV_END(4);
    AV_BEGIN(); __asm__ volatile(AV_ASM("leal 8(%%ecx), %%eax") : [skip] "=m"(av_skip), [at] "=m"(at[5]), "+c"(e), "=a"(x) : : "memory"); AV_END(5);
    if (round == 0) faults0 = av_faults;
  }
  uninstall(&av);
  for (int k = 0; k < 6; k++) {
    put(out, "av code "); puthex(out, codes[k]); put(out, "av info "); puthex(out, i0[k]); put(out, "av addr "); puthex(out, i1[k]);
    put(out, "av at insn "); puthex(out, codes[k] ? pc[k] == at[k] : pc[k]); put(out, "av ecx "); puthex(out, ecxs[k]);
  }
  put(out, "av faults "); puthex(out, av_faults); put(out, "av faults per round "); puthex(out, faults0);
  ExitProcess(q == 77 && inner.code == 0xC0000094 && inner.hits == 101 && top == &outer ? 0 : 1);
}
```

`tools/pe/sleepspin.c`:

```c
// Frame-limiter benchmark (tools/sleepspin-bench.mjs): the pacing loop many games run between frames — a little work,
// then Sleep(0) + timeGetTime until the next 16 ms boundary — under timeBeginPeriod(1), with a second thread polling
// with Sleep(1) as background threads do. The harness times the frames (GetVersion marks the end of a frame's work) and
// reads the emulator's Sleep counters and the process CPU time: the emulator's cost of the spin, which is pacing.
#include "win.h"

DLLIMPORT DWORD WINAPI timeGetTime(void);
DLLIMPORT UINT WINAPI timeBeginPeriod(UINT);
DLLIMPORT UINT WINAPI timeEndPeriod(UINT);
DLLIMPORT DWORD WINAPI GetVersion(void);

#define FRAMES 150
#define PERIOD 16

static volatile LONG stop;
static volatile DWORD polls;

static DWORD WINAPI poller(void* p) {
  (void)p;
  while (!stop) { Sleep(1); polls++; }
  return 0;
}

void __stdcall start(void) {
  volatile DWORD sink = 0;
  timeBeginPeriod(1);
  HANDLE th = CreateThread(0, 0, poller, 0, 0, 0);
  GetCommandLineA(); // mark: start
  DWORD next = timeGetTime();
  for (int f = 0; f < FRAMES; f++) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 200000; i++) sink += i ^ f; // the frame's work (well under the period)
    GetVersion(); // mark: the frame's work is done
    next += PERIOD;
    while ((LONG)(timeGetTime() - next) < 0) Sleep(0);
  }
  GetCommandLineA(); // mark: end
  stop = 1;
  WaitForSingleObject(th, 0xffffffff);
  timeEndPeriod(1);
  ExitProcess(polls > 0 ? 0 : 1);
}

```

`tools/pe/sleepspin_lower.c`:

```c
// Frame limiter beside a lower-priority busy thread (tests/sleep-throttle.test.js): the main thread paces 16 ms frames
// with Sleep(0) + timeGetTime as tools/pe/sleepspin.c does, while a THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL thread computes
// without ever waiting (a loader, a worker set below normal). Sleep(0) does not hand the processor to the lower thread
// (it only yields to equal or higher priorities); the emulator's Sleep(0) throttle must still recognise the spin, and
// the lower thread then runs during its 1 ms waits. Exit code 0 when the worker made progress during the frames.
#include "win.h"

DLLIMPORT DWORD WINAPI timeGetTime(void);
DLLIMPORT UINT WINAPI timeBeginPeriod(UINT);
DLLIMPORT UINT WINAPI timeEndPeriod(UINT);
DLLIMPORT DWORD WINAPI GetVersion(void);
DLLIMPORT BOOL WINAPI SetThreadPriority(HANDLE, int);

#define FRAMES 100
#define PERIOD 16

static volatile LONG stop;
static volatile DWORD work;

static DWORD WINAPI worker(void* p) {
  (void)p;
  while (!stop) { for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) work += (DWORD)i; } // (busy: no API call, no wait)
  return 0;
}

void __stdcall start(void) {
  volatile DWORD sink = 0;
  timeBeginPeriod(1);
  HANDLE th = CreateThread(0, 0, worker, 0, 0, 0);
  SetThreadPriority(th, -1); // THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL
  GetCommandLineA(); // mark: start
  DWORD next = timeGetTime();
  for (int f = 0; f < FRAMES; f++) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 200000; i++) sink += i ^ f; // the frame's work (well under the period)
    GetVersion(); // mark: the frame's work is done
    next += PERIOD;
    while ((LONG)(timeGetTime() - next) < 0) Sleep(0);
  }
  GetCommandLineA(); // mark: end
  DWORD done = work;
  stop = 1;
  WaitForSingleObject(th, 0xffffffff);
  timeEndPeriod(1);
  ExitProcess(done > 0 ? 0 : 1);
}
```

`tools/pe/sync.c`:

```c
// Test program: wait satisfaction semantics of the green-thread scheduler.
//  - a released mutex / left critical section goes to the parked waiter even when the releaser re-acquires
//    it immediately in a tight loop (Windows hands the object over at release time: no starvation),
//  - and never to two threads (no double ownership when the waiter runs later),
//  - an auto-reset event / a semaphore unit wakes exactly one waiter,
//  - the "wait until another thread holds the mutex" handshake: WaitForSingleObject(m, 1) times out while
//    the holder sleeps,
//  - a mutex owned by an exiting thread is reported abandoned to the next waiter.
#include "win.h"

#define WAIT_TIMEOUT 0x102
#define WAIT_ABANDONED 0x80
#define INFINITE 0xffffffff

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static HANDLE out;
static void put(const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(out, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void putnum(unsigned v) {
  char buf[12]; int i = 11; buf[i] = 0;
  if (v == 0) buf[--i] = '0';
  while (v) { buf[--i] = '0' + v % 10; v /= 10; }
  put(buf + i);
}
static void report(const char* name, unsigned v) { put(name); put("="); putnum(v); put("\n"); }

// ---- 1. mutex hand-off under a re-acquiring releaser, mutual exclusion
static HANDLE mtx;
static volatile int inside, violations, workerDone;
static DWORD WINAPI mutexWorker(void* p) {
  for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
    WaitForSingleObject(mtx, INFINITE);
    if (inside) violations++;
    inside = 1; Sleep(0); inside = 0;
    ReleaseMutex(mtx);
  }
  workerDone = 1;
  return 0;
}

// ---- 2. critical section hand-off
static unsigned char cs[24];
static volatile int csInside, csViolations, csDone;
static DWORD WINAPI csWorker(void* p) {
  for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
    EnterCriticalSection(cs);
    if (csInside) csViolations++;
    csInside = 1; Sleep(0); csInside = 0;
    LeaveCriticalSection(cs);
  }
  csDone = 1;
  return 0;
}

// ---- 3/4. one wake-up per auto-reset event signal / semaphore unit
static HANDLE ev, sem;
static LONG evWakes, semWakes;
static DWORD WINAPI evWaiter(void* p) { WaitForSingleObject(ev, INFINITE); InterlockedIncrement(&evWakes); return 0; }
static DWORD WINAPI semWaiter(void* p) { WaitForSingleObject(sem, INFINITE); InterlockedIncrement(&semWakes); return 0; }

// ---- 5. handshake: A signals "worker alive" by being held, B (owned by main) signals "stop" when released
static HANDLE mA, mB;
static DWORD WINAPI aliveWorker(void* p) {
  WaitForSingleObject(mA, INFINITE);
  for (;;) { Sleep(5); if (WaitForSingleObject(mB, 0) != WAIT_TIMEOUT) break; }
  ReleaseMutex(mB);
  ReleaseMutex(mA);
  return 0;
}

// ---- 6. abandonment
static HANDLE mX;
static DWORD WINAPI abandoner(void* p) { WaitForSingleObject(mX, INFINITE); return 0; }

void __stdcall start(void) {
  out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  int fails = 0;

  mtx = CreateMutexA(0, 0, 0);
  HANDLE t = CreateThread(0, 0, mutexWorker, 0, 0, 0);
  unsigned spins = 0, releaseFailures = 0;
  while (!workerDone && spins < 5000000) { spins++; WaitForSingleObject(mtx, INFINITE); if (!ReleaseMutex(mtx)) releaseFailures++; }
  DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(t, 5000);
  report("mutex_handoff", workerDone); report("mutex_join", r); report("mutex_violations", violations); report("mutex_release_failures", releaseFailures);
  if (!workerDone || r != 0 || violations || releaseFailures) fails++;

  InitializeCriticalSection(cs);
  t = CreateThread(0, 0, csWorker, 0, 0, 0);
  spins = 0;
  while (!csDone && spins < 5000000) { spins++; EnterCriticalSection(cs); LeaveCriticalSection(cs); }
  r = WaitForSingleObject(t, 5000);
  report("cs_handoff", csDone); report("cs_join", r); report("cs_violations", csViolations);
  if (!csDone || r != 0 || csViolations) fails++;

  ev = CreateEventA(0, 0, 0, 0);
  HANDLE e1 = CreateThread(0, 0, evWaiter, 0, 0, 0), e2 = CreateThread(0, 0, evWaiter, 0, 0, 0);
  Sleep(10);
  SetEvent(ev); Sleep(20); LONG w1 = evWakes;
  SetEvent(ev); Sleep(20); LONG w2 = evWakes;
  WaitForSingleObject(e1, 5000); WaitForSingleObject(e2, 5000);
  report("event_first", w1); report("event_second", w2);
  if (w1 != 1 || w2 != 2) fails++;

  sem = CreateSemaphoreA(0, 0, 10, 0);
  HANDLE s1 = CreateThread(0, 0, semWaiter, 0, 0, 0), s2 = CreateThread(0, 0, semWaiter, 0, 0, 0);
  Sleep(10);
  ReleaseSemaphore(sem, 1, 0); Sleep(20); LONG sw1 = semWakes;
  ReleaseSemaphore(sem, 1, 0); Sleep(20); LONG sw2 = semWakes;
  WaitForSingleObject(s1, 5000); WaitForSingleObject(s2, 5000);
  report("sem_first", sw1); report("sem_second", sw2);
  if (sw1 != 1 || sw2 != 2) fails++;

  mA = CreateMutexA(0, 0, 0);
  mB = CreateMutexA(0, 1, 0);
  t = CreateThread(0, 0, aliveWorker, 0, 0, 0);
  unsigned iters = 0; // (the worker runs once main has used its quantum: a few million fast iterations at most)
  for (;;) {
    r = WaitForSingleObject(mA, 1);
    iters++;
    if (r == 0) { ReleaseMutex(mA); if (iters > 5000000) break; continue; }
    if (r != WAIT_TIMEOUT) continue;
    break;
  }
  report("handshake", r == WAIT_TIMEOUT); report("handshake_bounded", iters <= 5000000);
  ReleaseMutex(mB);
  DWORD j = WaitForSingleObject(t, 5000);
  DWORD a = WaitForSingleObject(mA, 0);
  report("handshake_join", j); report("handshake_A_free", a);
  if (r != WAIT_TIMEOUT || j != 0 || a != 0) fails++;

  mX = CreateMutexA(0, 0, 0);
  t = CreateThread(0, 0, abandoner, 0, 0, 0);
  WaitForSingleObject(t, 5000);
  DWORD ab = WaitForSingleObject(mX, 1000);
  report("abandoned", ab);
  if (ab != WAIT_ABANDONED) fails++;

  ExitProcess(fails);
}
```

`tools/pe/syncstress.c`:

```c
// Test program: synchronization and shared file objects under every interleaving the scheduler can produce. Several
// threads hammer a critical section, a mutex (infinite and timed waits), an InterlockedExchange spin lock and one file
// object they read without any lock of their own (Windows reads and advances a synchronous handle's file pointer
// atomically: every 4-byte record of the file is read exactly once in all). Inside the locked sections the threads
// yield (Sleep(0), Sleep(1)) and read a network-backed file whose data may arrive asynchronously (the reading thread
// parks). Reports mutual-exclusion violations, lost or duplicated records, wrong record contents and counter totals.
#include "win.h"

#define WAIT_TIMEOUT 0x102
#define WAIT_ABANDONED 0x80
#define INFINITE 0xffffffff
#define THREADS 4
#define ITERS 300
#define RECORDS 4096

DLLIMPORT LONG WINAPI InterlockedExchange(LONG*, LONG);
DLLIMPORT BOOL WINAPI EnumWindows(BOOL (WINAPI*)(HWND, LPARAM), LPARAM);

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static HANDLE out;
static void put(const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(out, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void putnum(unsigned v) {
  char buf[12]; int i = 11; buf[i] = 0;
  if (v == 0) buf[--i] = '0';
  while (v) { buf[--i] = '0' + v % 10; v /= 10; }
  put(buf + i);
}
static void report(const char* name, unsigned v) { put(name); put("="); putnum(v); put("\n"); }

static unsigned char cs[24];
static HANDLE mtx, shared, net[3];
static volatile LONG spin;
static volatile int csInside, mxInside, spInside;
static volatile LONG csViol, mxViol, spViol, csCount, mxCount, spCount, timeouts, badData, readFails;
static unsigned char seen[RECORDS];
static volatile LONG recordsRead;

static unsigned rnd(unsigned* s) { *s = *s * 1103515245u + 12345u; return (*s >> 16) & 0x7fff; }

/** something that lets the other threads run inside a locked section: a yield, a sleep, a read that may park */
static void pause(unsigned* s, int lock) {
  unsigned k = rnd(s) % 6;
  if (k == 0) Sleep(0);
  else if (k == 1) Sleep(1);
  else if (k == 2) { // a read of the network file at a position of its own (an explicit seek under the lock: one file
    // object per lock)
    unsigned rec = rnd(s) % 32768; unsigned v = 0; DWORD got = 0;
    SetFilePointer(net[lock], rec * 4, 0, 0);
    if (!ReadFile(net[lock], &v, 4, &got, 0) || got != 4) readFails++;
    else if (v != rec * 2654435761u) badData++;
  }
}

/** the shared file object read without a lock: each record exactly once over all threads */
static void readShared(void) {
  unsigned v = 0; DWORD got = 0;
  if (!ReadFile(shared, &v, 4, &got, 0)) { readFails++; return; }
  if (got != 4) return; // (end of file)
  unsigned rec = v ^ 0x5a5a0000u;
  if (rec >= RECORDS) { badData++; return; }
  if (seen[rec]++) badData++;
  InterlockedIncrement((LONG*)&recordsRead);
}

static DWORD WINAPI worker(void* p) {
  unsigned s = (unsigned)(DWORD)p * 7919u + 17u;
  for (int i = 0; i < ITERS; i++) {
    EnterCriticalSection(cs);
    if (csInside) csViol++;
    csInside = 1; pause(&s, 0); csCount++; csInside = 0;
    LeaveCriticalSection(cs);

    DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(mtx, rnd(&s) % 3 ? INFINITE : rnd(&s) % 4);
    if (r == 0 || r == WAIT_ABANDONED) {
      if (mxInside) mxViol++;
      mxInside = 1; pause(&s, 1); mxCount++; mxInside = 0;
      ReleaseMutex(mtx);
    } else if (r == WAIT_TIMEOUT) InterlockedIncrement((LONG*)&timeouts);
    else readFails++;

    while (InterlockedExchange((LONG*)&spin, 1)) Sleep(rnd(&s) & 1);
    if (spInside) spViol++;
    spInside = 1; pause(&s, 2); spCount++; spInside = 0;
    InterlockedExchange((LONG*)&spin, 0);

    readShared(); readShared();
    if (rnd(&s) % 4 == 0) { unsigned k = rnd(&s) & 1; Sleep(k); }
  }
  return 0;
}

// an API callback (EnumWindows calls it from its handler) making API calls of its own and letting the other threads run:
// the handler's own arguments (callback, lParam) must still be its own when the callback returns
static volatile LONG enumCalls, enumBadParam;
static BOOL WINAPI enumProc(HWND h, LPARAM l) {
  if (l != 0x1234) enumBadParam++;
  enumCalls++;
  Sleep(0); Sleep(1); SetLastError(0);
  return 1;
}
static LRESULT WINAPI wndproc(HWND h, UINT m, WPARAM w, LPARAM l) { return DefWindowProcA(h, m, w, l); }

void __stdcall start(void) {
  out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  InitializeCriticalSection(cs);
  mtx = CreateMutexA(0, 0, 0);
  shared = CreateFileA("C:\\Net\\records.bin", 0x80000000, 1, 0, 3, 0, 0);
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) net[i] = CreateFileA("C:\\Net\\random.bin", 0x80000000, 1, 0, 3, 0, 0);
  if (shared == (HANDLE)-1 || net[0] == (HANDLE)-1 || net[2] == (HANDLE)-1) { put("open failed\n"); ExitProcess(99); }
  HANDLE t[THREADS];
  for (int i = 0; i < THREADS; i++) t[i] = CreateThread(0, 0, worker, (void*)(DWORD)i, 0, 0);
  for (int i = 0; i < THREADS; i++) WaitForSingleObject(t[i], INFINITE);
  WNDCLASSA wc = {0};
  wc.lpfnWndProc = wndproc; wc.hInstance = GetModuleHandleA(0); wc.lpszClassName = "syncstress";
  RegisterClassA(&wc);
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) CreateWindowExA(0, "syncstress", "syncstress", 0, 0, 0, 100, 100, 0, 0, wc.hInstance, 0);
  HANDLE e = CreateThread(0, 0, worker, (void*)7, 0, 0); // (runs while the callbacks wait)
  EnumWindows(enumProc, 0x1234);
  WaitForSingleObject(e, INFINITE);
  report("enum_calls", enumCalls); report("enum_bad_param", enumBadParam);
  report("cs_violations", csViol); report("mutex_violations", mxViol); report("spin_violations", spViol);
  report("cs_count", csCount); report("spin_count", spCount);
  report("mutex_plus_timeouts", mxCount + timeouts);
  report("records_read", recordsRead); report("bad_data", badData); report("read_failures", readFails);
  ExitProcess(csViol + mxViol + spViol + badData + readFails + enumBadParam + (enumCalls < 3));
}
```

```c
// Test program: GDI text with an outline font — metrics, extents, per-character widths, antialiased TextOut into
// a 32 bpp DIB section, DrawText word wrapping. Prints key=value lines checked by tests/browser.test.js.
#include "win.h"

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static void put(HANDLE h, const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(h, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void putnum(HANDLE h, int v) { char buf[12]; int i = 11, neg = v < 0; unsigned u = neg ? -v : v; buf[i] = 0; if (u == 0) buf[--i] = '0'; while (u) { buf[--i] = '0' + u % 10; u /= 10; } if (neg) buf[--i] = '-'; put(h, buf + i); }
static void line(HANDLE h, const char* k, int v) { put(h, k); put(h, "="); putnum(h, v); put(h, "\n"); }

void start(void) {
  HANDLE out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  HDC dc = CreateCompatibleDC(0);
  BITMAPINFO bi = { { sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER), 256, -64, 1, 32, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 }, { 0 } };
  unsigned* bits = 0;
  HBITMAP bm = CreateDIBSection(dc, &bi, 0, (void**)&bits, 0, 0);
  SelectObject(dc, bm);
  for (int i = 0; i < 256 * 64; i++) bits[i] = 0x00ffffff;
  HFONT f = CreateFontA(-20, 0, 0, 0, 400, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4 /* ANTIALIASED_QUALITY */, 0, "Arial");
  SelectObject(dc, f);
  TEXTMETRICA tm; GetTextMetricsA(dc, &tm);
  line(out, "tm_height", tm.tmHeight); line(out, "tm_ascent", tm.tmAscent); line(out, "tm_descent", tm.tmDescent);
  line(out, "tm_internal", tm.tmInternalLeading); line(out, "tm_ave", tm.tmAveCharWidth); line(out, "tm_pitch", tm.tmPitchAndFamily);
  SIZE sz; GetTextExtentPoint32A(dc, "Hello, World", 12, &sz);
  line(out, "extent_cx", sz.cx); line(out, "extent_cy", sz.cy);
  int wi = 0, ww = 0; GetCharWidth32A(dc, 'i', 'i', &wi); GetCharWidth32A(dc, 'W', 'W', &ww);
  line(out, "width_i", wi); line(out, "width_W", ww);
  SetTextColor(dc, 0); SetBkMode(dc, 1 /* TRANSPARENT */);
  TextOutA(dc, 4, 4, "Hello, World", 12);
  int black = 0, gray = 0, right = 0;
  for (int y = 0; y < 64; y++) for (int x = 0; x < 256; x++) { unsigned p = bits[y * 256 + x] & 0xffffff; if (p == 0) black++; else if (p != 0xffffff) gray++; if (p != 0xffffff && x > right) right = x; }
  line(out, "px_black", black); line(out, "px_gray", gray); line(out, "px_right", right);
  RECT r = { 0, 0, 60, 0 };
  int h = DrawTextA(dc, "one two three four", -1, &r, 0x400 /* DT_CALCRECT */ | 0x10 /* DT_WORDBREAK */);
  line(out, "drawtext_h", h); line(out, "drawtext_w", r.right - r.left);
  ExitProcess(0);
}
```

`tools/pe/threads.c`:

```c
// Test program: threads, critical sections, events, waits (exercises the green-thread scheduler).
#include "win.h"

static int counter = 0;
static unsigned char cs[24];
static HANDLE evDone;
static LONG finished = 0;

static DWORD WINAPI worker(void* param) {
  int id = (int)param;
  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
    EnterCriticalSection(cs);
    counter++;
    LeaveCriticalSection(cs);
    if ((i & 63) == 0) Sleep(0);
  }
  if (InterlockedIncrement(&finished) == 2) SetEvent(evDone);
  return 100 + id;
}

static int slen(const char* s) { int n = 0; while (s[n]) n++; return n; }
static void put(HANDLE h, const char* s) { DWORD w; WriteFile(h, s, slen(s), &w, 0); }
static void putnum(HANDLE h, unsigned v) {
  char buf[12]; int i = 11; buf[i] = 0;
  if (v == 0) buf[--i] = '0';
  while (v) { buf[--i] = '0' + v % 10; v /= 10; }
  put(h, buf + i);
}

void __stdcall start(void) {
  HANDLE out = GetStdHandle((DWORD)-11);
  InitializeCriticalSection(cs);
  evDone = CreateEventA(0, 1, 0, 0);
  DWORD tid1, tid2;
  HANDLE t1 = CreateThread(0, 0, worker, (void*)1, 0, &tid1);
  HANDLE t2 = CreateThread(0, 0, worker, (void*)2, 0, &tid2);
  DWORD start = GetTickCount();
  Sleep(30);
  DWORD elapsed = GetTickCount() - start;
  DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(evDone, 5000);
  WaitForSingleObject(t1, 5000);
  WaitForSingleObject(t2, 5000);
  put(out, "counter="); putnum(out, counter); put(out, "\n");
  put(out, "wait="); putnum(out, r); put(out, "\n");
  put(out, "slept ok="); putnum(out, elapsed >= 30 ? 1 : 0); put(out, "\n");
  put(out, "tids differ="); putnum(out, tid1 != tid2 && tid1 != GetCurrentThreadId() ? 1 : 0); put(out, "\n");
  DeleteCriticalSection(cs);
  ExitProcess(counter == 2000 ? 0 : 1);
}
```

```c
// Test program: a GDI window with a paint handler, timers, GetPixel readback, message loop.
#include "win.h"

#define WM_CREATE 1
#define WM_DESTROY 2
#define WM_PAINT 0xF
#define WM_TIMER 0x113
#define WM_KEYDOWN 0x100
#define WM_LBUTTONDOWN 0x201

static int paints = 0, timers = 0, result = 0, keys = 0, clicks = 0;

static LRESULT WINAPI wndproc(HWND h, UINT m, WPARAM w, LPARAM l) {
  switch (m) {
    case WM_CREATE:
      SetTimer(h, 1, 20, 0);
      return 0;
    case WM_PAINT: {
      PAINTSTRUCT ps;
      HDC dc = BeginPaint(h, &ps);
      RECT r = { 10, 10, 110, 60 };
      HBRUSH b = CreateSolidBrush(0x000000FF); // COLORREF red
      FillRect(dc, &r, b);
      DeleteObject(b);
      SetPixel(dc, 200, 100, 0x00FF0000); // blue
      TextOutA(dc, 20, 100, "Orthros", 7);
      paints++;
      EndPaint(h, &ps);
      return 0;
    }
    case WM_KEYDOWN: keys += (int)w; return 0;
    case WM_LBUTTONDOWN: clicks += (int)(l & 0xffff) + (int)(l >> 16); return 0;
    case WM_TIMER:
      timers++;
      if (timers == 3) {
        HDC dc = GetDC(h);
        COLORREF c1 = GetPixel(dc, 50, 30);
        COLORREF c2 = GetPixel(dc, 200, 100);
        ReleaseDC(h, dc);
        result = (c1 == 0x000000FF && c2 == 0x00FF0000) ? 7 : 1;
        InvalidateRect(h, 0, 0);
      }
      if (timers == 6) DestroyWindow(h);
      return 0;
    case WM_DESTROY:
      PostQuitMessage(result + paints * 10 + keys * 1000 + clicks * 100000);
      return 0;
  }
  return DefWindowProcA(h, m, w, l);
}

void __stdcall start(void) {
  WNDCLASSA wc;
  wc.style = 3; wc.lpfnWndProc = wndproc; wc.cbClsExtra = 0; wc.cbWndExtra = 0; wc.hInstance = GetModuleHandleA(0);
  wc.hIcon = 0; wc.hCursor = LoadCursorA(0, (const char*)32512); wc.hbrBackground = (HBRUSH)(1 + 5); // COLOR_WINDOW+1
  wc.lpszMenuName = 0; wc.lpszClassName = "OrthrosTest";
  if (!RegisterClassA(&wc)) ExitProcess(200);
  HWND h = CreateWindowExA(0, "OrthrosTest", "Orthros test window", 0x00CF0000 | 0x10000000, 100, 100, 320, 240, 0, 0, wc.hInstance, 0);
  if (!h) ExitProcess(201);
  UpdateWindow(h);
  MSG msg;
  while (GetMessageA(&msg, 0, 0, 0)) {
    TranslateMessage(&msg);
    DispatchMessageA(&msg);
  }
  ExitProcess((UINT)msg.wParam);
}
```

`tools/port-perf.mjs`:

```mjs
// The browser ports' frame measurement, one for every port tool (tools/re3/perf.mjs, tools/goldsrc/perf.mjs, the
// ports' checks): the browser's launch flags for a rendering mode, a probe installed before the page's scripts (the
// engine's work a frame, the frames shown, the WebGL calls a frame by kind, the synchronous ones apart, the WebGL
// renderer), its reading, and a CPU profile's summary (self time, the longest busy stretches).
//
// Rendering modes (--gl): headless Chromium here always renders WebGL with SwiftShader (ANGLE's null backend,
// --use-angle=null, is ignored: the renderer string stays SwiftShader's with every flag combination — checked
// 2026-10-21), so a frame's time includes the CPU drawing its pixels.
// - `swiftshader`: drawn, the GPU's share on the CPU (slow: mostly SwiftShader's own time).
// - `discard`: the same, with RASTERIZER_DISCARD kept on (turned on at the context's creation, the engine's disable
//   ignored): every WebGL call is still validated and sent, the vertex work still done, no pixel drawn — the closest
//   this machine gets to the engine's own CPU cost a frame (an upper bound: SwiftShader's vertex threads still compete).
//   Nothing is visible on the screenshots; readPixels reads nothing meaningful.
// - `gpu`: no rendering flag — the machine's own GPU when it has one (the renderer printed tells).
// The synchronous calls (`sync`): those that wait for the GPU process' answer (getError, checkFramebufferStatus,
// readPixels, shader/program queries, …) — on a real GPU each one stops the CPU and the GPU working in parallel.

import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { v8LogArgs } from './v8-logs.mjs';

export const GL_MODES = ['swiftshader', 'discard', 'gpu'];

/** Chromium's launch flags for a rendering mode (GL_MODES). */
export function chromeArgs(gl = 'swiftshader') {
  if (gl === 'null') throw new Error("--gl null: ANGLE's null backend is ignored by this Chromium (it still renders with SwiftShader); use --gl discard for the CPU cost without drawing");
  if (!GL_MODES.includes(gl)) throw new Error(`--gl ${gl}: one of ${GL_MODES.join(', ')}`);
  return ['--no-sandbox', ...(gl === 'gpu' ? [] : ['--use-gl=angle', '--use-angle=swiftshader', '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader']), '--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required'];
}

// Browsers (--channel): `chromium` (the default) is Chromium itself in its new headless mode, as the bench suite
// (tools/bench-suite-check.mjs) and the re3 check run it: its page composited through the GPU process as a browser
// does. `shell` is Playwright's lighter headless shell: it composites otherwise (OpenMW's glide 47 fps there, 31 in
// Chromium, 2026-10-23), and once a page holds the pointer lock it sends that page ~40,000 synthetic mouse moves a
// second (zero movement; its browser and renderer compositor threads each a whole core; Chromium sends none) — a
// headless shell artifact, no browser does that.
export const CHANNELS = ['chromium', 'shell'];
/**
 * Playwright's launch options for a port measurement: the rendering mode's flags (chromeArgs), the channel (CHANNELS),
 * `args` besides (a --js-flags' V8 logs under the scratch, tools/v8-logs.mjs). Chromium's profile socket must stay
 * under 108 bytes: its temporary directory (TMPDIR) is moved to a short one under the scratch when the caller's is long.
 */
export function launchOptions({ gl = 'swiftshader', channel = 'chromium', args = [] } = {}) {
  if (!CHANNELS.includes(channel)) throw new Error(`--channel ${channel}: one of ${CHANNELS.join(', ')}`);
  if (channel === 'chromium' && (process.env.TMPDIR ?? '/tmp').length > 48) {
    process.env.TMPDIR = '/tmp/orthros-scratch/pw';
    mkdirSync(process.env.TMPDIR, { recursive: true });
  }
  // (ORTHROS_CHROME_ARGS: more flags, space-separated — a diagnosis', e.g. '--enable-logging=stderr --v=0' for a renderer
  // crash's reason in the browser's log, DEBUG=pw:browser printing it)
  const extra = (process.env.ORTHROS_CHROME_ARGS ?? '').split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
  return { headless: true, ...(channel === 'shell' ? {} : { channel }), args: v8LogArgs([...chromeArgs(gl), ...args, ...extra]) };
}

/** The WebGL methods that wait for the GPU process' answer. */
export const SYNC_CALLS = ['getError', 'checkFramebufferStatus', 'readPixels', 'finish', 'clientWaitSync', 'getSyncParameter', 'getQueryParameter',
  'getBufferSubData', 'getShaderParameter', 'getProgramParameter', 'getShaderInfoLog', 'getProgramInfoLog', 'getUniformLocation', 'getAttribLocation',
  'getActiveUniform', 'getActiveAttrib', 'getUniformBlockIndex', 'getFragDataLocation', 'getUniform', 'getVertexAttrib', 'getTexParameter',
  'getFramebufferAttachmentParameter', 'getRenderbufferParameter', 'getInternalformatParameter'];

/**
 * The probe, in the page before its scripts (a Playwright page or context): `window.perfProbe`. `discard`: the
 * rasterizer discarded (the `discard` mode); `stacks`: WebGL methods whose callers are kept (their JS/wasm stacks,
 * counted, in the measured seconds).
 */
export async function addProbe(target, { discard = false, stacks = [] } = {}) {
  await target.addInitScript(({ discard, stacks, sync }) => {
    const P = window.perfProbe = { calls: new Map(), counting: false, draws: 0, frames: 0, work: [], resumedAt: 0, shown: [], drawsAt: 0, renderer: null, discard, stacks: new Map(), sync };
    const RASTERIZER_DISCARD = 0x8C89, traced = new Set(stacks);
    for (const type of [window.WebGLRenderingContext, window.WebGL2RenderingContext]) {
      if (!type) continue;
      const proto = type.prototype;
      for (const k of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(proto)) {
        const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(proto, k); if (typeof d.value !== 'function' || k === 'constructor') continue;
        const o = d.value, draw = ['drawArrays', 'drawElements', 'drawRangeElements', 'drawArraysInstanced', 'drawElementsInstanced'].includes(k);
        const keep = traced.has(k), skipDisable = discard && k === 'disable';
        proto[k] = function (...a) {
          if (draw) P.draws++;
          if (P.counting) {
            P.calls.set(k, (P.calls.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
            if (keep) { const s = (new Error().stack ?? '').split('\n').slice(2, 9).map((l) => l.trim()).join(' < '); P.stacks.set(`${k}: ${s}`, (P.stacks.get(`${k}: ${s}`) ?? 0) + 1); }
          }
          if (skipDisable && a[0] === RASTERIZER_DISCARD) return undefined;
          return o.apply(this, a);
        };
      }
    }
    // (the context's creation: its renderer, and the rasterizer discarded from its start)
    const getContext = HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext;
    HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext = function (kind, ...rest) {
      const gl = getContext.call(this, kind, ...rest);
      if (gl && /webgl/.test(kind) && !gl.__perfSeen) {
        gl.__perfSeen = true;
        try { const info = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info'); P.renderer ??= gl.getParameter(info ? info.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER); } catch { /* lost */ }
        if (discard && window.WebGL2RenderingContext && gl instanceof WebGL2RenderingContext) gl.enable(RASTERIZER_DISCARD);
      }
      return gl;
    };
    // (a frame: one browser frame, whatever number of callbacks the page has in it — the engine's, the frame meter's;
    // the work a frame: from its first callback to the last request for the next one made in it — the engine asks for
    // it at the end of its iteration, with an asynchronous main loop as well; the frames shown: a browser frame after
    // one the engine drew in)
    const raf = window.requestAnimationFrame.bind(window);
    const tick = (t) => {
      if (t === P.tickT) return;
      if (P.lastAsk) { P.work.push(P.lastAsk - P.tickAt); if (P.work.length > 20000) P.work.shift(); }
      P.tickT = t; P.tickAt = performance.now(); P.lastAsk = 0; P.frames++;
      if (P.draws !== P.drawsAt) { P.drawsAt = P.draws; P.shown.push(t); if (P.shown.length > 20000) P.shown.shift(); }
    };
    window.requestAnimationFrame = (cb) => {
      if (P.tickAt) P.lastAsk = performance.now();
      return raf((t) => { tick(t); cb(t); });
    };
  }, { discard, stacks, sync: SYNC_CALLS });
}

/** The WebGL renderer of the page's canvas (its context as the engine made it; null before), for the checks' logs. */
export const rendererOf = (page, selector = '#canvas') => page.evaluate((selector) => {
  const c = document.querySelector(selector), gl = c?.getContext('webgl2') ?? c?.getContext('webgl');
  if (!gl) return null;
  const info = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
  return gl.getParameter(info ? info.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER);
}, selector);

/**
 * The page's reports kept off the server (a measuring session is not a player's): its posts to the telemetry and to
 * what the server learns from sessions (prefetch order, first-launch profile, heat, programs, regions) answered here.
 */
export const quietReports = (page) => page.route(/\/api\/(telemetry|prefetch|profile-seed|heat|programs|regions)\b/, (route) =>
  (route.request().method() === 'GET' ? route.continue() : route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: '{}' })));

/** The measured seconds start (the counters reset; `calls`: the WebGL calls counted by kind). */
export const startMeasure = (page, { calls = true } = {}) => page.evaluate((calls) => {
  const P = perfProbe; P.work = []; P.shown = []; P.calls.clear(); P.stacks.clear(); P.counting = calls; P.f0 = P.frames; P.d0 = P.draws; P.t0 = performance.now();
}, calls);

/** The measured seconds' summary: frames, the engine's work a frame, gaps between shown frames, WebGL calls a frame. */
export const readMeasure = (page) => page.evaluate(() => {
  const P = perfProbe, frames = Math.max(1, P.frames - P.f0), ms = performance.now() - P.t0, w = P.work.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const q = (a, f) => Math.round((a[Math.min(a.length - 1, Math.floor(a.length * f))] ?? 0) * 100) / 100;
  const calls = [...P.calls].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]), total = calls.reduce((n, [, c]) => n + c, 0), per = (c) => Math.round(c / frames * 10) / 10;
  const gaps = P.shown.slice(1).map((t, i) => t - P.shown[i]), hist = {}, sortedGaps = gaps.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
  for (const g of gaps) { const b = g < 25 ? '<25' : g < 42 ? '25-42' : g < 58 ? '42-58' : '58+'; hist[b] = (hist[b] ?? 0) + 1; }
  const sync = calls.filter(([k]) => P.sync.includes(k));
  return {
    renderer: P.renderer, discard: P.discard, fps: Math.round(frames / ms * 1000 * 10) / 10, shownFps: Math.round(gaps.length / ms * 1000 * 10) / 10, frames,
    work: { p50: q(w, 0.5), p90: q(w, 0.9), p99: q(w, 0.99), max: q(w, 1) },
    gaps: { p50: q(sortedGaps, 0.5), p99: q(sortedGaps, 0.99), max: Math.round(Math.max(0, ...gaps)), over50: gaps.filter((g) => g > 50).length, over250: gaps.filter((g) => g > 250).length },
    intervals: hist, draws: Math.round((P.draws - P.d0) / frames),
    glCalls: per(total), top: Object.fromEntries(calls.slice(0, 14).map(([k, c]) => [k, per(c)])),
    syncCalls: per(sync.reduce((n, [, c]) => n + c, 0)), sync: Object.fromEntries(sync.map(([k, c]) => [k, per(c)])),
    stacks: [...P.stacks].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, 8).map(([s, n]) => ({ n, s })),
    heapMB: Math.round((performance.memory?.usedJSHeapSize ?? 0) / 1048576)
  };
});

/** A CPU profile of the measured seconds starts (CDP's sampling profiler, 250 µs). */
export async function startProfile(page) {
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  await cdp.send('Profiler.enable'); await cdp.send('Profiler.setSamplingInterval', { interval: 250 }); await cdp.send('Profiler.start');
  return cdp;
}

/**
 * A browser trace (CDP Tracing, every process: the page's thread, the compositor, the GPU process) started on `page`'s
 * session — what the page's rendering, the GPU's queue and input do around a load (a diagnosis: place-load.mjs
 * ORTHROS_PLACE_TRACE=1). Ended by stopTrace.
 */
export async function startTrace(page, categories = TRACE_CATEGORIES) {
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  await cdp.send('Tracing.start', { transferMode: 'ReturnAsStream', streamCompression: 'gzip', traceConfig: { recordMode: 'recordContinuously', includedCategories: categories } });
  return cdp;
}
/** The categories of startTrace: tasks and frames of every process, the GPU's scheduling, input's path. */
export const TRACE_CATEGORIES = ['toplevel', 'devtools.timeline', 'disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline', 'disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline.frame', 'blink', 'cc', 'viz', 'gpu', 'gpu.service',
  'disabled-by-default-gpu.service', 'input', 'latencyInfo', 'benchmark', 'v8.execute', 'scheduler', 'renderer.scheduler'];
/** The trace of startTrace ended and written, gzipped (Chrome's JSON trace: chrome://tracing, Perfetto), to `file`. */
export async function stopTrace(cdp, file) {
  const fs = await import('node:fs');
  const done = new Promise((resolve) => cdp.once('Tracing.tracingComplete', resolve));
  await cdp.send('Tracing.end');
  const { stream } = await done;
  const out = fs.openSync(file, 'w');
  try {
    for (;;) {
      const r = await cdp.send('IO.read', { handle: stream, size: 1 << 20 });
      if (r.data) fs.writeSync(out, r.base64Encoded ? Buffer.from(r.data, 'base64') : Buffer.from(r.data, 'binary'));
      if (r.eof) break;
    }
  } finally { fs.closeSync(out); await cdp.send('IO.close', { handle: stream }).catch(() => {}); }
  return file;
}

/**
 * The profile's summary: self time by function (the WebAssembly's share apart), and the longest stretches without an
 * idle sample — the hitches: their length and the functions they spent it in (a function counted once a sample
 * wherever it is on the stack). `frames`: the measured frames (the WebAssembly's milliseconds a frame); `save`: a file
 * the raw profile is written to (a .cpuprofile, for a closer look). busy: the page's thread busy — every task, not
 * only the engine's frame (work done between frames counts too) — in ms a frame, and its stretches without an idle
 * sample over 16.7, 33 and 50 ms (busy.over16 ...).
 */
export async function stopProfile(cdp, frames, save = null) {
  const { profile: pr } = await cdp.send('Profiler.stop');
  if (save) (await import('node:fs')).writeFileSync(save, JSON.stringify(pr));
  const byId = new Map(pr.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n])), self = new Map();
  let total = 0;
  pr.samples.forEach((id, i) => { const n = byId.get(id), us = pr.timeDeltas[i] ?? 0, k = `${n.callFrame.functionName || '(anon)'} ${n.callFrame.url.split('/').pop()}`.trim(); self.set(k, (self.get(k) ?? 0) + us); total += us; });
  const wasm = [...self].filter(([k]) => k.endsWith('.wasm')).reduce((n, [, us]) => n + us, 0);
  const runs = []; let run = null;
  pr.samples.forEach((id, i) => {
    const n = byId.get(id), us = pr.timeDeltas[i] ?? 0;
    if (n.callFrame.functionName === '(idle)') { if (run) runs.push(run); run = null; return; }
    run ??= { us: 0, ids: [] }; run.us += us; run.ids.push([id, us]);
  });
  if (run) runs.push(run);
  const busyUs = runs.reduce((n, r) => n + r.us, 0), over = (ms) => runs.filter((r) => r.us > ms * 1000).length;
  const busy = { msPerFrame: Math.round(busyUs / 1000 / Math.max(1, frames) * 100) / 100, over16: over(1000 / 60), over33: over(100 / 3), over50: over(50) };
  const parent = new Map(); for (const n of pr.nodes) for (const c of n.children ?? []) parent.set(c, n.id);
  const hitches = runs.sort((a, b) => b.us - a.us).slice(0, 4).map((r) => {
    const incl = new Map();
    for (const [id, us] of r.ids) {
      const seen = new Set();
      for (let at = id; at != null; at = parent.get(at)) { const f = byId.get(at).callFrame.functionName || '(anon)'; if (!seen.has(f)) { seen.add(f); incl.set(f, (incl.get(f) ?? 0) + us); } }
    }
    return { ms: Math.round(r.us / 1000), top: Object.fromEntries([...incl].filter(([f]) => f !== '(root)').sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, 18).map(([f, us]) => [f, Math.round(us / 1000)])) };
  });
  return { wasmMsPerFrame: Math.round(wasm / 1000 / Math.max(1, frames) * 100) / 100, wasmShare: `${(100 * wasm / total).toFixed(1)}%`, busy,
    top: Object.fromEntries([...self].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, 25).map(([k, us]) => [k, `${(100 * us / total).toFixed(1)}%`])), hitches };
}

/**
 * The game data's indicator (src/host/web/data-meter-worker.js, its worker in `page`) sampled every `everyMs` until
 * stop(): stop() returns { samples, shownS, waitingS, shownAt } — the seconds it was shown, those the engine's reads
 * waited for the network (the shared counter it reads, ctrl[6]), and when it was shown ([from, to] s from the start). Read
 * in its worker: sampled while the page's thread is held too. `shots`: a directory — a screenshot at the start of each
 * time it is shown (meter-<s>.png, the first 5), and one where it is not (no-meter-<s>.png, every 20 s).
 */
export async function meterSampler(page, { everyMs = 250, shots = null } = {}) {
  const seen = [], t0 = Date.now();
  let on = true, taken = 0, plainAt = -Infinity;
  const shot = (name) => page.screenshot({ path: `${shots}/${name}-${Math.round((Date.now() - t0) / 1000)}.png` }).catch(() => {});
  const loop = (async () => {
    while (on) {
      const w = page.workers().find((x) => x.url().includes('data-meter-worker'));
      // (the worker's own top-level state: `shown` drawn, `arrived` the game data's counters)
      const s = w ? await w.evaluate(() => ({ shown, waiting: arrived ? Atomics.load(arrived, 6) : 0 })).catch(() => null) : null;
      if (s) {
        const was = seen.at(-1)?.shown, t = (Date.now() - t0) / 1000;
        seen.push({ t, ...s });
        if (shots && s.shown && !was && taken < 5) { taken++; await shot('meter'); }
        if (shots && !s.shown && t - plainAt >= 20) { plainAt = t; await shot('no-meter'); }
      }
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, everyMs));
    }
  })();
  return async () => {
    on = false; await loop;
    const secs = (k) => +(seen.filter(k).length * everyMs / 1000).toFixed(1), shownAt = [];
    for (const s of seen) { const last = shownAt.at(-1); if (!s.shown) continue; if (last && s.t - last[1] < 2 * everyMs / 1000) last[1] = +s.t.toFixed(1); else shownAt.push([+s.t.toFixed(1), +s.t.toFixed(1)]); }
    return { samples: seen.length, shownS: secs((s) => s.shown), waitingS: secs((s) => s.waiting > 0), shownAt };
  };
}

/**
 * A long session's memory, sampled every `everyS` seconds until stop(): the JS heap used, the engine's WebAssembly heap
 * (`wasmBytes`: a page function's source returning it, e.g. '() => Module.HEAPU8.length'), and the page's DOM nodes,
 * event listeners and documents (CDP Performance.getMetrics: a listener or node count that only grows is a leak).
 * stop() returns { samples: [{ t, heapMB, heapTotalMB, wasmMB, nodes, listeners, docs }] — the last one after a full
 * collection (afterGc) —, growthPer10min: least squares of each after the first `settleS` seconds }.
 */
export async function memSampler(page, everyS, wasmBytes = '() => 0', settleS = 120) {
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  await cdp.send('Performance.enable');
  const samples = [], t0 = Date.now();
  const one = async () => {
    const { metrics } = await cdp.send('Performance.getMetrics'), m = Object.fromEntries(metrics.map((x) => [x.name, x.value]));
    const wasm = await page.evaluate(`(() => { try { return (${wasmBytes})(); } catch { return 0; } })()`).catch(() => 0);
    const s = { t: Math.round((Date.now() - t0) / 1000), heapMB: +(m.JSHeapUsedSize / 1048576).toFixed(1), heapTotalMB: +(m.JSHeapTotalSize / 1048576).toFixed(1), wasmMB: +(wasm / 1048576).toFixed(1), nodes: m.Nodes, listeners: m.JSEventListeners, docs: m.Documents };
    samples.push(s); console.log('[mem]', JSON.stringify(s));
  };
  await one();
  const timer = setInterval(() => { one().catch(() => {}); }, everyS * 1000);
  return async () => {
    clearInterval(timer); await one().catch(() => {});
    // (then a full collection and a last sample: what only grew because nothing collected it yet is told apart)
    await cdp.send('HeapProfiler.collectGarbage').catch(() => {}); await one().catch(() => {}); samples.at(-1).afterGc = true;
    const later = samples.filter((s) => s.t >= settleS && !s.afterGc), slope = (k) => {
      const n = later.length; if (n < 2) return null;
      const mx = later.reduce((a, s) => a + s.t, 0) / n, my = later.reduce((a, s) => a + s[k], 0) / n;
      const b = later.reduce((a, s) => a + (s.t - mx) * (s[k] - my), 0) / Math.max(1e-9, later.reduce((a, s) => a + (s.t - mx) ** 2, 0));
      return +(b * 600).toFixed(2);
    };
    return { samples, growthPer10min: Object.fromEntries(['heapMB', 'wasmMB', 'nodes', 'listeners', 'docs'].map((k) => [k, slope(k)])) };
  };
}
```

`tools/prepare-bench.mjs`:

```mjs
// "Prepare" (the home's launch-set download, src/host/web/download-worker.js) replayed in Node for every version of the
// catalog × link — no browser: the download worker's own code (openVersion, launchSet, the engine's files, then
// HttpBackend.prefetch with learnedOnly) over the player's-link proxy (tools/net-proxy.mjs, plain HTTP here) in front
// of one Orthros server of a code tree (--code: this tree, or a copy of another commit) on a learned directory's copy
// and a frozen copy of the precompressed units. A port's page waits for the same set at a first launch (data-worker.js
// startup()), so its time is the floor of the time to the menu on that link. One JSON line per run: seconds, wire
// bytes (engine apart), requests, unit answers, the card's sizes (/api/manifests launch); `readyS` / `readyWireMB`: the
// time and wire bytes to the first progress that says done — "Ready" — (an engine that reloads in place, the card's
// `reloads`: its light set's end, the files themselves coming after as a second stage counted in `seconds`).
//
//   node tools/prepare-bench.mjs --pristine <dir with learn/ brcache/ covers/> [--code <tree>] [--links 85k:150,1m:60,7m:75]
//     [--only a,b] [--out file] [--max-seconds 1800] [--logs <dir>: the proxy's logs kept] [--known-bw]
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import net from 'node:net';
import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { startProxy } from './net-proxy.mjs';
import { parseLink, summarize } from './data-matrix.mjs';
import { DEFAULT_GAMES_DIR } from '../src/host/game-catalog.js';
import { DEFAULT_ENGINES_DIR } from '../src/host/goldsrc.js';

const args = process.argv.slice(2), opt = (k, d) => { const i = args.indexOf('--' + k); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : d; };
const code = path.resolve(opt('code', path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')));
const pristine = opt('pristine'); if (!pristine) { console.error('--pristine <dir>'); process.exit(2); }
const links = opt('links', '85k:150,1m:60,7m:75').split(',').map(parseLink);
const out = opt('out', '/dev/stdout'), maxSeconds = Number(opt('max-seconds', 1800)), keepLogs = opt('logs', null);
const only = opt('only')?.split(',');
const work = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(path.dirname(path.resolve(pristine)), 'prep-'));
const freePort = () => new Promise((resolve) => { const s = net.createServer(); s.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => { const { port } = s.address(); s.close(() => resolve(port)); }); });

execFileSync('cp', ['-a', path.join(pristine, 'learn'), path.join(work, 'learn')]);
const sport = await freePort();
const srv = spawn(process.execPath, [path.join(code, 'src/host/server.js'), '--port', String(sport), '--learn', path.join(work, 'learn'), '--br-cache', path.join(pristine, 'brcache'), '--br-cache-frozen',
  '--covers', 'off', '--games-dir', opt('games-dir', DEFAULT_GAMES_DIR), '--engines-dir', opt('engines-dir', DEFAULT_ENGINES_DIR)], { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'inherit'] });
await new Promise((r) => { srv.stdout.on('data', (d) => { if (String(d).includes('orthros: http')) r(); }); setTimeout(r, 30000); });
const catalog = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${sport}/api/manifests`)).json();

const { download } = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(code, 'src/host/web/download-worker.js')).href);
const { MemBlockStore } = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(code, 'src/vfs/opfs-store.js')).href);
const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;
let base = null;
// (a new player's browser: nothing in its HTTP cache — an "only-if-cached" request fails, as Chrome's 504)
globalThis.fetch = (u, o = {}) => { const { cache, mode, ...rest } = o; if (cache === 'only-if-cached') return Promise.resolve(new Response(null, { status: 504 })); return realFetch(typeof u === 'string' && u.startsWith('/') ? base + u : u, rest); };
// (the last progress message: the worker's last post is 'stopped')
let last = null, readyAt = null; globalThis.self = { postMessage: (m) => { if (m.type !== 'stopped') last = m; if (m.type === 'progress' && m.done && readyAt === null) readyAt = performance.now(); } };

try {
  for (const link of links) for (const m of catalog) {
    if (!m.available || (only && !only.includes(m.name))) continue;
    const langs = m.launch?.langs ? Object.keys(m.launch.langs) : [];
    const lang = langs.includes('en') ? 'en' : langs[0] ?? (m.languages.includes('en') ? 'en' : m.languages[0] ?? null);
    const card = (lang && m.launch?.langs?.[lang]) ?? m.launch;
    const logf = path.join(work, `${m.name}-${link.name}.jsonl`);
    const proxy = await startProxy({ upstream: `127.0.0.1:${sport}`, listen: 0, rate: link.rate, rtt: link.rtt, log: logf, http1: true });
    base = `http://127.0.0.1:${proxy.port}`; last = null; readyAt = null;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    const engine = card?.engineFiles?.length ? { files: card.engineFiles, bytes: card.engine } : null;
    const timer = setTimeout(() => { globalThis.self.onmessage?.({ data: { type: 'stop' } }); }, maxSeconds * 1000);
    // (--known-bw: the page knew the link's rate — a player who came before —, else a new player's unmeasured link)
    await download(m.name, args.includes('--known-bw') ? link.rate : undefined, 'launch', lang, engine, { openStore: async () => new MemBlockStore(2 ** 32) }, card?.reloads === true);
    clearTimeout(timer);
    const seconds = Math.round((performance.now() - t0) / 100) / 10;
    await proxy.close();
    const recs = fs.readFileSync(logf, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
    const s = summarize(recs), ready = readyAt === null ? null : summarize(recs, readyAt - t0);
    const row = { manifest: m.name, runtime: m.runtime, lang, link: link.name, marked: !!m.launch, seconds, done: !!last?.done, error: last?.error ?? null,
      cardMB: card ? Math.round((card.wire ?? 0) / 1e4) / 100 : null, cardLightMB: card ? Math.round((card.lightWire ?? 0) / 1e4) / 100 : null, engineCardMB: card?.engine ? Math.round(card.engine / 1e4) / 100 : 0,
      reloads: card?.reloads === true, readyS: readyAt === null ? null : Math.round((readyAt - t0) / 100) / 10, readyWireMB: ready?.wireMB ?? null,
      wireMB: s.wireMB, engineMB: s.byKind.engine?.MB ?? 0, dataMB: s.byKind.background?.MB ?? 0, requests: s.requests, dataRequests: s.dataRequests, units: s.units };
    fs.appendFileSync(out, JSON.stringify(row) + '\n');
    console.error(`[prepare] ${m.name} ${link.name}: ready ${row.readyS} s (${row.readyWireMB} MB), all ${seconds} s, ${s.wireMB} MB (engine ${row.engineMB}), ${s.requests} req, units ${JSON.stringify(s.units)}${row.error ? ' ' + row.error : ''}`);
    if (keepLogs) { fs.mkdirSync(keepLogs, { recursive: true }); fs.copyFileSync(logf, path.join(keepLogs, path.basename(logf))); }
    fs.rmSync(logf, { force: true });
  }
} finally { srv.kill(); fs.rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true }); process.exit(0); }
```

`tools/probe.mjs`:

```mjs
// Conformance probe: runs one generated suite through the interpreter (default) or the JIT
// (--jit) with per-case timing and prints failures.
// Usage: node tools/probe.mjs <suite> [showN] [onlyIndex] [--jit]
import { Conformance, CODE, isStackFaultCase } from '../tests/conformance/runner.js';
import { Interp } from '../src/cpu/interp.js';
import '../src/cpu/interp-x87.js';
import '../src/cpu/interp-sse.js';
import { Jit } from '../src/cpu/jit/jit.js';

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const useJit = args.includes('--jit');
const pos = args.filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
const suite = pos[0];
const show = +(pos[1] || 15);
const only = pos[2] !== undefined ? +pos[2] : -1;
const dir = new URL('../tests/generated/', import.meta.url).pathname;
const c = new Conformance(dir, suite);
const I = new Interp(c.mem, c.cpu);
const jit = useJit ? new Jit(c.mem, I) : null;
let fails = 0;
const t0 = Date.now();
const kinds = new Map();
for (let i = 0; i < c.count; i++) {
  if (only >= 0 && i !== only) continue;
  if (jit && isStackFaultCase(i, c)) continue;
  const { end } = c.load(i);
  c.cpu.eip = CODE;
  I.cache.clear();
  let exit;
  const t = Date.now();
  try {
    if (jit) { jit.reset(); jit.boundaries = new Set([end]); jit.cpu = c.cpu; exit = jit.run({ stopAt: end, maxInsns: 100000 }); c.lastFault = jit.lastFault ? jit.lastFault.message : null; }
    else { exit = I.run({ stopAt: end, maxInsns: 100000 }); c.lastFault = I.lastFault ? I.lastFault.message : null; }
  } catch (e) {
    fails++; if (fails <= show) console.log(`#${i} ${c.meta[i].asm}\n    exception: ${e.stack.split('\n').slice(0, 4).join('\n    ')}`); continue;
  }
  const dt = Date.now() - t;
  if (dt > 500) console.log(`SLOW #${i} ${c.meta[i].asm} ${dt}ms`);
  const d = c.compare(i, exit);
  if (d) {
    fails++;
    const k = c.meta[i].asm.split(' ')[0];
    kinds.set(k, (kinds.get(k) || 0) + 1);
    if (fails <= show) console.log(`#${i} ${c.meta[i].asm}\n    ${d}`);
  }
}
console.log(`${suite}${jit ? ' [jit]' : ''}: ${fails}/${c.count} failures in ${Date.now() - t0}ms` + (fails ? ` — by mnemonic: ${[...kinds].map(([k, v]) => `${k}:${v}`).join(' ')}` : '') + (jit ? ` stats=${JSON.stringify(jit.stats)}` : ''));

```

`tools/profile-seed-make.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Canonical first-launch profiles (docs/startup.md "Shared first-launch profile"): an operator makes, per Win32 version
// and game language, the set of profile files a new player's empty profile receives (the server offers it before any
// set the sessions reported: <learn>/seedcanon-<manifest>.json, read again when it changes). Generic: it iterates the
// game catalog, names no game.
//
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs plan --games-dir <dir> [--learn <dir>] [--only id[:lang],...]
//       every win32 version × declared language, and what the learn dir holds for it (canonical, learned candidates)
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs make --games-dir <dir> --learn <dir> [--only id[:lang],...] [--runs 2] [--seconds 170]
//       [--scratch <dir>] [--missing] [--accept agree|first] [-- <extra headless.mjs args>]
//       for each: `--runs` first launches with an empty profile (tools/with-browser-slot.sh node tools/headless.mjs <id>
//       --game-lang <l> --profile-seed 0 --profile-dir <empty dir> --seconds <s> --gl-discard --memprefetch), one after
//       the other; their profiles' seed files (seedSelect) compared; written as the canonical set when they agree (or,
//       --accept first, the first run's set, the others reported). --missing: only those without a canonical set yet.
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs put <manifest> <lang> <profile-dir> --learn <dir> [--note <text>]
//       the seed files of a profile directory (e.g. a headless run's --profile-dir, edited by hand) as the canonical set
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs promote <manifest> <lang> --learn <dir> [--key <set key>]
//       a set the sessions reported (the most reported one, or that key) as the canonical set
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs show|remove <manifest> [<lang>] --learn <dir>
//   node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs moves --games-dir <dir> --learn <dir> [--only id[:lang],...] [--dry]
//       the canonical sets of the versions whose manifest declares profileMoves (src/vfs/profile-moves.js) rewritten
//       with those moves applied (the same files at the game's new place: what a first launch writes since the
//       change, without running it again); the learned candidates that still hold files at an old place listed
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { seedSelect, seedKey, toBase64, fromBase64, seedCanonFile, canonSets } from '../src/host/profile-seed.js';
import { loadGameCatalog } from '../src/host/game-catalog.js';
import { MemBackend } from '../src/vfs/vfs.js';
import { applyProfileMoves } from '../src/vfs/profile-moves.js';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
const dash = argv.indexOf('--');
const args = dash >= 0 ? argv.slice(0, dash) : argv, extra = dash >= 0 ? argv.slice(dash + 1) : [];
const opt = (k, d) => { const i = args.indexOf('--' + k); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : d; };
const pos = args.filter((a, i) => !a.startsWith('--') && !args[i - 1]?.startsWith('--'));
const [cmd] = pos;
const learn = opt('learn');
const die = (m) => { console.error(m); process.exit(2); };

const canonPath = (name) => path.join(learn, seedCanonFile(name));
const readCanon = (name) => { try { return canonSets(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(canonPath(name), 'utf8'))); } catch { return []; } };
/** the canonical sets of `name` with `set` for its language (null: that language's removed), written atomically */
function writeCanon(name, lang, set) {
  const sets = readCanon(name).filter((s) => s.lang !== lang);
  if (set) sets.push({ lang, files: set.files, at: Date.now(), note: set.note ?? '' });
  sets.sort((a, b) => (a.lang < b.lang ? -1 : 1));
  const f = canonPath(name);
  if (!sets.length) { fs.rmSync(f, { force: true }); return; }
  fs.mkdirSync(learn, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(f + '.tmp', JSON.stringify({ v: 1, sets: sets.map(({ lang: l, files, at, note }) => ({ lang: l, files, at, note })) }, null, 1));
  fs.renameSync(f + '.tmp', f);
  const back = readCanon(name).find((s) => s.lang === lang);
  if (set && !back) throw new Error('the canonical set did not read back');
  return back;
}
/** a profile directory's files ({ path, data }), '/'-separated paths */
function dirFiles(dir) {
  const out = [];
  const walk = (d, rel) => { if (!fs.existsSync(d)) return; for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) { const p = rel ? rel + '/' + e.name : e.name; if (e.isDirectory()) walk(path.join(d, e.name), p); else if (e.isFile()) out.push({ path: p, data: new Uint8Array(fs.readFileSync(path.join(d, e.name))) }); } };
  walk(dir, '');
  return out;
}
const asSet = (files) => { const sel = seedSelect(files); return { key: seedKey(sel), files: sel.map((f) => [f.path, toBase64(f.data)]) }; };
const describe = (files) => files.map(([p, d]) => `    ${p} (${fromBase64(d).length} bytes)${/\.(ini|cfg|txt)$/i.test(p) ? '\n' + new TextDecoder().decode(fromBase64(d)).trim().split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => '      | ' + l).join('\n') : ''}`).join('\n');
const learnedSets = (name) => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(learn, `profileseed-${name.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, '_')}.json`), 'utf8')).sets ?? []; } catch { return []; } };

/** a game language as the canonical and learned sets name it: lowercased, as the server looks it up (server.js seedLang) */
const langKey = (l) => String(l ?? '').toLowerCase();

/** the win32 versions × languages of a catalog (--only id[:lang],... to restrict) */
function targets() {
  const dir = opt('games-dir') ?? die('--games-dir <dir> needed');
  const only = opt('only') ? opt('only').split(',').map((s) => s.split(':')) : null;
  const out = [];
  for (const [id, m] of loadGameCatalog(dir)) {
    if ((m.runtime ?? 'win32') !== 'win32' || m.profileSeed === false) continue;
    for (const declared of m.languages?.length ? m.languages : ['']) {
      const lang = langKey(declared);
      if (only && !only.some(([i, l]) => i === id && (l === undefined || langKey(l) === lang))) continue;
      out.push({ id, lang, declared });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function runHeadless(id, lang, profileDir, logFile) {
  const a = ['tools/with-browser-slot.sh', 'node', 'tools/headless.mjs', id, '--games-dir', opt('games-dir'), '--profile-seed', '0', '--profile-dir', profileDir,
    '--seconds', String(Number(opt('seconds', 170))), '--gl-discard', '--memprefetch', '--shots', '1000', '--out', path.join(path.dirname(profileDir), 'shots'), ...(lang ? ['--game-lang', lang] : []), ...extra];
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const log = fs.openSync(logFile, 'w');
    const p = spawn(a[0], a.slice(1), { cwd: ROOT, stdio: ['ignore', log, log] });
    p.on('exit', (code) => { fs.closeSync(log); resolve(code); });
  });
}

if (cmd === 'plan') {
  for (const { id, lang } of targets()) {
    const canon = learn ? readCanon(id).find((s) => s.lang === lang) : null;
    const cands = learn ? learnedSets(id).filter((s) => s.lang === lang) : [];
    console.log(`${id} ${lang || '-'}: ${canon ? `canonical ${canon.key} (${canon.files.length} file(s))` : 'no canonical set'}; learned candidates: ${cands.length ? cands.map((s) => `${s.key} × ${s.sessions.length}`).join(', ') : 'none'}`);
  }
} else if (cmd === 'make') {
  if (!learn) die('--learn <dir> needed');
  const runs = Math.max(1, Number(opt('runs', 2))), accept = opt('accept', 'agree');
  const scratch = path.resolve(opt('scratch', '/tmp/orthros-scratch/profile-seed-make'));
  let failed = 0;
  for (const { id, lang, declared } of targets()) {
    if (args.includes('--missing') && readCanon(id).some((s) => s.lang === lang)) { console.log(`${id} ${lang}: canonical set present, skipped`); continue; }
    const sets = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < runs; r++) {
      const dir = path.join(scratch, `${id}-${lang || 'x'}-${r}`), prof = path.join(dir, 'profile');
      fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); fs.mkdirSync(prof, { recursive: true });
      const t0 = Date.now(), code = await runHeadless(id, declared, prof, path.join(dir, 'run.log'));
      const set = asSet(dirFiles(prof));
      console.log(`${id} ${lang} run ${r + 1}/${runs}: exit ${code}, ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(0)} s, ${set.files.length} seed file(s), key ${set.files.length ? set.key : '-'} (log ${path.join(dir, 'run.log')})`);
      if (set.files.length) sets.push(set);
    }
    const agree = sets.length === runs && sets.every((s) => s.key === sets[0].key);
    if (!sets.length || (accept === 'agree' && !agree)) {
      failed++;
      console.log(`${id} ${lang}: NOT written — ${sets.length ? 'the runs disagree:' : 'no profile files (the game wrote nothing in the time given: --seconds)'}`);
      for (const s of sets) console.log(`  set ${s.key}\n${describe(s.files)}`);
      continue;
    }
    const kept = writeCanon(id, lang, { files: sets[0].files, note: `profile-seed-make ${new Date().toISOString()}, ${runs} run(s)${agree ? ' agreeing' : ', first kept'}` });
    console.log(`${id} ${lang}: canonical set ${kept.key} written to ${canonPath(id)}\n${describe(kept.files)}`);
    if (!agree) for (const s of sets.slice(1)) if (s.key !== sets[0].key) console.log(`  (another run gave ${s.key}:)\n${describe(s.files)}`);
  }
  if (!args.includes('--keep')) fs.rmSync(scratch, { recursive: true, force: true });
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
} else if (cmd === 'put') {
  const [, name, lang0, dir] = pos, lang = lang0 === undefined ? undefined : langKey(lang0);
  if (!learn || !name || lang === undefined || !dir) die('usage: put <manifest> <lang> <profile-dir> --learn <dir>');
  const set = asSet(dirFiles(dir));
  if (!set.files.length) die(`no seed file in ${dir}`);
  const kept = writeCanon(name, lang, { files: set.files, note: opt('note', `put from ${dir}`) });
  console.log(`${name} ${lang}: canonical set ${kept.key}\n${describe(kept.files)}`);
} else if (cmd === 'promote') {
  const [, name, lang0] = pos, lang = lang0 === undefined ? undefined : langKey(lang0);
  if (!learn || !name || lang === undefined) die('usage: promote <manifest> <lang> --learn <dir> [--key K]');
  const c = learnedSets(name).filter((s) => s.lang === lang && (!opt('key') || s.key === opt('key'))).sort((a, b) => b.sessions.length - a.sessions.length || b.at - a.at)[0];
  if (!c) die(`no learned set for ${name} ${lang}${opt('key') ? ' with key ' + opt('key') : ''}`);
  const kept = writeCanon(name, lang, { files: c.files, note: `promoted from the learned set ${c.key} (${c.sessions.length} reporter(s))` });
  console.log(`${name} ${lang}: canonical set ${kept.key}\n${describe(kept.files)}`);
} else if (cmd === 'show' || cmd === 'remove') {
  const [, name, lang0] = pos, lang = lang0 === undefined ? undefined : langKey(lang0);
  if (!learn || !name) die(`usage: ${cmd} <manifest> [<lang>] --learn <dir>`);
  if (cmd === 'remove') { for (const s of readCanon(name)) if (lang === undefined || s.lang === lang) writeCanon(name, s.lang, null); console.log('removed'); }
  for (const s of readCanon(name)) console.log(`${name} ${s.lang}: canonical set ${s.key}${s.note ? ' — ' + s.note : ''}\n${describe(s.files)}`);
} else if (cmd === 'moves') {
  if (!learn) die('--learn <dir> needed');
  const catalog = loadGameCatalog(opt('games-dir'));
  /** a set's files ([path, base64]) with the manifest's moves applied, and whether any moved */
  const moved = (files, moves) => {
    const b = new MemBackend();
    for (const [p, d] of files) { const parts = p.split('/'); for (let i = 1; i < parts.length; i++) b.mkdir(parts.slice(0, i).join('/')); b.open(p, { create: true }).write(0, fromBase64(d)); }
    const r = applyProfileMoves(b, moves);
    return { files: [...b.files.keys()].map((k) => { const parts = k.split('/'); return { path: parts.map((_, i) => b.names.get(parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/')) ?? parts[i]).join('/'), data: b.files.get(k).data.subarray(0, b.files.get(k).len) }; }), count: r.moved.length };
  };
  for (const { id, lang } of targets()) {
    const moves = catalog.get(id)?.profileMoves;
    if (!moves?.length) continue;
    const canon = readCanon(id).find((s) => s.lang === lang);
    if (canon) {
      const m = moved(canon.files, moves);
      if (!m.count) console.log(`${id} ${lang}: canonical set ${canon.key} already at the new place`);
      else if (args.includes('--dry')) console.log(`${id} ${lang}: canonical set ${canon.key} would be rewritten (${m.count} entr${m.count === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'} moved)\n${describe(asSet(m.files).files)}`);
      else { const kept = writeCanon(id, lang, { files: asSet(m.files).files, note: `${canon.note ? canon.note + '; ' : ''}profileMoves applied ${new Date().toISOString()}` }); console.log(`${id} ${lang}: canonical set ${canon.key} -> ${kept.key} (profileMoves applied)\n${describe(kept.files)}`); }
    } else console.log(`${id} ${lang}: no canonical set`);
    for (const c of learnedSets(id).filter((s) => s.lang === lang)) if (moved(c.files, moves).count) console.log(`${id} ${lang}: learned candidate ${c.key} (${c.sessions?.length ?? 0} reporter(s)) holds files at an old place: purge <learn>/profileseed-${id}.json (moved at the client meanwhile)`);
  }
} else {
  die('usage: node tools/profile-seed-make.mjs plan|make|put|promote|show|remove|moves ... (see the header)');
}
```
